We said: "O Messenger of Allah, is there a people with greater reward than us? We believed in you and followed you." He said: "What prevents you from that, while the Messenger of Allah is among you, bringing you revelation from heaven? Rather, a people after you will be given a book between two covers, and they will believe in it and act by what is in it; those are greater in reward than you."' (twice)"

He then related it from the hadith of Damrah ibn Rabi'ah, from Marzuq ibn Nafi', from Salih ibn Jubayr, from Abu Jum'ah, in similar wording.

This hadith contains evidence for acting upon al-wijadah (acquiring knowledge from a written source without direct hearing), a matter on which the people of hadith disagreed, as I established at the beginning of my commentary on al-Bukhari; for he praised them for it and mentioned that they are greater in reward in this respect, not absolutely.

Similarly, another hadith related by al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah al-'Abdi: Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash al-Himsi related to us, from al-Mughirah ibn Qays al-Tamimi, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Which of creation is most admirable to you in faith?" They said: "The angels." He said: "And why would they not believe, when they are in the presence of their Lord?" They said: "Then the prophets." He said: "And why would they not believe, when revelation descends upon them?" They said: "Then we." He said: "And what is wrong with you that you do not believe, while I am among you?" He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then said: "Behold, the most admirable of creation to me in faith are a people who will come after you, who will find pages in which there is a book, and they will believe in what is in them."

Abu Hatim al-Razi said: "al-Mughirah ibn Qays al-Basri is munkar al-hadith (his narrations are rejected)."

I say: However, Abu Ya'la in his Musnad, Ibn Mardawayh in his tafsir, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, related from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Abi Humayd, in which there is weakness, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from 'Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ, something similar or close to it. al-Hakim said: "Its chain is sahih, though they did not record it." [al-Dhahabi criticized al-Hakim, saying: "Rather, they declared it weak."] It has also been related similarly from Anas ibn Malik, raised (to the Prophet ﷺ). And Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Musnadi related to us, Ishaq ibn Idris related to us, Ibrahim ibn Ja'far ibn Mahmud ibn Salamah al-Ansari informed me, Ja'far ibn Mahmud informed me, from his grandmother Tuwaylah bint Aslam, who said: "I prayed the Dhuhr or the 'Asr in the mosque of Banu Harithah, and we faced the direction of Iliya' (Jerusalem), and we prayed two prostrations. Then someone came to us and informed us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had faced the Sacred House (the Ka'bah), so the women moved to the men's place and the men to the women's place, and we prayed the remaining two prostrations facing the Sacred House."

Ibrahim said: Men from Banu Harithah related to me that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ learned of that, he said: "Those are a people who believed in the unseen."

This is a gharib (singular) hadith from this route.

﴿wa yuqimuna al-salata wa mimma razaqnahum yunfiqun﴾ [3]

Ibn 'Abbas said: That is, they establish the prayer with its obligatory parts.

al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas: "Iqamat al-salah (establishing the prayer) is completing the bowing and prostration, the recitation, the humility, and attentiveness to it within it."

Qatadah said: "Iqamat al-salah is guarding its appointed times, its ablution, its bowing and its prostration."

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "Its establishment is guarding its appointed times, performing the ablution thoroughly, completing its bowing and prostration, reciting the Qur'an within it, and the tashahhud and sending blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ. This is its establishment."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah and others related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿wa mimma razaqnahum yunfiqun﴾: "the zakat of their wealth."

al-Suddi related from Abu Malik, and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ regarding ﴿wa mimma razaqnahum yunfiqun﴾: "It is a man's expenditure on his family, and this was before zakat was prescribed."

Juwaybir related from al-Dahhak: "Expenditures were acts of drawing near to Allah, according to their means and effort, until the obligatory charities were revealed: seven verses in Surah Bara'ah mention charities in them; these are the abrogating and confirming verses."

Qatadah said regarding ﴿wa mimma razaqnahum yunfiqun﴾: "So spend from what Allah has given you. These wealths are loans and deposits with you, O son of Adam; soon you will part with them."

Ibn Jarir chose that the verse is general, covering zakat and the (obligatory) expenditures, for he said: "The most preferred of the interpretations, and the most fitting for the description of these people, is that they fulfil all that is obligatory upon them from their wealth, whether it is zakat or the maintenance of one whose maintenance is incumbent upon them, from among family or dependants and others, whom they are obliged to support by kinship, ownership, or otherwise; because God, exalted is He, described them in general terms and praised them for it, and each of spending and zakat is praiseworthy and commendable."

I say: God, exalted is He, often links prayer with spending from wealth, for prayer is the right of God and His worship. It includes affirming His oneness, praising Him, glorifying Him, supplicating to Him, calling upon Him, and relying upon Him. Spending is doing good to created beings through benefit that reaches them, and the people most deserving of it are relatives, family members and slaves, then strangers. So each of the obligatory maintenance payments and the prescribed zakat falls within His saying: ﴿And from what We have provided them, they spend﴾. For this reason it is established in the two Sahihs from Ibn Umar that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Islam is built upon five: testifying that there is no god but God, establishing prayer, paying zakat, fasting Ramadan, and pilgrimage to the House." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 8, and Sahih Muslim, no. 16.] And the hadiths on this are many.

The original meaning of ṣalāh (prayer, in the sense of linguistic root) in the speech of the Arabs is supplication (du'a'). Al-A'sha said:

"Over her is a guardian who never leaves her house, and if she is slaughtered, he prays over her and blesses her (ṣallā ʿalayhā wa-zamzama)."

He also said, and another (i.e., al-A'sha again) said:

"The wind met her in her jar, and prayed over her jar and was stamped (wa-ṣallā ʿalā dannihā wa-ارtasama)."

Ibn Jarir cited both verses as evidence for this meaning.

And another, who is also al-A'sha, said:

"My daughter says, when I have made ready to depart: 'O Lord, keep my father far from ailments and pain.'
Upon you is like what you have prayed (for me), so close your eyes in sleep, for the side of a man will lie down (in rest)."

He means: upon you is of supplication the like of what you have made for me. This is clear. Then the word ṣalāh was used in the Sharia for the actions of bowing and prostration and the specific acts at specific times, with their known conditions, attributes, and well-known types [prescribed].

Ibn Jarir said: "I think that the obligatory prayer was called ṣalāh because the one who prays exposes himself to the attainment of his request for reward from God through his action, along with what he asks his Lord of his need."

[It was said: it is derived from the two ṣalawān (two veins), which move during prayer at bowing; they are two veins extending from the back until they encompass the coccyx, and from this the one who prays (al-muṣallī) is named, and he is the second to the leader in a horse race. This is open to question. It was also said: it is derived from ṣalā (burning), meaning constant attachment to something, from His saying: ﴿None will enter it except the most wretched﴾ [al-Layl: 15], i.e., he will be bound to it and remain in it. It was also said: it is derived from the heating of a piece of wood in fire so that it is straightened, just as the one who prays straightens his crookedness through prayer: ﴿Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of God is greatest﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 45]. Its derivation from supplication is more sound and more well-known, and God knows best.]

As for zakat, the discussion of it will come in its proper place, God willing.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿And those who believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you﴾ means: they affirm what you have brought from Allah, and what those messengers before you brought, without making any distinction between them, and they do not deny what they were brought from their Lord. ﴿And in the Hereafter they are certain﴾ means: in the Resurrection, the Garden, the Fire, the Reckoning, and the Balance.

The Hereafter (al-akhirah) is so named because it comes after this world (al-dunya). The exegetes have differed about who is meant here. Are they the same people described earlier in His words, ﴿who believe in the unseen and establish prayer and spend of what We have provided for them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 3], or are they a different group? On this, Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) relates three opinions:

The first [[In manuscripts ج، ط، ب، أ، و: "أحدها" (ahaduha).]]: the first-described people and the second-described people are the same, namely every believer, whether Arab believers, People of the Book believers, or others. This was said by Mujahid, Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and Qatadah.

The second: they are one group, namely the believers among the People of the Book. According to these two views, the "waw" (and) is a conjunction joining attributes to attributes, as Allah says: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, who created and proportioned, and who determined and guided, and who brought forth the pasture, and made it a dark stubble﴾ [al-A'la: 1-5], and as the poet says:

To the king, the lord and son of the lord, and the lion of the battalion in the crowded press...

Here he joins attributes to one another while the described subject is one.

The third: the first-described people are the Arab believers, and the second-described people, described by His words ﴿And those who believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you﴾ up to the end of the verse, are the believers among the People of the Book. This was related by al-Suddi in his tafsir from Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud, and some of the Companions, and Ibn Jarir chose it. In support of what he said, one cites Allah's words: ﴿And among the People of the Book are those who believe in Allah and in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down to them, humbly submissive to Allah﴾ [Al 'Imran: 199], and His words: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book before it, they believe in it. And when it is recited to them, they say: "We believe in it; indeed it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed we were Muslims before it." Those will be given their reward twice, for what they patiently endured, and they repel evil with good, and they spend of what We have provided for them﴾ [al-Qasas: 52-54]. And it is established in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of al-Sha'bi, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Three people will be given their reward twice: a man of the People of the Book who believed in his prophet and believed in me; a slave who fulfilled the rights of Allah and the rights of his masters; and a man who disciplined his slave-girl, disciplined her well, then freed her and married her." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (97), and Sahih Muslim, no. (154).]]

As for Ibn Jarir, he cited evidence for the soundness of what he said only by way of a connection: Allah described, at the beginning of this surah, the believers and the disbelievers. Just as He divided the disbelievers into two categories, the hypocrite and the disbeliever, so He divided the believers into Arab and People of the Book.

I say: The apparent view is the opinion of Mujahid, as related by al-Thawri, from a man, from Mujahid. It was also related by more than one, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, that he said: "Four verses from the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah describe the believers, two verses describe the disbelievers, and thirteen describe the hypocrites." These four verses are general to every believer who has these qualities, whether Arab or non-Arab, whether of the People of the Book, from humans or jinn. None of these qualities is valid without the others; rather, each one necessitates the others and is a condition alongside them. Belief in the unseen, establishing prayer and zakah, are not valid except together with belief in what the Messenger ﷺ brought and what those messengers before him brought, and certainty concerning the Hereafter. Just as this is not valid without that, that is not valid without this. Allah has commanded the believers to do this, as He says: ﴿O you who believe, believe in Allah and His Messenger, and in the Book which He sent down to His Messenger, and the Book which He sent down before﴾ [al-Nisa': 136], up to the end of the verse. He also says: ﴿And do not dispute with the People of the Book except in a way that is best, except with those of them who have wronged. And say: "We believe in what has been sent down to us and what has been sent down to you, and our God and your God is one"﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 46], up to the end of the verse. Allah also says: ﴿O you who have been given the Book, believe in what We have sent down, confirming what is with you﴾ [al-Nisa': 47]. He also says: ﴿Say: "O People of the Book, you are not upon anything until you establish the Torah and the Gospel and what has been sent down to you from your Lord"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 68]. And Allah informed about all the believers with this, saying: ﴿The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and the believers. Each believes in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers. We make no distinction between any of His messengers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 285], up to the end of the verse. And He says: ﴿And those who believe in Allah and His messengers and do not make distinction between any of them, those – He will give them their rewards﴾ [al-Nisa': 152]. And other verses besides these indicate the command to all believers to believe in Allah, His messengers, and His books. But the believers among the People of the Book have a particular distinction, which is that they believe in what is in their hands in detail. So when they enter Islam and believe in it in detail, they receive two rewards for that. As for others, faith is acquired by what has been mentioned in summary, as came in the Sahih: "When the People of the Book narrate to you, do not believe them and do not disbelieve them, but say: 'We believe in what has been sent down to us and what has been sent down to you.'" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (4485, 7362), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] However, the faith of many Arabs in the religion of Islam with which Muhammad ﷺ was sent may be more complete, more perfect, more comprehensive, and more inclusive than the faith of those of them who entered Islam. Although they receive two rewards on that account, another may receive from affirmation a reward exceeding the two rewards that they have obtained. And Allah knows best.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Those﴾, meaning those who possess the qualities mentioned before: belief in the Unseen, establishing the prayer, spending from what Allah has provided them, belief in what Allah has sent down to the Messenger and to those before him among the messengers, and certainty concerning the Last Abode. This necessarily entails preparing for it through righteous deeds and abandoning what is forbidden.

﴿upon guidance﴾, meaning light, clarity and insight from Allah the Exalted. ﴿And those are the successful﴾, meaning in this world and the Hereafter.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Those are upon guidance from their Lord﴾, meaning upon light from their Lord and steadfastness in what has come to them. ﴿And those are the successful﴾, meaning those who attained what they sought and were saved from the evil of what they fled from.

Ibn Jarir said: As for the meaning of His saying ﴿Those are upon guidance from their Lord﴾, the meaning is that they are upon light from their Lord, proof, steadfastness and rectitude, through Allah's making them firm and granting them success. And the interpretation of His saying ﴿And those are the successful﴾ is: the ones who prevail, who attain what they sought with Allah through their deeds and their belief in Allah, His books and His messengers, namely the winning of reward, abiding forever in the Gardens, and deliverance from what Allah has prepared for His enemies of punishment [[Tafsir al-Tabari (1/249).]].

Ibn Jarir also related an opinion from some of them that the demonstrative in His saying ﴿Those are upon guidance from their Lord and those are the successful﴾ refers back to the believers among the People of the Book described by His saying ﴿And those who believe in what has been sent down to you﴾ and so on, according to the difference of opinion mentioned earlier. On this view, it is permissible that His saying ﴿And those who believe in what has been sent down to you﴾ is a separate statement from what precedes it, and that it is in the nominative as a subject (mubtada'), whose predicate is ﴿Those are upon guidance from their Lord and those are the successful﴾. He chose that the reference is to all of those previously mentioned, from the believers among the Arabs and the People of the Book, based on what as-Suddi narrated from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, and from Murrah al-Hamdani, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "As for those who believe in the Unseen, they are the believers among the Arabs; and those who believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you are the believers among the People of the Book." Then He gathered both groups and said: ﴿Those are upon guidance from their Lord and those are the successful﴾. It has already been stated in the preferred view that this is a description of the believers in general, and the demonstrative refers back to them, and Allah knows best. This has been transmitted from Mujahid, Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas and Qatadah, may Allah have mercy on them.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Yahya ibn 'Uthman ibn Salih al-Misri related to us, my father related to us, Ibn Lahi'ah related to us, 'Ubayd Allah ibn al-Mughirah related to me, from Abu al-Haytham, whose name is Sulayman ibn 'Abd, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, from the Prophet ﷺ, and it was said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, we recite from the Qur'an and we hope, and we recite from the Qur'an and we nearly despair," or as he said. He said: So he said: "Shall I not inform you about the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. That is the Book, there is no doubt in it﴾" up to His saying ﴿the successful﴾: "These are the people of Paradise." They said: "We hope that we are these." Then he said: "﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, it is all the same for them﴾" up to His saying ﴿a great punishment﴾: "These are the people of the Fire." They said: "We are not them, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Indeed [they are]" [[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/40).]].

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve﴾, meaning: those who cover over the truth and conceal it. Allah the Exalted has decreed this for them. It makes no difference to them whether you warn them or not; they will not believe in what you have brought them. As Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, those against whom the word of your Lord has been justified will not believe. Even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment.﴾ [Yunus: 96-97] And He said concerning the obstinate among the People of the Book: ﴿And even if you brought those who were given the Scripture every sign, they would not follow your qiblah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 145], and so on. That is: whoever Allah has decreed wretchedness for, there is no one to make him happy, and whoever He has led astray, there is no guide for him. So do not let your soul go to waste in grief over them. Convey the message to them; whoever responds to you will have the greatest share, and whoever turns away, do not grieve over them and do not let that distress you. ﴿Your duty is only to convey, and upon Us is the reckoning﴾ [al-Ra'd: 40], and ﴿You are only a warner, and Allah is Disposer over all things﴾ [Hud: 12].

ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, it is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe﴾, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was eager that all people would believe and follow him in guidance. So Allah informed him that none will believe except one for whom happiness has already preceded from Allah in the First Reminder (the eternal decree), and none will go astray except one for whom wretchedness has already preceded from Allah in the First Reminder.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me, from ʿIkrimah or Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve﴾, meaning: in what has been revealed to you, even if they say, "We have believed in what came to us before you." ﴿It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe﴾, meaning: they have disbelieved in what is with them of your mention, and denied the covenant that was taken from them. Thus they have disbelieved in what came to you and in what they possess of what others brought them. So how would they listen to you giving warning and admonition, when they have disbelieved in what they have of your knowledge?!

Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: These two verses were revealed concerning the leaders of the factions, those about whom Allah said: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of Allah for ingratitude and caused their people to settle in the house of destruction? Hell, which they will burn in﴾ [Ibrahim: 28-29].

The meaning we mentioned first, which is related from Ibn ʿAbbas through the narration of ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah, is the most apparent, and it is explained by the other verses that have a similar meaning. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim has also mentioned a hadith here. He said: My father narrated to us, Yahya ibn ʿUthman ibn Salih al-Misri narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mughirah narrated to me, from Abu al-Haytham, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, we recite from the Qur'an and we hope, and we recite and we almost despair." He said: "Shall I not inform you?" Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, it is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe﴾, "These are the people of the Fire." They said: "Are we not among them, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes."

[His words ﴿they will not believe﴾ grammatically constitute a clause emphasizing what precedes it: ﴿it is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe﴾, meaning they are disbelievers in both states; therefore this is emphasized by His words ﴿they will not believe﴾. It is also possible that ﴿they will not believe﴾ is the predicate of "inna" (indeed), its implied construction being: "Indeed, those who disbelieve will not believe," and His words ﴿it is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them﴾ are a parenthetical clause. And Allah knows best.]

Al-Suddi said: "﴿Allah has sealed﴾ means: Allah has stamped (ṭaba'a)."

Qatadah said concerning this verse: "Satan overcame them when they obeyed him; so Allah sealed upon their hearts, and upon their hearing, and upon their sight is a covering (ghishawah). Thus they do not see guidance, nor do they hear, nor do they understand, nor do they reason."

Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said concerning ﴿Allah has sealed upon their hearts﴾: "I have been told that sins settle upon the heart and surround it from all its sides until they converge upon it. Their convergence upon it is the ṭab' (stamping), and the ṭab' is the khatm (sealing)." Ibn Jurayj said: "The khatm is upon the heart and the hearing."

Ibn Jurayj also said: "‘Abdullah ibn Kathir narrated to me that he heard Mujahid say: 'The rayn (rust) is milder than the ṭab', the ṭab' is milder than the locks (aqfal), and the locks are more severe than all of that.'"

Al-A‘mash said: "Mujahid showed us with his hand and said: 'They used to regard the heart as being like this'—meaning the palm—'so when the servant commits a sin, a part of it is closed up.' He then pointed with his little finger, like this, and said: 'When he sins, it closes.' Then he pointed with another finger, and when he sins it closes; then with another finger, and so on, until he had closed all his fingers. Then he said: 'It is stamped upon with a seal.'"

Mujahid said: "They used to consider that this is the rayn."

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) narrated it: from Abu Kurayb, from Waki‘, from al-A‘mash, from Mujahid, in similar wording.

Ibn Jarir said: "Some of them said: The meaning of His saying ﴿Allah has sealed upon their hearts﴾ is only a report from Allah about their arrogance and their turning away from listening to the truth to which they were called, as one says: 'So-and-so is deaf to this speech,' when he refuses to hear it and lifts himself above understanding it out of arrogance."

He said: "This is not sound, because Allah has informed that it is He who sealed upon their hearts and their hearing."

(I say): Al-Zamakhshari has indeed gone at length in establishing what Ibn Jarir rejected here, and he interpreted the verse in five ways, all of which are very weak. What emboldened him to this was nothing but his Mu‘tazilism (i‘tizal, the Mu‘tazilite school), because sealing upon their hearts and preventing the truth from reaching them is, in his view—exalted is Allah above it according to his belief—ugly. Yet if he had understood His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [al-Saff: 5], and His saying ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [al-An‘am: 110], and what resembles these verses that indicate that He, Exalted is He, only sealed upon their hearts and placed between them and guidance as a recompense in kind for their persistence in falsehood and their abandonment of the truth—and this is a just act from Him, Exalted is He, and is good, not ugly—then had he comprehended this fully, he would not have said what he said. And Allah knows best.

Al-Qurtubi said: "The Ummah is unanimous that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has described Himself as sealing and stamping upon the hearts of the disbelievers as a recompense for their disbelief, as He said: ﴿Rather, Allah has stamped upon them because of their disbelief﴾ [al-Nisa': 155]." He mentioned the hadith of the turning of hearts: "O Turner of hearts, make our hearts firm upon Your religion," and the hadith of Hudhayfah, which is in the Sahih, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who said: "Trials are presented to the hearts like a mat, strand by strand. Any heart that absorbs them has a black spot put upon it, and any heart that rejects them has a white spot put upon it, until the hearts become of two kinds: one white like a polished stone, which no trial will harm as long as the heavens and the earth endure; and the other black and dark like an overturned cup, not recognising any good nor rejecting any evil." The hadith continues.

[Ibn Jarir] said: "The truth in my view on this is what has been reported by a corresponding narration from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which is what Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Safwan ibn ‘Isa narrated to us: Ibn ‘Ajlan narrated to us, from al-Qa‘qa‘, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: '(Indeed, when a believer commits a sin, a black spot appears on his heart. If he repents, gives it up, and seeks to make amends, his heart is polished. But if he increases (in sin), the spot increases until it covers his heart. That is the rayn of which Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Nay! Rather, what they used to earn has covered over their hearts﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 14].)'"

This hadith through this chain has also been narrated by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa’i, from Qutaybah, from al-Layth ibn Sa‘d; and by Ibn Majah from Hisham ibn ‘Ammar, from Hatim ibn Isma‘il and al-Walid ibn Muslim, all three from Muhammad ibn ‘Ajlan, with the same wording.

Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih (good and authentic)."

Then Ibn Jarir said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informed that when sins follow one another upon the hearts, they close them off; and when they close them off, then the khatm (sealing) from Allah, Exalted is He, and the ṭab' (stamping) come upon them at that point, so there is no route for faith to reach them and no escape for disbelief from them. That is the khatm and ṭab' which Allah mentioned in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Allah has sealed upon their hearts and upon their hearing﴾. It is like the stamping and sealing upon what vessels and containers contain, which sight perceives, and which cannot be reached in what they contain except by breaking that seal off them and then untying them. Likewise, faith cannot reach the hearts of those whom Allah described as having sealed upon their hearts and their hearing, except after breaking His seal and untying its fastening [from them]."

Know that the complete pause (waqf tam) is at His saying, ﴿Allah has sealed upon their hearts and upon their hearing﴾, and His saying ﴿and upon their sight is a covering﴾ is a complete sentence. For the stamping is upon the heart and upon the hearing, while the ghishawah—which is the covering—is upon the sight. As al-Suddi said in his tafsir, from Abu Malik, from Abu Salih, from Ibn ‘Abbas, and from Murrah al-Hamdani, from Ibn Mas‘ud, and from some companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning His saying: ﴿Allah has sealed upon their hearts and upon their hearing﴾, he said: "So they do not understand and do not hear." And concerning ﴿and upon their sight is a covering﴾, he said: "Upon their eyes, so they do not see."

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Sa‘d narrated to me: my father narrated to us: my paternal uncle al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ibn ‘Abbas: ﴿Allah has sealed upon their hearts and upon their hearing﴾, and the ghishawah is upon their sight.

And he said: al-Qasim narrated to us: al-Husayn narrated to us, meaning Ibn Dawud, who is Sunayd: Hajjaj narrated to me, who is Ibn Muhammad al-A‘war: Ibn Jurayj narrated to me, saying: "The khatm is upon the heart and the hearing, and the ghishawah is upon the sight." Allah says: ﴿If Allah wills, He would seal upon your heart﴾ [al-Shura: 24], and He says: ﴿And He sealed upon his hearing and his heart, and placed a covering upon his sight﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 23].

Ibn Jarir said: As for the one who put ghishawah in the accusative (naṣb) in His saying, ﴿and upon their sight is a covering﴾, it is possible that he put it in the accusative by supposing a verb, its estimated form being: "and He placed upon their sight a covering." It is also possible that its accusative is by coordination (ittibā‘), upon the position (maḥall) of ﴿and upon their hearing﴾, as in His saying: ﴿and houris with wide, lovely eyes﴾ [al-Waqi‘ah: 22], and the words of the poet:

*I fed her chaff and cool water,*
*until her two eyes wept tears flowing.*

And the other said:

*And I saw your spouse in the battle,*
*girded with a sword and a spear.*

Its estimated form: "and I gave her cool water," and "carrying a spear."

When the description of the believers was presented at the beginning of the surah in four verses, then He described the state of the disbelievers with these two verses, Exalted is He began to explain the state of the hypocrites (munafiqun), who display faith and conceal disbelief. And since their matter is confused for many people, He elaborated on their mention with multiple attributes, each of which is hypocrisy, just as He sent down Surat Bara’ah concerning them, and Surat al-Munafiqun concerning them, and mentioned them in Surat al-Nur and other surahs, to make their states known so that they may be avoided, and so that whoever is afflicted with them may also avoid them. Then Allah, Exalted is He, said:

Hypocrisy (nifaq) is showing good while concealing evil. It is of several kinds: doctrinal (i'tiqadi), which is the kind for which its possessor abides forever in the Fire, and practical ('amali), which is among the greatest of sins, as its detail will come in its place, God willing. This is as Ibn Jurayj said: "The hypocrite's speech contradicts his action, his secret contradicts his public, his entrance contradicts his exit, and his presence contradicts his absence."

The attributes of the hypocrites were revealed in the Medinan surahs, because there was no hypocrisy in Mecca; rather, its opposite prevailed. Among the people there were those who openly showed disbelief under compulsion while being believers inwardly. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) migrated to Medina, where the Ansar of the Aws and the Khazraj were, and who in their pre-Islamic ignorance worshipped idols in the manner of the polytheists of the Arabs, and where the Jews, People of the Book, were present, following the way of their forefathers, and they were three tribes: Banu Qaynuqa', allies of the Khazraj, Banu al-Nadir, and Banu Qurayza, allies of the Aws. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) arrived in Medina, those among the Ansar of the two tribes of the Aws and the Khazraj who embraced Islam did so, and few of the Jews embraced Islam except 'Abdullah ibn Salam, may God be pleased with him. Hypocrisy did not yet exist at that time either, because the Muslims did not yet have a power to be feared. Indeed, (ﷺ) had made a truce with the Jews and many tribes of the Arab tribes around Medina. When the Great Battle of Badr took place, God made His word prevail and exalted Islam and its people, 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul said, and he was a leader in Medina, from the Khazraj, and he had been the chief of both factions in the pre-Islamic period, and they had resolved to make him their king, but good came to them and they embraced Islam and became occupied away from him, so he remained in his heart with resentment toward Islam and its people. When the Battle of Badr took place, he said: "This is a matter that has taken its course," so he openly entered Islam, and groups of those who followed his way and creed entered with him, and others from the People of the Book. From then on hypocrisy was found among the people of Medina and those of the Bedouins around it. As for the Emigrants (Muhajirun), there was none among them, because no one emigrated under compulsion; rather, he emigrated and left his wealth, his children, and his land, desiring what is with God in the Hereafter.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me, from Ikrimah, or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And among the people is he who says, 'We believe in God and the Last Day,' but they are not believers" means: the hypocrites of the Aws and the Khazraj and whoever was upon their affair.

Likewise, Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and al-Suddi interpreted it as referring to the hypocrites.

For this reason God, glorified is He, drew attention to the attributes of the hypocrites, lest the believers be deceived by the outward appearance of their affair, and thereby widespread corruption would result from not guarding against them and from believing in their faith, while they are in reality disbelievers. This is among the grave dangers: that good be presumed of the people of immorality. God, exalted is He, said: "And among the people is he who says, 'We believe in God and the Last Day,' but they are not believers," meaning: they say this as a statement with nothing behind it, as He said: "When the hypocrites come to you, they say, 'We testify that you are indeed the Messenger of God'" [al-Munafiqun: 1], meaning: they say this only when they come to you, not in reality. For this reason they emphasize their testimony with "inna" and the emphatic lam in its predicate, just as they emphasized their saying: "We believe in God and the Last Day." But the matter is not so, and God refuted them in their testimony, and in this statement of theirs regarding their belief, by His saying: "And God testifies that the hypocrites are indeed liars" [al-Munafiqun: 1], and by His saying "and they are not believers."

And His saying, exalted is He: "They seek to deceive God and those who believe" means: by displaying what they display of faith while concealing disbelief. They think in their ignorance that they deceive God by this, and that it benefits them with Him, and that it passes over Him as it passes over some believers. As He said: "On the day when God raises them all, and they swear to Him as they swear to you, and they think they are upon something. Indeed, they are the liars" [al-Mujadilah: 18]. For this reason He answered their belief in this with His saying: "And they deceive none but themselves, and they do not perceive." He says: they do not deceive by this conduct of theirs, and they deceive none but themselves, and they do not perceive this about themselves, as He said: "Indeed, the hypocrites seek to deceive God, but He is their Deceiver" [al-Nisa': 142].

Some readers recited: "wa-ma yukhadi'una illa anfusahum" ("and they deceive none but themselves"), and both readings return to one meaning.

Ibn Jarir said: If someone says: how can the hypocrite be deceiving God and the believers, when he does not display with his tongue anything other than what he believes, except out of taqiyyah (precautionary dissimulation)?

It is said: The Arabs do not refuse to call one who gives with his tongue other than what is in his heart "taqiyyah," so that he may escape what he fears, "deceiver." Likewise the hypocrite is called a deceiver of God and the believers, by his display of what he displays with his tongue as taqiyyah, by which he saves himself from killing, captivity, and immediate punishment, while he conceals something other than what he displays. And that from his action, though it is deception of the believers in the immediate life of this world, is for himself by this action a deceiver, because he shows to it by his action that he gives it its wish and gives it the cup of its joy, while he is leading it to the watering places of its ruin, making it drink the cup of its punishment, and increasing it in God's anger and painful punishment beyond its endurance. That is his deception of himself, supposing, despite his harm to it regarding its final return, that he is doing good to it. As He said: "And they deceive none but themselves, and they do not perceive," informing His servants, the believers, that the hypocrites, by harming themselves in provoking their Lord against them through their disbelief, doubt and denial, are neither aware nor discerning, but are upon a blind state regarding their affair.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Mubarak informed us, in what he wrote to me, Zayd ibn al-Mubarak told us, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying, exalted is He: "They seek to deceive God," he said: they display "There is no god but God," desiring by it to secure their blood and their wealth, while in themselves is other than that.

Sa'id said, from Qatadah: "And among the people is he who says, 'We believe in God and the Last Day,' but they are not believers. They seek to deceive God and those who believe, and they deceive none but themselves, and they do not perceive." The description of the hypocrite according to many: corrupt of character, he affirms with his tongue, denies in his heart, and opposes with his deeds; he becomes upon one state and in the evening upon another, and in the evening upon one state and in the morning upon another, and he tilts like a ship, whenever a wind blows, he blows with it.

Ibn Abbas, and Murrah al-Hamdani on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud, and some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, said regarding this verse: ﴿In their hearts is a disease﴾, he said: doubt. ﴿So Allah increased them in disease﴾, he said: doubt.

Muhammad [ibn] Ishaq said, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, on the authority of Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿In their hearts is a disease﴾, he said: doubt.

Likewise said Mujahid, Ikrimah, al-Hasan al-Basri, Abu al-Aliyah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and Qatadah.

It is related from Ikrimah and Tawus: ﴿In their hearts is a disease﴾, meaning: showing off (riya').

al-Dahhak said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: ﴿In their hearts is a disease﴾, he said: hypocrisy. ﴿So Allah increased them in disease﴾, he said: increased them in hypocrisy. This is similar to the first.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿In their hearts is a disease﴾, he said: this is a disease in the religion, not a disease in the bodies, and they are the hypocrites. And the disease is the doubt that entered them in Islam. ﴿So Allah increased them in disease﴾, he said: He increased them in filth (rijs). He recited: ﴿As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice. And as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it has added to them filth upon their filth﴾ [al-Tawbah: 124, 125], he said: evil upon their evil and misguidance upon their misguidance.

What Abd al-Rahman said, may Allah have mercy on him, is good, and it is the recompense being of the same kind as the deed. Thus said the earlier scholars as well, and it is similar to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety﴾ [Muhammad: 17].

As for His saying ﴿because they used to lie﴾, it has been recited as "yukadhdhibun" (they deny). They were characterized by both of these: they were liars, and they denied the truth; they combined both of these.

Al-Qurtubi and others among the exegetes were asked about the wisdom of the Prophet's, peace be upon him, restraint from killing the hypocrites, despite knowing the identities of some of them. They mentioned answers to this, among them what is established in the two Sahihs: that he said to Umar: "I dislike that the Arabs should say that Muhammad kills his companions."[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4902) and Sahih Muslim no. (3314).]] The meaning of this is the fear that, because of that, many of the Bedouins would turn away from entering Islam, not knowing the wisdom of his killing them, and that his killing them was only for their disbelief, since they would take him only by what appeared to them, saying: Muhammad kills his companions. Al-Qurtubi said: This is the statement of our scholars and others, just as he used to give to those whose hearts were to be reconciled (al-Mu'allafah qulubuhum) while knowing the evil of their belief. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is the approach of the followers of Malik; Muhammad ibn al-Jahm, al-Qadi Isma'il, al-Abhari, and Ibn al-Majishun explicitly stated it.

Among the answers is what Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only refrained from the hypocrites so that he might make clear to his community that a judge does not judge by his own knowledge.

Al-Qurtubi said: The scholars have unanimously agreed, all of them, that a judge does not execute by his knowledge, although they differ regarding the rest of the rulings. He said: Among the answers is what al-Shafi'i said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, was only prevented from killing the hypocrites by what they displayed of Islam, together with his knowledge of their hypocrisy, because what they display erases what came before it. This is supported by his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, in the hadith whose authenticity is agreed upon in the two Sahihs and others: "I have been commanded to fight the people until they say: There is no god but Allah. So when they say it, they have protected their blood and their property from me, except by its right, and their reckoning is with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (25) and Sahih Muslim no. (22), from the hadith of Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]] The meaning of this: whoever says it, the rulings of Islam apply to him outwardly. If he believes in it, he finds its reward in the Hereafter; if he does not believe in it, the application of the ruling to him in this world will not benefit him in the Hereafter. He was among the companions of the believers: ﴿They will call out to them: Were we not with you? They will say: Yes, but you tempted yourselves, and you waited, and you doubted, and false hopes deceived you until the command of Allah came﴾ [al-Hadid: 14], so they mix with them in some of the place of gathering, and when the separation takes place, they are distinguished from them and left behind: ﴿And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire﴾ [Saba': 54], and they will not be able to prostrate with them, as the hadiths have stated. Among the answers is what some of them said: He did not kill them only because he feared their evil while he, peace be upon him, was among them, reciting to them the clear verses of Allah. But after him, they are killed when they display hypocrisy and the Muslims know it. Malik said: The hypocrite in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is the zindiq (heretic) of today.

I say: The scholars have differed regarding the killing of the zindiq when he displays disbelief: whether he is to be asked to repent or not; or a distinction is made between whether he is a propagandist or not; or whether his apostasy recurs or not; or whether his Islam and return were of his own accord or after it became apparent against him. These are various opinions, the detailed explanation, establishment, and attribution of which is the subject of the book of rulings (al-Ahkam).

(Note) The statement of those who say that the Prophet, peace be upon him, knew the identities of some of the hypocrites is based only on the hadith of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman about the naming of those fourteen hypocrites in the expedition of Tabuk, who intended to assassinate the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the darkness of the night at a mountain pass there; they resolved to startle the she-camel so that he would fall from it. Allah revealed their plot to him, and so He informed Hudhayfah of it. Perhaps the restraint from killing them was due to one of these grounds or to something else, and Allah knows best.

As for others than these, Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites, and among the people of Madinah are those who have become adept at hypocrisy. You do not know them; We know them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 101], and He, exalted is He, said: ﴿If the hypocrites do not desist, and those in whose hearts is a disease, and the agitators in Madinah, We will surely incite you against them; then they will not remain your neighbors therein except briefly. Cursed, wherever they are found, they will be seized and killed with killing﴾ [al-Ahzab: 60, 61]. In this is evidence that he was not shown them and did not know them individually; rather, their attributes were mentioned to him, and he would discern them in some of them, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if We willed, We would have shown them to you, and you would know them by their marks; and you will surely know them by the tone of their speech﴾ [Muhammad: 30]. Among the most famous of them for hypocrisy was Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, and Zayd ibn Arqam testified against him with that statement which preceded in the description of the hypocrites. Despite this, when he died, the Prophet ﷺ prayed over him and attended his burial as he would do for the rest of the Muslims. Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, rebuked him about it, and he said: "Indeed, I dislike that the Arabs should say that Muhammad kills his companions." In a narration in the Sahih: "I was given a choice, so I chose." And in another narration: "If I knew that if I increased it beyond seventy, Allah would forgive him, I would increase it."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verses 11–12:

Al-Suddi said in his tafsir, from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, and from Murrah al-Tayyib al-Hamdani, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some (ناس) of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth," they say, "We are only reformers."﴾ As for ﴿Do not cause corruption on the earth﴾, he said: corruption is disbelief (kufr) and acting in disobedience.

Abu Ja'far said, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth"﴾, he said: meaning, "Do not disobey on the earth." Their corruption was disobedience to Allah, because whoever disobeys Allah on the earth, or commands disobedience to Allah, has caused corruption on the earth, since the reform of the earth and the heavens is by obedience.

Likewise said al-Rabi' ibn Anas and Qatadah.

Ibn Jurayj said, from Mujahid: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth"﴾, he said: when they engage in disobedience to Allah and it is said to them, "Do not do such and such," they say, "We are only upon guidance, reformers."

Waki', 'Isa ibn Yunus, and 'Uthham ibn 'Ali have said, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from 'Abbad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Asadi, from Salman al-Farisi: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth," they say, "We are only reformers."﴾ Salman said: the people of this verse have not yet come.

Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn 'Uthman ibn Hakim related to me, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Shurayk related to us, my father related to me, from al-A'mash, from Zayd ibn Wahb and others, from Salman, regarding this verse, he said: "These have not yet come."

Ibn Jarir said: It is possible that Salman meant by this that those who come with this description are greater in corruption than those who were in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), not that he meant that no one with that description had passed.

Ibn Jarir said: The hypocrites are corrupters on the earth through their disobedience to their Lord therein, their committing therein what He forbade them from committing, their neglect of His obligations, their doubt about His religion, by which no deed is accepted from anyone except with belief in it and certainty of its truth, their lying to the believers with their claim other than what they actually hold of doubt and suspicion, and their supporting the people of disbelief in Allah, His books and His messengers against the friends of Allah whenever they find a way to do so. That is the corruption of the hypocrites on the earth, while they think that by their doing so they are reformers therein.

What he said is good, for among corruption on the earth is the taking of disbelievers as allies by believers, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those who disbelieve are allies of one another. If you do not do this, there will be fitnah on the earth and great corruption﴾ [al-Anfal: 73]. So Allah cut off allegiance between the believers and the disbelievers, as He said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers. Do you want to give Allah a clear case against yourselves?﴾ [an-Nisa': 144]. Then He said: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire, and you will not find for them a helper﴾ [an-Nisa': 145]. Since the hypocrite's outward appearance is that of faith, his affair became confused for the believers, so it is as if the corruption comes from the side of the hypocrite, because he is the one who deceived the believers with his statement, which has no reality, and allied the disbelievers against the believers. Had he remained in his first state, his evil would have been lighter; and had he made his deeds sincerely for Allah and his speech matched his action, he would have prospered and succeeded. For this reason, Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth," they say, "We are only reformers."﴾ That is, they want to placate both groups, the believers and the disbelievers, and to reconcile with these and with those, as Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth," they say, "We are only reformers."﴾ That is: we only want reconciliation between the two groups, the believers and the People of the Book. Allah says: ﴿Unquestionably, they are the corrupters, but they do not perceive﴾. He says: Unquestionably, this which they adopt and claim to be reform is in fact corruption itself, but due to their ignorance they do not perceive that it is corruption.

By "the foolish" they mean, may Allah curse them, the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), may Allah be pleased with them. This was said by Abu al-'Aliyah and al-Suddi in his tafsir, with his chain of narration from Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud and other than one of the Companions, and Al-Rabi' ibn Anas, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam and others also say this, saying: "Shall we and these be on one level, on one path, while they are foolish?!"

As-sufaha' (the foolish) is the plural of safih, just as al-hukama' is the plural of hakim (wise), and al-halama' is the plural of halim (forbearing). The safih is the ignorant, weak-minded person who has little knowledge of where benefit and harm lie. For this reason Allah called women and children "foolish" in His saying: ﴿And do not give the foolish your wealth, which Allah has made a means of support for you﴾ [An-Nisa: 5]. The majority of the scholars of the early generations said: they are women and children.

Allah, glorified is He, has answered them in all these instances, saying: ﴿Unquestionably, it is they who are the foolish﴾, affirming and restricting foolishness to them.

﴿But they do not know﴾, meaning: and it is part of the completeness of their ignorance that they do not know their own state of misguidance and ignorance. That is more ruinous for them and more emphatic in blindness and distance from guidance.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿with their devils﴾ means the Jews who command them to deny and oppose what the Messenger brought.

Mujahid said: ﴿with their devils﴾ means with their companions among the hypocrites and the polytheists.

Qatadah said: ﴿with their devils﴾: he said, with their chiefs and leaders in polytheism and evil.

Abu Malik, Abu al-'Aliyah, as-Suddi and ar-Rabi' ibn Anas explained it in a similar way.

Ibn Jarir said: The devils (shayatin) of every thing are its rebellious ones. The devils may be from among mankind and the jinn, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy – devils of mankind and jinn, inspiring one another with decorated speech as deception﴾ [al-An'am: 112].

In the Musnad, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We seek refuge in Allah from the devils of mankind and jinn." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, do mankind have devils?" He said: "Yes."

* *

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They say, "Indeed we are with you"﴾. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from Ikrimah, or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: meaning, we are upon the same as you are upon. ﴿We are only mockers﴾, meaning: we only mock the people and make sport of them.

Ad-Dahhak said, from Ibn Abbas: They say, "We are only mockers," scoffing at the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Ar-Rabi' ibn Anas and Qatadah said likewise.

* *

His saying, the Exalted, as a reply to them and a requital for their conduct: ﴿Allah mocks them and extends them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾.

Ibn Jarir said: Allah, the Exalted, informed that He will do this to them on the Day of Resurrection, in His saying: ﴿On the Day the hypocrite men and hypocrite women will say to those who believed, "Wait for us that we may acquire some of your light." It will be said, "Return behind you and seek light." So a wall will be struck between them with a door, its inner part containing mercy and its outer part facing torment﴾ [al-Hadid: 13], and His saying: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think that the respite We give them is good for them. We only give them respite that they may increase in sin, and they will have a humiliating punishment﴾ [Al 'Imran: 178]. He said: So this and what is similar to it, of Allah's mockery, His derision, His plotting and His deception toward the hypocrites and the people of polytheism, in the view of the one who says this and interprets it this way.

He said: Others said: Rather, His mocking them is His rebuke of them and His blaming them for what they committed of His disobedience and of disbelief in Him.

He said: Others said: This and its like are by way of reply, like a man's saying to one who deceived him when he has gained power over him: "I am the one who deceived you," when no deception came from him, but he said it when the matter had come into his hands. Ibn Jarir said: The correct meaning is that He increases them by way of giving them respite and leaving them in their insolence and rebellion, as He said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their eyes, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [al-An'am: 110].

And at-tughyan (transgression) is exceeding the limit in a thing, as He said: ﴿Indeed, when the water rose beyond its limit, We carried you in the sailing ship﴾ [al-Haqqah: 11]. Ad-Dahhak said, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾: in their disbelief, hesitating.

Likewise as-Suddi explained it with his chain from the Companions, and Abu al-'Aliyah, Qatadah, ar-Rabi' ibn Anas, Mujahid, Abu Malik and 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Zayd said so: in their disbelief and their misguidance.

Ibn Jarir said: al-'Amah (wandering blindly) is misguidance. It is said: "'Amiha fulan ya'mahu 'amahan and 'umuhan," when he went astray.

He said: His saying: ﴿in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ means in their misguidance and their disbelief, by which its filth has engulfed them and its uncleanness has overcome them, as they hesitate in misguidance, not finding a way out of it, because Allah, the Exalted, has sealed their hearts and set a seal upon them, and blinded their eyes to guidance and covered them, so they do not see right guidance nor are they guided to a path.

[Some said: blindness (al-'ama) is in the eye, and wandering (al-'amah) is in the heart. Blindness may also be used of the heart: Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿For indeed, it is not the eyes that go blind, but blind are the hearts within the breasts﴾ [al-Hajj: 46]. It is said: "'Amiha al-rajulu ya'mahu 'umuhan, so he is 'amih and 'amih, and its plural is 'ummah; and his camels went astray (al-'amha'), when he did not know where they had gone."]

Al-Suddi said in his tafsir, on the authority of Abu Malik and of Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some of the Companions regarding: ﴿Those are the ones who have bartered away guidance for error﴾, he said: they took error and abandoned guidance.

Muhammad [[addition from J.]] ibn Ishaq said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from Ikrimah, or from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding: ﴿Those are the ones who have bartered away guidance for error﴾, i.e., disbelief in exchange for faith.

Mujahid said: they believed and then disbelieved.

Qatadah said: they preferred error over guidance [i.e., disbelief in exchange for faith] [[addition from T.]]. What Qatadah said resembles in meaning the statement of Allah the Exalted concerning Thamud: ﴿As for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾ [Fussilat: 17] [[In H: "fa-amma", which is an error.]].

The summary of what the exegetes have stated above is that the hypocrites turned away from guidance to misguidance, and exchanged guidance for error. This is the meaning of His statement: ﴿Those are the ones who have bartered away guidance for error﴾, i.e., they gave up guidance as the price for error. This applies whether one of them had attained faith and then reverted to disbelief, as Allah said of them: ﴿That is because they believed and then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 3], or whether they preferred error over guidance, as the case may be for another group among them, for they are of various types and categories. For this reason Allah said: ﴿So their commerce did not profit them, nor were they guided﴾, i.e., their transaction did not yield profit in this exchange, ﴿nor were they guided﴾, i.e., they were not rightly guided in their conduct.

Ibn Jarir said: Bishr related to us, Yazid related to us, Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah regarding: ﴿So their commerce did not profit them, nor were they guided﴾: By Allah, you have seen them leave guidance for error, the community for division, security for fear, and the Sunnah for innovation. And likewise Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, from the hadith of Yazid ibn Zuray', from Sa'id, from Qatadah, with the same wording.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 17–18:

It is said: mathal (مَثَلٌ), mithl (مِثْلٌ) and mathil (مَثِيلٌ) — also — and the plural is amthal (أَمْثَالٌ). Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And these parables We present to the people, but none understands them except the knowledgeable.﴾ [Al-Ankabut: 43]

The meaning of this parable is: Allah, glorified is He, likened their exchanging guidance for misguidance, and their turning, after clear insight, to blindness, to a man who kindled a fire. When it illuminated what was around him, and he benefited from it and saw by it what was on his right and his left, and felt at ease with it, then while he was in that state, its fire went out, and he was in intense darkness, unable to see or find the way. He is also deaf, unable to hear, and mute, unable to speak, and blind; even if there were light, he would not see. Therefore he does not return to what he was upon before that. So likewise are these hypocrites, in their exchanging misguidance in place of guidance, and their preferring error over right guidance. In this parable there is an indication that they had believed and then disbelieved, as Allah the Exalted informed about them in other than this place, and Allah knows best.

Al-Fakhr al-Razi related what we have said in his tafsir from al-Suddi, then said: "The comparison here is in the utmost correctness, because by their faith they first acquired light, then by their hypocrisy they subsequently nullified that light, so they fell into a great bewilderment, for there is no bewilderment greater than the bewilderment of religion."

Ibn Jarir claimed that those to whom the parable is struck here never believed at any time, and he argued with the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And among the people are those who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day," but they are not believers.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 8]

The correct view is that this is information about them in their state of hypocrisy and disbelief, and this does not negate that faith had occurred for them before that, after which it was taken from them and a seal was set upon their hearts. Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, did not recall here this verse, which is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿That is because they believed, then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed, and they do not understand.﴾ [Al-Munafiqun: 3] Therefore Ibn Jarir interpreted this parable to mean that they were illuminated by what they displayed of the word of faith, meaning in the worldly life, and then darknesses followed them on the Day of Resurrection.

He said: It is valid to strike a parable for a group with a single individual, as He said: ﴿You see them looking at you, their eyes revolving like one who has fainted from death﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 19], meaning: like the revolving of the eyes of one who has fainted from death. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Your creation and your resurrection are not but as a single soul﴾ [Luqman: 28], and Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The example of those who were entrusted with the Torah and then did not carry it is like the example of a donkey that carries volumes﴾ [Al-Jumu'ah: 5]. Some of them said: the sense of the speech is: "the example of their situation is like the situation of the one who kindled a fire." Some said: "the one who kindled" (al-mustawqid) is singular referring to a group with him. Others said: "alladhi" here means "alladhina" (those), as the poet said:

"Indeed, those whose blood was spilled at Falj — they are the people, all of the people, O Umm Khalid." [The verse is by al-Ashhab ibn Rumaylah, as in Lisan al-Arab, entry "falaj".]

I say: In the course of the parable he shifted from the singular to the plural, in His saying: ﴿So when it illuminated what was around him, Allah took away their light and left them in darknesses, not seeing. Deaf, dumb, blind, so they will not return.﴾ This is more eloquent in speech and more compelling in arrangement. His saying: ﴿Allah took away their light﴾ means: He removed from them what would benefit them, which is the light, and left for them what would harm them, which is burning and smoke. ﴿And left them in darknesses﴾ is what they are in of doubt, disbelief and hypocrisy. ﴿Not seeing﴾: they are not guided to paths of goodness, nor do they recognize them. And they are, along with that, ﴿deaf﴾: they do not hear good; ﴿dumb﴾: they do not speak what benefits them; ﴿blind﴾: in misguidance and blindness of insight, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿For indeed, it is not the eyes that go blind, but blind are the hearts within the breasts﴾ [Al-Hajj: 46]. Therefore they do not return to the guidance they had, which they exchanged for misguidance.

Mention of the statements of the Salaf among the commentators, in a similar manner to what we have mentioned:

Al-Suddi said in his tafsir, from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some of the Companions, regarding His saying: ﴿So when it illuminated what was around him﴾, that he claimed: some people entered Islam at the arrival of the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah, then they became hypocrites. Their example was like the example of a man who was in darkness, who kindled a fire, and it illuminated what was around him of filth or harm, so he saw it until he knew what to guard against from it. Then while he was in that state, his fire went out, and he remained not knowing what harm to guard against. So likewise is the hypocrite: he was in the darkness of polytheism, then he embraced Islam, and he knew the lawful and the unlawful, and the good and the evil. Then while he was in that state, he disbelieved, and he no longer knew the lawful from the unlawful, nor the good from the evil.

Mujahid said: ﴿So when it illuminated what was around him﴾: as for the illumination of the fire, it is their turning toward the believers and the guidance.

'Ata' al-Khurasani, regarding His saying: ﴿Their example is like the example of one who kindled a fire﴾, said: This is the example of the hypocrite: he sees at times and knows at times, then the blindness of the heart overtakes him.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It is narrated from Ikrimah, al-Hasan, al-Suddi and al-Rabi' ibn Anas something similar to the saying of 'Ata' al-Khurasani.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, regarding His saying: ﴿Their example is like the example of one who kindled a fire﴾ to the end of the verse, said: This is the attribute of the hypocrites. They had believed, until faith illuminated in their hearts, just as the fire illuminated for those who kindled it. Then they disbelieved, so Allah took away their light, removing it, just as the light of this fire departed, and He left them in darknesses, not seeing.

Al-'Awfi, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding this verse, said: As for the light, it is their faith which they spoke with; and as for the darkness, it is their misguidance and disbelief which they spoke with. They were a people upon guidance, then it was taken from them, so they transgressed after that.

As for the statement of Ibn Jarir, it resembles what 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Their example is like the example of one who kindled a fire﴾, he said: This is a parable which Allah struck for the hypocrites, that they used to gain honor through Islam, so the Muslims would marry them, inherit from them, and share the spoils with them. Then when they died, Allah stripped them of that honor, just as the owner of the fire was stripped of its light.

Abu Ja'far al-Razi said, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah: ﴿Their example is like the example of one who kindled a fire﴾: indeed the light of the fire is only for as long as you kindle it; when it dies down, its light departs. Likewise is the hypocrite: whenever he speaks the word of sincerity, "There is no god but Allah," it shines for him; but when he doubts, he falls into darkness.

Al-Dahhak, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah took away their light﴾, said: As for their light, it is their faith which they spoke with.

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿Their example is like the example of one who kindled a fire, and when it illuminated what was around him﴾: it is "There is no god but Allah." It illuminated for them, so they ate by it, drank, and were secure in the world, married women, and preserved their blood; until when they died, Allah took away their light and left them in darknesses, not seeing.

Sa'id, from Qatadah, regarding this verse, said: The meaning is that the hypocrite spoke "There is no god but Allah," and the world shone for him, so he married Muslims by it, fought alongside them by it, inherited from them by it, and his blood and property were preserved by it. But when death came, the hypocrite was stripped of it, because it had no root in his heart and no reality in his deeds.

﴿And left them in darknesses﴾: 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas, said: "And left them in darknesses" means: in punishment when they die.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And left them in darknesses," i.e., they see the truth and speak by it, until when they came out of the darkness of disbelief, they extinguished it by their disbelief and hypocrisy regarding it, so Allah left them in the darknesses of disbelief, so they do not see guidance and do not remain upon the truth.

Al-Suddi said in his tafsir with his chain: "And left them in darknesses": the darkness was their hypocrisy.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: ﴿And left them in darknesses, not seeing﴾: that is when the hypocrite dies, his evil deeds darken upon him, and he finds no good deed by which he might affirm his saying, "There is no god but Allah."

﴿Deaf, dumb, blind﴾: Al-Suddi said with his chain: ﴿Deaf, dumb, blind﴾: they are mute and blind.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Deaf, dumb, blind﴾ means: they do not hear guidance, nor see it, nor understand it. Likewise said Abu al-'Aliyah and Qatadah ibn Di'amah.

﴿So they will not return﴾: Ibn 'Abbas said: i.e., they will not return to guidance. Likewise said al-Rabi' ibn Anas.

Al-Suddi said with his chain: ﴿Deaf, dumb, blind, so they will not return﴾ to Islam.

Qatadah said: ﴿So they will not return﴾, i.e., they will not repent, nor do they remember.

This is another parable which Allah, the Exalted, struck for another category of the hypocrites. They are a people for whom the truth sometimes becomes apparent, and at other times they doubt. So their hearts, in their state of doubt, disbelief and wavering, are ﴿like a rain-cloud﴾. *Sayyib* means rain. This is the view of Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, some of the Companions, Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ata', al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatadah, 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, al-Suddi, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas.

Al-Dahhak said: it is the cloud.

The more well-known view is that it is the rain that descends from the sky in a state of ﴿darkness﴾, which is doubt, disbelief and hypocrisy. ﴿And thunder﴾, which is what agitates the hearts with fear, for it is a characteristic of the hypocrites to have intense dread and terror, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿They think every shout is against them [they are the enemy]﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 4]. And He said: ﴿And they swear by Allah that they are surely of you, but they are not of you; rather they are a people who are afraid. If they could find a refuge, or caves, or a place to enter, they would turn towards it at full speed﴾ [al-Tawbah: 56-57].

﴿And lightning﴾ is that which flashes in the hearts of this type of hypocrite at certain times, from the light of faith. Therefore He said: ﴿They put their fingers in their ears against the thunderbolts, fearing death, and Allah encompasses the disbelievers﴾. That is: their caution will not avail them anything, because Allah encompasses them [with] His power, and they are under His will and decree, as He said: ﴿Has the story of the hosts reached you? Pharaoh and Thamud? Nay, those who disbelieve are in denial. And Allah is behind them, encompassing﴾ [al-Buruj: 17-20].

[*Sawa'iq* is the plural of *sa'iqah* (thunderbolt), which is fire that descends from the sky at the time of intense thunder. Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad transmitted from some people *sa'iqah*, and some transmitted *sa'iqah*, *sa'qah* and *sa'iqah* [with a different vowelling]. It is reported from al-Hasan al-Basri that he recited "min al-sawaqi' hadhar al-mawt" with the qaf placed before the waw. They recited, as proof, a line of Abu al-Najm:

*yahkunaka bi-al-mathquulati al-qawati' ... shaqqa al-barqu 'an al-sawaqi'* [[The verse is in Lisan al-'Arab, under the root ṣ-q-ʻ, where it reads: "yahkūnaka bi-al-maṣqūlati al-qawāṭiʻ ... tashaqqaqa al-barqu ʻan al-ṣawāqiʻ"]]

Al-Nahhas said: this is the dialect of the Banu Tamim and some of the Banu Rabi'ah, as transmitted.]

Then He said: ﴿The lightning nearly snatches away their sight﴾, that is: because of its intensity and power in itself, and the weakness of their insight, and its inability to remain firm in faith.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿The lightning nearly snatches away their sight﴾ means: the clear verses of the Qur'an nearly expose the faults of the hypocrites.

They are lighter in condition than those before them.
