Muqatil ibn Hayyan, concerning His words: ﴿Those are the losers﴾, said: [it means] in the Hereafter. This is like His words: ﴿For them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode﴾ [al-Ra'd: 25].

Al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas: every name God attributed to people other than the people of Islam, such as "losers," He means by it disbelief, and what He attributed to the people of Islam He means by it sin.

Ibn Jarir said concerning His words: ﴿Those are the losers﴾: al-khasirun is the plural of khasir, and they are those who diminish their own selves and their shares by their disobedience to God, of His mercy. It is like a man who loses in his trade by having something deducted from his capital in his sale. Likewise the disbeliever and the hypocrite lose by God's depriving them of His mercy, which He created for His servants, on the Day of Resurrection, when they are most in need of His mercy. It is said of this: khasira al-rajulu yakhsaru khasran wa khusranan wa khasaran, as Jarir ibn 'Atiyyah said:

Indeed Sulayt is in loss, indeed he is
a son of a people who were created as slaves.

Allah the Exalted says, arguing for His existence and power, and that He is the Creator who disposes of His servants as He wills: "How can you disbelieve in Allah?" That is, how can you deny His existence, or worship others alongside Him! "And you were dead and He gave you life." That is, you were non-existent and He brought you forth into existence, as Allah says: "Or were they created from nothing, or were they the creators? Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Rather, they are not certain" [At-Tur: 35-36]; and He says: "Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning?" [Al-Insan: 1]. The verses on this are many.

Sufyan ath-Thawri narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, regarding "They said: Our Lord, You have caused us to die twice and You have given us life twice" [Ghafir: 11], that he said: "It is the one in al-Baqarah: 'And you were dead and He gave you life; then He causes you to die, then He gives you life again.'"

Ibn Juraij narrated from Ata', from Ibn Abbas: "And you were dead and He gave you life." Dead in the loins of your fathers, you were nothing until He created you; then He causes you to die the death of truth; then He gives you life when He resurrects you. He said: And it is like His saying: "Our Lord, You have caused us to die twice and You have given us life twice."

Ad-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "Our Lord, You have caused us to die twice and You have given us life twice," that he said: "You were dust before He created you; this is one death. Then He gave you life and created you; this is life. Then He causes you to die, and you return to the graves; this is another death. Then He resurrects you on the Day of Resurrection; this is another life. So these are two deaths and two lives." So it is like His saying: "How can you disbelieve in Allah, when you were dead and He gave you life, then He causes you to die, then He gives you life again."

Similarly, it was narrated from As-Suddi with his chain, from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from a number of the Companions, and from Abu al-Aliyah, al-Hasan al-Basri, Mujahid, Qatadah, Abu Salih, ad-Dahhak and Ata al-Khurasani, something similar.

Ath-Thawri narrated from As-Suddi, from Abu Salih: "How can you disbelieve in Allah, when you were dead and He gave you life, then He causes you to die, then He gives you life, then to Him you will be returned." He said: "He gives you life in the grave, then He causes you to die."

Ibn Jarir narrated from Yunus, from Ibn Wahb, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam: that He created them in the back of Adam, then took the covenant from them, then caused them to die, then created them in the wombs, then caused them to die, then gave them life on the Day of Resurrection. And this is like the saying of Allah the Exalted: "They said: Our Lord, You have caused us to die twice and You have given us life twice."

This view is strange, and so is the one before it. The correct view is what was transmitted earlier from Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas, and that group of the Successors, and it is like His saying: "Say: Allah gives you life, then causes you to die, then will gather you to the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt, but most people do not know" [Al-Jathiyah: 26].

[The state before existence is expressed as death, by the common factor they share, which is lack of perception, as He said regarding the idols: "They are dead, not living" [An-Nahl: 21], and He said: "And a sign for them is the dead earth which We have brought to life and brought forth from it grain, and from it they eat" [Ya-Sin: 33].]

The Almighty, when He mentioned a sign from their own creation and what they witness in themselves, mentioned another proof from what they witness of the creation of the heavens and the earth. He said: ﴿It is He who created for you all that is on the earth, then turned to the heaven﴾. That is, He intended toward the heaven. The *istiwa'* (turning or rising, here) includes the meaning of intention and turning, because it is followed by *ila* (to). ﴿And then made them seven heavens﴾, that is, He created the heaven as seven. "Heaven" here is a generic noun (*ism jins*), which is why He said ﴿them﴾ (*hunna*). ﴿And He is Knowing of all things﴾, that is, His knowledge encompasses all that He created, as He said: ﴿Should not He who created know?﴾ [al-Mulk: 14]. The detail of this verse is in Surah Ha Mim al-Sajdah, where He says: ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days, and you set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds. And He placed in it firm mountains from above it, and blessed it, and measured therein its sustenance in four days, alike for those who ask. Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: Come willingly or unwillingly. They said: We come willingly. So He completed them as seven heavens in two days, and inspired in each heaven its command. And We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps and as a guard. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾ [Fussilat: 9–12].

This indicates that He began by creating the earth first, then created the seven heavens. This is the way of a building: one begins by building its lower parts, then its upper parts afterward. The exegetes have stated this explicitly, as we will mention after this, God willing. As for His saying: ﴿Are you more difficult to create, or the heaven He built? He raised its height and made it proportioned. And He darkened its night and brought forth its morning. And the earth, after that, He spread out. He brought forth from it its water and its pasture, and the mountains He set firm﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 27–32], it has been said that the *thumma* ("then") here merely conjoins one statement to another, not one action to another, as the poet said:

*Say to one who ruled, then his father ruled after him, then his grandfather had ruled before that.*¹

It was also said that the spreading (*dahw*) of the earth occurred after the creation of the heavens. This was narrated by Ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn Abbas.

Al-Suddi, in his tafsir, related from Abu Malik, and from Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas, and from Murrah from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some of the Companions, regarding ﴿It is He who created for you all that is on the earth, then turned to the heaven, and made them seven heavens [and He is Knowing of all things]﴾: Indeed Allah, blessed and exalted, His Throne was upon the water, and He had created nothing except what He had created before the water. When He wished to create the creation, He brought forth smoke from the water, and it rose above the water and towered over it, so He named it "heaven" (*sama'*). Then He dried the water and made it one earth, then split it and made it seven earths in two days, on Sunday and Monday. He created the earth upon a fish (*hut*), and the fish is the Nun which Allah mentioned in the Qur'an: ﴿Nun, and the pen﴾,² and the fish is in the water, and the water is on the back of a rock, and the rock is on the back of an angel, and the angel is on a stone, and the stone is in the wind, and that is the stone which Luqman mentioned, which is neither in the heaven nor in the earth. Then the fish moved and stirred, so the earth shook, and He set the mountains upon it so it became still. The mountains then boast over the earth. That is His saying: ﴿And He cast into the earth firm mountains lest it shake with you﴾ [al-Nahl: 15]. He created the mountains in it, its sustenance and the sustenance of its people, its trees, and what is fitting for it, in two days, on Tuesday and Wednesday. That was when He said: ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days, and you set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds. And He placed in it firm mountains from above it, and blessed it﴾ [Fussilat: 9–10]. He means: He caused its trees to grow. ﴿And measured therein its sustenance﴾, He means: its sustenance for its people. ﴿In four days, alike for those who ask﴾ [Fussilat: 10], He means: for whoever asks, the matter is thus. ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke﴾ [Fussilat: 11]. That smoke was from the breath of the water when it breathed, so He made it one heaven, then split it and made it seven heavens, in two days, on Thursday and Friday. The day of Friday was named *al-Jumu'ah* because creation of the heavens and the earth was gathered (*jumi'a*) in it. ﴿And He inspired in each heaven its command﴾ [Fussilat: 12]. He said: Allah created in each heaven its creation of angels and the creatures in it, of seas, mountains of hail, and what we do not know. Then He adorned the lowest heaven with the stars, making them an adornment and a guard, protected from the devils. When He finished creating what He willed, He turned to the Throne, and that was when He said: ﴿Indeed your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself upon the Throne﴾ [al-A'raf: 54], and He says: ﴿Were not the heavens and the earth a joined mass, then We split them﴾ [al-Anbiya': 30].

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna related to me, Abdullah ibn Salih related to us, Abu Ma'shar related to me from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id, from Abdullah ibn Salam, that he said: Indeed Allah began creation on Sunday. He created the earths on Sunday and Monday, and He created the provisions and the firm mountains on Tuesday and Wednesday, and He created the heavens on Thursday and Friday, and He finished in the last hour of Friday, and He created Adam in it hastily. That is the hour in which the Hour (*al-sa'ah*) will occur.

Mujahid said regarding His saying ﴿It is He who created for you all that is on the earth﴾: Allah created the earth before the heaven, and when He created the earth, smoke erupted from it, and that is when He says: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke﴾.

﴿And made them seven heavens﴾: He said: some of them above others, and seven earths, meaning some of them beneath others.

This verse indicates that the earth was created before the heaven, as He said in the verse of Sajdah: ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days ...﴾ [Fussilat: 9–12]. These two (verses) both indicate that the earth was created before the heaven. I know of no dispute among the scholars about this, except what Ibn Jarir related from Qatadah, that he claimed the heaven was created before the earth. Al-Qurtubi, in his tafsir, hesitated about this in commenting on His saying: ﴿Are you more difficult to create, or the heaven He built? He raised its height and made it proportioned. And He darkened its night and brought forth its morning. And the earth, after that, He spread out. He brought forth from it its water and its pasture﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 27–31]. They said: He mentioned the creation of the heaven before the earth.

In Sahih al-Bukhari³ it is reported that Ibn Abbas was asked about this very matter, and he answered that the earth was created before the heaven, and that the earth was only spread out (*duhiyat*) after the creation of the heaven. Likewise, more than one of the scholars of tafsir, past and present, answered. We have settled this in the tafsir of Surah al-Nazi'at. The summary of that is that the spreading is explained by His saying: ﴿And the earth, after that, He spread out. He brought forth from it its water and its pasture, and the mountains He set firm﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 30–32]. So He explained the spreading as the bringing out of what was latent within it from potential into actuality. When the form of the earthly creatures was completed, and then the heavenly ones, He spread out the earth after that, and it brought forth what was latent in it of waters, and plants grew with their varied kinds, qualities, colours and shapes. Likewise these orbits (*aflak*) moved and revolved with what is in them of fixed and wandering stars. And Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh mentioned, in the tafsir of this verse, the hadith which Muslim and al-Nasa'i in his Tafsir also related, through Ibn Juraij, who said: Isma'il ibn Umayya informed me, from Ayyub ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Rafi', client of Umm Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took my hand and said: "Allah created the clay on Saturday, and created the mountains in it on Sunday, and created the trees in it on Monday, and created the disliked things on Tuesday, and created the light on Wednesday, and scattered the creatures in it on Thursday, and created Adam after the 'Asr prayer on Friday, from the last hour of the hours of Friday, between the 'Asr and the night."⁴

This hadith is among the strange (*gharib*) reports in Sahih Muslim. Ali ibn al-Madini, al-Bukhari, and more than one of the memorizers of hadith have criticised it, and they regarded it as a statement of Ka'b (al-Ahbar), and that Abu Hurayrah only heard it from the words of Ka'b al-Ahbar, and that it was confused for some narrators, who made it marfu' (attributed to the Prophet). Al-Bayhaqi⁵ has clarified this.

Allah, exalted is He, informs of His favour upon the children of Adam by honouring them with mention in the Highest Assembly before their creation. He says: ﴿And when your Lord said to the angels﴾. That is: and mention, O Muhammad, when your Lord said to the angels, and relate this to your people.

Ibn Jarir reported from some of the people of Arabic grammar [and he was Abu 'Ubaydah] [[Addition from ج, ط, أ, و.]] that he claimed that "idh" (when) here is superfluous and that the sense of the sentence is: "And your Lord said." Ibn Jarir rejected this.

Al-Qurtubi said: All the exegetes likewise rejected it, to the point that al-Zajjaj said: "This is audacity (ijtira') on the part of Abu 'Ubaydah."

﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a khalifah (successor)﴾. That is: a people who succeed one another, generation after generation and age after age, as Allah says: ﴿And it is He who made you successors (khala'if) upon the earth﴾ [al-An'am: 165], and He says: ﴿and makes you successors (khulafa') of the earth﴾ [an-Naml: 62], and He says: ﴿And if We willed, We would make among you angels upon the earth succeeding (yakhlufun)﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 60], and He says: ﴿Then there succeeded them a successor (khalf)﴾ [Maryam: 59]. [It is recited in the irregular reading: "Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a khaliqah (creation)," related by al-Zamakhshari and others, and al-Qurtubi transmitted it from Zayd ibn 'Ali] [[Addition from ج, ط, أ, و.]]. The intended meaning of "khalifah" here is not Adam alone, peace be upon him, as some exegetes say, and al-Qurtubi attributed this to Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas and all the people of interpretation. But this requires examination; rather, the disagreement on this is great, as Fakhr al-Din al-Razi related in his tafsir and others. The apparent meaning is that it did not refer to Adam as an individual, for if it were so, the words of the angels would not be fitting: ﴿Will You place therein one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood?﴾ For they only meant that some of this kind would do that, and it seems they knew this through special knowledge, or through what they understood of human nature, since He had informed them that He would create this kind from clay, from black mud moulded [or they understood from "khalifah" that it is one who judges between people, settles the wrongs among them, and repels from them the prohibited things and sins, as al-Qurtubi said] [[Addition from ج, ط, ب, أ, و.]], or they compared them to those who came before, as we will mention the exegetes' statements on this.

The words of the angels were not in the manner of objecting to Allah, nor out of envy of the children of Adam, as some exegetes may imagine [Allah has described them as those who do not precede Him in speech, meaning they do not ask Him for anything He has not permitted them, and here, when He informed them that He would create a creation upon the earth, Qatadah said: "It had been made known to them beforehand that they (the descendants) would cause corruption therein, so they said: ﴿Will You place therein...﴾ the verse"] [[Addition from ج, ط, ب, أ, و.]]. Rather, it was a question of seeking information and inquiring about the wisdom in this, saying: "O our Lord, what is the wisdom in creating these, when among them are some who cause corruption on the earth and shed blood? If the purpose is Your worship, then we glorify You with Your praise and sanctify You, that is, we pray to You, as will come, so nothing of that proceeds from us. Why not limit it to us?" Allah, exalted, answered them concerning this question: ﴿Indeed, I know that which you do not know﴾. That is: Indeed, I know, of the benefit that outweighs the corruptions you have mentioned in creating this kind, what you do not know. For I will place among them prophets, send among them messengers, and there will exist among them the truthful (siddiqun), the martyrs, the righteous, the worshippers, the ascetics, the friends (of Allah), the pious, those brought near, the scholars who act, the humble, and those who love Him, blessed and exalted is He, following His messengers, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them.

It is established in the Sahih [Sahih Muslim, no. 632, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him] that the angels, when they ascend to the Lord, exalted is He, with the deeds of His servants, He asks them, and He is most knowing: "How did you leave My servants?" They say: "We came to them while they were praying, and we left them while they were praying." That is because they succeed one another among us, and they gather at the Fajr prayer and the 'Asr prayer, so those remain and those ascend with the deeds, as he, peace be upon him, said: "The deed of the night is raised to Him before the day, and the deed of the day before the night." So their saying: "We came to them while they were praying and we left them while they were praying" is part of the explanation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, I know that which you do not know﴾. It was also said: the meaning of His answer to them, ﴿Indeed, I know that which you do not know﴾, is that I have a detailed wisdom in creating these, while the situation is as you mentioned, which you do not know. It was also said: it was an answer to their saying: ﴿And we glorify You with Your praise and sanctify You﴾, so He said: ﴿Indeed, I know that which you do not know﴾, that is, of the existence of Iblis among you, and he is not as you described yourselves. It was also said: rather, their saying: ﴿Will You place therein one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we glorify You with Your praise and sanctify You?﴾ included a request from them that they should inhabit the earth instead of the children of Adam, so Allah, exalted is He, said to them: ﴿Indeed, I know that which you do not know﴾, namely that your remaining in the heaven is more beneficial for you and more suitable for you. Fakhr al-Din mentioned it along with other answers, and Allah knows best.

Mention of the statements of the exegetes, expanding on what we have mentioned:

Ibn Jarir said: al-Qasim ibn al-Hasan related to me, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: al-Hajjaj related to me, from Jarir ibn Hazim and Mubarak, from al-Hasan and Abu Bakr, from al-Hasan and Qatadah, who said: Allah said to the angels: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successor﴾. He said to them: "Indeed, I am going to do." This meaning indicates that He informed them of that.

Al-Suddi said: He consulted the angels concerning the creation of Adam. Ibn Abi Hatim related it, saying: Something similar was related from Qatadah. If this expression does not return to the meaning of informing, then it is loose, and the expression of al-Hasan and Qatadah in Ibn Jarir's narration is better, and Allah knows best.

﴿upon the earth﴾: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Abu Salamah related to us, Hammad related to us, 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib related to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The earth was spread out from Makkah, and the first to circumambulate the House were the angels. Then Allah said: 'Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successor,' meaning Makkah." [Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/108)].

This is a mursal report, and its chain has weakness, and in it there is an interpolation (mudraj), namely that by "the earth" is meant Makkah. Allah knows best. The apparent meaning is that "the earth" is more general than that.

﴿successor﴾: al-Suddi said in his tafsir, from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some of the Companions, that Allah, exalted is He, said to the angels: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successor﴾.

They said: "Our Lord, and what will that successor be?" He said: "He will have offspring who will cause corruption on the earth, envy one another, and some of them will kill others."

Ibn Jarir said: So the interpretation of the verse according to this is: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successor﴾ from Me, who will succeed Me in judging among My creation, and that successor is Adam and whoever stands in his place in obedience to Allah and in judging justly among His creation. As for causing corruption and shedding blood without right, that is from others than His successors.

Ibn Jarir said: And the interpretation of the verse on this basis [was] [[Addition from ج.]] that the succession Allah mentioned is only the succession of one generation after another.

He said: And "khalifah" (successor) is derived from your saying: "So-and-so succeeded so-and-so in this matter" when he stood in his place in it after him, as Allah says: ﴿Then We made you successors upon the earth after them, to see how you would act﴾ [Yunus: 14]. From this, the supreme ruler is called "khalifah," because he succeeds the one who was before him, standing in the affair in his place, so he became a successor to him.

He said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq used to say concerning Allah's saying: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successor﴾: he would say: a resident and one who builds it, who dwells in it and populates it as successors, not from among you.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb related to us, 'Uthman ibn Sa'id related to us, Bishr ibn 'Umarah related to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The first to inhabit the earth were the jinn, and they caused corruption in it and shed blood in it, and some of them killed others. He said: So Allah sent Iblis to them, and Iblis and those with him killed them, until they pursued them to the islands of the seas and the edges of the mountains. Then He created Adam and settled him in it, and therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successor﴾ [Tafsir al-Tabari (1/450)].

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Ibn Sabit: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successor﴾ ﴿They said: Will You place therein one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood?﴾ He said: They meant by it the children of Adam.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: Allah said to the angels: "Indeed, I want to create a creation upon the earth, and place therein a successor," and there is no creation of Allah, mighty and majestic is He, except the angels, and there was no creature upon the earth. They said: ﴿Will You place therein one who causes corruption therein [and sheds blood]?!﴾ [[Addition from ج.]]

It has already passed what al-Suddi related from Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud and others from the Companions: that Allah informed the angels of what the descendants of Adam would do, so the angels said that. And it has already passed just now [[in ج, ط: "also"]] what al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas: that the jinn caused corruption on the earth before the children of Adam, so the angels said that, and they compared these to those.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi related to us, Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, al-A'mash related to us, from Bukayr [[In أ: "Bakr."]] ibn al-Akhnas, from Mujahid, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The jinn, the sons of the jann, were on the earth two thousand years before Adam was created, and they caused corruption on the earth and shed blood. So Allah sent a host of angels who struck them, until they pursued them to the islands of the seas. Then Allah said to the angels: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successor﴾. They said: "Will You place therein one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood?" He said: ﴿Indeed, I know that which you do not know﴾ [Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/109)].

Abu Ja'far al-Razi said, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successor﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And I know what you reveal and what you have been concealing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 33]: He said: Allah created the angels on Wednesday, and created the jinn on Thursday, and created Adam on Friday. So a people among the jinn disbelieved, and the angels would descend to them upon the earth and fight them, so there was bloodshed between them, and there was corruption upon the earth. Therefore they said: ﴿Will You place therein one who causes corruption therein﴾, as the jinn had caused corruption, ﴿and sheds blood﴾, as they had shed it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us: Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us: Mubarak ibn Fadalah narrated to us: al-Hasan narrated to us, who said: Allah said to the angels: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successive authority﴾. He said to them: "Indeed, I am going to do so." So they believed in their Lord [[In manuscripts A and W: "Did they then trust their own opinion?"]]. He taught them knowledge and withheld from them knowledge that He knew and they did not know. So they spoke with the knowledge He had taught them: ﴿Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood?﴾ He said: ﴿Indeed, I know that which you do not know﴾.

Al-Hasan said: Indeed, the jinn had been on the earth causing corruption and shedding blood, but Allah placed in their hearts that this would happen again, so they spoke the words He had taught them.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein﴾: Allah [[added from manuscripts J, T, B, A]] had informed them that if there were creatures on the earth, they would cause corruption therein and shed blood, and that is when they said: ﴿Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein﴾ [[Tafsir ʿAbd al-Razzaq (1/65).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: My father narrated to us: Hisham al-Razi narrated to us: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Maʿruf, meaning Ibn Kharrabudh al-Makki, from one who heard Abu Jaʿfar Muhammad ibn ʿAli say: "The Sijill is an angel, and Harut and Marut were among his helpers. He had three glances each day that he looked upon in Umm al-Kitab (the Mother of the Book). He glanced once at a time when he was not supposed to, and in that glance he saw the creation of Adam and what would happen in it. He confided that to Harut and Marut, who were among his helpers. When He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successive authority﴾, they said: ﴿Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood?﴾ They said this out of arrogance toward the angels."

This is a strange report (athar). Even if it is authentically traced to Abu Jaʿfar Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn al-Husayn al-Baqir, he took it from the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab), and it contains an objectionable element that requires its rejection. Allah knows best. Its implication is that only two of them said this, which contradicts the context.

Even stranger than this is what Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated, where he said: My father narrated to us: Hisham ibn Abi ʿAbd Allah narrated to us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us, who said: I heard my father say: "The angels who said: ﴿Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we glorify You with Your praise and sanctify You?﴾ were ten thousand, so a fire came forth from Allah and burned them."

This too is an objectionable Israʾiliyyat (narration from Jewish or Christian sources), like the one before it. Allah knows best.

Ibn Jurayj said: They only spoke about what Allah had informed them would come from the creation of Adam, so they said: ﴿Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood?﴾

Ibn Jarir said: Some of them said: The angels only said what they said: ﴿Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood?﴾ because Allah permitted them to ask about it after He had informed them that this would come from the children of Adam. So the angels asked Him, saying, in wonder: "How can they disobey You, my Lord, when You are their Creator?" Their Lord replied: ﴿Indeed, I know that which you do not know﴾, meaning: that this will come from them, even if you do not know it, and that among them will be some whom you see as obedient to Me.

He said: Some of them said: That was from the angels as a request for guidance about what they did not know. It was as if they said: "My Lord, inform us." The angels' question was an inquiry, not a rejection. Ibn Jarir preferred this view.

Sa'id narrated from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿And when your Lord said to the angels: Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successive authority﴾ that He consulted the angels about the creation of Adam, so they said: ﴿Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood?﴾ The angels had known from Allah's knowledge that nothing is more hateful to Allah than shedding blood and corruption on the earth. ﴿While we glorify You with Your praise and sanctify You﴾. He said: ﴿Indeed, I know that which you do not know﴾. So it was in Allah's knowledge that from that creation would come prophets, messengers, righteous people, and inhabitants of Paradise. He said: It was also reported to us from Ibn ʿAbbas that he used to say: When Allah began to create Adam, the angels said: "Allah creates no creature more honored by Him than us, and none more knowledgeable than us." So they were tested with the creation of Adam. Every creature is tested, just as the heavens and the earth were tested with obedience. He said: ﴿Come willingly or unwillingly.﴾ They said: ﴿We come willingly﴾ [Fussilat: 11].

* *

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿while we glorify You with Your praise and sanctify You﴾: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated from Maʿmar, from Qatadah: "Tasbih (glorification) is tasbih, and taqdis (sanctification) is prayer" [[Tafsir ʿAbd al-Razzaq (1/65).]].

Al-Suddi said, narrating from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from Ibn ʿAbbas, and from Murrah, from Ibn Masʿud, and from a group of the Companions: ﴿while we glorify You with Your praise and sanctify You﴾ means: they say, "We pray to You."

Mujahid said: ﴿while we glorify You with Your praise and sanctify You﴾: "We exalt You and magnify You."

Al-Dahhak said: Taqdis means purification.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: ﴿while we glorify You with Your praise and sanctify You﴾: "We do not disobey and do not do anything You dislike."

Ibn Jarir said: Taqdis means magnifying and purifying. From it comes their saying "Subbuh, Quddus" (Most Glorified, Most Holy). By their saying "Subbuh" they mean exalting Him above imperfection, and by "Quddus" they mean purity and magnification of Him. For this reason the land is called "a sacred land" (ardun muqaddasah), meaning purified. So the meaning of the angels' words, ﴿while we glorify You with Your praise﴾, is: "We declare You free of and clear You of what the people of polytheism attribute to You," and ﴿and sanctify You﴾ means: "We ascribe to You what belongs to Your attributes, namely purity from defects and from what the people of disbelief ascribe to You."

[In Sahih Muslim, from Abu Dhar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked: "Which speech is best?" He said: "What Allah chose for His angels: Subhan Allah wa bihamdih (Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him)" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (2731).]]. Al-Bayhaqi narrated from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Qurt that on the night of the Isra' (Night Journey), the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard glorification in the high heavens: "Subhan al-ʿAli al-A'la, subhanahu wa taʿala (Glory be to the Most High, the Most Exalted, glorified and exalted is He)" [[Also narrated by Abu Nuʿaym in al-Hilyah (2/7), through Maskin ibn Maymun from ʿUrwah ibn Ruwaym, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Qurt, may Allah be pleased with him, as a marfuʿ (traced to the Prophet) report. It will come from al-Tabarani's narration at the commentary on verse 44 of Surah al-Isra'.]]].

﴿He said: Indeed, I know that which you do not know﴾. Qatadah said: So it was in Allah's knowledge that in that creation would come prophets, messengers, righteous people, and inhabitants of Paradise. Views will come from Ibn Masʿud, Ibn ʿAbbas, and many other Companions and Successors (Tabiʿun) about the wisdom in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He said: Indeed, I know that which you do not know﴾.

Al-Qurtubi and others have used this verse to establish that it is obligatory to appoint a caliph (khalifah) to judge between people in matters they dispute, to end their conflicts, to defend their oppressed against their oppressors, to establish the hudud (prescribed punishments), to deter people from indecency, and for other important matters that cannot be carried out except through an imam. Whatever is necessary and cannot be fulfilled without something else is itself obligatory.

The imamah (leadership of the Muslim community) is attained by explicit designation (nass), as a group of Ahl al-Sunnah say regarding Abu Bakr; or by indication (iymaʾ) toward him, as others among them say; or by the current caliph appointing another successor after him, as al-Siddiq (Abu Bakr) did with ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab; or by leaving the matter to a council (shura) of righteous men, as ʿUmar did; or by the agreement of the people who loose and bind (ahl al-hall wa al-ʿaqd) on giving him allegiance; or by the allegiance of one of them to him. The obligation to adhere to these methods is the view of the majority. Imam al-Haramayn (al-Juwayni) reported a consensus (ijmaʿ) on this. Allah knows best. Or it is attained by one man compelling people to obey him, and obedience is then obligatory so that it does not lead to division and discord. Al-Shafiʿi explicitly stated this.

Is it required to have witnesses for the contract of the imamah? There is disagreement. Some say it is not required. It was also said: Yes, and two witnesses are sufficient. Al-Jubba'i said: Four are required, plus the one who makes the contract and the one for whom it is made, just as ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, left the matter to a council of six. The contract was made by one who contracted it, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf, and it was made for one for whom it was made, ʿUthman. He derived the requirement of four witnesses from the remaining four. There is room for consideration in this. Allah knows best.

It is required that the caliph be male, free, adult, sane, Muslim, just, qualified to exercise independent judgment (mujtahid), perceptive, physically sound, knowledgeable about warfare and strategy, and, according to the correct view, from the Quraysh. Being from the Banu Hashim is not required, nor is being free from error, contrary to the extremist Rafidah (Rawafid). If the imam commits sin (fisq), is he deposed or not? There is disagreement. The correct view is that he is not deposed, based on the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "Unless you see clear disbelief about which you have proof from Allah" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (7055), from the hadith of ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. Can he depose himself? There is disagreement. al-Hasan ibn ʿAli deposed himself and handed over the affair to Muʿawiyah, but that was for a valid excuse, and he was praised for it.

As for appointing two imams or more in the earth, it is not permissible, based on the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "Whoever comes to you while your affair is united, intending to divide you, kill him, whoever he may be" [[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (1852), from the hadith of ʿArfajah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. This is the view of the majority, and many have reported a consensus on it, including Imam al-Haramayn. The Karramiyyah said: It is permissible to appoint two imams or more, as ʿAli and Muʿawiyah were two imams whose obedience was obligatory. They said: If it is permissible to send two or more prophets at the same time, it is permissible for imamate too, since prophethood is of higher rank, without disagreement. Imam al-Haramayn reported from Ustadh Abu Ishaq that he permitted appointing two or more imams if the regions were far apart and the territories were wide between them, and Imam al-Haramayn was hesitant about this. I say: This resembles the situation of the ʿAbbasid caliphs in Iraq, the Fatimids in Egypt, and the Umayyads in the Maghrib.

This is a station in which Allah the Exalted mentions the nobility of Adam over the angels, by the knowledge of the names of everything that He singled him out with, to the exclusion of them. This came after their prostration to him. He placed this section before that one because of the connection between this station and their lack of knowledge of the wisdom behind creating the khalifah (vicegerent), when they asked about that. So Allah the Exalted informed them that He knows what they do not know. For this reason, He mentioned this station right after that, to make clear to them the nobility of Adam through the knowledge he was given over them. So He said, the Exalted: ﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them﴾.

Al-Suddi said, from someone who narrated to him, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them﴾. He said: He presented to him the names of his offspring, person by person, and of the animals. It was said: "This is the donkey, this is the camel, this is the horse."

Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them﴾. He said: They are these names by which people recognize one another: human, animal, sky, earth, plain, sea, camel, donkey, and similar things, among the nations and others.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated, through the hadith of 'Asim ibn Kulayb, from Sa'id ibn Ma'bad, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them﴾. He said: He taught him the name of the bowl and the pot. He said: Yes, even the faswah and the fusayyah.

Mujahid said: ﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them﴾. He said: He taught him the name of every animal, every bird, and everything.

Likewise it is narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, and others among the early generations, that He taught him the names of everything. Al-Rabi' said in one narration from him: the names of the angels. Humayd al-Shami said: the names of the stars. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: He taught him the names of all his descendants.

Ibn Jarir chose that He taught him the names of the angels and the names of the offspring, because He said: ﴿Then He presented them﴾, and this is an expression for those who have intellect. But this basis for preference is not conclusive, for it does not negate that others may be included with them, and the whole may be expressed with the form used for those who have intellect, by way of prevalence (taghlib), as He said: ﴿And Allah created every moving creature from water. Of them are those that move on their bellies, of them are those that walk on two legs, and of them are those that walk on four. Allah creates what He wills; indeed, Allah is over all things competent﴾ [al-Nur: 45].

[Abdullah ibn Mas'ud recited: "Then He presented them (feminine plural: hunna)," and Ubayy ibn Ka'b recited: "Then He presented them (feminine singular: ha)," referring to the heavens.]

The correct view is that He taught him the names of all things: their essences and their actions, as Ibn 'Abbas said, "even the faswah and the fusayyah." He means the names of essences and actions, the large and the small. For this reason al-Bukhari said in his commentary on this verse in the Book of Tafsir of his Sahih: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Muslim narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ. And Khalifah said to me: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The believers will gather on the Day of Resurrection and say: 'If only we could seek intercession with our Lord!' So they will come to Adam and say: 'You are the father of mankind. Allah created you with His hand, made His angels prostrate to you, and taught you the names of everything. So intercede for us with your Lord, that He may relieve us from this place.' He will say: 'I am not fit for that,' and he will mention his sin and feel shy. Go to Nuh, for he was the first messenger Allah sent to the people of the earth.' They will come to Nuh, and he will say: 'I am not fit for that,' and he will mention his asking his Lord about what he had no knowledge of, and feel shy. He will say: 'Go to the Khalil of the Most Merciful.' They will come to him, and he will say: 'I am not fit for that. Go to Musa, a servant whom Allah spoke to and to whom He gave the Torah.' They will come to him, and he will say: 'I am not fit for that,' and he will mention killing a soul without a soul, and feel shy before his Lord. He will say: 'Go to 'Isa, the servant of Allah, His messenger, His word and His spirit.' They will come to him, and he will say: 'I am not fit for that. Go to Muhammad, a servant whose past and future sins Allah has forgiven.' They will come to me, and I will go and ask permission to enter upon my Lord. It will be granted to me, and when I see my Lord I will fall down in prostration. He will leave me as long as Allah wills, then it will be said: 'Raise your head, ask and you will be given, speak and you will be heard, intercede and your intercession will be accepted.' I will raise my head and praise Him with a praise He will teach me. Then I will intercede, and He will set a limit for me, and I will admit them into Paradise. Then I will return to Him, and when I see my Lord, I will do the same. Then I will intercede, and He will set a limit for me, and I will admit them into Paradise. Then I will return a fourth time and say: None remains in the Fire except those whom the Qur'an has restrained and for whom eternal abiding is due." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4476.]

Thus al-Bukhari narrated this hadith here. It was also narrated by Muslim and al-Nasa'i through the hadith of Hisham, who is Ibn Abi 'Abd Allah al-Dastuwa'i, from Qatadah, with the same wording. Muslim, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah also narrated it through the hadith of Sa'id, who is Ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah. The purpose of citing it here, and the point intended by it, is the words of the Prophet ﷺ: "They will come to Adam and say: 'You are the father of mankind. Allah created you with His hand, made His angels prostrate to you, and taught you the names of everything.'" This indicates that He taught him the names of all created things. For this reason He said: ﴿Then He presented them to the angels﴾, meaning: the named things, as 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: "Then He presented those names to the angels, ﴿and said: Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful﴾."

Al-Suddi said in his tafsir, from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some of the Companions: ﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them﴾, then He presented the creation to the angels.

Ibn Jurayj said, from Mujahid: ﴿Then He presented them﴾: He presented the owners of the names to the angels.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, al-Hajjaj narrated to me, from Jarir ibn Hazim and Mubarak ibn Fadalah, from al-Hasan, and Abu Bakr, from al-Hasan and Qatadah, who both said: He taught him the name of everything, and began naming everything by its name, and they were presented to him nation by nation.

By the same chain, from al-Hasan and Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿if you are truthful﴾: "I did not create any creature except that you would have known more about it than it. So inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful."

Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿if you are truthful﴾, meaning: "if you know," that "I have not placed in the earth a khalifah."

Al-Suddi said, from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some of the Companions: "if you are truthful" that the children of Adam would corrupt in the earth and shed blood.

Ibn Jarir said: The most preferable of the statements on this is the interpretation of Ibn 'Abbas and of those who speak according to his view. The meaning is: He said, "Inform Me of the names of those I have presented to you, O angels, who said: 'Will You place in it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, from other than us or from us, while we glorify You with Your praise and sanctify You?' If you are truthful in your saying: 'If I make a khalifah in the earth from other than you, his descendants will disobey Me, corrupt, and shed blood; and if I make you in it, you will obey Me and follow My command by exalting and sanctifying Me.' If you do not know the names of those I have presented to you while you are witnessing them, then you are more deserving of not knowing the matters that are not yet existent and have not come into being."

﴿They said: Glory be to You, we have no knowledge except what You have taught us; indeed, You are the All-Knowing, the All-Wise﴾. This is a glorification and declaration of Allah's transcendence by the angels, that anyone should encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills, and that they should know anything except what Allah the Exalted has taught them. For this reason they said: ﴿Glory be to You, we have no knowledge except what You have taught us; indeed, You are the All-Knowing, the All-Wise﴾, meaning: the All-Knowing of every thing, the All-Wise in Your creating and Your command, and in Your teaching whom You will and Your withholding from whom You will. To You belongs the wisdom in that, and perfect justice.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from Hajjaj, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Subhan Allah" (Glory be to Allah): he said: Allah's declaring Himself free from evil. Then 'Umar said to 'Ali and his companions who were with him: "La ilaha illa Allah (there is no god but Allah), we know it. But what is Subhan Allah?" 'Ali said to him: "A word which Allah loved for Himself, was pleased with, and loved to be said." [Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/117).]

He said: And my father narrated to us, Ibn Nufayl narrated to us, al-Nadr ibn 'Arabi narrated to us, who said: A man asked Maymun ibn Mihran about "Subhan Allah," and he said: "It is a name by which Allah is exalted, and by which He is declared free from evil."

* *

His Exalted words: ﴿He said: O Adam, inform them of their names. And when he informed them of their names, He said: Did I not tell you that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and I know what you reveal and what you have been concealing?﴾ Zayd ibn Aslam said: "You are Jibril, you are Mika'il, you are Israfil," until he counted all the names, up to the crow.

Mujahid said regarding Allah's words: ﴿O Adam, inform them of their names﴾: "The name of the dove, the crow, and the name of everything."

Similar to that was narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, and Qatadah.

When the excellence of Adam, upon him be peace, over the angels, upon them be peace, became evident through his recounting what Allah the Exalted had taught him of the names of things, Allah the Exalted said to the angels: ﴿Did I not tell you that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and I know what you reveal and what you have been concealing?﴾ That is: Did I not forewarn you that I know the unseen, the apparent and the hidden? As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if you speak aloud, indeed He knows the secret and what is more hidden﴾. And as the Exalted said, relating about the hoopoe that it said to Sulayman: ﴿Why do they not prostrate to Allah, who brings out what is hidden in the heavens and the earth and knows what you conceal and what you declare? Allah – there is no deity except Him, Lord of the Great Throne﴾.

It has been said regarding His words: ﴿and I know what you reveal and what you have been concealing﴾ other than what we have mentioned. Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and I know what you reveal and what you have been concealing﴾, he said: "He says: I know the secret as I know the open, meaning: what Iblis concealed in himself of arrogance and self-deception."

Al-Suddi said, from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some of the Companions: "Their saying: ﴿Will You place in it one who causes corruption therein?﴾ – this is what they revealed. ﴿And what you have been concealing﴾ means: what Iblis secretly held in himself of arrogance."

Likewise Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, and al-Thawri said. Ibn Jarir chose this view.

Abu al-'Aliyah, Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: it is their saying, "Our Lord will not create any creation except that we will be more knowledgeable than it and more noble."

Abu Ja'far al-Razi related from Rabi' ibn Anas regarding ﴿And I know what you reveal and what you conceal﴾: what they revealed was their saying, ﴿Will You place therein one who causes corruption therein?﴾, and what they concealed among themselves was their saying: "Our Lord will never create any creation except that we will be more knowledgeable than it and more noble." Thus they came to know that Allah had preferred Adam over them in knowledge and nobility.

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, concerning the story of the angels and Adam: Allah said to the angels, "Since you did not know these names, you have no knowledge. I only wished to make them [i.e., Adam and his descendants] so that they would cause corruption therein. This I know, and therefore I concealed from you that I will place therein one who disobeys Me and one who obeys Me." He said: And there had preceded from Allah, ﴿Surely I will fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together.﴾ He said: The angels did not know that and were not aware of it. He said: When they saw what Allah had given Adam of knowledge, they acknowledged his superiority.

Ibn Jarir said: The most preferable of the opinions on this matter is the statement of Ibn 'Abbas, namely that the meaning of His saying, ﴿And I know what you reveal﴾, is: And I know—along with My knowledge of the unseen of the heavens and the earth—what you manifest with your tongues and what you used to hide within yourselves; nothing is hidden from Me, and My knowledge of your inner secrets and your outward matters is the same.

What they manifested with their tongues was their saying, "Will You place therein one who causes corruption therein?" And what they used to conceal was what Iblis had hidden within himself of opposition to Allah in His commands and arrogance against obeying Him.

He said: This is correct, just as the Arabs say, "The army was killed and defeated," when in fact only one or some of them were killed or defeated; so the report about the defeated and slain part is expressed as a report about all of them. Likewise Allah says, ﴿Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the chambers﴾ [al-Hujurat: 4], and it is mentioned that the one who called out was only one man from the Banu Tamim. He said: And likewise is His saying, ﴿And I know what you reveal and what you conceal﴾.

This is a station in which Allah the Exalted mentions the nobility of Adam over the angels, by the knowledge of the names of everything that He singled him out with, to the exclusion of them. This came after their prostration to him. He placed this section before that one because of the connection between this station and their lack of knowledge of the wisdom behind creating the khalifah (vicegerent), when they asked about that. So Allah the Exalted informed them that He knows what they do not know. For this reason, He mentioned this station right after that, to make clear to them the nobility of Adam through the knowledge he was given over them. So He said, the Exalted: ﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them﴾.

Al-Suddi said, from someone who narrated to him, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them﴾. He said: He presented to him the names of his offspring, person by person, and of the animals. It was said: "This is the donkey, this is the camel, this is the horse."

Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them﴾. He said: They are these names by which people recognize one another: human, animal, sky, earth, plain, sea, camel, donkey, and similar things, among the nations and others.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated, through the hadith of 'Asim ibn Kulayb, from Sa'id ibn Ma'bad, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them﴾. He said: He taught him the name of the bowl and the pot. He said: Yes, even the faswah and the fusayyah.

Mujahid said: ﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them﴾. He said: He taught him the name of every animal, every bird, and everything.

[Abdullah ibn Mas'ud recited: "Then He presented them (feminine plural: hunna)," and Ubayy ibn Ka'b recited: "Then He presented them (feminine singular: ha)," referring to the heavens.]
