He said: So Allah sent Iblis against them with an army of angels, and they were this tribe called the Jinn. Iblis and those with him killed them until he drove them to the islands of the seas and the edges of the mountains. When Iblis had done this, he became vain and said: "I have done something no one else has done." He said: Allah became aware of this from his heart, but did not inform the angels who were with him. So Allah said to the angels who were with him: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place a successor on earth﴾. The angels replied to Him, saying: ﴿Will You place therein one who will cause corruption therein and shed blood?﴾ as the Jinn did, corrupting and shedding blood; and You only sent us against them for that? He said: ﴿Indeed, I know that which you do not know﴾, meaning: I have perceived from the heart of Iblis what you have not perceived of his arrogance and vanity. [[In J: "from" (instead of "on").]] He said: Then He commanded that the dust of Adam be raised, and Allah created Adam from *lazib* clay, and *al-lazib* is the sticky, hard [[In B, A, and W: "good" (al-tayyib).]] clay, from black, putrid, moulded mud (*hama masnun*). It was only moulded mud after it had been dust. So He created Adam with His Hand. He said: He remained for forty nights as a body lying prostrate. Iblis would come to him and strike him with his foot, and it would resound, that is, it would make a sound. He said: This is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿from clay like pottery﴾. [Ar-Rahman: 14] It means: like something hollow that is not solid. He said: Then it would enter through his mouth and exit from his anus, and enter from his anus and exit from his mouth. Then Iblis would say: "You are nothing... for the clay; and you were created for nothing. If I am given power over you, I will destroy you, and if you are given power over me, I will disobey you." He said: When Allah breathed into him of His spirit, the breath reached him from the direction of his head, and nothing of it passed into his body without becoming flesh and blood. When the breath reached his navel, he looked at his body and was pleased with what he saw of his body. He tried to stand up but could not. This is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And man was ever hasty﴾. He said: Impatient, who has no patience in ease or hardship. He said: When the breath was complete in his body, he sneezed and said, by inspiration from Allah: "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds." Then Allah [[Allah added in A and W.]] said to him: "May your Lord have mercy upon you, O Adam." [[In J: "May Allah have mercy upon you, O Adam, your Lord."]] He said: Then Allah, the Exalted, said to the angels who were with Iblis specifically, not the angels who were in the heavens: "Prostrate to Adam." They all prostrated together, except Iblis, who refused and was arrogant, because of the pride and vanity he had harboured in himself. He said: "I will not prostrate to him; I am better than him, older than him, and stronger in creation. You created me from fire and created him from clay." He means: fire is stronger than clay. He said: When Iblis refused to prostrate, Allah made him despair (*ablasahu*), that is, He made him lose hope of all good, and made him a cursed devil (*shaytan rajim*) as a punishment for his disobedience. Then He taught Adam all the names, and these are the names by which people know one another: human, animal, earth, plain, sea, mountain, donkey, and similar things, among the nations and others. Then He presented these names to those angels, meaning the angels who were with Iblis, who were created from the fire of the scorching wind, and said to them: ﴿Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful﴾, meaning: tell Me the names of these, ﴿if you are truthful﴾, if you know why I am placing a successor on earth. He said: When the angels knew of Allah's displeasure with them for what they had said about the unseen knowledge that none knows but Him, which they did not possess, they said: "Glory be to You," exalting Allah above anyone knowing the unseen besides Him. "We repent to You," ﴿We have no knowledge except what You have taught us﴾, disavowing knowledge of the unseen, except what You have taught us, just as You taught Adam. He said: ﴿O Adam, inform them of their names﴾, meaning: tell them their names. ﴿So when he had informed them of their names﴾ [He said: he informed them] ﴿of their names, He said: Did I not tell you﴾, O angels in particular, ﴿that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾, which no one else knows, ﴿and I know what you disclose and what you conceal﴾, meaning: what you make apparent, ﴿and what you have been concealing﴾, meaning: I know the secret as I know the open, that is, what Iblis concealed in himself of pride and vanity.[[Tafsir al-Tabari (1/455).]]

This is a strange chain (*siyaq gharib*), and it contains matters open to scrutiny, the discussion of which would be lengthy. This chain to Ibn 'Abbas is one through which a well-known tafsir is transmitted.

As-Suddi said in his tafsir, from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some companions of the Prophet ﷺ: When Allah finished creating what He loved, He established Himself upon the Throne. He made Iblis ruler over the lowest heaven. He was from a tribe of angels called the Jinn, and they were named Jinn only because they were guardians of the Garden. Iblis, with his kingship, was a guardian. Pride entered his chest, and he said: "Allah has given me this only because of an excellence over the angels." When that pride entered his soul, Allah became aware of it. So Allah said to the angels: ﴿Indeed, I am placing a successor on earth﴾. They said: "Our Lord, what will that successor be?" He said: "He will have descendants who will cause corruption on earth, envy one another, and some of them will kill others." They said: "Our Lord, ﴿Will You place therein one who will cause corruption therein and shed blood, while we exalt You with Your praise and sanctify You?﴾ He said: ﴿Indeed, I know that which you do not know﴾, meaning: regarding the affair of Iblis. Then Allah sent Jibril to the earth to bring some of its clay. The earth said: "I seek refuge in Allah from you, that you should take from me or disfigure me." So he returned without taking anything and said: "My Lord, it sought refuge in You, so You granted it refuge." Then He sent Mika'il, and it sought refuge from him, so He granted it refuge. He returned and said the same as Jibril had said. Then He sent the Angel of Death, and it sought refuge from him. He said: "I seek refuge in Allah that I should return without carrying out His command." So he took from the surface of the earth, and mixed it, and did not take from one place. He took red, white, and black soil, and for this reason the children of Adam came out varied. Then he raised it and wet the dust until it became sticky clay (*tin lazib*). *Al-lazib* is that which sticks part to part. Then He said to the angels: ﴿Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay. So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down before him in prostration﴾. [Sad: 71, 72] So Allah created him with His Hand, lest Iblis should be arrogant toward him, so that He might say to him: "You are too proud before what I have made with My Hand, while I am not proud before him." He created him as a human being, and he was a body of clay for forty years, measured by the length of a Friday. The angels passed by him and were terrified when they saw him, and Iblis was the most terrified of him. He would pass by him and strike him, and the body would resound as pottery resounds, making a sound. This is when He says: ﴿from clay like pottery﴾. [Ar-Rahman: 14] And he would say: "He was created for something." He entered through his mouth and exited from his anus, and said to the angels: "Do not be afraid of this, for your Lord is Eternal (*samad*), and this is hollow. If I am given power over him, I will destroy him." When the time came that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wished to breathe the spirit into him, He said to the angels: "When I breathe into him of My spirit, prostrate to him." When He breathed the spirit into him, and the spirit entered his head, he sneezed. The angels said: "Say: All praise is due to Allah." He said: "All praise is due to Allah." Allah said to him: "May your Lord have mercy upon you." When the spirit entered his eyes, he looked at the fruits of the Garden. When the spirit entered his body, he desired food, and before the spirit reached his feet, he leapt hastily toward the fruits of the Garden. This is when Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Man was created of haste﴾. [Al-Anbiya: 37] ﴿So the angels prostrated, all of them entirely, except Iblis; he refused to be among those who prostrated﴾. [Al-Hijr: 30, 31] He refused, was arrogant, and was among the disbelievers. Allah said to him: "What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you, regarding what I created with My Hand?" He said: "I am better than him; I would not prostrate to one whom You created from clay." Allah said to him: ﴿Get out of it, for it is not for you to be arrogant therein; so get out, for you are among the humiliated﴾. [Al-A'raf: 13] *As-Saghar* is humiliation. He said: ﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them﴾. Then He presented the creation to the angels, ﴿and said: Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful﴾, that the children of Adam would cause corruption on earth and shed blood. They said: ﴿Glory be to You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, You are the Knowing, the Wise﴾. Allah said: ﴿O Adam, inform them of their names.﴾ ﴿So when he had informed them of their names, He said: Did I not tell you that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and I know what you disclose and what you conceal?﴾ He said: Their saying: ﴿Will You place therein one who will cause corruption therein?﴾ So this is what they disclosed. "And I know what you conceal" means what Iblis secretly held in himself of pride.

This chain to these companions is well known in the tafsir of as-Suddi, and it contains many Israiliyyat (narratives derived from Jewish and Christian sources). Perhaps some of them are interpolated (*mudraj*) and not the words of the companions, or they took them from some earlier books. And Allah knows best. Al-Hakim narrates in his Mustadrak, with this very same chain, various matters, and he says: [It is] [[Added in J, T, B, A, and W.]] according to the condition of al-Bukhari.

The purpose here is that when Allah, exalted is He, commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam, Iblis entered into the address to them. Although he was not of their substance, he had imitated them and taken on their characteristics, so he was included in the address to them and was blamed for opposing the command. We will expand on this question, God willing, when we reach His words: ﴿Except Iblis. He was of the jinn, so he defied the command of his Lord﴾ [al-Kahf: 50].

Accordingly, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Khallad, from 'Ata', from Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Iblis, before he committed disobedience, was one of the angels, named 'Azazil. He was one of the inhabitants of the earth, and among the most diligent of the angels in worship and the most knowledgeable of them. This led him to pride, and he was from a tribe called the jinn.

In another report from Khallad, from 'Ata', from Tawus, or Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, or someone else, with similar wording.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman related to us, 'Abbad (that is, Ibn al-'Awwam) related to us, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from Ya'la ibn Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Iblis's name was 'Azazil, and he was one of the noblest of the angels, among those with four wings. Then he was made despairing afterward.

Sunayd said, from Hajjaj, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: Iblis was among the noblest of the angels and the most honourable of them in lineage. He was a guardian over the Gardens, he had authority over the lowest heaven, and he had authority over the earth.

Likewise, al-Dahhak and others related from Ibn 'Abbas, the same.

Salih, the freedman of al-Tawama, said, from Ibn 'Abbas: Among the angels there is a group called the jinn, and Iblis was one of them. He governed what is between heaven and earth. Then he disobeyed, so Allah transformed him into a accursed devil. Ibn Jarir narrated it.

Qatadah said, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: Iblis was the chief of the angels of the lowest heaven.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, 'Adiyy ibn Abi 'Adiyy related to us, from 'Awf, from al-Hasan, who said: Iblis was never one of the angels for even the blink of an eye. He was truly the origin of the jinn, just as Adam is the origin of mankind. This is a sound chain from al-Hasan. Likewise 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said the same.

Shahr ibn Hawshab said: Iblis was one of the jinn whom the angels had expelled. Some angels captured him and took him to heaven. Ibn Jarir narrated it.

Sunayd ibn Dawud said: Hushaym related to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Yahya informed us, from Musa ibn Numayr and 'Uthman ibn Sa'id ibn Kamil, from Sa'd ibn Mas'ud, who said: The angels used to fight the jinn, and Iblis was taken captive while he was young. He was with the angels and worshipped with them. When they were commanded to prostrate to Adam, they prostrated, but Iblis refused. For this reason Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Except Iblis. He was of the jinn﴾ [al-Kahf: 50].

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz related to us, Abu 'Asim related to us, from Sharik, from a man, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Allah created a creation and said: Prostrate to Adam. They said: We will not do it. So Allah sent fire upon them and it burned them. Then He created another creation and said: "I am creating a human from clay; prostrate to Adam." He said: They refused. So Allah sent fire upon them and it burned them. Then He created these, and said: Prostrate to Adam. They said: Yes. Iblis was among those who refused to prostrate to Adam. [Tafsir al-Tabari (1/508).] This report is strange, and its chain is hardly sound, for in it is an unidentified man, and such a one is not used as evidence. And Allah knows best.

Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And when We said to the angels: Prostrate to Adam﴾, said: Obedience was to Allah, and the prostration was an honour by which Allah gave Adam precedence, by making His angels prostrate to him.

He also said, regarding His words: ﴿So they all prostrated, except Iblis. He refused and was arrogant, and was among the disbelievers﴾: The enemy of Allah, Iblis, envied Adam, peace be upon him, for the honour Allah had given him, and said: "I am from fire, and he is from clay." The beginning of sins was pride. The enemy of Allah became arrogant and refused to prostrate to Adam, peace be upon him.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj related to us, Abu Usamah related to us, Salih ibn Hayyan related to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Buraydah related to us: As for His words: ﴿and was among the disbelievers﴾, it means among those who refused, so the fire burned them.

Abu Ja'far related from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah: ﴿and was among the disbelievers﴾, meaning among the disobedient.

al-Suddi said: ﴿and was among the disbelievers﴾, meaning among those whom Allah had not yet created on that day, who would come into being later.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: Allah began the creation of Iblis upon disbelief and misguidance, and he acted in the manner of the angels, until He brought about through what He had made manifest in him of disbelief what He had created him for. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿and was among the disbelievers﴾.

Some people said: This prostration was a greeting, salutation and honouring, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they fell down before him in prostration. And he said: O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision of before; my Lord has made it true﴾ [Yusuf: 100]. This was prescribed in past nations, but it was abrogated in our religion. Mu'adh [in one manuscript: Mu'awiyah] said: I came to Syria and saw them prostrating to their bishops and scholars, so you, O Messenger of Allah, are more deserving that you be prostrated to. He said: "No. If I were to command a human to prostrate to another human, I would command a woman to prostrate to her husband, because of the great right he has over her." [Musnad Ahmad (5/227).] Al-Razi preferred this view. Others said: Rather, the prostration was to Allah, and Adam was a qiblah in it, as He said: ﴿Establish prayer at the decline of the sun﴾ [al-Isra': 78]. But there is consideration in this analogy. The more apparent view is that the first opinion is preferable: the prostration to Adam was out of honour, veneration, respect and greeting, and it was obedience to Allah, mighty and majestic, because it was compliance with His command, exalted is He. Al-Razi, in his tafsir, strengthened this and weakened the other two opinions, namely that he was made a qiblah, since no nobility appears in that, and the other, that the intended prostration is submission and not bowing and placing the forehead on the ground. The latter is weak, as he said.

I say: It is established in the Sahih: "No one who has in his heart an atom's weight of pride will enter Paradise." [Sahih Muslim, no. 91, from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.] Iblis had in his heart pride, disbelief and obstinacy that required his expulsion and removal from the threshold of mercy and the presence of holiness. Some grammarians said: "and was among the disbelievers" means: "and became among the disbelievers" because of his refusal, as He said: ﴿So he was among the drowned﴾ [Hud: 43], and He said: ﴿Then you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 35]. And the poet said:

In a barren wilderness, and the mounts like the sandgrouse of grief, whose eggs had been chicks...

Meaning: they had become. Ibn Fawrak said: Its estimation is: "and he had been among the disbelievers in the knowledge of Allah." Al-Qurtubi preferred this, and he mentioned here an issue, saying: Our scholars said: whoever Allah manifests miracles and extraordinary events through, who is not a prophet, that does not indicate his sainthood, contrary to some Sufis and Rafidah. This is his wording. Then he argued for what he said: that we do not affirm with certainty that the one through whose hands the extraordinary event occurred will be with Allah in faith, and he himself does not affirm this for himself, meaning that the true saint is the one for whom this is affirmed in reality.

I say: Some have argued that the extraordinary may occur through the hands of someone other than a saint, rather even through the hands of the wicked and the disbeliever, by what is established concerning Ibn Sayyad, that he said: "It is smoke," when the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, concealed for him: ﴿So watch for the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke﴾ [al-Dukhan: 10]; and by what he used to do, that he would fill the road when angry, until 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar struck him; and by what the hadiths have established concerning the Dajjal, of the many extraordinary things that will occur through his hands: that he commands the sky to rain and it rains, and the earth to grow and it grows, and the treasures of the earth follow him like bees, and that he kills a young man then brings him back to life, and other terrifying matters. Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la al-Sadafi said: I said to al-Shafi'i: Al-Layth ibn Sa'd used to say: When you see a man walking on water and flying in the air, do not be deceived by him until you present his affair to the Book and the Sunnah. Al-Shafi'i said: Al-Layth fell short, may Allah have mercy on him. Rather, when you see a man walking on water and flying in the air, do not be deceived by him until you present his affair to the Book and the Sunnah. Fakhr al-Din and others related two opinions of the scholars: whether the one commanded to prostrate to Adam was specific to the angels of the earth, or general to the angels of the heavens and the earth. A group preferred each of the two opinions. The apparent meaning of the noble verse is generality: ﴿So all the angels prostrated, every one of them, except Iblis﴾ [al-Hijr: 30-31; Sad: 73-74]. These are four aspects that strengthen the generality. And Allah knows best.

Allah the Exalted says, relating what He honoured Adam with, after He commanded the angels [in some manuscripts: "His angels"] to prostrate to him, and they prostrated except Iblis: that He allowed him to dwell in the Garden, to dwell in it wherever he wills, and to eat from it whatever he wills [in some manuscripts: "whatever He wills"] in ease (raghadan), meaning: comfortably, abundantly and pleasantly.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated, from the hadith of Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Damghani, who said: Salamah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, from Mikha'il, from Layth, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father, from Abu Dharr, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, was Adam a prophet?" He said: "Yes, a prophet and a messenger, whom Allah addressed directly, saying: ﴿Dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden﴾" [Ibn Sa'd narrated it in al-Tabaqat al-Kubra (1/10) through Abu 'Umar al-Shami, from 'Ubayd al-Khashkhash, from Abu Dharr, in similar wording; Abu al-Shaykh narrated it in al-'Azamah, no. 1016, through Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, from Abu Dharr, in similar wording; and Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad (5/265) through 'Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, as a marfu' report in similar wording.]

There is difference of opinion concerning the Garden in which Adam was made to dwell: is it in the heavens or on the earth? Most scholars hold the first view. [Al-Qurtubi related from the Mu'tazilah and the Qadariyyah the view that it is on the earth.] This will be discussed in Surah al-A'raf, if Allah wills. The context of the verse indicates that Hawwa' (Eve) was created before Adam entered the Garden. Muhammad ibn Ishaq clearly stated this, saying: When Allah had finished rebuking Iblis, He turned to Adam, having taught him all the names, and said: ﴿O Adam, inform them of their names﴾ up to His words: ﴿Indeed You are the Knowing, the Wise﴾ [in one manuscript: "and what you used to conceal"]. He said: Then sleep was cast upon Adam, according to what has reached us from the People of the Book, from the People of the Torah and others among the people of knowledge, from Ibn 'Abbas and others. Then He took one of his ribs from his left side, closed the place with flesh, while Adam was sleeping and did not stir from his sleep, until Allah created from that rib his wife Hawwa', fashioning her as a woman so that he might find rest in her. When the sleep was lifted from him and he awoke, he saw her beside him, and he said, as they claim, and Allah knows best: "My flesh, my blood and my soul [in some manuscripts: "and my wife"]." So he found rest in her. When Allah had joined him in marriage and made for him a dwelling from his own self, He said to him directly: ﴿O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden, and eat from it in ease wherever you two wish, and do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers.﴾

It is also said that the creation of Hawwa' was after his entering the Garden, as al-Suddi stated in his tafsir, relating it from Abu Malik, and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some of the Companions: Iblis was expelled from the Garden, and Adam was made to dwell in the Garden. He would walk in it, lonely, having no wife to rest with. He slept a sleep and then awoke, and beside his head was a woman sitting, whom Allah had created from his rib. He asked her: "What are you?" She said: "A woman." He said: "Why were you created?" She said: "So that you may find rest in me." The angels said to him, examining how far his knowledge reached: "What is her name, O Adam?" He said: "Hawwa'." They said: "Why was she named Hawwa'?" He said: "Because she was created from a living thing." Allah said: ﴿O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden, and eat from it in ease wherever you two wish.﴾

As for His saying: ﴿And do not approach this tree﴾, it was a test and trial from Allah the Exalted for Adam. Scholars differed concerning what this tree was.

Al-Suddi said, from one who narrated to him, from Ibn 'Abbas: the tree that Adam, peace be upon him, was forbidden was the grapevine (al-karm). Likewise said Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Suddi, al-Sha'bi, Ja'dah ibn Hubayrah, and Muhammad ibn Qays.

Al-Suddi also said, in a report he mentioned from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some of the Companions: ﴿And do not approach this tree﴾ is the grapevine. The Jews claim that it is wheat.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Samurah al-Ahmasi narrated to us, Abu Yahya al-Himmani narrated to us, al-Nadr Abu 'Umar al-Kharraz narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The tree that Adam, peace be upon him, was forbidden was the ear of grain (al-sunbulah).

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ibn 'Uyaynah and Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from al-Hasan ibn 'Imarah, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: It is the ear of grain.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from a man of knowledge, from Hajjaj, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: It is wheat (al-burr).

Ibn Jarir said: al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, al-Qasim narrated to us, a man from Banu Tamim narrated to me, that Ibn 'Abbas wrote to Abu al-Jald asking him about the tree from which Adam ate and the tree at which Adam repented. Abu al-Jald wrote back to him: "You asked me about the tree from which Adam, peace be upon him, was forbidden, and it is the ear of grain; and you asked me about the tree at which Adam repented, and it is the olive tree (al-zaytunah)."

Likewise, al-Hasan al-Basri, Wahb ibn Munabbih, 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi, Abu Malik, Muharib ibn Dithar, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla interpreted it so. [In one manuscript: "Mujahid" in place of "Muharib".]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from some people of Yemen, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: that he used to say: it is wheat, but its grain in the Garden is like the kidneys of a cow, softer than butter and sweeter than honey.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Husayn, from Abu Malik: ﴿And do not approach this tree﴾ — he said: it is the date palm.

Ibn Jarir said, from Mujahid: ﴿And do not approach this tree﴾ — he said: it is the fig. Qatadah and Ibn Jurayj also said so.

Abu Ja'far al-Razi said, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah: the tree was such that whoever ate from it would become impure (ahdatha), and it is not fitting that there be any impurity in the Garden. 'Abd al-Razzaq said: 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhrib narrated to us, saying: I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: When Allah made Adam and his wife dwell in the Garden and forbade him to eat from the tree — and it was a tree whose branches intertwined, some of them within others, and it had fruit which the angels ate for their immortality — that is the fruit which Allah forbade to Adam and his wife.

These are six opinions concerning the identity of this tree.

The Imam, the great scholar Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The correct position on this is to say that Allah, may His praise be exalted, forbade Adam and his wife to eat from a specific tree among the trees of the Garden, apart from its other trees; they ate from it. We have no knowledge of which tree it was specifically, because Allah did not place for His servants any indication of it in the Qur'an or in authentic Sunnah. It has been said: it was the wheat tree; it has been said: it was the grapevine; it has been said: it was the fig tree. It is possible that it was one of these, and that is knowledge which, if known, benefits the one who knows it, and if a person is ignorant of it, his ignorance does not harm him. And Allah knows best. [Likewise, Imam Fakhr al-Din al-Razi preferred this in his tafsir and elsewhere, and it is the correct view.]

And the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So Satan caused them to slip from it﴾. The pronoun in His words ﴿from it﴾ may refer to the Garden, so the meaning of the statement would be as Hamza and ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdala, that is Ibn Abi al-Najud, read it: ﴿fa-azālahumā﴾, meaning, "He removed them," that is, "He saved them." It may also refer to the nearest of the two things mentioned, which is the tree. In that case the meaning would be, as al-Hasan and Qatada said, ﴿fa-azallahumā﴾, meaning, "He caused them to slip" (from the side of slipping). On this reading the sense of the statement is ﴿So Satan caused them to slip from it﴾, that is, "because of it," as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Turned away from it is whoever is turned away﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 9], that is, "Whoever is turned away is turned away because of it." For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So He brought them out of that in which they were﴾, that is, out of the clothing, the spacious dwelling, the pleasant provision and the comfort.

﴿And We said, "Go down, some of you to others an enemy, and for you on the earth is a dwelling place and provision for a time."﴾ That is, a place of settlement, provisions and lifespans. ﴿For a time﴾ means until a specified time and a determined measure, after which the Resurrection will occur.

The exegetes from the early generation, such as al-Suddi with his chains of narration, Abu al-ʿAliya, Wahb ibn Munabbih and others, have mentioned here reports from the Israelite sources (Isra'iliyyat) about the story of the serpent and Iblis, and how Iblis entered the Garden and whispered to them. We will expand on that, God willing, in Surat al-Aʿraf, for the story there is more detailed than it is here, and Allah is the Granter of success.

Ibn Abi Hatim has said here: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ishkab related to us, ʿAli ibn ʿĀṣim related to us, from Saʿid ibn Abi ʿArouba, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah created Adam as a tall man with abundant hair on his head, as if he were a towering palm tree. When he tasted the tree, his garment fell from him, and the first thing that appeared of him was his private part. When he looked at his private part he began to run about in the Garden, and a tree seized his hair, and he struggled with it. The Merciful called out to him: 'O Adam, are you fleeing from Me?' When he heard the speech of the Merciful he said: 'O Lord, no, but out of shame.'"[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/129).]

He said: And Ja'far ibn Ahmad ibn al-Hakam al-Qawmashi related to me in the year 254 AH, Sulaym ibn Mansur ibn ʿAmmar related to us, ʿAli ibn ʿĀṣim related to us, from Saʿid, from Qatada, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Adam tasted from the tree he fled in flight, so a tree caught hold of his hair. He was called: 'O Adam, is it fleeing from Me?' He said: 'No, rather out of shame before You.' He said: 'O Adam, leave My neighbourhood, for by My might, no one who disobeys Me shall dwell in it with Me. Even if I had created the like of you, filling the earth with creatures, and then they disobeyed Me, I would have housed them in the abode of the disobedient.'"[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/130).]

This is a rare hadith (gharib), and there is a break in its chain, indeed a serious break (iʿdal), between Qatada and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, may Allah be pleased with them both.

Al-Hakim said: Abu Bakr ibn Balawayh related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Muʿawiya ibn ʿAmr, from Zaʾida, from ʿAmmar ibn Muʿawiya al-Bajali, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Adam was not made to dwell in the Garden except for the period between the afternoon prayer and the setting of the sun. Then he said: "It is sound according to the conditions of al-Bukhari and Muslim, though they did not record it."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd said in his Tafsir: Rawh related to us, from Hisham, from al-Hasan, who said: Adam remained in the Garden for an hour of a day, and that hour was one hundred and thirty years of the days of this world.

Abu Jaʿfar al-Razi said, from al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas: Adam went out of the Garden at the ninth or tenth hour, and Adam took with him a branch from the trees of the Garden, and on his head was a crown from the trees of the Garden, which is a diadem of the leaves of the Garden.

Al-Suddi said: Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Go down from it, all of you﴾, so they went down. Adam descended in India, and the Black Stone descended with him, and a handful of the leaves of the Garden, and he scattered it in India, and the tree of fragrance grew. The origin of all the fragrance brought from India is from that handful of leaves with which Adam descended. Adam only gathered it out of grief for the Garden when he was expelled from it.

ʿImran ibn ʿUyayna said, from ʿAta ibn al-Saʾib, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Adam was sent down from the Garden to Dahna, the land of India.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zurʿa related to us, ʿUthman ibn Abi Shayba related to us, Jarir related to us, from ʿAta, from Saʿid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Adam, peace be upon him, was sent down to a land called Dahna, between Mecca and al-Taʾif.

And from al-Hasan al-Basri, who said: Adam was sent down in India, Eve in Jeddah, Iblis at Dastumisan near Basra by a few miles, and the serpent was sent down at Isfahan. Ibn Abi Hatim related it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn ʿAmmar ibn al-Harith related to us, Muhammad ibn Saʿid ibn Sabiq related to us, ʿAmr ibn Abi Qays related to us, from Ibn ʿAdi, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: Adam was sent down at al-Safa, and Eve at al-Marwa.

Rajaʾ ibn Salama said: Adam, peace be upon him, was sent down with his hands on his knees, his head bowed, and Iblis was sent down interlacing his fingers, raising his head to the sky.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq said: Maʿmar said: ʿAwf informed me, from Qassama ibn Zuhayr, from Abu Musa, who said: When Allah sent Adam down from the Garden to the earth, He taught him the craft of everything and provided him with fruits of the Garden. So your fruits are these, from the fruits of the Garden, except that these change and those do not change.[Tafsir ʿAbd al-Razzaq (1/66).]

Al-Zuhri related, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz al-Aʿraj, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best day on which the sun has risen is Friday. On it Adam was created, on it he was admitted into the Garden, and on it he was expelled from it." Related by Muslim and al-Nasa'i.[Sahih Muslim, no. (854), and Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/89).]

Fakhr al-Din said: Know that in these verses there is a great warning against all sins from several aspects. The first: whoever contemplates what befell Adam because of his committing this small slip would be in intense dread of sins. The poet said:

O you who gaze with the eye of one asleep, and witness the matter without witnessing it...

You add sins to sins, and hope to attain the ranks of the Gardens and the success of the worshipper...

Have you forgotten your Lord when He expelled Adam from it into this world for a single sin?

Fakhr al-Din related from Fath al-Mawsili that he said: We were a people of the people of the Garden, then Iblis took us captive to this world, so we have nothing but worry and grief until we are returned to the abode from which we were expelled. If it is said: If the Garden of Adam in which he was made to dwell is in the heaven, as most scholars maintain, how can Iblis be enabled to enter the Garden, when he was driven out from there by a decree, and one who is decreed cannot oppose or resist it? The answer: This very objection has been used by those who say that the Garden in which Adam was on the earth, not in the heaven. We have expounded this in the beginning of our book al-Bidaya wa al-Nihaya. The majority answered with several replies. One of them: he was prevented from entering the Garden honourably; but entering it in a manner of rebuke and humiliation is not impossible. For this reason some said: as it came in the Torah, that he entered the mouth of the serpent into the Garden. Some said: It is possible that he whispered to them while he was outside the gate of the Garden. Others said: It is possible that he whispered to them while he was on the earth and they were in the heaven. These were mentioned by al-Zamakhshari and others. Al-Qurtubi has also cited here hadiths about serpents and killing them, and the ruling on that, and he did well and was beneficial.[Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1/313-317).]

The commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on Surah 2, verse 37:

It has been said that these words are explained by His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿They said, "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers."﴾ [Al-A'raf: 23] This was narrated from Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, Khalid ibn Ma'dan, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam. Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i said, on the authority of a man from the Banu Tamim: "I came to Ibn 'Abbas and asked him, 'What are the words that Adam received from his Lord?' He said: 'He taught Adam the rites of the Hajj (pilgrimage).'"

Sufyan al-Thawri said, on the authority of 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Rufay', who said: "Someone told me that he had heard 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr." In another narration, he said: "Mujahid informed me, on the authority of 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, that he said: Adam said: 'O Lord, my sin that I committed, is it something You wrote against me before You created me, or is it something I invented from my own self?' He said: 'Rather, it is something I wrote against you before I created you.' He said: 'Then, as You wrote it against me, forgive me.' He said: 'That is His saying: ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words﴾.'"

Al-Suddi said, on the authority of someone who narrated to him, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Then Adam received from his Lord words." He said: Adam (peace be upon him) said: "O Lord, did You not create me with Your own hand?" It was said to him: "Yes." "And did You breathe into me of Your spirit?" It was said to him: "Yes." "And I sneezed and You said: 'May Allah have mercy on you,' and Your mercy preceded Your wrath?" It was said to him: "Yes." "And did You write against me that I would do this?" It was said to him: "Yes." He said: "Do you think, if I repent, will You return me to Paradise?" He said: "Yes."

Similarly, al-'Awfi, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Sa'id ibn Ma'bad narrated from Ibn 'Abbas something similar. Al-Hakim narrated it in his al-Mustadrak from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, and said: "Its isnad is sahih, but the two (Shaykhs) did not record it." [al-Mustadrak (2/545).] Likewise al-Suddi and 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi explained it.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated here a hadith similar to this, saying: "'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ishkab narrated to us, 'Ali ibn 'Asim narrated to us, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Adam (peace be upon him) said: "Tell me, O Lord, if I repent and return, will You return me to Paradise?" He said: "Yes." That is His saying: ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words﴾.'" [Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/135).]

This is a gharib (singular) hadith through this route, and in it there is inqita' (a break in the chain).

Abu Ja'far al-Razi said, on the authority of al-Rabi' ibn Anas, on the authority of Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding His saying: ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words﴾: "When Adam committed the sin, he said: 'O Lord, do You see that if I repent and amend, (will You forgive me)?' Allah said: 'Then I will return you to Paradise.' So that is among the words. And also among the words: ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers.﴾" [Al-A'raf: 23.]

Ibn Abi Najih said, on the authority of Mujahid, that he used to say, regarding Allah's saying: ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words﴾: "The words are: 'O Allah, there is no god but You, glory be to You and praise be to You. My Lord, I have wronged myself, so forgive me, for You are the best of forgivers. O Allah, there is no god but You, glory be to You and praise be to You. My Lord, I have wronged myself, so have mercy upon me, for You are the best of the merciful. O Allah, there is no god but You, glory be to You and praise be to You. My Lord, I have wronged myself, so turn to me in repentance, for You are the Ever-Returning, the Most Merciful.'"

*   *

His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿Indeed, He is the Ever-Returning, the Most Merciful﴾ means: He turns (in forgiveness) to whoever turns to Him in repentance and returns (to Him), as in His saying: ﴿Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants?﴾ [At-Tawbah: 104], and His saying: ﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself and then seeks forgiveness of Allah will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [An-Nisa': 110], and His saying: ﴿And whoever repents and does righteousness, then indeed he turns to Allah with (accepted) repentance﴾ [Al-Furqan: 71], and other verses that indicate that He, the Exalted, forgives sins and turns in mercy to whoever repents. This is among His kindness to His creation and His mercy to His servants. There is no god except Him, the Ever-Returning, the Most Merciful.

We mentioned in the al-Musnad al-Kabir (the Great Musnad), through the route of Sulayman ibn Sulaym, from Ibn Buraydah, and this is Sulayman, on the authority of his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "When Allah sent Adam down to the earth, he circumambulated the House seven times and prayed two rak'ahs behind the Maqam (the Station of Abraham). Then he said: 'O Allah, You know my secret and my openness, so accept my excuse. You know my need, so give me my request. You know what is within me, so forgive my sins. I ask You for a faith that penetrates my heart and a sincere certainty, until I know that nothing will befall me except what You have written for me.' Then Allah revealed to him: 'You have called upon Me with a supplication by which I will respond to you and to whoever calls upon Me with it. I will relieve his worries and griefs, remove his poverty from between his eyes, and I will make the trade of every merchant come to him, even if he does not desire it, and the adornment of the world (will come to him) even if he does not desire it.'" Narrated by al-Tabarani in his al-Mu'jam al-Kabir. [Jami' al-Masanid wa al-Sunan, no. (742); I have not located it in the printed al-Mu'jam al-Kabir.]

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said, relating what Allah warned Adam, his wife, and Iblis of before He brought them down from the Garden. The intended meaning concerns their offspring: that He will send down the Books and raise up the prophets and messengers. As Abu al-'Aliyah said, "al-huda" (guidance) means the prophets, the messengers, and the clear explanation. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said, "al-huda is Muhammad (ﷺ)." Al-Hasan said, "al-huda is the Qur'an." Both of these views are sound, but Abu al-'Aliyah's view is more comprehensive.

﴿Whoever follows My guidance﴾, that is, whoever turns to what I have sent down in the Books and sent through the messengers, ﴿there shall be no fear for them﴾, that is, concerning what they will face of the matters of the Hereafter, ﴿nor shall they grieve﴾ over what they have missed of the affairs of this world. As He said in Surah Ta-Ha: ﴿He said: "Go down from it, all of you, some of you enemies to others. But when there comes to you guidance from Me, whoever follows My guidance will not go astray nor be distressed"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 123]. Ibn 'Abbas said: "He will not go astray in this world, nor be distressed in the Hereafter." ﴿But whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed for him is a constricted life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾ [Ta-Ha: 124]. As He said here: ﴿And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever﴾, that is, they will be eternally abiding in it, with no escape from it and no way out.

Ibn Jarir (may Allah have mercy on him) has cited here a hadith which he transmitted by two chains, from Abu Maslamah Sa'id ibn Yazid, from Abu Nadrah al-Mundhir ibn Malik ibn Qut'ah [in one manuscript: "Qus'ah"], from Abu Sa'id, whose name is Sa'd ibn Malik ibn Sinan al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "As for the people of the Fire, who are its people, they will neither die therein nor live. But there are people whom the Fire will afflict because of their sins or their misdeeds, and it will cause them to die a death, until when they become charcoal, intercession will be permitted." Muslim also narrated it from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Abu Salamah, with the same wording. [Source references: Tafsir al-Tabari (1/552) and Sahih Muslim, no. 185.]

[Mentioning this second descent is because what follows it carries a meaning different from the first. Some scholars claimed that it is an emphasis and repetition, as one says "stand up, stand up." Others said: rather, the first descent was from the Garden to the lowest heaven, and the second was from the lowest heaven to the earth. The correct view is the first, and Allah the Exalted knows best the secrets of His Book.] [Addition from manuscripts Jim, Ta, Ba, Alif, and Waw.]

The correct view is the first, and Allah the Exalted knows best the secrets of His Book.] [Addition from manuscripts Jim, Ta, Ba, Alif, and Waw.]

Allah, the Exalted, says, commanding the Children of Israel to enter Islam and follow Muhammad (ﷺ), upon whom be the best of blessings and peace from Allah, and stirring them by mentioning their father Israel, who is the Prophet of Allah, Ya'qub (Jacob), upon him be peace. The implied meaning is: "O children of the righteous servant who obeyed Allah, be like your father in following the truth," just as you would say: "O son of the generous man, do such-and-such. O son of the brave man, challenge the champions. O son of the scholar, seek knowledge," and similar expressions.

Another example of this is His saying: ﴿The offspring of those whom We carried with Noah. Indeed, he was a grateful servant﴾ [al-Isra': 3]. Israel is Jacob, upon him be peace, as evidenced by what Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated: Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram narrated to us, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: Abdullah ibn Abbas narrated to me, saying: A group of Jews came to the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), and he said to them: "Do you know that Israel is Jacob?" They said: "Yes, by Allah." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, bear witness."[[In C: "O Allah, then bear witness."]][[Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (1/273), from Husayn, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram with this chain.]] Al-A'mash also said, from Isma'il ibn Raja', from Umayr, the freedman of Ibn Abbas, from Abdullah ibn Abbas, that Israel means, as your saying, "Abdullah" (the servant of Allah).

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Remember My favour which I bestowed upon you﴾. Mujahid said: The favour of Allah which He bestowed upon them, both those mentioned and others: He made water gush for them from the rock, sent down upon them the manna and the quails, and delivered them from the bondage of Pharaoh's people.

Abu al-Aliyah said: His favour was that He made among them prophets and messengers, and sent down to them the Books.

I say: This is like the statement of Musa, upon him be peace, to them: ﴿O my people, remember the favour of Allah upon you, when He made among you prophets and made you kings and gave you what He had not given to anyone among the worlds﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 20], meaning in their time.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Remember My favour which I bestowed upon you﴾, meaning: My trial for you and for your fathers, when He delivered them from Pharaoh and his people. ﴿And fulfil My covenant, I will fulfil your covenant﴾. He said: My covenant which I took upon your necks for the Prophet (ﷺ) when he comes to you. ﴿I will fulfil your covenant﴾, meaning: I will carry out for you what I promised you in return, by affirming him and following him, by removing from you the burden and the shackles that were upon your necks because of your sins, which were of your own innovation.

[Al-Hasan al-Basri said: It is His saying: ﴿And Allah had taken the covenant of the Children of Israel, and We raised among them twelve leaders. And Allah said: "Indeed, I am with you. If you establish prayer and give zakah and believe in My messengers and support them and loan Allah a goodly loan, I will surely remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 12], to the end of the verse. Others said: It is what Allah took from them in the Torah, that He would send from the descendants of Isma'il a great prophet whom all peoples would obey, and by him is meant Muhammad (ﷺ). Whoever follows him, his sin will be forgiven, he will be admitted to Paradise, and he will be given a double reward. Fakhr al-Din al-Razi has cited here many glad tidings about Muhammad (ﷺ) from the prophets, upon them be peace.]

Abu al-Aliyah said regarding ﴿And fulfil My covenant﴾: He said: His covenant to His servants is His religion, Islam, that they follow it.

Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿I will fulfil your covenant﴾: He said: I will be pleased with you and admit you into Paradise.

Likewise said al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, Abu al-Aliyah, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas.

* *

His saying: ﴿And of Me, fear Me﴾, meaning: so stand in awe of Me. This was said by Abu al-Aliyah, al-Suddi, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and Qatadah.

Ibn Abbas said regarding His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And of Me, fear Me﴾, meaning: I will bring upon you what I brought upon those before you of your forefathers, of the punishments that you know of, such as transformation and other things.

This is a transition from encouragement to warning. He called them to it through desire and dread, that perhaps they would return to the truth, follow the Messenger, take admonition from the Qur'an and its warnings, carry out its commands, and affirm its reports. Allah is the Guide of whom He wills to His straight path. Therefore He said: ﴿And believe in what I have sent down, confirming what you have﴾ [[﴿Confirming﴾ is a past participle in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier of ﴿what﴾, meaning: "in what I have sent down, confirming," or of the implied pronoun in their saying: "I sent it down confirming." It may also be a verbal noun not from the verb itself, namely His saying: ﴿in what I have sent down, confirming﴾.]] [[Added from C, B, W.]] meaning by it the Qur'an, which He sent down to Muhammad, the unlettered Arab Prophet, as a bringer of glad tidings, a warner, a shining lamp, comprising the truth from Allah, the Exalted, confirming what is before it of the Torah and the Gospel.

Abu al-Aliyah, may Allah have mercy on him, said regarding His saying: ﴿And believe in what I have sent down, confirming what you have﴾: He says: O People of the Book, believe in what I have sent down, confirming what you have. He says: Because they find Muhammad (ﷺ) written in their possession in the Torah and the Gospel.

Similar has been related from Mujahid, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and Qatadah.

* *

His saying: ﴿And do not be the first to disbelieve in it﴾ [[Some commentators said: "the first group to disbelieve in it" and similar.]] [[Added from C, B, W.]]. Ibn Abbas said: ﴿And do not be the first to disbelieve in it﴾, while you have in it knowledge that others do not have.

Abu al-Aliyah said: He says: ﴿And do not be the first [to disbelieve in it]﴾ [[Added from C.]] of those who disbelieved in Muhammad (ﷺ) [meaning, of your kind, the People of the Book, after they had heard of Muhammad and his mission].

Likewise said al-Hasan, al-Suddi, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas.

Ibn Jarir preferred that the pronoun in His saying ﴿in it﴾ refers to the Qur'an, which was mentioned earlier in His saying ﴿in what I have sent down﴾.

The intended meaning is the first of the Children of Israel to disbelieve in it directly, for the Jews of Medina were the first of the Children of Israel to be addressed by the Qur'an, so their disbelief in it entails that they were the first of their kind to disbelieve in it.

* *

His saying: ﴿And do not exchange My verses for a small price﴾. He says: Do not trade away belief in My verses and affirmation of My Messenger for the world and its desires, for they are small and perishing. As Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir informed us, from Harun ibn Zayd, who said: Al-Hasan, meaning al-Basri, was asked about His saying, the Exalted: ﴿a small price﴾, and he said: "The small price is the world in its entirety."

Ibn Lahi'ah said: Ata' ibn Dinar narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying: ﴿And do not exchange My verses for a small price﴾: His verses are His Book which He sent down to them, and the small price is the world and its desires.

Al-Suddi said: ﴿And do not exchange My verses for a small price﴾, he says: Do not take a small greed, and do not conceal the name of Allah for the sake of that greed, which is the price.

Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliyah regarding His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And do not exchange My verses for a small price﴾, said: Do not take a wage for it. He said: And it is written among them in the former Scripture: "O son of Adam, teach freely as you were taught freely."

It was also said: Its meaning is: do not trade away explanation, clarification, and spreading beneficial knowledge among people in exchange for concealment and confusion, in order to remain in your leadership over the worldly life, which is small, worthless, and soon to vanish.

In the Sunan of Abu Dawud, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever learns knowledge of that which is sought for the Face of Allah, but learns it only to obtain some worldly good, will not smell the fragrance of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection."[[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (3664).]]

As for teaching knowledge for a wage: if it has become obligatory upon the teacher, then he may not take a wage for it, but he may take from the public treasury (bayt al-mal) what suffices him and his dependents. If he receives nothing from it and teaching prevents him from earning a living, then it is like the case where it is not obligatory on him. When it is not obligatory on him, it is permissible for him to take a wage for it according to Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and the majority of scholars, as in Sahih al-Bukhari from Abu Sa'id in the story of the one stung by a scorpion: "The most deserving of what you take a wage for is the Book of Allah."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5007). This wording is the wording of the hadith of Ibn Abbas.]] And his saying in the story of the woman proposed to in marriage: "I have married her to you for what you have of the Qur'an."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (5149), from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd, may Allah be pleased with him.]] As for the hadith of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, that he taught a man from the People of the Suffah (the companions of the bench, poor emigrants who lived in the mosque) some of the Qur'an, and he was given a bow as a gift, and he asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about it, and he said: "If you would love to be garlanded with a bow of fire, then accept it." So he left it. Abu Dawud narrated it.[[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (3416).]] Similar has been related from Ubayy ibn Ka'b as a marfu' report.[[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (6/125) through Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Muslim, from Atiyyah ibn Qays, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, with it as marfu', and it is munqati' (broken chain).]] If its chain is sound, then according to many scholars, among them Abu Umar ibn Abd al-Barr, it is to be understood as meaning that when Allah taught him, it was no longer permissible for him, after this, to exchange Allah's reward for that bow. But if from the beginning the teaching was on the basis of a wage, then it is valid, as in the hadith of the stung man and the hadith of Sahl about the proposed woman. And Allah knows best.

﴿And of Me, be mindful of Me﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Umar al-Duri narrated to us, Abu Isma'il al-Mu'addib narrated to us, from Asim al-Ahwal, from Abu al-Aliyah, from Talq ibn Habib, who said: Taqwa (God-consciousness) is that you act in obedience to Allah, hoping for the mercy of Allah, upon a light from Allah, and taqwa is that you abandon the disobedience of Allah, fearing the punishment of Allah, upon a light from Allah.

The meaning of His saying ﴿And of Me, be mindful of Me﴾ is that He, the Exalted, threatens them for what they deliberately do of concealing the truth, displaying its opposite, and opposing the Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him.

Allah, the Exalted, says, commanding the Children of Israel to enter Islam and follow Muhammad (ﷺ), upon whom be the best of blessings and peace from Allah, and stirring them by mentioning their father Israel, who is the Prophet of Allah, Ya'qub (Jacob), upon him be peace. The implied meaning is: "O children of the righteous servant who obeyed Allah, be like your father in following the truth," just as you would say: "O son of the generous man, do such-and-such. O son of the brave man, challenge the champions. O son of the scholar, seek knowledge," and similar expressions.

Another example of this is His saying: ﴿The offspring of those whom We carried with Noah. Indeed, he was a grateful servant﴾ [al-Isra': 3]. Israel is Jacob, upon him be peace, as evidenced by what Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated: Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram narrated to us, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: Abdullah ibn Abbas narrated to me, saying: A group of Jews came to the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), and he said to them: "Do you know that Israel is Jacob?" They said: "Yes, by Allah." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, bear witness."[[In C: "O Allah, then bear witness."]][[Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (1/273), from Husayn, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram with this chain.]] Al-A'mash also said, from Isma'il ibn Raja', from Umayr, the freedman of Ibn Abbas, from Abdullah ibn Abbas, that Israel means, as your saying, "Abdullah" (the servant of Allah).

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Remember My favour which I bestowed upon you﴾. Mujahid said: The favour of Allah which He bestowed upon them, both those mentioned and others: He made water gush for them from the rock, sent down upon them the manna and the quails, and delivered them from the bondage of Pharaoh's people.

Abu al-Aliyah said: His favour was that He made among them prophets and messengers, and sent down to them the Books.

I say: This is like the statement of Musa, upon him be peace, to them: ﴿O my people, remember the favour of Allah upon you, when He made among you prophets and made you kings and gave you what He had not given to anyone among the worlds﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 20], meaning in their time.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Remember My favour which I bestowed upon you﴾, meaning: My trial for you and for your fathers, when He delivered them from Pharaoh and his people. ﴿And fulfil My covenant, I will fulfil your covenant﴾. He said: My covenant which I took upon your necks for the Prophet (ﷺ) when he comes to you. ﴿I will fulfil your covenant﴾, meaning: I will carry out for you what I promised you in return, by affirming him and following him, by removing from you the burden and the shackles that were upon your necks because of your sins, which were of your own innovation.

[Al-Hasan al-Basri said: It is His saying: ﴿And Allah had taken the covenant of the Children of Israel, and We raised among them twelve leaders. And Allah said: "Indeed, I am with you. If you establish prayer and give zakah and believe in My messengers and support them and loan Allah a goodly loan, I will surely remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 12], to the end of the verse. Others said: It is what Allah took from them in the Torah, that He would send from the descendants of Isma'il a great prophet whom all peoples would obey, and by him is meant Muhammad (ﷺ). Whoever follows him, his sin will be forgiven, he will be admitted to Paradise, and he will be given a double reward. Fakhr al-Din al-Razi has cited here many glad tidings about Muhammad (ﷺ) from the prophets, upon them be peace.]

Abu al-Aliyah said regarding ﴿And fulfil My covenant﴾: He said: His covenant to His servants is His religion, Islam, that they follow it.

Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿I will fulfil your covenant﴾: He said: I will be pleased with you and admit you into Paradise.

Likewise said al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, Abu al-Aliyah, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas.

* *

His saying: ﴿And of Me, fear Me﴾, meaning: so stand in awe of Me. This was said by Abu al-Aliyah, al-Suddi, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and Qatadah.

Ibn Abbas said regarding His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And of Me, fear Me﴾, meaning: I will bring upon you what I brought upon those before you of your forefathers, of the punishments that you know of, such as transformation and other things.

This is a transition from encouragement to warning. He called them to it through desire and dread, that perhaps they would return to the truth, follow the Messenger, take admonition from the Qur'an and its warnings, carry out its commands, and affirm its reports. Allah is the Guide of whom He wills to His straight path. Therefore He said: ﴿And believe in what I have sent down, confirming what you have﴾ [[﴿Confirming﴾ is a past participle in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier of ﴿what﴾, meaning: "in what I have sent down, confirming," or of the implied pronoun in their saying: "I sent it down confirming." It may also be a verbal noun not from the verb itself, namely His saying: ﴿in what I have sent down, confirming﴾.]] [[Added from C, B, W.]] meaning by it the Qur'an, which He sent down to Muhammad, the unlettered Arab Prophet, as a bringer of glad tidings, a warner, a shining lamp, comprising the truth from Allah, the Exalted, confirming what is before it of the Torah and the Gospel.

Abu al-Aliyah, may Allah have mercy on him, said regarding His saying: ﴿And believe in what I have sent down, confirming what you have﴾: He says: O People of the Book, believe in what I have sent down, confirming what you have. He says: Because they find Muhammad (ﷺ) written in their possession in the Torah and the Gospel.

Similar has been related from Mujahid, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and Qatadah.

* *

His saying: ﴿And do not be the first to disbelieve in it﴾ [[Some commentators said: "the first group to disbelieve in it" and similar.]] [[Added from C, B, W.]]. Ibn Abbas said: ﴿And do not be the first to disbelieve in it﴾, while you have in it knowledge that others do not have.

Abu al-Aliyah said: He says: ﴿And do not be the first [to disbelieve in it]﴾ [[Added from C.]] of those who disbelieved in Muhammad (ﷺ) [meaning, of your kind, the People of the Book, after they had heard of Muhammad and his mission].

Likewise said al-Hasan, al-Suddi, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas.

﴿And of Me, be mindful of Me﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Umar al-Duri narrated to us, Abu Isma'il al-Mu'addib narrated to us, from Asim al-Ahwal, from Abu al-Aliyah, from Talq ibn Habib, who said: Taqwa (God-consciousness) is that you act in obedience to Allah, hoping for the mercy of Allah, upon a light from Allah, and taqwa is that you abandon the disobedience of Allah, fearing the punishment of Allah, upon a light from Allah.

[Ibn Kathir's text has: "تلبيسهم" in some manuscripts, "تمويههم" in others, which are variant readings of the same sense.] So He says: ﴿And do not mix up the truth with falsehood, nor conceal the truth while you know it.﴾ He forbade them from both things together, and commanded them to make the truth manifest and state it clearly. For this reason, al-Dahhak reported from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿do not mix up the truth with falsehood﴾: do not mingle the truth with falsehood, nor the sincere with the false.

Abu al-Aliyah said: ﴿do not mix up the truth with falsehood﴾ means: do not mingle the truth with falsehood, and give sincere counsel to the servants of God from the community of Muhammad (ﷺ).

It is also narrated from Said ibn Jubayr and al-Rabi' ibn Anas, something similar.

Qatadah said: ﴿do not mix up the truth with falsehood﴾ means: do not mix Judaism and Christianity with Islam. Indeed, the religion of God is Islam, while Judaism and Christianity are innovations that are not from God.

Something similar is narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad related to me, from Ikrimah or Said ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and conceal the truth while you know it﴾ means: do not conceal what you possess of knowledge of My Messenger and of what he brought, while you find it written with you in what you know of the books that are in your hands. Something similar is narrated from Abu al-Aliyah.

Mujahid, al-Suddi, Qatadah, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: ﴿and conceal the truth﴾ refers to Muhammad (ﷺ).

[I say: ﴿wa-taktumu﴾ may be read in the jussive (majzum) or in the subjunctive (mansub). The meaning is: do not combine this with that, as one says: "Do not eat the fish and drink the milk." Al-Zamakhshari said: In the codex of Ibn Mas'ud it reads "wa-taktumuna al-haqq," meaning: while you conceal the truth; and ﴿wa-antum ta'lamun﴾ is also a circumstantial clause (hal), and its meaning is: while you know the truth. It may also mean: while you know the great harm this causes people, misleading them from guidance which leads them to the Fire, until they follow what you show them of falsehood mixed with some kind of truth, so that you may pass it off upon them. Al-bayan (clarification) is elucidation, and its opposite is concealment (kitman) and mixing truth with falsehood.]

﴿And establish prayer and give zakah and bow with those who bow.﴾ Muqatil said: God's words to the People of the Book, ﴿establish prayer﴾, commanded them to pray with the Prophet (ﷺ); ﴿give zakah﴾ commanded them to pay zakah, that is, to hand it over to the Prophet (ﷺ); ﴿bow with those who bow﴾ commanded them to bow with the bowers of the community of Muhammad (ﷺ).

That is, be among them and with them.

Ali ibn Talhah reported from Ibn Abbas: ﴿give zakah﴾ means by zakah: obedience to God and sincerity.

Waki' related from Abu Janab, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿give zakah﴾: he said: What makes zakah obligatory? He said: two hundred [dirhams] and above.

Mubarak ibn Fudalah related from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿give zakah﴾: it is an obligatory duty, without which deeds are not beneficial, together with prayer.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah related to us, Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah related to us, Jarir related to us, from Abu Hayyan al-Ajami al-Taymi, from al-Harith al-Ukli, regarding His words ﴿give zakah﴾: it is the zakat al-fitr (charity of fast-breaking).

* *

His words ﴿and bow with those who bow﴾ mean: be with the believers in their best deeds, and most especially and most completely, prayer.
