Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 44 (part 1 of 2):

He, may He be exalted, says: How is it fitting for you, O People of the Book, while you order people to do righteousness (al-birr), which is the sum of all good, that you forget yourselves and do not do what you command people to do, while you recite the Book and know what it contains concerning the punishment of those who fall short in obeying Allah's commands? Do you not then reason about what you are doing to yourselves, so that you may wake from your slumber and see clearly after your blindness?

This is like what 'Abd al-Razzaq related from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Do you order people to righteousness and forget yourselves?﴾ He said: The Children of Israel used to order people to obey Allah, to fear Him, and to do righteousness, and then they would oppose it themselves, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, rebuked them. Al-Suddi also said the same.

Ibn Juraij said: ﴿Do you order people to righteousness?﴾ The People of the Book and the hypocrites used to order people to fast and to pray, and they would abandon acting upon what they ordered people to do, so Allah rebuked them for that. Whoever commands good, let him be the most eager of people to do it.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq related, from Muhammad, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And you forget yourselves﴾ means you leave yourselves (unguided). ﴿And you recite the Book; will you not then reason?﴾ means: you forbid people from disbelief, despite what you have of prophethood and the covenant in the Torah, while you yourselves leave off; that is, while you disbelieve in what it contains of My covenant with you concerning the confirmation of My Messenger, and you break My pact, and you deny what you know of My Book.

Al-Dahhak related, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning this verse: He says: Do you command people to enter the religion of Muhammad (ﷺ) and other things you have been commanded, such as establishing the prayer, while you forget yourselves?

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: 'Ali ibn al-Hasan related to me, Muslim al-Jarmi related to us, Makhlad ibn al-Husayn related to us, from Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani, from Abu Qilabah, concerning the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Do you order people to righteousness and forget yourselves while you recite the Book?﴾ He said: Abu al-Darda' (may Allah be pleased with him) said: A man does not truly comprehend the religion until he hates people for the sake of Allah, then returns to himself and hates himself even more.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said concerning this verse: These are the Jews. When a man came to them asking about something in which there was no truth, no bribe, and nothing else, they would order him to do what is right. So Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Do you order people to righteousness and forget yourselves, while you recite the Book? Will you not then reason?﴾

The point is that Allah, the Exalted, censured them for this conduct and alerted them to their error regarding their own selves, since they would order good and not do it. The intent is not to censure them for commanding righteousness while failing to practice it, but for their abandoning it. Commanding what is good is itself good and is obligatory upon the scholar, but it is more fitting for the scholar to do it along with commanding others to do it, and not to be remiss. This is like the words of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him: ﴿I do not want to oppose you by doing what I forbid you from. I only want reform as far as I am able, and my success is only through Allah. In Him I have put my trust, and to Him I turn in repentance﴾ [Hud: 88]. So each of commanding good and doing it is obligatory, and neither one is dropped by neglecting the other, according to the most correct of the two opinions of the scholars, both of the early generations (salaf) and the later generations (khalaf). Some of them held that one who commits sins should not forbid others from them, but this view is weak, and even weaker is their reliance on this verse, for they have no proof in it. The correct position is that the scholar commands good even if he does not practice it, and forbids evil even if he commits it. [Malik related from Rabi'ah: I heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr say to him: If a person did not command good or forbid evil until he was free of all fault, no one would ever command good or forbid evil. Malik said: He spoke truly. Who is it that has no fault? I say:] Yet such a person, in this state, is blameworthy for abandoning obedience and for committing disobedience, because he knows and opposes it with clear insight; for he who knows is not like he who does not know. For this reason, the hadiths have come with warnings concerning this, as Imam Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said in his al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: Ahmad ibn al-Mu'alla al-Dimashqi and al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Ma'mari related to us, both saying: Hisham ibn 'Ammar related to us, 'Ali ibn Sulayman al-Kalbi related to us, al-A'mash related to us, from Abu Tamimah al-Hujaymi, from Jundub ibn 'Abd Allah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The likeness of the scholar who teaches people good but does not act upon it is like a lamp that gives light to people while burning itself." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/165), and al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/185): "Its narrators are trustworthy."]

This is a strange (gharib) hadith from this route.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said in his Musnad: Waki' related to us, Hammad ibn Salamah related to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, namely Ibn Jud'an, from Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I passed by a people whose lips were being cut with scissors of fire." I said: "Who are these?" They said: "Preachers from among the people of the world, who used to order people to righteousness and forget themselves, while they recited the Book. Do they not reason?" [al-Musnad (3/120).]

'Abd ibn Humayd related it in his Musnad and his Tafsir, from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same chain.

Ibn Mardawayh related it in his Tafsir from the hadith of Yunus ibn Muhammad al-Mu'addib and al-Hajjaj ibn Minhal, both from Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same chain.

Yazid ibn Harun also related it similarly from Hammad ibn Salamah.

Then Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim related to us, Musa ibn Harun related to us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Tustari related to us in Balkh, Makki ibn Ibrahim related to us, 'Umar ibn Qays related to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd [in A: "ibn Yazid"], from Thumamah, from Anas, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I passed by people whose lips and tongues were being cut with scissors of fire." I said: "Who are these, O Jibril?" He said: "These are the preachers of your Ummah, who order people to righteousness and forget themselves."

Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh also related it, from the hadith of Hisham al-Dastawa'i, from al-Mughirah, namely Ibn Habib, the in-law of Malik ibn Dinar, from Malik ibn Dinar, from Thumamah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken up on the Ascension, he passed by a people whose lips were being cut. He said: "O Jibril, who are these?" He said: "These are the preachers from your Ummah, who order people to righteousness and forget themselves. Do they not reason?" [Sahih Ibn Hibban, no. (35) in the Mawarid edition, and Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/151).]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ya'la ibn 'Ubayd related to us, al-A'mash related to us, from Abu Wa'il, who said: It was said to Usamah, while I was riding behind him: "Will you not speak to 'Uthman?" He said: "You think I do not speak to him except in your hearing? I do speak to him privately, without opening a matter that I do not want to be the first to open. By Allah, I will not tell a man, 'You are the best of people,' even if he is over me as a ruler, after I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say..." They said: "And what did you hear him say?" He said: "I heard him say: 'A man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and thrown into the Fire, and his intestines will spill out, and he will go around with them in the Fire as a donkey goes around its millstone. The people of the Fire will gather around him and say: O so-and-so, what has befallen you? Did you not used to command us to do good and forbid us from evil?' He will say: 'I used to command you to do good but I did not do it, and I used to forbid you from evil and I committed it.'" [al-Musnad (5/205).]

al-Bukhari and Muslim related it from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Mihran al-A'mash, with the same meaning in substance. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3267), and Sahih Muslim, no. (2989).]

[Ahmad said: Sayyar ibn Hatim related to us, Ja'far ibn Sulayman related to us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah will pardon the unlettered (ummiyyin) on the Day of Resurrection in a way He will not pardon the scholars." [Abu Nu'aym related it in al-Hilyah (2/7) through the route of Imam Ahmad and said: "This is a strange hadith; Sayyar is alone in narrating it from Ja'far, and we have only written it from the hadith of Ahmad ibn Hanbal." 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad said: "This is a munkar hadith; my father related it to me and only once."] It has come in some reports that Allah forgives the ignorant seventy times before He forgives the scholar once, for he who knows is not like he who does not know. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know? Only the people of understanding take heed﴾ [al-Zumar: 9]. Ibn 'Asakir related in the biography of al-Walid ibn 'Uqbah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Some people of Paradise will look down upon some people of the Fire and say: Why did you enter the Fire? By Allah, we only entered Paradise because of what we learned from you. They will say: We used to say things and not do them." [See: Mukhtasar Tarikh Dimashq of Ibn Manzur (26/336).] He narrated it from the hadith of al-Tabarani, from Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Hayyan al-Raqqi, from Zuhayr ibn 'Abbad al-Rawasi, from Abu Bakr al-Dahiri [in J: "al-Zahiri", the correct reading is what we have recorded], from 'Abd Allah ibn Hakim, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from al-Sha'bi, from al-Walid ibn 'Uqbah, and mentioned it.]

Al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas that a man came to him and said: "O Ibn 'Abbas, I want to command good and forbid evil." He said: "Have you reached that level?" He said: "I hope so." He said: "If you do not fear being exposed by three verses of the Book of Allah, then do it." He said: "And what are they?" He said: "The words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Do you order people to righteousness and forget yourselves?﴾ Have you implemented this?" He said: "No." He said: "Then the second letter (verse)." He said: "The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Why do you say what you do not do? It is greatly hateful to Allah that you say what you do not do﴾ [al-Saff: 2-3]. Have you implemented this?" He said: "No." He said: "Then the third letter." He said: "The words of the righteous servant Shu'ayb, peace be upon him: ﴿I do not want to oppose you by doing what I forbid you from﴾ [Hud: 88]. Have you implemented this verse?" He said: "No." He said: "Then begin with yourself."

Ibn Mardawayh related it in his Tafsir.

Al-Tabarani said: 'Abdan ibn Ahmad related to us, Zayd ibn al-Hurayish related to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Khirash related to us, from al-'Awwam ibn Hawshab, from [Sa'id ibn al-] Musayyab ibn Rafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever calls people to a saying or an action while he himself does not act upon it, will continue under the shadow of Allah's wrath until he stops or does what he said or called to." [Abu Nu'aym related it in al-Hilyah (2/7) through the route of al-Tabarani, and al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/276): "In its chain is 'Abd Allah ibn Khirash, whom Ibn Hibban declared trustworthy but said he makes mistakes, and the majority weakened him, while the rest of its narrators are reliable."]

Its chain of narration is weak. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: "I dislike storytelling for three reasons." [He cited] His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do you enjoin righteousness on the people while you forget yourselves?﴾ And His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? Greatly hateful in the sight of Allah is that you say what you do not do.﴾ [al-Saff: 2-3] And His saying, relating about Shu'ayb: ﴿And I do not intend to differ from you in that which I forbid you from. I intend only reform as much as I am able. And my success is not but through Allah. upon Him I have relied, and to Him I turn back.﴾ [Hud: 88]

How well Muslim ibn 'Amr said:

How ugly is the admonition of a preacher
who makes people abstain while he does not abstain.
If he were sincere in his asceticism,
his house would be the mosque, morning and evening.
If people shun the world, why is he
seeking to win them and to lull them to sleep?
Provision is divided among those you see;
white and black are both given drink from it.

Some of them said: Abu 'Uthman al-Hiri, the ascetic, once sat at a session of admonition and kept silent for a long time. Then he began to recite:

A non-pious man who enjoins piety on the people
is a physician who treats others while he himself is sick.

He said: So the people burst into weeping. Abu al-'Atahiya the poet said:

You described piety until it seemed you were its possessor,
but the stench of your sins comes from you.

Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali said:

Do not forbid a character trait while you yourself commit its like;
it is a great disgrace upon you when you do it.
Begin with yourself and restrain it from its error;
when it desists from it, then you are wise.
Then your admonition is accepted, and you are followed
by your words, and instruction benefits.

Al-Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir mentioned, in the biography of 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Zayd al-Basri, the worshipper and preacher, that he said: "I asked Allah to show me my companion in Paradise. It was said to me in a dream: 'She is a woman in Kufa called Maymuna al-Sawda'. So I set out for Kufa to see her. It was said to me: 'She is tending sheep in a valley there.' So I came to her, and behold, she was standing praying while the sheep grazed around her, and among them were wolves, which did not flee from her, and the wolves did not attack them." When she finished the prayer she said: "O Ibn Zayd, the appointment is not here; the appointment is there." I asked her about the matter of the wolves and the sheep. She said: "I put right what is between me and my Master, so He put right what is between the wolves and the sheep." I said to her: "Admonish me." She said: "How strange, an admonisher being admonished!" Then she said: "O Ibn Zayd, if you were to set the scales of justice upon your limbs, I would inform you of what is hidden and concealed within them. O Ibn Zayd, it has reached me that no servant who is given something of this world and then turns to it in repentance, except that Allah strips from him the love of solitude, and replaces for him, after closeness, distance, and after intimacy, loneliness." Then she recited:

O preacher who stood up, you have no reckoning,
rebuking a people for their sins.
You forbid them, while you are truly sick;
this is a strange and reprehensible matter.
You forbid them from error and persistence,
while in prohibiting it you are like one in doubt.
If you had reformed before this
your error, or repented recently,
then what you say, O beloved,
would have had a place of sincerity in hearts.

[[See: Mukhtasar Tarikh Dimashq by Ibn Manzur (15/253).]]

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 45–46:

Allah, exalted is He, says, commanding His servants, regarding what they hope for of the good of this world and the Hereafter, to seek help through patience (sabr) and prayer (salah). Mujahid ibn Jabr said regarding the interpretation of this verse, as did Muqatil ibn Hayyan: "Seek help in pursuing the Hereafter through patience in observing the obligations, and through prayer."

As for patience, it has been said that it is fasting, as stated explicitly by Mujahid.

Al-Qurtubi and others said: For this reason Ramadan was called the month of patience, as the Hadith states.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Abu Ishaq, from Juray ibn Kulayb, from a man of Banu Sulaym, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Fasting is half of patience."

It has also been said that patience means refraining from sins. For this reason Allah linked it with the performance of acts of worship, the highest of which is prayer.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, 'Abdullah ibn Hamzah ibn Isma'il told us, Ishaq ibn Sulayman told us, from Abu Sinan, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "Patience is of two kinds: patience at calamity, which is good, and better than that is patience in refraining from what Allah has forbidden."

Al-Hasan al-Basri is also reported to have said something similar to the words of Umar.

Ibn al-Mubarak said, from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Malik ibn Dinar, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "Patience is the servant's acknowledgement to Allah of what has befallen him, his seeking reward from Allah, and his hope for His reward. A man may be distressed while exerting self-control, and nothing is seen from him but patience."

Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding His words, ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer﴾, said: "Seek help for the pleasure of Allah, and know that these are part of obedience to Allah."

As for His words, ﴿and prayer﴾, prayer is among the greatest aids to steadfastness in the matter, as Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book, and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 45].

Imam Ahmad said: Khalaf ibn al-Walid told us, Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah told us, from 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar, from Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah al-Du'ali, who said: 'Abd al-'Aziz, the brother of Hudhayfah, said: Hudhayfah, meaning Ibn al-Yaman, said: "When a matter distressed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he would pray."

Abu Dawud also narrated it, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yahya ibn Zakariyya, from 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar, as will come.

Ibn Jarir also narrated it through a Hadith of Ibn Juraj, from 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar, from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd ibn Abi Qudamah, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn al-Yaman, from Hudhayfah, who said: "When a matter distressed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he would turn to prayer."

[Some narrated it from 'Abd al-'Aziz, the nephew of Hudhayfah, and it is said: "the brother of Hudhayfah," as a mursal report from the Prophet (ﷺ). Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi said in his Kitab al-Salah: Sahl ibn 'Uthman Abu Mas'ud al-'Askari told us, Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah told us, who said: 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar said: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah al-Du'ali said: 'Abd al-'Aziz said: Hudhayfah said: "I returned to the Prophet (ﷺ) on the night of the Confederates, and he was wrapped in a garment, praying, and when a matter distressed him, he would pray." And 'Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh told us, my father told us, Shu'bah told us, from Abu Ishaq, who heard Harithah ibn Mudarrib, who heard 'Ali say: "We were on the night of Badr, and none of us was awake except the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was praying and supplicating until morning."]

Ibn Jarir said: It is also reported from him (peace be upon him) that he passed by Abu Hurayrah while he was lying on his stomach, and said to him: "Are you in pain in your belly?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Rise and pray, for prayer is a cure."

Its meaning: Does your stomach hurt you? He said: Yes.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' and Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim both told us, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah told us, 'Uyaynah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman told us, from his father, that Ibn 'Abbas was informed of the death of his brother Qutham while he was on a journey. He said "Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un," then he moved off the road, made his camel kneel, and prayed two rak'ahs, prolonging his sitting in them. Then he rose and walked toward his mount, saying: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed it is burdensome except for the humble﴾ [al-Baqarah: 45].

Sunayd said, from Hajjaj, from Ibn Jarir: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer﴾, he said: They are two aids to the mercy of Allah.

The pronoun in His words, ﴿and indeed it﴾, refers to prayer, as Mujahid stated explicitly, and Ibn Jarir chose this view.

It is possible that it refers to what the context indicates, namely the charge to that, as in His words, exalted is He, in the story of Qarun: ﴿But those who had been given knowledge said: "Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for one who believes and does righteousness. And none is granted it except the patient"﴾ [al-Qasas: 80]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And not equal are the good deed and the bad. Repel [evil] with that which is better; and thereupon the one between whom and you there is enmity [will become] as if he were a devoted friend. But none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great good fortune﴾ [Fussilat: 34–35]. That is: this charge is not received except by those who are patient. ﴿And none is granted it﴾, that is, it is given and inspired, ﴿except one of great good fortune﴾.

In every case, His words, exalted is He, ﴿and indeed it is burdensome﴾, that is, it is a heavy hardship, ﴿except for the humble﴾. Ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "That is, those who affirm what Allah has sent down." Mujahid said: "The truly faithful believers." Abu al-'Aliyah said: "Except for the humble, the fearful." Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "Except for the humble, meaning those who are humble." Al-Dahhak said: ﴿And indeed it is burdensome﴾, he said: It is indeed heavy, except for those who are submissive to His obedience, fearful of His punishment, and who affirm His promise and His threat.

This resembles what came in the Hadith: "You have asked about something great, but it is easy for whom Allah makes it easy." [Ahmad reported it in al-Musnad (5/231) from the Hadith of Mu'adh, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Ibn Jarir said: The meaning of the verse is: "And seek help, O rabbis among the People of the Book, by restraining yourselves to obey Allah, and by establishing prayer, which prevents immorality and wrongdoing, which brings one close to the pleasure of Allah, and whose establishment is great, except upon the humble before Allah, the submissive to His obedience, and those humbled by His fear."

That is what he said. The apparent meaning is that although the verse is an address in the context of warning the Children of Israel, it is not intended for them exclusively, but is general to them and to others. And Allah knows best.

* *

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Those who are certain that they will meet their Lord and that they will return to Him﴾. This is a continuation of the preceding statement; that is: "Indeed, prayer, or the charge, is burdensome except for the humble, those who are certain [that they will meet their Lord]", that is, [they know] that they will be gathered to Him on the Day of Resurrection, presented before Him, and that they will return to Him, meaning their affairs return to His will, and He judges them as He wills with His justice. Therefore, when they were certain of the return and the recompense, the performance of acts of obedience and the abandonment of prohibited acts became easy for them.

As for His words, ﴿those who are certain that they will meet their Lord﴾, Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The Arabs sometimes call certainty "ẓann" (supposition), and doubt "ẓann" as well, like their calling darkness "sudfah" and light "sudfah," and the helper "ṣārikh" and the one seeking help "ṣārikh," and other such words where a thing is named with its opposite. Durayd ibn al-Simmah said:

"I said to them: 'Be certain of two thousand armored men, their chiefs in the Persian mail'."

He meant by this: be certain of two thousand armored men coming to you. 'Umayrah ibn Tariq said:

"That my people be strengthened, and I sit among you, and make my supposition a hidden thing thrown [at a target]."

He meant: and make my certainty a hidden thing thrown. He said: The evidence from the poetry and speech of the Arabs that supposition has the meaning of certainty is more than can be counted, and what we have mentioned is sufficient for one whom Allah has granted understanding of it. From it is the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And the criminals will see the Fire and will be certain that they are going to fall into it﴾ [al-Kahf: 53].

Then Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, Abu 'Asim told us, Sufyan told us, from Jabir, from Mujahid, who said: "Every ẓann in the Qur'an means certainty," that is, "I thought" and "they thought."

Al-Muthanna told me, Ishaq told us, Abu Dawud al-Hafari told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "Every ẓann in the Qur'an is knowledge." And this chain is sound.

Abu Ja'far al-Razi said, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding His words, exalted is He: ﴿Those who are certain that they will meet their Lord﴾, he said: "The ẓann here is certainty."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It is also reported from Mujahid, al-Suddi, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and Qatadah something similar to the statement of Abu al-'Aliyah.

Sunayd said, from Hajjaj, from Ibn Juraj: ﴿Those who are certain that they will meet their Lord﴾, they knew that they would meet their Lord, like His saying: ﴿Indeed, I was certain that I would meet my account﴾ [al-Haqqah: 20], meaning: I knew.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said the same.

I say: In the Sahih it is reported: "Allah, exalted is He, will say to the servant on the Day of Resurrection: 'Did I not marry you? Did I not honor you? Did I not subject to you horses and camels, and leave you to lead and to enjoy the good life?' He will say: 'Yes.' Allah, exalted is He, will say: 'Did you think that you would meet Me?' He will say: 'No.' Allah will say: 'Today I will forget you as you forgot Me.'" This will come in detail at His words: ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 67], if Allah wills. And Allah, exalted is He, knows best.

Imam Ahmad said: Khalaf ibn al-Walid told us, Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah told us, from 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar, from Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah al-Du'ali, who said: 'Abd al-'Aziz, the brother of Hudhayfah, said: Hudhayfah, meaning Ibn al-Yaman, said: "When a matter distressed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he would pray."

Abu Dawud also narrated it, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yahya ibn Zakariyya, from 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar, as will come.

Ibn Jarir also narrated it through a Hadith of Ibn Juraj, from 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar, from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd ibn Abi Qudamah, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn al-Yaman, from Hudhayfah, who said: "When a matter distressed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he would turn to prayer."

[Some narrated it from 'Abd al-'Aziz, the nephew of Hudhayfah, and it is said: "the brother of Hudhayfah," as a mursal report from the Prophet (ﷺ). Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi said in his Kitab al-Salah: Sahl ibn 'Uthman Abu Mas'ud al-'Askari told us, Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah told us, who said: 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar said: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah al-Du'ali said: 'Abd al-'Aziz said: Hudhayfah said: "I returned to the Prophet (ﷺ) on the night of the Confederates, and he was wrapped in a garment, praying, and when a matter distressed him, he would pray." And 'Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh told us, my father told us, Shu'bah told us, from Abu Ishaq, who heard Harithah ibn Mudarrib, who heard 'Ali say: "We were on the night of Badr, and none of us was awake except the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was praying and supplicating until morning."]

Ibn Jarir said: It is also reported from him (peace be upon him) that he passed by Abu Hurayrah while he was lying on his stomach, and said to him: "Are you in pain in your belly?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Rise and pray, for prayer is a cure."

Its meaning: Does your stomach hurt you? He said: Yes.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' and Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim both told us, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah told us, 'Uyaynah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman told us, from his father, that Ibn 'Abbas was informed of the death of his brother Qutham while he was on a journey. He said "Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un," then he moved off the road, made his camel kneel, and prayed two rak'ahs, prolonging his sitting in them. Then he rose and walked toward his mount, saying: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed it is burdensome except for the humble﴾ [al-Baqarah: 45].

Sunayd said, from Hajjaj, from Ibn Jarir: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer﴾, he said: They are two aids to the mercy of Allah.

The pronoun in His words, ﴿and indeed it﴾, refers to prayer, as Mujahid stated explicitly, and Ibn Jarir chose this view.

It is possible that it refers to what the context indicates, namely the charge to that, as in His words, exalted is He, in the story of Qarun: ﴿But those who had been given knowledge said: "Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for one who believes and does righteousness. And none is granted it except the patient"﴾ [al-Qasas: 80]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And not equal are the good deed and the bad. Repel [evil] with that which is better; and thereupon the one between whom and you there is enmity [will become] as if he were a devoted friend. But none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great good fortune﴾ [Fussilat: 34–35]. That is: this charge is not received except by those who are patient. ﴿And none is granted it﴾, that is, it is given and inspired, ﴿except one of great good fortune﴾.

In every case, His words, exalted is He, ﴿and indeed it is burdensome﴾, that is, it is a heavy hardship, ﴿except for the humble﴾. Ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "That is, those who affirm what Allah has sent down." Mujahid said: "The truly faithful believers." Abu al-'Aliyah said: "Except for the humble, the fearful." Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "Except for the humble, meaning those who are humble." Al-Dahhak said: ﴿And indeed it is burdensome﴾, he said: It is indeed heavy, except for those who are submissive to His obedience, fearful of His punishment, and who affirm His promise and His threat.

This resembles what came in the Hadith: "You have asked about something great, but it is easy for whom Allah makes it easy." [Ahmad reported it in al-Musnad (5/231) from the Hadith of Mu'adh, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Ibn Jarir said: The meaning of the verse is: "And seek help, O rabbis among the People of the Book, by restraining yourselves to obey Allah, and by establishing prayer, which prevents immorality and wrongdoing, which brings one close to the pleasure of Allah, and whose establishment is great, except upon the humble before Allah, the submissive to His obedience, and those humbled by His fear."

That is what he said. The apparent meaning is that although the verse is an address in the context of warning the Children of Israel, it is not intended for them exclusively, but is general to them and to others. And Allah knows best.

* *

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Those who are certain that they will meet their Lord and that they will return to Him﴾. This is a continuation of the preceding statement; that is: "Indeed, prayer, or the charge, is burdensome except for the humble, those who are certain [that they will meet their Lord]", that is, [they know] that they will be gathered to Him on the Day of Resurrection, presented before Him, and that they will return to Him, meaning their affairs return to His will, and He judges them as He wills with His justice. Therefore, when they were certain of the return and the recompense, the performance of acts of obedience and the abandonment of prohibited acts became easy for them.

As for His words, ﴿those who are certain that they will meet their Lord﴾, Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The Arabs sometimes call certainty "ẓann" (supposition), and doubt "ẓann" as well, like their calling darkness "sudfah" and light "sudfah," and the helper "ṣārikh" and the one seeking help "ṣārikh," and other such words where a thing is named with its opposite. Durayd ibn al-Simmah said:

"I said to them: 'Be certain of two thousand armored men, their chiefs in the Persian mail'."

He meant by this: be certain of two thousand armored men coming to you. 'Umayrah ibn Tariq said:

"That my people be strengthened, and I sit among you, and make my supposition a hidden thing thrown [at a target]."

He meant: and make my certainty a hidden thing thrown. He said: The evidence from the poetry and speech of the Arabs that supposition has the meaning of certainty is more than can be counted, and what we have mentioned is sufficient for one whom Allah has granted understanding of it. From it is the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And the criminals will see the Fire and will be certain that they are going to fall into it﴾ [al-Kahf: 53].

Then Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, Abu 'Asim told us, Sufyan told us, from Jabir, from Mujahid, who said: "Every ẓann in the Qur'an means certainty," that is, "I thought" and "they thought."

Al-Muthanna told me, Ishaq told us, Abu Dawud al-Hafari told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "Every ẓann in the Qur'an is knowledge." And this chain is sound.

Abu Ja'far al-Razi said, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding His words, exalted is He: ﴿Those who are certain that they will meet their Lord﴾, he said: "The ẓann here is certainty."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It is also reported from Mujahid, al-Suddi, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and Qatadah something similar to the statement of Abu al-'Aliyah.

Sunayd said, from Hajjaj, from Ibn Juraj: ﴿Those who are certain that they will meet their Lord﴾, they knew that they would meet their Lord, like His saying: ﴿Indeed, I was certain that I would meet my account﴾ [al-Haqqah: 20], meaning: I knew.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said the same.

I say: In the Sahih it is reported: "Allah, exalted is He, will say to the servant on the Day of Resurrection: 'Did I not marry you? Did I not honor you? Did I not subject to you horses and camels, and leave you to lead and to enjoy the good life?' He will say: 'Yes.' Allah, exalted is He, will say: 'Did you think that you would meet Me?' He will say: 'No.' Allah will say: 'Today I will forget you as you forgot Me.'" This will come in detail at His words: ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 67], if Allah wills. And Allah, exalted is He, knows best.

He (exalted is He) reminds them of the past blessings bestowed upon their fathers and forefathers, and of the favour He conferred on them by sending messengers from among them and revealing scriptures to them, and above all other nations of their time. As He says: ﴿And We chose them knowingly over the worlds﴾ [al-Dukhan: 32], and He says: ﴿And when Moses said to his people, "O my people, remember the blessing of God upon you when He made prophets among you, made you kings, and gave you what He had not given anyone else among the worlds"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 20].

Abu Ja'far al-Razi said, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding His words ﴿and that I preferred you over the worlds﴾: "[It means] by what they were given of kingship, messengers and scriptures, over the worlds of whoever was in that time, for every age has its own world."

The same has been narrated from Mujahid, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Qatadah and Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid. This interpretation must be adopted, because this Ummah (nation) is better than them, as He says addressing this Ummah: ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind: you enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and believe in God. Had the People of the Book believed, it would have been better for them﴾ [Al 'Imran: 110]. In the Masanid (collections of hadith arranged by the narrator's name) and the Sunan (collections of hadith arranged by topic) it is narrated from Mu'awiyah ibn Haydah al-Qushayri, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "You make up seventy nations; you are the best of them and the most honoured before God." The hadiths on this are numerous and will be mentioned at His words: ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind﴾.

[It has been said that the meaning is preference in some kind of excellence over all other people, and that it does not necessarily mean preference in every respect; this was related by Fakhr al-Din al-Razi, but it is open to scrutiny. It has also been said that they were preferred over all other nations because their nation included prophets from among them; this was related by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir, but it too is open to scrutiny, because ﴿the worlds﴾ is a general term that includes those before them and those after them among the prophets. Ibrahim the Friend of God came before them and is better than all the prophets of their nation, and Muhammad came after them and is better than all creation, the master of the children of Adam in this world and the Hereafter, may the blessings and peace of God be upon him and upon his brother prophets and messengers.]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 48:

When Allah, exalted is He, had first reminded them of His blessings, He followed that with a warning of the arrival of His retribution upon them on the Day of Resurrection, saying: ﴿And fear a Day﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection, ﴿when no soul will avail another soul at all﴾, that is, no one will suffice for anyone else, as He said: ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾ [al-An'am: 164], and He said: ﴿For every person that Day will be a matter that will occupy him﴾ [Abasa: 37], and He said: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord and dread a Day when no father will avail his son, nor will a son be at all availing for his father﴾ [Luqman: 33]. This is the most emphatic of situations: that neither the parent nor the child can avail the other at all. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿nor will intercession be accepted from it﴾, means on behalf of the disbelievers, as He said: ﴿So the intercession of the interceders will not benefit them﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 48], and as He said concerning the people of the Fire: ﴿So we have no intercessors, nor any close friend﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 100-101]. His saying: ﴿nor will ransom be taken from it﴾, that is, no ransom will be accepted from it, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers, never will be accepted from one of them the earth filled with gold even if he should ransom himself by it﴾ [Al 'Imran: 91], and He said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, even if they had all that is in the earth and the like of it with it to ransom themselves thereby from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it will not be accepted from them, and they will have a painful punishment﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 36]. Allah, exalted is He, also said: ﴿And even if they offer every ransom, it will not be taken from them﴾ [al-An'am: 70], and He said: ﴿So today no ransom will be taken from you or from those who disbelieved﴾ [al-Hadid: 15], up to the end of the verse. Thus He informed that if they do not believe in His Messenger and follow him in what he was sent with, and they meet Allah on the Day of Resurrection in the state they were in, then neither the kinship of a relative nor the intercession of a person of standing will benefit them, and no ransom will be accepted from them, even if it were the earth filled with gold, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Before there comes a Day in which there is no trade, nor friendship, nor intercession﴾ [al-Baqarah: 254], and He said: ﴿There is no trade therein, nor any friendship﴾ [Ibrahim: 31].

[Sunayd said: Hajjaj narrated to me, Ibn Jurayj narrated to me, he said: Mujahid said: Ibn 'Abbas said concerning ﴿nor will ransom be taken from it﴾: "It is 'badal' (substitute/compensation), and the badal is the ransom." Al-Suddi said: "As for 'adl', it equals it of the punishment; he says: even if it came with the earth filled with gold, to ransom itself with it, it would not be accepted from it." And 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said likewise.] Abu Ja'far al-Razi said, on the authority of al-Rabi' ibn Anas, on the authority of Abu al-'Aliyah, concerning His saying: ﴿nor will ransom be taken from it﴾: "It means: ransom."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It is also related from Abu Malik, al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas, something similar to that.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: al-Thawri informed us, on the authority of al-A'mash, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Taymi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, in a long hadith, he said: "As for al-sarf and al-'adl: they are the voluntary act and the obligatory act."

Likewise said al-Walid ibn Muslim, on the authority of 'Uthman ibn Abi al-'Atikah, on the authority of 'Umayr ibn Hani'.

This statement is strange here, and the first statement is more apparent in the interpretation of this verse. A hadith strengthens it, which Ibn Jarir narrated: Najih ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, 'Ali ibn Hakim narrated to us, Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of 'Amr ibn Qays al-Mula'i, on the authority of a man from the Banu Umayyah, from the people of Syria, whose praise was excellent, who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is al-'adl?" He said: "Al-'adl is the ransom."

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿nor will they be helped﴾, means: no one will be angered on their behalf so as to help them and rescue them from the punishment of Allah, as has preceded, that no relative will incline towards them, nor any person of standing, nor will any ransom be accepted from them. All of this is from the aspect of leniency. Nor will they have any helper from themselves or from others, as He said: ﴿So he will have no power nor any helper﴾ [al-Tariq: 10], meaning: He, exalted is He, will not accept from those who disbelieved in Him either ransom or intercession, and no rescuer will rescue anyone from His punishment, and no one will grant protection from it, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿And He grants protection, while none can grant protection against Him﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 88]. He said: ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds﴾ [al-Fajr: 25-26], and He said: ﴿What is [wrong] with you that you do not help one another? Rather, they are on that Day in surrender﴾ [al-Saffat: 25-26], and He said: ﴿Then why did those they had taken besides Allah as means of approach [to Him] not help them? But they had vanished from them﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 28], up to the end of the verse.

Al-Dahhak said, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿What is [wrong] with you that you do not help one another?﴾: "What is [wrong] with you today, that you are not protected from Us? Far from it! That is not for you today."

Ibn Jarir said: The interpretation of His saying: ﴿nor will they be helped﴾ means: on that Day no helper will help them, just as no intercessor will intercede for them, and no compensation or ransom will be accepted from them. Favouritism is nullified there, bribes and intercessions vanish, and mutual cooperation and support are removed from the people, and the judgment becomes that of the justice of the Almighty, before whom intercessors and helpers benefit nothing. So He will recompense an evil deed with its like, and a good deed with its multiples. This is similar to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And stop them, indeed they are to be questioned. What is [wrong] with you that you do not help one another? Rather, they are on that Day in surrender﴾ [al-Saffat: 24-26].

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him:

Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, says: "O Children of Israel, remember My favour upon you, when We delivered you from the people of Pharaoh" (﴿وَاذْكُرُوا يَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ نِعْمَتِي عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ نَجَّيْنَاكُم مِّنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾), that is, We freed you from them and rescued you from their hands, along with Musa, peace be upon him. They had been subjecting you (﴿يَسُومُونَكُمْ﴾) to evil torment, meaning they inflicted it upon you, made you taste it, and assigned you to the worst of punishments.

That was because Pharaoh, may Allah curse him, had seen a dream that terrified him. He saw a fire come out of Bayt al-Maqdis, and it entered the houses of the Copts in the land of Egypt, but not the houses of the Children of Israel. Its meaning was that the end of his kingdom would come at the hands of a man from the Children of Israel. It is also said that his advisers spoke in his presence about how the Children of Israel were expecting the emergence of a man from among them through whom they would gain power and elevation. This is also what came in the hadith of the Trials (Hadith al-Futun), as will come in its place (in Surah Ta-Ha), Allah willing. At that point, Pharaoh, may Allah curse him, ordered that every male child born thereafter among the Children of Israel be killed, and that the females be spared. He also ordered that the Children of Israel be employed in the hardest and most degrading labours.

Here the torment is explained as the slaughter of their sons, and in Surah Ibrahim it is mentioned as a further element, as He said: ﴿They subjected you to evil torment, slaughtering your sons and sparing your women﴾ [Ibrahim]. The explanation of this will come at the beginning of Surah al-Qasas, Allah willing. In Him is trust, help and support.

The meaning of ﴿يَسُومُونَكُمْ﴾ is "they assign you," as said by Abu 'Ubayda, as one says "sama-hu khutta khasf" (he assigned him a humiliating task) when he assigns it to him. 'Amr ibn Kulthum said:

"When the kingdom imposes humiliation upon people, / We refuse to let humiliation be established among us."

It is also said that its meaning is: "they perpetuate your torment," as one says "sa'imat al-ghanam" (the sheep that graze continuously) from their continuing to graze. This was related by al-Qurtubi. Here He said ﴿they slaughter your sons and spare your women﴾ to explain the favour upon them in His words ﴿they subjected you to evil torment﴾. Then He explained it with this in His words here: ﴿Remember My favour which I bestowed upon you﴾. As for Surah Ibrahim, when He said ﴿And remind them of the days of Allah﴾ [Ibrahim: 5], meaning His bounties and favours upon them, it was fitting there to say: ﴿they subjected you to evil torment, slaughtering your sons and sparing your women﴾, and so He joined slaughter to it to indicate the multiplicity of favours and bounties.

"Fir'awn" is a title applied to every ruler of Egypt who was a disbeliever, including the 'Amaliqa and others, just as "Qaysar" is applied to every ruler of Rome together with al-Sham who was a disbeliever, "Kisra" to every ruler of Persia, and "Tubba'" to every ruler of Yemen who was a disbeliever, [and "al-Najashi" to every ruler of Abyssinia, and "Batlaymus" to every ruler of India]. It is said that the name of the Pharaoh of Musa's time was al-Walid ibn Mus'ab ibn al-Rayyan, and it is also said: Mus'ab ibn al-Rayyan. Whichever it was, upon him be the curse of Allah. [He was of the lineage of 'Imliq ibn Dawud ibn Iram ibn Sam ibn Nuh, his kunya was Abu Murra, and his origin was Persian from Istakhr.]

* *

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And in that was a great trial from your Lord﴾. Ibn Jarir said: In what We did for you, by delivering you from what you were suffering from the torment of the people of Pharaoh, there was a great trial (bala') for you from your Lord, that is, a great favour upon you in that.

'Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words ﴿a great trial from your Lord﴾ that he said: "a favour." Mujahid said concerning ﴿a great trial from your Lord﴾: "a great favour from your Lord." Abu al-'Aliya, Abu Malik, al-Suddi and others said likewise.

The origin of bala' is testing, and it may be by good or by evil, as He said: ﴿And We test you with evil and good as a trial﴾ [al-Anbiya: 35], and He said: ﴿And We tested them with good things and bad things﴾ [al-A'raf: 168].

Ibn Jarir said: Most often, for evil one says "balawtuhu abluhu bala'an," and for good one says "abli-hi ibla'an wa bala'an." Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma said:

"May Allah reward with goodness what the two of them did for you, / and what they bestowed upon them, the best of tests that tests."

[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (2/49).]

He said: So he combined the two usages, because he meant that Allah bestowed upon them the best of the favours by which He tests His servants.

[It is also said that the intended meaning of His words ﴿And in that was a trial﴾ is a reference to what they were suffering of the humiliating torment, namely the slaughter of sons and the sparing of women. Al-Qurtubi said: This is the view of the majority, and his wording after relating the first view, then saying: The majority said: the reference is to the slaughter and the like, and the trial here is in the sense of evil, and the meaning of slaughter is that it is hateful and a test.]

* *

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when We parted the sea for you and delivered you and drowned the people of Pharaoh while you were looking on﴾. Its meaning: after We rescued you from the people of Pharaoh and you went out with Musa, peace be upon him, Pharaoh went out in pursuit of you, so We parted the sea for you, as Allah, exalted is He, informed about that in detail, as will come in its places, and most extensively in Surah al-Shu'ara', Allah willing.

﴿فَأَنْجَيْنَاكُمْ﴾ means: We freed you from them, placed a barrier between you and them, and drowned them while you were watching, so that this would be more healing for your hearts and more complete in humiliating your enemy.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani, from 'Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi concerning His words ﴿And when We parted the sea for you﴾ to His words ﴿while you were looking on﴾, he said: When Musa set out with the Children of Israel, news of that reached Pharaoh, and he said: "Do not follow them until the roosters crow." He said: By Allah, no rooster crowed that night until morning. So he called for a sheep, which was slaughtered, then he said: "I will not finish with its liver until six hundred thousand of the Copts have gathered to me." He had not finished with its liver before six hundred thousand of the Copts had gathered to him, then he set out. When Musa reached the sea, a man among his companions, called Yusha' ibn Nun, said to him: "Where has your Lord commanded?" He said: "Ahead of you," pointing to the sea. Yusha' then urged his horse into the sea until it reached the deep water, and the deep water carried him away, then he returned and said: "Where has your Lord commanded, O Musa? By Allah, you have not lied, nor have you been lied to." He did this three times. Then Allah revealed to Musa: ﴿Strike the sea with your staff﴾ and he struck it, ﴿so it split, and each part was like a great mountain﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 63], meaning like a mountain. Then Musa and those with him set out, and Pharaoh followed them on their path, until when they were all in it, Allah closed it over them. This is why He said: ﴿And We drowned the people of Pharaoh while you were looking on﴾. [The reference is Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (1/67).]

Similarly, more than one of the early scholars said, as its explanation will come in its place. It has been reported that this day was the Day of 'Ashura, as Imam Ahmad said:

Affan narrated to us, 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Madinah and saw the Jews fasting on the Day of 'Ashura. He said: "What is this day on which you fast?" They said: "This is a righteous day; this is the day on which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, delivered the Children of Israel from their enemy," so Musa, peace be upon him, fasted it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have a greater claim to Musa than you." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fasted it and ordered that it be fasted.

Al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah related this hadith through various chains from Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani, with the same wording as above. [Musnad (1/291), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2004), and Sahih Muslim no. (1130).]

Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Abu al-Rabi' narrated to us, Sallam, that is Ibn Sulaym, narrated to us, from Zayd al-'Ammi, from Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah split the sea for the Children of Israel on the Day of 'Ashura." [Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/133).]

This chain is weak, for Zayd al-'Ammi is weak, and his teacher Yazid al-Raqqashi is weaker than him.

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him:

Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, says: "O Children of Israel, remember My favour upon you, when We delivered you from the people of Pharaoh" (﴿وَاذْكُرُوا يَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ نِعْمَتِي عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ نَجَّيْنَاكُم مِّنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾), that is, We freed you from them and rescued you from their hands, along with Musa, peace be upon him. They had been subjecting you (﴿يَسُومُونَكُمْ﴾) to evil torment, meaning they inflicted it upon you, made you taste it, and assigned you to the worst of punishments.

That was because Pharaoh, may Allah curse him, had seen a dream that terrified him. He saw a fire come out of Bayt al-Maqdis, and it entered the houses of the Copts in the land of Egypt, but not the houses of the Children of Israel. Its meaning was that the end of his kingdom would come at the hands of a man from the Children of Israel. It is also said that his advisers spoke in his presence about how the Children of Israel were expecting the emergence of a man from among them through whom they would gain power and elevation. This is also what came in the hadith of the Trials (Hadith al-Futun), as will come in its place (in Surah Ta-Ha), Allah willing. At that point, Pharaoh, may Allah curse him, ordered that every male child born thereafter among the Children of Israel be killed, and that the females be spared. He also ordered that the Children of Israel be employed in the hardest and most degrading labours.

Here the torment is explained as the slaughter of their sons, and in Surah Ibrahim it is mentioned as a further element, as He said: ﴿They subjected you to evil torment, slaughtering your sons and sparing your women﴾ [Ibrahim]. The explanation of this will come at the beginning of Surah al-Qasas, Allah willing. In Him is trust, help and support.

The meaning of ﴿يَسُومُونَكُمْ﴾ is "they assign you," as said by Abu 'Ubayda, as one says "sama-hu khutta khasf" (he assigned him a humiliating task) when he assigns it to him. 'Amr ibn Kulthum said:

"When the kingdom imposes humiliation upon people, / We refuse to let humiliation be established among us."

It is also said that its meaning is: "they perpetuate your torment," as one says "sa'imat al-ghanam" (the sheep that graze continuously) from their continuing to graze. This was related by al-Qurtubi. Here He said ﴿they slaughter your sons and spare your women﴾ to explain the favour upon them in His words ﴿they subjected you to evil torment﴾. Then He explained it with this in His words here: ﴿Remember My favour which I bestowed upon you﴾. As for Surah Ibrahim, when He said ﴿And remind them of the days of Allah﴾ [Ibrahim: 5], meaning His bounties and favours upon them, it was fitting there to say: ﴿they subjected you to evil torment, slaughtering your sons and sparing your women﴾, and so He joined slaughter to it to indicate the multiplicity of favours and bounties.

"Fir'awn" is a title applied to every ruler of Egypt who was a disbeliever, including the 'Amaliqa and others, just as "Qaysar" is applied to every ruler of Rome together with al-Sham who was a disbeliever, "Kisra" to every ruler of Persia, and "Tubba'" to every ruler of Yemen who was a disbeliever, [and "al-Najashi" to every ruler of Abyssinia, and "Batlaymus" to every ruler of India]. It is said that the name of the Pharaoh of Musa's time was al-Walid ibn Mus'ab ibn al-Rayyan, and it is also said: Mus'ab ibn al-Rayyan. Whichever it was, upon him be the curse of Allah. [He was of the lineage of 'Imliq ibn Dawud ibn Iram ibn Sam ibn Nuh, his kunya was Abu Murra, and his origin was Persian from Istakhr.]

* *

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And in that was a great trial from your Lord﴾. Ibn Jarir said: In what We did for you, by delivering you from what you were suffering from the torment of the people of Pharaoh, there was a great trial (bala') for you from your Lord, that is, a great favour upon you in that.

'Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words ﴿a great trial from your Lord﴾ that he said: "a favour." Mujahid said concerning ﴿a great trial from your Lord﴾: "a great favour from your Lord." Abu al-'Aliya, Abu Malik, al-Suddi and others said likewise.

The origin of bala' is testing, and it may be by good or by evil, as He said: ﴿And We test you with evil and good as a trial﴾ [al-Anbiya: 35], and He said: ﴿And We tested them with good things and bad things﴾ [al-A'raf: 168].

Ibn Jarir said: Most often, for evil one says "balawtuhu abluhu bala'an," and for good one says "abli-hi ibla'an wa bala'an." Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma said:

"May Allah reward with goodness what the two of them did for you, / and what they bestowed upon them, the best of tests that tests."

[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (2/49).]

He said: So he combined the two usages, because he meant that Allah bestowed upon them the best of the favours by which He tests His servants.

[It is also said that the intended meaning of His words ﴿And in that was a trial﴾ is a reference to what they were suffering of the humiliating torment, namely the slaughter of sons and the sparing of women. Al-Qurtubi said: This is the view of the majority, and his wording after relating the first view, then saying: The majority said: the reference is to the slaughter and the like, and the trial here is in the sense of evil, and the meaning of slaughter is that it is hateful and a test.]

* *

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when We parted the sea for you and delivered you and drowned the people of Pharaoh while you were looking on﴾. Its meaning: after We rescued you from the people of Pharaoh and you went out with Musa, peace be upon him, Pharaoh went out in pursuit of you, so We parted the sea for you, as Allah, exalted is He, informed about that in detail, as will come in its places, and most extensively in Surah al-Shu'ara', Allah willing.

﴿فَأَنْجَيْنَاكُمْ﴾ means: We freed you from them, placed a barrier between you and them, and drowned them while you were watching, so that this would be more healing for your hearts and more complete in humiliating your enemy.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani, from 'Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi concerning His words ﴿And when We parted the sea for you﴾ to His words ﴿while you were looking on﴾, he said: When Musa set out with the Children of Israel, news of that reached Pharaoh, and he said: "Do not follow them until the roosters crow." He said: By Allah, no rooster crowed that night until morning. So he called for a sheep, which was slaughtered, then he said: "I will not finish with its liver until six hundred thousand of the Copts have gathered to me." He had not finished with its liver before six hundred thousand of the Copts had gathered to him, then he set out. When Musa reached the sea, a man among his companions, called Yusha' ibn Nun, said to him: "Where has your Lord commanded?" He said: "Ahead of you," pointing to the sea. Yusha' then urged his horse into the sea until it reached the deep water, and the deep water carried him away, then he returned and said: "Where has your Lord commanded, O Musa? By Allah, you have not lied, nor have you been lied to." He did this three times. Then Allah revealed to Musa: ﴿Strike the sea with your staff﴾ and he struck it, ﴿so it split, and each part was like a great mountain﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 63], meaning like a mountain. Then Musa and those with him set out, and Pharaoh followed them on their path, until when they were all in it, Allah closed it over them. This is why He said: ﴿And We drowned the people of Pharaoh while you were looking on﴾. [The reference is Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (1/67).]

Similarly, more than one of the early scholars said, as its explanation will come in its place. It has been reported that this day was the Day of 'Ashura, as Imam Ahmad said:

Affan narrated to us, 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Madinah and saw the Jews fasting on the Day of 'Ashura. He said: "What is this day on which you fast?" They said: "This is a righteous day; this is the day on which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, delivered the Children of Israel from their enemy," so Musa, peace be upon him, fasted it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have a greater claim to Musa than you." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fasted it and ordered that it be fasted.

Al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah related this hadith through various chains from Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani, with the same wording as above. [Musnad (1/291), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2004), and Sahih Muslim no. (1130).]

Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Abu al-Rabi' narrated to us, Sallam, that is Ibn Sulaym, narrated to us, from Zayd al-'Ammi, from Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah split the sea for the Children of Israel on the Day of 'Ashura." [Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/133).]

This chain is weak, for Zayd al-'Ammi is weak, and his teacher Yazid al-Raqqashi is weaker than him.

Allah the Exalted says: "And remember My favour upon you in My pardoning you, when you worshipped the calf after Musa (Moses) had gone off to the appointed time with his Lord, at the end of the appointed period, and it was forty days, which is the period mentioned in al-A'raf, in His saying, ﴿And We appointed for Musa thirty nights and completed them with ten﴾ [al-A'raf: 142]. It has been said: it was the whole of Dhu al-Qa'dah and ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah. And this occurred after their deliverance from the people of Pharaoh and their being brought safely across the sea."

Allah the Exalted says: "And remember My favour upon you in My pardoning you, when you worshipped the calf after Musa (Moses) had gone off to the appointed time with his Lord, at the end of the appointed period, and it was forty days, which is the period mentioned in al-A'raf, in His saying, ﴿And We appointed for Musa thirty nights and completed them with ten﴾ [al-A'raf: 142]. It has been said: it was the whole of Dhu al-Qa'dah and ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah. And this occurred after their deliverance from the people of Pharaoh and their being brought safely across the sea."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 53:

And His saying: ﴿And [remember] when We gave Moses the Book﴾, meaning: the Torah, ﴿and the Criterion﴾, which is that which distinguishes between truth and falsehood, and guidance and misguidance, ﴿that you may be guided﴾. And this was also after their coming out of the sea, as the context of the discourse in Surat al-A'raf indicates. And like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book after We had destroyed the former generations, as clear evidence for mankind and a guidance and a mercy, that they might remember﴾ [al-Qasas: 43].

It has been said: the waw (and) is extra, and the meaning is: "And We certainly gave Moses the Book and the Criterion." This is a strange view. It has also been said: it is coordinated (ʿaṭf) upon the preceding, even though the meaning is one, as in the saying of the poet:

"She presented the hide to her Raqishi, so he found her words to be a lie and a falsehood."

And another said:

"Ah, how delightful is Hind, and a land in which is Hind, and Hind, between her and it are distance and remoteness."

So al-kadhib (lie) is al-main (falsehood), and al-nai (distance) is al-bu'd (remoteness). And ʿAntarah said:

"Greetings to you from a ruin whose traces have long aged, which has become desolate and bare after Umm al-Haytham."

So he coordinated al-iqfar (becoming bare) upon al-iqwa' (becoming desolate), and they are one and the same.

This is the description of His forgiveness toward the Children of Israel for worshipping the calf. Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said regarding His words, ﴿And when Moses said to his people, "O my people, you have wronged yourselves by taking the calf [for worship]"﴾, that this was at the time when what had happened in their hearts over their worship of the calf occurred, when Allah said, ﴿And when they repented and saw that they had gone astray, they said, "If our Lord does not have mercy upon us and forgive us..."﴾ to the end of the verse [al-A'raf: 149].

He said: So that is when Moses said, ﴿O my people, you have wronged yourselves by taking the calf [for worship]﴾.

Abu al-'Aliyah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: ﴿So turn in repentance to your Bari'* (Creator)﴾, meaning, to your Creator.

I say: In His words here, ﴿to your Bari'﴾, there is a warning of the magnitude of their sin, meaning: turn in repentance to the One who created you, while you worshipped others alongside Him.

Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated, through the hadith of Yazid ibn Harun, from al-Asbagh ibn Zayd al-Warraq, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Allah said: Their repentance is that each one of them kills every one he meets, whether a child or a parent,* [[In T: "or a parent".]] striking him with the sword, and does not care whom he kills in that place. So those who had hidden their sins from Moses and Aaron, which Allah had made known, repented, confessed them, and did what they were commanded. Then Allah forgave both the killer and the killed. This is a portion of the Hadith al-Futun (the narrative of the trials), and it will come in full in the tafsir of Surah Taha, Allah willing.* [[It is in Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11326), and it will come at the place to which al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir referred.]]

Ibn Jarir said: Abd al-Karim ibn al-Haytham related to me, Ibrahim ibn Bashshar related to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah related to us, who said: Abu Sa'id said, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Moses said to his people: ﴿So turn in repentance to your Bari', and kill yourselves. That is better for you in the sight of your Bari'. Then He accepted your repentance. Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾. He said: Moses commanded his people, by the command of his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, to kill themselves. He said: Those who had worshipped the calf sat down, cross-legged,* [[In J, T, B: "who had clung to (ukkaf)".]] and those who had not clung to the calf stood up and took daggers in their hands, and a severe darkness came upon them, so they began killing one another. Then the darkness cleared from them, and they had cleared away seventy thousand slain. Everyone who was killed had repentance, and everyone who remained had repentance.

Ibn Juraij said: Al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah informed me that he heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid say regarding His words, ﴿so kill yourselves﴾: They said: Some of them rose against others with daggers, and some killed others. No man showed compassion to a near or distant relative, until Moses wrapped his garment [over his face]. Then they threw down what was in their hands, and seventy thousand slain were uncovered. Allah revealed to Moses: "Enough, I am satisfied." That is when Moses wrapped his garment. [It was also narrated from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, something similar to that.]*

Qatadah said: He commanded the people with a severe command, so they rose, slaughtering one another with blades, some killing others, until Allah's vengeance reached them. Then the blades fell from their hands, and He withheld the killing from them. He made repentance for the living, and martyrdom for the slain.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: A pitch-dark darkness came upon them, so some killed others, [vengeance]* [[Addition from A.]] then it cleared from them, and He made their repentance in that.

Al-Suddi, regarding His words, ﴿so kill yourselves﴾, said: Those who had worshipped it and those who had not worshipped it fought with swords, and whoever was killed from either group was a martyr, until the killing increased, until they nearly perished, until seventy thousand were killed among them. Moses and Aaron then prayed: "Our Lord, You have destroyed the Children of Israel! Our Lord, spare the remnant, spare the remnant!" So He commanded them to lay down their weapons, and He accepted their repentance. Whoever was killed from either group was a martyr, and whoever remained had his sins expiated. That is His words: ﴿Then He accepted your repentance. Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾.

Al-Zuhri said: When the Children of Israel were commanded to kill themselves, they went out, with Moses among them. They struck at one another with swords and stabbed one another with daggers, while Moses raised his hands, until they had destroyed a number of them. They said: "O Prophet of Allah, pray to Allah for us." They took hold of his upper arms, supporting his hands. Their affair continued in this way until Allah accepted their repentance; He restrained their hands from one another, so they cast down their weapons. Moses and the Children of Israel grieved over the killing that had taken place among them. Allah, may His praise be exalted, revealed to Moses: "What saddens you? As for those among you who were killed, they are alive with Me and provided for. As for those who remained, I have accepted their repentance." So Moses and the Children of Israel were gladdened by that.

Ibn Jarir narrated this with a good chain of transmission from him.

Ibn Ishaq said: When Moses returned to his people, having burned the calf and scattered its ashes into the sea, he went out to his Lord with those of his people whom he had chosen, and the thunderbolt seized them. Then they were raised again. Moses asked his Lord for repentance for the Children of Israel from worshipping the calf. He said: "No, unless they kill themselves." He said: It reached me that they said to Moses: "We will be patient with Allah's command." So Moses commanded those who had not worshipped the calf to kill those who had worshipped it. They sat in the courtyards, and the people drew their swords upon them, and began killing them. Moses wept, and women and children came to him, seeking pardon for them. Then Allah accepted their repentance, pardoned them, and Moses commanded that the swords be lifted from them.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: When Moses returned to his people, there were seventy men who had withdrawn with Aaron from the calf and had not worshipped it. Moses said to them: "Go to the appointed time of your Lord." They said: "O Moses, is there any repentance?" He said: "Yes, ﴿so kill yourselves. That is better for you in the sight of your Bari'. Then He accepted your repentance﴾," to the end of the verse. So they drew out the swords, the clubs, the daggers, and the knives. He said: Allah sent over them a haze. He said: They began feeling for one another with their hands, and some killed others. He said: A man would meet his father or his brother and kill him without knowing it. He said: They called out to one another in it: "May Allah have mercy on a servant who restrains himself until he attains Allah's pleasure." He said: So their slain were martyrs, and their living were forgiven. Then he recited: ﴿Then He accepted your repentance. Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾.

God, exalted is He, says: Remember My favour upon you in raising you up for you after the thunderbolt (al-sa'q), when you asked to see Me openly and directly (jahratan 'iyanan), something that is not possible for you or for those like you, as Ibn Jurayj said. Ibn 'Abbas said regarding this verse: ﴿And when you said, "O Musa, we will never believe you until we see Allah openly"﴾ He said: "Openly" ( 'alaniyatan).[[In ج: "yatatallaʿ".]]

Similarly, Ibrahim ibn Tahman narrated from 'Abbad ibn Ishaq, from Abu al-Huwayrith, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said regarding the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿We will never believe you until we see Allah openly﴾: "That is, openly, that is, until we see Allah."

Qatadah and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: ﴿Until we see Allah openly﴾ means directly ('iyanan).

Abu Ja'far narrated from al-Rabi' ibn Anas: They were the seventy whom Musa chose, and they went with him. He said: They heard speech, and they said: ﴿We will never believe you until we see Allah openly.﴾ He said: Then they heard a voice and were struck down (fasu'iqu), meaning they died.

Marwan ibn al-Hakam, in a sermon he delivered on the pulpit of Makkah, said: The thunderbolt (al-sa'iqah) is a cry from the sky.

Al-Suddi said regarding His words: ﴿So the thunderbolt seized you﴾: The thunderbolt is fire.

'Urwah ibn Ruwaym said regarding His words: ﴿while you were looking on﴾: He said: Some of them were struck down while others were looking on. Then these were raised up and those were struck down.

Al-Suddi also said: ﴿So the thunderbolt seized you﴾ means they died. Musa stood up weeping and calling upon Allah, saying: "My Lord, what shall I say to the Children of Israel when I come to them, after You have destroyed their best men? ﴿If You had willed, You would have destroyed them before, and me too. Would You destroy us for what the foolish among us did?﴾" [Al-A'raf: 155]. Then Allah revealed to Musa that these seventy were among those who had taken the calf. Then Allah brought them back to life, and they stood up and lived, man by man, looking at one another, asking: "How are we living?" He said: That is His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Then We raised you up after your death, that you might be grateful.﴾

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: Their death was a punishment for them, and they were raised after death so that they might complete their appointed terms (ajal). Qatadah said the same.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to us, Salamah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: When Musa returned to his people and saw what they were doing in worshipping the calf, and said what he said to his brother and to al-Samiri, and burned the calf and scattered it into the sea, Musa chose from among them seventy men, the best of the best, and said: "Go to Allah, repent to Allah for what you have done, and ask Him to accept your repentance on behalf of those whom you left behind among your people. Fast, purify yourselves, and purify your garments." He set out with them toward Mount Sinai (Tur Sina') for an appointed time that his Lord had set for him. He would not come to it except with His permission and knowledge. The seventy said to him, as has been related to me, when they had done what they were commanded and went out to meet Allah: "O Musa, ask your Lord on our behalf that we may hear the speech of our Lord." He said: "I will do so." When Musa drew near the mountain, the cloud covered it entirely. Musa drew near and entered it, and said to the people: "Come near." Whenever Allah spoke to him, a bright light would fall upon his forehead, so that no one of the children of Adam could look at it. A veil was placed between him and them. The people drew near until, when they entered the cloud, they fell down in prostration, and they heard Him speaking to Musa, commanding him and forbidding him: "Do, and do not do." When He had finished His command to him, the cloud withdrew from Musa and he came to them. They said to Musa: ﴿We will never believe you until we see Allah openly﴾, so the quake (al-rajfah) seized them, which is the thunderbolt, and they all died. Musa stood up, pleading with his Lord, calling upon Him, and begging Him, saying: ﴿My Lord, if You had willed, You would have destroyed them before and me [too]﴾ [Al-A'raf: 155]. "They have acted foolishly. Will You destroy those who are behind me of the Children of Israel for what the foolish among us have done?" That is: this would be their destruction. "I chose from them seventy men, the best of the best. I will return to them, and not one man from them is with me! What then will they believe me about, and trust me in, after this?" ﴿We have turned back to You﴾ [Al-A'raf: 156]. Musa continued pleading with his Lord, mighty and majestic, and asking Him, until He returned their souls to them. He asked Him to accept the repentance of the Children of Israel from worshipping the calf. He said: "No, unless they kill themselves."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (2/77).]]

This is the narration of Muhammad ibn Ishaq.

Ismail ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Suddi al-Kabir said: When the Children of Israel repented from worshipping the calf, and Allah accepted their repentance by having some of them kill others, as He had commanded them, Allah commanded Musa to come to Him with a group of people from the Children of Israel, who would apologise to Him for worshipping the calf. Musa had promised them, so Musa chose seventy men from his people, by his own choice, then went with them so that they could make their apology. He related the rest.

[This narration implies that the address was directed to the Children of Israel in His words: ﴿And when you said, "O Musa, we will never believe you until we see Allah openly"﴾, and the intended meaning is the seventy chosen from among them. Most of the commentators did not relate anything other than this. Fakhr al-Din al-Razi was strange in his commentary when he related, concerning the story of these seventy, that after they were brought back to life they said: "O Musa, you do not ask Allah for anything without Him giving it to you. So ask Him to make us prophets." He prayed for that and Allah answered his supplication. This is extremely strange, since no prophet is known in the time of Musa besides Harun and then Yusha' ibn Nun. The People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab) also erred in their claim that these people saw Allah, mighty and majestic, for Musa the Interlocutor (al-Kalim), peace be upon him, asked for that and was refused. How then could these seventy attain it?]

The second opinion regarding the verse: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said, in explaining this verse: When Musa returned from his Lord with the tablets, on which he had written the Torah (al-Tawrat, the Torah), he found them worshipping the calf. He commanded them to kill themselves, and they did so, and Allah accepted their repentance. He said: "These tablets contain the Book of Allah, in which is your command, which He commanded you, and your prohibition, which He forbade you." They said: "And who will take it on the basis of your word? No, by Allah, not until we see Allah openly, until Allah looks upon us and says: 'This is My Book, so take it.' Why does He not speak to us as He speaks to you, O Musa!" He recited the words of Allah: ﴿We will never believe you until we see Allah openly﴾.
