* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then you turned away after that﴾ — Allah, exalted is He, says: then after this firm, great covenant, you turned away from it, deviated, and broke it. ﴿Had it not been for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy﴾ — that is, His forgiveness of you and His sending to you the prophets and messengers — ﴿you would have been among the losers﴾ by your breaking that covenant, in this world and the Hereafter.

He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And you certainly knew﴾, O assembly of the Jews, of the punishment that befell the people of the town who disobeyed the command of Allah and broke His covenant and pledge regarding what He had taken from them: the glorification of the Sabbath (al-Sabt) and the observance of its command, since it had been prescribed for them. They devised a stratagem to hunt fish on the Sabbath day, by setting up weirs, snares and pools for them before the Sabbath. When the fish came on the Sabbath day in their usual abundance, they became entangled in those snares and tricks and could not escape them that day. When night came after the Sabbath had ended, they took them. When they did this, Allah transformed them into the form of apes, which resemble humans in their outward appearance but are not truly human. Likewise, their deeds and tricks, since they resembled the truth outwardly but opposed it inwardly, their recompense was of the same kind as their deeds. This story is set out fully in Surat al-A'raf, where He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And ask them about the town that was by the sea, when they transgressed in the Sabbath, when their fish came to them on their Sabbath day openly, and on the day they did not observe the Sabbath, they did not come to them. Thus did We test them because they were defiant﴾ [al-A'raf: 163], the whole story.

As-Suddi said: The people of this town were the people of Aylah (Ayla). Qatadah said the same. We shall cite the views of the exegetes there in detail, if Allah wills, and in Him is trust.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Be apes, despised﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿So We said to them, "Be apes, despised"﴾: He said, "Their hearts were transformed, and they were not transformed into apes; rather it is a parable that Allah set forth, like the example of the donkey that carries books" [al-Jumu'ah: 5].

Ibn Jarir narrated it from al-Muthanna, from Abu Hudhayfah; and from Muhammad ibn Amr al-Bahili, from Abu 'Asim, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, with the same.

This is a sound chain (sanad) from Mujahid, but it is a strange view, contrary to the apparent sense of the context in this place and elsewhere. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Say, "Shall I inform you of something worse than that as a recompense from Allah? Those whom Allah cursed and with whom He was angry, and of whom He made apes and swine, and who worshipped the Taghut"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 60], and so on.

Al-Awfi said in his tafsir, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿So We said to them, "Be apes, despised"﴾, and Allah made some of them apes and swine. He claimed that the young men of the people became apes and the elders became swine.

Shaybran al-Nahwi said, from Qatadah: ﴿So We said to them, "Be apes, despised"﴾: the people became apes with tails wagging, after having been men and women.

'Ata' al-Khurasani said: They were called out, "O people of the town, be apes, despised." So those who had forbidden them would enter upon them and say, "O so-and-so, did we not forbid you?" And they would nod their heads, meaning, "Yes."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Rabi'ah narrated to us at al-Mis-sisah, Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Ta'ifi narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Those who transgressed on the Sabbath were made apes for a moment (fuwaqan), then they perished, and the transformed had no offspring.

Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn 'Abbas: Allah transformed them into apes because of their disobedience. He meant that they did not live on earth beyond three days. He said: No transformed creature ever lived beyond three days; they did not eat, drink or beget offspring. Allah had created apes, swine and all other creatures in the six days which Allah mentioned in His Book. So Allah transformed these people into the form of apes, and He does so with whomever He wills, as He wills, and He changes him as He wills.

Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding His saying: ﴿Be apes, despised﴾: he said, meaning "humbled and abased." It was also narrated from Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Rabi' and Abu Malik, something similar.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from 'Ikrimah, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah only prescribed for the Children of Israel the day that He prescribed for you on your festival, the day of Friday, but they turned aside to the Sabbath and glorified it, and abandoned what they were commanded. When they insisted on keeping the Sabbath, Allah tested them with it, and forbade them in it what He had permitted them on other days. They were in a town between Ayla and Tur called Madyan. Allah forbade them, on the Sabbath, the fish: hunting them and eating them. When the Sabbath day came, the fish came to them openly, to the shore of their sea, and when the Sabbath ended they went away, so that they saw neither small nor large fish. Then when the next Sabbath came, they came openly again, and when the Sabbath ended they went away. So it continued until, after a long time had passed over them and they craved fish, a man among them secretly took a fish on the Sabbath day, tied it with a thread, released it into the water, drove a stake into the shore and fastened it to it, and left it. When the next day came, he came and took it, saying, in effect, "I did not catch it on the Sabbath," and then went off with it and ate it. When the next Sabbath came, he did the same, and the people smelled the scent of fish. The people of the town said, "By Allah, we have smelled the scent of fish," then they discovered the doings of that man. He said: They did as he did, and they secretly made and ate for a long time, and Allah did not hasten the punishment upon them, until they hunted them openly and sold them in the markets. A group among them, from the remnant (al-baqiyyah), said, "Woe to you! Fear Allah," and they forbade them from what they were doing. Another group, which had not eaten the fish and had not forbidden the people from what they had done, said: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?" They said, "As an excuse to your Lord"﴾ — meaning, as a denial of their deeds to our Lord — ﴿and perhaps they will fear Him﴾ [al-A'raf: 164].

Ibn 'Abbas said: While they were in that state, that remnant woke up in their assemblies and mosques and found the people missing and not seen. He said: Some of them said to others, "Something has happened to the people! Let us look and see what it is." They went to look in their houses and found them locked from within. They had entered them at night and locked them on themselves, as people lock themselves in, and in the morning they were apes in them. They recognised a man by his eye, and he was an ape; and a woman by her eye, and she was an ape; and a child by his eye, and he was an ape. He said: Ibn 'Abbas said: Had Allah not mentioned that He saved those who forbade evil, we would have said that He destroyed all of them. He said: This is the town about which Allah, exalted is His praise, said to Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿And ask them about the town that was by the sea﴾, and so on [al-A'raf: 163]. Al-Dahhak narrated something similar from Ibn 'Abbas.

Al-Suddi said, regarding the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And you certainly knew those among you who transgressed in the Sabbath, so We said to them, "Be apes, despised"﴾: He said: They are the people of Ayla, and it is the town that was by the sea. The fish, on the Sabbath day, when Allah had forbidden the Jews to do any work on the Sabbath, would come out, until they thrust their snouts out of the water. When Sunday came they stayed at the bottom of the sea, and none of them was seen until the Sabbath came. That is the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And ask them about the town that was by the sea, when they transgressed in the Sabbath, when their fish came to them on their Sabbath day openly, and on the day they did not observe the Sabbath, they did not come to them [Thus did We test them because they were defiant]﴾. Some of them craved fish, so a man would dig a pit and make a channel from it to the sea. When the Sabbath came, the channel was opened and the waves brought the fish, striking them until they threw them into the pit. The fish wanted to leave, but could not because of the shallowness of the channel's water, so it stayed. When Sunday came, he came and took it. The man would roast the fish, and his neighbour would smell its scent and ask him, and he would tell him, so the neighbour would do the same as his neighbour did, until the eating of fish spread among them. Their scholars said to them, "Woe to you! You are only hunting on the Sabbath, and it is not lawful for you." They said, "We only hunted it on Sunday when we took it." The scholars said, "No, rather you hunted it on the day you opened the water and it entered." He said: They refused to desist. Then some of those who had forbidden them said to others: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?﴾, meaning: Why do you admonish them, when you have admonished them and they did not obey you? Then some of them said: ﴿As an excuse to your Lord, and perhaps they will fear Him﴾ [al-A'raf: 164]. When they refused, the Muslims said, "By Allah, we will not dwell with you in one town." They divided the town with a wall. The Muslims opened one door, and the transgressors on the Sabbath opened another. Dawud, peace be upon him, had cursed them. The Muslims would go out through their door and the unbelievers through theirs. One day the Muslims went out, and the unbelievers did not open their door. When they were slow to appear, the Muslims climbed over the wall toward them, and behold, they were apes leaping upon one another. They opened for them, and they went off into the land. That is the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿So when they rebelled against what they had been forbidden, We said to them, "Be apes, despised"﴾ [al-A'raf: 166]. That is when He says: ﴿Those among the Children of Israel who disbelieved were cursed upon the tongue of Dawud and 'Isa, son of Maryam﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 78]. They are the apes.

I say: The purpose of quoting these imams is to show the error of what Mujahid, may Allah have mercy on him, held: that their transformation was only figurative (ma'nawi), not in form (suri). Rather, the correct view is that it was both figurative and in form. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿So We made it a deterrent for its contemporaries and for those after it, and an admonition for the God-fearing﴾. Some said: the pronoun in ﴿We made it﴾ refers to the apes; it was said that it refers to the fish; it was said that it refers to the punishment; and it was said that it refers to the town. Ibn Jarir related these views.

The correct view is that the pronoun refers to the town, meaning: Allah made this town, that is its people, because of their transgression in their Sabbath, ﴿a deterrent﴾, meaning: We punished them with a punishment, and We made them ﴿a lesson﴾, as Allah said about Pharaoh: ﴿So Allah seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter and the first﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 25].

* *

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 65–66 (part 2 of 2):

Allah's saying: ﴿for those before it and those after it﴾, i.e., of the towns. Ibn 'Abbas said: meaning, We made it, by the punishment We inflicted upon it, a lesson (ʿibrah) for the towns around it. As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We had already destroyed the towns around you and varied the signs, that they might return﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 27]. And from this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outskirts?﴾ [al-Ra'd: 41], according to one of the opinions. So the meaning is: those before it and after it in place. As Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "for those before it of the towns and those after it of the towns." Likewise Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿for those before it and those after it﴾ [meaning] the people present in its vicinity at that time.

It is related from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, Qatadah, and 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi: ﴿So We made it an example for those before it [and those after it]﴾, he said: what was before it of the past (generations) regarding the matter of the Sabbath.

Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Rabi' and 'Atiyyah said: ﴿and those after it﴾ [means] for those among the Children of Israel who remained after them of the people, that they should do the like of their deeds.

These (scholars) used to say: the meaning of ﴿those before it and those after it﴾ is in time.

This is sound with regard to those who come after them of the people, that the people of that town be a lesson for them. But as for those who preceded them of the people, how can this statement be valid, that the verse be interpreted as (meaning) that it is a lesson for those who preceded them? Perhaps no one would say this after reflecting upon it. Therefore it is established that the meaning of ﴿those before it and those after it﴾ is in place, namely the towns around it; as Ibn 'Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, and Allah knows best.

Abu Ja'far al-Razi related from al-Rabi' from Abu al-'Aliyah: ﴿So We made it an example for those before it﴾, i.e., a punishment for the sins of those who had passed.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: and it is related from Ikrimah, Mujahid, al-Suddi, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas, something similar to that.

Al-Qurtubi related from Ibn 'Abbas, al-Suddi, al-Farra', and Ibn 'Atiyyah: ﴿for those before it﴾ [means] among the sins of the people, ﴿and those after it﴾ [means] for whoever would do such sins after it. Fakhr al-Din related three opinions:

The first: that the meaning of ﴿those before it and those after it﴾ is: the towns that preceded it, by what they had of knowledge of its news from the earlier books, and those after it.

The second: that by this is meant those present in its vicinity from the towns and nations.

The third: that He made it a punishment for all that they committed before this act and after it. He said: this is the opinion of al-Hasan.

I say: the most preponderant of the opinions is that the meaning of ﴿those before it and those after it﴾ is: those in its vicinity from the towns whose news reaches them, and what befell it, as He said: ﴿And We had already destroyed the towns around you and varied the signs, that they might return﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 27]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease to be struck by a calamity for what they have done, or it will descend close to their home﴾ [al-Ra'd: 31], and He said: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outskirts?﴾ [al-Anbiya': 44]. So He made them a lesson and a deterrent for those in their time, and a lesson for those who come after them through the widely transmitted report about them. Hence He said: ﴿and an admonition for the God-fearing﴾.

* *

Allah's saying, the Exalted: ﴿and an admonition for the God-fearing﴾. Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and an admonition for the God-fearing﴾, those after them until the Day of Resurrection.

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: ﴿and an admonition for the God-fearing﴾ after them, so that they fear the vengeance of Allah and beware of it.

Al-Suddi and 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi said: ﴿and an admonition for the God-fearing﴾, he said: the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ.

I say: the meaning of "admonition" here is a restraining warning, i.e., We made what We inflicted upon these people of severity and punishment in return for what they committed of the prohibitions of Allah, and the stratagems they devised, so let the God-fearing beware of their conduct lest there befall them what befell them, as Imam Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Battah said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah al-Za'farani narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Amr [from Abu Salamah] narrated to us, from Abu Hurayrah: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not commit what the Jews committed, lest you make the prohibitions of Allah lawful through the slightest of stratagems."

This is a good chain, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim was deemed trustworthy by the memorizer Abu Bakr al-Khatib al-Baghdadi, and the rest of its narrators are well known and meet the criteria of authenticity. And Allah knows best.

He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And you certainly knew﴾, O assembly of the Jews, of the punishment that befell the people of the town who disobeyed the command of Allah and broke His covenant and pledge regarding what He had taken from them: the glorification of the Sabbath (al-Sabt) and the observance of its command, since it had been prescribed for them. They devised a stratagem to hunt fish on the Sabbath day, by setting up weirs, snares and pools for them before the Sabbath. When the fish came on the Sabbath day in their usual abundance, they became entangled in those snares and tricks and could not escape them that day. When night came after the Sabbath had ended, they took them. When they did this, Allah transformed them into the form of apes, which resemble humans in their outward appearance but are not truly human. Likewise, their deeds and tricks, since they resembled the truth outwardly but opposed it inwardly, their recompense was of the same kind as their deeds. This story is set out fully in Surat al-A'raf, where He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And ask them about the town that was by the sea, when they transgressed in the Sabbath, when their fish came to them on their Sabbath day openly, and on the day they did not observe the Sabbath, they did not come to them. Thus did We test them because they were defiant﴾ [al-A'raf: 163], the whole story.

As-Suddi said: The people of this town were the people of Aylah (Ayla). Qatadah said the same. We shall cite the views of the exegetes there in detail, if Allah wills, and in Him is trust.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Be apes, despised﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿So We said to them, "Be apes, despised"﴾: He said, "Their hearts were transformed, and they were not transformed into apes; rather it is a parable that Allah set forth, like the example of the donkey that carries books" [al-Jumu'ah: 5].

Ibn Jarir narrated it from al-Muthanna, from Abu Hudhayfah; and from Muhammad ibn Amr al-Bahili, from Abu 'Asim, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, with the same.

This is a sound chain (sanad) from Mujahid, but it is a strange view, contrary to the apparent sense of the context in this place and elsewhere. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Say, "Shall I inform you of something worse than that as a recompense from Allah? Those whom Allah cursed and with whom He was angry, and of whom He made apes and swine, and who worshipped the Taghut"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 60], and so on.

Al-Awfi said in his tafsir, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿So We said to them, "Be apes, despised"﴾, and Allah made some of them apes and swine. He claimed that the young men of the people became apes and the elders became swine.

Shaybran al-Nahwi said, from Qatadah: ﴿So We said to them, "Be apes, despised"﴾: the people became apes with tails wagging, after having been men and women.

'Ata' al-Khurasani said: They were called out, "O people of the town, be apes, despised." So those who had forbidden them would enter upon them and say, "O so-and-so, did we not forbid you?" And they would nod their heads, meaning, "Yes."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Rabi'ah narrated to us at al-Mis-sisah, Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Ta'ifi narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Those who transgressed on the Sabbath were made apes for a moment (fuwaqan), then they perished, and the transformed had no offspring.

Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn 'Abbas: Allah transformed them into apes because of their disobedience. He meant that they did not live on earth beyond three days. He said: No transformed creature ever lived beyond three days; they did not eat, drink or beget offspring. Allah had created apes, swine and all other creatures in the six days which Allah mentioned in His Book. So Allah transformed these people into the form of apes, and He does so with whomever He wills, as He wills, and He changes him as He wills.

Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding His saying: ﴿Be apes, despised﴾: he said, meaning "humbled and abased." It was also narrated from Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Rabi' and Abu Malik, something similar.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from 'Ikrimah, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah only prescribed for the Children of Israel the day that He prescribed for you on your festival, the day of Friday, but they turned aside to the Sabbath and glorified it, and abandoned what they were commanded. When they insisted on keeping the Sabbath, Allah tested them with it, and forbade them in it what He had permitted them on other days. They were in a town between Ayla and Tur called Madyan. Allah forbade them, on the Sabbath, the fish: hunting them and eating them. When the Sabbath day came, the fish came to them openly, to the shore of their sea, and when the Sabbath ended they went away, so that they saw neither small nor large fish. Then when the next Sabbath came, they came openly again, and when the Sabbath ended they went away. So it continued until, after a long time had passed over them and they craved fish, a man among them secretly took a fish on the Sabbath day, tied it with a thread, released it into the water, drove a stake into the shore and fastened it to it, and left it. When the next day came, he came and took it, saying, in effect, "I did not catch it on the Sabbath," and then went off with it and ate it. When the next Sabbath came, he did the same, and the people smelled the scent of fish. The people of the town said, "By Allah, we have smelled the scent of fish," then they discovered the doings of that man. He said: They did as he did, and they secretly made and ate for a long time, and Allah did not hasten the punishment upon them, until they hunted them openly and sold them in the markets. A group among them, from the remnant (al-baqiyyah), said, "Woe to you! Fear Allah," and they forbade them from what they were doing. Another group, which had not eaten the fish and had not forbidden the people from what they had done, said: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?" They said, "As an excuse to your Lord"﴾ — meaning, as a denial of their deeds to our Lord — ﴿and perhaps they will fear Him﴾ [al-A'raf: 164].

Ibn 'Abbas said: While they were in that state, that remnant woke up in their assemblies and mosques and found the people missing and not seen. He said: Some of them said to others, "Something has happened to the people! Let us look and see what it is." They went to look in their houses and found them locked from within. They had entered them at night and locked them on themselves, as people lock themselves in, and in the morning they were apes in them. They recognised a man by his eye, and he was an ape; and a woman by her eye, and she was an ape; and a child by his eye, and he was an ape. He said: Ibn 'Abbas said: Had Allah not mentioned that He saved those who forbade evil, we would have said that He destroyed all of them. He said: This is the town about which Allah, exalted is His praise, said to Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿And ask them about the town that was by the sea﴾, and so on [al-A'raf: 163]. Al-Dahhak narrated something similar from Ibn 'Abbas.

Al-Suddi said, regarding the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And you certainly knew those among you who transgressed in the Sabbath, so We said to them, "Be apes, despised"﴾: He said: They are the people of Ayla, and it is the town that was by the sea. The fish, on the Sabbath day, when Allah had forbidden the Jews to do any work on the Sabbath, would come out, until they thrust their snouts out of the water. When Sunday came they stayed at the bottom of the sea, and none of them was seen until the Sabbath came. That is the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And ask them about the town that was by the sea, when they transgressed in the Sabbath, when their fish came to them on their Sabbath day openly, and on the day they did not observe the Sabbath, they did not come to them [Thus did We test them because they were defiant]﴾. Some of them craved fish, so a man would dig a pit and make a channel from it to the sea. When the Sabbath came, the channel was opened and the waves brought the fish, striking them until they threw them into the pit. The fish wanted to leave, but could not because of the shallowness of the channel's water, so it stayed. When Sunday came, he came and took it. The man would roast the fish, and his neighbour would smell its scent and ask him, and he would tell him, so the neighbour would do the same as his neighbour did, until the eating of fish spread among them. Their scholars said to them, "Woe to you! You are only hunting on the Sabbath, and it is not lawful for you." They said, "We only hunted it on Sunday when we took it." The scholars said, "No, rather you hunted it on the day you opened the water and it entered." He said: They refused to desist. Then some of those who had forbidden them said to others: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?﴾, meaning: Why do you admonish them, when you have admonished them and they did not obey you? Then some of them said: ﴿As an excuse to your Lord, and perhaps they will fear Him﴾ [al-A'raf: 164]. When they refused, the Muslims said, "By Allah, we will not dwell with you in one town." They divided the town with a wall. The Muslims opened one door, and the transgressors on the Sabbath opened another. Dawud, peace be upon him, had cursed them. The Muslims would go out through their door and the unbelievers through theirs. One day the Muslims went out, and the unbelievers did not open their door. When they were slow to appear, the Muslims climbed over the wall toward them, and behold, they were apes leaping upon one another. They opened for them, and they went off into the land. That is the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿So when they rebelled against what they had been forbidden, We said to them, "Be apes, despised"﴾ [al-A'raf: 166]. That is when He says: ﴿Those among the Children of Israel who disbelieved were cursed upon the tongue of Dawud and 'Isa, son of Maryam﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 78]. They are the apes.

I say: The purpose of quoting these imams is to show the error of what Mujahid, may Allah have mercy on him, held: that their transformation was only figurative (ma'nawi), not in form (suri). Rather, the correct view is that it was both figurative and in form. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿So We made it a deterrent for its contemporaries and for those after it, and an admonition for the God-fearing﴾. Some said: the pronoun in ﴿We made it﴾ refers to the apes; it was said that it refers to the fish; it was said that it refers to the punishment; and it was said that it refers to the town. Ibn Jarir related these views.

The correct view is that the pronoun refers to the town, meaning: Allah made this town, that is its people, because of their transgression in their Sabbath, ﴿a deterrent﴾, meaning: We punished them with a punishment, and We made them ﴿a lesson﴾, as Allah said about Pharaoh: ﴿So Allah seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter and the first﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 25].

* *

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 65–66 (part 2 of 2):

Allah's saying: ﴿for those before it and those after it﴾, i.e., of the towns. Ibn 'Abbas said: meaning, We made it, by the punishment We inflicted upon it, a lesson (ʿibrah) for the towns around it. As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We had already destroyed the towns around you and varied the signs, that they might return﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 27]. And from this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outskirts?﴾ [al-Ra'd: 41], according to one of the opinions. So the meaning is: those before it and after it in place. As Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "for those before it of the towns and those after it of the towns." Likewise Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿for those before it and those after it﴾ [meaning] the people present in its vicinity at that time.

It is related from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, Qatadah, and 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi: ﴿So We made it an example for those before it [and those after it]﴾, he said: what was before it of the past (generations) regarding the matter of the Sabbath.

Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Rabi' and 'Atiyyah said: ﴿and those after it﴾ [means] for those among the Children of Israel who remained after them of the people, that they should do the like of their deeds.

These (scholars) used to say: the meaning of ﴿those before it and those after it﴾ is in time.

This is sound with regard to those who come after them of the people, that the people of that town be a lesson for them. But as for those who preceded them of the people, how can this statement be valid, that the verse be interpreted as (meaning) that it is a lesson for those who preceded them? Perhaps no one would say this after reflecting upon it. Therefore it is established that the meaning of ﴿those before it and those after it﴾ is in place, namely the towns around it; as Ibn 'Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, and Allah knows best.

Abu Ja'far al-Razi related from al-Rabi' from Abu al-'Aliyah: ﴿So We made it an example for those before it﴾, i.e., a punishment for the sins of those who had passed.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: and it is related from Ikrimah, Mujahid, al-Suddi, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas, something similar to that.

Al-Qurtubi related from Ibn 'Abbas, al-Suddi, al-Farra', and Ibn 'Atiyyah: ﴿for those before it﴾ [means] among the sins of the people, ﴿and those after it﴾ [means] for whoever would do such sins after it. Fakhr al-Din related three opinions:

The first: that the meaning of ﴿those before it and those after it﴾ is: the towns that preceded it, by what they had of knowledge of its news from the earlier books, and those after it.

The second: that by this is meant those present in its vicinity from the towns and nations.

The third: that He made it a punishment for all that they committed before this act and after it. He said: this is the opinion of al-Hasan.

I say: the most preponderant of the opinions is that the meaning of ﴿those before it and those after it﴾ is: those in its vicinity from the towns whose news reaches them, and what befell it, as He said: ﴿And We had already destroyed the towns around you and varied the signs, that they might return﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 27]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease to be struck by a calamity for what they have done, or it will descend close to their home﴾ [al-Ra'd: 31], and He said: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outskirts?﴾ [al-Anbiya': 44]. So He made them a lesson and a deterrent for those in their time, and a lesson for those who come after them through the widely transmitted report about them. Hence He said: ﴿and an admonition for the God-fearing﴾.

* *

Allah's saying, the Exalted: ﴿and an admonition for the God-fearing﴾. Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and an admonition for the God-fearing﴾, those after them until the Day of Resurrection.

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: ﴿and an admonition for the God-fearing﴾ after them, so that they fear the vengeance of Allah and beware of it.

Al-Suddi and 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi said: ﴿and an admonition for the God-fearing﴾, he said: the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ.

I say: the meaning of "admonition" here is a restraining warning, i.e., We made what We inflicted upon these people of severity and punishment in return for what they committed of the prohibitions of Allah, and the stratagems they devised, so let the God-fearing beware of their conduct lest there befall them what befell them, as Imam Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Battah said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah al-Za'farani narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Amr [from Abu Salamah] narrated to us, from Abu Hurayrah: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not commit what the Jews committed, lest you make the prohibitions of Allah lawful through the slightest of stratagems."

This is a good chain, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim was deemed trustworthy by the memorizer Abu Bakr al-Khatib al-Baghdadi, and the rest of its narrators are well known and meet the criteria of authenticity. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 67 (part 1 of 2):

Allah says: Remember, O Children of Israel, My favor upon you in the breaking of custom for you in the matter of the cow, and in clarifying who the killer was through it, and Allah's bringing the murdered man back to life, and His specifying who among them had killed him. [The ruling on camels and sheep: camels are slaughtered by throat-cutting (nahr) and sheep are slaughtered (dhabh). They differed about cows. It was said: they are slaughtered (dhabh). It was said: they are throat-cut (nahr). Slaughter (dhabh) is preferable, due to the text of the Qur'an and because the place of its nahr is close to its dhabh. Ibn al-Mundhir said: "I know of no valid disagreement between what is throat-cut and the throat-cutting of what is slaughtered, except that Malik disliked it. A person may dislike what is not forbidden." Abu 'Abdullah said: "I know that the revelation of the story of the cow to Musa, peace be upon him, concerning the matter of the slain man was before the revelation of the qasamah (the procedure of oaths in cases of homicide) in the Torah."]

Expansion of the story [as Ibn Abi Hatim narrated]:

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: Hisham ibn Hassan informed us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from 'Ubaydah al-Salmani, who said: There was a man from the Children of Israel who was sterile and could not have children, and he had much wealth, and his nephew was his heir. So he killed him, then carried him at night and placed him at the door of a man among them. Then in the morning he accused them of it, until they armed themselves, and some of them rode against others. The people of judgment and reason among them said: "Why should some of you kill others while the Messenger of Allah is among you?" So they came to Musa, peace be upon him, and told him about it. He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to slaughter a cow.﴾ They said: ﴿Do you make a mockery of us?﴾ He said: ﴿I seek refuge in Allah from being among the ignorant.﴾ He said: "Had they not raised objections regarding the cow, any cow would have sufficed for them. But they were strict, so it was made strict for them, until they reached the cow they had been commanded to slaughter, and they found it with a man who had no other cow. He said: 'By Allah, I will not reduce its price below its hide filled with gold.' So they took it for its hide filled with gold and slaughtered it. Then they struck him with part of it, and he rose up. They said: 'Who killed you?' He said: 'This one, his nephew.' Then he fell dead, and he was not given any of his wealth. Thereafter, a killer was not made an heir."

Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from 'Ubaydah, with something similar to that. [Sources: Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/214) and Tafsir al-Tabari (1/337).] And Allah knows best.

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated it in his Tafsir: Yazid ibn Harun informed us, with it.

Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated it in his Tafsir, from Abu Ja'far, who is al-Razi, from Hisham ibn Hassan, with it. Adam ibn Abi Iyas also said in his Tafsir: Abu Ja'far al-Razi informed us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, concerning the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to slaughter a cow.﴾ He said: There was a man from the Children of Israel who was wealthy and had no child, and he had a relative who was his heir. So he killed him in order to inherit from him, then threw him at a crossroads. He came to Musa, peace be upon him, and said: "My relative has been killed, and I am facing a grave matter, and I find no one who can clarify for me who killed him except you, O Prophet of Allah." He said: So Musa called out among the people, saying: "I adjure you by Allah, whoever has knowledge of this, to make it clear to us." There was no knowledge among them. Then the killer approached Musa, peace be upon him, and said to him: "You are the Prophet of Allah, so ask your Lord to make it clear to us." So he asked his Lord, and Allah revealed to him: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to slaughter a cow.﴾ They were astonished at that and said: ﴿Do you make a mockery of us?﴾ He said: ﴿I seek refuge in Allah from being among the ignorant.﴾ They said: ﴿Call upon your Lord for us to make clear to us what it is.﴾ He said: ﴿Indeed, He says it is a cow neither old nor young, but between that.﴾ That is: neither aged (harimah). ﴿Nor young﴾ means: nor small. ﴿Between that﴾ means: midway between the young and the aged. They said: ﴿Call upon your Lord for us to make clear to us what its color is.﴾ He said: ﴿Indeed, He says it is a yellow cow, bright in its color﴾ meaning: pure in its color. ﴿Pleasing to the beholders﴾ meaning: pleasing to those who look at it. They said: ﴿Call upon your Lord for us to make clear to us what it is. Indeed, the cows are alike to us, and we, if Allah wills, will be guided.﴾ He said: ﴿Indeed, He says it is a cow not broken to labor﴾ meaning: not tamed by work, ﴿plowing the earth﴾ meaning: and not one that is tame, plowing the earth, ﴿nor irrigating the field﴾ meaning: nor working at tilling, ﴿sound﴾ meaning: free of defects, ﴿with no blemish in it﴾ meaning: no white spot in it. ﴿They said: Now you have brought the truth.﴾ He said: Had the people, when they were commanded to slaughter a cow, taken any cow and slaughtered it, it would have sufficed for them. But they were strict upon themselves, so it was made strict for them. Had the people not made an exception, saying: ﴿and we, if Allah wills, will be guided﴾, they would never have been guided to it. It has reached us that they did not find the cow described to them except with an old woman who had orphans in her care, and she was their guardian. When she knew that no other cow would be sufficient for them, she multiplied its price upon them. So they came to Musa and informed him that they had not found this description except with so-and-so, and that she had asked them for many times its price. Musa said to them: "Indeed, Allah had made it easy for you, but you were strict upon yourselves. So give her her satisfaction and her judgment." They did so, bought it, and slaughtered it. Then Musa, peace be upon him, commanded them to take a bone of it and strike the slain man with it. They did so, and his soul returned to him. He named for them his killer. Then he returned dead as he had been. The killer, who was the one who had come to Musa and complained to him about the killing, was seized, and Allah killed him for the worst of his deed.

Muhammad ibn Jarir said: Ibn Sa'd (in some manuscripts: Ibn Abi Sa'id) narrated to me: my father narrated to me: my paternal uncle narrated to me: my father narrated to me, from his father [from his grandfather], from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words about the matter of the cow: The reason was that an elderly man from the Children of Israel in the time of Musa, peace be upon him, was rich in wealth, while his brother's sons were poor with no wealth. The elderly man had no child, and his brother's sons were his heirs. They said: "Would that our uncle would die, so we might inherit his wealth." When his life lengthened over them and their uncle did not die, Satan came to them and said: "Would you like to kill your uncle, so you inherit his wealth, and make the people of the city in which you are not impose the blood-money upon them?" That was because there were two cities; they lived in one of them, and when a slain person was killed and thrown between the two cities, the distance between the slain man and the two cities was measured, and whichever of them was closer to him had to pay the blood-money. When Satan made that appealing to them, and their uncle's life lengthened over them, they set out against him and killed him, then they set out and threw him at the gate of the city in which they were not. When the people of the city awoke, the sons of the elderly man's brother came and said: "Our uncle has been killed at the gate of your city, so by Allah you must pay us the blood-money of our uncle." The people of the city said: "We swear by Allah that we did not kill him, nor did we know of any killer, nor did we open the gate of our city since it was closed until we awoke." They went to Musa, peace be upon him. When they came to him, the sons of the elderly man's brother said: "We found our uncle killed at the gate of their city." The people of the city said: "We swear by Allah that we did not kill him, nor did we open the gate of the city from the time we closed it until we awoke." Indeed, Jibril came with the command of the All-Hearing, All-Knowing, to Musa, peace be upon him, and said: "Tell them: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to slaughter a cow﴾, and strike him with part of it."

Al-Suddi said: ﴿And when Musa said to his people: Indeed, Allah commands you to slaughter a cow﴾. He said: There was a man from the Children of Israel who was wealthy in property, and he had a daughter, and he had a needy nephew. The nephew proposed to his uncle's daughter, but the uncle refused to marry her to him. The young man became angry and said: "By Allah, I will kill my uncle, take his wealth, marry his daughter, and eat his blood-money." Then the young man went to him, when merchants from one of the tribes of the Children of Israel had arrived. He said: "O uncle, come with me and take for me from the merchandise of these people, perhaps I may profit from it, for when they see you with me, they will give me something." The uncle set out with the young man at night. When the uncle reached that tribe, the young man killed him, then returned to his family. In the morning he came as if seeking his uncle, as if he did not know where he was, and did not find him. He went toward him and found him with that tribe gathered around him. He seized them and said: "You have killed my uncle, so pay me his blood-money." He began weeping, throwing dust upon his head, and calling out: "O my uncle!" He brought them up to Musa, and he judged against them with the blood-money. They said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, ask Allah for us that He make clear to us who the companion is, so that the perpetrator may be seized. By Allah, his blood-money is trivial to us, but we are ashamed to be disgraced by it." That is when Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when you killed a soul and disputed over it, while Allah would bring forth what you were concealing.﴾ Then Musa, peace be upon him, said to them: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to slaughter a cow.﴾ They said: "We ask you about the slain man and about the one who killed him, and you say: slaughter a cow? Do you mock us!" ﴿He said: I seek refuge in Allah from being among the ignorant.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: Had they taken any cow and slaughtered it, it would have sufficed them. But they were strict and provoked Musa, so Allah made it strict for them. They said: ﴿Call upon your Lord for us to make clear to us what it is.﴾ He said: ﴿Indeed, He says it is a cow neither old nor young, but between that.﴾ Al-Fari�d is the aged one that does not bear, and al-Bikr is the one that has borne only one offspring. Al-'Awan is the middle one, that has borne and whose offspring has borne. ﴿So do what you are commanded.﴾ They said: ﴿Call upon your Lord for us to make clear to us what its color is.﴾ He said: its color is pure. ﴿Pleasing to the beholders﴾ he said: pleasing to those who look at it. They said: ﴿Call upon your Lord for us to make clear to us what it is, indeed the cows are alike to us, and we, if Allah wills, will be guided.﴾ He said: ﴿Indeed, He says it is a cow not broken to labor, plowing the earth nor irrigating the field, sound, with no blemish in it﴾, neither white, nor black, nor reddish. ﴿They said: Now you have brought the truth.﴾ So they searched for it and could not find it.

There was a man among the Children of Israel who was among the most dutiful of people to his father. A man passed by him carrying pearls to sell, while his father was sleeping with the key under his head. The man said to him: "Will you buy this pearl from me for seventy thousand?" The youth said to him: "Stay as you are until my father awakens, and I will take it from you for eighty thousand." The other said: "Wake your father, and it is yours for sixty thousand." So the merchant kept lowering the price for him until it reached thirty thousand, while the other kept raising it, on condition that he wait for his father to awaken, until it reached one hundred thousand. When the merchant insisted, he said: "By Allah, I will not buy it from you for anything, ever." He refused to wake his father. So Allah compensated him for that pearl by giving him that cow. Then the Children of Israel passed by him, seeking the cow, and they saw the cow with him. They asked him to sell it to them for a cow in exchange for a cow, but he refused. They offered him two, and he refused. They kept increasing until they reached ten, and he still refused. They said: "By Allah, we will not leave you until we take it from you." So they took him to Moses, peace be upon him, and said: "O Prophet of Allah, we found it with this man, and he refuses to give it to us, though we have offered him its price." Moses said to him: "Give them your cow." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have more right to my property." He said: "You have spoken the truth." And he said to the people: "Satisfy your companion." So they gave him its weight in gold, but he refused. They doubled for him what they had given, multiplied by its weight, until they gave him its weight in gold ten times over. So he sold it to them and took its price, and they slaughtered it. He said: "Strike him with a piece of it." They struck him with the piece between the shoulders, and he lived. They asked him: "Who killed you?" He said to them: "My nephew." He said: "I would kill him, take his wealth, and marry his daughter." So they took the boy and killed him.

Sunayd said: Hajjaj, who is Ibn Muhammad, narrated to us from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, and Hajjaj, from Abu Ma'shar, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and Muhammad ibn Qays, some of whose narrations entered into the narrations of others, and they said: A tribe of the Children of Israel, when they saw the great prevalence of people's evils, built a city and withdrew from the evils of people. When evening came, they did not leave anyone outside of them without letting him in. When they woke up in the morning, their leader would stand, look, and climb up; if he saw nothing, he would open the city, and they would be among the people until evening. He said: A man from the Children of Israel had a great deal of wealth, and he had no heir other than his brother. His life became prolonged for him, so he killed him in order to inherit from him. Then he carried him and placed him at the city gate, and then he and his companions hid in a place. He said: The head of the city climbed up to the city gate, looked, and saw nothing, so he opened the gate. When he saw the slain man, he closed the gate. The brother of the slain man and his companions called out to him: "Far-fetched! You killed him and then close the gate!" When Moses saw much killing among his companions, the Children of Israel, whenever he saw a slain man among the people, he would seize them, and nearly there was fighting between the brother of the slain man and the people of the city, until both parties took up arms. Then some of them withheld from others, and they came to Moses and told him their situation. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, these people killed a slain man and then closed the gate." The people of the city said: "O Messenger of Allah, you know our withdrawal from the evils, and we built a city, as you have seen, withdrawing from the evils of people. By Allah, we have neither killed nor known of a killer." Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed to him that they should slaughter a cow. So Moses said to them: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to slaughter a cow﴾.

These narrations, all of them, from Ubaydah, Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Suddi and others, contain some differences. It is apparent that they are taken from the books of the Children of Israel, and such material is permissible to relate, but we neither confirm nor deny it. Therefore we do not rely upon them, except what agrees with the truth according to us. And Allah knows best.

Allah, the Exalted, informs about the obstinacy of the Children of Israel and how much they questioned their Messenger. Therefore, when they made things hard for themselves, they were made hard for. Had they slaughtered any cow whatsoever, it would have sufficed them, as Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ubaidah, and others said. But they were strict, so Allah was strict with them. They said: ﴿Call upon your Lord for us to make clear to us what it is﴾, meaning: what is this cow, and what is its description?

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us: 'Atham ibn 'Ali narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Had they taken the least cow, they would have been satisfied with it, but they were strict, so Allah was strict with them."

The chain is sound, and it has been related by more than one narrator from Ibn 'Abbas. Likewise said 'Ubaidah, as-Suddi, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Abu al-'Aliyah and others.

Ibn Jurayj said: 'Ata' said to me: "Had they taken the least cow, it would have sufficed them." Ibn Jurayj said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "They were only commanded to take the least cow, but when they made things hard upon themselves, Allah made things hard upon them. By Allah, had they not made an exception, they would never have been shown it until the end of time."

﴿He said: Indeed, He says it is a cow neither old nor virgin﴾, meaning: neither aged and decrepit, nor young that has not been covered by the stallion, as said by Abu al-'Aliyah, as-Suddi, Mujahid, Ikrimah, 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, Wahb ibn Munabbih, adh-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ibn 'Abbas also said so.

Ad-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿between that﴾ [meaning: half], between the old and the young, and it is the strongest and most beautiful state of animals and cows. Similar has been related from Ikrimah, Mujahid, Abu al-'Aliyah, ar-Rabi' ibn Anas, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, and ad-Dahhak.

As-Suddi said: "'Awan" means the middle-aged one, which has given birth and whose offspring has also given birth.

Hushaym narrated from Juwaybir, from Kathir ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan concerning the cow: it was a wild cow.

Ibn Jurayj said, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas: "Whoever wears a yellow sandal will remain in happiness as long as he wears it, and that is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿yellow, its color is intense, pleasing the beholders﴾." Likewise Mujahid and Wahb ibn Munabbih said it was yellow.

From Ibn 'Umar: it was yellow of hoof. From Sa'id ibn Jubayr: it was yellow of horn and hoof.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Nasr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, Nuh ibn Qays narrated to us, Abu Raja' informed us, from al-Hasan concerning His saying: ﴿a yellow cow, its color is intense﴾, he said: "Black, intensely black."

This is gharib (unusual), and the first (view) is the sound one; for this reason He emphasized its yellowness by saying ﴿its color is intense﴾.

'Atiyyah al-'Awfi said: ﴿its color is intense﴾ means nearly black from the intensity of its yellowness.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿its color is intense﴾: he said, "pure in color." Similar has been related from Abu al-'Aliyah, ar-Rabi' ibn Anas, as-Suddi, al-Hasan, and Qatadah.

Sharik narrated from Maghra', from Ibn 'Umar: ﴿its color is intense﴾, he said: "pure."

Al-'Awfi said in his tafsir, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿its color is intense﴾ means very yellow, nearly turning white from its yellowness.

As-Suddi said: ﴿pleasing the beholders﴾ means it pleases those who look at it. Likewise said Abu al-'Aliyah, Qatadah, and ar-Rabi' ibn Anas.

[In the Torah, it is said that it was red. Perhaps this is a mistake in translation, or as the first (view) said: it was intensely yellow, tending toward red and black, and Allah knows best.]

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: When you look at its skin, it seems to you that the rays of the sun are coming out of its skin.
