Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 70:

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, the cattle are alike to us﴾, meaning: because of their multitude. So specify for us this cow, describe it for us, and clarify it for us ﴿and indeed, we, if Allah wills, will surely be guided﴾, meaning: to it, if you make it clear to us.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Awdi [[In ج and ط: "al-Azdi".]] al-Sufi narrated to us, Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Dawud al-Haddad narrated to us, Surur ibn al-Mughirah al-Wasiti narrated to us, the nephew of Mansur ibn Zadhan, from 'Abbad ibn Mansur, from al-Hasan, from Abu Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Had the Children of Israel not said: ﴿And indeed, we, if Allah wills, will surely be guided﴾, they would never have been given (the cow). But they made an exception (by saying 'if Allah wills')." [[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/223).]]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his tafsir by another route, from Surur ibn al-Mughirah, from [[In ج، ط، ب: "ibn".]] Zadhan, from 'Abbad ibn Mansur, from al-Hasan, from the hadith of Abu Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Had the Children of Israel not said: ﴿And indeed, we, if Allah wills, will surely be guided﴾, they would never have been given it. And if they had taken any cow at random and slaughtered it, it would have sufficed them. But they made it strict, so Allah made it strict for them." [[The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said: "In it is 'Abbad ibn Mansur, who is weak."]]

This is a strange (gharib) hadith by this route, and at best it may be a saying of Abu Hurayrah, as a similar report from al-Suddi was mentioned earlier. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 71:

﴿He said: "Indeed, He says it is a cow neither broken to plough the earth nor to water the tilth."﴾ That is: it is not trained for ploughing, nor prepared for irrigating with the water-wheel (sāniyah); rather, it is noble, good-looking and handsome. ﴿Sound, with no blemish﴾, meaning: free of defect. ﴿There is no mark on it﴾, meaning: there is no colour in it other than its own colour.

Qatadah, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, said, reported by 'Abd al-Razzaq: ﴿Sound﴾ means: it has no defect. Abu al-'Aliyah and al-Rabi' said likewise. Mujahid said: ﴿Sound﴾ means free of marks (shiyah).

'Ata' al-Khurasani said: ﴿Sound﴾ means of sound legs and form. ﴿There is no mark on it﴾: Mujahid said: no white and no black. Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Rabi', al-Hasan and Qatadah said: there is no white in it. 'Ata' al-Khurasani said: ﴿There is no mark on it﴾, meaning its colour is uniform, entirely one colour. Similar views are also reported from 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi, Wahb ibn Munabbih and Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid. As-Suddi said: ﴿There is no mark on it﴾ means no white, no black and no red. All these statements are close in meaning. [Some of them claimed that the meaning of His words, ﴿It is a cow neither broken﴾, is that it is not trained by work; then He resumed, saying: ﴿to plough the earth﴾, meaning it is worked for ploughing, but it does not water the tilth. This is weak, because it explains "unbroken" as "not trained by work" and then explains it as "does not plough the earth nor water the tilth," as al-Qurtubi and others affirmed.] ﴿They said: "Now you have brought the truth."﴾ Qatadah said: "Now you have made it clear to us." 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "Rather, before that—by Allah, [and Allah knows best]—the truth had already come to them."

﴿So they slaughtered it, though they almost did not do it﴾. Ad-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, said: "They almost did not do it, and that was not what they wanted, for they wished not to slaughter it."

That is: despite this clarification, these questions, answers and explanation, they did not slaughter it except after great difficulty. In this there is a rebuke of them, for their aim was nothing but obstinacy; therefore they "almost did not slaughter it."

Muhammad ibn Ka'b and Muhammad ibn Qays said: ﴿So they slaughtered it, though they almost did not do it﴾ because of its high price.

But this is open to question, for the high price of it is only attested through the transmissions of the Children of Israel, as already mentioned from the narrations of Abu al-'Aliyah and as-Suddi, and al-'Awfi related it from Ibn 'Abbas. 'Ubaydah, Mujahid, Wahb ibn Munabbih, Abu al-'Aliyah and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: they bought it for a large amount of wealth. There is disagreement on this, and other figures have been mentioned for its price. 'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, Muhammad ibn Suqah told me, from 'Ikrimah, who said: its price was no more than three dinars. [Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (1/71).] This is a good chain from 'Ikrimah, and it is apparent that he too took it from the People of the Scripture.

Ibn Jarir said: Others said: they almost did not do it for fear of exposure, lest Allah reveal the killer of the slain man over whom they disputed. He did not attribute this to anyone by chain, and then he preferred that the correct view is that they almost did not do it because of the high cost of the cow and for fear of exposure. But this is open to question; rather, the correct view—and Allah knows best—is what preceded from the narration of ad-Dahhak from Ibn 'Abbas, according to what we have explained. And success is from Allah.

Issue: This verse has been cited to define the attributes of this cow, so that it became specific, or that its description after being general was completed, as evidence for the validity of salam (advance sale with deferred delivery) in animals, as is the position of Malik, al-Awza'i, al-Layth, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and the majority of scholars, earlier and later, based on what is established in the two Sahihs from the Prophet ﷺ: "A woman should not describe another woman to her husband as if he were looking at her." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5241.] Also, the Prophet ﷺ described the camels of blood-money for accidental killing and quasi-deliberate killing by the attributes mentioned in the hadith. Abu Hanifah, al-Thawri and the Kufans said: salam is not valid in animals, because their conditions cannot be controlled. The same view is reported from Ibn Mas'ud, Huzayfah ibn al-Yaman, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah and others.

Al-Bukhari said: "*Fa-dara'tum* (﴿فَادَّارَأْتُمْ﴾) means you disputed." Mujahid also said this, as transmitted by Ibn Abi Hatim, from his father, from Abu Hudhayfa, from Shibl, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, that he said regarding the words of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿And when you killed a soul and disputed concerning it﴾, that it means "you disagreed."

ʿAta al-Khurasani and al-Dahhak said: "you contended with one another over it." Ibn Jurayj said regarding ﴿And when you killed a soul and disputed concerning it﴾: "Some of them said, 'You killed him,' while others said, 'No, you killed him.'" Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said the same.

As for ﴿Allah will bring forth that which you were concealing﴾, Mujahid said: "What you were hiding." Ibn Abi Hatim said: Amr ibn Muslim al-Basri narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Tufayl al-Abdi narrated to us, Sadaqa ibn Rustum narrated to us, I heard al-Musayyab ibn Rafi say: "No man does a good deed in seven houses but Allah makes it manifest, and no man does an evil deed in seven houses but Allah makes it manifest. The confirmation of this is in the words of Allah: ﴿Allah will bring forth that which you were concealing. So We said, 'Strike him with a part of it'﴾." This "part," whatever it was from the limbs of that cow, is the source of the miracle.

The breaking of the customary order through it is real, and its specific identity was determined in reality. Had specifying it benefited us in matters of religion or of this world, Allah would have made it clear to us. But He left it vague, and no sound report has come from an infallible source explaining it [in another copy: "from an infallible source narrated to us its explanation"]. So we leave it vague as Allah left it vague.

For this reason Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, Affan ibn Muslim narrated to us, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The companions of the cow of the Children of Israel sought it for forty years until they found it with a man who had a cow that pleased him. They began offering him gold for it, but he refused, until they gave him a skin filled with dinars. They slaughtered it and struck him (meaning the slain man) with a piece of it. He rose, his veins gushing blood, and they asked him, 'Who killed you?' He said, 'So-and-so killed me.'"

Al-Hasan and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam likewise said: "It was struck with part of it."

In a report from Ibn Abbas: "They struck him with the bone that is next to the cartilage."

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, saying: Ayyub said, from Ibn Sirin, from Ubayda: "They struck the slain man with part of its flesh." Ma'mar said: Qatada said: "They struck him with a piece of its thigh, and he lived, and said, 'So-and-so killed me.'"

Abu Usama said, from al-Nadr ibn Arabi, from Ikrima, regarding ﴿So We said, "Strike him with a part of it"﴾: "He struck him with its thigh, and he rose and said, 'So-and-so killed me.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim said: "Similar reports have been narrated from Mujahid and Qatada."

al-Suddi said: "They struck him with the piece between the two shoulders, and he lived. They asked him, and he said, 'My nephew killed me.'"

Abu al-ʿAliya said: "Musa (peace be upon him) commanded them to take a bone from its bones and strike the slain man with it. They did so, and his soul returned to him. He named his killer for them, then he went back to being dead as he had been."

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "They struck him with some of its limbs." [It was said: with its tongue; it was said: with the tip of its tail.]

* *

As for His words, ﴿Thus Allah brings the dead to life﴾, that is: they struck him and he came to life. Exalted is He drew attention to His power and His bringing the dead to life through what they witnessed concerning the slain man. Blessed and Exalted is He made that act a proof for them regarding the Resurrection, and a means of settling the dispute and corruption [in another copy: "and enmity"] that existed among them. Allah, Exalted is He, mentioned in this surah five instances of His bringing the dead to life: ﴿Then We resurrected you after your death﴾ [al-Baqarah: 56]. And this story, and the story of those who left their homes in their thousands fearing death, and the story of the one who passed by a town fallen upon its roofs, and the story of Ibrahim and the four birds.

By bringing the earth to life after its death, Exalted is He drew attention to the restoration of bodies after they have become dust, as Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Shu'ba narrated to us, Ya'la ibn Ata informed me, he said: I heard Waki' ibn Udus narrate from Abu Razin al-ʿUqayli, who said: "I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, how does Allah bring the dead to life?' He said, 'Have you not passed by a barren valley, then passed by it green?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'That is how the resurrection is,' or he said, 'That is how Allah brings the dead to life.'" The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿And a sign for them is the dead earth which We have brought to life and brought forth from it grain, of which they eat. And We placed therein gardens of date palms and grapevines, and We caused springs to gush forth within it, that they may eat of its fruit, and of what their hands have made. Will they not then be grateful?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 33–35].

Issue: The reasoning of the Maliki school regarding the statement of the wounded man, "So-and-so killed me," as a *lawth* (a strong presumptive indication, i.e., a circumstantial sign that makes a claim plausible), is supported by this story. When the slain man was brought back to life and was asked who killed him, and he said, "So-and-so killed me," that was accepted from him, because at that moment he would only report the truth, and he would not be suspected in that situation. They supported this with the hadith of Anas: that a Jew killed a girl for her silver anklets, crushing her head between two stones. It was said to her, "Who did this to you? So-and-so? So-and-so?" until the Jew was named, and she nodded her head. The Jew was seized, and he was pressed until he confessed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered that his head be crushed between two stones. [Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 6885.] According to Malik, if there is a *lawth*, the heirs of the slain man swear an oath called *qasama* (a collective oath by the heirs in cases of suspected murder). The majority (*jumhur*) disagreed on this and did not consider the slain man's statement to be a *lawth*.

Al-Bukhari said: "*Fa-dara'tum* (﴿فَادَّارَأْتُمْ﴾) means you disputed." Mujahid also said this, as transmitted by Ibn Abi Hatim, from his father, from Abu Hudhayfa, from Shibl, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, that he said regarding the words of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿And when you killed a soul and disputed concerning it﴾, that it means "you disagreed."

ʿAta al-Khurasani and al-Dahhak said: "you contended with one another over it." Ibn Jurayj said regarding ﴿And when you killed a soul and disputed concerning it﴾: "Some of them said, 'You killed him,' while others said, 'No, you killed him.'" Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said the same.

As for ﴿Allah will bring forth that which you were concealing﴾, Mujahid said: "What you were hiding." Ibn Abi Hatim said: Amr ibn Muslim al-Basri narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Tufayl al-Abdi narrated to us, Sadaqa ibn Rustum narrated to us, I heard al-Musayyab ibn Rafi say: "No man does a good deed in seven houses but Allah makes it manifest, and no man does an evil deed in seven houses but Allah makes it manifest. The confirmation of this is in the words of Allah: ﴿Allah will bring forth that which you were concealing. So We said, 'Strike him with a part of it'﴾." This "part," whatever it was from the limbs of that cow, is the source of the miracle.

The breaking of the customary order through it is real, and its specific identity was determined in reality. Had specifying it benefited us in matters of religion or of this world, Allah would have made it clear to us. But He left it vague, and no sound report has come from an infallible source explaining it [in another copy: "from an infallible source narrated to us its explanation"]. So we leave it vague as Allah left it vague.

For this reason Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, Affan ibn Muslim narrated to us, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The companions of the cow of the Children of Israel sought it for forty years until they found it with a man who had a cow that pleased him. They began offering him gold for it, but he refused, until they gave him a skin filled with dinars. They slaughtered it and struck him (meaning the slain man) with a piece of it. He rose, his veins gushing blood, and they asked him, 'Who killed you?' He said, 'So-and-so killed me.'"

Al-Hasan and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam likewise said: "It was struck with part of it."

In a report from Ibn Abbas: "They struck him with the bone that is next to the cartilage."

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, saying: Ayyub said, from Ibn Sirin, from Ubayda: "They struck the slain man with part of its flesh." Ma'mar said: Qatada said: "They struck him with a piece of its thigh, and he lived, and said, 'So-and-so killed me.'"

Abu Usama said, from al-Nadr ibn Arabi, from Ikrima, regarding ﴿So We said, "Strike him with a part of it"﴾: "He struck him with its thigh, and he rose and said, 'So-and-so killed me.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim said: "Similar reports have been narrated from Mujahid and Qatada."

al-Suddi said: "They struck him with the piece between the two shoulders, and he lived. They asked him, and he said, 'My nephew killed me.'"

Abu al-ʿAliya said: "Musa (peace be upon him) commanded them to take a bone from its bones and strike the slain man with it. They did so, and his soul returned to him. He named his killer for them, then he went back to being dead as he had been."

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "They struck him with some of its limbs." [It was said: with its tongue; it was said: with the tip of its tail.]

* *

As for His words, ﴿Thus Allah brings the dead to life﴾, that is: they struck him and he came to life. Exalted is He drew attention to His power and His bringing the dead to life through what they witnessed concerning the slain man. Blessed and Exalted is He made that act a proof for them regarding the Resurrection, and a means of settling the dispute and corruption [in another copy: "and enmity"] that existed among them. Allah, Exalted is He, mentioned in this surah five instances of His bringing the dead to life: ﴿Then We resurrected you after your death﴾ [al-Baqarah: 56]. And this story, and the story of those who left their homes in their thousands fearing death, and the story of the one who passed by a town fallen upon its roofs, and the story of Ibrahim and the four birds.

By bringing the earth to life after its death, Exalted is He drew attention to the restoration of bodies after they have become dust, as Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Shu'ba narrated to us, Ya'la ibn Ata informed me, he said: I heard Waki' ibn Udus narrate from Abu Razin al-ʿUqayli, who said: "I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, how does Allah bring the dead to life?' He said, 'Have you not passed by a barren valley, then passed by it green?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'That is how the resurrection is,' or he said, 'That is how Allah brings the dead to life.'" The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿And a sign for them is the dead earth which We have brought to life and brought forth from it grain, of which they eat. And We placed therein gardens of date palms and grapevines, and We caused springs to gush forth within it, that they may eat of its fruit, and of what their hands have made. Will they not then be grateful?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 33–35].

Issue: The reasoning of the Maliki school regarding the statement of the wounded man, "So-and-so killed me," as a *lawth* (a strong presumptive indication, i.e., a circumstantial sign that makes a claim plausible), is supported by this story. When the slain man was brought back to life and was asked who killed him, and he said, "So-and-so killed me," that was accepted from him, because at that moment he would only report the truth, and he would not be suspected in that situation. They supported this with the hadith of Anas: that a Jew killed a girl for her silver anklets, crushing her head between two stones. It was said to her, "Who did this to you? So-and-so? So-and-so?" until the Jew was named, and she nodded her head. The Jew was seized, and he was pressed until he confessed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered that his head be crushed between two stones. [Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 6885.] According to Malik, if there is a *lawth*, the heirs of the slain man swear an oath called *qasama* (a collective oath by the heirs in cases of suspected murder). The majority (*jumhur*) disagreed on this and did not consider the slain man's statement to be a *lawth*.

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, commentary on Surah 2, verse 74:

Allah, the Exalted, says, rebuking the Children of Israel and reproaching them for what they witnessed of the signs of Allah, the Exalted, and His giving life to the dead: ﴿Then your hearts hardened after that﴾ all of it, ﴿so they became like stones﴾ that never soften at all. For this reason Allah forbade the believers from being like them, saying: ﴿Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should humble themselves to the remembrance of Allah and to what has been revealed of the truth, and that they should not be like those who were given the Scripture before, and the term seemed long to them, so their hearts hardened? And many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-Hadid: 16].

Al-'Awfi said in his *Tafsir*, from Ibn 'Abbas: When the slain man was struck with part of the cow, he sat up, more alive than he had ever been. He was asked, "Who killed you?" He said, "My nephews killed me." Then he died again. His nephews, when he died, said, "By Allah, we did not kill him." So they denied the truth after they had seen it. Then Allah said: ﴿Then your hearts hardened after that﴾, meaning: the sons of my brother the shaykh. ﴿So they became like stones or even harder in hardness.﴾ So the hearts of the Children of Israel, with the passage of a long time, became hard and far from admonition after they had witnessed the signs and miracles. They were, in their hardness, like stones that cannot be softened, or even harder than stones. For among stones there are those from which flowing rivers burst forth, and among them are those that split and water comes out of them, though it does not flow, and among them are those that fall from the top of a mountain out of fear of Allah. In each there is a kind of perception suited to it, as He said: ﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him. There is nothing that does not glorify His praise, but you do not understand their glorification. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving﴾ [al-Isra': 44].

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid, that he used to say: Every stone from which water gushes, or which splits and releases water, or which falls from the top of a mountain, does so out of fear of Allah. The Qur'an was revealed with this meaning.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding: ﴿And indeed, among stones are those from which rivers burst forth, and indeed, among them are those that split and water comes out of them, and indeed, among them are those that fall out of fear of Allah﴾. That is: indeed, among stones are those softer than your hearts in regard to the truth to which you are called. ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what you do.﴾

[Abu 'Ali al-Jubba'i said in his *Tafsir*: ﴿And indeed, among them are those that fall out of fear of Allah﴾ refers to the falling of hail from the clouds. Al-Qadi al-Baqillani said: This is a distant interpretation. Fakhr al-Din al-Razi followed him in considering it distant, and they were right, for this is a departure from the apparent wording without evidence. And Allah knows best.] [[Addition from ج، ط، ب، أ، و.]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Hisham ibn 'Ammar told us, al-Hakam ibn Hisham al-Thaqafi told us, Yahya ibn Abi Talib told me, meaning Yahya ibn Ya'qub, regarding His saying: ﴿And indeed, among stones are those from which rivers burst forth﴾. He said: It is abundant weeping. ﴿And indeed, among them are those that split and water comes out of them﴾. He said: It is little weeping. ﴿And indeed, among them are those that fall out of fear of Allah﴾. He said: It is weeping of the heart, without tears of the eye.

Some have claimed that this is of the category of metaphor (*majaz*), namely the attribution of humility to stones, as the act of wanting was attributed to a wall in His saying: ﴿that wants to collapse﴾. Al-Razi, al-Qurtubi and other imams said: There is no need for this, for Allah, the Exalted, creates this attribute in them, as in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to bear it and were apprehensive of it﴾ [al-Ahzab: 72], and His saying: ﴿And the star and the tree prostrate﴾ [al-Rahman: 6], and ﴿Have they not considered what things Allah has created, whose shadows incline﴾ [al-Nahl: 48], and ﴿They said: We come willingly﴾ [Fussilat: 11], and ﴿If We had sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain﴾ [al-Hashr: 21], and ﴿They will say to their skins: Why have you testified against us? They will say: Allah has made us speak﴾ [Fussilat: 21]. In the authentic collection (*Sahih*) there is: "This is a mountain that loves us and we love it." Also the trunk's yearning, whose report is widely transmitted. In *Sahih Muslim* there is: "Indeed I know a stone in Makkah that used to greet me before I was sent as a prophet. Indeed I know it now." And regarding the Black Stone, it is said that it will bear witness for whoever touched it with truth on the Day of Resurrection, and other things of this kind.

Al-Qurtubi relayed an opinion that the "aw" here is for choice (*takhyir*), meaning: like this or like that, as in "Sit with al-Hasan or Ibn Sirin." Al-Razi also related this in his *Tafsir* and added another opinion: that it is for ambiguity relative to the addressee, like the saying of one who says, "I ate bread or dates," while knowing which one he ate. Another said: It means like the saying, "Eat something sweet or sour," i.e., he does not go beyond either of them. That is: your hearts became like stones or harder than them in hardness, and do not go beyond either of these two things. And Allah knows best.

**Note:**

The scholars of Arabic grammar differed regarding the meaning of His saying: ﴿so they became like stones or even harder in hardness﴾, after agreeing that it cannot be for doubt (*shakk*). Some said: "Aw" here means "wa" (and). Its implied sense: so they became like stones and even harder in hardness, as in His saying: ﴿And do not obey from among them a sinner or a disbeliever﴾ [al-Insan: 24], and as al-Nabighah al-Dhubyani said:

She said, "If only this dove were ours,
to our dove, or half of it, then ..."

meaning: "and half of it." This was said by Ibn Jarir. Jarir ibn 'Atiyyah said:

He attained the caliphate, or it was for him a decree,
as Musa came to his Lord at an appointed measure.

Ibn Jarir said: That is, he attained the caliphate, and it was a decree for him.

Al-Qurtubi related an opinion that it is for choice in its meaning, "like this or like that," as in "Sit with al-Hasan or Ibn Sirin." Fakhr al-Din likewise related it in his *Tafsir* and added another opinion, which is that it is for ambiguity relative to the addressee, like the saying of one who says, "I ate bread or dates," while he knows which one he ate. And another opinion, that it means the saying of one who says, "My food is sweet or sour," i.e., it does not go beyond either of them: that is, your hearts in their hardness became like stones or harder than them, not departing from either of these two things. And Allah knows best.

Others said: "Aw" here means "bal" (rather). Its implied sense: so they are like stones, rather harder in hardness, as in His saying: ﴿When a group of them fear people as they fear Allah or with even greater fear﴾ [al-Nisa': 77], ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more﴾ [al-Saffat: 147], and ﴿And he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or nearer﴾ [al-Najm: 9]. Others said: The meaning of that, ﴿so they became like stones or even harder in hardness﴾, is "in your estimation." Ibn Jarir related this.

Others said: The intended meaning is ambiguity toward the addressee, as Abu al-Aswad said:

I love Muhammad with a strong love,
and 'Abbas, Hamzah, and the executor ('Ali),
If their love is right guidance, I will attain it,
and I am not mistaken if it is error.

Ibn Jarir said: They said: There is no doubt that Abu al-Aswad was not doubtful that the love of those he named is right guidance, but he made it ambiguous to the one he addressed. He said: It was related from Abu al-Aswad that when he recited these verses he was asked, "Did you doubt?" He said, "Certainly not, by Allah." Then he cited the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And indeed, we or you are surely upon guidance or in clear error﴾ [Saba': 24], and said: Would one who conveys this be doubtful about who among them is guided and who is in error?

Others said: The meaning of that is: Your hearts do not depart from one of these two examples: either they are like stones in hardness, or they are harder than them in hardness.

Ibn Jarir said: The meaning of this interpretation is: some of them are like stones in hardness, and some are harder than stones in hardness. Ibn Jarir preferred this, along with other interpretations.

I say: This last opinion is similar to His saying: ﴿Their likeness is that of one who kindled a fire﴾ [al-Baqarah: 17], together with His saying: ﴿or like a rainstorm from the sky﴾ [al-Baqarah: 19], and His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain﴾ [al-Nur: 39], together with His saying: ﴿or like darknesses in a deep sea﴾ [al-Nur: 40], etc. That is: some of them are like this, and some of them are like that. And Allah knows best.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim told us, Muhammad ibn Ayyub told us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi al-Thalj told us, 'Ali ibn Hafs told us, Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hatib told us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not multiply speech without the remembrance of Allah, for multiplying speech without the remembrance of Allah is hardness of the heart, and indeed the people farthest from Allah is the hard-hearted one."

It was related by al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Asceticism (*Zuhd*) of his *Jami'*, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi al-Thalj, companion of Imam Ahmad, with this chain. And by another route, from Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn Hatib, with it. He said: It is gharib (singular); we do not know it except from the hadith of Ibrahim. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2411. Imam Malik also cited it in the *Muwatta'* (2/986) as a mursal report from 'Isa (peace be upon him).]

[Al-Bazzar related from Anas, as a marfu' report: "Four things are of wretchedness: dryness of the eye, hardness of the heart, long hope, and greed for the world."] [[Addition from ج، ط، ب، أ، و.]]

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Do you hope, [O believers], that they will believe you?﴾ That is, that they will submit to you in obedience — this misguided sect of the Jews, whose forefathers witnessed clear signs, witnessing what they witnessed, and then their hearts hardened after that. ﴿And there was a party of them who heard the words of Allah, then they distorted them﴾ — that is, they interpreted them other than their proper interpretation — ﴿after they had understood them﴾ — that is, they comprehended them clearly — and yet they opposed them knowingly. ﴿While they knew﴾ that they were in error in what they went to of distorting and interpreting it? This situation is similar to His saying: ﴿So for their breaking their covenant, We cursed them and made their hearts hard; they distort words from their places﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 13].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad related to me, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: Then Allah the Exalted said to His Prophet ﷺ and to those believers with him, despairing them of them: ﴿Do you hope that they will believe you, while a party of them used to hear the words of Allah﴾. The saying ﴿they hear the words of Allah﴾ does not refer to hearing the Torah; all of them had heard it. Rather, it refers to those who asked Moses to show them his Lord, and the thunderbolt seized them for it.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: It was related to me by some of the people of knowledge that they said to Moses: "O Moses, a barrier has been placed between us and seeing Allah the Exalted, so let us hear His speech when He speaks to you." Moses requested that of his Lord the Exalted, and He said: "Yes. Command them to purify themselves, and let them purify their garments and fast." They did so. Then he went out with them until they came to the mount (al-Tur). When the cloud enveloped them, Moses commanded them to prostrate, and they fell prostrate. His Lord the Exalted spoke to him, and they heard His speech commanding and forbidding them, until they comprehended from it what they had heard. Then he returned with them to the Children of Israel. When they came to them, a party of them distorted what he had commanded them, and they said, when Moses said to the Children of Israel: "Indeed Allah has commanded you such and such" — that party whom Allah mentioned said: "He only said such and such, contrary to what Allah the Mighty and Majestic said to them." They are the ones whom Allah meant for His Messenger ﷺ.

Al-Suddi said concerning ﴿And there was a party of them who heard the words of Allah, then they distorted them﴾: it is the Torah; they distorted it.

What al-Suddi mentioned is more general than what Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Ishaq mentioned, although Ibn Jarir chose it for the apparent context. For hearing the words of Allah does not necessarily mean that it comes directly from Him, as the Kalim (the one who spoke with Allah), Musa ibn 'Imran, peace be upon him, heard it. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if any of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him protection until he hears the words of Allah﴾ [at-Tawbah: 6] — that is, conveyed to him. Therefore Qatadah said concerning His saying: ﴿Then they distort it after they had understood it, while they knew﴾: They are the Jews, who used to hear the words of Allah, then distort them after they had understood and retained them.

Mujahid said: Those who distort it and those who conceal it are their scholars.

Abu al-'Aliyah said: They deliberately went to what Allah had revealed in their book concerning the description of Muhammad ﷺ, and distorted it from its places.

Al-Suddi said concerning ﴿while they knew﴾: that is, that they had committed sin. Ibn Wahb said: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: ﴿they hear the words of Allah, then they distort it﴾: It is the Torah which Allah revealed to them; they distort it, making the lawful in it unlawful and the unlawful in it lawful, the truth in it falsehood and the falsehood in it truth. When the one with the right comes to them with a bribe, they produce for him the Book of Allah, and when the one who is in falsehood comes to them with a bribe, they produce for him that same book, and he is in the right according to it. If anyone comes to them asking about something that has no truth in it, no bribe, and nothing, they command him to the truth. So Allah said to them: ﴿Do you command the people to righteousness and forget yourselves, while you recite the Scripture? Will you not then reason?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 44].

* *

His saying: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"﴾ — the verse.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad related to us, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"﴾ — that is, in your companion, the Messenger of Allah, but only to you specifically. ﴿And when they are alone with one another, they say﴾: Do not tell the Arabs of this, for you used to seek victory over them through it, and so it was from them. Then Allah revealed: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"; and when they are alone with one another, they say, "Do you tell them what Allah has disclosed to you so that they may argue with you about it before your Lord?"﴾ — that is, you acknowledge that he is a Prophet, and you know that He has taken the covenant from you to follow him, and he informs them that he is the Prophet whom we were awaiting and whom we find in our book. Deny him and do not acknowledge him. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Do they not know that Allah knows what they conceal and what they declare?﴾

Al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas: It means the hypocrites among the Jews, who, whenever they met the companions of Muhammad ﷺ, said: "We believe."

Al-Suddi said: These are people from among the Jews who believed and then became hypocrites. Likewise said al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Qatadah, and others among the early and later scholars. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam even said, as related by Ibn Wahb from him: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said: "Let no one enter upon us through the outskirts of Madinah except a believer." Their leaders among the people of disbelief and hypocrisy said: "Go and say, 'We believe,' and disbelieve when you return to us." So they would come to Madinah in the early morning and return to them after the afternoon prayer. And he recited the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And a party of the People of the Book said, "Believe in what has been revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day, and disbelieve at its end, that perhaps they will return."﴾ [Al 'Imran: 72]. They used to say, when they entered Madinah, "We are Muslims," in order to learn the news of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his affair. When they returned, they returned to disbelief. When Allah informed His Prophet ﷺ of this, He cut that off from them, and they no longer entered. The believers used to think that they were believers, so they would say: "Did Allah not say to you such and such?" And they would say: "Yes." But when they returned to their people [meaning the leaders], they said: ﴿Do you tell them what Allah has disclosed to you?﴾ — the verse. [Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (2/254) from Yunus from Ibn Wahb.]

Abu al-'Aliyah said: ﴿Do you tell them what Allah has disclosed to you?﴾ means: what Allah revealed to you in your Book concerning the description of Muhammad ﷺ.

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿Do you tell them what Allah has disclosed to you so that they may argue with you about it before your Lord?﴾ He said: They used to say: "A Prophet will come." So some of them were alone with others and said: ﴿Do you tell them what Allah has disclosed to you?﴾ [Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (1/71).]

Another opinion regarding the meaning of "disclosed" (fath): Ibn Jurayj said: Al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah related to me, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿Do you tell them what Allah has disclosed to you?﴾ He said: The Prophet ﷺ stood on the day of Qurayzah beneath their fortresses and said: "O brothers of the apes and the swine, and worshippers of the Taghut!" They said: "Who told Muhammad about this matter? This statement came only from you." ﴿Do you tell them what Allah has disclosed to you?﴾ — by what Allah judged, for the victory, so that it would be a proof against you. Ibn Jurayj said, from Mujahid: This was when he sent 'Ali to them, and they harmed Muhammad ﷺ.

Al-Suddi said: ﴿Do you tell them what Allah has disclosed to you?﴾ — of the punishment — ﴿so that they may argue with you about it before your Lord?﴾ These are people from among the Jews who believed and then became hypocrites, and they would tell the believers among the Arabs about what they had been punished with. So some of them said to others: "Do you tell them what Allah has disclosed to you?" — of the punishment — so that they would say: "We are more beloved to Allah than you, and more honoured by Allah than you."

'Ata' al-Khurasani said: ﴿Do you tell them what Allah has disclosed to you?﴾ means: what Allah has decreed for you and against you.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: These were the Jews; when they met those who believed, they said, "We believe," and when some of them were alone with others, some of them said: "Do not tell the companions of Muhammad of what Allah has disclosed to you of what is in your Book, lest they argue with you about it before your Lord and overcome you."

* *

His saying: ﴿Do they not know that Allah knows what they conceal and what they declare?﴾ Abu al-'Aliyah said: It means what they concealed of their disbelief in Muhammad ﷺ and their denial of him, while they find him written among them. Likewise said Qatadah.

Al-Hasan said: ﴿that Allah knows what they conceal﴾ — He said: What they concealed was that whenever they turned away from the companions of Muhammad ﷺ and were alone with one another, they agreed that none of them should inform the companions of Muhammad ﷺ of what Allah had disclosed to them of what is in their Book, fearing that the companions of Muhammad ﷺ would argue with them about what is in their Book before their Lord. ﴿And what they declare﴾ means: when they said to the companions of Muhammad ﷺ, "We believe." Likewise said Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Rabi', and Qatadah.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Do you hope, [O believers], that they will believe you?﴾ That is, that they will submit to you in obedience — this misguided sect of the Jews, whose forefathers witnessed clear signs, witnessing what they witnessed, and then their hearts hardened after that. ﴿And there was a party of them who heard the words of Allah, then they distorted them﴾ — that is, they interpreted them other than their proper interpretation — ﴿after they had understood them﴾ — that is, they comprehended them clearly — and yet they opposed them knowingly. ﴿While they knew﴾ that they were in error in what they went to of distorting and interpreting it? This situation is similar to His saying: ﴿So for their breaking their covenant, We cursed them and made their hearts hard; they distort words from their places﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 13].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad related to me, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: Then Allah the Exalted said to His Prophet ﷺ and to those believers with him, despairing them of them: ﴿Do you hope that they will believe you, while a party of them used to hear the words of Allah﴾. The saying ﴿they hear the words of Allah﴾ does not refer to hearing the Torah; all of them had heard it. Rather, it refers to those who asked Moses to show them his Lord, and the thunderbolt seized them for it.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: It was related to me by some of the people of knowledge that they said to Moses: "O Moses, a barrier has been placed between us and seeing Allah the Exalted, so let us hear His speech when He speaks to you." Moses requested that of his Lord the Exalted, and He said: "Yes. Command them to purify themselves, and let them purify their garments and fast." They did so. Then he went out with them until they came to the mount (al-Tur). When the cloud enveloped them, Moses commanded them to prostrate, and they fell prostrate. His Lord the Exalted spoke to him, and they heard His speech commanding and forbidding them, until they comprehended from it what they had heard. Then he returned with them to the Children of Israel. When they came to them, a party of them distorted what he had commanded them, and they said, when Moses said to the Children of Israel: "Indeed Allah has commanded you such and such" — that party whom Allah mentioned said: "He only said such and such, contrary to what Allah the Mighty and Majestic said to them." They are the ones whom Allah meant for His Messenger ﷺ.

Al-Suddi said concerning ﴿And there was a party of them who heard the words of Allah, then they distorted them﴾: it is the Torah; they distorted it.

What al-Suddi mentioned is more general than what Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Ishaq mentioned, although Ibn Jarir chose it for the apparent context. For hearing the words of Allah does not necessarily mean that it comes directly from Him, as the Kalim (the one who spoke with Allah), Musa ibn 'Imran, peace be upon him, heard it. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if any of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him protection until he hears the words of Allah﴾ [at-Tawbah: 6] — that is, conveyed to him. Therefore Qatadah said concerning His saying: ﴿Then they distort it after they had understood it, while they knew﴾: They are the Jews, who used to hear the words of Allah, then distort them after they had understood and retained them.

Mujahid said: Those who distort it and those who conceal it are their scholars.

Abu al-'Aliyah said: They deliberately went to what Allah had revealed in their book concerning the description of Muhammad ﷺ, and distorted it from its places.

Al-Suddi said concerning ﴿while they knew﴾: that is, that they had committed sin. Ibn Wahb said: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: ﴿they hear the words of Allah, then they distort it﴾: It is the Torah which Allah revealed to them; they distort it, making the lawful in it unlawful and the unlawful in it lawful, the truth in it falsehood and the falsehood in it truth. When the one with the right comes to them with a bribe, they produce for him the Book of Allah, and when the one who is in falsehood comes to them with a bribe, they produce for him that same book, and he is in the right according to it. If anyone comes to them asking about something that has no truth in it, no bribe, and nothing, they command him to the truth. So Allah said to them: ﴿Do you command the people to righteousness and forget yourselves, while you recite the Scripture? Will you not then reason?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 44].

* *

His saying: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"﴾ — the verse.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad related to us, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"﴾ — that is, in your companion, the Messenger of Allah, but only to you specifically. ﴿And when they are alone with one another, they say﴾: Do not tell the Arabs of this, for you used to seek victory over them through it, and so it was from them. Then Allah revealed: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"; and when they are alone with one another, they say, "Do you tell them what Allah has disclosed to you so that they may argue with you about it before your Lord?"﴾ — that is, you acknowledge that he is a Prophet, and you know that He has taken the covenant from you to follow him, and he informs them that he is the Prophet whom we were awaiting and whom we find in our book. Deny him and do not acknowledge him. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Do they not know that Allah knows what they conceal and what they declare?﴾

Al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas: It means the hypocrites among the Jews, who, whenever they met the companions of Muhammad ﷺ, said: "We believe."

Al-Suddi said: These are people from among the Jews who believed and then became hypocrites. Likewise said al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Qatadah, and others among the early and later scholars. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam even said, as related by Ibn Wahb from him: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said: "Let no one enter upon us through the outskirts of Madinah except a believer." Their leaders among the people of disbelief and hypocrisy said: "Go and say, 'We believe,' and disbelieve when you return to us." So they would come to Madinah in the early morning and return to them after the afternoon prayer. And he recited the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And a party of the People of the Book said, "Believe in what has been revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day, and disbelieve at its end, that perhaps they will return."﴾ [Al 'Imran: 72]. They used to say, when they entered Madinah, "We are Muslims," in order to learn the news of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his affair. When they returned, they returned to disbelief. When Allah informed His Prophet ﷺ of this, He cut that off from them, and they no longer entered. The believers used to think that they were believers, so they would say: "Did Allah not say to you such and such?" And they would say: "Yes." But when they returned to their people [meaning the leaders], they said: ﴿Do you tell them what Allah has disclosed to you?﴾ — the verse. [Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (2/254) from Yunus from Ibn Wahb.]

Abu al-'Aliyah said: ﴿Do you tell them what Allah has disclosed to you?﴾ means: what Allah revealed to you in your Book concerning the description of Muhammad ﷺ.

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿Do you tell them what Allah has disclosed to you so that they may argue with you about it before your Lord?﴾ He said: They used to say: "A Prophet will come." So some of them were alone with others and said: ﴿Do you tell them what Allah has disclosed to you?﴾ [Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (1/71).]

Another opinion regarding the meaning of "disclosed" (fath): Ibn Jurayj said: Al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah related to me, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿Do you tell them what Allah has disclosed to you?﴾ He said: The Prophet ﷺ stood on the day of Qurayzah beneath their fortresses and said: "O brothers of the apes and the swine, and worshippers of the Taghut!" They said: "Who told Muhammad about this matter? This statement came only from you." ﴿Do you tell them what Allah has disclosed to you?﴾ — by what Allah judged, for the victory, so that it would be a proof against you. Ibn Jurayj said, from Mujahid: This was when he sent 'Ali to them, and they harmed Muhammad ﷺ.

Al-Suddi said: ﴿Do you tell them what Allah has disclosed to you?﴾ — of the punishment — ﴿so that they may argue with you about it before your Lord?﴾ These are people from among the Jews who believed and then became hypocrites, and they would tell the believers among the Arabs about what they had been punished with. So some of them said to others: "Do you tell them what Allah has disclosed to you?" — of the punishment — so that they would say: "We are more beloved to Allah than you, and more honoured by Allah than you."

'Ata' al-Khurasani said: ﴿Do you tell them what Allah has disclosed to you?﴾ means: what Allah has decreed for you and against you.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: These were the Jews; when they met those who believed, they said, "We believe," and when some of them were alone with others, some of them said: "Do not tell the companions of Muhammad of what Allah has disclosed to you of what is in your Book, lest they argue with you about it before your Lord and overcome you."

* *

Al-Hasan said: ﴿that Allah knows what they conceal﴾ — He said: What they concealed was that whenever they turned away from the companions of Muhammad ﷺ and were alone with one another, they agreed that none of them should inform the companions of Muhammad ﷺ of what Allah had disclosed to them of what is in their Book, fearing that the companions of Muhammad ﷺ would argue with them about what is in their Book before their Lord. ﴿And what they declare﴾ means: when they said to the companions of Muhammad ﷺ, "We believe." Likewise said Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Rabi', and Qatadah.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Do you hope, [O believers], that they will believe you?﴾ That is, that they will submit to you in obedience — this misguided sect of the Jews, whose forefathers witnessed clear signs, witnessing what they witnessed, and then their hearts hardened after that. ﴿And there was a party of them who heard the words of Allah, then they distorted them﴾ — that is, they interpreted them other than their proper interpretation — ﴿after they had understood them﴾ — that is, they comprehended them clearly — and yet they opposed them knowingly. ﴿While they knew﴾ that they were in error in what they went to of distorting and interpreting it? This situation is similar to His saying: ﴿So for their breaking their covenant, We cursed them and made their hearts hard; they distort words from their places﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 13].

Likewise said Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Rabi', and Qatadah.

Allah the Exalted says: "And among them are unlettered ones (ummiyyun)" — that is, among the People of the Book. This is the view of Mujahid. The word ummiyyun is the plural of ummi, which refers to a man who does not know how to write. This is the view of Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Rabi', Qatadah, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and others. It is evident from His saying: "They know not the Scripture, except wishful beliefs" (ila amaniyya), meaning they do not understand what it contains. For this reason, the Prophet ﷺ is described as ummi, because he did not know how to write, as Allah says: "And you did not recite before it any Book, nor did you write it with your right hand; for then would the falsifiers have had doubt" [al-'Ankabut: 48]. The Prophet ﷺ also said: "Verily, we are an unlettered nation; we do not write and we do not calculate. The month is thus and thus and thus," (the hadith). That is, we do not depend in our worship and its timings on writing or calculation. Allah also says: "It is He who sent among the unlettered a messenger from themselves" [al-Jumu'ah: 2].

Ibn Jarir said: The Arabs ascribed a man who neither writes nor draws letters to his mother rather than his father, due to his ignorance of writing. He said: A view contrary to this has been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, and it is what Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Bishr ibn 'Umarah, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: "And among them are unlettered ones." He said: The unlettered ones are a people who did not believe in a messenger Allah had sent, nor a book Allah had revealed; so they wrote a book with their own hands, then said to a lowly, ignorant people: "This is from Allah." He said: He has informed that they write with their hands, then named them unlettered, because of their denial of the Books of Allah and His messengers. Then Ibn Jarir said: This interpretation is contrary to what is known from the widespread usage of the Arabs among themselves, for the ummi in the Arabs' usage is the one who does not write.

I say: Then, regarding the soundness of this report from Ibn 'Abbas through this chain, there is scrutiny. And Allah knows best.

As for His saying: "except wishful beliefs" (illa amaniyya), Ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "illa amaniyya" — except tales (ahadith).

Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: "illa amaniyya": he says, except a saying they utter with their mouths, a lie. Mujahid said: except a lie. Sunayd narrated from Hajjaj, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: "And among them are unlettered ones who know not the Scripture, except wishful beliefs" — he said: People from among the Jews who did not know anything of the Scripture, and they spoke by conjecture, not according to what is in the Book of Allah, and they would say: "It is from the Scripture," wishful beliefs they wished for. A similar report is narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri.

Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Rabi' and Qatadah said: "illa amaniyya" — they wish upon Allah what is not theirs.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "illa amaniyya" — he said: They wished, and said: "We are of the People of the Book," and they were not of them.

Ibn Jarir said: The more correct view is the saying of al-Dahhak from Ibn 'Abbas. Mujahid said: The unlettered ones whom Allah described as not understanding from the Scripture that was revealed to Moses anything, but they fabricate lies and invent falsehoods, lies and fabrications. The "tamanni" (wishing) in this context is the fabrication of lies and inventing them. From this is the report narrated from Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him: "I have never sung nor wished (tamanniytu)." That is, I have not invented falsehood nor fabricated lies.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: "They know not the Scripture, except wishful beliefs, and they do not but conjecture" — and they do not understand what is in it, and they deny your prophethood by conjecture.

Mujahid said: "And they do not but conjecture" — they lie.

Qatadah, Abu al-'Aliyah and al-Rabi' said: They conjecture conjectures without truth.

And His saying: "So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands, then say, 'This is from Allah,' to exchange it for a small price" (to the end of the verse). These are another category of the Jews: they are the callers to misguidance through falsehood and lying about Allah, and consuming people's wealth unjustly.

Al-Wayl (woe) means destruction and perdition, and it is a well-known word in the language. Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Ziyad ibn Fayyad: I heard Abu 'Iyad say: Wayl is pus in the bottom of Hell. 'Ata' ibn Yasar said: Wayl is a valley in Hell, which, if mountains were moved through it, would melt.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Wayl is a valley in Hell, into which the disbeliever falls for forty autumns before reaching its bottom."

al-Tirmidhi narrated it from 'Abd ibn Humayd, from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Darraj, with it. He said: This is a gharib hadith; we do not know it except from the hadith of Ibn Lahi'ah.

I say: Ibn Lahi'ah was not alone in it, as you see, but the defect is from those after him, and this hadith with this chain, marfu', is munkar. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Salam ibn Salih al-'Ushayri narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Jarir narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far, from Kinanah al-'Adawi, from Uthman ibn Affan, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "So woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they earn." He said: "Al-wayl is a mountain in the Fire. It was revealed concerning the Jews, because they distorted the Torah, adding to it what they loved and erasing from it what they disliked, and they erased the name of Muhammad ﷺ from the Torah. For this reason Allah became angry with them, and He removed some of the Torah," and He said: "So woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they earn."

This is also very strange indeed.

[And from Ibn 'Abbas: al-wayl is the blazing of the punishment. Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said: al-wayl is the intensity of evil. Sibawayh said: wayl is for one who has fallen into destruction, and wayh for one who is near it. Al-Asma'i said: al-wayl is lamentation, and al-wayl is compassion. Others said: al-wayl is grief. Al-Khalil said: In the meaning of wayl are: wayh, ways, wayh, wayk and wayb, and some distinguish between them. Some grammarians said: It is permissible to begin with it though it is indefinite, because it carries the meaning of supplication. Some permitted its being put in the accusative, in the sense of: "may He impose upon them woe." I say: But no one has read it that way.]

From Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands": they are the rabbis of the Jews. Likewise Sa'id narrated from Qatadah: they are the Jews.

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Alqamah: I asked Ibn 'Abbas about His saying: "So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands," and he said: It was revealed concerning the polytheists and the People of the Book.

al-Suddi said: Some people from the Jews wrote a book from their own selves, selling it to the Arabs, and telling them that it was from Allah, so that they might take a small price for it.

al-Zuhri said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah informed me, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: O assembly of Muslims, how do you ask the People of the Book about anything, when your Book which Allah revealed to His Prophet is the most recent of the news of Allah, which you read fresh and unaltered? Allah has told you that the People of the Book have changed the Book of Allah and altered it, and wrote the book with their own hands, and said: "This is from Allah," to exchange it for a small price. Does not the knowledge that has come to you forbid you from asking them? By Allah, we have never seen any of them ask you about what was revealed to you. Narrated by al-Bukhari from several chains from al-Zuhri.

al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Basri said: The small price is the whole world in its entirety.

And His saying: "So woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they earn": that is, woe to them for what they wrote with their hands of lies, slander and fabrication, and woe to them for what they consumed by it of unlawful gain. As al-Dahhak said from Ibn 'Abbas: "So woe to them" — he says: the punishment is upon them, for what they wrote with their hands of that lie; "and woe to them for what they earn" — he says: for what they devour by it from the lowly people and others.
