For this reason, the Prophet ﷺ is described as ummi, because he did not know how to write, as Allah says: "And you did not recite before it any Book, nor did you write it with your right hand; for then would the falsifiers have had doubt" [al-'Ankabut: 48]. The Prophet ﷺ also said: "Verily, we are an unlettered nation; we do not write and we do not calculate. The month is thus and thus and thus," (the hadith). That is, we do not depend in our worship and its timings on writing or calculation. Allah also says: "It is He who sent among the unlettered a messenger from themselves" [al-Jumu'ah: 2].

Ibn Jarir said: The Arabs ascribed a man who neither writes nor draws letters to his mother rather than his father, due to his ignorance of writing. He said: A view contrary to this has been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, and it is what Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Bishr ibn 'Umarah, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: "And among them are unlettered ones." He said: The unlettered ones are a people who did not believe in a messenger Allah had sent, nor a book Allah had revealed; so they wrote a book with their own hands, then said to a lowly, ignorant people: "This is from Allah." He said: He has informed that they write with their hands, then named them unlettered, because of their denial of the Books of Allah and His messengers. Then Ibn Jarir said: This interpretation is contrary to what is known from the widespread usage of the Arabs among themselves, for the ummi in the Arabs' usage is the one who does not write.

I say: Then, regarding the soundness of this report from Ibn 'Abbas through this chain, there is scrutiny. And Allah knows best.

As for His saying: "except wishful beliefs" (illa amaniyya), Ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "illa amaniyya" — except tales (ahadith).

Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: "illa amaniyya": he says, except a saying they utter with their mouths, a lie. Mujahid said: except a lie. Sunayd narrated from Hajjaj, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: "And among them are unlettered ones who know not the Scripture, except wishful beliefs" — he said: People from among the Jews who did not know anything of the Scripture, and they spoke by conjecture, not according to what is in the Book of Allah, and they would say: "It is from the Scripture," wishful beliefs they wished for. A similar report is narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri.

Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Rabi' and Qatadah said: "illa amaniyya" — they wish upon Allah what is not theirs.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "illa amaniyya" — he said: They wished, and said: "We are of the People of the Book," and they were not of them.

Ibn Jarir said: The more correct view is the saying of al-Dahhak from Ibn 'Abbas. Mujahid said: The unlettered ones whom Allah described as not understanding from the Scripture that was revealed to Moses anything, but they fabricate lies and invent falsehoods, lies and fabrications. The "tamanni" (wishing) in this context is the fabrication of lies and inventing them. From this is the report narrated from Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him: "I have never sung nor wished (tamanniytu)." That is, I have not invented falsehood nor fabricated lies.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: "They know not the Scripture, except wishful beliefs, and they do not but conjecture" — and they do not understand what is in it, and they deny your prophethood by conjecture.

Mujahid said: "And they do not but conjecture" — they lie.

Qatadah, Abu al-'Aliyah and al-Rabi' said: They conjecture conjectures without truth.

And His saying: "So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands, then say, 'This is from Allah,' to exchange it for a small price" (to the end of the verse). These are another category of the Jews: they are the callers to misguidance through falsehood and lying about Allah, and consuming people's wealth unjustly.

Al-Wayl (woe) means destruction and perdition, and it is a well-known word in the language. Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Ziyad ibn Fayyad: I heard Abu 'Iyad say: Wayl is pus in the bottom of Hell. 'Ata' ibn Yasar said: Wayl is a valley in Hell, which, if mountains were moved through it, would melt.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Wayl is a valley in Hell, into which the disbeliever falls for forty autumns before reaching its bottom."

al-Tirmidhi narrated it from 'Abd ibn Humayd, from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Darraj, with it. He said: This is a gharib hadith; we do not know it except from the hadith of Ibn Lahi'ah.

I say: Ibn Lahi'ah was not alone in it, as you see, but the defect is from those after him, and this hadith with this chain, marfu', is munkar. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Salam ibn Salih al-'Ushayri narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Jarir narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far, from Kinanah al-'Adawi, from Uthman ibn Affan, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "So woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they earn." He said: "Al-wayl is a mountain in the Fire. It was revealed concerning the Jews, because they distorted the Torah, adding to it what they loved and erasing from it what they disliked, and they erased the name of Muhammad ﷺ from the Torah. For this reason Allah became angry with them, and He removed some of the Torah," and He said: "So woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they earn."

This is also very strange indeed.

[And from Ibn 'Abbas: al-wayl is the blazing of the punishment. Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said: al-wayl is the intensity of evil. Sibawayh said: wayl is for one who has fallen into destruction, and wayh for one who is near it. Al-Asma'i said: al-wayl is lamentation, and al-wayl is compassion. Others said: al-wayl is grief. Al-Khalil said: In the meaning of wayl are: wayh, ways, wayh, wayk and wayb, and some distinguish between them. Some grammarians said: It is permissible to begin with it though it is indefinite, because it carries the meaning of supplication. Some permitted its being put in the accusative, in the sense of: "may He impose upon them woe." I say: But no one has read it that way.]

From Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands": they are the rabbis of the Jews. Likewise Sa'id narrated from Qatadah: they are the Jews.

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Alqamah: I asked Ibn 'Abbas about His saying: "So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands," and he said: It was revealed concerning the polytheists and the People of the Book.

al-Suddi said: Some people from the Jews wrote a book from their own selves, selling it to the Arabs, and telling them that it was from Allah, so that they might take a small price for it.

al-Zuhri said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah informed me, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: O assembly of Muslims, how do you ask the People of the Book about anything, when your Book which Allah revealed to His Prophet is the most recent of the news of Allah, which you read fresh and unaltered? Allah has told you that the People of the Book have changed the Book of Allah and altered it, and wrote the book with their own hands, and said: "This is from Allah," to exchange it for a small price. Does not the knowledge that has come to you forbid you from asking them? By Allah, we have never seen any of them ask you about what was revealed to you. Narrated by al-Bukhari from several chains from al-Zuhri.

al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Basri said: The small price is the whole world in its entirety.

And His saying: "So woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they earn": that is, woe to them for what they wrote with their hands of lies, slander and fabrication, and woe to them for what they consumed by it of unlawful gain. As al-Dahhak said from Ibn 'Abbas: "So woe to them" — he says: the punishment is upon them, for what they wrote with their hands of that lie; "and woe to them for what they earn" — he says: for what they devour by it from the lowly people and others.

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on Surah 2, verse 80:

Allah says, reporting about the Jews concerning what they transmitted and claimed for themselves, that the Fire would not touch them except for a few counted days, after which they would be saved from it. Allah refuted this claim by His saying: ﴿Say: "Have you taken a covenant with Allah?"﴾ [[Following this in one manuscript: "Then Allah will not break His covenant."]] meaning: Have you taken such a covenant? If a covenant had indeed been made, then He would not break His covenant [[In manuscripts ج, ط, ب, أ, و: "His promise."]].

But this did not happen, and it never existed. For this reason He used "am" (أَمْ), which carries the meaning of "bal" (بَلْ, "rather"), meaning: Rather, you say about Allah what you do not know, of lies and fabrication against Him.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Sayf ibn Sulayman [[In manuscript ج: "Salman."]], from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas: The Jews used to say: "This world is seven thousand years, and we will only be punished one day in the Fire for every thousand years, and it will only be seven counted days." So Allah revealed: ﴿And they said, "The Fire will not touch us except for a few countable days"﴾ up to His saying: ﴿abiding therein﴾ [al-Baqarah: 82].

He then narrated it from Muhammad, from Sa'id or Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, in similar terms.

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿And they said, "The Fire will not touch us except for a few countable days"﴾: The Jews said: "The Fire will not touch us except for forty nights." [Another added: this is the duration of their worship of the calf; this was related by al-Qurtubi from Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah.]

Al-Dahhak said, Ibn 'Abbas said: The Jews claimed that they found written in the Torah that the distance between the two edges of Hell is forty years' journey, until they reach the tree of al-Zaqqum, which grows at the root of the Hellfire. The enemies of Allah said: "We will only be punished until we reach the tree of al-Zaqqum, and then Hell will go away and perish." This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And they said, "The Fire will not touch us except for a few countable days"﴾.

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And they said, "The Fire will not touch us except for a few countable days"﴾, meaning: the days in which we worshipped the calf [[Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (1/71, 72).]].

Ikrimah said: The Jews disputed with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "We will not enter the Fire except for forty nights, and after us will come other people in it," meaning Muhammad (ﷺ) and his companions. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) pointed with his hand at their heads and said: "Rather, you are eternal, abiding forever, and no one will succeed you in it." So Allah revealed: ﴿And they said, "The Fire will not touch us except for a few countable days"﴾, the verse.

The Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ja'far related to us, Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sakhr related to us, Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri' related to us, Layth ibn Sa'd related to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id related to me, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: When Khaybar was conquered, a sheep containing poison was presented as a gift to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Gather for me whoever among the Jews is here." He said to them: "Who is your father?" They said: "Our father is so-and-so." He said: "You lie, rather your father is so-and-so." They said: "You have spoken truly and righteously." Then he said to them: "Will you be truthful with me about something if I ask you about it?" They said: "Yes, O Abu al-Qasim, and if we lie to you, you will know our lie as you knew it concerning our father." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Who are the people of the Fire?" They said: "We will be in it a short time, and then you will succeed us in it." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Be gone! By Allah, we will never succeed you in it, ever." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Will you be truthful with me about something if I ask you about it?" They said: "Yes, O Abu al-Qasim." He said: "Have you put poison in this sheep?" They said: "Yes." He said: "What moved you to that?" They said: "We wanted, if you were a liar, to be rid of you, and if you were a prophet, it would not harm you."

Ahmad, al-Bukhari and al-Nasa'i related it, with similar wording, from the hadith of Layth ibn Sa'd [[Musnad (2/451), Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (3161, 4249), and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11355).]].

The matter is not as you wish, nor as you desire. Rather, the matter is this: whoever commits an evil deed and his sin encompasses him, and he meets the Day of Resurrection with no good deed at all, but all of his deeds are evil, then he is among the people of the Fire. As for those who believe in Allah and His Messenger [[In A: "and His messengers".]] and do righteous deeds, meaning deeds that conform to the Shari'ah (the revealed law), they [[In J, T, B, A, and W: "he".]] are among the people of Paradise. This situation resembles His saying: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and will not find for himself, besides Allah, any protector or helper. And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer, those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged, even by the size of a speck.﴾ [An-Nisa: 123, 124].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad related to me, from Sa'id, or Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Yes, whoever earns an evil deed﴾, meaning: he does the same as your deeds and disbelieves in the same way that you disbelieved, until his disbelief encompasses him, so he has no good deed.

In a narration from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: It is shirk (associating partners with Allah).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was related from Abu Wa'il, Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas something similar to this.

Al-Hasan and al-Suddi also said: The evil deed (sayyi'ah) is a major sin (kabirah, pl. kaba'ir) from among the major sins.

Ibn Jurayj related from Mujahid regarding ﴿and his sin encompasses him﴾ that he said: with his heart.

Abu Hurayrah, Abu Wa'il, 'Ata', and al-Hasan said regarding ﴿and his sin encompasses him﴾: they said, his shirk encompasses him.

Al-A'mash said, from Abu Razin, from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym regarding ﴿and his sin encompasses him﴾: He said: It is the one who dies while upon sins [[In A and W: "upon his sins".]] before repenting. And from al-Suddi and Abu Razin, something similar.

Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, al-Hasan in one narration from them both, Qatadah, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said regarding ﴿and his sin encompasses him﴾: it is the major sin that necessitates (the Fire).

All these statements are close in meaning, and Allah knows best. Here is mentioned the hadith which Imam Ahmad related, where he said:

Sulayman ibn Dawud told us: 'Amr ibn Qatadah told us, from 'Abd Rabbihi, from Abu 'Iyad, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of minor sins, for they will gather upon a man until they destroy him." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) struck an example for them, like a people who descended upon a barren land, and the time for the people's meal arrived, so a man went out and came back with a stick, and another man came with a stick, until they gathered a pile and kindled a fire, and cooked what they had cast into it.

[[Al-Musnad (1/402).]]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad related to me, from Sa'id, or Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds, those are the companions of Paradise, they will abide therein forever﴾: meaning, whoever believes in what you disbelieved in, and acts upon what you abandoned of his religion, then for them is Paradise, abiding therein. He informs them that the reward for good and for evil remains upon its people, with no cessation for it ever, [[In J, T, B: "ever, with no cessation."]].

The matter is not as you wish, nor as you desire. Rather, the matter is this: whoever commits an evil deed and his sin encompasses him, and he meets the Day of Resurrection with no good deed at all, but all of his deeds are evil, then he is among the people of the Fire. As for those who believe in Allah and His Messenger [[In A: "and His messengers".]] and do righteous deeds, meaning deeds that conform to the Shari'ah (the revealed law), they [[In J, T, B, A, and W: "he".]] are among the people of Paradise. This situation resembles His saying: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and will not find for himself, besides Allah, any protector or helper. And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer, those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged, even by the size of a speck.﴾ [An-Nisa: 123, 124].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad related to me, from Sa'id, or Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Yes, whoever earns an evil deed﴾, meaning: he does the same as your deeds and disbelieves in the same way that you disbelieved, until his disbelief encompasses him, so he has no good deed.

In a narration from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: It is shirk (associating partners with Allah).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was related from Abu Wa'il, Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas something similar to this.

Al-Hasan and al-Suddi also said: The evil deed (sayyi'ah) is a major sin (kabirah, pl. kaba'ir) from among the major sins.

Ibn Jurayj related from Mujahid regarding ﴿and his sin encompasses him﴾ that he said: with his heart.

Abu Hurayrah, Abu Wa'il, 'Ata', and al-Hasan said regarding ﴿and his sin encompasses him﴾: they said, his shirk encompasses him.

Al-A'mash said, from Abu Razin, from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym regarding ﴿and his sin encompasses him﴾: He said: It is the one who dies while upon sins [[In A and W: "upon his sins".]] before repenting. And from al-Suddi and Abu Razin, something similar.

Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, al-Hasan in one narration from them both, Qatadah, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said regarding ﴿and his sin encompasses him﴾: it is the major sin that necessitates (the Fire).

All these statements are close in meaning, and Allah knows best. Here is mentioned the hadith which Imam Ahmad related, where he said:

Sulayman ibn Dawud told us: 'Amr ibn Qatadah told us, from 'Abd Rabbihi, from Abu 'Iyad, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of minor sins, for they will gather upon a man until they destroy him." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) struck an example for them, like a people who descended upon a barren land, and the time for the people's meal arrived, so a man went out and came back with a stick, and another man came with a stick, until they gathered a pile and kindled a fire, and cooked what they had cast into it.

[[Al-Musnad (1/402).]]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad related to me, from Sa'id, or Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds, those are the companions of Paradise, they will abide therein forever﴾: meaning, whoever believes in what you disbelieved in, and acts upon what you abandoned of his religion, then for them is Paradise, abiding therein. He informs them that the reward for good and for evil remains upon its people, with no cessation for it ever, [[In J, T, B: "ever, with no cessation."]].

The Exalted, may He be blessed, reminds the Children of Israel of the commands He gave them and of the covenant He took from them to observe them. He informs them that they turned away from all of it, deliberately and intentionally, although they knew it and remembered it. So He commanded them to worship Him and not to associate anything with Him. He commanded all of His creation with this, and for this He created them, as He said: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 25] And He said: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid the taghut."﴾ [al-Nahl: 36]

This is the highest and greatest of rights, which is the right of Allah, the Exalted, that He alone be worshipped with no partner. After it comes the right of the created beings, and the most emphatic and most deserving of them by this is the right of the two parents. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, joins His right with the right of the parents, as He said: ﴿Be grateful to Me and to your parents; to Me is the final destination.﴾ [Luqman: 14] And He said: ﴿And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him, and to parents, good treatment...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And give the near relative his right, and [also] the needy and the traveler.﴾ [al-Isra': 23-26]

In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud, he said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, which deed is best?' He said: 'Prayer at its proper time.' I said: 'Then which?' He said: 'Kindness to parents.' I said: 'Then which?' He said: 'Jihad in the way of Allah.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (527, 5970, 7534) and Sahih Muslim, no. (85).]

For this reason it came in the sound hadith that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, who is most deserving of my kindness?" He said: "Your mother." He said: "Then who?" He said: "Your mother." He said: "Then who?" He said: "Your mother." He said: "Then who?" He said: "Your father. Then the nearest, the nearest." [This came from the hadith of Mu'awiyah ibn Haydah, narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Sunan, no. (5139), and from the hadith of Kulayb ibn Munfi' from his father from his grandfather, narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Sunan, no. (5140).]

[As for His saying: ﴿La ta'budun illa Allah﴾ (You shall not worship except Allah): al-Zamakhshari said: it is a statement in the form of a report but with the meaning of a command, and it is more emphatic. It was also said that its original form was: "Alla ta'budu" (that you not worship), as some of the early generation read it, so "an" was omitted and the verb became marfu'. It is related from Ubayy and Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with them both, that they read it: "La ta'budu illa Allah." It was also said: ﴿La ta'budun﴾ is marfu' because it is an oath, meaning: "By Allah, you shall not worship except Allah." Al-Qurtubi, in his tafsir, transmitted this explanation from Sibawayh, and said: it was chosen by al-Mubarrid, al-Kisa'i and al-Farra'.]

He said: ﴿And the orphans﴾, who are the young children who have no earner among their fathers. [The lexicographers said: the orphan (yatim) among human beings is one who has lost his father, and among animals is one who has lost his mother. Al-Mawardi related that the term yatim is also applied among human beings to one who has lost his mother.] ﴿And the needy﴾, who do not have what they can spend on themselves and their dependents. The discussion of these categories will come at the verse of al-Nisa', in which Allah, the Exalted, explicitly commanded us with them in His saying: ﴿And worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and be good to parents...﴾ [al-Nisa': 36] up to the end of the verse.

* *

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And speak to people kindly﴾, that is: speak to them good words and be gentle to them in manner. This includes enjoining what is good and forbidding what is evil with what is good, as al-Hasan al-Basri said regarding His saying: ﴿And speak to people kindly.﴾ "Good speech is: to enjoin what is good, to forbid what is evil, to be forbearing, to pardon, to overlook, and to speak to people kindly as Allah said. It is every good character that Allah is pleased with."

Imam Ahmad said: Rawh related to us, Abu 'Amir al-Kharraz related to us, from Abu 'Imran al-Jawni, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Samit, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Do not belittle any act of goodness, even if you find nothing [to give], meet your brother with a cheerful face."

Muslim recorded it in his Sahih, and al-Tirmidhi [and graded it sahih] from the hadith of Abu 'Amir al-Kharraz, whose name is Salih ibn Rustum, with this chain. [Al-Musnad (5/173), Sahih Muslim, no. (2626), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (1833).]

It is fitting that He commanded them to speak kindly to people after He commanded them to do good to them by deed, thus combining the two aspects of good: the practical and the verbal. Then He emphasized the command to worship Him and to be good to people through the specific form of this, which is prayer and zakat, so He said: ﴿And establish prayer and give zakat.﴾ He then informed them that they turned away from all of that, that is, they left it behind their backs and turned away from it deliberately after knowing it, except for a few of them. Allah, the Exalted, commanded this Ummah with the like of this in Surat al-Nisa', in His saying: ﴿And worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and [be good] to parents, the near relative, the orphans, the needy, the near neighbor, the distant neighbor, the companion at your side, the traveler, and those your right hands possess. Indeed, Allah does not like whoever is self-deluded and boastful.﴾ [al-Nisa': 36] So this Ummah fulfilled this to a degree that no nation before it had fulfilled, and to Allah belongs all praise and favor.

Among the strange reports related here is what Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned in his tafsir:

My father related to us, Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-'Asqalani related to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf (meaning al-Tinnisi) related to us, Khalid ibn Subayh related to us, from Humayd ibn 'Uqbah, from Asad ibn Wada'ah: that he used to leave his home and would not meet a Jew or a Christian without greeting him. It was said to him: "What is your matter? You greet the Jew and the Christian?" He said: "Indeed Allah says: ﴿And speak to people kindly,﴾ and it is: the greeting (al-salam)." He said: It was also related from 'Ata' al-Khurasani something similar.

I say: It has been established in the Sunnah that they should not be greeted first with the salam. And Allah knows best. [Muslim recorded it in his Sahih, no. (2167), from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not initiate the greeting of salam to the Jews or the Christians, and when you meet one of them on the road, force him to its narrowest side."]

He, blessed and exalted, says, rebuking the Jews who were in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Madinah, and for what they were engaged in of fighting with the Aws and the Khazraj. This is because the Aws and the Khazraj, who are the Ansar (the Helpers), were idol-worshippers in the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance), and there were many wars between them. The Jews of Madinah were three tribes: Banu Qaynuqa', Banu al-Nadir, allies of the Khazraj, and Banu Qurayzah, allies of the Aws. When war broke out between them, each party fought alongside its allies. A Jew would kill his enemies, and another Jew might kill someone from the other party. This was forbidden to them in their religion and by the explicit text of their Book. They would expel them from their homes and plunder what was in them of furnishings, goods and wealth. Then, when the war laid down its burdens, they would ransom the captives from the defeated party, acting upon the ruling of the Tawrah (Torah). For this reason, He, exalted, said: ﴿Do you believe in part of the Book and disbelieve in part?﴾ And for this reason He, exalted, said: ﴿And [recall] when We took your covenant: You shall not shed your blood, nor expel yourselves from your homes﴾, meaning: none of you shall kill another, nor expel him from his dwelling, nor support [others] against him, as He, exalted, said: ﴿So repent to your Creator and kill yourselves; that is better for you in the sight of your Creator﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 54]. This is because the people of one religion are like one soul, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said, peace and blessings be upon him: "The likeness of the believers in their mutual love, mercy and kindness is that of one body: when one of its limbs complains, the rest of the body responds to it with wakefulness and fever."

[And His saying] [[Addition from ج، ط، أ.]] ﴿Then you affirmed while you were witnesses﴾, meaning: then you acknowledged the knowledge of this covenant and its validity while you were witnessing to it.

﴿Then you are those who kill yourselves and expel a party of you from their homes, supporting [their enemies] against them in sin and aggression. And if they come to you as captives, you ransom them, while their expulsion was forbidden to you.﴾ Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad related to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, or Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿Then you are those who kill yourselves﴾ to the end of the verse, he said: Allah rebuked them for their deed, [[In ج، ط، ب، أ، و: "Allah informed them of that."]] although He had forbidden them in the Tawrah to shed their blood, and had made it obligatory upon them in it to ransom their captives. They were two groups: a section of them, Banu Qaynuqa', and they [[In ج: "and they are."]] were allies of the Khazraj; and al-Nadir and Qurayzah, and they [[In ج: "and they are."]] were allies of the Aws. Whenever war broke out between the Aws and the Khazraj, Banu Qaynuqa' went out with the Khazraj, and al-Nadir and Qurayzah went out with the Aws. Each of the two parties supported its allies against their own brethren, until they shed each other's blood among themselves, while the Tawrah was in their hands, in which they knew what was obligatory upon them and what was lawful for them. The Aws and the Khazraj were people of shirk who worshipped idols, and did not know of Paradise or Hell, nor of resurrection or the Last Day, nor of a Book, nor of the lawful and the unlawful. When the war laid down its burdens, they ransomed their captives, in confirmation of what was in the Tawrah and in acting upon it: some of them from others. Banu Qaynuqa' would ransom whatever captives of theirs were in the hands of the Aws, and al-Nadir and Qurayzah would ransom whatever of theirs was in the hands of the Khazraj. They would also demand what they had taken of their blood, [[In ج، ط، ب، أ، و: "of the blood and killed."]] and the slain whom they had killed among themselves, supporting the people of shirk against them. Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says, when He rebuked them for this: ﴿Do you believe in part of the Book and disbelieve in part?﴾, meaning: they ransom him according to the ruling of the Tawrah, and yet they kill him, while the ruling of the Tawrah is that they should not do so, nor expel him from his home, nor support against him one who associates partners with Allah and worships idols besides Him, seeking the goods of this worldly life. Regarding this deed of theirs with the Aws and the Khazraj, as has reached me, this account was revealed.

Asbat related from al-Suddi: Qurayzah were allies of the Aws, and al-Nadir were allies of the Khazraj. They used to fight one another in the war of Sumayr. Banu Qurayzah would fight with their allies against al-Nadir and their allies, and al-Nadir would fight Qurayzah and their allies, and they would overcome them, destroy their homes and expel them from them. When a man from either of the two parties was taken captive, they would gather [money] for him until they ransomed him. The Arabs would reproach them for this and say: How do you fight them and then ransom them? They said: We have been commanded to ransom them, and fighting them has been forbidden to us. They said: Then why do you fight them? They said: We are ashamed that our allies be humiliated. So when Allah reproached them, He said: ﴿Then you are those who kill yourselves and expel a party of you from their homes﴾.

Shu'bah said, from al-Suddi: This verse was revealed concerning Qays ibn al-Khatim: ﴿Then you are those who kill yourselves and expel a party of you from their homes, supporting [their enemies] against them in sin and aggression﴾.

Asbat said, from al-Suddi, from Abd Khayr, who said: We fought alongside Salman ibn Rabi'ah al-Bahili at Balanjar. We besieged its people, conquered the city, and took captives. Abd Allah ibn Salam bought a Jewish woman for seven hundred. When he passed by Ra's al-Jalut, he dismounted near him. Abd Allah said to him: O Ra's al-Jalut, would you like an old woman here from your religion, to buy from me? He said: Yes. He said: I took her for seven hundred dirhams. He said: I will give you seven hundred more. He said: I have sworn not to reduce her price below four thousand. He said: I have no need of her. He said: By Allah, you will buy her from me, or you will disbelieve in your religion which you follow. He said: Come close to me. So he drew near, and he recited into his ear what is in the Tawrah: "You will not find a slave from the Children of Israel except that you buy him and free him," ﴿And if they come to you as captives, you ransom them, while their expulsion was forbidden to you﴾. He said: Are you Abd Allah ibn Salam? He said: Yes. He said: So he brought four thousand. Abd Allah took two thousand and returned two thousand to him.

Adam ibn Abi Iyas said in his Tafsir: Abu Ja'far, meaning al-Razi, related to us, al-Rabi' ibn Anas related to us, Abu al-'Aliyah informed us: that Abd Allah ibn Salam passed by Ra's al-Jalut in Kufah, while he was ransoming women whom the Arabs had not had intercourse with, but was not ransoming those whom the Arabs had had intercourse with. Abd Allah ibn Salam said to him: Surely it is written for you in your Book that you must ransom all of them.

Those are the ones who have bought the worldly life in exchange for the Hereafter﴾, meaning: they preferred it over the Hereafter and chose it. ﴿So the punishment will not be lightened for them﴾, meaning: it will not be relaxed for them for a single moment. ﴿Nor will they be helped﴾.

Meaning: they have no helper who will rescue them from the perpetual, everlasting punishment in which they are, nor will anyone give them protection from it.
