He (may He be blessed and exalted) describes the Children of Israel as arrogant, stubborn, opposing, and proud toward the prophets, and as following only their own desires. He mentions that He gave Moses the Book, which is the Torah, but they distorted and altered it, opposed its commands, and interpreted them away. He sent after him messengers and prophets who ruled by his law, as He said: ﴿Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which is guidance and light. By it the prophets who submitted judged for those who were Jews, and the rabbis and scholars, by what they were entrusted of the Book of Allah and to which they were witnesses﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 44], and the verse continues. Therefore He said: ﴿And We followed after him with messengers﴾. As-Suddi related from Abu Malik: "We sent after him." Others said: "We sent in succession." Both meanings are close, as He said: ﴿Then We sent Our messengers in succession﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 44]. Until He concluded the prophets of the Children of Israel with Jesus, son of Mary. He came with some rulings that opposed the Torah. For this reason Allah gave him clear proofs (al-bayyinat), which are the miracles. Ibn 'Abbas said: these include raising the dead, creating from clay the likeness of a bird, then breathing into it so that it becomes a bird by the permission of Allah, healing the blind and the leper, informing them of the unseen, and being supported with the Holy Spirit (Ruh al-Qudus), who is Gabriel (peace be upon him), all of which proves to them his truthfulness in what he brought them. So the Children of Israel's denial of him intensified, along with their envy and their stubbornness, because he opposed the Torah in part, as He said, relating from Jesus: ﴿And to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you, and I have come to you with a sign from your Lord﴾ [Al 'Imran: 50], and the verse continues. The Children of Israel treated the prophets, peace be upon them, in the worst manner: a group they denied, and a group they killed. This was only because they brought them matters that opposed their desires and opinions, and obligated them to the rulings of the Torah, which they had altered by opposing it. Therefore this was hard for them, so they denied them, and sometimes they killed some of them. For this reason He said: ﴿Is it that whenever a messenger came to you with what your souls did not desire, you became arrogant? A group you denied, and a group you kill﴾.

The evidence that the Ruh al-Qudus is Gabriel is what Ibn Mas'ud stated in the explanation of this verse, and Ibn 'Abbas and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, as-Suddi, ar-Rabi' ibn Anas, 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi, and Qatadah agreed with him, along with His statement: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart, that you may be of the warners, in clear Arabic language﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 193-195]. Al-Bukhari said: Ibn Abi az-Zinad related from his father, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set up a pulpit for Hassan ibn Thabit in the mosque, so he would defend the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, support Hassan with the Holy Spirit, as he defended Your Prophet." This is a suspended narration (ta'liq) by al-Bukhari. Al-Mizzi, in Tuhfat al-Ashraf (12/10), also attributed it to al-Bukhari, and al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in an-Nukat az-Zira: "I have not found this place in the Sahih of al-Bukhari, but Ahmad and at-Tabarani connected it, and al-Hakim authenticated it."

Abu Dawud related it in his Sunan from Lu'ayn, and at-Tirmidhi from 'Ali ibn Hujr and Isma'il ibn Musa al-Fazari, all three from 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Abi az-Zinad, from his father and Hisham ibn 'Urwah, both from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, with it. At-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih, and it is the hadith of Abu az-Zinad.

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from az-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Abu Hurayrah: 'Umar passed by Hassan while he was reciting poetry in the mosque, so he looked at him and said: "I used to recite in it, and in it was one better than you." Then he turned to Abu Hurayrah and said: "I ask you by Allah, did you hear the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Answer on my behalf. O Allah, support him with the Holy Spirit'?" He said: "By Allah, yes."

In some narrations, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Hassan: "Satirize them, or satirize them, and Gabriel is with you."

[In Hassan's poetry is his saying:

"And Gabriel, the messenger of Allah, calls out... and the Holy Spirit is not hidden in him."]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Abi Husayn al-Makki related to me, from Shahr ibn Hawshab al-Ash'ari, that some Jews asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Tell us about the Spirit." He said: "I implore you by Allah and by His days among the Children of Israel, do you know that it is Gabriel, who comes to me?" They said: "Yes."

[In the Sahih of Ibn Hibban, I think from Ibn Mas'ud, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the Holy Spirit breathed into my heart that no soul will die until it completes its provision and its term. So fear Allah and seek provision well."]

Other sayings:

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah told us, Minjab ibn al-Harith told us, Bishr told us, from Abu Rawq, from ad-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿with the Holy Spirit﴾: "It is the Greatest Name, by which Jesus used to revive the dead." Ibn Jarir said: I was told from al-Minjab, and he mentioned it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: it is also related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr something similar. [al-Qurtubi also related it from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, and said: "It is the Greatest Name."]

Ibn Abi Najih said: the Ruh is a guardian over the angels.

Abu Ja'far ar-Razi related from ar-Rabi' ibn Anas: al-Qudus is the Lord, blessed and exalted. This is also the saying of Ka'b. As-Suddi said: al-Qudus is blessing. al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas: al-Qudus is purity.

[al-Qurtubi related from Mujahid and al-Hasan al-Basri that they both said: al-Qudus is Allah, the Exalted, and His Ruh is Gabriel. According to this, the first saying stands.]

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la told us, Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, ﴿And We supported him with the Holy Spirit﴾: "Allah supported Jesus with the Gospel as a Spirit, just as He made the Qur'an a Spirit. Both are a Spirit from Allah, as He said: ﴿And thus We revealed to you a Spirit from Our command﴾ [ash-Shura: 52]."

Then Ibn Jarir said: The most correct of the interpretations is the saying of the one who said: the Ruh in this place is Gabriel, because Allah, mighty and majestic, informed that He supported Jesus with him, as He said: ﴿When Allah said, "O Jesus, son of Mary, remember My favor upon you and upon your mother, when I supported you with the Holy Spirit, you spoke to people in the cradle and in maturity, and when I taught you the Book and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 110], and the verse continues. He mentioned that He supported him with it. If the Spirit with which He supported him were the Gospel, then His saying ﴿when I supported you with the Holy Spirit﴾ and ﴿when I taught you the Book and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel﴾ would be a repetition of a statement with no meaning, and Allah is too exalted to address His servants with what does not benefit them.

I (Ibn Kathir) say: Among the evidence that it is Gabriel is what preceded at the beginning of the context. And to Allah belongs praise.

Az-Zamakhshari said: ﴿with the Holy Spirit﴾ means "with the holy spirit," as one says "Hatim of generosity" and "a man of truthfulness." Describing it as holy is like His saying: ﴿and a spirit from Him﴾. Describing him with exclusivity and nearness is an honor. It was also said: because the loins and the wombs did not contain him, the menstruating ones. It was also said: it means Gabriel. It was said: it means the Gospel, as He said about the Qur'an: ﴿a spirit from Our command﴾ [ash-Shura: 52]. It was also said: it means the Greatest Name of Allah, by which he used to revive the dead. His statement also includes another saying, which is that what is meant is the very holy and purified spirit of Jesus himself.

Az-Zamakhshari also said, regarding His statement ﴿so a group you denied, and a group you kill﴾: He did not say "and a group you killed," because He intended by this to describe them in the future as well, since they tried to kill the Prophet (ﷺ) by poison and sorcery. He, peace be upon him, said during his final illness: "The morsel of Khaybar has continued to afflict me, and this is the time for the severing of my aorta." This hadith is in Sahih al-Bukhari and elsewhere.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 88:

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad related to me, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And they say, "Our hearts are uncovered"﴾ meaning: they are in coverings.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And they say, "Our hearts are uncovered"﴾ meaning: they do not understand.

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And they say, "Our hearts are uncovered"﴾ [he said:] they are the hearts upon which a seal has been set.

Mujahid said: ﴿And they say, "Our hearts are uncovered"﴾ upon them is a veil.

Ikrimah said: upon them is a seal. Abu al-'Aliyah said: meaning they do not understand. As-Suddi said: They say, "Upon them is a sheath (ghilaf)," which is a covering.

'Abd al-Razzaq related, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And they say, "Our hearts are uncovered"﴾ It is like His saying: ﴿And they say, "Our hearts are in coverings from that to which you invite us"﴾ [Fussilat: 5].

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, regarding His saying ﴿uncovered﴾, said: He says, "My heart is in a sheath, so what you say does not reach it," and he recited: ﴿And they say, "Our hearts are in coverings from that to which you invite us"﴾.

This is the view preferred by Ibn Jarir, and he cited in support what was narrated in the hadith of 'Amr ibn Murrah al-Jamali, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Hudhayfah, who said: The hearts are four. He mentioned among them: "And a heart that is uncovered (aghlaf), upon which is anger, and that is the heart of the disbeliever."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-'Arzami related to us, my father informed us, from my grandfather, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan regarding His saying: ﴿Our hearts are uncovered﴾ He said: They have not been circumcised.

The meaning of this statement returns to what preceded regarding the impurity of their hearts and that they are far from goodness.

Another view:

Ad-Dahhak said, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And they say, "Our hearts are uncovered"﴾ He said: They said, "Our hearts are filled with knowledge; they have no need of the knowledge of Muhammad or of anyone else."

'Ata' al-'Awfi said: ﴿And they say, "Our hearts are uncovered"﴾ meaning: receptacles for knowledge.

On this meaning is the reading of some of the Ansar (some of the cities) as transmitted by Ibn Jarir: "wa qalu qulubuna ghulof," with a damma on the lam, meaning the plural of ghilaf, i.e., receptacles, in the sense that they claimed their hearts are filled with knowledge with which they need no other knowledge, just as they used to boast of the knowledge of the Torah. For this reason He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Rather, Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so little is it that they believe﴾, meaning: the matter is not as they claimed; rather their hearts are cursed and sealed upon, as He said in Surat an-Nisa': ﴿And for their saying, "Our hearts are uncovered." Rather, Allah has sealed them for their disbelief, so they do not believe except a little﴾ [an-Nisa': 155]. They have differed regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿so little is it that they believe﴾ and His saying ﴿so they do not believe except a little﴾. Some of them said: little of them believe. [Fakhr al-Din al-Razi preferred this and related it from Qatadah, al-Asamm and Abu Muslim al-Isfahani.] It was also said: little is their faith, meaning that they believe in what Moses brought them concerning the Return, the reward and the punishment, but it is a faith that does not benefit them, because it is overwhelmed by what they disbelieved of what Muhammad ﷺ brought them.

Some of them said: they were not believers in anything at all, and He said ﴿so little is it that they believe﴾ while they are disbelievers in all of it, just as the Arabs say: "Seldom have I seen the like of this ever," meaning: I have never seen the like of this ever. [Al-Kisa'i said: The Arabs say: "Whoever commits fornication in a land where little grows (qallama tunbit)," meaning: it grows nothing.]

Ibn Jarir related it, and Allah knows best.

The Most High says: ﴿And when there came to them﴾ meaning the Jews ﴿a Book from Allah﴾, which is the Qur'an revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿confirming what was with them﴾, meaning the Torah. His saying ﴿and before this they used to seek victory over those who disbelieved﴾ means: before this Messenger came with this Book, they used to seek victory through his coming over their enemies among the polytheists when they fought them. They would say: "A Prophet will be sent at the end of time, and we will kill you alongside him, a killing like that of 'Ad and Iram," as Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated, on the authority of Asim ibn Umar, on the authority of Qatadah al-Ansari, on the authority of some of their elders, who said: They said: "By Allah, this story was revealed about us and about them, meaning about the Ansar and about the Jews who were their neighbours: ﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming what was with them, and before this they used to seek victory over those who disbelieved; but when there came to them that which they recognised, they disbelieved in it﴾." They said: "We had dominated them for ages in the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance), while we were people of polytheism and they were people of the Book. They used to say: 'A Prophet is about to be sent now, and we will follow him; his time has drawn near. We will kill you alongside him, a killing like that of 'Ad and Iram.' When Allah sent His Messenger from the Quraysh [and we followed him], they disbelieved in him." Allah the Most High says: ﴿So when there came to them that which they recognised, they disbelieved in it; so the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers﴾ [al-Nisa': 155].

Al-Dahhak narrated, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿and before this they used to seek victory over those who disbelieved﴾, that he said: "They would seek support, saying: 'We will help Muhammad against them,' and they were not so; they were lying."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad informed me: Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr informed me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that the Jews used to seek victory against the Aws and the Khazraj through the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) before his mission. When Allah sent him from among the Arabs, they disbelieved in him and denied what they used to say about him. Mu'adh ibn Jabal and Bishr ibn al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur, brother of the Banu Salamah, said to them: "O assembly of Jews, fear Allah and embrace Islam; you used to seek victory over us through Muhammad (ﷺ) while we were people of polytheism, and you used to inform us that he would be sent, and you would describe him to us by his description." Salam ibn Mishkam, brother of the Banu al-Nadir, said: "He has brought us nothing that we recognise, and he is not the one we used to mention to you." So Allah revealed concerning that saying of theirs: ﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming what was with them, and before this they used to seek victory over those who disbelieved; but when there came to them that which they recognised, they disbelieved in it; so the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers﴾. [See: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (1/547) and Tafsir al-Tabari (2/233).]

Al-Awfi narrated, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: ﴿and before this they used to seek victory over those who disbelieved﴾ means: they used to seek help through the coming out of Muhammad (ﷺ) against the polytheists of the Arabs, meaning by this the People of the Book. But when Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent and they saw him from other than their own people, they disbelieved in him and envied him.

Abu al-Aliyah said: The Jews used to seek help through Muhammad (ﷺ) against the polytheists of the Arabs, saying: "O Allah, send this Prophet whom we find written with us, so that we may punish the polytheists and kill them." But when Allah sent Muhammad (ﷺ), and they saw that he was from other than them, they disbelieved in him out of envy for the Arabs, while they knew that he was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So Allah said: ﴿So when there came to them that which they recognised, they disbelieved in it; so the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers﴾.

Qatadah said concerning ﴿and before this they used to seek victory over those who disbelieved﴾: "They used to say: 'Indeed a Prophet will come.' ﴿But when there came to them that which they recognised, they disbelieved in it﴾."

Mujahid said concerning ﴿So when there came to them that which they recognised, they disbelieved in it; so the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers﴾: "They are the Jews."

Imam Ahmad said: Ya'qub narrated to us, my father narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, Salih ibn Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf narrated to me, on the authority of Mahmud ibn Labid, brother of the Banu Abd al-Ashhal, on the authority of Salamah ibn Salamah ibn Waqsh, who was among the people of Badr (the battle), who said: We had a Jewish neighbour among the Banu Abd al-Ashhal. He came out to us one day from his house, a short while before the mission of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), until he stood at the gathering of the Banu Abd al-Ashhal. Salamah said: I was on that day the youngest of them in age, lying on a cloak in the courtyard of my family's house. He mentioned the Resurrection, the Day of Reckoning, the good deeds, the Balance, Paradise and Hellfire. He said this to people of polytheism, worshippers of idols, who did not believe in any resurrection after death. They said to him: "Woe to you, so-and-so! Do you think this will indeed happen, that people will be raised after their death to an abode in which there is Paradise and Hellfire, where they will be recompensed for their deeds?" He said: "Yes, by the One by whom oaths are sworn, he would wish that he had, as his share of that Fire, the greatest oven in the world, which they would heat up, then put him into it and seal it over him, and that he might be saved from that Fire tomorrow." They said to him: "Woe to you, and what is the sign of that?" He said: "A Prophet who will be sent from the direction of these lands," and he pointed with his hand towards Makkah and Yemen. They said: "And when will we see him?" Salamah said: He looked at me, and I was the youngest of them in age, and said: "If this boy lives out his lifespan, he will reach him." Salamah said: "By Allah, the night and the day had not passed before Allah sent His Messenger (ﷺ) while he was among us; so we believed in him, and he disbelieved in him out of rebellion and envy."

We said: "Woe to you, so-and-so! Are you not the one who said this to us?" He said: "Yes, but he is not the one." Ahmad alone narrated it. [al-Musnad (3/467).]

Al-Qurtubi and others related, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Jews of Khaybar fought in the time of Jahiliyyah with the Ghatafan, and the Ghatafan defeated them. So the Jews then supplicated, saying: "O Allah, we ask You by the right of the unlettered Prophet whom You promised us to bring forth at the end of time, that You help us against them." He said: "So they were given victory over them." He said: "And thus they used to do: they would call upon Allah, and they would be given victory over their enemies and those who attacked them." Allah the Most High said: ﴿So when there came to them that which they recognised﴾, meaning of the truth and the description of Muhammad (ﷺ), "they disbelieved in it"; so the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers.

Mujahid said: "Wretched is that for which they sold themselves" (Qur'an 2:90): the Jews sold the truth for falsehood, and concealed what Muhammad ﷺ had brought by not making it clear.

As-Suddi said: "Wretched is that for which they sold themselves" means: they sold themselves for it, i.e., how wretched is what they exchanged for their souls and were content with, [and they turned from disbelief in what Allah had sent down to Muhammad ﷺ to confirming him, supporting him and aiding him].

What drove them to this was rebellion (al-baghy), envy and hatred, "that Allah should send down of His bounty upon whom He wills of His servants." There is no envy greater than this.

Ibn Ishaq narrated from Muhammad, from Ikrimah or Sa'id, from Ibn Abbas: "Wretched is that for which they sold themselves: that they should disbelieve in what Allah has sent down, out of rebellion that Allah should send down of His bounty upon whom He wills of His servants." That is: Allah made it [prophethood] to be from others than them. "So they returned with anger upon anger." Ibn Abbas said: "Anger upon anger: His anger upon them for what they had wasted of the Torah, which was with them, and His anger upon them for their disbelief in this Prophet whom Allah had sent to them."

I say: The meaning of "they returned" (ba'u) is that they deserved, merited and settled into anger upon anger. Abu al-Aliyah said: Allah became angry with them for their disbelief in the Gospel and in Jesus, then He became angry with them for their disbelief in Muhammad and the Qur'an [in the editions: "for their disbelief in Muhammad and the Qur'an"], peace be upon them both. [And from Ikrimah and Qatadah the like of it.]

As-Suddi said: As for the first anger, it was when He became angry with them over the calf; as for the second anger, He became angry with them when they disbelieved in Muhammad ﷺ. [And from Ibn Abbas the like of it.]

* *

As for His saying: "And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment": since their disbelief was caused by rebellion and envy, and the origin of that was arrogance, they were repaid with humiliation and abasement in this world and the Hereafter, as the Exalted said: "Indeed, those who are too arrogant to worship Me will enter Hell humiliated" (Ghafir 40:60) [i.e., abased, despised, debased, subdued].

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya narrated to us, Ibn Ajlan narrated to us, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The arrogant will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection in the forms of men, like ants (al-dharr), overwhelmed by abasement from every direction, until they enter a prison in Hell called Bulas; the fire of fires will overwhelm them, and they will be given to drink from *tinat al-khabal*, the residue of the people of the Fire." [Al-Musnad (2/179).]

God says: ﴿And when it is said to them﴾, meaning to the Jews and those like them among the People of the Book, ﴿"Believe in what Allah has sent down"﴾, meaning [in] what He sent down upon Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿"and affirm him and follow him,"﴾ they say, ﴿"We believe in what was sent down to us,"﴾ meaning: believing in what was sent down to us, the Torah and the Gospel, suffices us, and we acknowledge nothing but that. ﴿And they disbelieve in what is beyond it﴾, meaning: what comes after it, ﴿while it is the truth, confirming what is with them﴾. That is, while they know that what was sent down to Muhammad (ﷺ) is the truth. ﴿Confirming﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: in the state of confirming what they have of the Torah and the Gospel. Thus the proof is established against them by this, as God says: ﴿Those to whom We have given the Scripture recognize it as they recognize their own sons﴾ [al-Baqarah: 146]. Then God says: ﴿Say, "Why did you kill the prophets of Allah before, if you were believers?"﴾, meaning: if you were truthful in your claim to believe in what was sent down to you, then why did you kill the prophets who came to you confirming the Torah that is in your hands, judging by it, and not abrogating it (naskh, abrogation), while you know their truthfulness? You killed them out of insolence, envy, obstinacy, and arrogance toward the messengers of Allah. So you follow nothing but mere desires, opinions, and whims, as God says: ﴿Is it that whenever a messenger came to you with what your souls did not desire, you were arrogant? So some you denied and some you killed﴾ [al-Baqarah: 87].

Al-Suddi said: In this verse, God rebukes them: ﴿Say, "Why then did you kill the prophets of Allah before, if you were believers?"﴾

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: Say, O Muhammad, to the Jews of the Children of Israel, when you say to them, "Believe in what Allah has sent down," they say, "We believe in what was sent down to us": "Why do you kill—if you, O assembly of Jews, are believers in what Allah has sent down to you—His prophets, when Allah has forbidden their killing in the Book that was sent down to you? Rather, He has commanded you in it to follow them, obey them, and affirm them." This is God's denial of their statement, "We believe in what was sent down to us," and a rebuke to them.

﴿And Moses had certainly come to you with clear evidences﴾, meaning: with clear signs and conclusive proofs that he was the messenger of Allah and that there is no god but Allah. The clear evidences are: the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the staff, the hand, the splitting of the sea, the shading of them with clouds, the manna and quails, the stone, and other signs that they witnessed. ﴿Then you took the calf﴾, meaning: as a deity besides Allah, in the time of Moses and after his signs. His words ﴿after him﴾ mean: after he had gone away from you to Mount Sinai for private conversation with Allah, as God says: ﴿And the people of Moses took, after him, from their ornaments a calf, a body having a lowing sound﴾ [al-A'raf: 148]. ﴿And you were wrongdoers﴾, meaning: in this deed you did, in worshipping the calf, while you knew that there is no god but Allah, as God says: ﴿And when they regretted and saw that they had gone astray, they said, "If our Lord does not have mercy upon us and forgive us, we will surely be among the losers"﴾ [al-A'raf: 149].

God says: ﴿And when it is said to them﴾, meaning to the Jews and those like them among the People of the Book, ﴿"Believe in what Allah has sent down"﴾, meaning [in] what He sent down upon Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿"and affirm him and follow him,"﴾ they say, ﴿"We believe in what was sent down to us,"﴾ meaning: believing in what was sent down to us, the Torah and the Gospel, suffices us, and we acknowledge nothing but that. ﴿And they disbelieve in what is beyond it﴾, meaning: what comes after it, ﴿while it is the truth, confirming what is with them﴾. That is, while they know that what was sent down to Muhammad (ﷺ) is the truth. ﴿Confirming﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: in the state of confirming what they have of the Torah and the Gospel. Thus the proof is established against them by this, as God says: ﴿Those to whom We have given the Scripture recognize it as they recognize their own sons﴾ [al-Baqarah: 146]. Then God says: ﴿Say, "Why did you kill the prophets of Allah before, if you were believers?"﴾, meaning: if you were truthful in your claim to believe in what was sent down to you, then why did you kill the prophets who came to you confirming the Torah that is in your hands, judging by it, and not abrogating it (naskh, abrogation), while you know their truthfulness? You killed them out of insolence, envy, obstinacy, and arrogance toward the messengers of Allah. So you follow nothing but mere desires, opinions, and whims, as God says: ﴿Is it that whenever a messenger came to you with what your souls did not desire, you were arrogant? So some you denied and some you killed﴾ [al-Baqarah: 87].

Al-Suddi said: In this verse, God rebukes them: ﴿Say, "Why then did you kill the prophets of Allah before, if you were believers?"﴾

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: Say, O Muhammad, to the Jews of the Children of Israel, when you say to them, "Believe in what Allah has sent down," they say, "We believe in what was sent down to us": "Why do you kill—if you, O assembly of Jews, are believers in what Allah has sent down to you—His prophets, when Allah has forbidden their killing in the Book that was sent down to you? Rather, He has commanded you in it to follow them, obey them, and affirm them." This is God's denial of their statement, "We believe in what was sent down to us," and a rebuke to them.

﴿And Moses had certainly come to you with clear evidences﴾, meaning: with clear signs and conclusive proofs that he was the messenger of Allah and that there is no god but Allah. The clear evidences are: the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the staff, the hand, the splitting of the sea, the shading of them with clouds, the manna and quails, the stone, and other signs that they witnessed. ﴿Then you took the calf﴾, meaning: as a deity besides Allah, in the time of Moses and after his signs. His words ﴿after him﴾ mean: after he had gone away from you to Mount Sinai for private conversation with Allah, as God says: ﴿And the people of Moses took, after him, from their ornaments a calf, a body having a lowing sound﴾ [al-A'raf: 148]. ﴿And you were wrongdoers﴾, meaning: in this deed you did, in worshipping the calf, while you knew that there is no god but Allah, as God says: ﴿And when they regretted and saw that they had gone astray, they said, "If our Lord does not have mercy upon us and forgive us, we will surely be among the losers"﴾ [al-A'raf: 149].

He, may He be blessed and exalted, enumerates their errors, their violation of the covenant, their obstinacy, and their turning away from it, to the point that He raised the Mount (al-Tur) over them until they accepted it, and then they broke it. For this reason He said: ﴿They said, "We hear and we disobey."﴾ The explanation of this has already passed.

﴿And the calf was made to sink into their hearts because of their disbelief.﴾ 'Abd al-Razzaq related from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and the calf was made to sink into their hearts [because of their disbelief]﴾ [[Addition from manuscripts J, T, B, W.]], that he said: "They were made to drink [into their hearts] [[Addition from manuscripts J, T, B, W.]] its love, until that love reached deep into their hearts." Abu al-'Aliyah and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said the same.

Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il [[In manuscript A: "Isma'il"]]... (chain as follows): Isam ibn Khalid related to us, Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Maryam al-Ghassani related to me, from Khalid ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, from Bilal ibn Abi al-Darda', from Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Your love for a thing blinds you and deafens you."

Abu Dawud also related it from Hayawah ibn Shurayh, from Baqiyyah, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Maryam, with the same wording [[Al-Musnad (5/194) and Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 5130.]].

al-Suddi said: Musa (peace be upon him) took the calf, slaughtered it, then burned it with a file (al-mibrad), then scattered it into the sea. No sea that flowed that day was left without some of it falling into it. Then Musa said to them, "Drink from it." So they drank, and whoever had loved it had gold come out on his upper lip. This is when Allah, exalted, says: ﴿And the calf was made to sink into their hearts.﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Raja' related to us, Isra'il related to us [[In manuscript A: "Isma'il related to us."]], from Abu Ishaq, from 'Umarah ibn 'Abd [[In manuscript H: "'Abd Allah," which is an error.]] and Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: Musa went to the calf, placed files upon it, and filed it down while it was on the bank of a river. No one among those who had worshipped the calf drank from that water without his face turning yellow like gold [[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/282).]].

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said regarding ﴿and the calf was made to sink into their hearts﴾: "When the calf was burned, it was ground down and then scattered, and they drank the water until their faces became like saffron."

al-Qurtubi related from the book of al-Qushayri that no one who had worshipped the calf drank from it except that he was [[Addition from manuscripts A, W.]] then al-Qurtubi said: "This is something other than what is meant here, because the purpose of this context is that the traces of the gold appeared on their lips and faces, whereas what is mentioned here is that they were made to drink the love of the calf into their hearts, meaning during their worship of it." Then he recited the words of al-Nabighah regarding his wife 'Athmah:

The love of 'Athmah has seeped into my heart,
so what is apparent of it and what is hidden are equal.

It has seeped where no drink reaches,
nor sorrow, nor joy can reach.

Whenever I recall our covenant with her,
I nearly fly, if a human could fly.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Say: "Wretched is what your faith commands you, if you are believers."﴾ That is: Wretched is what you rely upon, in the ancient and recent times, of your disbelief in the signs of Allah and your opposition to the prophets. Then your reliance on your disbelief in Muhammad (ﷺ), and this is the greatest of your sins and the most grievous of matters for you, since you disbelieved in the Seal of the Messengers, the master of the prophets and messengers, sent to all people. So how can you claim faith for yourselves when you have committed these ugly deeds: breaking your covenants, disbelieving in the signs of Allah, and worshipping the calf?!

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 94–96 (part 1 of 2):

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: Allah said to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Say: If the Last Abode with Allah is exclusively for you, to the exclusion of the people, then wish for death, if you are truthful.﴾ That is: call for death upon whichever of the two groups is the liar. But they refused this of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). ﴿And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forward. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾ That is: due to their knowledge of what they have of knowledge about you, and their disbelief in that. Had they wished for it on the day he said that to them, not a Jew would have remained on the earth but would have died.

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Then wish for death﴾ means: ask for death.

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from 'Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, from Ikrimah, regarding His words: ﴿Then wish for death, if you are truthful﴾, he said: Ibn 'Abbas said: If the Jews had wished for death, they would have died.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi narrated to us, 'Abbad narrated to us, I heard al-A'mash say — he said: I think it is only from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr — from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: If they had wished for death, one of them would have choked on his saliva.

These are sound chains of narration to Ibn 'Abbas.

Ibn Jarir said in his Tafsir: "It has reached us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'If the Jews had wished for death, they would have died, and they would have seen their seats in the Fire. And if those who challenged the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to mubahala had gone out, they would have returned finding neither family nor property.'" This was narrated to us by Abu Kurayb, who said: Zakariyya ibn 'Adi narrated to us, who said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Karim, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Imam Ahmad also narrated it from Isma'il ibn Yazid al-Raqqi (Abu Yazid), who said: Furat narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Karim, with the same wording. [Tafsir al-Tabari (2/362) and al-Musnad (1/248).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Surur ibn al-Mughira narrated to us, from 'Abbad ibn Mansur, from al-Hasan, who said regarding Allah's words: ﴿They would never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forward.﴾ I said: What do you think, if they had loved death when it was said to them, "Wish for it," would they have been dead? He said: No, by Allah, they would not have died even if they had wished for death, and they would not have wished for it, and Allah has said what you have heard: ﴿And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forward. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾

This is a strange report from al-Hasan. Then, this interpretation that Ibn 'Abbas gave of the verse is the most evident, and it is the invocation of a curse upon whichever of the two groups is more lying, of them or of the Muslims, by way of mubahala. Ibn Jarir transmitted it from Qatadah, Abu al-'Aliyah, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas, may Allah have mercy on them.

A parallel to this verse is His words in Surah al-Jumu'ah: ﴿Say: O you who have become Jews, if you claim that you are allies of Allah, to the exclusion of the people, then wish for death, if you are truthful. But they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forward. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers. Say: Indeed, the death from which you flee will surely meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do.﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 6–8]. Since they claimed that they were the sons of Allah and His beloved, and said: "None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian," they were called to mubahala and to invoke a curse upon the more lying of the two groups, of them or of the Muslims. When they shrank from this, everyone knew that they were wrongdoers, for had they been firm in what they held, they would have proceeded to it; and since they held back, their lie became known. This is like what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did with the delegation of Najran from the Christians, after the proof had been established against them in the debate, and in their obstinacy and stubbornness, by calling them to mubahala. Allah says: ﴿Whoever argues with you concerning it after the knowledge has come to you, say: "Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves; then let us invoke and place the curse of Allah upon the liars."﴾ [Al 'Imran: 61]. When they saw that, some of the people said to others: "By Allah, if you invoke a curse upon this Prophet, not one eye among you will remain that blinks." At that, they inclined to peace and offered the jizyah, "willingly, and they are humbled," so he imposed it upon them, and he sent with them Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, may Allah be pleased with him, as a trustee. A similar meaning, or something close to it, is His saying to His Prophet (ﷺ) that he should say to the polytheists: ﴿Say: Whoever is in error, the Most Merciful will extend for him an extension﴾ [Maryam: 75], that is: whoever among us or among you is in error, Allah increases him in what he is in and extends for him, and leads him gradually (istidraj), as will come its explanation in its proper place, Allah willing.

As for those who interpret the verse according to the meaning: ﴿Say: If the Last Abode with Allah is exclusively for you, to the exclusion of the people, then wish for death, if you are truthful﴾, meaning: if you are truthful in your claim, then wish for death now. These did not address mubahala, as some of the theologians and others have affirmed, and Ibn Jarir inclined to it after he had come close to the first view. He said: The discussion regarding the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words: ﴿Say: If the Last Abode with Allah is exclusively for you, to the exclusion of the people, then wish for death, if you are truthful﴾ — this verse is among those by which Allah argued with His Prophet (ﷺ) against the Jews who were among the inhabitants of his place of migration (Medina), and by which He exposed their rabbis and scholars. That is because Allah the Exalted commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to a just judgment between him and them regarding the dispute that existed between them, just as He commanded him to call the other group of Christians, if they opposed him concerning 'Isa ibn Maryam, peace be upon him, and argued with him about it, to a decisive resolution between him and them through mubahala. He said to a group of the Jews: "If you are right, then wish for death, for that will not harm you, if you are right in what you claim of faith and nearness of station to Allah. Rather, I will give you your wish of death if you wish it, for you will only go to rest from the toil of this world and its hardship and the turbidity of its life, and to the triumph of being in the neighborhood of Allah in His gardens, if the matter is as you claim: that the Last Abode is exclusively yours, to the exclusion of us. And if you do not wish for it, the people will know that you are the falsifiers and we are the right ones in our claim, and our matter and yours will be revealed to them." So the Jews refrained from answering this, because they knew that if they wished for death they would perish, their worldly life would go, and they would reach everlasting disgrace in their afterlife, just as a group of the Christians refrained.

This speech of his, its beginning is good, but as for its ending there is an issue: for on this interpretation the proof does not become manifest against them, since it may be said: it does not follow from their believing that they are truthful in their claim that they would wish for death, for there is no necessary link between being righteous and wishing for death. How many a righteous person does not wish for death, but rather loves to be granted a long life so that he may increase in good and raise his rank in Paradise, as came in the hadith: "The best of you is the one whose life is long and whose deeds are good." [This came from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Busr, Abu Bakrah, and Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with them. As for the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Busr, al-Tirmidhi narrated it in al-Sunan (no. 2329) and said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith from this route." As for the hadith of Abu Bakrah, al-Tirmidhi narrated it in al-Sunan (no. 2330) and said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." As for the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad (2/235).] [And it has come in the Sahih the prohibition of wishing for death, and in some of its wordings: "Let none of you wish for death because of a harm that has befallen him; if he is a good-doer, perhaps he will increase, and if he is an evildoer, perhaps he will repent." [Sahih al-Bukhari (no. 5671) and Sahih Muslim (no. 2680) from the hadith of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him.]] And they could also say on this: "Behold, you, O Muslims, believe that you are the people of Paradise, and yet you do not wish for death in a state of health; how then do you oblige us to what we do not oblige you?"

All of this arises only from interpreting the verse in this sense. But according to the interpretation of Ibn 'Abbas nothing of this follows, rather it is said to them a decisive statement: If you believe that you are the allies of Allah to the exclusion of the people, and that you are the sons of Allah and His beloved, and that you are among the people of Paradise while whoever else there is among the people of Hell, then invoke the curse upon one another and call down a curse upon the liars among you or among others, and know that mubahala will certainly uproot the liar. When they were certain of this and recognized its truth, they shrank from mubahala because of what they knew of their lying, their fabrication, their concealment of the truth concerning the attributes and description of the Messenger (ﷺ), though they recognize him as they recognize their own sons and are certain of him. So everyone knew their falsehood, their disgrace, their error and their obstinacy — upon them be the successive curses of Allah until the Day of Resurrection.

[This mubahala was named "wishing" (tamanni) because every person of truth wishes that Allah would destroy the falsifier who debates with him, especially when in that is a proof for him by which his truth and its manifestation are made clear. And the mubahala was by death, because life is precious and great to them, for they know the evil of their final destination after death.]

For this reason Allah said: ﴿And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forward. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers. And you will surely find them the most eager of people for life﴾ — that is: [the most eager of creation for life], that is: for long life, because of what they know of their evil destination and their losing outcome with Allah; for this world is the prison of the believer and the paradise of the disbeliever, so they wish that they could delay from the station of the Hereafter by every means possible. And what they fear is certain to befall them without doubt, even though they are the most eager [of people] of the polytheists who have no scripture. This is from the category of specific mentioned after general.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Muslim al-Batin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿And of those who associated partners﴾: he said: They are the non-Arabs (al-a'ajim).

Ibn Abi Hatim (1/286) and al-Mustadrak (2/263).

Al-Hakim also narrated it in his al-Mustadrak from the hadith of al-Thawri, and said: "It is sahih according to their (al-Bukhari and Muslim's) condition, though they did not record it." He said: "They both agreed upon the chain of a companion's tafsir."

Al-Hasan al-Basri said regarding ﴿And you will surely find them the most avid of people for life﴾: "The hypocrite is the most avid of people for life, and he is more avid for life than the polytheist." ﴿Each one of them wishes﴾ means: each one of the Jews, as the context of the wording indicates.

Abu al-Aliyah said: ﴿Each one of them wishes﴾ refers to the Magians (Majus), and it returns to the first (group).

﴿Were he given a life of a thousand years﴾. Al-A'mash narrated from Muslim al-Bateen, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Each one of them wishes, were he given a life of a thousand years﴾. He said: "It is like the Persian saying, 'Zeh hazar sal', meaning ten thousand years." The same was also narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr himself.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq narrated to us, saying: I heard my father say: Abu Hamzah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Each one of them wishes, were he given a life of a thousand years﴾. He said: "It refers to the non-Arabs: 'Hazarsal, Nowruz, Mihrajan'."

Mujahid said regarding ﴿Each one of them wishes, were he given a life of a thousand years﴾: "Sin was made beloved to them throughout the length of their lives."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Muhammad, from Sa'id or Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿And it is not one who will remove him from the punishment by being granted life﴾: that is, it will not save him from the punishment. This is because the polytheist does not hope for resurrection after death, so he loves a long life; and the Jew has known what disgrace awaits him in the Hereafter because of what he did, through the knowledge he possesses.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿And it is not one who will remove him from the punishment by being granted life﴾: "They are the ones who opposed Jibril."

Abu al-Aliyah and Ibn Umar said: ﴿So that will not save him from the punishment, nor will it deliver him from it.﴾

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said regarding this verse: "The Jews are more avid for this life than these (the Magians). And these wish that one of them be given a life of a thousand years, yet that would not remove him from the punishment even if he were granted life, just as Iblis was granted life but it did not benefit him, since he was a disbeliever."

﴿And Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾: that is, Knowing of what His servants do of good and evil, and He will recompense every doer for his deed.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said regarding ﴿And you will surely find them the most avid of people for life﴾: "The hypocrite is the most avid of people for life, and he is more avid for life than the polytheist." ﴿Each one of them wishes﴾ means: each one of the Jews, as the context of the wording indicates.

Abu al-Aliyah said: ﴿Each one of them wishes﴾ refers to the Magians (Majus), and it returns to the first (group).

﴿Were he given a life of a thousand years﴾. Al-A'mash narrated from Muslim al-Bateen, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Each one of them wishes, were he given a life of a thousand years﴾. He said: "It is like the Persian saying, 'Zeh hazar sal', meaning ten thousand years." The same was also narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr himself.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq narrated to us, saying: I heard my father say: Abu Hamzah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Each one of them wishes, were he given a life of a thousand years﴾. He said: "It refers to the non-Arabs: 'Hazarsal, Nowruz, Mihrajan'."

Mujahid said regarding ﴿Each one of them wishes, were he given a life of a thousand years﴾: "Sin was made beloved to them throughout the length of their lives."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Muhammad, from Sa'id or Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿And it is not one who will remove him from the punishment by being granted life﴾: that is, it will not save him from the punishment. This is because the polytheist does not hope for resurrection after death, so he loves a long life; and the Jew has known what disgrace awaits him in the Hereafter because of what he did, through the knowledge he possesses.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿And it is not one who will remove him from the punishment by being granted life﴾: "They are the ones who opposed Jibril."

Abu al-Aliyah and Ibn Umar said: ﴿So that will not save him from the punishment, nor will it deliver him from it.﴾

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said regarding this verse: "The Jews are more avid for this life than these (the Magians). And these wish that one of them be given a life of a thousand years, yet that would not remove him from the punishment even if he were granted life, just as Iblis was granted life but it did not benefit him, since he was a disbeliever."

﴿And Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾: that is, Knowing of what His servants do of good and evil, and He will recompense every doer for his deed.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 94–96 (part 1 of 2):

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: Allah said to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Say: If the Last Abode with Allah is exclusively for you, to the exclusion of the people, then wish for death, if you are truthful.﴾ That is: call for death upon whichever of the two groups is the liar. But they refused this of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). ﴿And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forward. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾ That is: due to their knowledge of what they have of knowledge about you, and their disbelief in that. Had they wished for it on the day he said that to them, not a Jew would have remained on the earth but would have died.

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Then wish for death﴾ means: ask for death.

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from 'Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, from Ikrimah, regarding His words: ﴿Then wish for death, if you are truthful﴾, he said: Ibn 'Abbas said: If the Jews had wished for death, they would have died.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi narrated to us, 'Abbad narrated to us, I heard al-A'mash say — he said: I think it is only from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr — from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: If they had wished for death, one of them would have choked on his saliva.

These are sound chains of narration to Ibn 'Abbas.

Ibn Jarir said in his Tafsir: "It has reached us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'If the Jews had wished for death, they would have died, and they would have seen their seats in the Fire. And if those who challenged the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to mubahala had gone out, they would have returned finding neither family nor property.'" This was narrated to us by Abu Kurayb, who said: Zakariyya ibn 'Adi narrated to us, who said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Karim, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Imam Ahmad also narrated it from Isma'il ibn Yazid al-Raqqi (Abu Yazid), who said: Furat narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Karim, with the same wording. [Tafsir al-Tabari (2/362) and al-Musnad (1/248).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Surur ibn al-Mughira narrated to us, from 'Abbad ibn Mansur, from al-Hasan, who said regarding Allah's words: ﴿They would never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forward.﴾ I said: What do you think, if they had loved death when it was said to them, "Wish for it," would they have been dead? He said: No, by Allah, they would not have died even if they had wished for death, and they would not have wished for it, and Allah has said what you have heard: ﴿And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forward. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾

This is a strange report from al-Hasan. Then, this interpretation that Ibn 'Abbas gave of the verse is the most evident, and it is the invocation of a curse upon whichever of the two groups is more lying, of them or of the Muslims, by way of mubahala. Ibn Jarir transmitted it from Qatadah, Abu al-'Aliyah, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas, may Allah have mercy on them.

A parallel to this verse is His words in Surah al-Jumu'ah: ﴿Say: O you who have become Jews, if you claim that you are allies of Allah, to the exclusion of the people, then wish for death, if you are truthful. But they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forward. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers. Say: Indeed, the death from which you flee will surely meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do.﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 6–8]. Since they claimed that they were the sons of Allah and His beloved, and said: "None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian," they were called to mubahala and to invoke a curse upon the more lying of the two groups, of them or of the Muslims. When they shrank from this, everyone knew that they were wrongdoers, for had they been firm in what they held, they would have proceeded to it; and since they held back, their lie became known. This is like what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did with the delegation of Najran from the Christians, after the proof had been established against them in the debate, and in their obstinacy and stubbornness, by calling them to mubahala. Allah says: ﴿Whoever argues with you concerning it after the knowledge has come to you, say: "Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves; then let us invoke and place the curse of Allah upon the liars."﴾ [Al 'Imran: 61]. When they saw that, some of the people said to others: "By Allah, if you invoke a curse upon this Prophet, not one eye among you will remain that blinks." At that, they inclined to peace and offered the jizyah, "willingly, and they are humbled," so he imposed it upon them, and he sent with them Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, may Allah be pleased with him, as a trustee. A similar meaning, or something close to it, is His saying to His Prophet (ﷺ) that he should say to the polytheists: ﴿Say: Whoever is in error, the Most Merciful will extend for him an extension﴾ [Maryam: 75], that is: whoever among us or among you is in error, Allah increases him in what he is in and extends for him, and leads him gradually (istidraj), as will come its explanation in its proper place, Allah willing.

As for those who interpret the verse according to the meaning: ﴿Say: If the Last Abode with Allah is exclusively for you, to the exclusion of the people, then wish for death, if you are truthful﴾, meaning: if you are truthful in your claim, then wish for death now. These did not address mubahala, as some of the theologians and others have affirmed, and Ibn Jarir inclined to it after he had come close to the first view. He said: The discussion regarding the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words: ﴿Say: If the Last Abode with Allah is exclusively for you, to the exclusion of the people, then wish for death, if you are truthful﴾ — this verse is among those by which Allah argued with His Prophet (ﷺ) against the Jews who were among the inhabitants of his place of migration (Medina), and by which He exposed their rabbis and scholars. That is because Allah the Exalted commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to a just judgment between him and them regarding the dispute that existed between them, just as He commanded him to call the other group of Christians, if they opposed him concerning 'Isa ibn Maryam, peace be upon him, and argued with him about it, to a decisive resolution between him and them through mubahala. He said to a group of the Jews: "If you are right, then wish for death, for that will not harm you, if you are right in what you claim of faith and nearness of station to Allah. Rather, I will give you your wish of death if you wish it, for you will only go to rest from the toil of this world and its hardship and the turbidity of its life, and to the triumph of being in the neighborhood of Allah in His gardens, if the matter is as you claim: that the Last Abode is exclusively yours, to the exclusion of us. And if you do not wish for it, the people will know that you are the falsifiers and we are the right ones in our claim, and our matter and yours will be revealed to them." So the Jews refrained from answering this, because they knew that if they wished for death they would perish, their worldly life would go, and they would reach everlasting disgrace in their afterlife, just as a group of the Christians refrained.

This speech of his, its beginning is good, but as for its ending there is an issue: for on this interpretation the proof does not become manifest against them, since it may be said: it does not follow from their believing that they are truthful in their claim that they would wish for death, for there is no necessary link between being righteous and wishing for death. How many a righteous person does not wish for death, but rather loves to be granted a long life so that he may increase in good and raise his rank in Paradise, as came in the hadith: "The best of you is the one whose life is long and whose deeds are good." [This came from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Busr, Abu Bakrah, and Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with them. As for the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Busr, al-Tirmidhi narrated it in al-Sunan (no. 2329) and said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith from this route." As for the hadith of Abu Bakrah, al-Tirmidhi narrated it in al-Sunan (no. 2330) and said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." As for the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad (2/235).] [And it has come in the Sahih the prohibition of wishing for death, and in some of its wordings: "Let none of you wish for death because of a harm that has befallen him; if he is a good-doer, perhaps he will increase, and if he is an evildoer, perhaps he will repent." [Sahih al-Bukhari (no. 5671) and Sahih Muslim (no. 2680) from the hadith of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him.]] And they could also say on this: "Behold, you, O Muslims, believe that you are the people of Paradise, and yet you do not wish for death in a state of health; how then do you oblige us to what we do not oblige you?"

All of this arises only from interpreting the verse in this sense. But according to the interpretation of Ibn 'Abbas nothing of this follows, rather it is said to them a decisive statement: If you believe that you are the allies of Allah to the exclusion of the people, and that you are the sons of Allah and His beloved, and that you are among the people of Paradise while whoever else there is among the people of Hell, then invoke the curse upon one another and call down a curse upon the liars among you or among others, and know that mubahala will certainly uproot the liar. When they were certain of this and recognized its truth, they shrank from mubahala because of what they knew of their lying, their fabrication, their concealment of the truth concerning the attributes and description of the Messenger (ﷺ), though they recognize him as they recognize their own sons and are certain of him. So everyone knew their falsehood, their disgrace, their error and their obstinacy — upon them be the successive curses of Allah until the Day of Resurrection.

[This mubahala was named "wishing" (tamanni) because every person of truth wishes that Allah would destroy the falsifier who debates with him, especially when in that is a proof for him by which his truth and its manifestation are made clear. And the mubahala was by death, because life is precious and great to them, for they know the evil of their final destination after death.]

For this reason Allah said: ﴿And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forward. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers. And you will surely find them the most eager of people for life﴾ — that is: [the most eager of creation for life], that is: for long life, because of what they know of their evil destination and their losing outcome with Allah; for this world is the prison of the believer and the paradise of the disbeliever, so they wish that they could delay from the station of the Hereafter by every means possible. And what they fear is certain to befall them without doubt, even though they are the most eager [of people] of the polytheists who have no scripture. This is from the category of specific mentioned after general.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Muslim al-Batin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿And of those who associated partners﴾: he said: They are the non-Arabs (al-a'ajim).

Al-Hakim also narrated it in his al-Mustadrak from the hadith of al-Thawri, and said: "It is sahih according to their (al-Bukhari and Muslim's) condition, though they did not record it." He said: "They both agreed upon the chain of a companion's tafsir."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verses 97–98 (part 1 of 3):

The Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir al-Tabari (may Allah have mercy on him) said: All the people of knowledge of ta'wil (interpretation) agreed [upon] that this verse was revealed in response to the Jews from the Children of Israel, when they claimed that Jibril (Gabriel) was their enemy and that Mika'il (Michael) was their ally. Then they differed about the cause for which they said that. Some of them said: The cause of their saying that was a debate that took place between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning the matter of his prophethood. Mention of who said that:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: A group of the Jews came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Abu al-Qasim, tell us about some matters about which we will ask you, which none knows except a prophet." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ask whatever you wish, but make for me a covenant (dhimmah) and what Ya'qub (Jacob) took from his sons: if I tell you something and you recognise it, you will follow me in Islam." They said: "That is for you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ask me whatever you wish." They said: "Tell us about four matters we will ask you about: Tell us, what food did Isra'il (Israel) forbid to himself before the Torah was revealed? Tell us how the water of the woman and the water of the man [come together], and how a male and a female come from it? Tell us about this unlettered Prophet in sleep, and his companion among the angels?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Upon you is the covenant of Allah that if I inform you, you will follow me?" So they gave him whatever covenant and pact Allah willed. He said: "I adjure you by Him who revealed the Torah to Musa (Moses): Do you know that Isra'il, Ya'qub, fell seriously ill and his sickness lasted long, so he vowed to Allah that if Allah cured him of his sickness, he would forbid the most beloved food and drink to him, and the most beloved food to him was the meat of camels and the most beloved drink to him was their milk?" They said: "By Allah, yes." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, bear witness against them. And I adjure you by Allah, besides whom there is no god, who revealed the Torah to Musa: Do you know that the water of the man is white and thick, and that the water of the woman is yellow and thin? Whichever of them prevails, the child belongs to it and resembles it, by the permission of Allah; and when the water of the man prevails over the water of the woman, the child is male by the permission of Allah; and when the water of the woman prevails over the water of the man, the child is female by the permission of Allah?" They said: "By Allah, yes." He said: "O Allah, bear witness." He said: "And I adjure you by Allah who revealed the Torah to Musa: Do you know that this unlettered Prophet's eyes sleep but his heart does not sleep?" They said: "By Allah, yes." He said: "O Allah, bear witness." They said: "You now, tell us who is your ally among the angels, for then we will either unite with you or part from you." He said: "My ally is Jibril, and Allah has never sent a prophet except that he was his ally." They said: "Then at that point we part from you. If your ally were other than him among the angels, we would have followed you and believed you." He said: "What, then, prevents you from believing him?" They said: "He is our enemy." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Say: Whoever is an enemy to Jibril...﴾ up to His words: ﴿if they only knew﴾ [al-Baqarah: 103]. At that point they "returned with anger upon anger" (bi-ghadabin 'ala ghadab).

[Source: Tafsir al-Tabari (2/377).]

Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad, from Abu al-Nadr Hashim ibn al-Qasim, and 'Abd ibn Humayd in his Tafsir, from Ahmad ibn Yunus, both of them from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, with it.

Ahmad also narrated it from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi, from 'Abd al-Hamid, with something similar.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar also narrated it: "Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Husayn narrated to me, from Shahr ibn Hawshab," and he mentioned it as a mursal (incomplete chain), and he added in it: They said: "Then tell us about the Spirit." He said: "I adjure you by Allah and by His signs among the Children of Israel: Do you know that it is Jibril, and that he is the one who comes to me?" They said: "Yes, but he is our enemy; he is an angel who only brings severity and the shedding of blood. If not for that, we would have followed you." So Allah revealed concerning them: ﴿Say: Whoever is an enemy to Jibril, then indeed he has brought it down upon your heart by the permission of Allah...﴾ up to His words: ﴿as if they did not know﴾ [al-Baqarah: 101].

Ahmad said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn al-Walid al-'Ijli narrated to us, from Bukayr ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Jews came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Abu al-Qasim, we will ask you about five things. If you inform us of them, we will know that you are a prophet and we will follow you." So he took from them what Isra'il had taken from his sons when he said: ﴿Allah is Witness over what we say﴾ [Yusuf: 66]. He said: "Speak." They said: "Tell us the sign of the Prophet." He said: "His eyes sleep but his heart does not sleep." They said: "Tell us how the female becomes female and how the male becomes male?" He said: "The two waters meet; when the water of the man prevails over the water of the woman, [the child] becomes male, and when the water of the woman prevails over the water of the man, [the child] becomes female." They said: "Tell us what Isra'il forbade to himself." He said: "He used to suffer from sciatica (irq al-nasa), and he found nothing that suited him except the milk of such-and-such" — Ahmad said: Some of them said: "He meant the camels," so he forbade their meat — They said: "You have spoken the truth." They said: "Tell us what this thunder is?" He said: "An angel of the angels of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, who is charged with the clouds, in whose hands (or in whose hand) is a fiery whip with which he drives the clouds, guiding them wherever Allah commands him." They said: "Then what is this sound we hear?" He said: "Its sound." They said: "You have spoken the truth. Only one remains, and it is the one by which we will follow you if you inform us: There is no prophet except that he has an angel who brings him news. So tell us who your companion is?" He said: "Jibril, peace be upon him." They said: "Jibril! He is the one who descends with war, fighting and punishment; he is our enemy. If you had said Mika'il, who descends with mercy, plants and rain, we would have followed you." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Say: Whoever is an enemy to Jibril...﴾ to the end of the verse.

Al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i also narrated it from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Walid, with it. Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan gharib (good, strange).

Sunayd said in his Tafsir, from Hajjaj ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Juraij: al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah informed me that the Jews asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about his companion who descends to him with the revelation. He said: "Jibril." They said: "He is our enemy; he only comes with severity, war and fighting." So [the verse] was revealed: ﴿Say: Whoever is an enemy to Jibril...﴾ the verse. Ibn Juraij said: Mujahid said: The Jews said: "O Muhammad, Jibril only descends with severity, war and fighting, and he is our enemy." So [the verse] was revealed: ﴿Say: Whoever is an enemy to Jibril...﴾ the verse.

Al-Bukhari said: Regarding His words ﴿whoever is an enemy to Jibril﴾, 'Ikrimah said: "Jibr" and "Mik" and "Israf" mean "servant" ('abd), and "Il" means Allah. [Al-Bukhari] narrated to us: 'Abd Allah ibn Munir heard 'Abd Allah ibn Bakr narrate to us, from Humayd, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Salam heard of the arrival of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was in his land harvesting dates. He came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "I am going to ask you about three things that none knows except a prophet: What is the first sign of the Hour? What is the first food of the people of Paradise? And what makes a child resemble its father or its mother?" He said: "Jibril informed me of them just now." He said: "Jibril?" He said: "Yes." He said: "That is the enemy of the Jews among the angels." Then he recited this verse: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Jibril, then indeed he has brought it down upon your heart...﴾ [The Prophet said]: "As for the first sign of the Hour, it is a fire that will gather the people from the east to the west. As for the first food the people of Paradise will eat, it is the caudate lobe of the fish's liver. And when the water of the man precedes the water of the woman, the child resembles the father; and when the water of the woman precedes [the water of the man], [the child resembles the mother]." He said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah. O Messenger of Allah, the Jews are a people of slander (buhut), and if they learn of my Islam before you ask them, they will slander me." The Jews came, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "What sort of man is 'Abd Allah ibn Salam among you?" They said: "He is the best of us and the son of the best of us, and the chief of us and the son of the chief of us." He said: "What do you think if 'Abd Allah ibn Salam were to embrace Islam?" They said: "May Allah protect him from that!" Then 'Abd Allah came out and said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." They said: "He is the worst of us and the son of the worst of us," and they belittled him. He said: "This is what I was afraid of, O Messenger of Allah."

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it through this chain, and he narrated it through another chain, from Anas, with something similar. In Sahih Muslim, from Thawban, the freed slave of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), [there is a report] close to this context, as will come in its place.

As for al-Bukhari's report from 'Ikrimah, it is well known that "Il" means Allah. Sufyan al-Thawri also narrated it from Khasif, from 'Ikrimah.

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated it from Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam, from his father, from 'Ikrimah. Ibn Jarir narrated it from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Tahhan, from Ishaq ibn Mansur, from Qays, from 'Asim, from 'Ikrimah, that he said: The name of Jibril is 'Abd Allah and [the name of] Mika'il is 'Ubayd Allah; "Il" is Allah.

Yazid al-Nahwi also narrated it from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, the same. Likewise, more than one of the early generations (salaf) said, as will come shortly.

[Imam Ahmad said in the course of the hadith of Samurah ibn Jundub: Muhammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Ata narrated to us, who said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn said to me: The name of Jibril is 'Abd Allah, and the name of Mika'il is 'Ubayd Allah.]

Some people say: "Il" is an expression for "servant" ('abd), and the other word is the name of Allah, because the word "Il" does not change in all of them. Its pattern is: 'Abd Allah, 'Abd al-Rahman, 'Abd al-Malik, 'Abd al-Quddus, 'Abd al-Salam, 'Abd al-Kafi, 'Abd al-Jalil. So "'Abd" is present in all of these, while the names attached to it differ. Likewise [are] Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, 'Izra'il and similar names. In non-Arabic speech they place the attached word (mudaf ilayhi) before the one it is attached to (mudaf), and Allah knows best.

Then Ibn Jarir said: Others said: Rather, the cause of their saying that was a debate that took place between 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and them concerning the matter of the Prophet (ﷺ). Mention of who said that:

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verses 97–98 (part 2 of 3):

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me: Ribi' ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to me, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from al-Sha'bi, who said: 'Umar stopped at al-Rawha'. He saw men hurrying toward stones and praying toward them. He said: "What is the matter with these people?" They said: "They claim that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed here." He said: "That is false (fa-kafara dhalika)." And he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was overtaken by the prayer in a valley, prayed it, then departed and left it." Then he began to speak to them and said: "I used to attend the Jews on the day of their study (midrasihim), and I was amazed at the Torah: how does it confirm the Furqan, and how does the Furqan confirm the Torah?" One day, while I was with them, they said: "O Ibn al-Khattab, none of your companions is more beloved to us than you." I said: "Why is that?" They said: "You visit us and come to us." I said: "I come to you and am amazed at the Furqan: how does it confirm the Torah, and how does the Torah confirm the Furqan." He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by, and they said: 'O Ibn al-Khattab, that is your companion, so join him.'" He said: "At that point I said to them: 'I beseech you by Allah, besides whom there is no god, and by what He has entrusted you with of His right and of His Book: do you know that he is the Messenger of Allah?'" He said: "They were silent. Their scholar and elder said to them: 'He has indeed pressed you, so answer him.' They said: 'You are our scholar and our elder, so you answer him.' He said: 'As you have adjured us by what you adjured us, we indeed know that he is the Messenger of Allah.'" I said: "Woe to you! Then how have you been destroyed?" They said: "We have not been destroyed." I said: "How is that, when you know he is the Messenger of Allah, and yet you do not follow him nor believe him?" They said: "We have an enemy among the angels and a friend among the angels, and our enemy among the angels has been associated with his prophethood." I said: "Who is your enemy and who is your friend?" They said: "Our enemy is Jibril and our friend is Mika'il." I said: "Why did you take Jibril as an enemy and why did you make peace with Mika'il?" They said: "Jibril is the angel of harshness, severity, hardship, strictness, punishment and the like, while Mika'il is the angel of compassion, mercy, lightness and the like." I said: "And what is their station with their Lord, Mighty and Majestic?" They said: "One of them is on His right and the other on His left." I said: "By Allah, besides whom there is no god, they and whoever is between them are an enemy to whoever opposes them and a friend to whoever makes peace with them. It is not fitting for Jibril to make peace with the enemy of Mika'il, nor for Mika'il to make peace with the enemy of Jibril." Then I rose and followed the Prophet (ﷺ), and I caught up with him as he was coming out of a small door belonging to the Banu Fulan. He said: "O Ibn al-Khattab, shall I recite to you verses that were revealed before?" Then he recited to me: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Jibril, indeed he has brought it down upon your heart by the permission of Allah, confirming what is before it﴾, until he recited these verses. I said: "My father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of Allah! By the One who sent you with the truth, I came intending to inform you, but the Subtle, the All-Aware had already informed you of the news."
(Tafsir al-Tabari, 2/382.)

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Mujalid, who said: 'Amir informed us, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab went to the Jews and said: "I adjure you by Him who sent down the Torah to Musa: do you find Muhammad in your books?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then what prevents you from following him?" They said: "Allah has not sent a messenger without appointing for him a share (kifl) of the angels, and Jibril is the share of Muhammad. It is he who comes to him, and he is our enemy among the angels, while Mika'il is our friend. If it were Mika'il who came to him, we would have embraced Islam." He said: "I adjure you by Allah, who sent down the Torah to Musa: what is their station with the Lord of the worlds?" They said: "Jibril is on His right and Mika'il on His left." 'Umar said: "I testify that they do not descend except by the permission of Allah, and Mika'il would not make peace with the enemy of Jibril, nor would Jibril make peace with the enemy of Mika'il." While he was among them, the Prophet (ﷺ) passed by, and they said: "This is your companion, O Ibn al-Khattab."
