When night came, they wanted to ascend but could not, so they knew their destruction, and they were given the choice between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. They chose the punishment of this world, so they were hung at Babil, and they began to speak to people in their own language, which was magic.

Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid: As for the matter of Harut and Marut, the angels were astonished at the injustice of the children of Adam, although the messengers, books and clear proofs had come to them. Their Lord, exalted is He, said to them: "Choose from among you two angels, whom I will send down to judge among the children of Adam on the earth." They chose, and they did not hesitate, except for Harut and Marut. When He sent them down, He said to them: "Are you amazed at the children of Adam for their injustice and their disobedience? Messengers and books [and clear proofs] [[Addition from manuscript J.]] come to them from afar, but between Me and you there is no messenger. So do this and that, and leave that and this." He commanded them and forbade them, then they acted accordingly, and no one was more obedient to Allah than they were. They judged justly and were fair. They used to judge among the children of Adam during the day, and when evening came they ascended and were with the angels, and when morning came they descended and judged and were fair, until Venus was sent down to them in the most beautiful form of a woman who was disputing. They ruled against her. When she rose, each of them felt something in himself. One of them said to his companion: "Did you feel what I felt?" He said: "Yes." So they sent to her: "Come to us, and we will judge in your favour." When she returned, they judged in her favour, and she came to them, and they uncovered their private parts for her. Their desire was only within themselves, and they were not like the children of Adam in desire for women and their pleasure. When they reached that and considered it lawful, they were tempted. Venus flew away and returned to where she had been. When evening came, they tried to ascend, but they were rebuked, and they were not permitted, and their wings did not carry them. They sought help from a man among the children of Adam, and they came to him and said: "Pray to your Lord for us." He said: "How can the people of the earth intercede for the people of heaven?" They said: "We heard that your Lord mentions you favourably in heaven." So he promised them a day, and the next day he prayed for them, and his prayer was answered. They were given the choice between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. One of them looked at his companion and said: "Do you not know that the groups of Allah's punishment in the Hereafter are such-and-such for eternity, while in this world it is nine times as much?" So they were commanded to descend to Babil, and there is their punishment. And he claimed that they are suspended in iron, folded, beating their wings.

It has been narrated concerning the story of Harut and Marut from a group of the Followers (tabi'un), such as Mujahid, al-Suddi, al-Hasan [al-Basri] [[Addition from manuscripts J, T, B, A and W.]], Qatada, Abu al-Aliya, al-Zuhri, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Muqatil ibn Hayyan and others. Many of the exegetes, both earlier and later, have related it. Its essence, in its details, goes back to the reports of the Children of Israel, for there is no sound, elevated (marfu') hadith with a connected chain to the truthful, believed, infallible one who does not speak from desire (ﷺ). The apparent context of the Qur'an mentions the story in summary, without elaborate detail or lengthy explanation. So we believe in what has come in the Qur'an according to what Allah the Exalted intended, and Allah knows the reality of the matter.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verses 99–103 (part 6 of 7):

There is a strange report and a remarkable narrative on this matter, which we wish to draw attention to. Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman related to us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Ibn Abi al-Zinad informed me: Hisham ibn 'Urwah related to me, from his father, from 'Aishah, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ) [may Allah be pleased with her and with her father] [[addition from ج.]], that she said: A woman from the people of Dumat al-Jandal came to me, seeking the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) after his death, not long after it. She asked him about something [[in أ and و: "about things".]] into which she had entered concerning sorcery (sihr), and she had not acted upon it. 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said to 'Urwah: "O nephew! I saw her weeping when she could not find the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to cure her. She kept weeping until I felt pity for her, and she was saying: 'I fear that I have been ruined. I had a husband who went away from me, so I entered upon an old woman and complained to her about that. She said: If you do what I command you, I will make him come to you.' When night came, she brought me two black dogs. I mounted one of them, and she mounted the other. They did not move like anything until we stopped at Babil, and behold, there were two men hanging by their feet. They said: 'What brought you here?' I said: 'I want to learn sorcery.' They said: 'We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve; return.' But I refused and said: 'No.' They said: 'Go to that oven and urinate into it.' I went, became frightened, and did not do it. I returned to them, and they said: 'Did you do it?' I said: 'Yes.' They said: 'Did you see anything?' I said: 'I saw nothing.' They said: 'You did not do it. Return to your land and do not disbelieve [for you are at the beginning of your affair]' [[addition from ج.]]. I hesitated and refused. They said: 'Go to that oven and urinate into it.' I went and was seized with fear [and I was afraid] [[addition from ج، ب، أ، و.]], then returned to them and said: 'I have done it.' They said: 'What did you see?' I said: 'I saw nothing.' They said: 'You lied, you did not do it. Return to your land and do not disbelieve; for you are at the beginning of your affair.' I hesitated and refused. They said: 'Go to that oven and urinate into it.' I went to it and urinated into it, and I saw a masked horseman [[in ج: "suspended".]] with iron, who came out of me, rose into the sky, and disappeared [from me] [[addition from أ.]] until I could no longer see him. I came back to them and said: 'I have done it.' They said: 'What did you see?' I said: 'I saw a masked horseman who came out of me, rose into the sky, until I could no longer see him.' They said: 'You have spoken the truth. That was your faith, which left you. Go.' I said to the woman: 'By Allah, I know nothing, and they did not say anything to me.' She said: 'Yes, they did. You will never desire anything except that it happens. Take this wheat, sow it.' I sowed it and said: 'Sprout!' and it sprouted. I said: 'Ear!' and it ripened. I said: 'Dry!' and it dried. I said: 'Grind!' and it was ground. I said: 'Bake!' and it was baked. When I saw that I did not desire anything except that it happened, I was overcome with regret. By Allah, O Mother of the Believers, by Allah, I have never done anything at all, and I will never do it again."

[Source: Tafsir al-Tabari (2/439–441).]

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman, in the same form, at greater length as mentioned above [Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/312); al-Bayhaqi also narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra (8/137) through al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman, at greater length. This addition does not appear in the printed edition of Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim, and the esteemed editor, may Allah reward him well, has pointed this out.]. He added, after her words "and I will never do it again": "So I asked the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when the death of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was recent, and they were numerous at that time, and they did not know what to say to her. All of them were in awe and feared to give her a verdict on something they did not know, except that Ibn 'Abbas, or some of those who were with him, said to her: 'If your parents were alive, or one of them, they would suffice you.'"

Hisham said: "If she came to us, we would give her a verdict requiring compensation [said] [[addition from أ.]]." Ibn Abi al-Zinad said: Hisham used to say: "They were people of scrupulousness (wara') and fear of Allah." Then Hisham would say: "If someone like her came to us today, they would find us to be foolish people of ignorance who presume knowledge they do not have."

This is a sound chain (isnad) to 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her.

Those who hold that the sorcerer has the ability to change the essence of things have cited this report, because this woman sowed the wheat and it grew immediately. Others said: Rather, sorcery has no power except to create illusion (takhyil), as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They bewitched the eyes of the people and terrified them, and they produced a great sorcery﴾ [al-A'raf: 116], and He the Exalted said: ﴿Their sorcery made it appear to him that their ropes and staffs were moving﴾ [Ta-Ha: 66]. This report has also been cited as evidence that Babil mentioned in the Qur'an is Babil of Iraq, not Babil of Dunbawand [[in ط، ب، أ، و: "Dinawand".]], as al-Suddi and others said. The evidence that it is Babil of Iraq is what Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn related to us: Ahmad ibn Salih related to us: Ibn Wahb related to me: Ibn Lahi'ah and Yahya ibn Azhar related to me, from 'Ammar ibn Sa'd al-Muradi, from Abu Salih al-Ghifari, that 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, [passed by Babil while traveling. The caller to prayer came to him to call him to the 'Asr prayer. When he had left it, he ordered the caller to call the iqamah, and when he finished, he said:] "My beloved (ﷺ) forbade me to pray [in a cemetery, and forbade me to pray] in Babil, for it is cursed."

[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/304). The words in brackets are not in Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim.]

Abu Dawud said: Sulayman ibn Dawud related to us: Ibn Wahb related to us: Ibn Lahi'ah and Yahya ibn Azhar related to me, from 'Ammar ibn Sa'd al-Muradi, from Abu Salih al-Ghifari, that 'Ali passed by Babil while traveling, and the caller to prayer came to him to call him to the 'Asr prayer. When he had left it, he ordered the caller to call the iqamah, and when he finished he said: "My beloved (ﷺ) forbade me to pray in a cemetery, and forbade me to pray in the land of Babil, for it is cursed."

Ahmad ibn Salih related to us: Ibn Wahb related to us: Yahya ibn Azhar and Ibn Lahi'ah informed me, from al-Hajjaj ibn Shaddad, from Abu Salih al-Ghifari, from 'Ali, with the same meaning as the report of Sulayman ibn Dawud, and he said: "When he went out" in place of "when he had left."

[Sunan Abi Dawud, nos. 490, 491.]

This hadith is sound (hasan) according to Imam Abu Dawud, because he narrated it and remained silent about it [[in ج، ط، ب، أ، و: "and remained silent regarding it".]]. From it comes the jurisprudential point that praying in the land of Babil is disliked, just as it is disliked to enter the dwellings of Thamud, whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade entering unless one is weeping.

The astronomers said: The distance of Babil, which is in the region of Iraq, from the Western Ocean, which is called Oceanus [[in ب: "Oceanos".]], is seventy degrees. They call this longitude (tul). As for its latitude ('ard), which is the distance between it and the middle of the earth on the southern side, and which is aligned with the equator, it is thirty-two degrees. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And they did not teach anyone until they said: "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve"﴾. Abu Ja'far al-Razi related from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Qays ibn 'Abbad [[in أ: "from Bishr".]], from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the one who comes to them seeking sorcery reaches them, they forbid him most strongly and say to him: "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve." This is because they knew good and evil, disbelief and faith, and they knew that sorcery is from disbelief. [He said] [[addition from ج، أ، و.]] If he refuses them, they order him to go to such-and-such a place, and when he goes there he sees the devil, and he teaches him. When he has learned, light comes out from him, and he sees it shining in the sky, and he says: "Alas! Woe to me! What shall I do?"

It is also related from al-Hasan al-Basri that he said regarding the interpretation of this verse: "Yes, the two angels were sent down with sorcery, to teach people the trial with which Allah wished to test them. A covenant was taken from them that they would not teach anyone until they said: ﴿We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve﴾." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this. Qatadah said: A covenant was taken from them that they would not teach anyone until they said: ﴿We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve﴾ [i.e., a test with which we are tested] ﴿so do not disbelieve﴾.

Qatadah [and] [[addition from و.]] al-Suddi said: When a person comes to them wanting sorcery, they admonish him and say to him: "Do not disbelieve; we are only a trial." If he refuses, they say to him: "Go to this ash and urinate on it." When he urinates on it, light comes out from it and shines until it enters the sky, and that is faith. A black thing like smoke approaches until it enters his ears and everything [from him] [[addition from أ، و.]]. That is the wrath of Allah. When they inform them of that, they teach him sorcery. This is the meaning of Allah's saying: ﴿And they did not teach anyone until they said: "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve"﴾, and so on.

Sunayd said, from Hajjaj, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding this verse: "None dares to engage in sorcery except a disbeliever."

As for fitnah, it means trial and testing. From this is the saying of the poet:

"People have been tried in their religion, and Ibn 'Affan left a long evil."

[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (2/444), where the disagreement over its composer is also noted.]

Similarly is Allah's saying, reporting about Musa, upon him be peace, when he said: ﴿It is only Your trial; You lead astray by it whom You will and guide whom You will﴾ [al-A'raf: 155]; that is, Your testing and examination.

Some have cited this verse as evidence for the disbelief of one who learns sorcery, and they support this with the hadith that al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar narrated: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Hammam, from 'Abd Allah, who said: "Whoever goes to a soothsayer (kahin) or a sorcerer and believes what he says has disbelieved in what was revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ)."

This is a sound chain [[in ج، ط، ب، أ، و: "a sound isnad".]], and it has other corroborating reports.

* *

And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So they learn from the two of them that by which they cause division between a man and his wife﴾. That is, people learn from Harut and Marut the knowledge of sorcery (sihr), by which they act in reprehensible ways, including causing division between a married couple despite the closeness and affection between them. This is among the works of the devils, as Muslim narrated in his Sahih, from the hadith of al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan Talhah ibn Nafi', from Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him [[In B: "with them both".]], from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed, Satan places his throne upon the water, then sends his battalions among the people. The closest of them to him in rank is the one with the greatest mischief. One of them comes and says, 'I did not stop with so-and-so until I left him saying such-and-such.' Iblis says, 'No, by Allah, you have done nothing.' Another comes and says, 'I did not leave him until I separated him from his family [[In J: "from his wife".]].' He said: Then Iblis draws him near, brings him close, embraces him, and says, 'How excellent you are!'" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (2813).]]

The cause of separation between spouses through sorcery is that the man or the woman imagines the other to be ugly in appearance, or of bad character, or something similar, or that hatred or resentment is produced, or similar reasons that necessitate separation.

Al-mar' (the man) is a term for a male, its feminine form is imra'ah (the woman), and each of them is made dual, but they are not made plural together. And Allah knows best.

* *

And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿But they cannot harm anyone thereby except by the permission of Allah﴾. Sufyan al-Thawri said: "Except by the decree of Allah." Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: "Except by Allah's leaving him free between it and what He wills." Al-Hasan al-Basri said regarding ﴿But they cannot harm anyone thereby except by the permission of Allah﴾: "Yes, whomever Allah wills, He empowers them over him, and whomever Allah does not will, they are not empowered over him, and they cannot harm anyone except by the permission of Allah, as Allah the Exalted said." In another report from al-Hasan, he said: "This sorcery does not harm except the one who enters into it."

* *

And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And they learn that which harms them and does not benefit them﴾. That is, it harms them in their religion, and it has no benefit that could balance its harm.

﴿And they certainly knew that whoever purchases it would have no share in the Hereafter﴾. That is, the Jews who exchanged the following of the Messenger (ﷺ) for sorcery certainly knew that whoever did their deed, he would have no share (khalaq) in the Hereafter.

Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and al-Suddi said: "A share (nasib)." Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: "He has no portion in the Hereafter from the side of Allah." And al-Hasan said: "He has no religion."

Sa'd [[In T, B, W: "Sa'id".]] narrated from Qatadah regarding ﴿He has no share in the Hereafter﴾: "And the People of the Book certainly knew, in what Allah had covenanted to them, that the sorcerer has no share in the Hereafter."

[[The author's words have been abridged due to their great length.]]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verses 99–103 (part 1 of 7):

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said, regarding His statement, Exalted is He: ﴿And We have certainly sent down to you clear signs﴾, meaning: We have sent down to you, O Muhammad, clear signs and evident proofs [[Addition from manuscripts J, T, B, A, W.]] of your prophethood. These signs are what the Book of Allah contains of the hidden knowledge of the Jews, the concealed secrets of their reports, the reports of their earliest ancestors from the Children of Israel, and information about what their books contained, which only their rabbis and scholars knew, and what their earlier and later generations distorted and altered of their rulings that were in the Torah. So Allah made known in His Book, which He sent down to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, what was in that matter of clear signs for whoever is fair to himself, and envy and transgression did not lead him to his own destruction. For in the natural disposition of every person of sound nature there is the affirmation of whoever brings the like of what Muhammad ﷺ brought of the clear signs that he described, without any learning taken from a human being, and without taking anything from any son of Adam. [[In manuscript J: "affirmation of that from someone who would bring the like of…". In manuscript J: "from a human being".]] [[In manuscripts J, T, B: "a thing", which is an error.]] As al-Dahhak said, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And We have certainly sent down to you clear signs﴾: he said: You recite it to them and inform them of it morning and evening, and in between, while you are among them an unlettered man who does not read a book, and you inform them of what is in their hands exactly as it is. Allah says: in that there is a lesson and clear explanation for them, and a proof against them, if they had known.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Ibn Suriya al-Fitayuni said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "O Muhammad, you have brought us nothing that we recognize, and Allah has not sent down upon you any clear sign that we would follow you for." So Allah revealed concerning that, from His statement: ﴿And We have certainly sent down to you clear signs, and none disbelieves in them except the defiantly disobedient﴾.

Malik ibn al-Sayf said, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sent, and they were reminded of the covenant that had been taken from them and what had been enjoined upon them concerning Muhammad ﷺ: "By Allah, Allah did not enjoin upon us anything concerning Muhammad ﷺ, nor did He take a covenant from us concerning him." So Allah revealed: ﴿Is it not that whenever they make a covenant, a party among them casts it aside?﴾

Al-Hasan al-Basri, regarding His statement ﴿Rather, most of them do not believe﴾, said: Yes. There is no covenant on earth that they make a pact upon except that they break it and cast it aside. They make a covenant today and break it tomorrow.

Al-Suddi said: They do not believe in what Muhammad ﷺ brought. Qatadah said, regarding ﴿A party among them cast it aside﴾: meaning, a party among them broke it.

Ibn Jarir said: The origin of nabdh (casting aside) is throwing and tossing away. From it the foundling is called manbudh (cast-off), and from it the drink called nabidh is named, which is dates and raisins when they are put in water. Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali said:

I looked at its title, so I cast it aside, as you cast aside a sandal that has worn out from your sandals.

[[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (2/401).]]

I say: So Allah censured these people for casting aside the covenants that Allah had established with them, to hold fast to them and fulfil their rights. For this reason it followed that they denied the Messenger sent to them and to all mankind, whose description, attributes, and reports are in their books, and in which they were commanded to follow him, support him, and help him. As He said: ﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel﴾ [al-A'raf: 157]. And here He said: ﴿And when there came to them a Messenger from Allah confirming what was with them, a party of those who were given the Scripture cast the Book of Allah behind their backs, as if they did not know﴾. That is: a group of them discarded the Book of Allah that was in their hands, in which was the good news of Muhammad ﷺ, behind their backs, meaning they abandoned it, as if they did not know what was in it, and turned to learning magic and following it. For this reason they intended a plot against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and bewitched him with a comb, hair, and the sheath of a male date-palm spathe, beneath the rock of the well of Dhi Arwan. The one who undertook this among them was a man called Labid ibn al-A'sam, may Allah curse him. Allah then made His Messenger ﷺ aware of this, healed him from it, and rescued him, as this is established in detail in the two Sahihs from A'ishah, Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her, as its explanation will come [[In manuscript J: "as its explanation will come, Allah willing, and in Him is trust". In manuscript A: "as its explanation will come, Allah willing".]].

Al-Suddi said: ﴿And when there came to them a Messenger from Allah confirming what was with them﴾: When Muhammad ﷺ came to them, they opposed him with the Torah and argued with him by it, so the Torah and the Qur'an agreed, and they cast the Torah aside and took up the book of Asaf and the magic of Harut and Marut. It did not agree with the Qur'an, and this is His statement: ﴿as if they did not know﴾.

Qatadah, regarding His statement ﴿as if they did not know﴾, said: The people did know, but they cast aside their knowledge, concealed it, and denied it.

Al-Awfi, in his tafsir, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, Exalted is He: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon. Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved﴾: When Solomon's kingdom departed, a faction of the jinn and humans apostatized and followed their desires. When Allah restored Solomon's kingdom to him, and people stood upright in the religion as they had in Solomon's time, the devils uncovered their books and buried them beneath his throne. Solomon, peace be upon him, died shortly after that, so the humans and jinn uncovered the books after Solomon's death and said: "This is a book from Allah that was sent down to Solomon, and he hid it from us." So they took it and made it their religion. Then Allah revealed: ﴿And when there came to them a Messenger from Allah confirming what was with them, a party of those who were given the Scripture cast the Book of Allah behind their backs, as if they did not know﴾, and they followed the desires, [that is]: [[Addition from manuscript J.]] which the devils had been reciting, and these were musical instruments, play, and everything that turns one away from the remembrance of Allah.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Asaf was the scribe of Solomon, and he knew the Greatest Name, and he wrote everything by Solomon's command and buried it beneath his throne. When Solomon died, the devils brought it out, and they wrote between every two lines magic and disbelief, and said: "This is what Solomon used to practise." He said: So the ignorant people disbelieved him and reviled him, and their scholars stood aside, and their ignorant ones kept reviling him, until Allah sent down to Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon. Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved﴾ [[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/297).]].

Ibn Jarir said: Abu al-Sa'ib Salm [[In manuscripts J, T, B: "Muslim".]] ibn Junadah al-Sawa'i narrated to me, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Solomon, peace be upon him, when he wanted to enter the lavatory, or approach some of his wives, would give his ring to al-Jaradah, who was a woman. When Allah willed to test Solomon, peace be upon him, with what He tested him with, one day he gave his ring to al-Jaradah, and a devil came in the form of Solomon and said to her: "Give me my ring." So he took it and put it on. When he put it on, the devils, jinn, and humans submitted to him. He said: Then Solomon came to her and said: "Give me my ring," and she said: "You are lying, you are not Solomon." He said: So Solomon knew that it was a trial with which he had been tested. He said: The devils then went off and wrote books during those days, containing magic and disbelief. Then they buried them beneath the throne of Solomon, then they brought them out and read them to the people, and said: "Solomon only overcame the people by these books." He said: So the people disassociated themselves from Solomon, peace be upon him, and considered him a disbeliever, until Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ and revealed to him: ﴿Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved﴾.

Then Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Imran, who is Ibn al-Harith, who said: While we were with Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, a man came and said to him: "Where have you come from?" He said: "From Iraq." He said: "From which place?" He said: "From Kufah." He said: "What is the news?" He said: "I left them talking that Ali is going out to them." So he was alarmed and then said: "What are you saying? May you have no father! If we had known, we would not have married his wives, nor divided his inheritance. But I will tell you about that: the devils used to steal hearing from the sky, and one of them would bring a word of truth that he had heard. When some truth from him was tested, he would lie with it seventy lies, and the hearts of the people would absorb it. Allah made Solomon, peace be upon him, aware of this, so he buried them beneath his throne. When Solomon, peace be upon him, died, a devil of the road stood up and said: 'Shall I not direct you to his treasure, which has no equal treasure like it? It is beneath the throne.' So they brought it out and said: 'This is his magic.' And the nations spread it, until its remnants were what the people of Iraq still talk about." And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon. Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved﴾.

[Ibn Jarir's chain continues in the source text, and the commentary is treated as above.]

Al-Hakim related it in his Mustadrak, from Abu Zakariyya al-Anbari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Salam, from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, from Jarir, with it [[Tafsir al-Tabari (2/415) and al-Mustadrak (2/265).]].

And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon. Al-Suddi said, regarding the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon﴾, meaning: during the time of Solomon. He said: The devils used to ascend to the heaven and sit there in places for listening. They would listen to the speech of the angels concerning what would happen on earth, whether death, something unseen, or a matter [of decree]. Then they would come to the soothsayers and inform them. The soothsayers would then tell the people, and they would find it just as they had said. Until, when the people trusted the soothsayers, they lied to them and added to it other things. For every word they would add seventy words. The people then wrote that speech down in books, and it spread among the Children of Israel that the jinn know the unseen. So Solomon was sent to the people, and he gathered those books and put them in a chest, then buried it beneath his throne. No devil could approach the throne without being burnt. He said: "I will not hear anyone claim that the devils know the unseen except that I will strike off his neck." When Solomon, peace be upon him, died, and the scholars who knew the affair of Solomon departed, a successor came after them, and a devil took the form of a man. Then he came to a group of the Children of Israel and said to them: "Shall I guide you to a treasure that you will never eat of?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Dig beneath the throne." He went with them, showed them the place, and stood aside. They said to him: "Come closer." He said: "No, but I will remain here in your hands; if you do not find it, then kill me." So they dug and found those books. When they brought them out, the devil said: "Solomon only controlled mankind, the devils, and the birds by this magic." Then he flew away and left. It spread among the people that Solomon was a sorcerer. The Children of Israel adopted those books, and when Muhammad ﷺ came, they disputed with him using them; this is the time about which Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved﴾.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: The Jews asked Muhammad ﷺ for a period about matters from the Torah, and whenever they asked him about anything of that, Allah, the Exalted, would reveal to him what they asked about, so he would overcome them. When they saw that, they said: "This man knows what Allah has revealed to us better than we do." They asked him about magic and disputed with him concerning it, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon. Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic﴾. The devils had gone to a book, written magic and soothsaying and whatever Allah willed of that in it, and buried it beneath the seat of Solomon. Solomon, peace be upon him, did not know the unseen. When Solomon departed this world, they extracted that magic, deceived the people, and said: "This is knowledge that Solomon used to conceal and envied the people for." The Prophet ﷺ informed them of this account, so they returned from his presence grieved, and Allah refuted their argument.

Mujahid said regarding His words: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon﴾: The devils used to listen to the revelation, and whatever word they heard, they would add two hundred like it to it. Solomon, peace be upon him, then sent for what they had written of that. When Solomon died, the devils found it and taught it to the people, and it is magic.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Solomon, peace be upon him, used to trace what the devils had of magic and take it from them, and he would bury it beneath his throne in the room of his treasury. The devils could not reach it, so they approached mankind and said to them: "Do you know the knowledge by which Solomon subjugated the devils, the winds, and other things?" They said: "Yes." They said: "It is in his treasury room and beneath his throne." So mankind dug it up, extracted it, and acted by it. The people of wisdom said: "Solomon used to work by this, and this is magic." So Allah, the Exalted, sent down upon His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ the acquittal of Solomon, peace be upon him, saying: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon. Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved﴾.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said: When the devils learned of the death of Solomon ibn Dawud, peace be upon him, they set about writing kinds of magic: "Whoever wishes to reach such and such, let him say such and such." When they had classified the kinds of magic, they put it into a book, sealed it with a seal bearing the design of Solomon's seal, and wrote on its title: "This is what Asaf ibn Barkhiya the truthful wrote for King Solomon ibn Dawud, peace be upon them both, from the treasures of the storehouses of knowledge." Then they buried it beneath his throne. Afterwards, the remnants of the Children of Israel extracted it, until they did what they did. When they discovered it, they said: "By Allah, Solomon ibn Dawud was only by this." They spread magic among the people, and they learned it and taught it. It is found among no one more than among the Jews, may Allah curse them. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned, among what Allah had revealed to him, Solomon ibn Dawud and counted him among the messengers, some Jews in Madinah said: "Do you not marvel at Muhammad! He claims that the son of Dawud was a prophet; by Allah, he was nothing but a sorcerer." Allah revealed concerning their words: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon, and Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved﴾, to the end of the verse.

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Husayn narrated to us, al-Hajjaj narrated to us, from Abu Bakr, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: When Solomon was deprived of his kingdom, the devils would write magic during Solomon's absence. They wrote: "Whoever wishes to do such and such, let him face the sun and say such and such; and whoever wishes to do such and such, let him turn his back to the sun and say such and such." They wrote it and made its title: "This is what Asaf ibn Barkhiya wrote for King Solomon [ibn Dawud] from the treasures of the storehouses of knowledge." Then they buried it beneath his throne. When Solomon, peace be upon him, died, Iblis, may Allah curse him, stood up as a preacher and said: "O people, Solomon was not a prophet; he was only a sorcerer. So search for his magic in his goods and houses." Then he pointed them to the place where it was buried. They said: "By Allah, Solomon was indeed a sorcerer! This is his magic; by this he subdued us." The believers said: "Rather, he was a believing prophet." When Allah sent the Prophet ﷺ, he began mentioning the prophets until he mentioned Dawud and Solomon. The Jews, may Allah curse them, said: "Look at Muhammad mixing truth with falsehood. He mentions Solomon with the prophets, when he was only a sorcerer who rode the wind." So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon﴾, to the end of the verse.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la al-San'ani narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard Imran ibn Hudayr, from Abu Mijlaz, who said: Solomon, peace be upon him, took a covenant from every creature, so that whenever a man was afflicted and asked by that covenant, [the creature] would release him. The people then added rhyming prose and magic, and said: "Solomon used to work by this." Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic﴾ [[Tafsir al-Tabari (2/414).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Isam ibn Rawwad narrated to us, Adam narrated to us, al-Mas'udi narrated to us, from Ziyad, the freedman of Ibn Mus'ab, from al-Hasan: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited﴾, he said: a third of it is poetry, a third is magic, and a third is soothsaying.

He also said: al-Hasan ibn Ahmad narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah ibn Bashshar al-Wasiti narrated to us, Surur ibn al-Mughira narrated to me, from Abbad ibn Mansur, from al-Hasan: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon﴾, and the Jews followed it during his reign. Magic had existed on the earth before that and had never ceased to be there, but it was only followed during the reign of Solomon.

This is a selection of the sayings of the leading early scholars on this point. The summary of the account and the combining of its parts are not hidden, and there is no contradiction between the contexts for the discerning intellect; and Allah is the Guide. As for His words, the Exalted: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon﴾, meaning: the Jews, who were given the Book, followed, after turning away from the Book of Allah that was in their hands and opposing the Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, what the devils recited, i.e., what the devils narrated, related and spoke of during the reign of Solomon. He used "upon" (ʿalā) because "recite" (tatlū) includes the meaning of "falsely attribute." Ibn Jarir said: "ʿalā" here means "fī" (in), i.e., they recited in the reign of Solomon, and he transmitted this from Ibn Juraij and Ibn Ishaq.

I say: The inclusion of meaning (tadammun) is better and more preferable, and Allah knows best.

The statement of al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him: "Magic existed before the time of Solomon ibn Dawud," is correct beyond doubt, because sorcerers existed in the time of Musa, peace be upon him, and Solomon ibn Dawud came after him, as Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Have you not considered the chiefs of the Children of Israel after Musa, when they said to a prophet of theirs: Send for us a king, and we will fight in the way of Allah?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 246], then He mentioned the story after it, in which: ﴿And Dawud killed Jalut, and Allah gave him the kingdom and wisdom﴾ [al-Baqarah: 251]. And the people of Salih, who were before Abraham the Friend, peace be upon him, said to their prophet Salih: ﴿You are only one of the bewitched﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 153], meaning: among the bewitched, according to the well-known view.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And [they followed] what was sent down to the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut. But they did not teach anyone until they had said, "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve." And they learned from the two what they could use to cause division between a man and his wife.﴾ The scholars differed regarding this passage. Some of them held that "ma" (what) is a negating particle (ma nafiyah), namely the one in His saying, ﴿and what was sent down to the two angels﴾. Al-Qurtubi said: "'Ma' is a negating particle and is conjoined (ma'tufah) to His saying, ﴿And Sulayman did not disbelieve﴾. Then He said, ﴿But the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic and what was sent down﴾, meaning: the magic, ﴿upon the two angels﴾. This is because the Jews, may Allah curse them, used to claim that Jibril and Mika'il had brought it down. So Allah refuted them in that and made His saying, ﴿Harut and Marut﴾, a substitute (badal) for ﴿the devils﴾." He said: "This is valid, either because the plural may be applied to two, as in His saying, ﴿But if he has brothers﴾ [An-Nisa: 11], or because they had followers, or because they were singled out from among them for their rebelliousness. So the sense of the statement according to him is: 'They teach people magic at Babil: Harut and Marut.'" Then he said: "This is the most appropriate interpretation (ta'wil) of the verse and the most sound, and nothing else should be turned to."

Ibn Jarir narrated with his isnad (chain of narration), through the route of al-Awfi, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying, ﴿and what was sent down to the two angels at Babil, Harut and Marut﴾, that he said: "Allah did not send down magic." And with his isnad, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, regarding His saying, ﴿and what was sent down to the two angels﴾, he said: "Allah did not send down magic upon them both."

Ibn Jarir said: "The interpretation of the verse according to this view is: 'And they followed what the devils recited over the kingdom of Sulayman, and Sulayman did not disbelieve, nor did Allah send down magic upon the two angels, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic at Babil, Harut and Marut.' So His saying, ﴿at Babil Harut [and Marut [[Addition from MSS ج، ط، ب، أ، و.]]]﴾ is of the postponed (mu'akhkhar) which has the meaning of the preposed (muqaddam). He said: 'If someone asks us, how is this preposing?' It is said: The manner of its preposing is that it is said: '﴿And they followed what the devils recited over the kingdom of Sulayman﴾ — "of magic" — ﴿and Sulayman did not disbelieve﴾, and Allah did not send down "magic" upon the two angels, ﴿but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic﴾ at Babil, Harut and Marut.' Thus by the 'two angels' is meant Jibril and Mika'il, peace be upon them, because the sorcerers of the Jews, as is mentioned, used to claim that Allah sent down magic through the tongue of Jibril and Mika'il to Sulayman ibn Dawud. So Allah refuted them in that, and informed His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ that Jibril and Mika'il had not descended with magic, and He absolved Sulayman, peace be upon him, of what they attributed to him of magic. And He informed them that magic is from the work of the devils, and that they teach people that at Babil, and that the ones who teach them that are two men, one named Harut and the other named Marut. So, according to this interpretation, Harut and Marut are a rendering (tarjamah) of the people, and a refutation of them."

This is his wording, word for word. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (2/419, 420).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: "I was told (huddithtu) by Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, who informed us, Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from Ata': ﴿And what was sent down to the two angels﴾ — he said: 'Allah did not send down magic to Jibril and Mika'il.'"

Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan related to us, Muhammad ibn Isa related to us, Ya'la — meaning Ibn Asad — related to us, Bakr — meaning Ibn Mus'ab — related to us, al-Hasan ibn Abi Ja'far: that Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza used to recite it: "And what was sent down to the two kings, Dawud and Sulayman."

Abu al-Aliyah said: "Magic was not sent down upon the two of them. He means: they taught faith and disbelief, and magic is from disbelief, so they forbade it most strictly." Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Then Ibn Jarir began refuting this view, and that "ma" means "alladhi" (that which). He elaborated on this at length, and claimed that Harut and Marut were two angels whom Allah sent down to the earth and permitted to teach magic as a test and trial for His servants, after He had made clear to His servants that this is among the things forbidden through the tongues of the messengers. He claimed that Harut and Marut were obedient in teaching that, because they carried out what they were commanded.

This path he took is extremely strange! And stranger than it is the view of one who claimed that Harut and Marut were two tribes of the jinn [as Ibn Hazm claimed] [[Addition from MSS ج، ط.]]!

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with his isnad, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, that he used to recite it: ﴿And what was sent down to the two angels﴾ and would say: "They are two men (ilj) from the people of Babil."

The proponents of this view interpreted "sending down" (inzal) in His saying, ﴿And what was sent down to the two angels﴾, as meaning "creating" (khalq), not "revelation" (ihya'), just as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And He sent down for you eight pairs of livestock﴾ [Az-Zumar: 6], ﴿And We sent down iron, in which is great might﴾ [Al-Hadid: 25], ﴿And He sends down for you provision from the sky﴾ [Ghafir: 13]. And in the hadith: "Allah has not sent down a disease except that He has sent down its cure." And as one says: "Allah sent down good and evil."

[Al-Qurtubi related from Ibn Abbas, Ibn Abza, al-Dahhak and al-Hasan al-Basri that they recited: "And what was sent down to the two kings" with a kasrah on the lam. Ibn Abza said: "They are Dawud and Sulayman." Al-Qurtubi said: "According to this, 'ma' is also a negating particle."] [[Addition from MSS ج، ط.]]

Others held that one should stop (waqf) at His saying, ﴿they teach people magic﴾ [and "ma" is a negating particle] [[Addition from MSS ج، ط، ب، و.]]. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus related to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, al-Layth informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, and a man asked him about the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿They teach people magic and what was sent down to the two angels at Babil, Harut and Marut﴾. The man said: "Do they teach people magic which was sent down to them both, or do they teach people what was not sent down to them?" Al-Qasim said: "I do not care which of the two it was."

Then it was related from Yunus, from Anas ibn Iyad, from some of his companions, that al-Qasim said regarding this story: "I do not care which of these it was; I have believed in it."

Many of the earlier generations (salaf) held that they were two angels from the heaven, and that they were sent down to the earth, and that what happened to them happened. There is a raised (marfu') hadith regarding this which Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad, as we will mention, Allah willing. On this view, the reconciliation between this and what is established from the evidences of the infallibility (ismah) of the angels is that this was already decreed in the knowledge of Allah for these two, so it is a specification for them, and there is then no contradiction, just as what had been decreed in His knowledge regarding the matter of Iblis had been decreed. And in one opinion: he (Iblis) was among the angels, based on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," so they prostrated, except Iblis, who refused﴾ [Ta-Ha: 116], and other verses indicating that. Moreover, the affair of Harut and Marut, as has been mentioned, is lighter than what occurred from Iblis, may Allah curse him.

[Al-Qurtubi related this from Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, Ka'b al-Ahbar, al-Suddi and al-Kalbi] [[Addition from MSS ج، ط.]].

Mention of the hadith related regarding this, if its chain (sanad) and its raising (raf') are sound, and an explanation of what is said about it:

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his Musnad: Yahya ibn [Abi] [[Addition from MSS ط.]] Bukayr related to us, Zuhayr ibn Muhammad related to us, from Musa ibn Jubayr, from Nafi', from Abd Allah ibn Umar: that he heard the Prophet of Allah ﷺ say: "When Allah caused Adam, peace be upon him, to descend to the earth, the angels said: 'O Lord, [[In ج: "O Lord."]] "Will You place in it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we exalt You with Your praise and sanctify You?" He said: "Indeed I know that which you do not know" [Al-Baqarah: 30].' They said: 'Our Lord, we are more obedient to You than the children of Adam.' Allah, exalted is He, said to the angels: 'Bring forth two angels from among the angels, and We will send them down to the earth, and We will see how they act.' They said: 'Our Lord, Harut and Marut.' So they were sent down to the earth, and the planet Venus (al-Zuhrah) was made to appear to them as a woman among the most beautiful of human beings. She came to them, and they asked her to yield herself to them. She said: 'No, by Allah, not until you utter this word of polytheism (ishrak).' They said: 'By Allah, we will never associate anything with Allah.' So she left them, then returned with a boy she was carrying, and they asked her to yield herself to them. She said: 'No, by Allah, not until you kill this boy.' They said: 'No, by Allah, we will never kill him.' Then she went away and returned with a cup of wine she was carrying, and they asked her to yield herself to them. She said: 'No, by Allah, not until you drink this wine.' They drank, became intoxicated, lay with her, and killed the boy. When they came to their senses, the woman said: 'By Allah, you have left nothing which you refused me except that you have done it while you were intoxicated.' So they were given the choice between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter, and they chose the punishment of this world."

Likewise Abu Hatim Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih, from al-Hasan, from Sufyan, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Yahya ibn Bukayr, with it. [[The Musnad (2/134) and Sahih Ibn Hibban no. (1717) "Mawarid". Abu Hatim said in al-'Ilal (2/69): "This is a munkar hadith."]]

This hadith is gharib (singular) through this route, and all its narrators are trustworthy (thiqat) among the narrators of the two Sahihs, except this Musa ibn Jubayr, who is al-Ansari al-Sulami, their client (mawla), al-Madini al-Haddha'. He narrated from Ibn Abbas, Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, Nafi', and Abd Allah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik. And there narrated from him his son Abd al-Salam, Bakr ibn Mudar, Zuhayr ibn Muhammad, Sa'id ibn Salamah, Abd Allah ibn Lahi'ah, Amr ibn al-Harith, and Yahya ibn Ayyub. Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated from him. Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned him in al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil and did not record anything of criticism or praise regarding him, so he is of unknown condition (mastur al-hal). [[Al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil (8/139), and Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat (7/451) and said: "He errs and contradicts."]] He is alone in narrating it from Nafi', the client of Ibn Umar, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ. A follow-up (mutabi') has been narrated for him through another route from Nafi', as Ibn Mardawayh said: Da'laj ibn Ahmad related to us, Hisham [ibn Ali ibn Hisham] [[Addition from MSS ج، ط، و.]] related to us, Abd Allah ibn Raja' related to us, Sa'id ibn Salamah related to us, Musa ibn Sarjis related to us, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar: he heard the Prophet ﷺ say, and he mentioned it in full.

Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: Al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn (that is, Sunayd ibn Dawud, the author of the *tafsir* [exegesis]) narrated to us, al-Faraj ibn Fudala narrated to us, from Mu'awiya ibn Salih, from Nafi', who said: I travelled with Ibn Umar. When it was near the end of the night, he said: "O Nafi', look, has al-Hamra' risen?" I said: "No," twice or three times. Then I said: "It has risen." He said: "No welcome to her, nor any familiarity!" I said: "Glory be to Allah! It is a subjugated star, obedient and attentive." He said: "I only told you what I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)," or he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me": "The angels said: 'O Lord, how is Your patience with the children of Adam regarding their mistakes and sins?' He said: 'I tested them and I gave you well-being.' They said: 'If we were in their place, we would not disobey You.' He said: 'Then choose two angels from among you.' So they did not spare any effort in choosing, and they chose Harut and Marut."

These two reports are also extremely strange (*gharib jiddan*). The closest thing to this is that it comes from the narration of Abdullah ibn Umar, from Ka'b al-Ahbar, not from the Prophet (ﷺ), as 'Abd al-Razzaq said in his *tafsir*, from al-Thawri, from Musa ibn Uqba, from Salim, from Ibn Umar, from Ka'b, who said: "The angels mentioned the deeds of the children of Adam and the sins they commit, so it was said to them: 'Choose two of your number,' and they chose Harut and Marut. Then it was said to them: 'I send messengers to the children of Adam, and there is no messenger between Me and you. Descend, do not associate anything with Me, do not commit adultery, and do not drink wine.'" Ka'b said: "By Allah, they had not yet passed the evening of the day they were sent down until they had completed everything they had been forbidden."

Ibn Jarir narrated it through two chains from 'Abd al-Razzaq, with the same wording. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Ahmad ibn Isam, from Mu'ammal, from Sufyan al-Thawri, with the same wording.

Ibn Jarir also narrated: al-Muthanna narrated to me, al-Mu'alla (that is, Ibn Asad) narrated to us, Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, from Musa ibn Uqba: Salim narrated to me that he heard Abdullah speaking, from Ka'b al-Ahbar, and he mentioned it.

This chain (*isnad*) is more authentic and more reliable up to Abdullah ibn Umar than the two chains mentioned before, and Salim is more reliable regarding his father than Nafi', his freedman. So the report circles back to the transmission of Ka'b al-Ahbar from the books of the Children of Israel. And Allah knows best.

**Mention of the reports transmitted about this from the Companions and the Successors, may Allah be pleased with them all:**

Ibn Jarir said: al-Muthanna narrated to me, al-Hajjaj narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Umayr ibn Sa'id, who said: I heard Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) say: "Al-Zuhara was a beautiful woman from the people of Persia. She came to dispute before the two angels Harut and Marut, and they tried to seduce her, but she refused them unless they taught her the word which, when the speaker utters it, he ascends to the sky. So they taught her, she uttered it, and she ascended to the sky, and she was transformed into a star!"

This chain is good, its narrators are trustworthy, and the report is extremely strange (*gharib jiddan*).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Fadl ibn Shadhan narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Khalid, from Umayr ibn Sa'id, from Ali, who said: "They are two angels from the angels of the heaven." That is, the meaning of: ﴿And what was sent down upon the two angels﴾.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his *tafsir* with his chain, from Mughith, from his mawla (client) Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali, as a *marfu'* report (traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ)). But this does not stand as authentic through this route.

Then he narrated it through two other routes, from Jabir, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah curse al-Zuhara, for she is the one who tempted the two angels Harut and Marut." This also is not sound (*la yasahhu*), and it is very *munkar* (rejected). And Allah knows best.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, al-Hajjaj ibn Minhal narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, from Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas, that they both said together: "When the children of Adam multiplied and disobeyed, the angels, the earth, and the mountains called down upon them, saying: 'Our Lord, do not destroy them.' So Allah revealed to the angels: 'I have removed desire and Satan from your hearts, and if you were sent down, you would do the same.' They said to themselves that if they were tested, they would be steadfast. So Allah revealed to them: 'Choose two angels from the best of you.' So they chose Harut and Marut. They were sent down to the earth, and al-Zuhara was sent down to them in the most beautiful form of a woman from the people of Persia, whom they called Bidhukht. They then fell into sin. The angels used to seek forgiveness for those who believed: ﴿Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge﴾ [Ghafir: 7]. But when they fell into sin, they sought forgiveness for those on the earth: Indeed Allah is the Forgiving, the Merciful. Then they were given the choice between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter, and they chose the punishment of this world."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: my father narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Raqqi narrated to us, Ubayd Allah (that is, Ibn Amr) informed us, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysa, from al-Minhal ibn Amr and Yunus ibn Khabbab, from Mujahid, who said: "I was staying with Abdullah ibn Umar on a journey. When it was one night, he said to his servant: 'Look, has al-Hamra' risen? No welcome to her, nor any familiarity, nor may Allah greet her! She is the companion of the two angels.' The angels said: 'O Lord, how can You leave the sinful children of Adam, who shed forbidden blood, violate Your sanctities, and cause corruption on the earth?' He said: 'I have tested them. If I tested you with the same thing with which I tested them, you would do as they do.' They said: 'No.' He said: 'Then choose two of your best.' So they chose Harut and Marut. He said to them: 'I will send you down to the earth, and I make a covenant with you that you will not associate partners with Allah, nor commit adultery, nor betray.' They were sent down to the earth, and lust was cast upon them, and al-Zuhara was sent down to them in the most beautiful form of a woman. She presented herself to them, and they tried to seduce her. She said: 'I follow a religion that is not proper for anyone to approach me except one who is upon the same.' They said: 'And what is your religion?' She said: 'Magianism.' They said: 'That is polytheism! This is something we do not accept.' So she stayed away from them for as long as Allah willed. Then she presented herself to them again, and they desired her. She said: 'Whatever you wish, except that I have a husband, and I dislike that this should be seen of me so that I am disgraced. If you acknowledge my religion for me, and stipulate for me that you will take me up to the sky, I will do it.' So they acknowledged her religion for her, and they came to her in what they saw, then they took her up to the sky. When they brought her to the sky, she was snatched away from them, and their wings were cut off. They fell down, fearful, regretful, weeping. On the earth there was a prophet who would supplicate between the two Fridays, and on Friday his supplication would be answered. They said: 'If we go to so-and-so and ask him, he may seek repentance for us.' So they went to him, and he said: 'May Allah have mercy on you both! How can the people of the earth seek repentance for the people of the heavens!' They said: 'We have indeed been tested.' He said: 'Come to me on Friday.' They came to him, and he said: 'I have not been answered concerning you with anything; come to me on the second Friday.' They came to him, and he said: 'Choose, for you have been given a choice: if you wish the well-being of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter, or if you wish the punishment of this world, and you will be on the Day of Resurrection under the judgment of Allah.' One of them said: 'Indeed, little of this world remains.' The other said: 'Woe to you! I obeyed you in the first matter, so obey me now. Indeed, a punishment that perishes is not like a punishment that endures, and we will be on the Day of Resurrection under the judgment of Allah, so I fear that He will punish us.' He said: 'No. I hope that if Allah knows that we have chosen the punishment of this world out of fear of the punishment of the Hereafter, He will not combine both for us.' He said: 'So they chose the punishment of this world, and they were placed in iron pulleys in a well filled with fire, its upper part at the bottom.'"

This is a good chain up to Abdullah ibn Umar. It was previously mentioned in the narration of Ibn Jarir, from the report of Mu'awiya ibn Salih, from Nafi', from him, in a *marfu'* form. But this one is more established and sounder in its chain. Then it returns, and Allah knows best, to the narration of Ibn Umar from Ka'b, as its explanation was previously given from the narration of Salim from his father. And his statement that al-Zuhara descended in the form of a beautiful woman, and likewise in what is narrated from Ali, contains extreme strangeness (*gharaba jiddan*).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Isam ibn Rawwad narrated to us, Adam narrated to us, Abu Ja'far narrated to us, al-Rabi' ibn Anas narrated to us, from Qays ibn Abbad, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both [[In manuscripts J and T: "عنه", "with him."]], who said: When people came after Adam, peace be upon him, and fell into sins and disbelief in Allah, the angels in heaven said: "O Lord, these are the creatures whom You created only to worship You and obey You, and they have fallen into what they have fallen into. They have committed disbelief, murder, consuming unlawful wealth, adultery, theft and drinking wine." They began to invoke curses upon them and would not excuse them. It was said: "They are in the unseen (ghayb)." So they did not excuse them. It was then said to them: "Choose from among you two of your best angels, and I will command them and forbid them." They chose Harut and Marut. They were sent down to the earth, and the desires of the children of Adam were placed in them. Allah commanded them to worship Him and not to associate anything with Him, and they were forbidden from killing a soul unlawfully, from consuming unlawful wealth, from adultery, from theft and from drinking wine. They remained on the earth for a time, judging between people with truth, and that was in the time of Idris, peace be upon him. In that time there was a woman whose beauty among women was like the beauty of Venus (al-Zuhara) among the other stars. The two of them came to her, and they spoke to her humbly and sought to have her for themselves, but she refused, except that they should follow her command and her religion. They asked her about her religion, and she brought out an idol and said: "This is what I worship." They said: "We have no need to worship this." So they departed and stayed away for as long as Allah willed. Then they came to her again and sought her for themselves, and she did the same. They departed. Then they came to her again and sought her for themselves, and when she saw that they had refused to worship the idol, she said to them: "Choose one of three things: either you worship this idol, or you kill this soul, or you drink this wine." They said: "None of these is fitting, and the easiest of them is drinking wine." So they drank the wine, and it took effect on them, and they fell upon the woman. Then they feared that the man [[In manuscript J: "فقتلاها", "so they killed her."]] would inform about them, so they killed him. When the intoxication left them and they knew what they had fallen into of sin, they wanted to ascend to heaven, but they could not. Between them and that was an obstacle, and the veil was lifted between them and the people of heaven. The angels looked at what they had fallen into and were utterly astonished, and they knew that whoever is in the unseen is less fearful of Allah. After that, they began to seek forgiveness for those on earth. And in this regard it was revealed: ﴿And the angels glorify their Lord with praise and seek forgiveness for those on earth﴾ [al-Shura: 5]. It was then said to them: "Choose between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter." They said: "As for the punishment of this world, it will end and pass away. As for the punishment of the Hereafter, there is no end to it." So they chose the punishment of this world, and they were placed at Babil, and there they are being punished.

Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak at greater length, from Abu Zakariyya al-Anbari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Salam, from Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, from Hakkam ibn Salm al-Razi, who was trustworthy, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, with this chain. Then he said: "Its isnad is sound, but the two (Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it." This is the closest of what has been reported concerning the matter of Venus, and Allah knows best. [[Imam Ibn Hazm refuted the story of Harut and Marut and responded to those who claimed that they drank wine, committed adultery and killed, in his book al-Fasl (3/303–308, 4/61–65).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: My father narrated to us, Muslim narrated to us, al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl al-Huddani narrated to us, Yazid, meaning al-Farisi, narrated to us, from Ibn Abbas [who said] [[Addition from manuscripts J, T, B, A and W.]] that the people of the lowest heaven looked down upon the people of the earth and saw them committing sins. They said: "O Lord, the people of the earth were committing sins!" Allah said: "You are with Me, and they are absent from Me." It was said to them: "Choose three from among you." They chose three from among them to descend to the earth, on the condition that they judge among the people of the earth, and the desire of the children of Adam was placed in them. They were commanded not to drink wine, not to kill a soul, not to commit adultery, and not to prostrate to an idol. One of them asked to be excused, and he was excused. Two were sent down to the earth, and a woman from the most beautiful of people came to them, named Munahiya. Both of them fell in love with her. Then they went to her house and gathered with her, and they sought her, and she said to them: "No, not until you drink my wine, kill my neighbour's son, and prostrate to my idol." They said: "We will not prostrate." Then they drank the wine, then they killed, then they prostrated. The people of heaven looked down upon them, and she said to them: "Tell me the word, which if you say it, you will fly." They told her, and she flew, and was transformed into a burning star, and she is this Venus. As for the two of them, Sulayman ibn Dawud was sent to them, and he gave them the choice between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter, and they chose the punishment of this world. So they are suspended between heaven and earth.

This narration contains many additions, strangeness and irregularity, and Allah knows the truth.

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar said: Qatada and al-Zuhri said, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah, concerning the words ﴿And what was revealed to the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut﴾ [al-Baqarah: 102]: They were two angels from among the angels, and they were sent down to judge between people. That is because the angels mocked the judges of the children of Adam, so a woman came to them for judgment, and they inclined towards her. Then they went up, but an obstacle was placed between them and that, and they were given the choice between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter, and they chose the punishment of this world. Ma'mar said: Qatada said: They used to teach people magic, so it was taken from them that they should not teach anyone until they said: ﴿We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve﴾ [al-Baqarah: 102] [[Tafsir of Abd al-Razzaq (1/73).]].

Asbat narrated from al-Suddi that he said: Part of the matter of Harut and Marut was that they criticised the people of the earth regarding their judgments. It was said to them: "I have given the children of Adam ten desires, and by them they disobey Me." Harut and Marut said: "Our Lord, if You had given us those desires and then sent us down, we would have judged with justice." He said to them: "Descend, for I have given you those ten desires, so judge between people." They descended to Babil Dunbawand, and they used to judge. When evening came they ascended, and when morning came they descended. They continued like this until a woman came to them disputing with her husband, and her beauty pleased them. Her name in Arabic is "al-Zuhara," in Nabataean "Bidhukht," and in Persian "Anahid." One of them said to his companion: "She truly pleases me." The other said: "I wanted to mention her to you, but I was ashamed before you." The other said: "Would you like us to approach her ourselves?" He said: "Yes, but how can we face the punishment of Allah?" The other said: "Indeed, we hope for the mercy of Allah." When she came disputing with her husband, they offered themselves to her, and she said: "No, not until you judge in my favour against my husband." So they judged in her favour against her husband. Then she arranged with them a ruined place among the ruins where they would come to her. They came to her for that purpose. When the one who would lie with her wanted to, she said: "I will not do it until you tell me by what word you ascend to heaven, and by what word you descend from it." So they told her, and she spoke and ascended, and Allah made her forget the word by which she would descend, so she remained in her place, and Allah transformed her into a star. Abdullah ibn Umar, whenever he saw her, would curse her and say: "This is the one who tempted Harut and Marut." When night came, they wanted to ascend but could not, so they knew their destruction, and they were given the choice between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. They chose the punishment of this world, so they were hung at Babil, and they began to speak to people in their own language, which was magic.

Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid: As for the matter of Harut and Marut, the angels were astonished at the injustice of the children of Adam, although the messengers, books and clear proofs had come to them. Their Lord, exalted is He, said to them: "Choose from among you two angels, whom I will send down to judge among the children of Adam on the earth." They chose, and they did not hesitate, except for Harut and Marut. When He sent them down, He said to them: "Are you amazed at the children of Adam for their injustice and their disobedience? Messengers and books [and clear proofs] [[Addition from manuscript J.]] come to them from afar, but between Me and you there is no messenger. So do this and that, and leave that and this." He commanded them and forbade them, then they acted accordingly, and no one was more obedient to Allah than they were. They judged justly and were fair. They used to judge among the children of Adam during the day, and when evening came they ascended and were with the angels, and when morning came they descended and judged and were fair, until Venus was sent down to them in the most beautiful form of a woman who was disputing. They ruled against her. When she rose, each of them felt something in himself. One of them said to his companion: "Did you feel what I felt?" He said: "Yes." So they sent to her: "Come to us, and we will judge in your favour." When she returned, they judged in her favour, and she came to them, and they uncovered their private parts for her. Their desire was only within themselves, and they were not like the children of Adam in desire for women and their pleasure. When they reached that and considered it lawful, they were tempted. Venus flew away and returned to where she had been. When evening came, they tried to ascend, but they were rebuked, and they were not permitted, and their wings did not carry them. They sought help from a man among the children of Adam, and they came to him and said: "Pray to your Lord for us." He said: "How can the people of the earth intercede for the people of heaven?" They said: "We heard that your Lord mentions you favourably in heaven." So he promised them a day, and the next day he prayed for them, and his prayer was answered. They were given the choice between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. One of them looked at his companion and said: "Do you not know that the groups of Allah's punishment in the Hereafter are such-and-such for eternity, while in this world it is nine times as much?" So they were commanded to descend to Babil, and there is their punishment. And he claimed that they are suspended in iron, folded, beating their wings.

It has been narrated concerning the story of Harut and Marut from a group of the Followers (tabi'un), such as Mujahid, al-Suddi, al-Hasan [al-Basri] [[Addition from manuscripts J, T, B, A and W.]], Qatada, Abu al-Aliya, al-Zuhri, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Muqatil ibn Hayyan and others. Many of the exegetes, both earlier and later, have related it. Its essence, in its details, goes back to the reports of the Children of Israel, for there is no sound, elevated (marfu') hadith with a connected chain to the truthful, believed, infallible one who does not speak from desire (ﷺ). The apparent context of the Qur'an mentions the story in summary, without elaborate detail or lengthy explanation. So we believe in what has come in the Qur'an according to what Allah the Exalted intended, and Allah knows the reality of the matter.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verses 99–103 (part 6 of 7):

There is a strange report and a remarkable narrative on this matter, which we wish to draw attention to. Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman related to us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Ibn Abi al-Zinad informed me: Hisham ibn 'Urwah related to me, from his father, from 'Aishah, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ) [may Allah be pleased with her and with her father] [[addition from ج.]], that she said: A woman from the people of Dumat al-Jandal came to me, seeking the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) after his death, not long after it. She asked him about something [[in أ and و: "about things".]] into which she had entered concerning sorcery (sihr), and she had not acted upon it. 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said to 'Urwah: "O nephew! I saw her weeping when she could not find the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to cure her. She kept weeping until I felt pity for her, and she was saying: 'I fear that I have been ruined. I had a husband who went away from me, so I entered upon an old woman and complained to her about that. She said: If you do what I command you, I will make him come to you.' When night came, she brought me two black dogs. I mounted one of them, and she mounted the other. They did not move like anything until we stopped at Babil, and behold, there were two men hanging by their feet. They said: 'What brought you here?' I said: 'I want to learn sorcery.' They said: 'We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve; return.' But I refused and said: 'No.' They said: 'Go to that oven and urinate into it.' I went, became frightened, and did not do it. I returned to them, and they said: 'Did you do it?' I said: 'Yes.' They said: 'Did you see anything?' I said: 'I saw nothing.' They said: 'You did not do it. Return to your land and do not disbelieve [for you are at the beginning of your affair]' [[addition from ج.]]. I hesitated and refused. They said: 'Go to that oven and urinate into it.' I went and was seized with fear [and I was afraid] [[addition from ج، ب، أ، و.]], then returned to them and said: 'I have done it.' They said: 'What did you see?' I said: 'I saw nothing.' They said: 'You lied, you did not do it. Return to your land and do not disbelieve; for you are at the beginning of your affair.' I hesitated and refused. They said: 'Go to that oven and urinate into it.' I went to it and urinated into it, and I saw a masked horseman [[in ج: "suspended".]] with iron, who came out of me, rose into the sky, and disappeared [from me] [[addition from أ.]] until I could no longer see him. I came back to them and said: 'I have done it.' They said: 'What did you see?' I said: 'I saw a masked horseman who came out of me, rose into the sky, until I could no longer see him.' They said: 'You have spoken the truth. That was your faith, which left you. Go.' I said to the woman: 'By Allah, I know nothing, and they did not say anything to me.' She said: 'Yes, they did. You will never desire anything except that it happens. Take this wheat, sow it.' I sowed it and said: 'Sprout!' and it sprouted. I said: 'Ear!' and it ripened. I said: 'Dry!' and it dried. I said: 'Grind!' and it was ground. I said: 'Bake!' and it was baked. When I saw that I did not desire anything except that it happened, I was overcome with regret. By Allah, O Mother of the Believers, by Allah, I have never done anything at all, and I will never do it again."

[Source: Tafsir al-Tabari (2/439–441).]

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman, in the same form, at greater length as mentioned above [Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/312); al-Bayhaqi also narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra (8/137) through al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman, at greater length. This addition does not appear in the printed edition of Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim, and the esteemed editor, may Allah reward him well, has pointed this out.]. He added, after her words "and I will never do it again": "So I asked the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when the death of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was recent, and they were numerous at that time, and they did not know what to say to her. All of them were in awe and feared to give her a verdict on something they did not know, except that Ibn 'Abbas, or some of those who were with him, said to her: 'If your parents were alive, or one of them, they would suffice you.'"

Hisham said: "If she came to us, we would give her a verdict requiring compensation [said] [[addition from أ.]]." Ibn Abi al-Zinad said: Hisham used to say: "They were people of scrupulousness (wara') and fear of Allah." Then Hisham would say: "If someone like her came to us today, they would find us to be foolish people of ignorance who presume knowledge they do not have."

This is a sound chain (isnad) to 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her.

Those who hold that the sorcerer has the ability to change the essence of things have cited this report, because this woman sowed the wheat and it grew immediately. Others said: Rather, sorcery has no power except to create illusion (takhyil), as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They bewitched the eyes of the people and terrified them, and they produced a great sorcery﴾ [al-A'raf: 116], and He the Exalted said: ﴿Their sorcery made it appear to him that their ropes and staffs were moving﴾ [Ta-Ha: 66]. This report has also been cited as evidence that Babil mentioned in the Qur'an is Babil of Iraq, not Babil of Dunbawand [[in ط، ب، أ، و: "Dinawand".]], as al-Suddi and others said. The evidence that it is Babil of Iraq is what Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn related to us: Ahmad ibn Salih related to us: Ibn Wahb related to me: Ibn Lahi'ah and Yahya ibn Azhar related to me, from 'Ammar ibn Sa'd al-Muradi, from Abu Salih al-Ghifari, that 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, [passed by Babil while traveling. The caller to prayer came to him to call him to the 'Asr prayer. When he had left it, he ordered the caller to call the iqamah, and when he finished, he said:] "My beloved (ﷺ) forbade me to pray [in a cemetery, and forbade me to pray] in Babil, for it is cursed."

[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/304). The words in brackets are not in Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim.]
