God Most High said: ﴿Those who disbelieve among the People of the Book, nor the polytheists, wish that any good should be sent down upon you from your Lord﴾. By this God Most High shows the intensity of the enmity of the disbelievers among the People of the Book and the polytheists, whose imitation of the believers He warned against, in order to sever affection between them and the believers. He also draws attention to what He has blessed the believers with, of the complete and perfect law, which He prescribed for their Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), when He says: ﴿God specially chooses for His mercy whom He wills, and God is the Lord of great bounty.﴾

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verses 106–107 (part 1 of 2):

Ibn Abi Talha reported from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate﴾: "We replace any verse."

Ibn Jurayj reported from Mujahid regarding ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate﴾: that is, "We erase any verse."

Ibn Abi Najih reported from Mujahid regarding ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate﴾: he said, "We keep its writing but change its ruling." He narrated this from the companions of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was also reported from Abu al-'Aliyah and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi something similar to this.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate﴾ means "whatever We cause to be forgotten." 'Ata' said: As for ﴿Whatever We abrogate﴾, it means "whatever We leave out" of the Qur'an. Ibn Abi Hatim said: That is, it was left and was not revealed to Muhammad ﷺ.

Al-Suddi said: ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate﴾, its abrogation (naskh) is its taking away (qabd). Ibn Abi Hatim said: By its taking away is meant its removal, like his saying [regarding the stoning verse]: "If an old married man and an old married woman commit adultery, then stone them absolutely," and his saying: "If the son of Adam had two valleys of wealth, he would seek a third."

Ibn Jarir said: ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate﴾ means whatever is transferred from the ruling of one verse to another, so that We replace it and change it. This happens when the lawful becomes unlawful, the unlawful becomes lawful, the permitted becomes forbidden, and the forbidden becomes permitted. This occurs only in commands, prohibitions, restrictions, releases, prohibitions and permissions. As for reports (akhbar), there is no abrogating (nasikh) or abrogated (mansukh) element in them. The root of naskh (abrogation) is from the copying of a book (naskh al-kitab), which means transferring it from one copy to another. Likewise, the meaning of abrogating a ruling to something else is merely transferring it and moving the worship to something else. Whether the abrogation concerns its ruling or its writing, in both cases it is abrogated. As for the scholars of usul al-fiqh (the principles of jurisprudence), their definitions of naskh differ, but the matter is near, because the meaning of legal naskh is known to the scholars. Some of them summarized it as: the lifting of a ruling by a later legal proof. This includes the abrogation of a lighter ruling by a heavier one, and the reverse, and abrogation without a replacement. As for the detailed rulings of naskh, its types and its conditions, these are expounded in the discipline of usul al-fiqh.

Al-Tabarani said: Abu Shubayl 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Waqid narrated to us, my father narrated to us, al-'Abbas ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Arqam, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, who said: Two men recited a surah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had taught them, and they used to recite it. One night they stood to pray, but they could not recall a single letter of it. In the morning they went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned that to him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "It is among what was abrogated and made to be forgotten, so forget it." Al-Zuhri used to recite it: ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten﴾ with a damma on the nun and lightened. [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/288).] Sulayman ibn Arqam is weak.

[Abu Bakr ibn al-Anbari narrated from his father, from Nasr ibn Dawud, from Abu 'Ubayd, from 'Abd Allah ibn Salih, from al-Layth, from Yunus, 'Ubayd and 'Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, something similar to this, raised to the Prophet ﷺ. Al-Qurtubi mentioned it. [Al-Tahawi also narrated it in Mushkil al-Athar, no. (2034), by the route of Ibn Wahb, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Umamah, and no. (2035), by the route of Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamza, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Umamah.]]

* *

As for His saying ﴿or cause it to be forgotten﴾, it has been recited in two ways: "nansa'uha" and "nunsiha." As for the one who recited it as "nansa'uha," with a fatha on the nun and a hamza after the sin, its meaning is: We postpone it. 'Ali ibn Abi Talha reported from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate or postpone﴾: he said, "We replace any verse, or We leave it and do not replace it."

Mujahid said, from the companions of Ibn Mas'ud, regarding ﴿or postpone it﴾: "We keep its writing and change its ruling." 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, Mujahid and 'Ata' said regarding ﴿or postpone it﴾: "We delay it and defer it." 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi said regarding ﴿or postpone it﴾: "We delay it, so We do not abrogate it." Al-Suddi said the same, and likewise al-Rabi' ibn Anas. Al-Dahhak said regarding ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate or postpone﴾: it means "the abrogating from the abrogated." Abu al-'Aliyah said regarding ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate or postpone﴾: that is, "We delay it with Us."

Ibn Hatim said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Isma'il al-Baghdadi narrated to us, Khalaf narrated to us, al-Khaffaf narrated to us, from Isma'il, meaning Ibn Muslim, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, addressed us and said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate or postpone﴾, that is, "We delay it."

As for the reading ﴿or cause it to be forgotten﴾, 'Abd al-Razzaq reported from Qatadah regarding His saying ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten﴾: he said, "Allah used to cause His Prophet to forget whatever He wished and abrogate whatever He wished."

Ibn Jarir said: Sawwad ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us, 'Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan that he said regarding His saying ﴿or cause it to be forgotten﴾: "Indeed your Prophet ﷺ was taught a Qur'an and then forgot it."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ibn Nufayl narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Zubayr al-Harrani narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj, meaning al-Jazari, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Among what was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ was revelation at night which he forgot by day. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring one better than it or similar to it﴾.

Abu Hatim said: Abu Ja'far ibn Nufayl said to me: "It is not al-Hajjaj ibn Artah; he is a Jazari shaykh of ours."

'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr said: ﴿or cause it to be forgotten﴾ means "We raise it from among you."

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Hushaym narrated to us, from Ya'la ibn 'Ata', from al-Qasim ibn Rabi'ah, who said: I heard Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas reciting: "Whatever verse We abrogate or cause you to forget." I said to him: "Indeed Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib recites it: 'or postpone it.'" Sa'd said: "The Qur'an was not revealed to al-Musayyib, nor to the family of al-Musayyib. Allah, may His praise be exalted, says: ﴿We shall make you recite, so you will not forget﴾ [al-A'la: 6] and ﴿Remember your Lord when you forget﴾ [al-Kahf: 24]." [Tafsir al-Tabari (2/475).]

'Abd al-Razzaq narrated it likewise from Hushaym. [Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (1/75).] Al-Hakim also narrated it in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Abu Hatim al-Razi, from Adam, from Shu'bah, from Ya'la ibn 'Ata', with the same wording, and said: "It is according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs [al-Bukhari and Muslim], though they did not narrate it."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was reported from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, Qatadah and 'Ikrimah something similar to the saying of Sa'id.

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya informed us, Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'Umar said: "'Ali is the best judge among us, and Ubayy is the best reciter among us. Yet we leave some of what Ubayy says, and Ubayy says: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say it, so I will not leave it for anything.' And Allah says: ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate or postpone, We bring one better than it or similar to it﴾."

Al-Bukhari said: 'Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, Yahya narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Habib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'Umar said: "Ubayy is the best reciter among us, and 'Ali is the best judge among us. Yet we leave some of Ubayy's sayings, because Ubayy says: 'I will not leave anything I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.' And Allah has said: ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten﴾." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4481).]

* *

As for His saying ﴿We bring one better than it or similar to it﴾: that is, in the ruling, in relation to the benefit of those who are obligated, as 'Ali ibn Abi Talha said from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿We bring one better than it﴾ means: "better for you in benefit and more gentle toward you."

Abu al-'Aliyah said: ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate﴾ means "we do not act upon it," and ﴿or postpone it﴾ means "We defer it with Us; We bring it or its like."

Al-Suddi said: ﴿We bring one better than it or similar to it﴾ means: "We bring one better than what We abrogated, or similar to what We left."

Qatadah said: ﴿We bring one better than it or similar to it﴾ means: "a verse in which there is lightening, a concession, a command, or a prohibition."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Do you not know that Allah is over all things competent? Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and that you have not besides Allah any protector or helper?﴾ He, may He be exalted, guides by this that He is the One who disposes of His creation as He wills. To Him belong the creation and the command, and He is the Disposer. Just as He creates them as He wills, He makes whomever He wills happy, makes whomever He wills wretched, makes whomever He wills healthy, makes whomever He wills ill, grants success to whomever He wills, and forsakes whomever He wills. Likewise, He judges among His servants as He wills: He makes lawful what He wills, prohibits what He wills, permits what He wills, and forbids what He wills. He is the One who judges as He desires, and there is none to repel His judgment. He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned. He tests His servants and their obedience to His messengers through abrogation (naskh). He commands something because of the benefit in it that He knows, then He forbids it because of what He knows, may He be exalted. So obedience is complete obedience in carrying out His command, following His messengers in affirming what they reported, carrying out what they commanded, and abandoning what they forbade. In this context there is a great refutation and a clear explanation against the disbelief of the Jews and the exposure of their doubt, may Allah curse them, in their claim that abrogation is impossible, either rationally, as some of them foolishly and disbelievingly claimed, or by transmission, as others among them fabricated falsely and deceitfully. [In A: "the disbelief of the disbelievers."]

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The interpretation of the verse is: Do you not know, O Muhammad, that to Me belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and their authority, apart from any other? I judge in them and in what is in them as I will, I command in them and in what is in them as I will, I forbid what I will, and I abrogate, replace and change from My rulings, which I apply to My servants, whatever I will, when I will, and I confirm in them whatever I will.

Then he said: Although this report is from Allah, Exalted, addressed to His Prophet ﷺ in the form of a report about His greatness, it is also a refutation of the Jews who denied the abrogation of the rulings of the Torah and rejected the prophethood of Jesus and Muhammad, upon them both be blessings and peace, because of their coming with what they came with from Allah, by altering what Allah had altered in the rulings of the Torah. So Allah informed them that to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and their authority, that creation are the people of His kingdom and obedience, that upon them is hearing and obeying His command and prohibition, and that to Him belongs the right to command them as He wills, to forbid them what He wills, to abrogate what He wills, to confirm what He wills, and to originate what He wills of His confirmation, command and prohibition.

[And He commanded Abraham, peace be upon him, to slaughter his son, then He abrogated it before the act. And He commanded the majority of the Children of Israel to kill those among them who worshipped the calf, then He lifted the killing from them lest the killing eradicate them.]

I say: What drives the Jews to dispute the question of abrogation (naskh) is nothing but disbelief and obstinacy. For there is nothing in reason that proves the impossibility of abrogation in the rulings of God, the Exalted, since He decrees whatever He wills just as He does whatever He wishes. Moreover, this has indeed occurred in His earlier books and past laws. Just as He permitted Adam to marry his daughters to his sons and then forbade that; and just as He permitted Noah, after he left the ark, to eat all animals, then abrogated the permissibility of some of them; and the marriage of two sisters was permitted to Israel (Ya'qub) and his sons, but this was forbidden in the law of the Torah and what came after it. And there are many other things too lengthy to mention, and they acknowledge this, yet they turn away from it. As for what is answered to these proofs with verbal replies, the indication in meaning is not diverted, since that is the intended point. Likewise, in their books there is the well-known good news about Muhammad (ﷺ) and the command to follow him, which necessitates the obligation of following him (peace be upon him), and that no deed is accepted except in accordance with his law. Whether it is said that the earlier laws were limited (mughayyah) until his mission (peace be upon him), so that this is not called abrogation, as in His saying: ﴿Then complete the fast until the night﴾ [al-Baqarah: 187]; or it is said that they were unrestricted and that the law of Muhammad (ﷺ) abrogated them, in either case the obligation to follow him is definite (mu'ayyan), because he came with a Book which is the most recent (ahdath) of the books in terms of its connection with God, blessed and exalted is He.

Here, in this context, God, the Exalted, demonstrated the permissibility of abrogation, refuting the Jews, may the curses of God be upon them, when He said, the Exalted: ﴿Do you not know that God is All-Powerful over everything?﴾ ﴿Do you not know that to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and that you have, besides God, neither protector nor helper?﴾ and so on. Just as He has sovereignty without any rival, so too He has the right to judge by whatever He wills: ﴿Surely, to Him belong creation and command﴾ [al-A'raf: 54]. And in Surat Al 'Imran, whose beginning was revealed as an address to the People of the Book, the occurrence of abrogation is recited against the Jews in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel made unlawful for himself﴾ [Al 'Imran: 93], as its interpretation will come. All Muslims agree on the permissibility of abrogation in the rulings of God, the Exalted, because of the profound wisdoms in it, and all of them affirm that it has occurred. Abu Muslim al-Isfahani, the exegete, said: Nothing of that occurred in the Qur'an. But this statement of his is weak, rejected and discredited. He also strained greatly in his answers regarding what has occurred of abrogation. Among that is the matter of the waiting period (iddah) of four months and ten days after a year, for which he gave no acceptable answer; and the matter of the change of the qiblah to the Ka'bah from Bayt al-Maqdis, for which he gave no answer at all. Among it also is the abrogation of the requirement for a Muslim to stand firm against ten disbelievers to standing firm against two; and among it the abrogation of the obligation of charity before private consultation with the Messenger (ﷺ), and other things. And God knows best.

Ibn Hatim said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Isma'il al-Baghdadi narrated to us, Khalaf narrated to us, al-Khaffaf narrated to us, from Isma'il, meaning Ibn Muslim, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, addressed us and said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate or postpone﴾, that is, "We delay it."

As for the reading ﴿or cause it to be forgotten﴾, 'Abd al-Razzaq reported from Qatadah regarding His saying ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten﴾: he said, "Allah used to cause His Prophet to forget whatever He wished and abrogate whatever He wished."

Ibn Jarir said: Sawwad ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us, 'Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan that he said regarding His saying ﴿or cause it to be forgotten﴾: "Indeed your Prophet ﷺ was taught a Qur'an and then forgot it."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ibn Nufayl narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Zubayr al-Harrani narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj, meaning al-Jazari, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Among what was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ was revelation at night which he forgot by day. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring one better than it or similar to it﴾.

Abu Hatim said: Abu Ja'far ibn Nufayl said to me: "It is not al-Hajjaj ibn Artah; he is a Jazari shaykh of ours."

'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr said: ﴿or cause it to be forgotten﴾ means "We raise it from among you."

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Hushaym narrated to us, from Ya'la ibn 'Ata', from al-Qasim ibn Rabi'ah, who said: I heard Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas reciting: "Whatever verse We abrogate or cause you to forget." I said to him: "Indeed Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib recites it: 'or postpone it.'" Sa'd said: "The Qur'an was not revealed to al-Musayyib, nor to the family of al-Musayyib. Allah, may His praise be exalted, says: ﴿We shall make you recite, so you will not forget﴾ [al-A'la: 6] and ﴿Remember your Lord when you forget﴾ [al-Kahf: 24]." [Tafsir al-Tabari (2/475).]

'Abd al-Razzaq narrated it likewise from Hushaym. [Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (1/75).] Al-Hakim also narrated it in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Abu Hatim al-Razi, from Adam, from Shu'bah, from Ya'la ibn 'Ata', with the same wording, and said: "It is according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs [al-Bukhari and Muslim], though they did not narrate it."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was reported from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, Qatadah and 'Ikrimah something similar to the saying of Sa'id.

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya informed us, Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'Umar said: "'Ali is the best judge among us, and Ubayy is the best reciter among us. Yet we leave some of what Ubayy says, and Ubayy says: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say it, so I will not leave it for anything.' And Allah says: ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate or postpone, We bring one better than it or similar to it﴾."

Al-Bukhari said: 'Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, Yahya narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Habib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'Umar said: "Ubayy is the best reciter among us, and 'Ali is the best judge among us. Yet we leave some of Ubayy's sayings, because Ubayy says: 'I will not leave anything I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.' And Allah has said: ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten﴾." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4481).]

* *

As for His saying ﴿We bring one better than it or similar to it﴾: that is, in the ruling, in relation to the benefit of those who are obligated, as 'Ali ibn Abi Talha said from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿We bring one better than it﴾ means: "better for you in benefit and more gentle toward you."

Abu al-'Aliyah said: ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate﴾ means "we do not act upon it," and ﴿or postpone it﴾ means "We defer it with Us; We bring it or its like."

Al-Suddi said: ﴿We bring one better than it or similar to it﴾ means: "We bring one better than what We abrogated, or similar to what We left."

Qatadah said: ﴿We bring one better than it or similar to it﴾ means: "a verse in which there is lightening, a concession, a command, or a prohibition."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Do you not know that Allah is over all things competent? Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and that you have not besides Allah any protector or helper?﴾ He, may He be exalted, guides by this that He is the One who disposes of His creation as He wills. To Him belong the creation and the command, and He is the Disposer. Just as He creates them as He wills, He makes whomever He wills happy, makes whomever He wills wretched, makes whomever He wills healthy, makes whomever He wills ill, grants success to whomever He wills, and forsakes whomever He wills. Likewise, He judges among His servants as He wills: He makes lawful what He wills, prohibits what He wills, permits what He wills, and forbids what He wills. He is the One who judges as He desires, and there is none to repel His judgment. He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned. He tests His servants and their obedience to His messengers through abrogation (naskh). He commands something because of the benefit in it that He knows, then He forbids it because of what He knows, may He be exalted. So obedience is complete obedience in carrying out His command, following His messengers in affirming what they reported, carrying out what they commanded, and abandoning what they forbade. In this context there is a great refutation and a clear explanation against the disbelief of the Jews and the exposure of their doubt, may Allah curse them, in their claim that abrogation is impossible, either rationally, as some of them foolishly and disbelievingly claimed, or by transmission, as others among them fabricated falsely and deceitfully. [In A: "the disbelief of the disbelievers."]

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The interpretation of the verse is: Do you not know, O Muhammad, that to Me belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and their authority, apart from any other? I judge in them and in what is in them as I will, I command in them and in what is in them as I will, I forbid what I will, and I abrogate, replace and change from My rulings, which I apply to My servants, whatever I will, when I will, and I confirm in them whatever I will.

Then he said: Although this report is from Allah, Exalted, addressed to His Prophet ﷺ in the form of a report about His greatness, it is also a refutation of the Jews who denied the abrogation of the rulings of the Torah and rejected the prophethood of Jesus and Muhammad, upon them both be blessings and peace, because of their coming with what they came with from Allah, by altering what Allah had altered in the rulings of the Torah. So Allah informed them that to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and their authority, that creation are the people of His kingdom and obedience, that upon them is hearing and obeying His command and prohibition, and that to Him belongs the right to command them as He wills, to forbid them what He wills, to abrogate what He wills, to confirm what He wills, and to originate what He wills of His confirmation, command and prohibition.

[And He commanded Abraham, peace be upon him, to slaughter his son, then He abrogated it before the act. And He commanded the majority of the Children of Israel to kill those among them who worshipped the calf, then He lifted the killing from them lest the killing eradicate them.]

I say: What drives the Jews to dispute the question of abrogation (naskh) is nothing but disbelief and obstinacy. For there is nothing in reason that proves the impossibility of abrogation in the rulings of God, the Exalted, since He decrees whatever He wills just as He does whatever He wishes. Moreover, this has indeed occurred in His earlier books and past laws. Just as He permitted Adam to marry his daughters to his sons and then forbade that; and just as He permitted Noah, after he left the ark, to eat all animals, then abrogated the permissibility of some of them; and the marriage of two sisters was permitted to Israel (Ya'qub) and his sons, but this was forbidden in the law of the Torah and what came after it. And there are many other things too lengthy to mention, and they acknowledge this, yet they turn away from it. As for what is answered to these proofs with verbal replies, the indication in meaning is not diverted, since that is the intended point. Likewise, in their books there is the well-known good news about Muhammad (ﷺ) and the command to follow him, which necessitates the obligation of following him (peace be upon him), and that no deed is accepted except in accordance with his law. Whether it is said that the earlier laws were limited (mughayyah) until his mission (peace be upon him), so that this is not called abrogation, as in His saying: ﴿Then complete the fast until the night﴾ [al-Baqarah: 187]; or it is said that they were unrestricted and that the law of Muhammad (ﷺ) abrogated them, in either case the obligation to follow him is definite (mu'ayyan), because he came with a Book which is the most recent (ahdath) of the books in terms of its connection with God, blessed and exalted is He.

Here, in this context, God, the Exalted, demonstrated the permissibility of abrogation, refuting the Jews, may the curses of God be upon them, when He said, the Exalted: ﴿Do you not know that God is All-Powerful over everything?﴾ ﴿Do you not know that to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and that you have, besides God, neither protector nor helper?﴾ and so on. Just as He has sovereignty without any rival, so too He has the right to judge by whatever He wills: ﴿Surely, to Him belong creation and command﴾ [al-A'raf: 54]. And in Surat Al 'Imran, whose beginning was revealed as an address to the People of the Book, the occurrence of abrogation is recited against the Jews in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel made unlawful for himself﴾ [Al 'Imran: 93], as its interpretation will come. All Muslims agree on the permissibility of abrogation in the rulings of God, the Exalted, because of the profound wisdoms in it, and all of them affirm that it has occurred. Abu Muslim al-Isfahani, the exegete, said: Nothing of that occurred in the Qur'an. But this statement of his is weak, rejected and discredited. He also strained greatly in his answers regarding what has occurred of abrogation. Among that is the matter of the waiting period (iddah) of four months and ten days after a year, for which he gave no acceptable answer; and the matter of the change of the qiblah to the Ka'bah from Bayt al-Maqdis, for which he gave no answer at all. Among it also is the abrogation of the requirement for a Muslim to stand firm against ten disbelievers to standing firm against two; and among it the abrogation of the obligation of charity before private consultation with the Messenger (ﷺ), and other things. And God knows best.

Allah, exalted is He, forbids in this noble verse excessive questioning of the Prophet ﷺ about things before they occur, as He said: ﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would distress you; but if you ask about them while the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be disclosed to you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 101]. That is: if you ask about their details after they have been revealed, they will be explained to you. And do not ask about a matter before it exists, for it may be made unlawful because of that question. For this reason it has come in the Sahih: "The greatest of the Muslims in crime is the one who asked about something that had not been made unlawful, and so it became unlawful because of his question" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (7289), and Sahih Muslim, no. (2358), from the hadith of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, may Allah be pleased with him].

When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about a man who finds another man with his wife: if he speaks, he speaks of a grave matter, and if he keeps silent, he keeps silent over such a thing. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked questions and criticised them. Then Allah revealed the ruling of li'an (mutual cursing) [narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, nos. (5308, 5259), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (1492), from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd, may Allah be pleased with him]. For this reason it is established in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to forbid "qila wa qal" (idle talk), excessive questioning, and squandering of wealth [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (1477), and Sahih Muslim, no. (593)]. In Sahih Muslim: "Leave me alone with what I have left you, for those before you were destroyed by their excessive questioning and their disputing with their prophets. So when I command you to do something, do of it what you are able; and when I forbid you from something, avoid it" [Sahih Muslim, no. (1337), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him]. He said this only after informing them that Allah had prescribed the Hajj for them. A man said: "Is it every year, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained silent about him three times. Then he said, peace be upon him: "No. And if I had said yes, it would have become obligatory, and if it had become obligatory, you would not have been able to fulfil it." Then he said: "Leave me alone with what I have left you," and the hadith continues.

Thus also said Anas ibn Malik: "We were forbidden to ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about anything, and it used to please us that a man from the desert folk would come and ask him while we listened" [narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (12)].

The Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said in his Musnad: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' ibn Azib, who said: "A year would pass over me while I wished to ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about something, but I would be too awed to ask him. And we used to wish that a Bedouin would come and ask him."

Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "I have not seen a people better than the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ. They asked him only about twelve questions, all of which are in the Qur'an: ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling﴾ [al-Baqarah: 219], and ﴿They ask you about the sacred month﴾ [al-Baqarah: 217], and ﴿And they ask you about the orphans﴾ [al-Baqarah: 220]," meaning: this and similar matters [narrated also by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/454) through the chain of Abdullah ibn Umar ibn Aban, from Muhammad ibn Fudayl, at greater length].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Or do you wish to ask your Messenger as Moses was asked before?﴾ — that is, rather, you wish. Or it may be that the interrogative retains its original form, and it is a rebuke, and it encompasses both believers and disbelievers, for he, peace be upon him, is the Messenger of Allah to all of them, as He said: ﴿The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a Book from heaven. They asked Moses for greater than that, when they said: "Show us Allah openly," so the thunderbolt seized them for their wrongdoing﴾ [al-Nisa': 153].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me, from Ikrimah or Sa'id [ibn Jubayr], from Ibn Abbas, who said: Rafi' ibn Huraymilah — or Wahb ibn Zayd — said: "O Muhammad, bring us a Book from heaven that we may read, and cause rivers to gush forth for us, and we will follow you and believe you." So Allah revealed concerning their statement: ﴿Or do you wish to ask your Messenger as Moses was asked before? And whoever exchanges disbelief for faith has certainly strayed from the even way﴾.

Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah concerning His saying: ﴿Or do you wish to ask your Messenger as Moses was asked before? And whoever exchanges disbelief for faith has certainly strayed from the even way﴾, who said: A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, would that our expiations were like the expiations of the Children of Israel!" The Prophet ﷺ said: "O Allah, we do not desire it" — three times — "What Allah has given you is better than what He gave the Children of Israel. When one of the Children of Israel committed a sin, he would find it written on his door and its expiation: if he expiated it, it would be a disgrace for him in this world, and if he did not expiate it, it would be a disgrace for him in the Hereafter. So what Allah has given you is better than what He gave the Children of Israel." He said: ﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself, then seeks forgiveness of Allah, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Nisa': 110]. And he said: "The five prayers are expiations for what lies between them, from Friday to Friday." And he said: "Whoever intends an evil deed and does not do it, it is not written against him; and if he does it, one evil deed is written. Whoever intends a good deed and does not do it, one good deed is written for him; and if he does it, ten like it are written for him. And none perishes before Allah except one who is destined to perish." Then Allah revealed: ﴿Or do you wish to ask your Messenger as Moses was asked before?﴾

Mujahid said concerning ﴿Or do you wish to ask your Messenger as Moses was asked before?﴾ that it means asking that Allah show them Himself openly. He said: The Quraysh asked Muhammad ﷺ to make Safa gold for them. He said: "Yes, and it will be for you like the table (al-Ma'idah) for the Children of Israel, if you disbelieve." But they refused and withdrew.

Similar was narrated from al-Suddi and Qatadah, and Allah knows best.

The meaning is that Allah censured those who asked the Messenger ﷺ about something in a manner of obstinacy and demanding, as the Children of Israel asked Moses, peace be upon him, out of obstinacy, denial and stubbornness. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever exchanges disbelief for faith﴾, that is, whoever buys disbelief in exchange for faith, ﴿has certainly strayed from the even way﴾, that is, has departed from the straight path into ignorance and error. Such is the state of those who turned away from believing the prophets, following them and submitting to them, and turned instead to opposing and denying them, and to putting to them questions they have no need of, in a manner of obstinacy and disbelief, as He said: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to alight in the abode of perdition? Hell, which they will enter, and what an evil resting place﴾ [Ibrahim: 28-29].

Abu al-'Aliyah said: "yatabaddal al-shiddah bi'l-rakha'" — he exchanges hardship for ease.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 109–110:

Allah, the Exalted, warns His believing servants against adopting the ways of the disbelievers among the People of the Book, and informs them of their enmity towards them, both inwardly and outwardly, and of the envy they harbour towards the believers, despite their knowledge of the believers' virtue and the virtue of their Prophet. He commands His believing servants to pardon, forgive and bear with them until Allah's command comes, in the form of victory and conquest. He also commands them to establish the prayer and give the zakah, and urges them towards this and encourages them to it, as Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Huyayy ibn Akhtab and Abu Yasir ibn Akhtab were among the most envious of the Jews towards the Arabs, since Allah had singled them out with His Messenger ﷺ, and the two of them strove as hard as they could to turn people away from Islam. So Allah revealed concerning them: ﴿Many of the People of the Book wish they could turn you back﴾ to the end of the verse.

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, concerning the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Many of the People of the Book wish﴾, he said: It is Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Shu'ayb narrated to us, from al-Zuhri: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik informed me, from his father, that Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, the Jew, was a poet, and he used to satirise the Prophet ﷺ. Concerning him (and in another version, "concerning them") Allah revealed: ﴿Many of the People of the Book wish they could turn you back﴾ up to His words: ﴿so pardon and overlook﴾.

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: that an unlettered Messenger would inform them of what was in their hands of the Books, the Messengers and the signs, and then would confirm all of that just as they confirmed it; but they denied it out of disbelief, envy and insolence. Therefore Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿out of envy from themselves, after the truth has become clear to them﴾, meaning: after the truth has shone forth for them. They did not lack any knowledge of it, but envy drove them to denial. So He reproached them, rebuked them and blamed them most severely, and He prescribed for His Prophet ﷺ and the believers what they are upon of affirmation, faith and acknowledgement of what was revealed to them and what was revealed before them, with His honour, great reward and help for them.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: ﴿from themselves﴾ means from their own side. Abu al-'Aliyah said: ﴿after the truth has become clear to them﴾ means after it had become clear to them that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, which they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel; yet they disbelieved in him out of envy and insolence, since he was from other than them. Qatadah, al-Rabi' and al-Suddi said likewise.

* *

As for His words: ﴿So pardon and overlook until Allah brings His command﴾, it is like His words, the Exalted: ﴿You will certainly hear much hurtful talk from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with Allah. But if you are patient and mindful of Allah, indeed that is of the matters requiring determination﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 186].

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿So pardon and overlook until Allah brings His command﴾: it was abrogated by His words: ﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ and His words: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day ... while they are humbled﴾ [al-Tawbah: 29]. So this abrogated His pardon of the polytheists. Likewise said Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Qatadah and al-Suddi: it is abrogated by the verse of the sword. This is also indicated by His words: ﴿until Allah brings His command﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri: 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that Usamah ibn Zayd informed him, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions used to pardon the polytheists and the People of the Book, as Allah had commanded them, and they would bear patiently with harm. Allah said: ﴿So pardon and overlook until Allah brings His command. Indeed Allah is over all things competent﴾. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would interpret the pardon in the manner Allah had commanded him, until Allah permitted him to fight against them, and Allah killed by his hand whoever he killed of the leading men of Quraysh.

[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/333).]

Its chain is sound, and I have not found it in any of the Six Books; but it has a basis in the two Sahihs from Usamah ibn Zayd, may Allah be pleased with them both.

* *

As for His words, the Exalted: ﴿And establish the prayer and give the zakah. And whatever good you put forward for yourselves, you will find it with Allah﴾, Allah, the Exalted, urges them to occupy themselves with what benefits them and whose outcome returns to them on the Day of Resurrection, namely establishing the prayer and giving the zakah, so that Allah will establish victory for them in the worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses stand: ﴿the Day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, and for them is the curse and for them is the evil home﴾ [Ghafir: 52]. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed Allah, of what you do, is Seeing﴾, meaning: He, the Exalted, is not unaware of the deed of any doer, and it is not lost before Him, whether it be good or evil, for He will surely recompense every doer for his deed.

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said concerning His words: ﴿Indeed Allah, of what you do, is Seeing﴾: this is information from Allah to those among the believers whom He addressed with these verses, that whatever they do of good or evil, openly or secretly, He is Seeing of it, nothing of it is hidden from Him, and He will reward them with good for good and with its like for evil. Although this statement comes in the form of information, it contains promise, warning, command and restraint. For He informed the people that He is Seeing of all their deeds, so that they would strive in His obedience, since that is stored up for them with Him until He rewards them for it, as He said: ﴿And whatever good you put forward for yourselves, you will find it with Allah﴾, and so that they would beware of disobeying Him.

He said: As for His words ﴿Basir﴾, it is from "mubsir" (one who sees), transformed into "basir", just as "mubdi'" was transformed into "badi'" and "mu'lim" into "alim" (painful). And Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Ibn Bukayr narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, who said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite in this verse ﴿Hearing, Seeing﴾, saying: "[He is] Seeing of everything."

[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/336).]

Abu al-'Aliyah said: ﴿after the truth has become clear to them﴾ means after it had become clear to them that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, which they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel; yet they disbelieved in him out of envy and insolence, since he was from other than them. Qatadah, al-Rabi' and al-Suddi said likewise.

* *

As for His words: ﴿So pardon and overlook until Allah brings His command﴾, it is like His words, the Exalted: ﴿You will certainly hear much hurtful talk from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with Allah. But if you are patient and mindful of Allah, indeed that is of the matters requiring determination﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 186].

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿So pardon and overlook until Allah brings His command﴾: it was abrogated by His words: ﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ and His words: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day ... while they are humbled﴾ [al-Tawbah: 29]. So this abrogated His pardon of the polytheists. Likewise said Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Qatadah and al-Suddi: it is abrogated by the verse of the sword. This is also indicated by His words: ﴿until Allah brings His command﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri: 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that Usamah ibn Zayd informed him, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions used to pardon the polytheists and the People of the Book, as Allah had commanded them, and they would bear patiently with harm. Allah said: ﴿So pardon and overlook until Allah brings His command. Indeed Allah is over all things competent﴾. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would interpret the pardon in the manner Allah had commanded him, until Allah permitted him to fight against them, and Allah killed by his hand whoever he killed of the leading men of Quraysh.

[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/333).]

Its chain is sound, and I have not found it in any of the Six Books; but it has a basis in the two Sahihs from Usamah ibn Zayd, may Allah be pleased with them both.

* *

As for His words, the Exalted: ﴿And establish the prayer and give the zakah. And whatever good you put forward for yourselves, you will find it with Allah﴾, Allah, the Exalted, urges them to occupy themselves with what benefits them and whose outcome returns to them on the Day of Resurrection, namely establishing the prayer and giving the zakah, so that Allah will establish victory for them in the worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses stand: ﴿the Day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, and for them is the curse and for them is the evil home﴾ [Ghafir: 52]. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed Allah, of what you do, is Seeing﴾, meaning: He, the Exalted, is not unaware of the deed of any doer, and it is not lost before Him, whether it be good or evil, for He will surely recompense every doer for his deed.

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said concerning His words: ﴿Indeed Allah, of what you do, is Seeing﴾: this is information from Allah to those among the believers whom He addressed with these verses, that whatever they do of good or evil, openly or secretly, He is Seeing of it, nothing of it is hidden from Him, and He will reward them with good for good and with its like for evil. Although this statement comes in the form of information, it contains promise, warning, command and restraint. For He informed the people that He is Seeing of all their deeds, so that they would strive in His obedience, since that is stored up for them with Him until He rewards them for it, as He said: ﴿And whatever good you put forward for yourselves, you will find it with Allah﴾, and so that they would beware of disobeying Him.

He said: As for His words ﴿Basir﴾, it is from "mubsir" (one who sees), transformed into "basir", just as "mubdi'" was transformed into "badi'" and "mu'lim" into "alim" (painful). And Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Ibn Bukayr narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, who said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite in this verse ﴿Hearing, Seeing﴾, saying: "[He is] Seeing of everything."

[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/336).]

Allah the Exalted shows the self-deception of the Jews and Christians in what they hold. Each group among the Jews and Christians claimed that no one would enter Paradise except those who followed its religion. Allah related in Surah al-Ma'idah that they said: ﴿We are the sons of Allah and His beloved﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 18]. Allah refuted them by informing them that He would punish them for their sins. Had they been as they claimed, the matter would not have been so. This is like their earlier claim that the Fire would touch them only for a number of counted days, after which they would move on to Paradise. Allah responded to them about that, and likewise He addressed this claim they made without proof, evidence, or clear demonstration, saying: ﴿Those are their wishful fancies﴾.

Abu al-'Aliyah said: "They are wishes they wished upon Allah without right." Qatadah and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said likewise.

Then He said: ﴿Say﴾, meaning: O Muhammad, ﴿Produce your proof﴾.

Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, al-Suddi and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "Your argument." Qatadah said: "Your evidence for that." ﴿If you are truthful﴾ in what you claim.

Then He said: ﴿Yes, whoever submits his face to Allah while being a doer of good﴾, meaning: whoever sincerely devotes his deed to Allah alone, with no partner, as He said: ﴿And if they argue with you, say: I have submitted my face to Allah, and so have those who follow me﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 20], and the rest of the verse.

Abu al-'Aliyah and al-Rabi' said: ﴿Yes, whoever submits his face to Allah﴾ means: whoever is sincere to Allah.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿Whoever submits﴾ means sincerely devotes himself; ﴿his face﴾ he said: his religion; ﴿and is a doer of good﴾ means: following the Messenger (ﷺ) in it. For a deed to be accepted there are two conditions: first, that it be sincerely for Allah alone; and second, that it be correct and in accordance with the Sharia (the revealed law). Whenever a deed is sincere but not correct, it is not accepted. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected." Muslim narrated it from the hadith of 'Aishah, from him (ﷺ), peace be upon him.

Thus the worship of the monks and those who resemble them, even if it is assumed that they are sincere in it to Allah, is not accepted from them, unless it follows the Messenger, Muhammad (ﷺ), who was sent to them and to all mankind, and who includes them and their like. Allah said: ﴿And We will turn to whatever deeds they did and make them as scattered dust﴾ [al-Furqan: 23]. And He said: ﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a desert, which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing﴾ [al-Nur: 39].

It is narrated from the Commander of the Faithful 'Umar that he interpreted this verse as referring to the monks, as will come.

As for a deed that conforms to the Sharia in its outward form, but whose doer did not sincerely intend it for Allah, it too is rejected upon its doer. This is the condition of the hypocrites and those who show off, as Allah said: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites deceive Allah, but He is the one who deceives them. And when they stand up for prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to the people and not remembering Allah except a little﴾ [al-Nisa': 142]. And He said: ﴿So woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer, who make a show, and withhold small kindnesses﴾ [al-Ma'un: 4–7]. For this reason Allah said: ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾ [al-Kahf: 110]. And He said in this noble verse: ﴿Yes, whoever submits his face to Allah while being a doer of good﴾.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then he will have his reward with his Lord, and no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve﴾, He, the Exalted, guaranteed them, upon that, the attainment of rewards, and gave them security from what they feared of harm. So ﴿no fear will be upon them﴾ regarding what lies ahead, and ﴿nor will they grieve﴾ over what has passed and they have left behind. As Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿No fear will be upon them﴾ means in the Hereafter, ﴿nor will they grieve﴾ means: [that is, they will not grieve] over death.

* *

As for His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿And the Jews say, "The Christians are not upon anything," and the Christians say, "The Jews are not upon anything," while they recite the Scripture﴾, by this He shows their contradiction, their mutual hatred, their hostility, and their obstinacy. As Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the people of Najran from the Christians came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the rabbis of the Jews came to them, and they disputed in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Rafi' ibn Hurayml [[in A: "Ibn Khuzaymah"]] said: "You are not upon anything," and he disbelieved in Jesus and the Gospel. A man from the people of Najran from the Christians said to the Jews: "You are not upon anything," and he denied the prophethood of Moses and disbelieved in the Torah. So Allah revealed concerning their two statements: ﴿And the Jews say, "The Christians are not upon anything," and the Christians say, "The Jews are not upon anything," while they recite the Scripture﴾. He said: Indeed each of them recites in its book the confirmation of the one who disbelieved in it. That is, the Jews disbelieve in Jesus while the Torah is in their possession, in which is what Allah took from them through the tongue of Moses regarding belief in Jesus; and in the Gospel is what Jesus brought, confirming Moses and what came in the Torah from Allah. Each disbelieves in what is in the hand [[in J, T, B: "in my hand"]] of the other.

Mujahid said, in explaining this verse: "The earliest Jews and Christians were indeed upon something."

Qatadah said: ﴿And the Jews say, "The Christians are not upon anything"﴾ — he said: "Yes, the earliest Christians were indeed upon something, but they innovated and split apart." ﴿And the Christians say, "The Jews are not upon anything"﴾ — he said: "Yes, the earliest Jews were indeed upon something, but they innovated and split apart."

There is another report from him, like the statement of Abu al-'Aliyah and al-Rabi' ibn Anas in explaining this verse: ﴿And the Jews say, "The Christians are not upon anything," and the Christians say, "The Jews are not upon anything"﴾: these are the People of the Book who were in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

This view implies that each of the two groups was truthful in what it charged against the other. However, the apparent context of the verse implies their blame for what they said, while knowing the contrary. For this reason He said: ﴿while they recite the Scripture﴾, meaning: while they know the Sharia of the Torah and the Gospel, each of which had been prescribed at a time. But they denied one another out of obstinacy and disbelief, and by answering corruption with corruption, as was mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah in the first report from him regarding its explanation. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Likewise said those who do not know, the like of their word﴾, by this He shows the ignorance of the Jews and Christians regarding what they said to one another, and this is by way of allusion and indication. There has been disagreement about whom He meant by His saying: ﴿those who do not know﴾.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas and Qatadah said: ﴿Likewise said those who do not know﴾ — they said: the Christians said the like of the Jews' word and their saying. Ibn Jurayj said: I asked 'Ata': "Who are those who do not know?" He said: "Nations that existed before the Jews and Christians, and before the Torah and the Gospel." Al-Suddi said: ﴿Likewise said those who do not know﴾ — they are the Arabs, who said: "Muhammad is not upon anything."

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir chose that it is general, applicable to all of them, and there is no decisive proof specifying any one of these views. So applying it to all is more appropriate. And Allah knows best.

* *
