Qatadah said: ﴿And the Jews say, "The Christians are not upon anything"﴾ — he said: "Yes, the earliest Christians were indeed upon something, but they innovated and split apart." ﴿And the Christians say, "The Jews are not upon anything"﴾ — he said: "Yes, the earliest Jews were indeed upon something, but they innovated and split apart."

There is another report from him, like the statement of Abu al-'Aliyah and al-Rabi' ibn Anas in explaining this verse: ﴿And the Jews say, "The Christians are not upon anything," and the Christians say, "The Jews are not upon anything"﴾: these are the People of the Book who were in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

This view implies that each of the two groups was truthful in what it charged against the other. However, the apparent context of the verse implies their blame for what they said, while knowing the contrary. For this reason He said: ﴿while they recite the Scripture﴾, meaning: while they know the Sharia of the Torah and the Gospel, each of which had been prescribed at a time. But they denied one another out of obstinacy and disbelief, and by answering corruption with corruption, as was mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah in the first report from him regarding its explanation. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Likewise said those who do not know, the like of their word﴾, by this He shows the ignorance of the Jews and Christians regarding what they said to one another, and this is by way of allusion and indication. There has been disagreement about whom He meant by His saying: ﴿those who do not know﴾.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas and Qatadah said: ﴿Likewise said those who do not know﴾ — they said: the Christians said the like of the Jews' word and their saying. Ibn Jurayj said: I asked 'Ata': "Who are those who do not know?" He said: "Nations that existed before the Jews and Christians, and before the Torah and the Gospel." Al-Suddi said: ﴿Likewise said those who do not know﴾ — they are the Arabs, who said: "Muhammad is not upon anything."

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir chose that it is general, applicable to all of them, and there is no decisive proof specifying any one of these views. So applying it to all is more appropriate. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ﴾, meaning: He, the Exalted, will gather them together on the Day of Return and will separate them by His just judgment, in which He does not oppress and does not wrong even the weight of an atom. This is like His saying in Surah al-Hajj: ﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Sabeans, and the Christians, and the Magians, and those who associated [others with Allah] — indeed, Allah will decide between them on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, Allah is Witness over all things﴾ [al-Hajj: 17], and as He said: ﴿Say: Our Lord will bring us together, then He will open between us with truth, and He is the Opener, the All-Knowing﴾ [Saba': 26].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 114:

The commentators differed concerning the meaning of "those who prevented the mosques of Allah [[In manuscript C: "the mosques of Allah from having His name mentioned in them".]] and strove for their ruin," and there are two opinions:

The first: what al-'Awfi narrated in his tafsir from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of Allah from having His name mentioned therein﴾, that he said: "They are the Christians." Mujahid also said: "They are the Christians, who used to throw filth into Bayt al-Maqdis and prevent people from praying in it."

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿and strove for their ruin﴾: "It is Bukhtansar (Nebuchadnezzar) and his companions, who ruined Bayt al-Maqdis, and the Christians helped him in that."

Sa'id said, from Qatadah: "Those are the enemies of Allah, the Christians. The hatred of the Jews led them to help Bukhtansar the Babylonian, the Magian, in the destruction of Bayt al-Maqdis."

As-Suddi said: "They backed Bukhtansar in the ruin of Bayt al-Maqdis until he destroyed it, and he commanded that carrion be thrown into it. The Romans only helped him in its ruin because the Children of Israel had killed Yahya ibn Zakariyya." A similar report is also narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri.

The second opinion: what Ibn Jarir narrated: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to me, from Ibn Wahb, who said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of Allah from having His name mentioned therein and strives for their ruin﴾: "These are the polytheists who stood between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and entering Makkah on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, until he slaughtered his sacrificial animal at Dhi Tuwa and made a truce with them. He said to them: 'No one has ever been prevented from this House; a man would meet the killer of his father or brother and would not be prevented.' They said: 'Whoever killed our fathers at Badr will not enter upon us while any of us remains.'"

And concerning His saying: ﴿and strove for their ruin﴾, he said: "By cutting off those who would maintain them with His remembrance and who come to them for Hajj and 'Umrah."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: it was mentioned from Salamah, who said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad related to me, from 'Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Quraysh prevented the Prophet (ﷺ) from praying at the Ka'bah in the Masjid al-Haram, so Allah revealed: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of Allah from having His name mentioned therein﴾.

Then Ibn Jarir preferred the first opinion, and argued that the Quraysh did not strive for the ruin of the Ka'bah, whereas the Romans did strive for the destruction of Bayt al-Maqdis.

I say: what appears to be correct, and Allah knows best, is the second opinion, as Ibn Zayd said, and it is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas. This is because when the Christians prevented the Jews from praying in Bayt al-Maqdis, it was as if their religion were more upright than the religion of the Jews, and they were closer to them. Remembrance of Allah from the Jews was not accepted at that time, because they had been cursed earlier on the tongue of Dawud and 'Isa ibn Maryam: "That is because they disobeyed and used to transgress" (cf. 5:78). Also, when He, the Exalted, directed blame at the Jews and Christians, He began to censure the polytheists who expelled the Messenger (ﷺ) and his companions from Makkah and prevented them from praying in al-Masjid al-Haram. As for his reliance on the claim that the Quraysh did not strive for the ruin of the Ka'bah, what ruin could be greater than what they did? They expelled the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions from it, and took possession of it with their idols, their rivals and their polytheism, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them while they bar [people] from al-Masjid al-Haram, and they are not its guardians? Its guardians are only the God-fearing, but most of them do not know﴾ [al-Anfal: 34]. And the Exalted said: ﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah, while they testify against themselves to disbelief. Those, their deeds have become worthless, and in the Fire they will abide eternally. * The mosques of Allah are only maintained by those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, establish prayer, give zakah, and do not fear except Allah. For it is expected that those will be among the guided﴾ [at-Tawbah: 17-18]. And the Exalted said: ﴿They are the ones who disbelieved and barred you from al-Masjid al-Haram and the sacrifice detained from reaching its place. And were it not for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, that you might trample them and there would befall you from them harm without knowledge [i.e., the sin of killing them], [Allah would have permitted you to fight them]. [But that was so] that Allah might admit into His mercy whom He wills. If they had been separated, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment﴾ [al-Fath: 25]. Then He said: ﴿The mosques of Allah are only maintained by those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, establish prayer, give zakah, and do not fear except Allah﴾ [at-Tawbah: 18]. So if such people are expelled from it and barred from it, what ruin of it could be greater than that? The meaning of its maintenance is not merely its decoration and the building of its structure. Rather, its maintenance is by remembering Allah within it, establishing His law within it, and purifying it from defilement and polytheism.

* *

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿It was not for them to enter them except in fear﴾, this is a statement whose meaning is a command, i.e., do not enable these people, when you have power over them, to enter it except under a truce and the payment of the jizyah. For this reason, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conquered Makkah, in the following year, in the ninth year [AH], he ordered that it be proclaimed in the courtyards of Mina: "No polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year, and no one shall circumambulate the House naked, and whoever has a treaty with him, his term extends to its duration." This was a confirmation and an implementation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year﴾ [at-Tawbah: 28]. Some of them said: it was not fitting for them to enter the mosques of Allah except in fear, in a state of awe and trembling of the limbs, lest the believers should seize them, let alone that they should take control of it and prevent the believers from it. The meaning is: what was right and obligatory was only this, were it not for the oppression of the disbelievers and others.

It was also said: this is glad tidings from Allah to the Muslims that He would give them victory over al-Masjid al-Haram and over all the mosques, and that He would humble the polytheists before them, so that none of them would enter al-Masjid al-Haram except in fear, fearing that he would be seized and punished or killed if he did not embrace Islam. Allah fulfilled this promise, as has already been mentioned, by preventing the polytheists from entering al-Masjid al-Haram, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) instructed that no two religions should remain in the Arabian Peninsula, and that the Jews and Christians be expelled from it. To Allah belong praise and grace. This was nothing but the honouring of the surroundings of al-Masjid al-Haram and the purification of the blessed ground in which Allah sent His Messenger to mankind, all of them, as a bearer of good news and a warner, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him. And this is the disgrace for them in this world, because the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. Just as they barred the believers from al-Masjid al-Haram, they were barred from it; and just as they expelled them from Makkah, they were expelled from it. ﴿And for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment﴾ for what they violated of the sanctity of the House, what they degraded of it by setting up idols around it, calling upon other than Allah at it, circumambulating it naked, and other of their deeds which Allah and His Messenger abhor.

As for the one who interpreted it as Bayt al-Maqdis, Ka'b al-Ahbar said: when the Christians prevailed over Bayt al-Maqdis, they ruined it. Then when Allah sent Muhammad (ﷺ), He revealed to him: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of Allah from having His name mentioned therein and strives for their ruin? Those, it was not for them to enter them except in fear﴾, and so there is no Christian on earth who enters Bayt al-Maqdis except in fear.

As-Suddi said: so there is no Roman on earth who enters it today except that he is fearful that his neck will be struck, or he is frightened by the payment of the jizyah, so he pays it.

Qatadah said: they do not enter the mosques except furtively.

I say: this does not negate that it falls within the general meaning of the verse. The Christians did not wrong Bayt al-Maqdis by desecrating the rock toward which the Jews used to pray; they were punished, by the Law and by decree, with humiliation in it, except at certain times of history when Bayt al-Maqdis was tested through them. Likewise, the Jews, since their disobedience to Allah in it was also greater than the disobedience of the Christians, their punishment was greater. And Allah knows best.

These scholars interpreted "disgrace in this world" as the emergence of the Mahdi, according to As-Suddi, 'Ikrimah and Wa'il ibn Dawud. Qatadah interpreted it as paying the jizyah "out of hand while they are humbled" [9:29].

The correct view is that disgrace in this world is more general than all of that, and a hadith has come concerning seeking refuge from the disgrace of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter, as Imam Ahmad said: al-Haytham ibn Kharijah related to us, Muhammad ibn Ayyub ibn Maysarah ibn Halbas related to us: I heard my father narrate from Bus ibn Artah, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to supplicate: "O Allah, make the outcome of our affairs good in all matters, and protect us from the disgrace of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter" [al-Musnad 4/181].

This is a hasan hadith, and it is not in any of the Six Books, and his companion, Bus ibn Artah, who is said also to be Ibn Abi Artah, has no other narration except "Hands are not cut off on campaign" [and the one that is mentioned].

This, and Allah knows best, contains consolation for the Messenger (ﷺ) and his companions who were expelled from Makkah and left their mosque and place of prayer. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pray in Makkah facing Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), with the Ka'bah in front of him. When he came to Madinah, he was directed to face Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen or seventeen months, and then Allah turned him afterward toward the Ka'bah. For this reason Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west; wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾.

Abu 'Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam said in his book *al-Nasikh wa'l-Mansukh* (On Abrogating and Abrogated Verses; *naskh* means abrogation, the lifting of a earlier ruling by a later one): Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj and Uthman ibn 'Ata' narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The first thing abrogated from the Qur'an, so far as we have been told, and Allah knows best, was the matter of the qiblah (direction of prayer). Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west; wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) faced toward Bayt al-Maqdis and prayed toward it, and left the Ancient House (the Ka'bah). Then He turned him to His Ancient House and abrogated the earlier ruling, saying: ﴿And from wherever you go out, turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque; and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it﴾."
[[Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in his *Tafsir* (1/346) by way of Hajjaj ibn Muhammad. al-Hakim narrated it in *al-Mustadrak* (2/267) by way of Ibn Jurayj from 'Ata' with it, and said: "This is a sound hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not include it in this form."]]

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The first thing abrogated from the Qur'an was the qiblah." That was because when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) migrated to Madinah, and its inhabitants were Jews, Allah commanded him to face Bayt al-Maqdis. The Jews rejoiced, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) faced it for some ten-odd months. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) loved the qiblah of Abraham, so he would supplicate and look up toward the sky. Then Allah revealed: ﴿We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the sky; so We will surely turn you to a qiblah that you will like﴾ [the verse continues] up to His words: ﴿So turn your faces toward it﴾. The Jews doubted this and said: "What has turned them away from their qiblah which they were upon?" Then Allah revealed: ﴿Say: To Allah belong the east and the west; He guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾, and He said: ﴿Wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾.

'Ikrimah said, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿Wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾: "It means the qiblah of Allah, wherever you face, east or west." Mujahid said concerning ﴿Wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾: "It means the qiblah of Allah. Wherever you are, you have a qiblah that you face: the Ka'bah."

Ibn Abi Hatim, after narrating the earlier report from Ibn 'Abbas about the abrogation of the qiblah, from 'Ata', from him, said: "It has also been related from Abu'l-'Aliyah, al-Hasan, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, 'Ikrimah, Qatadah, al-Suddi and Zayd ibn Aslam, something similar to that."

Ibn Jarir said: "Others said: Rather, Allah revealed this verse before He made facing the Ka'bah obligatory. Allah, exalted is He, revealed it only to inform His Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions that they may direct their faces for prayer wherever they wish, from the directions of east and west, because whichever direction and side they turn their faces toward, He, exalted is His praise, is in that direction and that side; for to Him belong the easts and the wests, and no place is empty of Him, as He said: ﴿Nor is there a lesser number than that or greater except that He is with them wherever they are﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 7]." They said: "Then this was abrogated by the obligation He imposed upon them to face the Sacred Mosque."

I say: As for his statement, "no place is empty of Him": if he means His knowledge, exalted is He, then it is correct, for His knowledge encompasses all things known. But as for His Essence, exalted is He, it is not confined to anything of His creation; exalted is Allah far above that, a great exaltation.

Ibn Jarir said: "Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, as a permission from Allah that one may offer voluntary prayer wherever one faces, east or west, while traveling on a journey, and in a state of fighting and extreme fear."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ibn Idris narrated to us, 'Abd al-Malik, that is Ibn Abi Sulayman, narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Umar: that he used to pray wherever his mount turned him. He mentioned that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to do this, and interpreted this verse: ﴿Wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾.
[[Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through various chains from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman with it. (Tafsir al-Tabari 2/530; Sahih Muslim no. 700; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2958; Sunan al-Nasa'i 1/244; Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim 1/344.) Its origin is in the two Sahihs (of al-Bukhari and Muslim), from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar and 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah, without mention of the verse.]]

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar: that when he was asked about the prayer of fear, he described it. Then he said: "If the fear is more intense than that, pray standing on foot, or riding, facing the qiblah or not facing it."
Nafi' said: "I do not think Ibn 'Umar mentioned that except from the Prophet (ﷺ)."
[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4535.]]

Issue: Al-Shafi'i, in the well-known position attributed to him, did not distinguish between a journey of distance and a journey of enemy-fighting; so, according to him in all cases, voluntary prayer on the mount is permitted. This is also the view of Abu Hanifah, in contrast to Malik and his companions. Abu Yusuf and Abu Sa'id al-Istakhri chose voluntary prayer on a mount within a city. Abu Yusuf related this from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, and Abu Ja'far al-Tabari chose it, even for one walking.

Ibn Jarir said: "Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed concerning a people for whom the qiblah was obscured, so they did not know its direction, and they prayed in various directions. Then Allah said to them: ﴿To Me belong the easts and the wests; wherever you turn your faces, there is My Face, and it is your qiblah﴾, informing them by this that their prayer is valid."

Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi narrated to us, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, Abu'l-Rabi' al-Sammán narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn 'Ubayd Allah, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah, from his father, who said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a pitch-black dark night, and we stopped at a place. A man would take stones and make a mosque to pray in. When we awoke in the morning, we found that we had prayed without facing the qiblah. We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we prayed all this night not facing the qiblah!' Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west; wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah; indeed Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾ — the verse."
Then he narrated it from Sufyan ibn Waki', from his father, from Abu'l-Rabi' al-Sammán, with something similar.
[[Tafsir al-Tabari 2/531, 532.]]

al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Mahmud ibn Ghaylan, from Waki'. And Ibn Majah narrated it from Yahya ibn Hakim, from Abu Dawud, from Abu'l-Rabi' al-Sammán.
[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 345; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 1020.]]

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah, from Sa'id [in another copy: "Sa'd"] ibn Sulayman, from Abu'l-Rabi' al-Sammán — whose name is Ash'ath ibn Sa'id al-Basri — and he is weak in hadith.
[[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim 1/344.]]

al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan hadith. Its chain is not strong, and we only know it from the hadith of Ash'ath al-Sammán, and Ash'ath is considered weak in hadith."
I say: His teacher 'Asim is also weak.
al-Bukhari said: "Munkar al-hadith (of rejected narrations)." Ibn Ma'in said: "Weak, not to be used as evidence." Ibn Hibban said: "Matruk (abandoned)." And Allah knows best.

It has also been narrated through other chains, from Jabir.

The Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said in his *Tafsir* of this verse: Isma'il ibn 'Ali ibn Isma'il narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Shabib narrated to us, Ahmad ibn 'Ubayd Allah [in another copy: "Abd Allah"] ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: "I found in my father's book: 'Abd al-Malik al-'Arzami narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent out a detachment in which I was, and darkness overtook us, and we did not recognize the qiblah. A group among us said: 'We have recognized the qiblah; it is here, toward the north star (or: the north).' They prayed and drew lines. When they awoke and the sun rose, those lines were facing other than the qiblah. When we returned from our journey, we asked the Prophet (ﷺ), and he remained silent, and Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west; wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾."
Then he narrated it through Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-'Arzami, from 'Ata', from Jabir, with it.
[[al-Daraqutni narrated it in *al-Sunan* (1/271) by way of Isma'il ibn 'Ali from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Shabib with it. al-Bayhaqi narrated it in *al-Sunan al-Kubra* (2/12) by way of Muhammad ibn al-Harith from Ahmad ibn 'Ubayd Allah, who said: "I found in my father's book," and he mentioned something similar. He also narrated it (2/10) by way of Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Wasiti, from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-'Arzami, from 'Ata', with it.]]

al-Daraqutni said: "It was read to 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, while I was listening: Dawud ibn 'Amr narrated to you: Muhammad ibn Yazid [in another copy: "ibn Zayd"] al-Wasiti narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from 'Ata', from Jabir, who said: 'We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a journey, and a cloud overtook us, and we became confused, and we disagreed about the qiblah. Each one of us prayed separately, and one of us began drawing lines before himself so we would know our positions. We mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he did not order us to repeat (the prayer), and he said: "Your prayer is sufficient."'"
Then al-Daraqutni said: "So he said: from Muhammad ibn Salim. Another said: from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-'Arzami, from 'Ata'. And both of them are weak."
[[Sunan al-Daraqutni (1/271). al-Hakim narrated it in *al-Mustadrak* (1/206) by way of Dawud ibn 'Amr with it, and said: "This is a sound hadith; all its narrators are trustworthy except Muhammad ibn Salim, for I do not know him to have either integrity or fault." al-Dhahabi said: "I say: he is Abu Sahl, a weak narrator (wahin)."]]

Then Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it from the hadith of al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent out a detachment, and a haze overtook them, so they did not find the qiblah, and they prayed facing other than the qiblah. Then it became clear to them after the sunrise that they had prayed facing other than the qiblah. When they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him, Allah, exalted and mighty is He, revealed this verse: ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west; wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾.

These chains contain weakness, and perhaps some of them strengthen one another. As for repeating the prayer for one who has become aware of his error, there are two opinions among the scholars, and these reports are evidence for the view that there is no obligation to repeat it (qada'). And Allah knows best.

Ibn Jarir said: Others said: rather, this verse was revealed concerning the case of the Negus (al-Najashi), as Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us: Hisham ibn Mu'adh related to us, from my father, from Qatadah, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed, a brother of yours has died, so pray over him." They said: "Shall we pray over a man who is not a Muslim?" He said: Then the following was revealed: ﴿And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah and what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them, humbly submissive to Allah﴾ [Al 'Imran: 199]. Qatadah said: They said: "Indeed, he did not used to pray facing the qiblah." So Allah revealed: ﴿And to Allah belong the east and the west; so wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾ [[Tafsir al-Tabari (2/532).]].

This is strange, and Allah knows best.

It has also been said that he used to pray towards Bayt al-Maqdis before the abrogating ruling (al-nasikh) reached him, directing prayer to the Ka'bah, as al-Qurtubi related it from Qatadah. Al-Qurtubi also mentioned that when he died, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over him, and those who held the view of praying over an absent person (salat al-ghA'ib) took this as evidence. He said: This is specific according to our companions (the Malikis) for three reasons. The first: that he ﷺ witnessed him when he prayed over him, the earth was folded up for him. The second: that when there was no one with him to pray over him, he prayed over him, and Ibn al-'Arabi preferred this view. Al-Qurtubi said: It is unlikely that a Muslim king would have no one among his people who shared his religion; Ibn al-'Arabi answered this, saying: Perhaps they did not have the legislated practice of praying over the deceased. This is a good answer. The third: that the prayer and peace of Allah be upon him prayed over him only so that this would serve as a means of winning over the rest of the kings. And Allah knows best.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh cited in the tafsir of this verse a hadith from Abu Ma'shar, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Alqamah, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Between the east and the west is a qiblah for the people of Madinah, the people of Syria and the people of Iraq."

This has a relevance here. It was also related by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah from the hadith of Abu Ma'shar, whose name is Najih ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sindi al-Madani, with the wording: "Between the east and the west is a qiblah."

Al-Tirmidhi said: It has been related through more than one route from Abu Hurayrah. Some scholars spoke about Abu Ma'shar because of his memory. Then al-Tirmidhi said: al-Hasan ibn [Abi] Bakr al-Marwazi related to me, Al-Mu'alla ibn Mansur related to us, 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Makhzumi related to us, from 'Uthman ibn Muhammad al-Akhnasi, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Between the east and the west is a qiblah."

Then al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan sahih hadith.

He related from al-Bukhari that he said: This is stronger than the hadith of Abu Ma'shar and more authentic. Al-Tirmidhi said: It has been related from more than one of the Companions: "Between the east and the west is a qiblah," among them 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, 'Ali, and Ibn 'Abbas.

Ibn 'Umar said: If you place the west on your right and the east on your left, then what lies between them is a qiblah, when the qiblah is faced.

Then Ibn Mardawayh said: 'Ali ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, Ya'qub ibn Yunus, client of the Banu Hashim, related to us, Shu'ayb ibn Ayyub related to us, Ibn Numayr related to us, from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Between the east and the west is a qiblah."

al-Daraqutni and al-Bayhaqi also related it [[Sunan al-Daraqutni (1/270) and Sunan al-Bayhaqi (2/9), and it is mu'all (defective) and the correct version is that it is mawquf. Ibn Abi Hatim said in al-'Ilal (1/184): "Abu Zur'ah was asked about a hadith related by Yazid ibn Harun, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ: 'Between the east and the west is a qiblah.' Abu Zur'ah said: 'This is an error; the hadith is the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, mawquf.'"]]. The well-known version is from Ibn 'Umar, from 'Umar, as his statement.

Ibn Jarir said: It is also possible that the meaning is: wherever you turn your faces in your supplication to Me, there is My Face, and I will respond to your supplication, as al-Qasim related to us, al-Husayn related to us, Hajjaj related to me, who said: Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: When the verse ﴿Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾ [Ghafir: 60] was revealed, they said: "To where?" Then the following was revealed: ﴿So wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾.

Ibn Jarir said: His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾ means that He encompasses all His creation with sufficiency, bounty and generosity. As for His saying ﴿All-Knowing﴾, it means: He knows their deeds, nothing of them escapes Him, and nothing is hidden from His knowledge; rather, He knows all of them.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 116–117:

This noble verse and the one following it contain a refutation of the Christians—may the curses of Allah be upon them—as well as those who resemble them among the Jews and the idolaters of the Arabs, who made the angels the daughters of Allah. Allah refuted all of them in their claim and their saying that Allah has a son. So the Exalted said: ﴿Glory be to Him﴾, meaning: He is exalted, sanctified and far removed from that, high above it by a great elevation. ﴿Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning: the matter is not as they have fabricated. Rather, to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He is the one who disposes of them, the one who created them, provides for them, decrees for them, subjects them, drives them and directs them as He wills. All of them are servants of Him and His possession. How, then, could He have a son from among them? A son is only born from two compatible things, whereas He, blessed and exalted, has no equal, no partner in His greatness and His majesty, and no consort. So how could He have a son! As the Exalted said: ﴿The Originator of the heavens and the earth—how could He have a son when there is not for Him a companion? And He created all things, and He is, of all things, Knowing﴾ [al-An'am: 101]. And the Exalted said: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." You have certainly produced something horrendous. The heavens are almost rent therefrom, the earth split open, and the mountains collapse in devastation, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son. And it is not appropriate for the Most Merciful to take a son. There is no one in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant. He has enumerated them and counted them with [exact] counting. And all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection, alone﴾ [Maryam: 88–95]. And the Exalted said: ﴿Say, "He is Allah, [who is] One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, nor is there to Him any equivalent."﴾ [Surat al-Ikhlas].

In these noble verses the Exalted establishes that He is the Great Lord, having no peer and no likeness, and that all other things are created and nurtured by Him. So how could He have a son from among them! For this reason al-Bukhari said in his commentary on this verse from al-Baqarah: Abu al-Yaman informed us, Shu'ayb informed us, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Husayn, Nafi' ibn Jubayr—he is Ibn Mut'im—narrated to us, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Allah the Exalted said: The son of Adam denies Me, and it is not for him to do so; and he reviles Me, and it is not for him to do so. As for his denying Me, he claims that I cannot recreate him as he was. And as for his reviling Me, he says: 'Allah has a son.' Glory be to Me—that I should take a consort or a son!"

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it through this route [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4482].

Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Kamil narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Tirmidhi narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Muhammad al-Farwi narrated to us, Malik narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: The son of Adam denies Me, and it is not fitting for him to deny Me; and he reviles Me, and it is not fitting for him to revile Me. As for his denying Me, it is his saying: 'He will not recreate me as He originated me.' And the first creation is no easier for Me than its recreation. As for his reviling Me, it is his saying: 'Allah has taken a son.' And I am Allah, the One, the Eternal Refuge; I neither begot nor was I begotten, and there is none equal to Me."

[The hadith is narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 4974, through the route of Shu'ayb from Abu al-Zinad with the same meaning, where it reads: "and there is none equal to Me."]

In Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, it is related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "No one is more patient over a harm he hears than Allah; they ascribe to Him a son, yet He provides for them and grants them well-being" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6099, and Sahih Muslim, no. 2804, from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿All to Him are devoutly obedient﴾, Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj informed us, Asbat narrated to us, from Mutarrif, from Atiyyah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: ﴿Qanitin﴾ means "praying."

Ikrimah and Abu Malik said: ﴿All to Him are devoutly obedient﴾ means "acknowledging to Him servitude." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿All to Him are devoutly obedient﴾ means "sincerity." Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: it means "all standing before Him on the Day of Resurrection." Al-Suddi said: ﴿All to Him are devoutly obedient﴾ means "obedient to Him on the Day of Resurrection."

Khasif, from Mujahid, said: ﴿All to Him are devoutly obedient﴾ — he said: "obedient. Be a human, and he becomes one; say, 'Be a donkey,' and he becomes one."

Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, said: ﴿All to Him are devoutly obedient﴾ means "obedient"; he said: "The obedience of the disbeliever is in the prostration of his shadow while he is unwilling."

This statement from Mujahid—and it is the choice of Ibn Jarir—gathers all the sayings, namely that qunut is obedience and submission to Allah, and this is both legislated and predestined, as the Exalted said: ﴿And to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and so do their shadows in the mornings and the evenings﴾ [al-Ra'd: 15].

There is a hadith that explains what is meant by qunut in the Quran, as Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Amr ibn al-Harith informed me that Darraj Abu al-Samh narrated to him, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Every letter of the Quran in which qunut is mentioned means obedience."

Similarly, Imam Ahmad related it from Hasan ibn Musa, from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Darraj with its chain, like it.

However, this chain is weak and cannot be relied upon, and the marfu' attribution of this hadith is munkar; it may be from the words of a Companion or of the one who recorded it, and Allah knows best. Many tafsirs come with this chain containing objectionable material, so they should not be relied upon, for the chain is weak, and Allah knows best.

* *

As for the Exalted's saying: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, it means: their Creator without a precedent model. Mujahid and al-Suddi said: this is what the language requires, and from it one says of a newly-made thing: bid'ah (innovation). As is related in Sahih Muslim: "For every newly-introduced matter is an innovation, and every innovation is misguidance" [and every innovation is misguidance] [addition from the Tabaqat edition]. Innovation is of two kinds: sometimes it is a legal innovation (bid'ah shar'iyyah), as in his saying: "every newly-introduced matter is an innovation, and every innovation is misguidance"; and sometimes it is a linguistic innovation (bid'ah lughawiyyah), as in the saying of the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning his gathering of people for the prayer of tarawih and their continuing with it: "What an excellent innovation this is!"

Ibn Jarir said: "Originator of the heavens and the earth" means: the one who originated them. It is in the form mufil, changed to the form fa'il, just as mu'lim becomes alim and musmi' becomes sami'. The meaning of the mubdi' (originator) is: the one who brings into existence and creates what no one before him has brought into existence or created the like of.

He said: For this reason, one who innovates in religion is called mubtadi' (innovator), because he introduces into it what no one else has preceded him in. Likewise, every one who introduces an action or a saying in which no predecessor has preceded him is called mubtadi' by the Arabs. From this is the saying of A'sha Tha'labah, praising Hawdhah ibn Ali al-Hanafi:

He is guided by the words of the chiefs of men when they show him resolve, or he innovates whatever he wishes.

That is: he creates whatever he wishes.

Ibn Jarir said: The meaning of the statement is: "Glory be to Allah! How could Allah have a son, when He owns whatever is in the heavens and the earth, all of which bear witness to Him through their indication of His oneness, and acknowledge Him with obedience; He is their Creator, their Originator and their Bringer into existence, without any origin or model that He followed." This is a notification from Allah to His servants that among those who bear witness to this is al-Masih, whom they ascribed to Allah as a son; and it is also an information from Him to them that the One who originated the heavens and the earth without origin and without model is the One who originated al-Masih, 'Isa, without a father, by His power.

This, from Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, is a fine statement and a correct expression.

* *

As for the Exalted's saying: ﴿And when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is﴾, by this the Exalted shows the perfection of His power and the magnitude of His authority, and that when He decrees a matter and wills its existence, He only says to it: "Be." That is, one time, and it is, that is, it comes into being according to what He willed, as the Exalted said: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin: 82]. And the Exalted said: ﴿Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [al-Nahl: 40]. And the Exalted said: ﴿And Our command is but one, like a glance of the eye﴾ [al-Qamar: 50]. And the poet said:

When Allah wills a matter, it is only that He says to it, "Be," one utterance, and it is...

By this the Exalted also draws attention to the fact that the creation of 'Isa was by the word "Be," and so it was as Allah commanded. The Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of 'Isa to Allah is like that of Adam; He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he was﴾ [Al 'Imran: 59].

So Allah revealed concerning that, in His words: ﴿And those who do not know say: "Why does Allah not speak to us, or a sign come to us?"﴾

Mujahid said, regarding His words ﴿And those who do not know say: "Why does Allah not speak to us, or a sign come to us?"﴾: "The Christians say it."

This is the view chosen by Ibn Jarir, who said: "Because the context concerns them." But there is room for consideration in this.

[Al-Qurtubi related ﴿Why does Allah not speak to us?﴾ to mean: "Why does He not address us with your prophethood, O Muhammad?" I say: the apparent context is more general, and Allah knows best.]

Abu al-Aliyah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Qatadah and al-Suddi, in explaining this verse, said: this is the statement of the disbelievers of the Arabs. ﴿Likewise said those before them, saying the same as their words﴾ — they said: they are the Jews and the Christians. This view is supported, and the ones making this statement are the polytheists of the Arabs, by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when a sign comes to them, they say: "We will never believe until we are given the like of what was given to the messengers of Allah." Allah knows best where to place His message. Those who committed crimes will be struck with humiliation before Allah and a severe punishment for what they used to scheme.﴾ [al-An'am: 124]

* *

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say: "We will never believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth, or you have a garden of palm trees and grapes and make rivers gush forth within it abundantly, or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces as you claimed, or you bring Allah and the angels before us as a guarantee, or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky. And we will not believe in your ascending until you bring down to us a book we can read." Say: "Glory be to my Lord! Am I but a human messenger?"﴾ [al-Isra': 90-93], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who do not expect to meet Us say: "Why have angels not been sent down to us, or why do we not see our Lord?" They have become arrogant within themselves and have transgressed with great insolence.﴾ [al-Furqan: 21], and His saying: ﴿Rather, each one of them wishes to be given scrolls spread out.﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 52], and other verses indicating the disbelief, insolence, obstinacy and demands of the polytheists of the Arabs, for which they have no need; it is only disbelief and opposition, just as those before them among the past nations of the People of the Two Books and others said. As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a book from heaven. But they had asked Moses for something greater than that, when they said: "Show us Allah plainly."﴾ [an-Nisa': 153], and He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And when you said: "O Moses, we will never believe you until we see Allah plainly."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 55].

* *

And His saying: ﴿Their hearts are alike.﴾ That is: the hearts of the polytheists of the Arabs resembled the hearts of those who preceded them in disbelief, obstinacy and insolence, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Likewise, no messenger came to those before them but they said: "A sorcerer or a madman!" Did they bequeath this saying to one another? Rather, they are a transgressing people.﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 52-53]

* *

And His saying: ﴿We have certainly made the signs clear for a people who are certain.﴾ That is: We have made clear the proofs of the truthfulness of the messengers, in a manner that requires no further question or additional demand, for whoever is certain, affirms, follows the messengers, and understands what they brought from Allah, blessed and exalted is He. As for the one upon whose heart Allah has set a seal and upon whose sight He has placed a covering, those are the ones about whom Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, those against whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe, even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment.﴾ [Yunus: 96-97]

[His saying, exalted is He]

قَالَ ابْنُ أَبِي حَاتِمٍ: حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ صَالِحٍ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ الْفَزَارِيُّ عَنْ شَيْبَانَ النَّحْوِيِّ، أَخْبَرَنِي قَتَادَةُ، عَنْ عِكْرِمَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ قَالَ: "أُنْزِلَتْ عَلِيَّ: ﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ بِالْحَقِّ بَشِيرًا وَنَذِيرًا﴾ قَالَ: 'بَشِيرًا بِالْجَنَّةِ، وَنَذِيرًا مِنَ النَّارِ'" [Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/354).]

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿وَلا تُسْأَلُ عَنْ أَصْحَابِ الْجَحِيمِ﴾. قِرَاءَةُ أَكْثَرِهِمْ [In B, A and W: "qira'at ba'dihim" (the recitation of some of them).] ﴿وَلا تُسْأَلُ﴾ بِضَمِّ التَّاءِ عَلَى الْخَبَرِ. وَفِي قِرَاءَةِ أُبَيِّ بْنِ كَعْبٍ: "وَمَا تُسْأَلُ"، وَفِي قِرَاءَةِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ: "وَلَنْ تسأل عن أصحاب الجحيم". نَقَلَهُمَا [In B and T: "naqalahuma" (both were transmitted by).] ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ، أَيْ: لَا نَسْأَلُكَ عَنْ كُفْرِ مَنْ كَفَرَ بِكَ. ﴿فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ الْبَلاغُ وَعَلَيْنَا الْحِسَابُ﴾ [al-Ra'd: 40]. وَكَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿فَذَكِّرْ إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ مُذَكِّرٌ * لَسْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِمُصَيْطِرٍ﴾ الْآيَةَ [al-Ghashiyah: 21-22]. وَكَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ وَمَا أَنْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِجَبَّارٍ فَذَكِّرْ بِالْقُرْآنِ مَنْ يَخَافُ وَعِيدِ﴾ [Qaf: 45]. وَأَشْبَاهُ ذَلِكَ مِنَ الْآيَاتِ.

وَقَرَأَ آخَرُونَ [In A: "wa-qara'a al-Basriyyun" (and the people of Basra recited).] ﴿وَلَا تَسْأَلْ عَنْ أَصْحَابِ الْجَحِيمِ﴾ بِفَتْحِ التَّاءِ عَلَى النَّهْيِ، أَيْ: لَا تَسْأَلْ عَنْ حَالِهِمْ، كَمَا قَالَ عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ:

أَخْبَرَنَا الثَّوْرِيُّ، عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ عُبَيْدَةَ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ كَعْبٍ الْقُرَظِيِّ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: "لَيْتَ شِعْرِي مَا فَعَلَ أَبَوَايَ، لَيْتَ شِعْرِي مَا فَعَلَ أَبَوَايَ، لَيْتَ شِعْرِي مَا فَعَلَ أَبَوَايَ؟". فَنَزَلَتْ: ﴿وَلا تُسْأَلُ عَنْ أَصْحَابِ الْجَحِيمِ﴾، فَمَا ذَكَرَهُمَا [In A: "fa-ma dhakarahu" (he did not mention him).] حَتَّى تَوَفَّاهُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ.

وَرَوَاهُ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ، عَنْ أَبِي كُرَيْبٍ، عَنْ وَكِيعٍ، عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ عُبَيْدَةَ، [وَقَدْ تَكَلَّمُوا فِيهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ كَعْبٍ] [Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq (2/78) and Tafsir al-Tabari (2/558). Musa ibn Ubayda is very weak.] بِمِثْلِهِ. وَقَدْ حَكَاهُ الْقُرْطُبِيُّ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ وَمُحَمَّدِ بْنِ كَعْبٍ. قَالَ الْقُرْطُبِيُّ: وَهَذَا كَمَا يُقَالُ: لَا تُسْأَلُ عَنْ فُلَانٍ، أَيْ: قَدْ بَلَغَ فَوْقَ مَا تَحْسَبُ. وَقَدْ ذَكَرْنَا فِي التَّذْكِرَةِ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَحْيَا لَهُ أَبَوَيْهِ حَتَّى آمَنَا، وَأَجَبْنَا عَنْ قَوْلِهِ: "إِنَّ أَبِي وَأَبَاكَ فِي النَّارِ". (قُلْتُ): وَالْحَدِيثُ الْمَرْوِيُّ فِي حَيَاةِ أَبَوَيْهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ لَيْسَ فِي شَيْءٍ مِنَ الْكُتُبِ السِّتَّةِ وَلَا غَيْرِهَا، وَإِسْنَادُهُ ضَعِيفٌ. وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.

ثُمَّ قَالَ [ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ]: وَحَدَّثَنِي الْقَاسِمُ، حَدَّثَنَا الْحُسَيْنُ، حَدَّثَنِي حَجَّاجٌ، عَنِ ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ، أَخْبَرَنِي دَاوُدُ بْنُ أَبِي عَاصِمٍ: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ قَالَ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ: "أَيْنَ أَبَوَايَ؟". فَنَزَلَتْ: ﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ بِالْحَقِّ بَشِيرًا وَنَذِيرًا وَلا تُسْأَلُ عَنْ أَصْحَابِ الْجَحِيمِ﴾ [Tafsir al-Tabari (2/559).]

وَهَذَا مُرْسَلٌ كَالَّذِي قَبْلَهُ. وَقَدْ رَدَّ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ هَذَا الْقَوْلَ الْمَرْوِيَّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ كَعْبٍ [الْقُرَظِيِّ] وَغَيْرِهِ فِي ذَلِكَ، لِاسْتِحَالَةِ الشَّكِّ مِنَ الرَّسُولِ ﷺ فِي أَمْرِ أَبَوَيْهِ، وَاخْتَارَ الْقِرَاءَةَ الْأُولَى. وَهَذَا الَّذِي سَلَكَهُ هَاهُنَا فِيهِ نَظَرٌ، لِاحْتِمَالِ أَنَّ هَذَا كَانَ فِي حَالِ اسْتِغْفَارِهِ لِأَبَوَيْهِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَعْلَمَ أَمْرَهُمَا، فَلَمَّا عَلِمَ ذَلِكَ تَبَرَّأَ مِنْهُمَا، وَأَخْبَرَ عَنْهُمَا أَنَّهُمَا مِنْ أَهْلِ النَّارِ [كَمَا ثَبَتَ ذَلِكَ فِي الصَّحِيحِ]. وَلِهَذَا أَشْبَاهٌ كَثِيرَةٌ وَنَظَائِرُ، وَلَا يَلْزَمُ مَا ذَكَرَهُ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ. وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.

وَقَالَ الْإِمَامُ أَحْمَدُ: حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى بْنُ دَاوُدَ، حَدَّثَنَا فُلَيْحُ بْنُ سُلَيْمَانَ، عَنْ هِلَالِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ، عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ، قَالَ: لَقِيتُ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِ، فَقُلْتُ: أَخْبِرْنِي عَنْ صِفَةِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ فِي التَّوْرَاةِ. فَقَالَ: أَجَلْ، وَاللَّهِ إِنَّهُ لَمَوْصُوفٌ فِي التَّوْرَاةِ بِصِفَتِهِ فِي الْقُرْآنِ: "يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ شَاهِدًا وَمُبَشِّرًا وَنَذِيرًا، وَحِرْزًا لِلْأُمِّيِّينَ، وَأَنْتَ عَبْدِي وَرَسُولِي، سَمَّيْتُكَ الْمُتَوَكِّلَ، لَا فَظٌّ وَلَا غَلِيظٌ وَلَا سَخَّابٌ فِي الْأَسْوَاقِ، وَلَا يَدْفَعُ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ السَّيِّئَةَ، وَلَكِنْ يَعْفُو وَيَغْفِرُ، وَلَنْ يَقْبِضَهُ حَتَّى يُقِيمَ بِهِ الْمِلَّةَ الْعَوْجَاءَ، بِأَنْ يَقُولُوا: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، فَيَفْتَحَ بِهِ أَعْيُنًا عُمْيًا، وَآذَانًا صُمًّا، وَقُلُوبًا غُلْفًا".

انْفَرَدَ بِإِخْرَاجِهِ الْبُخَارِيُّ، فَرَوَاهُ فِي الْبُيُوعِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ، عَنْ فُلَيْحٍ، بِهِ [Musnad Ahmad (2/174) and Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2125.]. وَقَالَ: تَابَعَهُ عَبْدُ الْعَزِيزِ بْنُ أَبِي سَلَمَةَ، عَنْ هِلَالٍ. وَقَالَ سَعِيدٌ: عَنْ هِلَالٍ، عَنْ عَطَاءٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ سَلَامٍ. وَرَوَاهُ فِي التَّفْسِيرِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْعَزِيزِ بْنِ أَبِي سَلَمَةَ، عَنْ هِلَالٍ، عَنْ عَطَاءٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِ، بِهِ [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4838.]، فَذَكَرَ نَحْوَهُ. فَعَبْدُ اللَّهِ هَذَا هُوَ ابْنُ صَالِحٍ، كَمَا صَرَّحَ بِهِ فِي كِتَابِ الْأَدَبِ. وَزَعَمَ أَبُو مَسْعُودٍ الدِّمَشْقِيُّ أَنَّهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ رَجَاءٍ.

وَقَدْ رَوَاهُ الْحَافِظُ أَبُو بَكْرِ بْنُ مَرْدَوَيْهِ فِي تَفْسِيرِ هَذِهِ الْآيَةِ مِنَ الْبَقَرَةِ، عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ الْبَرَاءِ، عَنِ الْمُعَافَى بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ، عَنْ فُلَيْحٍ، بِهِ. وَزَادَ: قَالَ عَطَاءٌ: ثُمَّ لَقِيتُ كَعْبَ الْأَحْبَارِ، فَسَأَلْتُهُ، فَمَا اخْتَلَفَا فِي حَرْفٍ، إِلَّا أَنَّ كَعْبًا قَالَ بِلُغَتِهِ: "أَعْيُنًا عَمُومَى، وَآذَانًا صَمُومَى، وَقُلُوبًا غَلُوفًا" [In T: "wa-quluban ghalufa" (and hearts ghalufa).]

Ibn Jarir said: By His saying, exalted is His praise: ﴿Neither the Jews nor the Christians will be pleased with you until you follow their religion.﴾ O Muhammad, neither the Jews nor the Christians will ever be pleased with you. So abandon seeking what would please and agree with them, and turn instead to seeking the pleasure of Allah by calling them to the truth with which Allah has sent you.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the [only] guidance."﴾ That is, say, O Muhammad: indeed the guidance of Allah, with which He has sent me, is the [true] guidance. That is, it is the upright, correct, complete and comprehensive religion.

Qatadah said concerning His saying, ﴿Say, "Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the [only] guidance,"﴾ that it is an argument which Allah taught Muhammad (ﷺ) and his Companions, by which they dispute with the people of misguidance. Qatadah said: It has reached us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "A group from my Ummah will continue to fight for the truth, prevailing, and no one who opposes them will harm them, until the command of Allah comes."

I say: This hadith is recorded in the Sahih (the authentic collection) from Abdullah ibn Amr.[[Sahih Muslim, no. 1924.]]

﴿And if you were to follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you, you would have from Allah no protector or helper.﴾ In this there is a severe warning and threat to the Ummah against following the ways of the Jews and Christians after they have come to know the Qur'an and the Sunnah, we seek refuge in Allah from that. For the address is to the Messenger, while the command is for his Ummah.

[Many jurists have used as evidence His saying, ﴿until you follow their religion,﴾ where the word "religion" (millah) is singular, to show that all disbelief is one religion, like His saying: ﴿For you is your religion, and for me is my religion.﴾ [Al-Kafirun: 6]. Based on this, Muslims and disbelievers do not inherit from one another, and each of them inherits from his fellow, whether or not he is of the same religion, because they are all one religion. This is the view of al-Shafi'i, Abu Hanifah, and a narration from Ahmad. In another narration from him, he held, like Malik, that the people of two different religions do not inherit from one another, as came in the hadith. And Allah knows best.]

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those to whom We have given the Scripture recite it with its true recitation.﴾ Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: They are the Jews and the Christians. This is also the view of Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and Ibn Jarir chose it.

Sa'id narrated from Qatadah: They are the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Musa and Abdullah ibn Imran al-Asbahani narrated to us, both saying: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, Usamah ibn Zayd narrated to us, from his father, from Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), regarding ﴿reciting it with its true recitation﴾ that he said: When he passes a mention of Paradise, he asks Allah for Paradise, and when he passes a mention of the Fire, he seeks refuge in Allah from the Fire.[[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/357).]]

Abu al-Aliyah said: Ibn Mas'ud said: By Him in whose hand is my soul, the true recitation of it is to make lawful what it makes lawful, to make unlawful what it makes unlawful, to recite it as Allah revealed it, not to distort words from their places, and not to interpret any part of it in a way other than its correct interpretation.

Abd al-Razzaq narrated it likewise from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, and Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir narrated it from Ibn Mas'ud.

As-Suddi said, from Abu Malik, from Ibn Abbas regarding this verse: They make lawful its lawful and make unlawful its unlawful, and they do not distort it from its places.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Something similar has been narrated from Ibn Mas'ud.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: They act upon its clear verses (muhkam, the unambiguous), and they believe in its ambiguous verses (mutashabih, those open to multiple readings), and they leave to its Knower whatever is unclear to them.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Abi Za'idah informed us, Dawud ibn Abi Hind informed us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿reciting it with its true recitation,﴾ that he said: They follow it with its true following. Then he recited: ﴿And the moon when it follows it﴾ [Ash-Shams: 2], meaning it follows it. He said: Something similar has been narrated from Ikrimah, Ata', Mujahid, Abu Razin, and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i.

Sufyan al-Thawri said: Zubayd narrated to us, from Murrah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, regarding His saying: ﴿reciting it with its true recitation,﴾ he said: They follow it with its true following.

Al-Qurtubi said: Nasr ibn Isa narrated, from Malik, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding His saying: ﴿reciting it with its true recitation,﴾ that he said: "They follow it with its true following." Then he said: In its chain of narration are more than one of the unknown narrators whom al-Khatib mentioned, but its meaning is sound. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said: Whoever follows the Qur'an, it will lead him to the gardens of Paradise. And from Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him): They are those who, when they pass a verse of mercy, ask Allah for it, and when they pass a verse of punishment, they seek refuge from it. He said: This meaning has also been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ), that when he passed a verse of mercy he would ask, and when he passed a verse of punishment he would seek refuge.

* *

His saying: ﴿Those believe in it.﴾ This is the report about ﴿those to whom We have given the Scripture and who recite it with its true recitation.﴾ That is: whoever among the People of the Books revealed to the earlier Prophets establishes his Book in its true establishment, he will believe in what I have sent you with, O Muhammad, as Allah said: ﴿And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 66], up to the end of the verse. And He said: ﴿Say, "O People of the Scripture, you are not standing on anything until you uphold the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord."﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 68]. That is: if you establish them in their true establishment and believe in them with true belief, and confirm what is in them of the reports about the sending of Muhammad (ﷺ), his description and attributes, and the command to follow him, support him and assist him, this will lead you to the truth and to following what is good in this world and the Hereafter. As Allah said: ﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel﴾ [Al-A'raf: 157], up to the end of the verse. And He said: ﴿Say, "Believe in it or do not believe. Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall down upon their faces in prostration, and say, 'Exalted is our Lord; indeed, the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled.'"﴾ [Al-Isra': 107-108]. That is: if what He promised us concerning the affair of Muhammad (ﷺ) is indeed to come to pass. And He said: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it, they believe in it. And when it is recited to them, they say, "We believe in it; indeed it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed we were, before it, Muslims." Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured, and they repel evil with good, and from what We have provided them they spend﴾ [Al-Qasas: 52-54]. And He said: ﴿And say to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered, "Have you submitted?" If they submit, then they are [rightly] guided; but if they turn away, then upon you is only the notification, and Allah is Seeing of [His] servants﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 20]. Therefore He said: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in it, those are the losers.﴾ As He said: ﴿And whoever among the factions disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place﴾ [Hud: 17]. And in the Sahih: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, no one from this Ummah hears of me, whether a Jew or a Christian, and then does not believe in me, except that he will enter the Fire."[[Sahih Muslim, no. 153, from Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him).]]

Ibn Jarir said: By His saying, exalted is His praise: ﴿Neither the Jews nor the Christians will be pleased with you until you follow their religion.﴾ O Muhammad, neither the Jews nor the Christians will ever be pleased with you. So abandon seeking what would please and agree with them, and turn instead to seeking the pleasure of Allah by calling them to the truth with which Allah has sent you.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the [only] guidance."﴾ That is, say, O Muhammad: indeed the guidance of Allah, with which He has sent me, is the [true] guidance. That is, it is the upright, correct, complete and comprehensive religion.

Qatadah said concerning His saying, ﴿Say, "Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the [only] guidance,"﴾ that it is an argument which Allah taught Muhammad (ﷺ) and his Companions, by which they dispute with the people of misguidance. Qatadah said: It has reached us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "A group from my Ummah will continue to fight for the truth, prevailing, and no one who opposes them will harm them, until the command of Allah comes."

I say: This hadith is recorded in the Sahih (the authentic collection) from Abdullah ibn Amr.[[Sahih Muslim, no. 1924.]]

﴿And if you were to follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you, you would have from Allah no protector or helper.﴾ In this there is a severe warning and threat to the Ummah against following the ways of the Jews and Christians after they have come to know the Qur'an and the Sunnah, we seek refuge in Allah from that. For the address is to the Messenger, while the command is for his Ummah.

[Many jurists have used as evidence His saying, ﴿until you follow their religion,﴾ where the word "religion" (millah) is singular, to show that all disbelief is one religion, like His saying: ﴿For you is your religion, and for me is my religion.﴾ [Al-Kafirun: 6]. Based on this, Muslims and disbelievers do not inherit from one another, and each of them inherits from his fellow, whether or not he is of the same religion, because they are all one religion. This is the view of al-Shafi'i, Abu Hanifah, and a narration from Ahmad. In another narration from him, he held, like Malik, that the people of two different religions do not inherit from one another, as came in the hadith. And Allah knows best.]

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those to whom We have given the Scripture recite it with its true recitation.﴾ Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: They are the Jews and the Christians. This is also the view of Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and Ibn Jarir chose it.

Sa'id narrated from Qatadah: They are the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Musa and Abdullah ibn Imran al-Asbahani narrated to us, both saying: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, Usamah ibn Zayd narrated to us, from his father, from Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), regarding ﴿reciting it with its true recitation﴾ that he said: When he passes a mention of Paradise, he asks Allah for Paradise, and when he passes a mention of the Fire, he seeks refuge in Allah from the Fire.[[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/357).]]

Abu al-Aliyah said: Ibn Mas'ud said: By Him in whose hand is my soul, the true recitation of it is to make lawful what it makes lawful, to make unlawful what it makes unlawful, to recite it as Allah revealed it, not to distort words from their places, and not to interpret any part of it in a way other than its correct interpretation.

Abd al-Razzaq narrated it likewise from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, and Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir narrated it from Ibn Mas'ud.

As-Suddi said, from Abu Malik, from Ibn Abbas regarding this verse: They make lawful its lawful and make unlawful its unlawful, and they do not distort it from its places.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Something similar has been narrated from Ibn Mas'ud.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: They act upon its clear verses (muhkam, the unambiguous), and they believe in its ambiguous verses (mutashabih, those open to multiple readings), and they leave to its Knower whatever is unclear to them.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Abi Za'idah informed us, Dawud ibn Abi Hind informed us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿reciting it with its true recitation,﴾ that he said: They follow it with its true following. Then he recited: ﴿And the moon when it follows it﴾ [Ash-Shams: 2], meaning it follows it. He said: Something similar has been narrated from Ikrimah, Ata', Mujahid, Abu Razin, and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i.

Sufyan al-Thawri said: Zubayd narrated to us, from Murrah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, regarding His saying: ﴿reciting it with its true recitation,﴾ he said: They follow it with its true following.

Al-Qurtubi said: Nasr ibn Isa narrated, from Malik, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding His saying: ﴿reciting it with its true recitation,﴾ that he said: "They follow it with its true following." Then he said: In its chain of narration are more than one of the unknown narrators whom al-Khatib mentioned, but its meaning is sound. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said: Whoever follows the Qur'an, it will lead him to the gardens of Paradise. And from Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him): They are those who, when they pass a verse of mercy, ask Allah for it, and when they pass a verse of punishment, they seek refuge from it. He said: This meaning has also been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ), that when he passed a verse of mercy he would ask, and when he passed a verse of punishment he would seek refuge.

* *

His saying: ﴿Those believe in it.﴾ This is the report about ﴿those to whom We have given the Scripture and who recite it with its true recitation.﴾ That is: whoever among the People of the Books revealed to the earlier Prophets establishes his Book in its true establishment, he will believe in what I have sent you with, O Muhammad, as Allah said: ﴿And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 66], up to the end of the verse. And He said: ﴿Say, "O People of the Scripture, you are not standing on anything until you uphold the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord."﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 68]. That is: if you establish them in their true establishment and believe in them with true belief, and confirm what is in them of the reports about the sending of Muhammad (ﷺ), his description and attributes, and the command to follow him, support him and assist him, this will lead you to the truth and to following what is good in this world and the Hereafter. As Allah said: ﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel﴾ [Al-A'raf: 157], up to the end of the verse. And He said: ﴿Say, "Believe in it or do not believe. Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall down upon their faces in prostration, and say, 'Exalted is our Lord; indeed, the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled.'"﴾ [Al-Isra': 107-108]. That is: if what He promised us concerning the affair of Muhammad (ﷺ) is indeed to come to pass. And He said: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it, they believe in it. And when it is recited to them, they say, "We believe in it; indeed it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed we were, before it, Muslims." Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured, and they repel evil with good, and from what We have provided them they spend﴾ [Al-Qasas: 52-54]. And He said: ﴿And say to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered, "Have you submitted?" If they submit, then they are [rightly] guided; but if they turn away, then upon you is only the notification, and Allah is Seeing of [His] servants﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 20]. Therefore He said: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in it, those are the losers.﴾ As He said: ﴿And whoever among the factions disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place﴾ [Hud: 17]. And in the Sahih: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, no one from this Ummah hears of me, whether a Jew or a Christian, and then does not believe in me, except that he will enter the Fire."[[Sahih Muslim, no. 153, from Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him).]]

The verse and its counterpart were already mentioned earlier in the beginning of the surah. They are repeated here for emphasis and to urge the following of the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet (al-nabi al-ummi), whose description, attributes, name, command, and community they find in their books. He warns them against concealing this, and against concealing the blessings Allah bestowed upon them, and He commands them to remember the favour of Allah upon them, both the worldly and the religious blessings, and not to envy their paternal cousins among the Arabs for what Allah has granted them by sending the final Messenger from among them. Nor should that envy lead them to oppose him and deny him, or to turn away from supporting him, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him always until the Day of Judgment.

The verse and its counterpart were already mentioned earlier in the beginning of the surah. They are repeated here for emphasis and to urge the following of the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet (al-nabi al-ummi), whose description, attributes, name, command, and community they find in their books. He warns them against concealing this, and against concealing the blessings Allah bestowed upon them, and He commands them to remember the favour of Allah upon them, both the worldly and the religious blessings, and not to envy their paternal cousins among the Arabs for what Allah has granted them by sending the final Messenger from among them. Nor should that envy lead them to oppose him and deny him, or to turn away from supporting him, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him always until the Day of Judgment.

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 2, verse 124 (part 1 of 2):

He, exalted is He, says, drawing attention to the nobility of Ibrahim (Abraham), His intimate friend (khalil), upon him be peace, and that Allah the Exalted made him an imam (leader) for mankind, to be followed in tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness), until he fulfilled what Allah the Exalted had charged him with of commands and prohibitions. For this reason He said: ﴿And when Ibrahim was tested by his Lord with certain words﴾. That is: Mention, O Muhammad, to these polytheists and to the People of the Book, who claim the creed (millah) of Ibrahim while they are not upon it, whereas the one who is upon it is upright, namely you and those believers who are with you, mention to them the testing of Allah of Ibrahim, that is, His trying him with what He charged him with of commands and prohibitions. ﴿And he fulfilled them﴾, that is, he carried out all of them, as He said: ﴿And Ibrahim who fulfilled [his covenant]﴾ [An-Najm: 37], that is, he fulfilled all that was prescribed for him, and he acted upon it, may the blessings of Allah be upon him. He also said: ﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was a nation, devoutly obedient to Allah, a hanif (upright monotheist), and he was not of those who associate others with Allah. He was grateful for His favours. He chose him and guided him to a straight path. And We gave him good in this world, and indeed he is in the Hereafter among the righteous. Then We revealed to you: Follow the creed of Ibrahim, a hanif, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah﴾ [An-Nahl: 120-123]. He also said: ﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a correct religion, the creed of Ibrahim, a hanif, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah﴾ [Al-An'am: 161]. He also said: ﴿Ibrahim was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a hanif, a Muslim, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah. Indeed, the people most worthy of Ibrahim are those who followed him, and this Prophet and those who believe, and Allah is the Ally of the believers﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 67-68].

* *

His saying ﴿with words﴾ means: with laws, commands and prohibitions. The word "kalimat" (words) is used in two senses: it is used to mean the decreed words (al-kalimat al-qadariyyah), as in His saying about Maryam, upon her be peace: ﴿And she confirmed the words of her Lord and His scriptures, and she was among the devoutly obedient﴾ [At-Tahrim: 12]. It is also used to mean the legislated words (al-kalimat al-shar'iyyah), as in His saying: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice. None can change His words﴾ [Al-An'am: 115], that is, His legislated words. These are either a true report or a demand for justice if they are commands or prohibitions. Among this category is this noble verse: ﴿And when Ibrahim was tested by his Lord with words, and he fulfilled them﴾, that is, he carried them out. He said: ﴿Indeed, I will make you an imam for mankind﴾, that is, as a reward for what he did, since he carried out the commands and abstained from what was forbidden. Allah made him an example and an imam for mankind, to be followed and to have his footsteps emulated.

The scholars have differed in interpreting the words with which Allah tested Ibrahim the intimate friend, upon him be peace. Various narrations have been reported from Ibn 'Abbas on this matter:

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah tested him with the rites of pilgrimage (manasik). This was also narrated by Abu Ishaq al-Subay'i, from al-Tamimi, from Ibn 'Abbas.

'Abd al-Razzaq also said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿And when Ibrahim was tested by his Lord with certain words﴾: He said: Allah tested him with purification: five in the head and five in the body. In the head: trimming the moustache, rinsing the mouth, sniffing water into the nose, using the siwak (tooth-stick), and parting the hair. In the body: cutting the nails, removing the pubic hair, circumcision, plucking the armpit hair, and washing away the traces of excrement and urine with water.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Similar things have been reported from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Mujahid, al-Sha'bi, al-Nakha'i, Abu Salih and Abu al-Jald.

I say: Close to this is what is authentically established in Sahih Muslim, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ten are of the fitrah (natural disposition): trimming the moustache, letting the beard grow, using the siwak, sniffing water into the nose, cutting the nails, washing the joints of the fingers (barajim), plucking the armpit hair, removing the pubic hair, and istinja' (cleansing after relieving oneself) with water." [Mus'ab said:] I have forgotten the tenth, unless it is rinsing the mouth.

Waki' said: Intiqas al-ma' means istinja' (washing after relieving oneself).

In the Sahih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The fitrah is five: circumcision, shaving the pubic hair, trimming the moustache, cutting the nails, and plucking the armpit hair." The wording is that of Muslim.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la informed us, by recitation, that Ibn Wahb informed us, that Ibn Lahi'ah informed me, from Ibn Hubayrah, from Hanash ibn 'Abd Allah al-San'ani, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he used to say regarding this verse: ﴿And when Ibrahim was tested by his Lord with words, and he fulfilled them﴾: He said: Ten: six in the human body and four in the sacred places (mashi'r). As for those in the body: shaving the pubic hair, plucking the armpit hair, and circumcision. Ibn Hubayrah used to say: These three are one. Then cutting the nails, trimming the moustache, the siwak, and the Friday ghusl (ritual bath). The four in the sacred places are: the tawaf (circumambulation), the sa'y (running) between al-Safa and al-Marwah, throwing the pebbles at the jamarat, and the ifadah (the departure from Mina after the pilgrimage).

Dawud ibn Abi Hind said, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: No one was tested with this religion and carried all of it out except Ibrahim. Allah said: ﴿And when Ibrahim was tested by his Lord with words, and he fulfilled them﴾. I said to him: What are the words with which Allah tested Ibrahim and which he fulfilled? He said: Islam has thirty portions (sahm), of which ten are verses in Bara'ah (Surah At-Tawbah): ﴿The repentant, the worshippers, the praisers﴾ [At-Tawbah: 112] to the end of the verse; and ten verses at the beginning of Surah ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾ and ﴿A petitioner asked for a punishment that will occur﴾; and ten verses in Al-Ahzab: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 35] to the end of the verse. He fulfilled all of them, and so Bara'ah was written for him. Allah said: ﴿And Ibrahim who fulfilled [his covenant]﴾ [An-Najm: 37].

Thus it was narrated by al-Hakim, Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir, and Abu Muhammad ibn Abi Hatim, with their chains to Dawud ibn Abi Hind, with this same report. This is the wording of Ibn Abi Hatim.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from Sa'id or 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The words with which Allah tested Ibrahim and which he fulfilled were: his separation from his people for the sake of Allah, when he was commanded to part from them; his debate with Nimrod for the sake of Allah, when Nimrod confronted him with the grave matter in which he opposed him; his patience under being thrown into the fire by them so that they might burn him for the sake of Allah, despite the terror of that affair; the migration after that from his homeland and his country for the sake of Allah, when He commanded him to leave them; what he was commanded of hospitality and patience in it with his person and his wealth; and what he was tested with, the slaughter of his son when He commanded him to slaughter him. When all of this trial had passed over him, and Allah had made him sincere for the trial, Allah said to him: ﴿Submit,﴾ he said: ﴿I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 131], despite the opposition and separation of the people.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj informed us, Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah informed us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, that is al-Basri, regarding ﴿And when Ibrahim was tested by his Lord with words [and he fulfilled them]﴾: He said: He tested him with the star, and he was pleased with him; He tested him with the moon, and he was pleased with him; He tested him with the sun, and he was pleased with him; He tested him with the migration, and he was pleased with him; He tested him with circumcision, and he was pleased with him; He tested him with his son, and he was pleased with him.

Ibn Jarir said: Bishr ibn Mu'adh informed us, Yazid ibn Zuray' informed us, Sa'id informed us, from Qatadah, who said: Al-Hasan used to say: By Allah, He tested him with a matter and he was patient with it. He tested him with the star, the sun and the moon, and he responded well to that, and he knew that his Lord is ever-living and does not cease. So he turned his face to Him who originated the heavens and the earth, as a hanif, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah. Then He tested him with the migration, so he left his land and his people until he reached al-Sham as a migrant to Allah. Then He tested him with the fire before the migration, and he was patient with that. Allah tested him with the slaughter of his son and with circumcision, and he was patient with that.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from one who heard al-Hasan say regarding His saying: ﴿And when Ibrahim was tested by his Lord with words [and he fulfilled them]﴾: He said: Allah tested him with the slaughter of his son, with the fire, and with the star, the sun and the moon.

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar informed us, Salm ibn Qutaybah informed us, Abu Hilal informed us, from al-Hasan: ﴿And when Ibrahim was tested by his Lord with words﴾. He said: He tested him with the star, the sun and the moon, and found him patient.

Al-'Awfi said in his tafsir, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And when Ibrahim was tested by his Lord with words, and he fulfilled them﴾.
