Among them is: ﴿Indeed, I will make you an imam for mankind﴾; and among them: ﴿And when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House, and Isma'il [with him]﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 127]; and among them: the verses concerning the manasik (rites) and the maqam (station) that was made for Ibrahim, and the provision with which the inhabitants of the House were provided, and Muhammad was sent in their religion.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah informed us, Shababah informed us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿And when Ibrahim was tested by his Lord with words, and he fulfilled them﴾: Allah said to Ibrahim: Indeed, I am going to test you with a matter, so what is it? He said: You will make me an imam for mankind. He said: Yes. He said: And from my offspring? ﴿He said: My covenant does not include the wrongdoers﴾. He said: You will make the House a place of return for the people? He said: Yes. He said: And a sanctuary? He said: Yes. He said: And you will make us Muslims for You, and from our offspring a Muslim nation for You? He said: Yes. He said: And will You provide its people with fruits, those among them who believe in Allah? He said: Yes.

Ibn Abi Najih said: I heard this from 'Ikrimah, and I presented it to Mujahid, and he did not deny it.

Ibn Jarir also narrated it in this way through more than one channel, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And when Ibrahim was tested by his Lord with words, and he fulfilled them﴾. He said: He was tested with the verses that follow: ﴿Indeed, I will make you an imam for mankind.﴾ He said: ﴿And from my offspring?﴾ He said: ﴿My covenant does not include the wrongdoers﴾.

Abu Ja'far al-Razi said, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas: ﴿And when Ibrahim was tested by his Lord with words [and he fulfilled them]﴾. He said: The words are: ﴿Indeed, I will make you an imam for mankind﴾; and His saying: ﴿And when We made the House a place of return for the people and a sanctuary﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 125]; and His saying: ﴿And take the station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 125]; and His saying: ﴿And We entrusted Ibrahim and Isma'il﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 125] to the end of the verse; and His saying: ﴿And when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House, and Isma'il﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 127] to the end of the verse. He said: All of that is among the words with which Ibrahim was tested.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 124 (part 2 of 2):

Al-Suddi said: "The words with which Abraham was tested by his Lord" are: ﴿Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. Our Lord, and make us Muslims [submitting] to You, and from our descendants a Muslim nation [submitting] to You﴾, and ﴿Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses﴾.

[Al-Qurtubi said: In the Muwatta' (Muwatta' of Imam Malik) and elsewhere, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa'id, that he heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib say: Abraham, peace be upon him, was the first to be circumcised, the first to entertain a guest, the first to shave the pubic hair, the first to trim his nails, the first to trim the moustache, and the first to grow grey hair. When he saw the grey hair he said: "What is this?" It was said: "Dignity (waqar)." He said: "My Lord, increase me in dignity." Ibn Abi Shaybah also mentioned, on the authority of Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of his father, that he said: The first to deliver a sermon from pulpits was Abraham, peace be upon him. Others have added: and the first to send the post (barid), the first to strike with the sword, the first to use the siwak, the first to cleanse with water (istinja'), and the first to wear trousers (sarawil). It is also narrated from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If I take a pulpit, then my father Abraham took one; and if I take a staff, then my father Abraham took one." I say: This is a hadith that is not authentic, and Allah knows best. Then al-Qurtubi began to discuss the legal rulings (ahkam shar'iyyah) related to these matters.]

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said, in substance: It is permissible that the meaning of "the words" is all that has been mentioned, and it is permissible that it is some of it. One may not affirm with certainty that any one of them is specifically meant, except by a hadith or an ijma' (scholarly consensus). He said: No report has been authenticated on this matter, either through a single transmitter or through a group of transmitters which would require acceptance.

He said: However, two reports have been transmitted from the Prophet (ﷺ) with a similar meaning. One of them is what Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Rushdin ibn Sa'd narrated to us, Zabban ibn Fa'id narrated to me, on the authority of Sahl ibn Mu'adh ibn Anas, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "Shall I not tell you why Allah named Abraham His friend (khalil), [and] ﴿who fulfilled﴾ [al-Najm 53:37]? Because he used to say every morning and every evening: ﴿So glory be to Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning﴾ [al-Rum 30:17], until he finished the verse."

He said: The other of them: Abu Kurayb narrated it to us, [who said]: al-Hasan informed us, on the authority of Atiyyah, [who said]: Isra'il informed us, on the authority of Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "[Regarding] ﴿and Abraham, who fulfilled﴾, do you know what 'fulfilled' means?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "He fulfilled the work of his day: four rak'ahs during the day."

Adam narrated it in his tafsir, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah. And Abd ibn Humayd [narrated it], on the authority of Yunus ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, with the same chain.

Then Ibn Jarir began to declare these two hadiths weak, and he was right in that; for their transmission is not permissible except with an explanation of their weakness, and their weakness is from many aspects, since each of the two chains includes more than one weak narrator, in addition to what is in the text of the hadith that indicates its weakness. [And Allah knows best.]

Then Ibn Jarir said: If someone said that what Mujahid, Abu Salih and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said is more correct than what others said, it would be a valid position, since His saying: ﴿I am making you a leader for the people﴾ and His saying: ﴿And We charged Abraham and Ishmael: "Purify My House for those who circumambulate it"﴾, and the rest of the verses that are similar to it, serve as an explanation of the words with which Allah says He tested Abraham.

I say: What he first said, that the words include all that has been mentioned, is stronger than what he permitted from the saying of Mujahid and whoever said like him; because the context (siyaq) gives something other than what they said, and Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He said: "And from my descendants?" He said: "My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers."﴾ When Allah made Abraham a leader (imam), he asked Allah that the leaders after him be from his descendants. He was granted this, and he was informed that there would be wrongdoers among his descendants, and that the covenant of Allah would not reach them, and they would not be leaders, so they would not be followed. The evidence that his request was granted is the saying of Allah, the Exalted, in Surah al-'Ankabut: ﴿And We placed in his descendants prophethood and the Book﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:27]. So every prophet Allah sent and every book Allah revealed after Abraham came from his descendants, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him.

As for the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿He said: "My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers"﴾, they differed about it. Khasif narrated, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿He said: "My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers"﴾, that he said: "There will be wrongdoers among your descendants."

Ibn Abi Najih said, on the authority of Mujahid: ﴿He said: "My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers"﴾, he said: "There will not be for Me a wrongdoing leader [who is followed]." In another narration: "I will not appoint a wrongdoing leader who is followed." Sufyan said, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He said: "My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers"﴾, he said: "There will not be a wrongdoing leader who is followed."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to me, Malik ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Shurayk narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿and from my descendants﴾, he said: "As for whoever among them is righteous, I will make him a leader who is followed; and as for whoever is a wrongdoer, [he will not be made a leader], and there is no comfort of the eye (for him)."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers﴾ is meant to refer to the polytheist; there will not be a wrongdoing leader. He means: there will not be a polytheist leader.

Ibn Juraij said, on the authority of Ata', he said: ﴿I am making you a leader for the people." He said: "And from my descendants?"﴾ So He refused to make from his descendants a wrongdoing leader. I asked Ata': "What is His covenant?" He said: "His command."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Amr ibn Thawr al-Qaysari informed us, in what he wrote to me: al-Firyabi narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, Simak ibn Harb narrated to us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Allah said to Abraham: ﴿I am making you a leader for the people." He said: "And from my descendants?"﴾ So He refused to do so. Then He said: ﴿My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers.﴾

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, on the authority of Sa'id or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿He said: "And from my descendants?" He said: "My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers."﴾ It informs him that there will be a wrongdoer among his descendants whom His covenant will not reach—and it is not appropriate [for Him] to appoint him to any of His affairs, even if he is from the descendants of His friend—and a good-doer, whose supplication will be answered, and he will attain what he sought in his request.

Al-'Awfi said, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers﴾, he said: it means: there is no covenant for a wrongdoer upon you in his wrongdoing, that you obey him in it.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Muthanna narrated to us, Ishaq narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, on the authority of Isra'il, on the authority of Muslim al-A'war, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: ﴿My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers﴾, he said: "There is no covenant for the wrongdoers; and if you make a covenant with him, then break it."

It has been narrated from Mujahid, Ata' and Muqatil ibn Hayyan something similar to this.

Al-Thawri said, on the authority of Harun ibn 'Antarah, on the authority of his father, who said: "There is no covenant for a wrongdoer."

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, on the authority of Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers﴾, he said: "The covenant of Allah does not reach the wrongdoers in the Hereafter. As for in this world, the wrongdoer has attained it: he is secure through it, eats, and lives."

Similarly said Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Ata', al-Hasan and Ikrimah.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "The covenant of Allah which He made with His servants is His religion." He means: His religion does not reach the wrongdoers. Do you not see that He said: ﴿And We blessed him and Isaac, and among their descendants are the good-doer and the one who clearly wrongs himself﴾ [al-Saffat 37:113]? He means: not all your descendants, O Abraham, are upon the truth.

Similarly it has been narrated from Abu al-'Aliyah, Ata' and Muqatil ibn Hayyan.

Juwaybir said, on the authority of al-Dahhak: "My obedience will not reach an enemy of Mine who disobeys Me, and I will not grant it except to a friend of Mine who obeys Me."

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Hamid narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah ibn Sa'id al-Asadi narrated to us, Sulaym ibn Sa'id al-Damghani narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, on the authority of al-A'mash, on the authority of Sa'd ibn Ubaydah, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, on the authority of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said regarding: ﴿My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers﴾: "There is no obedience [owed] except in what is right (ma'ruf)." [Al-Bukhari said in his Sahih, no. 7257: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Ghundar narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, on the authority of Zayd, on the authority of Sa'd ibn Ubaydah, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) sent an army and appointed a man over them. He lit a fire and said: "Enter it." They wanted to enter it, but others said: "We only fled from it." This was mentioned to the Prophet (ﷺ). He said to those who wanted to enter it: "If they had entered it, they would have remained in it until the Day of Resurrection." And he said to the others: "There is no obedience in sin; obedience is only in what is right." This is the origin of this hadith, without mention of the verse, and Allah knows best.]

Al-Suddi said: ﴿My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers﴾: he says: "My covenant" is "My prophethood."

These are the sayings of the early exegetes (mufassirun al-salaf) regarding this verse, as transmitted by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim, may Allah have mercy on them both. Ibn Jarir chose that this verse, although it is apparent in the form of a report, means that the covenant of Allah concerning leadership (imamah) does not reach a wrongdoer. Thus it contains an announcement from Allah to Abraham the Friend, peace be upon him, that there will be found among your descendants one who wrongs himself, as was previously mentioned from Mujahid and others, and Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 125 (part 1 of 3):

Al-'Awfi reported from Ibn 'Abbas regarding the words of Allah Most High, ﴿And when We made the House a place of return for mankind﴾, that he said: "They never get enough of it. They come to it, then return to their families, then come back to it again."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "﴿A place of return for mankind﴾ means they keep returning (yathubuna)."

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) narrated both of these.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Our father informed us, 'Abd Allah ibn Raja' informed us, Isra'il informed us, from Muslim, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding the words of Allah Most High, ﴿And when We made the House a place of return for mankind﴾, that he said: "They return to it, then they go back." He said: It is also narrated from Abu al-'Aliyah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr (in one narration), 'Ata', Mujahid, al-Hasan, 'Atiyyah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas and al-Dahhak something similar.

Ibn Jarir said: 'Abd al-Karim ibn Abi 'Umayr narrated to me, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Amr (meaning al-Awza'i) said: 'Abdah ibn Abi Lubabah narrated to me, regarding the words of Allah Most High, ﴿And when We made the House a place of return for mankind﴾, that he said: "No one who goes to it turns away thinking he has had his fill of it."

Yunus narrated to me, from Ibn Wahb, who said: Ibn Zayd said regarding ﴿And when We made the House a place of return for mankind﴾: "They keep returning to it from all the lands, and they come to it."

[How excellently the poet expressed this meaning, as cited by al-Qurtubi:
The House was made a place of return for them,
Never will the age see them satisfied with it.]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr (in the other narration), 'Ikrimah, Qatadah and 'Ata' al-Khurasani said: ﴿A place of return for mankind﴾ means a gathering place.

On ﴿and a sanctuary﴾, al-Dahhak reported from Ibn 'Abbas: it means a sanctuary for the people.

Abu Ja'far al-Razi reported from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding ﴿And when We made the House a place of return for mankind and a sanctuary﴾, that he said: "A sanctuary from the enemy, and that weapons may not be carried in it. In the Jahiliyyah (the time of ignorance before Islam), people were snatched away from around them, while they themselves were safe and were not taken captive."

It is also narrated from Mujahid, 'Ata', al-Suddi, Qatadah and al-Rabi' ibn Anas that they said: Whoever enters it is safe.

The essence of what these leading scholars explained of this verse is this: Allah Most High mentions the nobility of the House and the attributes He gave it, both legislatively and by decree, in that it is a place of return for mankind, meaning He made it a place that souls yearn for and long for, and they never get enough of it, even if they visit it every year. This was in answer from Allah Most High to the prayer of His friend Ibrahim (peace be upon him) in His words: ﴿So make hearts among people yearn towards them﴾, up to His words: ﴿Our Lord, and accept my prayer﴾ [Ibrahim: 37–40]. He also describes it as a sanctuary: whoever enters it is safe, even if he has committed what he committed and then enters it, he is safe.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: A man would meet the killer of his father or brother within it, and he would not confront him. This is how it is described in Surah al-Ma'idah, in the words of Allah Most High: ﴿Allah made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a means of support for mankind﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 97], meaning that evil is lifted from them because of its honour. As Ibn 'Abbas said: "If people did not perform the Hajj (pilgrimage) to this House, Allah would have caused the sky to fall upon the earth." This honour belongs only to the honour of its first builder, who is the friend of the Most Merciful, as Allah Most High says: ﴿And when We settled Ibrahim at the site of the House, [saying], "Do not associate anything with Me"﴾ [al-Hajj: 26]. And Allah Most High says: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind is that at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds. In it are clear signs: the standing place of Ibrahim, and whoever enters it is safe﴾ [Al 'Imran: 96–97].

In this noble verse, Allah also points to the station of Ibrahim together with the command to pray there. He says: ﴿And take the station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer﴾. The exegetes differ over what is meant by "the station" (maqam). Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Umar ibn Shabbah al-Numayri informed us, Abu Khalaf (meaning 'Abd Allah ibn 'Isa) told us, Da'ud ibn Abi Hind told us, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And take from the station of Ibrahim a place of prayer﴾, that he said: "The station of Ibrahim is the entire Sacred Precinct (al-Haram)." Similar is narrated from Mujahid and 'Ata'.

He also said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I asked 'Ata' about ﴿And take from the station of Ibrahim a place of prayer﴾, and he said: "I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: As for the station of Ibrahim mentioned here, it is the station of Ibrahim that is in the mosque." Then he said: "And the station of Ibrahim has many meanings; 'the station of Ibrahim' is the whole of the Hajj." Then 'Ata' explained it to me: "The standing at 'Arafat (ta'rif), the two prayers at 'Arafat, al-Mash'ar, Mina, the stoning of the pillars (ramy al-jimar), and the circumambulation between al-Safa and al-Marwah." I said: "Did Ibn 'Abbas explain it that way?" He said: "No, but he said: 'The station of Ibrahim is the whole of the Hajj.'" I said: "Did you hear that from him?" He said: "Yes, I heard it from him."

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿And take from the station of Ibrahim a place of prayer﴾, that he said: "The stone is the station of Ibrahim, the Prophet of Allah. Allah made it a mercy. He would stand upon it, and Isma'il would hand him the stones." And if he had washed his head as they claim, his two feet would have sunk into it.

[Al-Suddi said: The station is the stone that the wife of Isma'il placed beneath the foot of Ibrahim until she washed his head. Al-Qurtubi related this and weakened it, while others preferred other views. Al-Razi, in his tafsir, related it from al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatadah and al-Rabi' ibn Anas.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, who heard Jabir narrating about the Farewell Hajj of the Prophet (ﷺ): When the Prophet (ﷺ) performed the circumambulation, 'Umar said to him: "Is this the station of our father Ibrahim?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Should we not take it as a place of prayer?" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And take from the station of Ibrahim a place of prayer﴾.

['Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah said: Abu Usamah informed us, from Zakariyya, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Maysarah, who said: 'Umar said: "I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, is this the station of the friend of our Lord?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Should we not take it as a place of prayer?' Then it was revealed: ﴿And take from the station of Ibrahim a place of prayer﴾."]

Ibn Mardawayh said: Da'laj ibn Ahmad narrated to us, Ghaylan ibn 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Masruq ibn al-Marzuban narrated to us, Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, that he passed by the station of Ibrahim and said: "O Messenger of Allah, are we not standing in the station of the friend of our Lord?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Should we not take it as a place of prayer?" It was not long before ﴿And take from the station of Ibrahim a place of prayer﴾ was revealed.

Ibn Mardawayh also said: Muhammad [in some copies: 'Ali] ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Qazwini narrated to us, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Junayd narrated to us, Hisham ibn Khalid narrated to us, al-Walid narrated to us, from Malik ibn Anas, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Jabir, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood on the Day of the Conquest of Makkah at the station of Ibrahim, 'Umar said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, is this the station of Ibrahim that Allah spoke of: ﴿And take from the station of Ibrahim a place of prayer﴾?" He said: "Yes." Al-Walid said: I said to Malik, "Did he narrate to you as 'wa-ttakhidhu' (and take)?" He said: "Yes." This is how it occurs in this narration. It is a strange (gharib) report.

al-Nasa'i also narrated something similar from the hadith of al-Walid ibn Muslim.

al-Bukhari said: "Chapter: the words of Allah, ﴿And take from the station of Ibrahim a place of prayer﴾ — mathabah (a place of return), yathubuna (they return), yarji'una (they go back)."

Musaddad narrated to us, Yahya narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "I agreed with my Lord in three things," or "my Lord agreed with me in three things." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, if only you took the station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer?" Then ﴿And take from the station of Ibrahim a place of prayer﴾ was revealed. And I said: "O Messenger of Allah, the righteous and the wicked enter upon your wives, so if only you ordered the Mothers of the Believers to observe hijab (veil)?" So Allah revealed the verse of hijab. He also said: "It reached me that the Prophet (ﷺ) had rebuked some of his wives, so I entered upon them and said: 'If you do not desist, Allah will surely replace His Messenger with someone better than you,' until I came to one of his wives, who said: 'O 'Umar, is there not in the Messenger of Allah what would admonish his wives, that you must admonish them?' So Allah revealed: ﴿It may be that if he divorces you, his Lord will substitute for him wives better than you﴾ [al-Tahrim: 5]."

Ibn Abi Maryam said: Yahya ibn Ayyub informed us, Humayd narrated to me, who said: I heard Anas from 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.

[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4483.]

Thus al-Bukhari narrated it here, and he suspended the second chain from his teacher Sa'id ibn al-Hakam, known as Ibn Abi Maryam al-Misri. Al-Bukhari alone among the authors of the six books narrated from him directly; the others narrated from him through an intermediary. His purpose in mentioning this chain in suspended form was to show the connection of the hadith's chain. He did not give it a full chain because Yahya ibn Abi Ayyub al-Ghafiqi has a weakness in it, as Imam Ahmad said of him: "He has poor memory." And Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad said: Hushaym narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us, from Anas, who said: 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him [in some copies: with them both], said: "I agreed with my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, in three things. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, if only we took the station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer?' Then ﴿And take from the station of Ibrahim a place of prayer﴾ was revealed. And I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, the righteous and the wicked enter upon your wives, so if only you ordered them to cover themselves?' Then the verse of hijab was revealed. The wives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gathered together in jealousy, so I said to them: ﴿It may be that if he divorces you, his Lord will substitute for him wives better than you﴾ [al-Tahrim: 5], and it was revealed in that same way."

[al-Musnad, 1/23.] Then Ahmad narrated it from Yahya and Ibn Abi 'Adi, both from Humayd, from Anas, from 'Umar, that he said: "I agreed with my Lord in three things," or "my Lord agreed with me in three things," and he mentioned it.

[The narration of Yahya in al-Musnad (1/36) and the narration of Ibn Abi 'Adi (1/24).]

And al-Bukhari narrated it from 'Amr ibn 'Awn, al-Tirmidhi from Ahmad ibn Mani', al-Nasa'i from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi, and Ibn Majah from Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah, all of them from Hushaym ibn Bushayr, with it [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4916); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2960); al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Nasa'i no. (11611); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (1009).]]. Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from 'Abd ibn Humayd, from Hajjaj ibn Minhal, from Hammad ibn Salamah, and al-Nasa'i from Hannad, from Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah, both of them from Humayd, who is Ibn Tirwayh al-Tawil, with it [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2959); al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Nasa'i no. (10998).]]. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih." Imam 'Ali ibn al-Madini narrated it from Yazid ibn Zuray', from Humayd, with it, and said: "This is among the sound hadiths, and he (Humayd) is from Basra." Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj also narrated it in his Sahih with a different chain and a different wording. He said: "'Uqbah ibn Mukram narrated to us, Sa'id ibn 'Amir informed us, from Juwayriyah ibn Asma', from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from 'Umar, who said: 'I agreed with my Lord in three matters: concerning the veil, concerning the captives of Badr, and concerning the Station of Ibrahim'" [[Sahih Muslim no. (2399).]].

Abu Hatim al-Razi said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ansari narrated to us, Humayd al-Tawil narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "My Lord agreed with me in three matters" – or "I agreed with my Lord" – "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, if only you would take the Station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer?' So there was revealed: ﴿And take the Station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer﴾. And I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, if only you would screen the women?' So the verse of the veil was revealed. And the third: when 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy died, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to pray over him. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, will you pray over this disbelieving hypocrite?' He said: 'Desist from me, O son of al-Khattab.' So there was revealed: ﴿And do not pray over any of them who has died, nor stand at his grave﴾ [al-Tawbah: 84]" [[Narrated also by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/88) by way of Abu Hatim al-Razi.]].

This chain is also sound, and there is no contradiction between this and that; rather, all of them are sound. The concept of number (mafhum al-'adad, the implicit meaning drawn from a number) is overridden by an explicit statement (mantuq), when the two conflict. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Jurayj said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad informed me, from his father, from Jabir, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed the ramal (a brisk walk) for three circuits and walked for four. When he finished, he went to the Station of Ibrahim and prayed two rak'ahs behind it, then recited: ﴿And take the Station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer﴾.

Ibn Jarir said: Yusuf ibn Salman narrated to us, Hatim ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from his father, from Jabir, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ touched the Corner (al-Rukn), then performed the ramal for three circuits and walked for four. Then he advanced to the Station of Ibrahim and recited: ﴿And take the Station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer﴾, and he made the Station between himself and the House, and prayed two rak'ahs."

This is a portion of the long hadith which Muslim narrated in his Sahih, from the hadith of Hatim ibn Isma'il [[Tafsir al-Tabari (3/36) and Sahih Muslim no. (1218).]].

Al-Bukhari narrated with his chain, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, who said: "I heard Ibn 'Umar say: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived, circumambulated the House seven times, and prayed two rak'ahs behind the Station.'" [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (395, 1793).]].

All of this indicates that what is meant by the Station (al-Maqam) is only the stone upon which Ibrahim, peace be upon him, used to stand to build the Ka'bah. When the wall rose, Isma'il, peace be upon him, brought it to him so that he could stand upon it, and he would hand him the stones, and he would place them with his own hand to raise the wall. Whenever he completed one side, he moved to the next side, circling around the Ka'bah while standing on it, and each time he finished one wall he moved it to the adjacent side in this manner, until the walls of the Ka'bah were completed, as its account will come in the story of Ibrahim and Isma'il in the building of the House, from the narration of Ibn 'Abbas in al-Bukhari. The marks of his two feet were clearly visible in it, and this remained known, recognized by the Arabs in their pre-Islamic era. For this reason Abu Talib said in his well-known Lamiyyah ode:

"And the footprint of Ibrahim on the rock was soft, upon his two feet, barefoot, without sandals."

[[The verse is in al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (1/273).]]

The Muslims also witnessed those marks in it. 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb said: Yunus ibn Yazid informed me, from Ibn Shihab, that Anas ibn Malik narrated to them, saying: "I saw the Station, and in it were the marks of his fingers, peace be upon him, and the hollow of his two feet, except that the wiping of people with their hands had erased it."

Ibn Jarir said: Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding: ﴿And take the Station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer﴾: "They were only commanded to pray beside it, and they were not commanded to wipe it. This community has burdened itself with something that the nations before it did not burden themselves with. We have been told of one who saw the trace of his heel and his fingers in it, and this community continued to wipe it until it wore away and was effaced."

I say: The Station was formerly attached to the wall of the Ka'bah, and its place is known today beside the door, on the side of the Black Stone, to the right of one who enters through the door, in the separate enclosure there. When al-Khalil, peace be upon him, finished building the House, he placed it against the wall of the Ka'bah, or the construction reached it and he left it there. For this reason – and Allah knows best – he was commanded to pray there at the conclusion of the circumambulation, and it was fitting that it be at the Station of Ibrahim, where the building of the Ka'bah ended. What moved it away from the wall of the Ka'bah was the Commander of the Faithful 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him [[In J: "may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him."]], [and he] [[Addition from J.]] is one of the rightly guided Imams and rightly guided Caliphs, whom we have been commanded to follow, and he is one of the two men concerning whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Follow the two after me, Abu Bakr and 'Umar." And he is the one whose agreement the Qur'an descended to confirm regarding prayer at it. For this reason none of the Companions denied that, may Allah be pleased with them all.

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ibn Jurayj: "'Ata' and others among our companions narrated to me, saying: 'The first to move it was 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him'" [[al-Musannaf of 'Abd al-Razzaq no. (8955).]]. 'Abd al-Razzaq also said, from Ma'mar, from Humayd al-A'raj, from Mujahid: "The first to move the Station to its present place was 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him" [[al-Musannaf of 'Abd al-Razzaq no. (8953).]].

The Hafiz Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Bayhaqi [[In A and W: "'Ali ibn al-Husayn."]] said: Abu [al-Husayn ibn] [[Addition from J, T, A, W.]] al-Fadl al-Qattan informed us, the Qadi Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Kamil informed us, Abu Isma'il Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Sulami narrated to us, Abu Thabit narrated to us, al-Darawardi narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her: "The Station, in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the time of Abu Bakr, was attached to the House. Then 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, moved it back." This chain is sound, together with what preceded it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Umar al-'Adani narrated to us, saying: Sufyan [i.e., Ibn 'Uyaynah] [[Addition from J, T, A, W.]], who was the Imam of the Meccans in his time, said: "The Station was in the vicinity of the House in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and 'Umar moved it to its place after the Prophet ﷺ and after the statement: ﴿And take the Station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer﴾." He said: "The flood carried it away after 'Umar moved it from this place, so 'Umar returned it to it."

Sufyan also said: "I do not know how far it was from the Ka'bah before its relocation." Sufyan said: "I do not know whether it was adjoining it or not?" [[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/372).]].

These reports support one another in what we have mentioned, and Allah knows best.

The Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Abu 'Amr narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, Adam narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Mujahid, who said: "'Umar said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what if we prayed behind the Station?' So Allah revealed: ﴿And take the Station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer﴾. The Station was near the House, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ moved it to this place." Mujahid said: "'Umar used to hold an opinion, and the Qur'an would descend in accordance with it" [[The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari (8/169): "Its chain is weak."]].

This is a mursal (a report in which a Successor cites the Prophet ﷺ directly, omitting the Companion) from Mujahid, and it contradicts what preceded from the narration of 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Humayd al-A'raj, from Mujahid, that the first to move the Station to its present place was 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him. This is more authentic than the route of Ibn Mardawayh, with this being supported by what preceded it, and Allah knows best [[Shaykh Muhammad ibn Ibrahim Al al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, wrote two treatises concerning the Station: the first, on the permissibility of moving the Station, titled "al-Jawab al-Mustaqim fi Jawaz Naql Maqam Ibrahim," published within his fatawa (5/17–55). The second, in refutation of Shaykh Sulayman ibn Hamdan's objection to the treatise of Shaykh 'Abd al-Rahman al-Mu'allimi on the permissibility of moving the Station, titled "Nasihat al-Ikhwan bi-Bayan Ba'd ma fi Naqd al-Mabani li-Ibn Hamdan min al-Khabt wa al-Jahl wa al-Buhtan," published within his fatawa (5/56–132). These are two valuable treatises in which he, may Allah have mercy on him, gathered the evidence for the permissibility of moving the Station, citing the words of the Hafiz Ibn Kathir here and the words of the Hafiz Ibn Hajar in Fath al-Bari. They demonstrate his mastery and breadth of knowledge, may Allah have mercy on him and house him in the expansive gardens of Paradise.]].

* *

al-Hasan al-Basri said regarding His saying: ﴿And We charged Ibrahim and Isma'il﴾: "Allah commanded them to purify it from filth and impurity, so that nothing of that would touch it."

Ibn Jurayj said: "I asked 'Ata': 'What is 'ahd (charge)?' He said: 'Its command.'"

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said regarding ﴿And We charged Ibrahim﴾: "That is: We commanded him." Thus he said. And it is apparent that this verb was construed with "ila" (to) because it carries the meaning of "We had enjoined" and "We had revealed."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿That purify My House for those who circle it and those who stay devoutly in it﴾: "From idols."

Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said regarding ﴿Purify My House for those who circle it﴾: "That is from idols, obscenity, false speech, and filth."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was narrated from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, Abu al-'Aliyah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, 'Ata' and Qatadah regarding ﴿That you purify My House﴾: "That is: by 'There is no god but Allah,' from polytheism."

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿for those who circle it﴾, circumambulation of the House is well known. And it is narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he said regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿for those who circle it﴾: "That is, those who come to it from afar. ﴿And those who stay devoutly in it﴾ are those who reside in it." Likewise it is narrated from Qatadah and al-Rabi' ibn Anas that they both interpreted "those who stay devoutly" as its residents who dwell in it, just as Sa'id ibn Jubayr said.

Yahya al-Qattan [ibn] [[Addition from A.]] said, from 'Abd al-Malik, who is Ibn Abi Sulayman, from 'Ata' regarding His saying: ﴿and those who stay devoutly﴾: "Those who come to it from the cities and then stay with it." And he said to us, while we were residing there: "You are among those who stay devoutly."

Waki' said, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "If he is sitting, then he is among those who stay devoutly."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Thabit narrated to us, who said: We said to Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr: "I think I shall only speak to the Amir about preventing those who sleep in the Sacred Mosque, for they become impure (junub) and break wind." He said: "Do not do that, for Ibn Umar was asked about them and said: 'They are the ones who remain in seclusion (al-'Akifun).'"
[And Abd ibn Humayd narrated it from Sulayman ibn Harb, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same wording.]

I say: It is established in the Sahih that Ibn Umar used to sleep in the Mosque of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) while he was unmarried.
[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 440.]

As for God's words, ﴿and those who bow and prostrate﴾, Waki' said, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from Ata', from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿and those who bow and prostrate﴾: "If he is praying, then he is among those who bow and prostrate." Ata' and Qatadah also said the same.

Ibn Jarir (may God have mercy on him) said: The meaning of the verse is: "And We commanded Ibrahim and Isma'il to purify My House for those who circumambulate." The purification they were commanded to carry out in the House is its purification from idols, the worship of idols in it, and from polytheism. Then he raised a question, saying: "If it is said: Was there before Ibrahim's building near the House any of that which he was commanded to purify it from?" He answered with two points:

The first: He commanded them to purify it from the idols and images that were worshipped near it in the time of the people of Nuh, so that this would be a precedent for those who came after them, since God, exalted is He, had made Ibrahim an imam to be followed. As 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said regarding ﴿that you purify My House﴾: "From the idols that they worship, which the polytheists used to venerate."

I say: This answer is based on the premise that idols were worshipped near it before Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and establishing this requires evidence from the infallible one, Muhammad (ﷺ).

The second answer: He commanded them to make its construction sincerely for God alone, with no partner, so that they would build it purified from polytheism and doubt. As His glorified praise says: ﴿Is he who founded his building upon piety from God and His good pleasure better, or he who founded his building upon the edge of a crumbling cliff that collapsed with him into the fire of Hell?﴾ [al-Tawbah: 109]. He said: Likewise His words: ﴿And We charged Ibrahim and Isma'il that they purify My House﴾ mean: "Build My House upon purity from associating others with Me and from doubt." As al-Suddi said regarding ﴿that you purify My House﴾: "Build My House for those who circumambulate."

The summary of this answer is that God, exalted is He, commanded Ibrahim and Isma'il (peace be upon them both) to build the Ka'bah for His name alone, with no partner, for those who circumambulate it in worship, those who remain in seclusion near it, and those who pray facing it, among those who bow and prostrate. As God, exalted is He, says: ﴿And when We settled Ibrahim in the place of the House, [saying]: Do not associate anything with Me, and purify My House for those who circumambulate and those who stand (in prayer) and those who bow and prostrate...﴾ [al-Hajj: 26-37, the verses continuing].

[The jurists have differed over which is better: prayer at the House or circumambulation? Malik said: circumambulating it is better than praying near it for the people of the cities. The majority said: prayer is better absolutely. The reasoning of each is mentioned in the Kitab al-Ahkam.]

The purpose of all this is to refute the polytheists who associated others with God near His House, which was founded on the worship of Him alone with no partner, and yet they barred its believing people from it, as God says: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and bar [others] from the way of God and from the Sacred Mosque, which We made [a place of] equality for the people, the resident therein and the visitor, and whoever intends therein deviation by wrongdoing – We will make him taste a painful punishment﴾ [al-Hajj: 25].

Then he mentioned that the House was only founded for the one who worships God alone with no partner, whether by circumambulation or by prayer. In Surat al-Hajj he mentioned its three parts: its standing, its bowing and its prostration, and he did not mention those in seclusion, because it has already been stated: ﴿the resident therein and the visitor being equal﴾. In this noble verse he mentioned those who circumambulate and those who remain in seclusion, and he suffices with mentioning bowing and prostration instead of standing, because it is known that there is no bowing or prostration except after standing.

In this there is also a refutation of those of the People of the Book who do not perform pilgrimage to it, namely the Jews and the Christians, for they believe in the virtue and greatness of Ibrahim, the Friend (al-Khalil), and they know that he built this House for circumambulation during Hajj and 'Umrah and other than that, and for seclusion and prayer near it. Yet they do none of that, so how can they be following the Friend when they do not do what God prescribed for him? Musa ibn 'Imran and other prophets (peace be upon them) performed Hajj to the House, as the Infallible One who does not speak from desire has informed us: ﴿It is not but a revelation revealed﴾ [al-Najm: 4].

The sense of the discourse, then, is: ﴿And We charged Ibrahim and Isma'il﴾ [i.e., We conveyed Our revelation to Ibrahim and Isma'il] ﴿that you purify My House for those who circumambulate, and those who remain in seclusion, and those who bow and prostrate﴾, i.e., purify it from polytheism and doubt, build it sincerely for God, and make it a refuge for those who circumambulate, those who remain in seclusion, and those who bow and prostrate. The purification of mosques is derived from this verse, and from His words: ﴿In houses which God has permitted to be raised and within which His name is mentioned; therein glorify Him in the mornings and the evenings﴾ [al-Nur: 36], and from the Sunnah through many hadiths, including the command to purify and perfume them and to keep them free from harm and impurities and what is similar to that. For this reason he (peace be upon him) said: "Mosques were only built for what they were built for." [Muslim in his Sahih, no. 569, from the hadith of Buraydah (may God be pleased with him).] I have compiled a separate treatise on this, and all praise and grace are due to God.

There has been disagreement about who first built the Ka'bah. It was said: the angels, before Adam. This was narrated from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn. Al-Qurtubi mentioned it and quoted its wording, and it is strange. It was also said: Adam (peace be upon him). Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ibn Juraij, from Ata' and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and others, that Adam built it from five mountains: Hira', Tur Sinai, Tur Zaita, the mountain of Lebanon, and al-Judi. This is also strange. Something similar was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Ka'b al-Ahbar, Qatadah, and from Wahb ibn Munabbih: that the first to build it was Shith (Seth), peace be upon him. Most of those who mention this take it from the books of the People of the Book, and these are of the kind that are neither believed nor denied, and one should not rely upon them alone. As for when a hadith is authentically established on this matter, then it is to be accepted with full submission.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verses 126–128 (part 1 of 7):

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And when Abraham said, "My Lord, make this a secure city and provide its people with fruits, those of them who believe in Allah and the Last Day"﴾.

The Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Abraham made the House of Allah sacred and granted it security, and I have made Medina sacred between its two lava plains (al-labatayn), so its game shall not be hunted and its 'idah (thorny trees) shall not be cut." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (3/48). Al-labatan are the two volcanic plains on either side of Medina. Al-'idah is every large tree that has thorns; it is also said to be any large tree in general.]]

Al-Nasa'i narrated it likewise, from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, from Bundar, with the same chain. [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 4284.]]

Muslim also narrated it, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Amr al-Naqid, both from Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri, from Sufyan al-Thawri. [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1362.]]

Ibn Jarir also said: Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us; and Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abd al-Rahim al-Razi narrated to us, both of them together saying: We heard Ash'ath, from Nafi', from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Abraham was the servant of Allah and His friend (khalil), and I am the servant of Allah and His Messenger. Abraham made Mecca sacred, and I have made Medina sacred between its two lava plains, its 'idah and its game. No weapon for fighting shall be carried in it, and no tree in it shall be cut except for the fodder of a camel." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (3/48).]]

This chain is unusual (gharib); it is not found in any of the Six Books (al-Kutub al-Sittah, the six canonical collections of hadith). The original version of the hadith is in Sahih Muslim through another route, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When people saw the first of the fruit, they would bring it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When he took it, he would say: "O Allah, bless for us our fruit, bless for us our city, bless for us our sa' (measure) and bless for us our mudd (measure). O Allah, indeed Abraham was Your servant, Your friend and Your prophet, and I am Your servant and Your prophet. He supplicated You for Mecca, and I supplicate You for Medina with the like of what he supplicated You for Mecca, and with its like besides it." Then he would give it to the youngest child present. In another wording: "a blessing added to a blessing," and then he would give it to the youngest of the children present. This is the wording of Muslim. [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1373.]]

Then Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Bukayr ibn Mudar narrated to us, from Ibn al-Had, from Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn Uthman, from Rafi' ibn Khadij, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Abraham made Mecca sacred, and I make sacred what lies between its two lava plains."

Muslim alone narrated it, from Qutaybah, from Bukayr ibn Mudar, with the same chain, and its wording is the same as the above. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (3/49).]]

In the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim), from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abu Talhah: "Look for a boy from among your young men to serve me." Abu Talhah set out with me, carrying me behind him on his mount, and I would serve the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) whenever he dismounted. In the hadith he also said: Then he came on until Uhud appeared to him, and he said: "This is a mountain that loves us and we love it." When he came in sight of Medina, he said: "O Allah, I make sacred what lies between its two mountains, just as Abraham made Mecca sacred. O Allah, bless them in their mudd and their sa'." In another wording of the two: "O Allah, bless them in their measure, bless them in their sa', and bless them in their mudd." Al-Bukhari added: meaning the people of Medina. [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1361.]]

Also in the two Sahihs, from Anas: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, make in Medina double the blessing You placed in Mecca." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1885; Sahih Muslim, no. 1369.]]

And from Abd Allah ibn Zayd ibn Asim, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed Abraham made Mecca sacred and supplicated for it, and I have made Medina sacred as Abraham made Mecca sacred, and I have supplicated for it concerning its mudd and its sa' with the like of what Abraham supplicated for Mecca." Narrated by al-Bukhari, and this is his wording [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2129]], and by Muslim, whose wording is: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Abraham made Mecca sacred and supplicated for its people. And I have made Medina sacred as Abraham made Mecca sacred, and I have supplicated for it concerning its sa' and its mudd with the like of what Abraham supplicated for the people of Mecca." [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1360.]]

And from Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "O Allah, indeed Abraham made Mecca sacred and made it a sanctuary, and I have made Medina a sanctuary between its two harrah (rocky tracts), where no blood is shed, no weapon for fighting is carried, and no tree is stripped of its leaves except for fodder. O Allah, bless for us our city. O Allah, bless for us our sa'. O Allah, bless for us our mudd. O Allah, make with the blessing two blessings." The hadith was narrated by Muslim. [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1374.]]

The hadiths concerning the sanctity of Medina are numerous, and we have cited only those related to Abraham's making Mecca sacred, because of their correspondence with the noble verse.

[Those who hold that the sanctity of Mecca was established only through the words of Abraham the Friend (al-Khalil) relied on these. It has also been said that it has been sacred since it was created together with the earth, and this is more apparent and stronger.] [[Addition from manuscripts ج, ط, أ.]]

Other hadiths have also come which indicate that Allah the Exalted made Mecca sacred before He created the heavens and the earth, as came in the two Sahihs, from Abd Allah ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said on the day of the Conquest of Mecca: "Indeed this city, Allah made it sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred by the sanctity of Allah until the Day of Resurrection. Fighting in it was not permitted to anyone before me, and it was permitted to me only for an hour of the day. So it is sacred by the sanctity of Allah until the Day of Resurrection. Its thorny trees shall not be cut, its game shall not be frightened, its lost property shall not be picked up except by one who announces it, and its grass shall not be cut." Al-Abbas said: "O Messenger of Allah, except the idhkhir, for it is for their smiths and their houses." He said: "Except the idhkhir." This is the wording of Muslim. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 1834, 1587, 3189, 3077; Sahih Muslim, no. 1353.]]

Both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) also narrated something similar from Abu Hurayrah. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 112, 6880; Sahih Muslim, no. 1355.]]

Then al-Bukhari said after that: Aban ibn Salih said, from al-Hasan ibn Muslim, from Safiyyah bint Shaybah: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ), the like of it. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1349.]]

This which al-Bukhari cited without a full chain (mu'allaq) was narrated by the Imam Abu Abd Allah ibn Majah, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Numayr, from Yunus ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Aban ibn Salih, from al-Hasan ibn Muslim ibn Yannaq, from Safiyyah bint Shaybah, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) delivering a sermon in the year of the Conquest, and he said: "O people, indeed Allah made Mecca sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred until the Day of Resurrection. Its trees shall not be cut and its game shall not be frightened, and no one shall pick up its lost property except one who announces it." Al-Abbas said: "Except the idhkhir, for it is for the houses and the graves." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Except the idhkhir." [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3109.]]

And from Abu Shurayh al-'Adawi, that he said to Amr ibn Sa'id, while he was sending armies to Mecca: "Permit me, O Amir, to relate to you a statement which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made on the day after the Conquest. My ears heard it, my heart understood it, and my eyes saw him when he said it. He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'Indeed Mecca was made sacred by Allah and not made sacred by people. So it is not lawful for a person who believes in Allah and the Last Day to shed blood in it, or to cut a tree in it. If anyone takes a concession to fight in it by the fighting of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), say: Indeed Allah permitted His Messenger (ﷺ) but did not permit you. He permitted me only for an hour of a day, and its sanctity has returned today as it was yesterday. So let the one present convey it to the absent.'" It was said to Abu Shurayh: "What did Amr say to you?" He said: "I know that better than you, O Abu Shurayh. Indeed the sanctuary does not protect a disobedient person, nor a fugitive who has shed blood, nor a fugitive who has committed theft (kharbah)." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1832; Sahih Muslim, no. 1354.]] Narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim, and this is his wording.

Given this, there is no contradiction between these hadiths which indicate that Allah made Mecca sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth, and the hadiths which indicate that Abraham made it sacred. This is because Abraham conveyed from Allah His ruling concerning it and His prohibition of it, and it had remained a sacred city with Allah before Abraham built it, just as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was recorded with Allah as the Seal of the Prophets while Adam was still between water and clay. Despite this, Abraham (peace be upon him) said: ﴿Our Lord, and send among them a Messenger from among them﴾, and Allah answered his supplication with what had preceded in His knowledge and decree. For this reason it came in a hadith that they said: "O Messenger of Allah, inform us about the beginning of your affair." He said: "The supplication of my father Abraham, and the good news of Jesus son of Mary, and my mother saw that there came forth from her a light by which the palaces of Syria were illuminated."

That is: Inform us about the beginning of the manifestation of your affair, as will come shortly, Allah willing.

As for the question of whether Mecca is superior to Medina, as is the view of the majority (al-Jumhur), or Medina is superior to Mecca, as is the position of Malik and his followers, it will be mentioned in another place with its evidences, Allah willing, and in Him is trust.

* *

His words, the Exalted, reporting about the Friend (Abraham) that he said: ﴿My Lord, make this a secure city﴾. That is: secure from fear, so that its people are not terrified. Allah did this both by law (shar') and by decree (qadar). Like His saying the Exalted: ﴿And whoever enters it is secure﴾ [Al 'Imran: 97], and His saying: ﴿Have they not seen that We have made a sanctuary secure while people are snatched away from around them?﴾ [Al-'Ankabut: 67], and other verses. The hadiths on the prohibition of fighting in it have already passed. In Sahih Muslim, from Jabir: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "It is not lawful for anyone to carry a weapon in Mecca." [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1356.]] He said in this surah: ﴿My Lord, make this a secure city﴾, meaning: make this plot of land a secure city. This fits, because it was before the building of the Ka'bah. He said in the surah of Abraham: ﴿And when Abraham said, "My Lord, make this city secure"﴾ [Ibrahim: 35], and this fits there because it was, and Allah knows best, as if it occurred as a second supplication (du'a' marrah thaniyah) after the building of the House and the settling of its people in it, and after the birth of Isaac, who was thirteen years younger than Ishmael. For this reason He said at the end of the supplication: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who has given me in old age Ishmael and Isaac. Indeed my Lord is the Hearer of supplication﴾ [Ibrahim: 39].

* *

His words, the Exalted: ﴿and provide its people with fruits, those of them who believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾. He said: ﴿And whoever disbelieves, I will grant him enjoyment for a little, then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination﴾.

Abu Ja'far al-Razi related from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "He said: 'And whoever disbelieves, I will let him enjoy [himself] briefly, then I will compel him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination'" [Qur'an 2:126]. He said: "This is the statement of Allah the Exalted." This is also the view of Mujahid and 'Ikrimah, and it is what Ibn Jarir (may Allah have mercy on him) favored. He said: "Others recited: '[He] said: And whoever disbelieves, I will let him enjoy [himself] briefly, then I will compel him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination,' and they made this part of Ibrahim's supplication," as Abu Ja'far related from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: "Ibn 'Abbas used to say: 'That is the statement of Ibrahim, asking his Lord that whoever disbelieves, He should let him enjoy [himself] briefly.'"

Abu Ja'far also related from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Mujahid, regarding: "And whoever disbelieves, I will let him enjoy [himself] briefly," that he said: "And whoever disbelieves, I will also provide for him. Then I will compel him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: When Ibrahim, peace be upon him, withdrew the call from those whom Allah refused to grant him authority over, in devotion to Allah and His love and separation from those who opposed His command, even if they were of his offspring, when he knew from Allah's informing him of it that they would be wrongdoers and that his covenant would not reach them, Allah said: "And whoever disbelieves, I will provide for the pious and the wicked alike, and I will let him enjoy [himself] briefly."

Hatim ibn Isma'il related from Humayd al-Kharrat, from 'Ammar al-Duhni, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning the words of Allah the Exalted: "My Lord, make this a secure city and provide its people with fruits, those of them who believe in Allah and the Last Day" [Qur'an 2:126]. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Ibrahim used to restrict it to the believers, to the exclusion of the people. So Allah revealed: 'And whoever disbelieves also—I will provide for them as I provide for the believers. Shall I create a creation that I do not provide for? I will let them enjoy [themselves] briefly, then I will compel them to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination.'" Then Ibn 'Abbas recited: "To each We extend—these and those—from the bounty of your Lord; and the bounty of your Lord is never restricted" [Qur'an 17:20]. Ibn Mardawayh related it. Similar was also narrated from 'Ikrimah and Mujahid. This is like His saying, the Exalted: "Indeed, those who fabricate lies against Allah will not succeed. [It is] an enjoyment in this world; then to Us is their return; then We will make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve" [Qur'an 10:69–70]; and His saying: "And whoever disbelieves, let not his disbelief grieve you. To Us is their return, and We will inform them of what they did. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts. We let them enjoy [themselves] briefly; then We will compel them to a harsh punishment" [Qur'an 31:23–24]; and His saying: "And if not that the people would be one community, We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful silver ceilings for their houses and stairways [of silver] on which they could ascend, and for their houses doors and couches on which they could recline, and ornaments of gold. But all of that is nothing but the enjoyment of the worldly life. And the Hereafter with your Lord is for the righteous" [Qur'an 43:33–35].

* *

As for His saying, "then I will compel him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination": that is, "then I will force him, after his enjoyment in this world and after We have spread over him of its shade, to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination." Its meaning is that Allah, the Exalted, gives them respite and grants them time, then seizes them with the seizure of the Mighty, the Omnipotent, as in His saying: "And how many a city have I granted respite while it was wrongdoing; then I seized it, and to Me is the [final] destination" [Qur'an 22:48]. In the two Sahihs: "No one is more patient with harm he hears than Allah; they attribute to Him a son, yet He provides for them and grants them well-being." [[The tradition was cited earlier.]] Also in the Sahih: "Indeed Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer until, when He seizes him, He does not release him." Then he recited His saying: "And thus is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are wrongdoing. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe" [Qur'an 11:102]. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4686, and Sahih Muslim, no. 2583, from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

As for His saying, "And [mention] when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House and Isma'il [, saying], 'Our Lord, accept [this] from us. Indeed You are the Hearing, the Knowing. Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. And show us our rites and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful'" [Qur'an 2:127–128]:

"Al-qawa'id" is the plural of "qa'idah," which means the pillars and the foundations. Allah the Exalted says: Mention, O Muhammad, to your people the building of Ibrahim and Isma'il, upon them both be peace, of the House, and their raising its foundations, while they were saying: "Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed You are the Hearing, the Knowing." They were engaged in righteous deed while asking Allah, the Exalted, to accept it from them, as Ibn Abi Hatim related through the hadith of Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Khunays al-Makki, from Wuhayb ibn al-Ward, that he recited: "And [mention] when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House and Isma'il, [saying], 'Our Lord, accept from us,'" and then he would weep and say: "O Khalil of the Most Merciful, you raise the pillars of the House of the Most Merciful while you are apprehensive that it will not be accepted from you." This is like what Allah, the Exalted, related about the state of the sincere believers in His saying: "And those who give what they give [of charity]" [Qur'an 23:60], that is, they give what they have given of charities, expenditures and acts of devotion, "while their hearts are fearful" [Qur'an 23:60], that is, fearful that it will not be accepted from them. As the authentic hadith from 'Aishah from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has it, as will come in its place.

Some of the exegetes said: The one who raised the foundations was Ibrahim, and the one who supplicated was Isma'il. The correct view is that both of them were raising and both were saying, as its explanation will come.

Al-Bukhari has related here a hadith which we will cite, then follow it with narrations related to it. Al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq related to us, Ma'mar related to us, from Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani and Kathir ibn Kathir ibn al-Muttalib ibn Abi Wada'ah (one of them exceeding the other in narration), from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "The first who used a waistband [mintaq] among women was the mother of Isma'il, upon them both be peace. She made a waistband so as to conceal her traces from Sarah. Then Ibrahim brought her and her son Isma'il, upon them both be peace, while she was nursing him, until he placed them by the House, beside a tree above Zamzam in the upper part of the mosque. At that time there was no one in Makkah, and there was no water there. So he placed them there, and placed beside them a leather bag containing dates and a waterskin containing water. Then Ibrahim, peace be upon him, turned back, departing. Isma'il's mother followed him and said: 'O Ibrahim, where are you going, leaving us in this valley in which there is no person and nothing?' She said this to him repeatedly, but he did not turn toward her. She said: 'Has Allah commanded you to do this?' He said: 'Yes.' She said: 'Then He will not let us be lost.' Then she returned. So Ibrahim, peace be upon him, went on until, when he was at the mountain pass where they could not see him, he faced the House, raised his hands, and supplicated with these supplications, saying: 'Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your Sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make hearts among the people incline toward them and provide for them from the fruits that they may be grateful' [Qur'an 14:37]. Isma'il's mother kept nursing Isma'il and drinking from that water, until the water in the waterskin was exhausted, and she and her son became thirsty. She began looking at him writhing—or he said: thrashing—so she departed, disliking to look at him. She found that Safa was the nearest mountain to her on the earth, so she stood upon it, then faced the valley, looking to see whether she could see anyone. She did not see anyone. She descended from Safa, until when she reached the valley, she lifted the edge of her garment and ran with the effort of an exhausted person until she crossed the valley. Then she came to Marwah, stood upon it, and looked to see whether she could see anyone. She did not see anyone. She did this seven times." Ibn 'Abbas said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "For this reason the people run between them."

When she ascended Marwah, she heard a voice and said: "Be quiet," wanting to hear herself; then she listened and heard it again. She said: "You have made me hear; if you have any help, then [help me]." Suddenly there was an angel at the place of Zamzam, who dug with his heel—or he said: with his wing—until water appeared. She began making a basin for it, saying with her hand thus, and she began scooping water into her waterskin while it gushed forth after she scooped. Ibn 'Abbas said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "May Allah have mercy on the mother of Isma'il. Had she left Zamzam—or he said: had she not scooped from the water—Zamzam would have been a flowing spring."

He said: So she drank and nursed her child. The angel said to her: "Do not fear neglect, for indeed here is the House of Allah, which this boy and his father will build, and indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, does not neglect His people." The House was raised above the ground like a mound, and the floods would come and divert from its right and left. It remained so until a caravan of Jurhum—or a household of Jurhum—passed by them, coming from the route of Kada'. They stopped at the lower part of Makkah, and they saw a bird circling, so they said: "This bird is surely circling over water, for we know this valley and there is no water in it." So they sent a scout or two scouts, who found the water. They returned and informed them of the water, so they came. He said: Isma'il's mother was at the water. They said: "Will you permit us to settle near you?" She said: "Yes, but you have no right to the water." They said: "Yes."

Ibn Abbas [in some editions: "Abdullah ibn Abbas"] said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Umm Ismail found that [the water] and she loved company. So they settled, and they sent for their families, and they came to settle with them. When some households of them had settled there, the boy grew up and learned Arabic from them, and they admired him and liked him as he grew up. When he reached [maturity] they married him to a woman from among them. Umm Ismail died, peace be upon them both. Then Ibrahim came, after Ismail had married, to check on his property. He did not find Ismail, so he asked his wife about him. She said: 'He went out to seek [food] for us.' Then he asked her about their livelihood and their condition, and she said: 'We are in a bad state, we are in hardship and distress,' and she complained to him. He said: 'When your husband comes, convey greetings to him and tell him: change the threshold of his door.' When Ismail, peace be upon him, came, it was as if he sensed something. He said: 'Has anyone come to you?' She said: 'Yes, an old man like so-and-so came, and he asked about you, and I informed him. He also asked me how our living was, and I told him that we are in hardship and distress.' He said: 'Did he advise you of anything?' She said: 'Yes, he commanded me to convey his greetings to you, and he says: change the threshold of your door.' He said: 'That was my father, and he has commanded me to part from you, so return to your family.' So he divorced her and married another woman from among them. Ibrahim stayed away from them for as long as Allah willed, then he came to them again but did not find him. He entered upon his wife and asked her about him, and she said: 'He went out to seek [food] for us.' He said: 'How are you?' and he asked her about their livelihood and condition. She said: 'We are well and in abundance,' and she praised Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. He said: 'What is your food?' She said: 'Meat.' He said: 'What is your drink?' She said: 'Water.' He said: 'O Allah, bless them in their meat and their water.'"

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There was no grain for them at that time, and if they had had any, he would have supplicated for them in it. He said: 'No one lives in those two [places] except in Makkah except that they will not agree with him.'" He said: "When your husband comes, convey greetings to him, and order him to make firm the threshold of his door." When Ismail, peace be upon him, came, he said: "Has anyone come to you?" She said: "Yes, an old man of good appearance came to us, and she praised him. He asked me about you, and I informed him, and he asked me: 'How is our living?' and I told him that we are well." He said: "Did he advise you of anything?" She said: "Yes, he sends his greetings to you and commands you to make firm the threshold of your door." He said: "That was my father, and you are the threshold; he commanded me to keep you." Then he stayed away from them for as long as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, willed. Then he came after that while Ismail was shaping arrows beneath a tree near Zamzam. When he saw him, he stood up to him, and they did as a child does with a parent and a parent does with a child. Then he said: "O Ismail, Allah has commanded me with a command." He said: "Do what your Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, has commanded you." He said: "Will you help me?" He said: "I will help you." He said: "Allah has commanded me to build a house here," and he pointed to a high hillock above what surrounded it. He said: "At that, they raised the foundations of the House, and Ismail began to bring the stones while Ibrahim built, until the building rose; he brought this stone and placed it for him, and he stood upon it while he built, and Ismail handed him the stones, and both of them were saying: ﴿Our Lord, accept from us; indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾." He said: "They continued building until they went around the House, and both of them were saying: ﴿Our Lord, accept from us; indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾."

[Abd ibn Humayd narrated it from Abd al-Razzaq with the same wording, in an expanded form.]

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Hammad al-Zahrani, and Ibn Jarir [al-Tabari] narrated it from Ahmad ibn Thabit al-Razi; both from Abd al-Razzaq with the same wording, in abridged form.

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Ismail ibn Ali ibn Ismail narrated to us, Bishr ibn Musa narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Azraqi narrated to us, Muslim ibn Khalid al-Zanji narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Juraij, from Kathir ibn Kathir, who said: I and Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman and Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Husayn were with a group of people with Sa'id ibn Jubayr, in the upper part of the Mosque at night, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Ask me before you no longer see me." They asked him about the Maqam [Station of Ibrahim], and he began to narrate to them from Ibn Abbas, and he related the hadith in full.

Then al-Bukhari said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Abu Amir Abd al-Malik ibn Amr narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Nafi narrated to us, from Kathir ibn Kathir, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When there was between Ibrahim and his family what there was, he set out with Ismail and Umm Ismail, and with them was a waterskin containing water. Umm Ismail began to drink from the waterskin, and her milk flowed for her child, until he came to Makkah and placed her beneath a tree. Then Ibrahim returned to his family, and Umm Ismail followed him, until they reached Kada, and she called to him from behind: "O Ibrahim, to whom are you leaving us?" He said: "To Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." She said: "I am content with Allah." He said: "So she returned, and began to drink from the waterskin, and her milk flowed for her child, until the water ran out. She said: 'If only I went and looked, perhaps I might sense someone.'" He said: "So she went and climbed al-Safa, and looked and looked to see whether she could sense anyone, but she did not sense anyone. When she reached the valley, she ran until she came to al-Marwa, and she did that several times. Then she said: 'If only I went and looked at what he is doing,' meaning the child. So she went and looked, and there he was in the same state, as if he were gasping for death, and her soul was not at ease, so she said: 'If only I went and looked, perhaps I might sense someone.'" He said: "So she went and climbed al-Safa, and looked and looked, but did not sense anyone, until she completed seven [circuits]. Then she said: 'If only I went and looked at what he is doing.' Then she heard a voice, and she said: 'Help, if you have any good!' And there was Jibril, peace be upon him." He said: "He struck with his heel like this, and pressed his heel into the ground." He said: "Water gushed forth, and Umm Ismail was astonished, and began to dig."

He said: Abu al-Qasim (ﷺ) said: "If she had left it, the water would have flowed on the surface."

He said: "So she began to drink from the water, and her milk flowed for her child."

He said: "Then some people of Jurhum passed by the lower part of the valley, and they saw birds, as if they were surprised by that, and they said: 'Birds only gather over water.' So they sent their messenger, who looked and found water. He came to them and informed them. So they came to her and said: 'O Umm Ismail, will you permit us to be with you, and settle with you?' Her son grew up and married a woman from among them."

He said: "Then it occurred to Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and he said to his family: 'I will check on my property.' He came and greeted [them], and said: 'Where is Ismail?' His wife said: 'He has gone hunting.' He said: 'Tell him when he comes: change the threshold of your house.' When he came, she informed him, and he said: 'You are that [threshold]; go back to your family.'"

He said: "Then it occurred to Ibrahim, and he said to his family: 'I will check on my property.' He came and said: 'Where is Ismail?' His wife said: 'He has gone hunting.' She said: 'Will you not dismount and eat and drink?' He said: 'What is your food and what is your drink?' She said: 'Our food is meat, and our drink is water.' He said: 'O Allah, bless them in their food and their drink.'"

He said: Abu al-Qasim (ﷺ) said: "A blessing by the supplication of Ibrahim."

He said: "Then it occurred to Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and he said to his family: 'I will check on my property.' He came and met Ismail behind Zamzam, adjusting his arrows [in another version: adjusting a house of his]. He said: 'O Ismail, your Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, has commanded me to build a house for Him.' He said: 'Obey your Lord, the Mighty and Majestic.' He said: 'He has commanded me that you should help me in it.' He said: 'Then I will do it' or as he said. He said: 'So they both stood up,' and Ibrahim began to build while Ismail handed him the stones, and they were saying: ﴿Our Lord, accept from us; indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾."

He said: "Until the building rose high and the old man became too weak to carry the stones. So he stood upon the Station stone, and began to hand him the stones, and they were saying: ﴿Our Lord, accept from us; indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾."
