Thus did he narrate it from these two routes in the Book of the Prophets [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3365].

It is strange that the Hafiz Abu Abdullah al-Hakim narrated it in his book al-Mustadrak (the "Mustadrak," al-Hakim's collection of hadith he considered to meet the criteria of authenticity not included in the Sahihs), from Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm, from Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz, from Abu Ali Ubayd Allah ibn Abd al-Majid al-Hanafi, from Ibrahim ibn Nafi, with the same [hadith]. He said: "It is sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs [al-Bukhari and Muslim], though they did not record it." So he said. Al-Bukhari has narrated it as you see, from the hadith of Ibrahim ibn Nafi, as though there is an abridgment in it, for he did not mention in it the matter of the sacrifice. It has come in the Sahih that the two horns of the ram were hanging in the Ka'bah. It has also been reported that Ibrahim, peace be upon him, would visit his family in Makkah swiftly on al-Buraq [the mythical steed], then return to his family in the blessed lands. And Allah knows best. The hadith, Allah knows best, contains, as a marfu' report [traced to the Prophet (ﷺ)], only places that Ibn Abbas explicitly attributed to the Prophet (ﷺ).

It has been reported from the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, in this context, something that differs from some of this, as Ibn Jarir said:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both said: Mu'ammal narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Harithah ibn Mudrib, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: When Ibrahim was commanded to build the House, Ismail and Hajar went out with him. He said: When he came to Makkah, he saw over the place of the House something like a cloud, in which there was something like a head. It spoke to him, [saying]: "O Ibrahim, build upon my shadow" — or he said "upon my measure" — "and do not add or subtract." When he built, he left, and left Ismail and Hajar. Hajar said: "O Ibrahim, to whom are you leaving us?" He said: "To Allah." She said: "Go, for He will not waste us." He said: "Ismail became very thirsty." He said: "Hajar climbed al-Safa, looked, and saw nothing; until she reached al-Marwa and saw nothing; then she returned to al-Safa, looked, and saw nothing; until she reached al-Marwa and saw nothing; then she returned to al-Safa, looked, and saw nothing; until she did that seven times." She said: "O Ismail, die where I cannot see you." She came to him while he was scraping the ground with his foot from thirst. Jibril called to her and said: "Who are you?" She said: "I am Hajar, the mother of Ibrahim's son." He said: "To whom did He entrust you both?" She said: "He entrusted us to Allah." He said: "He has entrusted you both to the Sufficient One." He said: "The boy scraped the ground with his finger, and Zamzam gushed forth." She began to hold back the water, and he said: "Leave it, for it is satisfying."

In this narration it is stated that he built the House before he parted from them both. It may be possible, if it is preserved, that he first laid out for it a boundary and marking, not that he built it to its full height until Ismail grew up, and then they built it together, as Allah the Exalted said.

Then Ibn Jarir said: Hannad ibn al-Sarri informed us, Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak, from Khalid ibn 'Ar'arah, that a man stood before Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: "Will you not tell me about the House (al-Bayt)? Is it the first house placed on the earth?" He said: "No. But it is the first house in which blessing was placed, the Station of Ibrahim (Maqam Ibrahim), and whoever enters it is safe. If you wish, I will inform you how it was built. Allah revealed to Ibrahim, 'Build for Me a house on the earth.' Ibrahim was distressed by this, so Allah sent the sakinah (tranquility), which is a wind with a head and two wings, and one of its heads followed the other until it reached Makkah. It coiled over the place of the House like a shield being rolled up, and Ibrahim was commanded to build where the sakinah settled. Ibrahim built, and one stone remained, so the boy went off to seek something. Ibrahim said, 'Bring me a stone as I command you.' The boy set off to find a stone and brought it to him, but he found that Ibrahim had already set the Black Stone (al-Hajar al-Aswad) in its place. He said, 'O father, who brought you this stone?' He replied, 'It was brought to me by one who will not depend on your building; Jibril, peace be upon him, brought it from the heaven.'" So they completed it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Hamad ibn Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Bishr ibn Asim, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Ka'b al-Ahbar, who said: "The House was a foam (ghuthA'ah) upon the water forty years before Allah created the earth, and from it the earth was spread out (duhiyat)."

Sa'id said: Ali ibn Abi Talib narrated to us that Ibrahim came from Armenia (Armeniyyah), and with him was the sakinah guiding him to the settling place of the House, just as the spider settles upon a house. He said: "It uncovered stones that only thirty men could lift." I said: "O Abu Muhammad, Allah says: ﴿And when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House﴾." He said: "That was after."

Al-Suddi said: Allah, mighty and majestic, commanded Ibrahim to build the House, he and Isma'il: "Build My House for those who circumambulate, those who stay in devotion, and those who bow and prostrate." So Ibrahim set out until he came to Makkah. He and Isma'il stood, taking the ma'awil (picks), not knowing where the House was. Allah sent a wind called the wind of al-Khujuj, which had two wings and a head in the form of a serpent. It uncovered for them, around the Ka'bah, the foundations of the first House, and they followed it with the picks, digging until they laid the foundation. This is when Allah, exalted, says: ﴿And when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House﴾ ﴿And when We settled for Ibrahim the place of the House﴾ [al-Hajj: 26]. When they had built the foundations and reached the place of the corner (rukn), Ibrahim said to Isma'il: "O my son, seek for me a good stone that I may place here." He said: "O father, I am lazy and exhausted." He said: "Do it for me." So he set out seeking a stone for him, and brought him a stone, but he did not accept it. He said: "Bring me a stone better than this." So he set out seeking another stone, and Jibril brought him the Black Stone from India. It had been white, a white ruby like the thaghamah (white flower), and Adam had brought it down from Paradise, but it turned black from the sins of the people. Isma'il brought him a stone and found the (Black Stone) already at the corner, so he said: "O father, who brought you this?" He said: "One brought it who is more energetic than you." Then they built, while supplicating with the words through which Ibrahim was tested by his Lord, and he said: ﴿Our Lord, accept from us; indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾.

In this context there is an indication that the foundations of the House were already built before Ibrahim, and that Ibrahim was only guided to them and settled there. Some scholars have held this view, as Imam Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿And when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House﴾: "The foundations were those that had been the foundations of the House before that."

Abd al-Razzaq also said: Hisham ibn Hassan informed us, from Sawwar, the son-in-law of Ata, from Ata ibn Abi Rabah, who said: "When Allah sent Adam down from Paradise, his feet were on the earth and his head was in the heaven, hearing the speech and supplications of the people of heaven, and he was at ease with them. The angels feared him until they complained to Allah about their supplication and their prayer. So Allah lowered him to the earth. When he lost what he used to hear from them, he became lonely, until he complained of that to Allah in his supplication and his prayer. He was directed to Makkah. The place of his step became a town, and his stride became a desert, until he reached Makkah. Allah sent down a ruby from the rubies of Paradise, and it was placed on the site of the House now. He continued to circumambulate it until Allah sent the Flood, and that ruby was lifted up, until Allah raised Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and he built it." And this is the statement of Allah, exalted: ﴿And when We settled for Ibrahim the place of the House﴾ [al-Hajj: 26].

Abd al-Razzaq also said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, from Ata, who said: Adam said: "I no longer hear the voices of the angels?!" He said: "Because of your sin. But descend to the earth and build for Me a house, then circumambulate it, just as you saw the angels circumambulating My House which is in the heaven." People claim that he built it from five mountains: from Hira', Tur Zayta, Tur Sinai, Mount Lebanon, and al-Judi. Its foundation was from Hira'. This was the building of Adam until Ibrahim, peace be upon him, rebuilt it after him.

And this is sound up to Ata, but there is some objectionable (nakarah) element in part of it, and Allah knows best.

Abd al-Razzaq also said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, who said: "Allah placed the House with Adam when Allah sent Adam down to the earth. His descent was in the land of India. His head was in the heaven and his feet were on the earth, and the angels feared him. He was reduced to sixty cubits. Adam grieved because he had lost the voices of the angels and their glorification. He complained of that to Allah, mighty and majestic, and Allah said: 'O Adam, I have sent down for you a house that you will circumambulate, just as the throne of Mine is circumambulated, and you will pray beside it as the throne of Mine is prayed beside.' So Adam set out toward it, and he was given extension in his stride, so that between every two steps there was a desert. That desert remained after that. Adam came to the House and circumambulated it, and those prophets after him did likewise."

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us (in another version: Abu Humayd narrated to us), Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Hafs ibn Humayd, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Allah placed the House upon the pillars of the water, on four pillars, two thousand years before the world was created. Then the earth was spread out from beneath the House."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Abd Allah ibn Abi Najih narrated to me, from Mujahid and others of the people of knowledge: "When Allah settled Ibrahim in the place of the House, he went out to it from al-Sham, and with him went Isma'il and his mother Hajar, while Isma'il was a small infant nursing. They were carried—according to what was narrated to me—upon the Buraq, and with him was Jibril, guiding him to the site of the House and the landmarks of the Haram. Jibril went out with him, and he would not pass a town without saying: 'Is it this one that I was commanded, O Jibril?' Jibril would say: 'Proceed.' Until he arrived with him in Makkah, which at that time was a thicket of acacia and samur trees, and there were people called the 'Amaliq' outside Makkah and around it. The House at that time was a red, clayey mound. Ibrahim said to Jibril: 'Is it here that I was commanded to place them?' He said: 'Yes.' So he went with them to the place of the Hijr and settled them there, and commanded Hajar, the mother of Isma'il, to make a shelter (arish) there. He said: ﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in a valley without cultivation, by Your sacred House﴾ up to His saying: ﴿so that they may be grateful﴾ [Ibrahim: 37]."

Abd al-Razzaq said: Hisham ibn Hassan informed us, Humayd informed me, from Mujahid, who said: "Allah created the site of this House two thousand years before He created anything, and its pillars are in the seventh earth."

Similarly Layth ibn Abi Sulaym said, from Mujahid: "The foundations are in the seventh earth."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Amr ibn Rafi' narrated to us, Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mu'awiyah informed us, from Abd al-Mu'min ibn Khalid, from Ulayya ibn Ahmar, that Dhu al-Qarnayn came to Makkah and found Ibrahim and Isma'il building the foundations of the House from five mountains. He said: "What is it to you two with my land?" They said: "We are two servants under command; we were commanded to build this Ka'bah." He said: "Then bring your evidence for what you claim." Five rams stood up and said: "We bear witness that Ibrahim and Isma'il are two servants under command, commanded to build this Ka'bah." He said: "I am satisfied and at peace," and then he went on.

Al-Azraqi mentioned in the History of Makkah that Dhu al-Qarnayn circumambulated the House with Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and this indicates the antiquity of his time, and Allah knows best.

Al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The statement of Allah, exalted: ﴿And when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House and Isma'il﴾ to the end of the verse. Al-qawa'id (the foundations): its base, its singular being qa'idah. And al-qawa'id min al-nisa' (the women past child-bearing) — its singular being qa'id.

Isma'il narrated to us: Malik narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim ibn Abd Allah, that Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr informed Abd Allah ibn Umar, from Aisha, wife of the Prophet ﷺ, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do you not see that your people, when they rebuilt the House (the Ka'bah), limited it below the foundations of Ibrahim?" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, will you not restore it upon the foundations of Ibrahim?" He said: "Were it not for the recentness of your people's disbelief (hidthan qawmiki bil-kufr)." Abd Allah ibn Umar said: "If Aisha truly heard this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I do not think that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left the two corners that are adjacent to the Hijr unkissed except that the House was not completed upon the foundations of Ibrahim, peace be upon him."

It was also narrated in the book of Hajj from al-Qa'nabi, and in the chapter on the stories of the Prophets from Abd Allah ibn Yusuf, and Muslim from Yahya ibn Yahya and from the narration of Ibn Wahb, and al-Nasa'i from the narration of Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, all of them from Malik with this chain.

Muslim also narrated it from the narration of Nafi', who said: I heard Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah narrating to Abd Allah ibn Umar, from Aisha, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Were it not that your people are recent in jahiliyyah, or said: in disbelief, I would have spent the treasure of the Ka'bah in the way of Allah, and I would have made its door level with the ground, and I would have included the Hijr in it."

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on Surah 2, verses 126–128 (part 5 of 7):

Al-Bukhari said: Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Aswad, who said: Ibn al-Zubayr said to me: "A‘ishah used to confide many things to you, so what did she tell you about the Ka'bah?" He said: I said: She told me: The Prophet ﷺ said: "O A'ishah, were it not that your people are recently (converted) from disbelief" — Ibn al-Zubayr said: "with disbelief" — "I would have demolished the Ka'bah and made for it two doors: a door through which people enter, and a door through which they exit." So Ibn al-Zubayr did this.

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it, and he related it thus in the Book of Knowledge of his Sahih [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (126).]].

Muslim said in his Sahih: Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah informed us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "Were it not for the recent time of your people's disbelief, I would have demolished the Ka'bah and placed it upon the foundations of Ibrahim, for when Quraysh rebuilt the House they made it smaller, and I would have made for it a second door."

He said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb also narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Hisham, with this same chain. Muslim alone narrated it [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1333).]]. He said: Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Ibn Mahdi narrated to me: Sulaym ibn Hayyan narrated to us, from Sa'id — i.e., Ibn Mina' — who said: I heard Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr say: My maternal aunt — i.e., A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her — told me, she said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "O A'ishah, were it not that your people are recently (converted) from shirk, I would have demolished the Ka'bah and levelled it with the ground, and I would have made for it two doors: an eastern door and a western door, and I would have added to it six cubits from al-Hijr, for Quraysh reduced it when they built the Ka'bah." Muslim alone narrated it as well [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1333).]].

The mention of Quraysh's rebuilding of the Ka'bah after Ibrahim the Friend of Allah, upon him be peace, after a long period, and five years before the Prophet ﷺ's mission, and that he (ﷺ) carried stones with them when he was thirty-five years old, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him always until the Day of Religion.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said in the Sirah:

When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached thirty-five years of age, Quraysh gathered to rebuild the Ka'bah. They intended to roof it, and they feared to demolish it, for it was only walls raised above the height of a man. They wished to raise it and roof it. The reason was that a group of men stole the treasure of the Ka'bah, which was kept in a well inside the Ka'bah. The one in whose possession the treasure was found was Duwayk, a freedman of Banu Mulayh ibn 'Amr of Khuza'ah, and Quraysh cut off his hand. People claim that those who stole it placed it with Duwayk. The sea had cast a ship onto Jeddah belonging to a man from the Roman merchants, and it was wrecked, so they took its timber and prepared it for the roofing. There was a Coptic carpenter in Mecca, who prepared for them some of what would fix it. A serpent used to come out of the well of the Ka'bah, in which what was offered to it was thrown each day, and it would rise up onto the wall of the Ka'bah, and this was something they feared. No one came near it without it trembling, hissing and opening its mouth, so they feared it. One day, while it was rising onto the wall of the Ka'bah as it customarily did, Allah sent a bird to it which seized it and carried it away. Quraysh said: "We hope that Allah has approved what we intended. We have a skilled and gentle craftsman, we have timber, and Allah has spared us the serpent."

When they resolved upon demolishing and rebuilding it, Abu Wahb ibn 'Amr ibn 'A'idh ibn 'Abd ibn 'Imran ibn Makhzum stood up, took a stone from the Ka'bah, and it leapt from his hand until it returned to its place. He said: "O assembly of Quraysh, do not put into its building anything from your earnings except what is good; no wages of a prostitute, no interest from usury, and no injustice to anyone from among the people shall enter into it."

Ibn Ishaq said: People attribute this statement to al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar [[in A: "al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah ibn 'Umar ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar"]] ibn Makhzum [[Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah li-Ibn Ishaq (text no. 103), ed. Hamidullah, Morocco.]].

He said: Then Quraysh divided the Ka'bah: the side of the door belonged to Banu 'Abd Manaf and Zuhrah; the part between the Black Stone and the Yemeni Corner belonged to Banu Makhzum and tribes of Quraysh who had joined them; the back of the Ka'bah belonged to Banu Jumah and Sahm; and the side of al-Hijr belonged to Banu 'Abd al-Dar ibn Qusayy, Banu Asad ibn 'Abd al-'Uzza ibn Qusayy, and Banu 'Adi ibn Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy, and it is al-Hatim.

Then the people feared demolishing it and shrank from it. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah said: "I will begin you in demolishing it." He took the pickaxe, stood upon it, and said: "O Allah, do not be alarmed; O Allah, we intend only good." Then he demolished from the side of the two corners. The people waited that night and said: "We will see: if he is harmed, we will not demolish any part of it and will return it as it was; but if nothing befalls him, then Allah has approved what we have done." Al-Walid rose the next morning going about his work, and he demolished, and the people demolished with him, until the demolition reached the foundations of Ibrahim, upon him be peace, and they came upon green stones like spear-heads, each interlocking with the next [[Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah li-Ibn Ishaq (text no. 105), ed. Hamidullah, Morocco.]].

[Muhammad ibn Ishaq] said: One of those who narrate the report told me that a man from Quraysh, among those who were demolishing it, inserted a lever between two of its stones to pry one of them out, and when the stone moved, all of Mecca shook, so they ceased from that foundation [[Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah li-Ibn Ishaq (text no. 106), ed. Hamidullah, Morocco.]].

Ibn Ishaq said: Then the tribes of Quraysh gathered stones for its building, each tribe gathering separately, and then they built it, until the building reached the place of the Rukn — that is, the Black Stone — and they disputed over it, each tribe wishing to raise it to its place to the exclusion of the others, until they argued and disagreed and prepared for battle. Banu 'Abd al-Dar brought forward a bowl full of blood, then they and Banu 'Adi ibn Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy pledged themselves to death, and they dipped their hands into that blood in that bowl, and they were called "those who lick the blood." Quraysh remained in that state for four or five nights. Then they gathered in the mosque, consulted together, and sought fairness.

Some narrators of reports claim that Abu Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar ibn Makhzum — who was then the oldest of all Quraysh — said: "O assembly of Quraysh, make between you, in what you dispute, the first one who enters by the door of this mosque to judge between you concerning it." They did so, and the first to enter was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When they saw him, they said: "This is al-Amin; we are content. This is Muhammad." When he reached them and they informed him of the matter, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Bring me a garment." It was brought to him, and he took the Rukn — that is, the Black Stone — and placed it in it with his own hand. Then he said: "Let each tribe take hold of a side of the garment," and then [he said]: "Lift it all together." They did so, until they brought it to its place, and he placed it himself with his hand ﷺ. Then he built upon it.

Quraysh used to call the Messenger of Allah ﷺ "al-Amin" before revelation came to him. When they had finished the building and built it as they intended, al-Zubayr ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib said, regarding the matter of the serpent which Quraysh had feared in building the Ka'bah:

"I marvelled when the eagle swooped down upon the serpent, while it was in turmoil...
And it used to have a hiss, and at times it would leap up...
When we stood to lay the foundation, it resisted, terrifying us with the building, though it was itself feared...
When we feared its rebuke, an eagle came, swooping down upon it with a rush...
It gathered it to itself, then left us the building, which has no screen...
So we stood, gathered, to a building of which the foundations and the earth are ours...
On the morning we raised the foundation of it, and there were no garments upon those of us who levelled it...
The King honoured by it the Banu Lu'ayy, and none of its origin shall perish from among them...
Banu 'Adi and Murrah gathered there, and Kilab went before them...
So the King settled us in honour through that, and reward is sought from Allah."

Ibn Ishaq said: At the time of the Prophet ﷺ the Ka'bah was eighteen cubits high, and it used to be covered with Coptic cloth, then it was covered with striped garments, and the first to clothe it in brocade was al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf.

I say: It remained upon the building of Quraysh until it was burned at the beginning of the governorship of Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, after the year sixty AH, and in the last period of the reign of Yazid ibn Mu'awiyah, when they besieged Ibn al-Zubayr. At that time Ibn al-Zubayr demolished it to the ground and rebuilt it upon the foundations of Ibrahim, upon him be peace, and he included al-Hijr in it, and made for it an eastern door and a western door, both level with the ground, as he had heard this from his maternal aunt A'ishah, Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. It remained so throughout his governorship until al-Hajjaj killed him, and he restored it to what it had been, by the command of Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan to him in this, as Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj said in his Sahih:

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verses 126–128 (part 6 of 7):

Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us: Ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us: Ibn Abi Sulayman informed us, from 'Ata', who said: When the House (the Ka'bah) was burned during the time of Yazid ibn Mu'awiyah, when the people of al-Sham (Syria) attacked it, and what happened happened, Ibn al-Zubayr left it alone until the people came for the season (of Hajj), wanting to embolden them or rally them against the people of al-Sham. When the people had returned (from Mina), he said: "O people, advise me about the Ka'bah. Should I tear it down and rebuild it, or should I repair what has crumbled of it?" Ibn 'Abbas said: "As for me, my opinion on it has become clear: I see that you should repair what has crumbled of it, and leave the House on which the people embraced Islam and the stones on which the people embraced Islam and on which the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent." Ibn al-Zubayr said: "If one of them had his house burned, he would not be content until he renewed it, so how about the House of your Lord, Mighty and Majestic? I will seek guidance from my Lord for three days, and then I will firmly resolve on my decision." When three days had passed, he resolved to tear it down. The people shrank from this, fearing that something from heaven would descend upon the first person who climbed onto it, until a man climbed onto it and threw down some stones. When the people saw that nothing had befallen him, they followed suit and tore it down until they had brought it down to the ground. Ibn al-Zubayr then set up pillars over which he hung curtains, until its structure rose again. Ibn al-Zubayr said: "I heard 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, say that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Were it not that the people are recent in their disbelief, and I did not have enough expenditure to strengthen me in building it, I would have included in it five cubits from the Hijr (the semicircular enclosure beside the Ka'bah), and I would have made for it a door through which people enter and a door through which they exit.'" He said: "So now I have what I need to spend, and I do not fear the people." He said: "So he added five cubits from the Hijr to it, until he uncovered its foundations, which the people looked at, and then he built upon them." The Ka'bah had been eighteen cubits in height. When he added to it, he found it too short, so he increased its height by ten cubits, and he made for it two doors: one through which one enters, and the other through which one exits. When Ibn al-Zubayr was killed, al-Hajjaj wrote to 'Abd al-Malik informing him of this, and informing him that Ibn al-Zubayr had set the structure upon a foundation which the just men of Makkah had seen. 'Abd al-Malik wrote back to him: "We have nothing to do with Ibn al-Zubayr's defilement. As for what he added to its height, leave it. As for what he added to it from the Hijr, return it to its former structure, and block the door that he opened." So he tore it down and restored it to its former structure.

[Sahih Muslim, no. 1333.]

Al-Nasa'i has narrated it in his Sunan, from Hannad, from Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, from 'Ata', from Ibn al-Zubayr, from 'A'ishah, with only the marfu' (prophetic attribution) part of it, and he did not mention the narrative. The Sunnah (the prophetic practice) had been to approve what 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with him, had done, because he was the one whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had wished for. But the Prophet (ﷺ) feared that the hearts of some people would reject it, because of their recent conversion to Islam and their closeness to disbelief. However, this Sunnah remained hidden from 'Abd al-Malik, and therefore, when he confirmed from 'A'ishah that she had narrated this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "We wish that we had left it as it was, and what it had been entrusted to." As Muslim said:

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr and al-Walid ibn 'Ata' narrating from al-Harith ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Rabi'ah. 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayd said: al-Harith ibn 'Abd Allah came as a delegation to 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan during his caliphate. 'Abd al-Malik said: "I do not think that Abu Khubayb (i.e., Ibn al-Zubayr) heard from 'A'ishah what he claimed he heard from her." al-Harith said: "Yes, I heard it from her myself." He said: "What did you hear her say?" He said: "She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Your people made the House short in its construction, and were it not for the recency of their association with polytheism, I would have restored what they left of it. If it becomes apparent to your people after me that they should rebuild it, then come, and I will show you what they left of it.'" So she showed him about seven cubits of it.

[Sahih Muslim, no. 1333.]

This is the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr. al-Walid ibn 'Ata' added to it: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I would have made for it two doors placed level with the ground, one facing east and the other facing west. Do you know why your people raised its door?" She said: "I said: No." He said: "Out of pride, so that none would enter it except those whom they wanted. A man would come wanting to enter it, and they would let him climb up, and when he was about to enter, they would push him and he would fall." 'Abd al-Malik said: "I asked al-Harith: Did you hear her say this?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then he tapped the ground with his stick for a while, and then said: 'I wish I had left it and what it had been entrusted with.'"

Muslim said: Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Jabalah narrated to us: Abu 'Asim narrated to us (transition); and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us; both of them from Ibn Jurayj with this chain, like the hadith of Ibn Bakr.

[Sahih Muslim, no. 1333.]

He said: Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: 'Abd Allah ibn Bakr al-Sahmi narrated to us: Hatim ibn Abi Saghirah narrated to us, from Abu Qaza'ah, that 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, while he was circumambulating the House, said: "May Allah fight Ibn al-Zubayr, for he lies about the Mother of the Believers. He claims: 'I heard her say: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O 'A'ishah, were it not for the recency of your people's disbelief, I would have torn down the House and added to it from the Hijr, for your people fell short in its construction."'" al-Harith ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Rabi'ah said: "Do not say this, O Commander of the Faithful, for I heard the Mother of the Believers narrate this." He said: "If I had heard it before I demolished it, I would have left it as Ibn al-Zubayr built it."

[Sahih Muslim, no. 1333.]

This hadith is almost definitively attributed to 'A'ishah, the Mother of the Believers, because it has been narrated from her through multiple sound chains, from al-Aswad ibn Yazid, al-Harith ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Rabi'ah, 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, and 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr. This indicates the correctness of what Ibn al-Zubayr did, and had it been left alone, it would have been good.

However, after the matter had returned to this state, some scholars disliked changing it from its condition. It is reported that the Commander of the Faithful Harun al-Rashid (or his father al-Mahdi) asked Imam Malik about demolishing the Ka'bah and restoring it to what Ibn al-Zubayr had done. Malik said to him: "O Commander of the Faithful, do not make the House of Allah a plaything for kings. No one wishes to demolish it except that it will be demolished." So al-Rashid abandoned that.

This was transmitted by Iyad and al-Nawawi. And it remains so, Allah knows best, until the end of time, until Dhu al-Suwaykatayn from Ethiopia destroys it, as is established in the two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim) from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Dhu al-Suwaykatayn from Ethiopia will destroy the Ka'bah." Both of them narrated it.

[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1596; Sahih Muslim, no. 2909.]

And from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "As if I see him: black, bow-legged, pulling it out stone by stone." Al-Bukhari narrated it.

[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1595.]

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said in his Musnad: Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Malik al-Harrani narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, may Allah be pleased with both of them, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Dhu al-Suwaykatayn from Ethiopia will destroy the Ka'bah, and will strip it of its ornaments and remove its covering. As if I can see him: bald, with receding hair, striking at it with his pickaxe and his mattock."

[Musnad, 2/220.]

Al-Fada' means a twist between the foot and the shin bone.

This, Allah knows best, will only occur after the emergence of Ya'juj and Ma'juj (Gog and Magog), because of what came in Sahih al-Bukhari from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The House will certainly be visited for Hajj and 'Umrah after the emergence of Ya'juj and Ma'juj."

[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1593.]

* *

Allah's statement, relating the supplication of Ibrahim and Isma'il, peace be upon them: ﴿Our Lord, make us submissive to You, and from our descendants a community submissive to You, and show us our rites and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾

Ibn Jarir said: They mean by this: "Make us submitting to Your command, humbled before Your obedience, not associating with You in obedience anyone other than You, nor in worship anyone besides You."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us: Isma'il ibn Raja' ibn Hayyan al-Husni al-Qurashi narrated to us: Ma'qil ibn 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Karim, regarding ﴿and make us submissive to You﴾, he said: "Sincere to You." ﴿And from our descendants a community submissive to You﴾, he said: "A sincere community."

He also said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us: al-Muqaddami narrated to us: Sa'id ibn 'Amir narrated to us, from Sallam ibn Abi Mut'i concerning this verse, ﴿make us submissive to You﴾, he said: "They were both submitting, but they asked Him for steadfastness."

'Ikrimah said regarding ﴿Our Lord, make us submissive to You﴾: "Allah said: I have done it." ﴿And from our descendants a community submissive to You﴾: "Allah said: I have done it."

Al-Suddi said regarding ﴿and from our descendants a community submissive to You﴾: "They meant the Arabs."

Ibn Jarir said: The correct view is that it encompasses the Arabs and others, because among the descendants of Ibrahim are the Children of Israel, and Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And among the people of Musa is a community who guide by the truth and act justly by it﴾ [al-A'raf: 159].

I say: What Ibn Jarir said does not negate what al-Suddi said, for specifying them with this does not exclude others. The context is indeed about the Arabs, and this is why He said after it: ﴿Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses, and teach them the Book and wisdom, and purify them﴾ to the end of the verse. What is meant by this is Muhammad (ﷺ), and he was indeed sent among them, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿It is He who sent among the unlettered a messenger from themselves﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 2]. Nevertheless, this does not negate his message being sent to the red and the black, based on Allah the Exalted's saying: ﴿Say: O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all﴾ [al-A'raf: 158], and other conclusive proofs.

This prayer was made by Ibrahim and Isma'il, peace be upon them both, just as Allah the Exalted related about His righteous, believing servants in His words: ﴿And those who say, "Our Lord, grant us from among our wives and offspring comfort to our eyes, and make us leaders for the righteous."﴾ [al-Furqan: 74]. This measure is legislatively desirable, for it is part of the completeness of love for the worship of Allah the Exalted that a person loves that from his own loins there should come one who worships Allah alone, with no partner. For this reason, when Allah the Exalted said to Ibrahim, peace be upon him: ﴿Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people,﴾ he said: ﴿And from my descendants?" He said, "My covenant does not include the wrongdoers.﴾ This is His saying: ﴿And keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols.﴾ [Ibrahim: 35].

It is established in Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When the son of Adam dies, his deeds are cut off except for three: ongoing charity (sadaqah jariyah), knowledge from which benefit is gained, or a righteous child who prays for him." [Sahih Muslim, no. (1631).]

"And show us our rites (manasik)." Ibn Juraij said, from 'Ata', regarding ﴿And show us our rites⁠﴾: bring them out for us, teach them to us. [In C, T: "And taught them to us."]

Mujahid said: "﴿And show us our rites﴾: our slaughtering places." Similar was narrated from 'Ata' as well, and from Qatadah.

Sa'id ibn Mansur said: Attab ibn Bashir narrated to us, from Khusayf, from Mujahid, who said: Ibrahim said, "Show us our rites," so Jibril came to him and took him to the House. He said: "Raise the foundations." So he raised the foundations and completed the building. Then he took his hand, brought him out, and went with him to al-Safa. He said: "This is from the symbols of Allah." Then he went with him to al-Marwah and said: "And this is from the symbols of Allah?" Then he went with him toward Mina. When they reached the 'Aqabah, behold, Iblis was standing by the tree. He said: "Say the takbir and throw at him." So he said the takbir and threw. Then Iblis moved and stood at the middle jamrah. When Jibril and Ibrahim passed by him, he said to him: "Say the takbir and throw at him." So he said the takbir and threw. Then Iblis departed, for the wretch had wanted to introduce something into the Hajj but could not, so he took Ibrahim by the hand until he brought him to al-Mash'ar al-Haram, and said: "This is al-Mash'ar al-Haram." Then he took Ibrahim by the hand until he brought him to 'Arafat. He said: "Do you know what I have shown you?" He said it three times. He said: "Yes."

Similar was narrated from Abu Mijlaz and Qatadah. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Abu al-'Asim al-Ghanawi, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Ibrahim was shown the commands of the rites, Satan appeared to him at al-Mas'a, so Ibrahim raced him. Then Jibril took him on until he brought him to Mina and said: "This is the resting place of the people." When he reached the Jamrat al-'Aqabah, Satan confronted him, and he threw seven pebbles at him until he departed. Then he brought him to the middle jamrah, and Satan confronted him, and he threw seven pebbles until he departed. Then he brought him to the furthest jamrah, and Satan confronted him, and he threw seven pebbles until he departed. Then he brought him to Jam'an and said: "This is al-Mash'ar." Then he brought him to 'Arafah and said: "This is 'Arafah." Jibril said to him: "Have you recognized it?" [Musnad al-Tayalisi, no. (2697).]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verses 126–128 (part 1 of 7):

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And when Abraham said, "My Lord, make this a secure city and provide its people with fruits, those of them who believe in Allah and the Last Day"﴾.

The Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Abraham made the House of Allah sacred and granted it security, and I have made Medina sacred between its two lava plains (al-labatayn), so its game shall not be hunted and its 'idah (thorny trees) shall not be cut." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (3/48). Al-labatan are the two volcanic plains on either side of Medina. Al-'idah is every large tree that has thorns; it is also said to be any large tree in general.]]

Al-Nasa'i narrated it likewise, from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, from Bundar, with the same chain. [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 4284.]]

Muslim also narrated it, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Amr al-Naqid, both from Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri, from Sufyan al-Thawri. [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1362.]]

Ibn Jarir also said: Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us; and Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abd al-Rahim al-Razi narrated to us, both of them together saying: We heard Ash'ath, from Nafi', from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Abraham was the servant of Allah and His friend (khalil), and I am the servant of Allah and His Messenger. Abraham made Mecca sacred, and I have made Medina sacred between its two lava plains, its 'idah and its game. No weapon for fighting shall be carried in it, and no tree in it shall be cut except for the fodder of a camel." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (3/48).]]

This chain is unusual (gharib); it is not found in any of the Six Books (al-Kutub al-Sittah, the six canonical collections of hadith). The original version of the hadith is in Sahih Muslim through another route, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When people saw the first of the fruit, they would bring it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When he took it, he would say: "O Allah, bless for us our fruit, bless for us our city, bless for us our sa' (measure) and bless for us our mudd (measure). O Allah, indeed Abraham was Your servant, Your friend and Your prophet, and I am Your servant and Your prophet. He supplicated You for Mecca, and I supplicate You for Medina with the like of what he supplicated You for Mecca, and with its like besides it." Then he would give it to the youngest child present. In another wording: "a blessing added to a blessing," and then he would give it to the youngest of the children present. This is the wording of Muslim. [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1373.]]

Then Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Bukayr ibn Mudar narrated to us, from Ibn al-Had, from Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn Uthman, from Rafi' ibn Khadij, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Abraham made Mecca sacred, and I make sacred what lies between its two lava plains."

Muslim alone narrated it, from Qutaybah, from Bukayr ibn Mudar, with the same chain, and its wording is the same as the above. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (3/49).]]

In the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim), from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abu Talhah: "Look for a boy from among your young men to serve me." Abu Talhah set out with me, carrying me behind him on his mount, and I would serve the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) whenever he dismounted. In the hadith he also said: Then he came on until Uhud appeared to him, and he said: "This is a mountain that loves us and we love it." When he came in sight of Medina, he said: "O Allah, I make sacred what lies between its two mountains, just as Abraham made Mecca sacred. O Allah, bless them in their mudd and their sa'." In another wording of the two: "O Allah, bless them in their measure, bless them in their sa', and bless them in their mudd." Al-Bukhari added: meaning the people of Medina. [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1361.]]

Also in the two Sahihs, from Anas: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, make in Medina double the blessing You placed in Mecca." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1885; Sahih Muslim, no. 1369.]]

And from Abd Allah ibn Zayd ibn Asim, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed Abraham made Mecca sacred and supplicated for it, and I have made Medina sacred as Abraham made Mecca sacred, and I have supplicated for it concerning its mudd and its sa' with the like of what Abraham supplicated for Mecca." Narrated by al-Bukhari, and this is his wording [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2129]], and by Muslim, whose wording is: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Abraham made Mecca sacred and supplicated for its people. And I have made Medina sacred as Abraham made Mecca sacred, and I have supplicated for it concerning its sa' and its mudd with the like of what Abraham supplicated for the people of Mecca." [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1360.]]

And from Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "O Allah, indeed Abraham made Mecca sacred and made it a sanctuary, and I have made Medina a sanctuary between its two harrah (rocky tracts), where no blood is shed, no weapon for fighting is carried, and no tree is stripped of its leaves except for fodder. O Allah, bless for us our city. O Allah, bless for us our sa'. O Allah, bless for us our mudd. O Allah, make with the blessing two blessings." The hadith was narrated by Muslim. [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1374.]]

The hadiths concerning the sanctity of Medina are numerous, and we have cited only those related to Abraham's making Mecca sacred, because of their correspondence with the noble verse.

[Those who hold that the sanctity of Mecca was established only through the words of Abraham the Friend (al-Khalil) relied on these. It has also been said that it has been sacred since it was created together with the earth, and this is more apparent and stronger.] [[Addition from manuscripts ج, ط, أ.]]

Other hadiths have also come which indicate that Allah the Exalted made Mecca sacred before He created the heavens and the earth, as came in the two Sahihs, from Abd Allah ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said on the day of the Conquest of Mecca: "Indeed this city, Allah made it sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred by the sanctity of Allah until the Day of Resurrection. Fighting in it was not permitted to anyone before me, and it was permitted to me only for an hour of the day. So it is sacred by the sanctity of Allah until the Day of Resurrection. Its thorny trees shall not be cut, its game shall not be frightened, its lost property shall not be picked up except by one who announces it, and its grass shall not be cut." Al-Abbas said: "O Messenger of Allah, except the idhkhir, for it is for their smiths and their houses." He said: "Except the idhkhir." This is the wording of Muslim. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 1834, 1587, 3189, 3077; Sahih Muslim, no. 1353.]]

Both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) also narrated something similar from Abu Hurayrah. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 112, 6880; Sahih Muslim, no. 1355.]]

Then al-Bukhari said after that: Aban ibn Salih said, from al-Hasan ibn Muslim, from Safiyyah bint Shaybah: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ), the like of it. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1349.]]

This which al-Bukhari cited without a full chain (mu'allaq) was narrated by the Imam Abu Abd Allah ibn Majah, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Numayr, from Yunus ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Aban ibn Salih, from al-Hasan ibn Muslim ibn Yannaq, from Safiyyah bint Shaybah, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) delivering a sermon in the year of the Conquest, and he said: "O people, indeed Allah made Mecca sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred until the Day of Resurrection. Its trees shall not be cut and its game shall not be frightened, and no one shall pick up its lost property except one who announces it." Al-Abbas said: "Except the idhkhir, for it is for the houses and the graves." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Except the idhkhir." [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3109.]]

And from Abu Shurayh al-'Adawi, that he said to Amr ibn Sa'id, while he was sending armies to Mecca: "Permit me, O Amir, to relate to you a statement which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made on the day after the Conquest. My ears heard it, my heart understood it, and my eyes saw him when he said it. He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'Indeed Mecca was made sacred by Allah and not made sacred by people. So it is not lawful for a person who believes in Allah and the Last Day to shed blood in it, or to cut a tree in it. If anyone takes a concession to fight in it by the fighting of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), say: Indeed Allah permitted His Messenger (ﷺ) but did not permit you. He permitted me only for an hour of a day, and its sanctity has returned today as it was yesterday. So let the one present convey it to the absent.'" It was said to Abu Shurayh: "What did Amr say to you?" He said: "I know that better than you, O Abu Shurayh. Indeed the sanctuary does not protect a disobedient person, nor a fugitive who has shed blood, nor a fugitive who has committed theft (kharbah)." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1832; Sahih Muslim, no. 1354.]] Narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim, and this is his wording.

Given this, there is no contradiction between these hadiths which indicate that Allah made Mecca sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth, and the hadiths which indicate that Abraham made it sacred. This is because Abraham conveyed from Allah His ruling concerning it and His prohibition of it, and it had remained a sacred city with Allah before Abraham built it, just as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was recorded with Allah as the Seal of the Prophets while Adam was still between water and clay. Despite this, Abraham (peace be upon him) said: ﴿Our Lord, and send among them a Messenger from among them﴾, and Allah answered his supplication with what had preceded in His knowledge and decree. For this reason it came in a hadith that they said: "O Messenger of Allah, inform us about the beginning of your affair." He said: "The supplication of my father Abraham, and the good news of Jesus son of Mary, and my mother saw that there came forth from her a light by which the palaces of Syria were illuminated."

That is: Inform us about the beginning of the manifestation of your affair, as will come shortly, Allah willing.

As for the question of whether Mecca is superior to Medina, as is the view of the majority (al-Jumhur), or Medina is superior to Mecca, as is the position of Malik and his followers, it will be mentioned in another place with its evidences, Allah willing, and in Him is trust.

* *

His words, the Exalted, reporting about the Friend (Abraham) that he said: ﴿My Lord, make this a secure city﴾. That is: secure from fear, so that its people are not terrified. Allah did this both by law (shar') and by decree (qadar). Like His saying the Exalted: ﴿And whoever enters it is secure﴾ [Al 'Imran: 97], and His saying: ﴿Have they not seen that We have made a sanctuary secure while people are snatched away from around them?﴾ [Al-'Ankabut: 67], and other verses. The hadiths on the prohibition of fighting in it have already passed. In Sahih Muslim, from Jabir: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "It is not lawful for anyone to carry a weapon in Mecca." [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1356.]] He said in this surah: ﴿My Lord, make this a secure city﴾, meaning: make this plot of land a secure city. This fits, because it was before the building of the Ka'bah. He said in the surah of Abraham: ﴿And when Abraham said, "My Lord, make this city secure"﴾ [Ibrahim: 35], and this fits there because it was, and Allah knows best, as if it occurred as a second supplication (du'a' marrah thaniyah) after the building of the House and the settling of its people in it, and after the birth of Isaac, who was thirteen years younger than Ishmael. For this reason He said at the end of the supplication: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who has given me in old age Ishmael and Isaac. Indeed my Lord is the Hearer of supplication﴾ [Ibrahim: 39].

* *

His words, the Exalted: ﴿and provide its people with fruits, those of them who believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾. He said: ﴿And whoever disbelieves, I will grant him enjoyment for a little, then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination﴾.

Abu Ja'far al-Razi related from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "He said: 'And whoever disbelieves, I will let him enjoy [himself] briefly, then I will compel him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination'" [Qur'an 2:126]. He said: "This is the statement of Allah the Exalted." This is also the view of Mujahid and 'Ikrimah, and it is what Ibn Jarir (may Allah have mercy on him) favored. He said: "Others recited: '[He] said: And whoever disbelieves, I will let him enjoy [himself] briefly, then I will compel him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination,' and they made this part of Ibrahim's supplication," as Abu Ja'far related from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: "Ibn 'Abbas used to say: 'That is the statement of Ibrahim, asking his Lord that whoever disbelieves, He should let him enjoy [himself] briefly.'"

Abu Ja'far also related from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Mujahid, regarding: "And whoever disbelieves, I will let him enjoy [himself] briefly," that he said: "And whoever disbelieves, I will also provide for him. Then I will compel him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: When Ibrahim, peace be upon him, withdrew the call from those whom Allah refused to grant him authority over, in devotion to Allah and His love and separation from those who opposed His command, even if they were of his offspring, when he knew from Allah's informing him of it that they would be wrongdoers and that his covenant would not reach them, Allah said: "And whoever disbelieves, I will provide for the pious and the wicked alike, and I will let him enjoy [himself] briefly."

Hatim ibn Isma'il related from Humayd al-Kharrat, from 'Ammar al-Duhni, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning the words of Allah the Exalted: "My Lord, make this a secure city and provide its people with fruits, those of them who believe in Allah and the Last Day" [Qur'an 2:126]. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Ibrahim used to restrict it to the believers, to the exclusion of the people. So Allah revealed: 'And whoever disbelieves also—I will provide for them as I provide for the believers. Shall I create a creation that I do not provide for? I will let them enjoy [themselves] briefly, then I will compel them to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination.'" Then Ibn 'Abbas recited: "To each We extend—these and those—from the bounty of your Lord; and the bounty of your Lord is never restricted" [Qur'an 17:20]. Ibn Mardawayh related it. Similar was also narrated from 'Ikrimah and Mujahid. This is like His saying, the Exalted: "Indeed, those who fabricate lies against Allah will not succeed. [It is] an enjoyment in this world; then to Us is their return; then We will make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve" [Qur'an 10:69–70]; and His saying: "And whoever disbelieves, let not his disbelief grieve you. To Us is their return, and We will inform them of what they did. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts. We let them enjoy [themselves] briefly; then We will compel them to a harsh punishment" [Qur'an 31:23–24]; and His saying: "And if not that the people would be one community, We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful silver ceilings for their houses and stairways [of silver] on which they could ascend, and for their houses doors and couches on which they could recline, and ornaments of gold. But all of that is nothing but the enjoyment of the worldly life. And the Hereafter with your Lord is for the righteous" [Qur'an 43:33–35].

* *

As for His saying, "then I will compel him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination": that is, "then I will force him, after his enjoyment in this world and after We have spread over him of its shade, to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination." Its meaning is that Allah, the Exalted, gives them respite and grants them time, then seizes them with the seizure of the Mighty, the Omnipotent, as in His saying: "And how many a city have I granted respite while it was wrongdoing; then I seized it, and to Me is the [final] destination" [Qur'an 22:48]. In the two Sahihs: "No one is more patient with harm he hears than Allah; they attribute to Him a son, yet He provides for them and grants them well-being." [[The tradition was cited earlier.]] Also in the Sahih: "Indeed Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer until, when He seizes him, He does not release him." Then he recited His saying: "And thus is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are wrongdoing. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe" [Qur'an 11:102]. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4686, and Sahih Muslim, no. 2583, from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

As for His saying, "And [mention] when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House and Isma'il [, saying], 'Our Lord, accept [this] from us. Indeed You are the Hearing, the Knowing. Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. And show us our rites and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful'" [Qur'an 2:127–128]:

"Al-qawa'id" is the plural of "qa'idah," which means the pillars and the foundations. Allah the Exalted says: Mention, O Muhammad, to your people the building of Ibrahim and Isma'il, upon them both be peace, of the House, and their raising its foundations, while they were saying: "Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed You are the Hearing, the Knowing." They were engaged in righteous deed while asking Allah, the Exalted, to accept it from them, as Ibn Abi Hatim related through the hadith of Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Khunays al-Makki, from Wuhayb ibn al-Ward, that he recited: "And [mention] when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House and Isma'il, [saying], 'Our Lord, accept from us,'" and then he would weep and say: "O Khalil of the Most Merciful, you raise the pillars of the House of the Most Merciful while you are apprehensive that it will not be accepted from you." This is like what Allah, the Exalted, related about the state of the sincere believers in His saying: "And those who give what they give [of charity]" [Qur'an 23:60], that is, they give what they have given of charities, expenditures and acts of devotion, "while their hearts are fearful" [Qur'an 23:60], that is, fearful that it will not be accepted from them. As the authentic hadith from 'Aishah from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has it, as will come in its place.

Some of the exegetes said: The one who raised the foundations was Ibrahim, and the one who supplicated was Isma'il. The correct view is that both of them were raising and both were saying, as its explanation will come.

Al-Bukhari has related here a hadith which we will cite, then follow it with narrations related to it. Al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq related to us, Ma'mar related to us, from Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani and Kathir ibn Kathir ibn al-Muttalib ibn Abi Wada'ah (one of them exceeding the other in narration), from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "The first who used a waistband [mintaq] among women was the mother of Isma'il, upon them both be peace. She made a waistband so as to conceal her traces from Sarah. Then Ibrahim brought her and her son Isma'il, upon them both be peace, while she was nursing him, until he placed them by the House, beside a tree above Zamzam in the upper part of the mosque. At that time there was no one in Makkah, and there was no water there. So he placed them there, and placed beside them a leather bag containing dates and a waterskin containing water. Then Ibrahim, peace be upon him, turned back, departing. Isma'il's mother followed him and said: 'O Ibrahim, where are you going, leaving us in this valley in which there is no person and nothing?' She said this to him repeatedly, but he did not turn toward her. She said: 'Has Allah commanded you to do this?' He said: 'Yes.' She said: 'Then He will not let us be lost.' Then she returned. So Ibrahim, peace be upon him, went on until, when he was at the mountain pass where they could not see him, he faced the House, raised his hands, and supplicated with these supplications, saying: 'Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your Sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make hearts among the people incline toward them and provide for them from the fruits that they may be grateful' [Qur'an 14:37]. Isma'il's mother kept nursing Isma'il and drinking from that water, until the water in the waterskin was exhausted, and she and her son became thirsty. She began looking at him writhing—or he said: thrashing—so she departed, disliking to look at him. She found that Safa was the nearest mountain to her on the earth, so she stood upon it, then faced the valley, looking to see whether she could see anyone. She did not see anyone. She descended from Safa, until when she reached the valley, she lifted the edge of her garment and ran with the effort of an exhausted person until she crossed the valley. Then she came to Marwah, stood upon it, and looked to see whether she could see anyone. She did not see anyone. She did this seven times." Ibn 'Abbas said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "For this reason the people run between them."

When she ascended Marwah, she heard a voice and said: "Be quiet," wanting to hear herself; then she listened and heard it again. She said: "You have made me hear; if you have any help, then [help me]." Suddenly there was an angel at the place of Zamzam, who dug with his heel—or he said: with his wing—until water appeared. She began making a basin for it, saying with her hand thus, and she began scooping water into her waterskin while it gushed forth after she scooped. Ibn 'Abbas said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "May Allah have mercy on the mother of Isma'il. Had she left Zamzam—or he said: had she not scooped from the water—Zamzam would have been a flowing spring."

He said: So she drank and nursed her child. The angel said to her: "Do not fear neglect, for indeed here is the House of Allah, which this boy and his father will build, and indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, does not neglect His people." The House was raised above the ground like a mound, and the floods would come and divert from its right and left. It remained so until a caravan of Jurhum—or a household of Jurhum—passed by them, coming from the route of Kada'. They stopped at the lower part of Makkah, and they saw a bird circling, so they said: "This bird is surely circling over water, for we know this valley and there is no water in it." So they sent a scout or two scouts, who found the water. They returned and informed them of the water, so they came. He said: Isma'il's mother was at the water. They said: "Will you permit us to settle near you?" She said: "Yes, but you have no right to the water." They said: "Yes."

Ibn Abbas [in some editions: "Abdullah ibn Abbas"] said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Umm Ismail found that [the water] and she loved company. So they settled, and they sent for their families, and they came to settle with them. When some households of them had settled there, the boy grew up and learned Arabic from them, and they admired him and liked him as he grew up. When he reached [maturity] they married him to a woman from among them. Umm Ismail died, peace be upon them both. Then Ibrahim came, after Ismail had married, to check on his property. He did not find Ismail, so he asked his wife about him. She said: 'He went out to seek [food] for us.' Then he asked her about their livelihood and their condition, and she said: 'We are in a bad state, we are in hardship and distress,' and she complained to him. He said: 'When your husband comes, convey greetings to him and tell him: change the threshold of his door.' When Ismail, peace be upon him, came, it was as if he sensed something. He said: 'Has anyone come to you?' She said: 'Yes, an old man like so-and-so came, and he asked about you, and I informed him. He also asked me how our living was, and I told him that we are in hardship and distress.' He said: 'Did he advise you of anything?' She said: 'Yes, he commanded me to convey his greetings to you, and he says: change the threshold of your door.' He said: 'That was my father, and he has commanded me to part from you, so return to your family.' So he divorced her and married another woman from among them. Ibrahim stayed away from them for as long as Allah willed, then he came to them again but did not find him. He entered upon his wife and asked her about him, and she said: 'He went out to seek [food] for us.' He said: 'How are you?' and he asked her about their livelihood and condition. She said: 'We are well and in abundance,' and she praised Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. He said: 'What is your food?' She said: 'Meat.' He said: 'What is your drink?' She said: 'Water.' He said: 'O Allah, bless them in their meat and their water.'"

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There was no grain for them at that time, and if they had had any, he would have supplicated for them in it. He said: 'No one lives in those two [places] except in Makkah except that they will not agree with him.'" He said: "When your husband comes, convey greetings to him, and order him to make firm the threshold of his door." When Ismail, peace be upon him, came, he said: "Has anyone come to you?" She said: "Yes, an old man of good appearance came to us, and she praised him. He asked me about you, and I informed him, and he asked me: 'How is our living?' and I told him that we are well." He said: "Did he advise you of anything?" She said: "Yes, he sends his greetings to you and commands you to make firm the threshold of your door." He said: "That was my father, and you are the threshold; he commanded me to keep you." Then he stayed away from them for as long as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, willed. Then he came after that while Ismail was shaping arrows beneath a tree near Zamzam. When he saw him, he stood up to him, and they did as a child does with a parent and a parent does with a child. Then he said: "O Ismail, Allah has commanded me with a command." He said: "Do what your Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, has commanded you." He said: "Will you help me?" He said: "I will help you." He said: "Allah has commanded me to build a house here," and he pointed to a high hillock above what surrounded it. He said: "At that, they raised the foundations of the House, and Ismail began to bring the stones while Ibrahim built, until the building rose; he brought this stone and placed it for him, and he stood upon it while he built, and Ismail handed him the stones, and both of them were saying: ﴿Our Lord, accept from us; indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾." He said: "They continued building until they went around the House, and both of them were saying: ﴿Our Lord, accept from us; indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾."

[Abd ibn Humayd narrated it from Abd al-Razzaq with the same wording, in an expanded form.]

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Hammad al-Zahrani, and Ibn Jarir [al-Tabari] narrated it from Ahmad ibn Thabit al-Razi; both from Abd al-Razzaq with the same wording, in abridged form.

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Ismail ibn Ali ibn Ismail narrated to us, Bishr ibn Musa narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Azraqi narrated to us, Muslim ibn Khalid al-Zanji narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Juraij, from Kathir ibn Kathir, who said: I and Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman and Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Husayn were with a group of people with Sa'id ibn Jubayr, in the upper part of the Mosque at night, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Ask me before you no longer see me." They asked him about the Maqam [Station of Ibrahim], and he began to narrate to them from Ibn Abbas, and he related the hadith in full.

Then al-Bukhari said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Abu Amir Abd al-Malik ibn Amr narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Nafi narrated to us, from Kathir ibn Kathir, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When there was between Ibrahim and his family what there was, he set out with Ismail and Umm Ismail, and with them was a waterskin containing water. Umm Ismail began to drink from the waterskin, and her milk flowed for her child, until he came to Makkah and placed her beneath a tree. Then Ibrahim returned to his family, and Umm Ismail followed him, until they reached Kada, and she called to him from behind: "O Ibrahim, to whom are you leaving us?" He said: "To Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." She said: "I am content with Allah." He said: "So she returned, and began to drink from the waterskin, and her milk flowed for her child, until the water ran out. She said: 'If only I went and looked, perhaps I might sense someone.'" He said: "So she went and climbed al-Safa, and looked and looked to see whether she could sense anyone, but she did not sense anyone. When she reached the valley, she ran until she came to al-Marwa, and she did that several times. Then she said: 'If only I went and looked at what he is doing,' meaning the child. So she went and looked, and there he was in the same state, as if he were gasping for death, and her soul was not at ease, so she said: 'If only I went and looked, perhaps I might sense someone.'" He said: "So she went and climbed al-Safa, and looked and looked, but did not sense anyone, until she completed seven [circuits]. Then she said: 'If only I went and looked at what he is doing.' Then she heard a voice, and she said: 'Help, if you have any good!' And there was Jibril, peace be upon him." He said: "He struck with his heel like this, and pressed his heel into the ground." He said: "Water gushed forth, and Umm Ismail was astonished, and began to dig."

He said: Abu al-Qasim (ﷺ) said: "If she had left it, the water would have flowed on the surface."

He said: "So she began to drink from the water, and her milk flowed for her child."

He said: "Then some people of Jurhum passed by the lower part of the valley, and they saw birds, as if they were surprised by that, and they said: 'Birds only gather over water.' So they sent their messenger, who looked and found water. He came to them and informed them. So they came to her and said: 'O Umm Ismail, will you permit us to be with you, and settle with you?' Her son grew up and married a woman from among them."

He said: "Then it occurred to Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and he said to his family: 'I will check on my property.' He came and greeted [them], and said: 'Where is Ismail?' His wife said: 'He has gone hunting.' He said: 'Tell him when he comes: change the threshold of your house.' When he came, she informed him, and he said: 'You are that [threshold]; go back to your family.'"

He said: "Then it occurred to Ibrahim, and he said to his family: 'I will check on my property.' He came and said: 'Where is Ismail?' His wife said: 'He has gone hunting.' She said: 'Will you not dismount and eat and drink?' He said: 'What is your food and what is your drink?' She said: 'Our food is meat, and our drink is water.' He said: 'O Allah, bless them in their food and their drink.'"

He said: Abu al-Qasim (ﷺ) said: "A blessing by the supplication of Ibrahim."

He said: "Then it occurred to Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and he said to his family: 'I will check on my property.' He came and met Ismail behind Zamzam, adjusting his arrows [in another version: adjusting a house of his]. He said: 'O Ismail, your Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, has commanded me to build a house for Him.' He said: 'Obey your Lord, the Mighty and Majestic.' He said: 'He has commanded me that you should help me in it.' He said: 'Then I will do it' or as he said. He said: 'So they both stood up,' and Ibrahim began to build while Ismail handed him the stones, and they were saying: ﴿Our Lord, accept from us; indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾."

He said: "Until the building rose high and the old man became too weak to carry the stones. So he stood upon the Station stone, and began to hand him the stones, and they were saying: ﴿Our Lord, accept from us; indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾."

Thus did he narrate it from these two routes in the Book of the Prophets [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3365].

It is strange that the Hafiz Abu Abdullah al-Hakim narrated it in his book al-Mustadrak (the "Mustadrak," al-Hakim's collection of hadith he considered to meet the criteria of authenticity not included in the Sahihs), from Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm, from Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz, from Abu Ali Ubayd Allah ibn Abd al-Majid al-Hanafi, from Ibrahim ibn Nafi, with the same [hadith]. He said: "It is sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs [al-Bukhari and Muslim], though they did not record it." So he said. Al-Bukhari has narrated it as you see, from the hadith of Ibrahim ibn Nafi, as though there is an abridgment in it, for he did not mention in it the matter of the sacrifice. It has come in the Sahih that the two horns of the ram were hanging in the Ka'bah. It has also been reported that Ibrahim, peace be upon him, would visit his family in Makkah swiftly on al-Buraq [the mythical steed], then return to his family in the blessed lands. And Allah knows best. The hadith, Allah knows best, contains, as a marfu' report [traced to the Prophet (ﷺ)], only places that Ibn Abbas explicitly attributed to the Prophet (ﷺ).

It has been reported from the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, in this context, something that differs from some of this, as Ibn Jarir said:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both said: Mu'ammal narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Harithah ibn Mudrib, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: When Ibrahim was commanded to build the House, Ismail and Hajar went out with him. He said: When he came to Makkah, he saw over the place of the House something like a cloud, in which there was something like a head. It spoke to him, [saying]: "O Ibrahim, build upon my shadow" — or he said "upon my measure" — "and do not add or subtract." When he built, he left, and left Ismail and Hajar. Hajar said: "O Ibrahim, to whom are you leaving us?" He said: "To Allah." She said: "Go, for He will not waste us." He said: "Ismail became very thirsty." He said: "Hajar climbed al-Safa, looked, and saw nothing; until she reached al-Marwa and saw nothing; then she returned to al-Safa, looked, and saw nothing; until she reached al-Marwa and saw nothing; then she returned to al-Safa, looked, and saw nothing; until she did that seven times." She said: "O Ismail, die where I cannot see you." She came to him while he was scraping the ground with his foot from thirst. Jibril called to her and said: "Who are you?" She said: "I am Hajar, the mother of Ibrahim's son." He said: "To whom did He entrust you both?" She said: "He entrusted us to Allah." He said: "He has entrusted you both to the Sufficient One." He said: "The boy scraped the ground with his finger, and Zamzam gushed forth." She began to hold back the water, and he said: "Leave it, for it is satisfying."

In this narration it is stated that he built the House before he parted from them both. It may be possible, if it is preserved, that he first laid out for it a boundary and marking, not that he built it to its full height until Ismail grew up, and then they built it together, as Allah the Exalted said.

Then Ibn Jarir said: Hannad ibn al-Sarri informed us, Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak, from Khalid ibn 'Ar'arah, that a man stood before Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: "Will you not tell me about the House (al-Bayt)? Is it the first house placed on the earth?" He said: "No. But it is the first house in which blessing was placed, the Station of Ibrahim (Maqam Ibrahim), and whoever enters it is safe. If you wish, I will inform you how it was built. Allah revealed to Ibrahim, 'Build for Me a house on the earth.' Ibrahim was distressed by this, so Allah sent the sakinah (tranquility), which is a wind with a head and two wings, and one of its heads followed the other until it reached Makkah. It coiled over the place of the House like a shield being rolled up, and Ibrahim was commanded to build where the sakinah settled. Ibrahim built, and one stone remained, so the boy went off to seek something. Ibrahim said, 'Bring me a stone as I command you.' The boy set off to find a stone and brought it to him, but he found that Ibrahim had already set the Black Stone (al-Hajar al-Aswad) in its place. He said, 'O father, who brought you this stone?' He replied, 'It was brought to me by one who will not depend on your building; Jibril, peace be upon him, brought it from the heaven.'" So they completed it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Hamad ibn Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Bishr ibn Asim, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Ka'b al-Ahbar, who said: "The House was a foam (ghuthA'ah) upon the water forty years before Allah created the earth, and from it the earth was spread out (duhiyat)."

Sa'id said: Ali ibn Abi Talib narrated to us that Ibrahim came from Armenia (Armeniyyah), and with him was the sakinah guiding him to the settling place of the House, just as the spider settles upon a house. He said: "It uncovered stones that only thirty men could lift." I said: "O Abu Muhammad, Allah says: ﴿And when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House﴾." He said: "That was after."

Al-Suddi said: Allah, mighty and majestic, commanded Ibrahim to build the House, he and Isma'il: "Build My House for those who circumambulate, those who stay in devotion, and those who bow and prostrate." So Ibrahim set out until he came to Makkah. He and Isma'il stood, taking the ma'awil (picks), not knowing where the House was. Allah sent a wind called the wind of al-Khujuj, which had two wings and a head in the form of a serpent. It uncovered for them, around the Ka'bah, the foundations of the first House, and they followed it with the picks, digging until they laid the foundation. This is when Allah, exalted, says: ﴿And when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House﴾ ﴿And when We settled for Ibrahim the place of the House﴾ [al-Hajj: 26]. When they had built the foundations and reached the place of the corner (rukn), Ibrahim said to Isma'il: "O my son, seek for me a good stone that I may place here."
