Five rams stood up and said: "We bear witness that Ibrahim and Isma'il are two servants under command, commanded to build this Ka'bah." He said: "I am satisfied and at peace," and then he went on.

Al-Azraqi mentioned in the History of Makkah that Dhu al-Qarnayn circumambulated the House with Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and this indicates the antiquity of his time, and Allah knows best.

Al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The statement of Allah, exalted: ﴿And when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House and Isma'il﴾ to the end of the verse. Al-qawa'id (the foundations): its base, its singular being qa'idah. And al-qawa'id min al-nisa' (the women past child-bearing) — its singular being qa'id.

Isma'il narrated to us: Malik narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim ibn Abd Allah, that Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr informed Abd Allah ibn Umar, from Aisha, wife of the Prophet ﷺ, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do you not see that your people, when they rebuilt the House (the Ka'bah), limited it below the foundations of Ibrahim?" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, will you not restore it upon the foundations of Ibrahim?" He said: "Were it not for the recentness of your people's disbelief (hidthan qawmiki bil-kufr)." Abd Allah ibn Umar said: "If Aisha truly heard this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I do not think that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left the two corners that are adjacent to the Hijr unkissed except that the House was not completed upon the foundations of Ibrahim, peace be upon him."

It was also narrated in the book of Hajj from al-Qa'nabi, and in the chapter on the stories of the Prophets from Abd Allah ibn Yusuf, and Muslim from Yahya ibn Yahya and from the narration of Ibn Wahb, and al-Nasa'i from the narration of Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, all of them from Malik with this chain.

Muslim also narrated it from the narration of Nafi', who said: I heard Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah narrating to Abd Allah ibn Umar, from Aisha, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Were it not that your people are recent in jahiliyyah, or said: in disbelief, I would have spent the treasure of the Ka'bah in the way of Allah, and I would have made its door level with the ground, and I would have included the Hijr in it."

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on Surah 2, verses 126–128 (part 5 of 7):

Al-Bukhari said: Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Aswad, who said: Ibn al-Zubayr said to me: "A‘ishah used to confide many things to you, so what did she tell you about the Ka'bah?" He said: I said: She told me: The Prophet ﷺ said: "O A'ishah, were it not that your people are recently (converted) from disbelief" — Ibn al-Zubayr said: "with disbelief" — "I would have demolished the Ka'bah and made for it two doors: a door through which people enter, and a door through which they exit." So Ibn al-Zubayr did this.

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it, and he related it thus in the Book of Knowledge of his Sahih [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (126).]].

Muslim said in his Sahih: Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah informed us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "Were it not for the recent time of your people's disbelief, I would have demolished the Ka'bah and placed it upon the foundations of Ibrahim, for when Quraysh rebuilt the House they made it smaller, and I would have made for it a second door."

He said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb also narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Hisham, with this same chain. Muslim alone narrated it [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1333).]]. He said: Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Ibn Mahdi narrated to me: Sulaym ibn Hayyan narrated to us, from Sa'id — i.e., Ibn Mina' — who said: I heard Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr say: My maternal aunt — i.e., A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her — told me, she said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "O A'ishah, were it not that your people are recently (converted) from shirk, I would have demolished the Ka'bah and levelled it with the ground, and I would have made for it two doors: an eastern door and a western door, and I would have added to it six cubits from al-Hijr, for Quraysh reduced it when they built the Ka'bah." Muslim alone narrated it as well [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1333).]].

The mention of Quraysh's rebuilding of the Ka'bah after Ibrahim the Friend of Allah, upon him be peace, after a long period, and five years before the Prophet ﷺ's mission, and that he (ﷺ) carried stones with them when he was thirty-five years old, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him always until the Day of Religion.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said in the Sirah:

When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached thirty-five years of age, Quraysh gathered to rebuild the Ka'bah. They intended to roof it, and they feared to demolish it, for it was only walls raised above the height of a man. They wished to raise it and roof it. The reason was that a group of men stole the treasure of the Ka'bah, which was kept in a well inside the Ka'bah. The one in whose possession the treasure was found was Duwayk, a freedman of Banu Mulayh ibn 'Amr of Khuza'ah, and Quraysh cut off his hand. People claim that those who stole it placed it with Duwayk. The sea had cast a ship onto Jeddah belonging to a man from the Roman merchants, and it was wrecked, so they took its timber and prepared it for the roofing. There was a Coptic carpenter in Mecca, who prepared for them some of what would fix it. A serpent used to come out of the well of the Ka'bah, in which what was offered to it was thrown each day, and it would rise up onto the wall of the Ka'bah, and this was something they feared. No one came near it without it trembling, hissing and opening its mouth, so they feared it. One day, while it was rising onto the wall of the Ka'bah as it customarily did, Allah sent a bird to it which seized it and carried it away. Quraysh said: "We hope that Allah has approved what we intended. We have a skilled and gentle craftsman, we have timber, and Allah has spared us the serpent."

When they resolved upon demolishing and rebuilding it, Abu Wahb ibn 'Amr ibn 'A'idh ibn 'Abd ibn 'Imran ibn Makhzum stood up, took a stone from the Ka'bah, and it leapt from his hand until it returned to its place. He said: "O assembly of Quraysh, do not put into its building anything from your earnings except what is good; no wages of a prostitute, no interest from usury, and no injustice to anyone from among the people shall enter into it."

Ibn Ishaq said: People attribute this statement to al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar [[in A: "al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah ibn 'Umar ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar"]] ibn Makhzum [[Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah li-Ibn Ishaq (text no. 103), ed. Hamidullah, Morocco.]].

He said: Then Quraysh divided the Ka'bah: the side of the door belonged to Banu 'Abd Manaf and Zuhrah; the part between the Black Stone and the Yemeni Corner belonged to Banu Makhzum and tribes of Quraysh who had joined them; the back of the Ka'bah belonged to Banu Jumah and Sahm; and the side of al-Hijr belonged to Banu 'Abd al-Dar ibn Qusayy, Banu Asad ibn 'Abd al-'Uzza ibn Qusayy, and Banu 'Adi ibn Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy, and it is al-Hatim.

Then the people feared demolishing it and shrank from it. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah said: "I will begin you in demolishing it." He took the pickaxe, stood upon it, and said: "O Allah, do not be alarmed; O Allah, we intend only good." Then he demolished from the side of the two corners. The people waited that night and said: "We will see: if he is harmed, we will not demolish any part of it and will return it as it was; but if nothing befalls him, then Allah has approved what we have done." Al-Walid rose the next morning going about his work, and he demolished, and the people demolished with him, until the demolition reached the foundations of Ibrahim, upon him be peace, and they came upon green stones like spear-heads, each interlocking with the next [[Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah li-Ibn Ishaq (text no. 105), ed. Hamidullah, Morocco.]].

[Muhammad ibn Ishaq] said: One of those who narrate the report told me that a man from Quraysh, among those who were demolishing it, inserted a lever between two of its stones to pry one of them out, and when the stone moved, all of Mecca shook, so they ceased from that foundation [[Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah li-Ibn Ishaq (text no. 106), ed. Hamidullah, Morocco.]].

Ibn Ishaq said: Then the tribes of Quraysh gathered stones for its building, each tribe gathering separately, and then they built it, until the building reached the place of the Rukn — that is, the Black Stone — and they disputed over it, each tribe wishing to raise it to its place to the exclusion of the others, until they argued and disagreed and prepared for battle. Banu 'Abd al-Dar brought forward a bowl full of blood, then they and Banu 'Adi ibn Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy pledged themselves to death, and they dipped their hands into that blood in that bowl, and they were called "those who lick the blood." Quraysh remained in that state for four or five nights. Then they gathered in the mosque, consulted together, and sought fairness.

Some narrators of reports claim that Abu Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar ibn Makhzum — who was then the oldest of all Quraysh — said: "O assembly of Quraysh, make between you, in what you dispute, the first one who enters by the door of this mosque to judge between you concerning it." They did so, and the first to enter was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When they saw him, they said: "This is al-Amin; we are content. This is Muhammad." When he reached them and they informed him of the matter, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Bring me a garment." It was brought to him, and he took the Rukn — that is, the Black Stone — and placed it in it with his own hand. Then he said: "Let each tribe take hold of a side of the garment," and then [he said]: "Lift it all together." They did so, until they brought it to its place, and he placed it himself with his hand ﷺ. Then he built upon it.

Quraysh used to call the Messenger of Allah ﷺ "al-Amin" before revelation came to him. When they had finished the building and built it as they intended, al-Zubayr ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib said, regarding the matter of the serpent which Quraysh had feared in building the Ka'bah:

"I marvelled when the eagle swooped down upon the serpent, while it was in turmoil...
And it used to have a hiss, and at times it would leap up...
When we stood to lay the foundation, it resisted, terrifying us with the building, though it was itself feared...
When we feared its rebuke, an eagle came, swooping down upon it with a rush...
It gathered it to itself, then left us the building, which has no screen...
So we stood, gathered, to a building of which the foundations and the earth are ours...
On the morning we raised the foundation of it, and there were no garments upon those of us who levelled it...
The King honoured by it the Banu Lu'ayy, and none of its origin shall perish from among them...
Banu 'Adi and Murrah gathered there, and Kilab went before them...
So the King settled us in honour through that, and reward is sought from Allah."

Ibn Ishaq said: At the time of the Prophet ﷺ the Ka'bah was eighteen cubits high, and it used to be covered with Coptic cloth, then it was covered with striped garments, and the first to clothe it in brocade was al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf.

I say: It remained upon the building of Quraysh until it was burned at the beginning of the governorship of Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, after the year sixty AH, and in the last period of the reign of Yazid ibn Mu'awiyah, when they besieged Ibn al-Zubayr. At that time Ibn al-Zubayr demolished it to the ground and rebuilt it upon the foundations of Ibrahim, upon him be peace, and he included al-Hijr in it, and made for it an eastern door and a western door, both level with the ground, as he had heard this from his maternal aunt A'ishah, Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. It remained so throughout his governorship until al-Hajjaj killed him, and he restored it to what it had been, by the command of Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan to him in this, as Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj said in his Sahih:

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verses 126–128 (part 6 of 7):

Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us: Ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us: Ibn Abi Sulayman informed us, from 'Ata', who said: When the House (the Ka'bah) was burned during the time of Yazid ibn Mu'awiyah, when the people of al-Sham (Syria) attacked it, and what happened happened, Ibn al-Zubayr left it alone until the people came for the season (of Hajj), wanting to embolden them or rally them against the people of al-Sham. When the people had returned (from Mina), he said: "O people, advise me about the Ka'bah. Should I tear it down and rebuild it, or should I repair what has crumbled of it?" Ibn 'Abbas said: "As for me, my opinion on it has become clear: I see that you should repair what has crumbled of it, and leave the House on which the people embraced Islam and the stones on which the people embraced Islam and on which the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent." Ibn al-Zubayr said: "If one of them had his house burned, he would not be content until he renewed it, so how about the House of your Lord, Mighty and Majestic? I will seek guidance from my Lord for three days, and then I will firmly resolve on my decision." When three days had passed, he resolved to tear it down. The people shrank from this, fearing that something from heaven would descend upon the first person who climbed onto it, until a man climbed onto it and threw down some stones. When the people saw that nothing had befallen him, they followed suit and tore it down until they had brought it down to the ground. Ibn al-Zubayr then set up pillars over which he hung curtains, until its structure rose again. Ibn al-Zubayr said: "I heard 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, say that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Were it not that the people are recent in their disbelief, and I did not have enough expenditure to strengthen me in building it, I would have included in it five cubits from the Hijr (the semicircular enclosure beside the Ka'bah), and I would have made for it a door through which people enter and a door through which they exit.'" He said: "So now I have what I need to spend, and I do not fear the people." He said: "So he added five cubits from the Hijr to it, until he uncovered its foundations, which the people looked at, and then he built upon them." The Ka'bah had been eighteen cubits in height. When he added to it, he found it too short, so he increased its height by ten cubits, and he made for it two doors: one through which one enters, and the other through which one exits. When Ibn al-Zubayr was killed, al-Hajjaj wrote to 'Abd al-Malik informing him of this, and informing him that Ibn al-Zubayr had set the structure upon a foundation which the just men of Makkah had seen. 'Abd al-Malik wrote back to him: "We have nothing to do with Ibn al-Zubayr's defilement. As for what he added to its height, leave it. As for what he added to it from the Hijr, return it to its former structure, and block the door that he opened." So he tore it down and restored it to its former structure.

[Sahih Muslim, no. 1333.]

Al-Nasa'i has narrated it in his Sunan, from Hannad, from Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, from 'Ata', from Ibn al-Zubayr, from 'A'ishah, with only the marfu' (prophetic attribution) part of it, and he did not mention the narrative. The Sunnah (the prophetic practice) had been to approve what 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with him, had done, because he was the one whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had wished for. But the Prophet (ﷺ) feared that the hearts of some people would reject it, because of their recent conversion to Islam and their closeness to disbelief. However, this Sunnah remained hidden from 'Abd al-Malik, and therefore, when he confirmed from 'A'ishah that she had narrated this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "We wish that we had left it as it was, and what it had been entrusted to." As Muslim said:

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr and al-Walid ibn 'Ata' narrating from al-Harith ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Rabi'ah. 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayd said: al-Harith ibn 'Abd Allah came as a delegation to 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan during his caliphate. 'Abd al-Malik said: "I do not think that Abu Khubayb (i.e., Ibn al-Zubayr) heard from 'A'ishah what he claimed he heard from her." al-Harith said: "Yes, I heard it from her myself." He said: "What did you hear her say?" He said: "She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Your people made the House short in its construction, and were it not for the recency of their association with polytheism, I would have restored what they left of it. If it becomes apparent to your people after me that they should rebuild it, then come, and I will show you what they left of it.'" So she showed him about seven cubits of it.

[Sahih Muslim, no. 1333.]

This is the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr. al-Walid ibn 'Ata' added to it: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I would have made for it two doors placed level with the ground, one facing east and the other facing west. Do you know why your people raised its door?" She said: "I said: No." He said: "Out of pride, so that none would enter it except those whom they wanted. A man would come wanting to enter it, and they would let him climb up, and when he was about to enter, they would push him and he would fall." 'Abd al-Malik said: "I asked al-Harith: Did you hear her say this?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then he tapped the ground with his stick for a while, and then said: 'I wish I had left it and what it had been entrusted with.'"

Muslim said: Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Jabalah narrated to us: Abu 'Asim narrated to us (transition); and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us; both of them from Ibn Jurayj with this chain, like the hadith of Ibn Bakr.

[Sahih Muslim, no. 1333.]

He said: Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: 'Abd Allah ibn Bakr al-Sahmi narrated to us: Hatim ibn Abi Saghirah narrated to us, from Abu Qaza'ah, that 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, while he was circumambulating the House, said: "May Allah fight Ibn al-Zubayr, for he lies about the Mother of the Believers. He claims: 'I heard her say: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O 'A'ishah, were it not for the recency of your people's disbelief, I would have torn down the House and added to it from the Hijr, for your people fell short in its construction."'" al-Harith ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Rabi'ah said: "Do not say this, O Commander of the Faithful, for I heard the Mother of the Believers narrate this." He said: "If I had heard it before I demolished it, I would have left it as Ibn al-Zubayr built it."

[Sahih Muslim, no. 1333.]

This hadith is almost definitively attributed to 'A'ishah, the Mother of the Believers, because it has been narrated from her through multiple sound chains, from al-Aswad ibn Yazid, al-Harith ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Rabi'ah, 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, and 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr. This indicates the correctness of what Ibn al-Zubayr did, and had it been left alone, it would have been good.

However, after the matter had returned to this state, some scholars disliked changing it from its condition. It is reported that the Commander of the Faithful Harun al-Rashid (or his father al-Mahdi) asked Imam Malik about demolishing the Ka'bah and restoring it to what Ibn al-Zubayr had done. Malik said to him: "O Commander of the Faithful, do not make the House of Allah a plaything for kings. No one wishes to demolish it except that it will be demolished." So al-Rashid abandoned that.

This was transmitted by Iyad and al-Nawawi. And it remains so, Allah knows best, until the end of time, until Dhu al-Suwaykatayn from Ethiopia destroys it, as is established in the two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim) from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Dhu al-Suwaykatayn from Ethiopia will destroy the Ka'bah." Both of them narrated it.

[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1596; Sahih Muslim, no. 2909.]

And from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "As if I see him: black, bow-legged, pulling it out stone by stone." Al-Bukhari narrated it.

[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1595.]

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said in his Musnad: Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Malik al-Harrani narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, may Allah be pleased with both of them, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Dhu al-Suwaykatayn from Ethiopia will destroy the Ka'bah, and will strip it of its ornaments and remove its covering. As if I can see him: bald, with receding hair, striking at it with his pickaxe and his mattock."

[Musnad, 2/220.]

Al-Fada' means a twist between the foot and the shin bone.

This, Allah knows best, will only occur after the emergence of Ya'juj and Ma'juj (Gog and Magog), because of what came in Sahih al-Bukhari from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The House will certainly be visited for Hajj and 'Umrah after the emergence of Ya'juj and Ma'juj."

[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1593.]

* *

Allah's statement, relating the supplication of Ibrahim and Isma'il, peace be upon them: ﴿Our Lord, make us submissive to You, and from our descendants a community submissive to You, and show us our rites and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾

Ibn Jarir said: They mean by this: "Make us submitting to Your command, humbled before Your obedience, not associating with You in obedience anyone other than You, nor in worship anyone besides You."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us: Isma'il ibn Raja' ibn Hayyan al-Husni al-Qurashi narrated to us: Ma'qil ibn 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Karim, regarding ﴿and make us submissive to You﴾, he said: "Sincere to You." ﴿And from our descendants a community submissive to You﴾, he said: "A sincere community."

He also said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us: al-Muqaddami narrated to us: Sa'id ibn 'Amir narrated to us, from Sallam ibn Abi Mut'i concerning this verse, ﴿make us submissive to You﴾, he said: "They were both submitting, but they asked Him for steadfastness."

'Ikrimah said regarding ﴿Our Lord, make us submissive to You﴾: "Allah said: I have done it." ﴿And from our descendants a community submissive to You﴾: "Allah said: I have done it."

Al-Suddi said regarding ﴿and from our descendants a community submissive to You﴾: "They meant the Arabs."

Ibn Jarir said: The correct view is that it encompasses the Arabs and others, because among the descendants of Ibrahim are the Children of Israel, and Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And among the people of Musa is a community who guide by the truth and act justly by it﴾ [al-A'raf: 159].

I say: What Ibn Jarir said does not negate what al-Suddi said, for specifying them with this does not exclude others. The context is indeed about the Arabs, and this is why He said after it: ﴿Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses, and teach them the Book and wisdom, and purify them﴾ to the end of the verse. What is meant by this is Muhammad (ﷺ), and he was indeed sent among them, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿It is He who sent among the unlettered a messenger from themselves﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 2]. Nevertheless, this does not negate his message being sent to the red and the black, based on Allah the Exalted's saying: ﴿Say: O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all﴾ [al-A'raf: 158], and other conclusive proofs.

This prayer was made by Ibrahim and Isma'il, peace be upon them both, just as Allah the Exalted related about His righteous, believing servants in His words: ﴿And those who say, "Our Lord, grant us from among our wives and offspring comfort to our eyes, and make us leaders for the righteous."﴾ [al-Furqan: 74]. This measure is legislatively desirable, for it is part of the completeness of love for the worship of Allah the Exalted that a person loves that from his own loins there should come one who worships Allah alone, with no partner. For this reason, when Allah the Exalted said to Ibrahim, peace be upon him: ﴿Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people,﴾ he said: ﴿And from my descendants?" He said, "My covenant does not include the wrongdoers.﴾ This is His saying: ﴿And keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols.﴾ [Ibrahim: 35].

It is established in Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When the son of Adam dies, his deeds are cut off except for three: ongoing charity (sadaqah jariyah), knowledge from which benefit is gained, or a righteous child who prays for him." [Sahih Muslim, no. (1631).]

"And show us our rites (manasik)." Ibn Juraij said, from 'Ata', regarding ﴿And show us our rites⁠﴾: bring them out for us, teach them to us. [In C, T: "And taught them to us."]

Mujahid said: "﴿And show us our rites﴾: our slaughtering places." Similar was narrated from 'Ata' as well, and from Qatadah.

Sa'id ibn Mansur said: Attab ibn Bashir narrated to us, from Khusayf, from Mujahid, who said: Ibrahim said, "Show us our rites," so Jibril came to him and took him to the House. He said: "Raise the foundations." So he raised the foundations and completed the building. Then he took his hand, brought him out, and went with him to al-Safa. He said: "This is from the symbols of Allah." Then he went with him to al-Marwah and said: "And this is from the symbols of Allah?" Then he went with him toward Mina. When they reached the 'Aqabah, behold, Iblis was standing by the tree. He said: "Say the takbir and throw at him." So he said the takbir and threw. Then Iblis moved and stood at the middle jamrah. When Jibril and Ibrahim passed by him, he said to him: "Say the takbir and throw at him." So he said the takbir and threw. Then Iblis departed, for the wretch had wanted to introduce something into the Hajj but could not, so he took Ibrahim by the hand until he brought him to al-Mash'ar al-Haram, and said: "This is al-Mash'ar al-Haram." Then he took Ibrahim by the hand until he brought him to 'Arafat. He said: "Do you know what I have shown you?" He said it three times. He said: "Yes."

Similar was narrated from Abu Mijlaz and Qatadah. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Abu al-'Asim al-Ghanawi, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Ibrahim was shown the commands of the rites, Satan appeared to him at al-Mas'a, so Ibrahim raced him. Then Jibril took him on until he brought him to Mina and said: "This is the resting place of the people." When he reached the Jamrat al-'Aqabah, Satan confronted him, and he threw seven pebbles at him until he departed. Then he brought him to the middle jamrah, and Satan confronted him, and he threw seven pebbles until he departed. Then he brought him to the furthest jamrah, and Satan confronted him, and he threw seven pebbles until he departed. Then he brought him to Jam'an and said: "This is al-Mash'ar." Then he brought him to 'Arafah and said: "This is 'Arafah." Jibril said to him: "Have you recognized it?" [Musnad al-Tayalisi, no. (2697).]

Allah says, relating the completion of Ibrahim's supplication for the people of the Sacred Precinct: "Our Lord, send among them a messenger from themselves," that is, from the descendants of Ibrahim. This answered supplication coincided with Allah's pre-decreed destiny in appointing Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him [in manuscript C: "may Allah bless him and grant him peace"], as a messenger to the unlettered (ummiyyin) among them, and to all the non-Arabs (a'jamiyyin) of mankind and the jinn, as Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Salih related to us, from Sa'id ibn Suwayd al-Kalbi, from Abd al-A'la ibn Hilal al-Sulami, from al-Irbad ibn Sariyah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed I am, with Allah, the Seal of the Prophets, while Adam was still lying in his clay. I will inform you of the beginning of that: it is the supplication of my father Ibrahim, the good news of Isa concerning me, and the vision my mother saw; and thus the mothers of the prophets see visions." [Musnad (4/127).]

And thus it was narrated by Ibn Wahb, al-Layth, and his scribe Abd Allah ibn Salih, from Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam followed him in narrating it from Sa'id ibn Suwayd, with the same wording.

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu al-Nadr related to us, al-Faraj related to us, Luqman ibn Amir related to us: I heard Abu Umamah say: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what was the beginning of your matter?" He said: "The supplication of my father Ibrahim, the good news of Isa concerning me, and my mother saw that a light came out from her by which the palaces of Syria were illuminated." [Musnad (5/262).]

The meaning is that the first to mention his name and make it known among the people was Ibrahim, peace be upon him. His mention remained among the people, noted, famous and spreading, until the seal of the prophets of the Children of Israel by lineage, who is Isa son of Maryam, peace be upon him, made his name clear when he stood among the Children of Israel preaching and said: ﴿Indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you, confirming what was before me of the Torah and giving good news of a messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad﴾ [al-Saff: 6]. For this reason, in this hadith he said: "the supplication of my father Ibrahim, and the good news of Isa son of Maryam."

* *

As for his saying: "my mother saw that a light came out from her by which the palaces of Syria were illuminated," it is said that it was a dream she saw when she was pregnant with him, and she related it to her people, so it spread among them and became known, and this was a preparation. Specifying Syria for the manifestation of his light is a sign of the establishment and firmness of his religion in the lands of Syria. For this reason, at the end of time Syria will be a stronghold for Islam and its people, and Isa son of Maryam will descend there, at Damascus, at the white eastern minaret. For this reason it came in the two Sahihs: "A group of my community will continue to be victorious upon the truth, not harmed by those who forsake them or oppose them, until the command of Allah comes while they are still so." [This is the wording of the hadith of Thawban in Sahih Muslim, no. (1920); it is also narrated in similar form from the hadith of Mu'awiyah, no. (1037), and it is in Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (7460), from the hadith of Mu'awiyah radiyallahu anhu, no. (7459), from the hadith of al-Mughirah radiyallahu anhu.] And in Sahih al-Bukhari: "and they are in Syria." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (7460), from the hadith of Mu'adh radiyallahu anhu.]

Abu Ja'far al-Razi said, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliyah, regarding His saying: ﴿Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from themselves﴾, that it refers to the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). It was said to him: "It has been answered for you, and it will occur at the end of time." Al-Suddi and Qatadah said likewise.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and teach them the Book﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿and the wisdom﴾, meaning the Sunnah, as said by al-Hasan, Qatadah, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Abu Malik and others. It was also said: it is understanding in the religion. There is no contradiction.

﴿And purify them﴾. Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn Abbas: it means obedience to Allah and sincerity.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said regarding ﴿and teach them the Book and the wisdom﴾: he teaches them good so that they do it, and evil so that they avoid it, and informs them of His pleasure with them when they obey Him and increase in obedience to Him, and of avoiding what displeases Him through disobedience.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed You, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾, meaning: the Mighty, whom nothing can overpower, who is capable of all things, the Wise in His actions and His words, who places things in their proper places; and His wisdom and His justice.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 130–132:

He, blessed and exalted, says, refuting the disbelievers for the shirk (association of others with Allah) they invented and introduced, which contradicts the religion of Ibrahim al-Khalil (Abraham, the intimate friend of Allah), the leader of the ḥunafā' (those who turn away from falsehood to pure monotheism). He devoted the worship of his Lord, blessed and exalted, to Him alone, did not invoke anyone alongside Him, did not associate anything with Him even for the blink of an eye, and disowned every object of worship other than Him. In this he opposed all his people, to the point that he disowned his own father. He said: ﴿O my people, I am free from what you associate with Allah. Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, as a ḥanīf, and I am not of those who associate others with Allah﴾ [al-An'am: 78–79]. He, exalted is He, also said: ﴿And when Ibrahim said to his father and his people, "Indeed, I am free from what you worship, except He who created me, for indeed He will guide me"﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 26–27]. He, exalted is He, also said: ﴿And the request of forgiveness by Ibrahim for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disassociated himself from him. Indeed, Ibrahim was tender-hearted and forbearing﴾ [al-Tawbah: 114]. He, exalted is He, also said: ﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was a community (ummah) devoutly obedient to Allah, a ḥanīf, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah. He was grateful for His favours. He chose him and guided him to a straight path. And We gave him good in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter he is among the righteous﴾ [al-Nahl: 120–122].

For these reasons and similar ones, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And who would turn away from the religion of Ibrahim﴾, meaning: from his way and his method, so that one would oppose it and turn away from it. ﴿except one who makes a fool of himself﴾, meaning: one who wrongs himself through his foolishness and bad judgment, by abandoning the truth for misguidance. He opposed the path of the one whom Allah chose in this world for guidance and rectitude, from his youth until Allah took him as a khalīl. And in the Hereafter he is among the righteous, the blessed. Yet such a person abandoned his path, his way and his religion, and followed the paths of misguidance and error. What folly is greater than this? Or what injustice is greater than this? As Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, association [with Allah] is a great injustice﴾.

Abu al-'Aliyah and Qatadah said: this verse was revealed concerning the Jews, who introduced a way that is not from Allah and opposed the religion of Ibrahim in what they had innovated. The saying of Allah, exalted is He, supports the soundness of this view: ﴿Ibrahim was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a ḥanīf, a Muslim, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah. Indeed, the people most worthy of Ibrahim are those who followed him, and this Prophet, and those who believe. And Allah is the Guardian of the believers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 67–68].

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When his Lord said to him, "Submit," he said, "I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds"﴾, meaning: Allah commanded him to devote himself sincerely to Him, to surrender and to submit, and he complied with that, both by legislation and by decree (shar'an wa qadaran).

* *

His saying: ﴿And Abraham instructed his sons, and [so did] Jacob﴾, meaning: he enjoined this religion, which is Islam, for Allah. [Or the pronoun refers to the statement: ﴿I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds﴾.] Because of their eagerness for it and their love for it, they remained steadfast in it until death, and they instructed their sons with it after them. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He made it a lasting word among his descendants﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 28]. Some of the salaf (early generations) recited "wa Ya'qūba" with a fatḥah (naṣb), as a conjunction with "banīhi" (his sons), as if Ibrahim instructed his sons and his grandson Ya'qub ibn Ishaq, who was present at that. Al-Qushayri has claimed, as al-Qurtubi reported from him, that Ya'qub was born only after the death of Ibrahim. Such a claim requires a sound proof. The apparent position, and Allah knows best, is that Ya'qub was born to Ishaq during the lifetime of the Khalil and Sarah, because the glad tidings were given to them both in His saying: ﴿So We gave her the good news of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub﴾ [Hud: 71]. It has also been recited with the naṣb of Ya'qub here, by omitting the preposition (naz' al-khāfid). If Ya'qub had not existed during their lifetimes, mentioning him among the descendants of Ishaq would have had no great benefit. Also, Allah said in Surat al-'Ankabut: ﴿And We gave him Ishaq and Ya'qub, and We placed in his descendants prophethood and the Scripture, and We gave him his reward in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter he is among the righteous﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 27, the verse]. In another verse He said: ﴿And We gave him Ishaq and Ya'qub as an additional gift﴾ [al-Anbiya': 72]. This indicates that he existed during Ibrahim's lifetime. Also, Ibrahim built Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem's sacred house), as the earlier Scriptures state, and it is established in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abu Dharr: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, which mosque was built first?" He said: "al-Masjid al-Haram." I said: "Then which?" He said: "Bayt al-Maqdis." I said: "How long between them?" He said: "Forty years." [al-Hadith]. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3366; Sahih Muslim, no. 520.] Ibn Hibban claimed that between Sulayman, whom it was believed built Bayt al-Maqdis (though he had only renewed it after its destruction and adorned it), and Ibrahim there were forty years. This has been criticised against Ibn Hibban, since the period between them exceeds thousands of years, and Allah knows best. Also, the mention of Ya'qub's instruction to his sons will come shortly, and this indicates that he was among those who gave instructions here.

* *

His saying: ﴿O my sons, indeed Allah has chosen for you this religion, so do not die except as Muslims﴾, meaning: do good during your lifetime and hold fast to this, so that Allah grants you a death upon it. A person generally dies upon what he was upon, and is resurrected upon what he died upon. Allah, the Generous, has made it His custom that whoever intends good is granted success in it and it is made easy for him, and whoever intends righteousness is steadfast in it. This does not contradict what has come in the [Sahih] hadith: "Indeed, a man may do the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is between him and it only a cubit or an arm's length, and then the Decree overtakes him, and he does the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it. And indeed, a man may do the deeds of the people of the Fire until there is between him and it only a cubit or an arm's length, and then the Decree overtakes him, and he does the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters it." [In the other narrations (jīm, ṭ, a, w): "enters the Fire".] This is because some narrations of this hadith state: "He does the deeds of the people of Paradise in what appears to the people, and does the deeds of the people of the Fire in what appears to the people." Allah, exalted is He, has said: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah, and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease. But as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward hardship﴾ [al-Layl: 5–10].

He said: "al-Masjid al-Haram." I said: "Then which?" He said: "Bayt al-Maqdis." I said: "How long between them?" He said: "Forty years." [al-Hadith]. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3366; Sahih Muslim, no. 520.] Ibn Hibban claimed that between Sulayman, whom it was believed built Bayt al-Maqdis (though he had only renewed it after its destruction and adorned it), and Ibrahim there were forty years. This has been criticised against Ibn Hibban, since the period between them exceeds thousands of years, and Allah knows best. Also, the mention of Ya'qub's instruction to his sons will come shortly, and this indicates that he was among those who gave instructions here.

* *

His saying: ﴿O my sons, indeed Allah has chosen for you this religion, so do not die except as Muslims﴾, meaning: do good during your lifetime and hold fast to this, so that Allah grants you a death upon it. A person generally dies upon what he was upon, and is resurrected upon what he died upon. Allah, the Generous, has made it His custom that whoever intends good is granted success in it and it is made easy for him, and whoever intends righteousness is steadfast in it. This does not contradict what has come in the [Sahih] hadith: "Indeed, a man may do the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is between him and it only a cubit or an arm's length, and then the Decree overtakes him, and he does the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it. And indeed, a man may do the deeds of the people of the Fire until there is between him and it only a cubit or an arm's length, and then the Decree overtakes him, and he does the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters it." [In the other narrations (jīm, ṭ, a, w): "enters the Fire".] This is because some narrations of this hadith state: "He does the deeds of the people of Paradise in what appears to the people, and does the deeds of the people of the Fire in what appears to the people." Allah, exalted is He, has said: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah, and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease. But as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward hardship﴾ [al-Layl: 5–10].

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 130–132:

He, blessed and exalted, says, refuting the disbelievers for the shirk (association of others with Allah) they invented and introduced, which contradicts the religion of Ibrahim al-Khalil (Abraham, the intimate friend of Allah), the leader of the ḥunafā' (those who turn away from falsehood to pure monotheism). He devoted the worship of his Lord, blessed and exalted, to Him alone, did not invoke anyone alongside Him, did not associate anything with Him even for the blink of an eye, and disowned every object of worship other than Him. In this he opposed all his people, to the point that he disowned his own father. He said: ﴿O my people, I am free from what you associate with Allah. Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, as a ḥanīf, and I am not of those who associate others with Allah﴾ [al-An'am: 78–79]. He, exalted is He, also said: ﴿And when Ibrahim said to his father and his people, "Indeed, I am free from what you worship, except He who created me, for indeed He will guide me"﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 26–27]. He, exalted is He, also said: ﴿And the request of forgiveness by Ibrahim for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disassociated himself from him. Indeed, Ibrahim was tender-hearted and forbearing﴾ [al-Tawbah: 114]. He, exalted is He, also said: ﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was a community (ummah) devoutly obedient to Allah, a ḥanīf, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah. He was grateful for His favours. He chose him and guided him to a straight path. And We gave him good in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter he is among the righteous﴾ [al-Nahl: 120–122].

For these reasons and similar ones, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And who would turn away from the religion of Ibrahim﴾, meaning: from his way and his method, so that one would oppose it and turn away from it. ﴿except one who makes a fool of himself﴾, meaning: one who wrongs himself through his foolishness and bad judgment, by abandoning the truth for misguidance. He opposed the path of the one whom Allah chose in this world for guidance and rectitude, from his youth until Allah took him as a khalīl. And in the Hereafter he is among the righteous, the blessed. Yet such a person abandoned his path, his way and his religion, and followed the paths of misguidance and error. What folly is greater than this? Or what injustice is greater than this? As Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, association [with Allah] is a great injustice﴾.

Abu al-'Aliyah and Qatadah said: this verse was revealed concerning the Jews, who introduced a way that is not from Allah and opposed the religion of Ibrahim in what they had innovated. The saying of Allah, exalted is He, supports the soundness of this view: ﴿Ibrahim was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a ḥanīf, a Muslim, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah. Indeed, the people most worthy of Ibrahim are those who followed him, and this Prophet, and those who believe. And Allah is the Guardian of the believers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 67–68].

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When his Lord said to him, "Submit," he said, "I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds"﴾, meaning: Allah commanded him to devote himself sincerely to Him, to surrender and to submit, and he complied with that, both by legislation and by decree (shar'an wa qadaran).

* *

His saying: ﴿And Abraham instructed his sons, and [so did] Jacob﴾, meaning: he enjoined this religion, which is Islam, for Allah. [Or the pronoun refers to the statement: ﴿I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds﴾.] Because of their eagerness for it and their love for it, they remained steadfast in it until death, and they instructed their sons with it after them. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He made it a lasting word among his descendants﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 28]. Some of the salaf (early generations) recited "wa Ya'qūba" with a fatḥah (naṣb), as a conjunction with "banīhi" (his sons), as if Ibrahim instructed his sons and his grandson Ya'qub ibn Ishaq, who was present at that. Al-Qushayri has claimed, as al-Qurtubi reported from him, that Ya'qub was born only after the death of Ibrahim. Such a claim requires a sound proof. The apparent position, and Allah knows best, is that Ya'qub was born to Ishaq during the lifetime of the Khalil and Sarah, because the glad tidings were given to them both in His saying: ﴿So We gave her the good news of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub﴾ [Hud: 71]. It has also been recited with the naṣb of Ya'qub here, by omitting the preposition (naz' al-khāfid). If Ya'qub had not existed during their lifetimes, mentioning him among the descendants of Ishaq would have had no great benefit. Also, Allah said in Surat al-'Ankabut: ﴿And We gave him Ishaq and Ya'qub, and We placed in his descendants prophethood and the Scripture, and We gave him his reward in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter he is among the righteous﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 27, the verse]. In another verse He said: ﴿And We gave him Ishaq and Ya'qub as an additional gift﴾ [al-Anbiya': 72]. This indicates that he existed during Ibrahim's lifetime. Also, Ibrahim built Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem's sacred house), as the earlier Scriptures state, and it is established in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abu Dharr: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, which mosque was built first?" He said: "al-Masjid al-Haram." I said: "Then which?" He said: "Bayt al-Maqdis." I said: "How long between them?" He said: "Forty years." [al-Hadith]. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3366; Sahih Muslim, no. 520.] Ibn Hibban claimed that between Sulayman, whom it was believed built Bayt al-Maqdis (though he had only renewed it after its destruction and adorned it), and Ibrahim there were forty years. This has been criticised against Ibn Hibban, since the period between them exceeds thousands of years, and Allah knows best. Also, the mention of Ya'qub's instruction to his sons will come shortly, and this indicates that he was among those who gave instructions here.

And indeed, a man may do the deeds of the people of the Fire until there is between him and it only a cubit or an arm's length, and then the Decree overtakes him, and he does the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters it." Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 2, verses 133–134:

Allah, exalted is He, says, presenting an argument against the polytheists among the Arabs, the descendants of Isma'il, and against the disbelievers among the Children of Israel, namely Ya'qub (Jacob) son of Ishaq (Isaac) son of Ibrahim (Abraham), upon them be peace [[في ط: "عليه".]], that when Ya'qub was approaching death, he enjoined upon his sons the worship of Allah alone, with no partner for Him. He said to them: ﴿What will you worship after me?﴾ They said: ﴿We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Ibrahim, Isma'il and Ishaq, one God.﴾ This is by way of ta'ghlib (the figure of speech in which one term covers a broader group), because Isma'il was his paternal uncle.

Al-Nahhas said: The Arabs call the paternal uncle "father." This was related by al-Qurtubi. Those who treat the paternal grandfather (jadd) as a father and use him to exclude the siblings (hajb al-ikhwah) have also cited this verse, as is the view of al-Siddiq (Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him), which al-Bukhari related from him through the chain of Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr. Then al-Bukhari said: "No one differed with him on this." To this view went 'A'isha, the Mother of the Believers, and it is what al-Hasan al-Basri, Tawus and 'Ata' said. It is the school of Abu Hanifa and of many scholars of the early and later generations. Malik, al-Shafi'i and Ahmad, in the well-known report from him, said that the grandfather shares the inheritance with the siblings (yuqasimu al-ikhwah). Malik related from 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, Zayd ibn Thabit and a group of the early and later generations this same view, and it was chosen by the two companions of Abu Hanifa, the judge Abu Yusuf and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan. The discussion of this matter has another place.

* *

His saying: ﴿One God﴾ means: we declare Him one in divinity, and we associate nothing else with Him. ﴿And to Him we are Muslims﴾ means: obedient and submissive to Him, as Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿To Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and to Him they will be returned﴾ [Al 'Imran: 83]. Islam is the religion of all the prophets, even though their laws varied and their methods differed, as Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no god but Me, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiya': 25]. The verses on this are numerous, and so are the hadiths. Among them is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "We, the company of the prophets, are the sons of 'Allat (half-brothers); our religion is one." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3443, from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him. Awlad 'Allat are brothers who share a father but have different mothers.]

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is a community that has passed away﴾, meaning: it has gone. ﴿It will have what it earned, and you will have what you earned﴾, meaning: the predecessors among your fathers, the prophets and the righteous, will not benefit you by your ancestry to them if you do not do good that returns its benefit to you. For them are their deeds, which they performed, and for you are your deeds: ﴿And you will not be asked about what they used to do.﴾

Abu al-'Aliya, al-Rabi' and Qatada said: ﴿That is a community that has passed away﴾ refers to Ibrahim, Isma'il, Ishaq, Ya'qub and the Asbat (the tribes descended from the sons of Ya'qub). For this reason it has come in a report: "Whoever is held back by his deeds, his lineage will not hasten him forward."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 135:

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad related to me, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah related to me, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'Abdullah ibn Suriya al-A'war said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Guidance is nothing but what we follow, so follow us, O Muhammad, and you will be guided." The Christians said the same. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And they say: "Be Jews or Christians, you will be guided."﴾

* *

As for His saying ﴿Rather, [we follow] the religion of Abraham, a hanif﴾: meaning, we do not want what you call us to of Judaism or Christianity, but rather we follow ﴿the religion of Abraham, a hanif﴾, that is, upright. This was said by Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and Isa ibn Jariyah.

Khasif related from Mujahid: "sincere (mukhlisan)." 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: "one who performs hajj (hajjan)." Similarly it was related from al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, 'Atiyyah, and al-Suddi.

Abu al-'Aliyah said: The hanif is one who faces the House (the Ka'bah) in his prayer, and believes that the hajj is obligatory upon him if he is able to make the journey to it.

Mujahid and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "hanifan" means "following (mutta'iban)." Abu Qilabah said: The hanif is one who believes in all the messengers, from the first of them to the last of them.

Qatadah said: The hanifiyyah is the testimony that there is no god but Allah. It includes the prohibition of mothers, daughters, maternal aunts, paternal aunts, and what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden, and circumcision.

Allah, exalted is He, guided His believing servants to believe in what was revealed to them through His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ in detail, and in what was revealed to the earlier prophets in summary. He specified some of the messengers by name and summarized the mention of the rest of the prophets, and [He commanded] that they not differentiate between any of them, but believe in all of them, and not be like those about whom Allah said: ﴿And they wish to make a distinction between Allah and His messengers, and say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and they wish to adopt a way between that. Those are the disbelievers in truth.﴾ [An-Nisa: 150-151].

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, ʿUthman ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, ʿAli ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The People of the Book would read the Torah in Hebrew and explain it in Arabic to the people of Islam. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not believe the People of the Book, nor disbelieve them, but say: 'We believe in Allah and in what has been revealed to us.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4485].

Muslim, Abu Dawud and al-Nasai related from the hadith of ʿUthman ibn Hakim, from Saʿid ibn Yasar, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ most often prayed the two rak'ahs before Fajr with ﴿We believe in Allah and in what has been revealed to us﴾, the verse, and the other with ﴿We believe in Allah, and bear witness that we are Muslims﴾ [Al ʿImran: 52]. [Sahih Muslim, no. 727; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1259; Sunan al-Nasai (2/155).]

Abu al-ʿAliyah, al-Rabiʿ and Qatadah said: The *asbat* (tribes): the sons of Yaʿqub, twelve men; each one of them fathered a nation of people, and so they were called the *asbat*.

Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad and others said: the *asbat* among the Children of Israel are like the tribes among the Children of Ismaʿil. Al-Zamakhshari said in al-Kashshaf: the *asbat* are the descendants (*hafadah*) of Yaʿqub, the offspring of his twelve sons. Al-Razi transmitted this from him, affirmed it, and did not object to it. Al-Bukhari said: the *asbat* are the tribes of the Children of Israel. This implies that what is meant by *asbat* here is the peoples (*shuʿub*) of the Children of Israel, and what Allah revealed to the prophets among them, as Musa said to them: ﴿Remember the favour of Allah upon you when He made among you prophets and made you kings and gave you what He had not given anyone among the worlds.﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 20]. And Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We divided them into twelve tribes, as nations﴾ [Al-A'raf: 160].

Al-Qurtubi said: They were called *asbat* from *sibt*, which means succession; they are a group in succession. It was also said: its root is *al-sabat* (with a fatha on the ba'), meaning a tree, i.e., in their multitude they are like a single tree whose branches (*sabatah*) are many. Al-Zajjaj said: What makes this clear to you is what Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Anbari narrated to us: Abu Nujayd al-Daqqaq narrated to us, al-Aswad ibn ʿAmir narrated to us, Israil narrated to us from Simak, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: All the prophets were from the Children of Israel except ten: Nuh, Hud, Salih, Shuʿayb, Ibrahim, Lut, Ishaq, Yaʿqub, Ismaʿil and Muhammad, peace be upon them. Al-Qurtubi said: *al-sibt* means a group and a tribe that trace back to one origin.

Qatadah said: Allah commanded the believers to believe in Him, and to affirm His books, all of them, and His messengers.

Sulayman ibn Habib said: We were only commanded to believe in the Torah and the Gospel, and not to act upon what is in them.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mus'ab al-Suri narrated to us, Mu'ammal narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allah ibn Abi Humayd narrated to us, from Abu al-Malih, from Maʿqil ibn Yasar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Believe in the Torah, the Psalms and the Gospel, and let the Qur'an suffice you." [Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/400). In its chain is ʿUbayd Allah ibn Abi Humayd, who is agreed to be weak, and who narrates strange reports from Abu al-Malih. See: al-Mizan (3/5) and al-Tahdhib (7/9).]

Allah says: ﴿And if they believe﴾ (i.e., the disbelievers among the People of the Book and others) ﴿in the like of what you believe﴾ (O believers), of believing in all the Books of Allah and His Messengers, and they make no distinction between any of them, ﴿then they are guided﴾ (i.e., they have attained the truth and been directed to it). ﴿But if they turn away﴾ (i.e., from the truth to falsehood) after the proof has been established against them, ﴿then they are only in opposition. So Allah will suffice you against them﴾ (i.e., He will give you victory over them and make you prevail over them), ﴿and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was read to Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la, who said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Ziyad ibn Yunus narrated to us, Nafi' ibn Abi Nu'aym narrated to us, who said: Some of the caliphs sent to me the Mushaf of 'Uthman ibn 'Affan so that I might repair it. Ziyad said: I said to him: "People say that his Mushaf was in his lap when he was killed, and blood fell upon ﴿So Allah will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾." Nafi' said: My eyes saw the blood upon this verse, and it had been [...]. [Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/402).]

* *

His saying: ﴿The dye of Allah﴾. Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "The religion of Allah." It is also narrated similarly from Mujahid, Abu al-'Aliyah, 'Ikrimah, Ibrahim, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, 'Abdullah ibn Kathir, 'Ata' al-'Awfi, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and al-Suddi.

The grammatical status (i'rab) of ﴿The dye of Allah﴾ is either as a warning (al-igra') (a form of exhortation to hold to something), like His saying ﴿the fitrah of Allah﴾ [al-Rum: 30], meaning: "Adhere to that, upon you is it." Some of them said it is a substitute (badal) for His saying: ﴿the religion of Ibrahim﴾. Sibawayh said: it is an emphatic verbal noun (masdar mu'akkad) in the accusative, governed by His saying ﴿We believe in Allah﴾, like His saying ﴿and worship Allah﴾ [al-Nisa': 36].

A hadith has been transmitted, related by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh, through the narration of Ash'ath ibn Ishaq from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The Children of Israel said: 'O Musa, does your Lord dye?' Musa said: 'Fear Allah.' Then his Lord called to him: 'O Musa, they asked you whether your Lord dyes? Say: Yes, I dye the colours: the red, the white and the black, and all colours are of My dye.'" And Allah revealed to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿The dye of Allah, and who is better than Allah in dye?﴾ [Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/403), and from his route Abu al-Shaykh in al-'Azamah, no. 138.]

This is how it occurs in the narration of Ibn Mardawayh as a marfu' (attributed to the Prophet) report, whereas in the narration of Ibn Abi Hatim it is mawquf (attributed to Ibn 'Abbas), and the latter is more likely, if its chain is sound. And Allah knows best.

Allah says: ﴿And if they believe﴾ (i.e., the disbelievers among the People of the Book and others) ﴿in the like of what you believe﴾ (O believers), of believing in all the Books of Allah and His Messengers, and they make no distinction between any of them, ﴿then they are guided﴾ (i.e., they have attained the truth and been directed to it). ﴿But if they turn away﴾ (i.e., from the truth to falsehood) after the proof has been established against them, ﴿then they are only in opposition. So Allah will suffice you against them﴾ (i.e., He will give you victory over them and make you prevail over them), ﴿and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was read to Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la, who said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Ziyad ibn Yunus narrated to us, Nafi' ibn Abi Nu'aym narrated to us, who said: Some of the caliphs sent to me the Mushaf of 'Uthman ibn 'Affan so that I might repair it. Ziyad said: I said to him: "People say that his Mushaf was in his lap when he was killed, and blood fell upon ﴿So Allah will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾." Nafi' said: My eyes saw the blood upon this verse, and it had been [...]. [Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/402).]

* *

His saying: ﴿The dye of Allah﴾. Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "The religion of Allah." It is also narrated similarly from Mujahid, Abu al-'Aliyah, 'Ikrimah, Ibrahim, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, 'Abdullah ibn Kathir, 'Ata' al-'Awfi, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and al-Suddi.

The grammatical status (i'rab) of ﴿The dye of Allah﴾ is either as a warning (al-igra') (a form of exhortation to hold to something), like His saying ﴿the fitrah of Allah﴾ [al-Rum: 30], meaning: "Adhere to that, upon you is it." Some of them said it is a substitute (badal) for His saying: ﴿the religion of Ibrahim﴾. Sibawayh said: it is an emphatic verbal noun (masdar mu'akkad) in the accusative, governed by His saying ﴿We believe in Allah﴾, like His saying ﴿and worship Allah﴾ [al-Nisa': 36].

A hadith has been transmitted, related by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh, through the narration of Ash'ath ibn Ishaq from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The Children of Israel said: 'O Musa, does your Lord dye?' Musa said: 'Fear Allah.' Then his Lord called to him: 'O Musa, they asked you whether your Lord dyes? Say: Yes, I dye the colours: the red, the white and the black, and all colours are of My dye.'" And Allah revealed to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿The dye of Allah, and who is better than Allah in dye?﴾ [Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/403), and from his route Abu al-Shaykh in al-'Azamah, no. 138.]

This is how it occurs in the narration of Ibn Mardawayh as a marfu' (attributed to the Prophet) report, whereas in the narration of Ibn Abi Hatim it is mawquf (attributed to Ibn 'Abbas), and the latter is more likely, if its chain is sound. And Allah knows best.

God Almighty says, guiding His Prophet (may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him) to turn away the disputation of the polytheists: ﴿Say: Do you argue with us concerning Allah, when He is our Lord and your Lord?﴾ That is: Do you debate with us about the Oneness of Allah, sincerity toward Him, submission to Him, following His commands and abstaining from what He has forbidden? ﴿And He is our Lord and your Lord,﴾ the One who disposes of us and of you, who alone deserves to be worshipped with sincere devotion, having no partner! ﴿For us are our deeds and for you are your deeds.﴾ That is: we are free of you and you are free of us, just as He said in another verse: ﴿And if they deny you, say: "For me is my work and for you is your work. You are free of what I do, and I am free of what you do."﴾ [Yunus: 41] And He said: ﴿Then if they argue with you, say: "I have submitted myself to Allah, and so have those who follow me." And say to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered: "Have you submitted?" If they submit, then they are guided; but if they turn away, then your duty is only to convey (the message), and Allah is Seeing of the servants.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 20] And Allah said, relating about Ibrahim (peace be upon him): ﴿And his people argued with him. He said: "Do you argue with me concerning Allah, when He has guided me? And I do not fear what you associate with Him, unless my Lord wills something. My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge. Will you not then be mindful?"﴾ [Al-An'am: 80] And He said: ﴿Have you not considered the one who argued with Ibrahim concerning his Lord...﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 258] to the end of the verse.

And He said in this noble verse: ﴿[For us are our deeds and for you are your deeds] and we are sincere to Him.﴾ That is: we are free of you just as you are free of us, and we are sincere to Him, that is, in worship and turning toward Him.

Then Allah rebuked them for their claim that Ibrahim and those mentioned after him among the Prophets and the Patriarchs were upon their religion, whether Judaism or Christianity. So He said: ﴿Say: "Are you more knowing, or is Allah?"﴾ meaning: rather, Allah is more knowing. He has informed that they were neither Jews nor Christians, as He said: ﴿Ibrahim was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a Hanif, a Muslim, and he was not of the polytheists﴾ and the verse that follows it. [Al 'Imran: 67-68]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who conceals a testimony he has from Allah?﴾ Al-Hasan al-Basri said: They used to read in the Book of Allah that had come to them: "Indeed the religion with Allah is Islam," and "Indeed Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," and that Ibrahim, Isma'il, Ishaq, Ya'qub and the Patriarchs were free of Judaism and Christianity. Allah bore witness to this, and they acknowledged it against themselves before Allah, but they concealed the testimony of Allah that was with them concerning that.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what you do﴾ it contains a threat and a severe warning, that is: His knowledge encompasses your deeds, and He will recompense you for them.

Then Allah said: ﴿That is a nation that has passed away.﴾ That is: it has gone by. ﴿It will have what it earned, and you will have what you earned.﴾ That is: for them are their deeds, and for you are your deeds. ﴿And you will not be asked about what they used to do.﴾ Your lineage to them does not benefit you without following them yourselves, and do not be deceived by mere affiliation to them until you become like them, submissive to the commands of Allah and following His Messengers, who were sent as bringers of glad tidings and warners. Whoever disbelieves in one Prophet has disbelieved in all the Messengers, and especially whoever disbelieves in the Master of the Prophets, the Seal of the Messengers, and the Messenger of the Lord of the worlds to all of mankind and jinn among all the responsible beings, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him and upon all the Prophets of Allah, all of them.
