Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verses 142–143 (part 1 of 2):

It has been said that the "foolish ones" (al-sufaha') here refers to the polytheists, the polytheists of the Arabs; this was said by al-Zajjaj. It has also been said that they are the rabbis of the Jews; this was said by Mujahid. It has also been said that they are the hypocrites; this was said by al-Suddi. The verse is general, encompassing all of these, and God knows best. [[Addition from ج, ط.]]

Al-Bukhari said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, having heard Zuhayr, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) for sixteen or seventeen months, and he liked that his qiblah (direction of prayer) be toward the House (the Ka'bah). The first prayer he prayed toward it was the 'Asr prayer, and a people prayed with him. Then a man who had prayed with him went out and passed by the people of the mosque while they were bowing, and he said: "I bear witness before Allah that I prayed with the Prophet ﷺ facing Makkah." So they turned around as they were, toward the House. Among those who had died upon the qiblah before it was changed toward the House were men who had been killed, and we did not know what to say about them. So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And Allah would never let your faith go to waste. Indeed, Allah is toward the people Kind and Merciful﴾. [[In ج: "إلى البيت" ("toward the House").]] [[In ط: "فخرج قوم" ("then a people went out").]] [[In ط: "فخرج قوم".]] Al-Bukhari alone narrated it through this route. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4486.]] Muslim narrated it through another route. [[Sahih Muslim, no. 525.]]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid narrated to me, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray toward Bayt al-Maqdis and would often look up to the sky, waiting for the command of Allah. So Allah revealed: ﴿We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven. We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased. So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram (the Sacred Mosque)﴾. Some men among the Muslims said: "We wish we knew the state of those among us who died before we were turned toward the qiblah, and how our prayer toward Bayt al-Maqdis will be (regarded)?" So Allah revealed: ﴿And Allah would never let your faith go to waste﴾. And the foolish among the people, who are the People of the Book, said: "What has turned them away from their qiblah that they were upon?" So Allah revealed: ﴿The foolish among the people will say...﴾, to the end of the verse. [[In أ: "حدثني المعلى" ("Al-Mu'alla narrated to me").]] [[In أ: "فقال رجل" ("a man said").]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn 'Atiyyah narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen or seventeen months, and he loved to be turned toward the Ka'bah. So Allah revealed: ﴿We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven...﴾ He said: So he was turned toward the Ka'bah. And the foolish among the people, who are the Jews, said: ﴿What has turned them away from their qiblah that they were upon?﴾ So Allah revealed: ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west. He guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ migrated to Madinah, Allah commanded him to face Bayt al-Maqdis, so the Jews rejoiced. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ faced it for some ten-odd months, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ loved the qiblah of Ibrahim (Abraham), so he would supplicate to Allah and look toward the sky. So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿So turn your faces toward it﴾, meaning: toward it. The Jews were then suspicious of this and said: "What has turned them away from their qiblah that they were upon?" So Allah revealed: ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west. He guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾.

Many hadiths have been transmitted on this topic, and the summary of the matter is that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had been commanded to face the rock of Bayt al-Maqdis. In Makkah, he would pray between the two corners (of the Ka'bah), so the Ka'bah was in front of him while he faced the rock of Bayt al-Maqdis. When he migrated to Madinah, it became impossible to combine the two, so Allah commanded him to face Bayt al-Maqdis. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and the majority. Then these scholars differed as to whether the command to do so came by the Qur'an or otherwise, into two opinions. Al-Qurtubi in his tafsir relates from Ikrimah, Abu al-'Aliyah and al-Hasan al-Basri that facing Bayt al-Maqdis was by his own ijtihad (independent reasoning), upon him be prayers and peace. The intended point is that facing Bayt al-Maqdis was after his arrival in Madinah ﷺ, and the matter continued thus for some ten-odd months. He would often supplicate and beseech that he be turned toward the Ka'bah, the qiblah of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. He was answered in this, and was commanded to face the Ancient House. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed the people and informed them of this. The first prayer he prayed toward it was the 'Asr prayer, as has preceded in the two Sahihs from the narration of al-Bara'. It occurs in al-Nasa'i's narration from Abu Sa'id ibn al-Mu'alla that it was the Zuhr prayer. [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11004.]] As for the people of Quba', the report did not reach them until the Fajr prayer of the following day, as came in the two Sahihs from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "While the people were at Quba' in the Fajr prayer, a messenger came to them and said: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has received a Qur'an tonight, and he has been commanded to face the Ka'bah, so face it.' Their faces had been toward Syria, so they turned around toward the Ka'bah." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 403, and Sahih Muslim, no. 526.]]

In this is evidence that the naskh (abrogation) of a ruling does not bind its application until one has knowledge of it, even if its revelation and conveyance came earlier, for they were not commanded to repeat the 'Asr, Maghrib and 'Isha' prayers. And God knows best.

When this occurred, doubt, deviation from guidance, confusion and uncertainty arose in some people, from among the hypocrites, the doubters, and the disbelievers among the Jews, and they said: ﴿What has turned them away from their qiblah that they were upon?﴾, meaning: What is the matter with these people, that at one time they face this and at another time they face that? So Allah revealed their answer in His saying: ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west﴾, meaning: the judgment, the disposal and the command all belong to Allah, and wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah. And (the verse): ﴿It is not righteousness that you turn your faces toward the east or the west, but righteousness is (in) one who believes in Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 177], meaning: the whole matter lies in complying with the commands of Allah. So wherever He directs us, we turn. Obedience lies in complying with His command, even if He directs us several times a day to multiple directions. We are His servants and His attendants, and wherever He directs us, we turn. He, exalted is He, has shown great care for His servant and Messenger Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, and his Ummah, for He guided them to the qiblah of Ibrahim, the Friend of the Most Merciful, and made their turning toward the Ka'bah, which was built in the name of Him alone, with no partner, the most noble of the houses of Allah on earth, since it is the building of Ibrahim the Friend, peace be upon him. For this reason He said: ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west. He guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Ali ibn 'Asim, from Husayn ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Amr [[In ط، أ، و: "عن عمرو" ("from Amr").]] ibn Qays, from Muhammad ibn al-Ash'ath, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, meaning regarding the People of the Book: "They do not envy us for anything as they envy us for Friday, which Allah guided us to, and they went astray from it, and for the qiblah which Allah guided us to, and they went astray from it, and for our saying behind the imam: Amin." [[Al-Musnad (6/134).]]

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And thus We have made you a median (wasat) nation, that you may be witnesses over the people, and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾. He, exalted is He, says: We only turned you toward the qiblah of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and We chose it for you, so that We may make you the best of nations, so that on the Day of Resurrection you may be witnesses over the nations, because all of them acknowledge your merit. Here, wasat means the best and most excellent, as one says: "Quraysh is the most noble of the Arabs in lineage and abode," meaning the best of them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was wasat among his people, meaning the most noble of them in lineage. From this comes the Salat al-Wusta (the middle prayer), which is the most excellent of the prayers, and it is the 'Asr, as is established in the Sahih collections and others. When Allah made this Ummah wasat, He singled it out with the most perfect of the laws, the most upright of the methods, and the clearest of the paths, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty; (it is) the religion of your father Ibrahim. He named you "Muslims" before (this) and in this (revelation), that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people﴾ [al-Hajj: 78].

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Nuh (Noah) will be called on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said to him: 'Did you convey (the message)?' He will say: 'Yes.' Then his people will be called and it will be said to them: 'Did he convey to you?' They will say: 'No warner came to us, and no one came to us.' Then it will be said to Nuh: 'Who will testify for you?' He will say: 'Muhammad and his Ummah.'" He said: That is His saying: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation﴾. [[Al-Musnad (3/32).]]

He (Abu Sa'id) said: The wasat is the just (al-'adl), so you will be called, and you will testify for him that he conveyed, then I will testify over you. [[In ج، ط: "قال: والوسط" ("He said: And the wasat").]] [[In ج: "بقول يشهد عليكم"; in ط: "وأشهد عليكم" ("and I will testify over you").]] It was narrated by al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah through several routes from al-A'mash, [with it] [[Addition from ج، ط، أ، و.]]. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 3339 and 4487; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2961; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11007; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4284.]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The Prophet will come on the Day of Resurrection, and with him a man, and a prophet with him two men, and more than that. Then his people will be called, and it will be said to them: 'Did this one convey to you?' They will say: 'No.' Then it will be said to him: 'Did you convey to your people?' He will say: 'Yes.' Then it will be said to him: 'Who will testify for you?' He will say: 'Muhammad and his Ummah.' Then Muhammad and his Ummah will be called, and it will be said to them: 'Did this one convey to his people?' They will say: 'Yes.' It will be said: 'And how do you know?' They will say: 'Our Prophet ﷺ came to us and informed us that the messengers had conveyed.'" That is the saying of Him, mighty and majestic: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation﴾. He said: "Just (adlan), ﴿that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾." [[Al-Musnad (3/58).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet ﷺ, regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation﴾, he said: "Just." [[Al-Musnad (3/9).]]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad, from Abu Malik al-Ashja'i, from al-Mughirah ibn 'Utaybah [[In ج: "بن عيينة" ("ibn 'Uyaynah").]] ibn Nahhas, who said: A slave of ours (muktib) narrated to me from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "I and my Ummah on the Day of Resurrection will be upon a mound, overlooking the creation. There is no one among the people but he would wish that he were of us. And there is no prophet whose people denied him but that we will bear witness that he conveyed the message of his Lord, mighty and majestic." [[It was narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir (3/147) through the route of Ibn Fudayl from Abu Malik al-Ashja'i, with it.]]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 2, verses 142–143 (part 2 of 2):

Al-Hakim narrated in his *Mustadrak*, and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it, with the wording being Ibn Mardawayh's, from the hadith of Mus'ab ibn Thabit, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) attended a funeral among Banu Salima, and I was beside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Some of them said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, what a fine man he was! He was chaste and a Muslim, and he was..." and they praised him well. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You are saying what you say." The man said: "Allah knows the hidden things; as for what appeared to us of him, that is what it is." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "It is due (wajabat)." Then he attended a funeral among Banu Haritha, and I was beside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Some of them said: "O Messenger of Allah, what a bad man he was! He was harsh in speech." They spoke ill of him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to some of them: "You are saying what you say." The man said: "Allah knows the hidden things; as for what appeared to us of him, that is what it is." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is due."

Mus'ab ibn Thabit said: Muhammad ibn Ka'b then said to us: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke the truth." Then he recited: ﴿And thus We have made you a middle nation, that you may be witnesses over the people, and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾.

Then al-Hakim said: "This is a hadith whose chain (isnad) is sahih, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not narrate it."
[[Al-Mustadrak (2/268). Al-Dhahabi criticized it with his words: "In it is Mus'ab ibn Thabit, who is not strong."]]

Imam Ahmad said: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Dawud ibn Abi al-Furat narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Buraydah, from Abu al-Aswad, that he said: I came to Medina and arrived when a disease had struck it, and they were dying in great numbers. I sat with 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and a funeral passed by him, and good was spoken of its companion. He said: "It is due, it is due." Then another passed by, and evil was spoken of its companion, and 'Umar said: "It is due." Abu al-Aswad said: "What is due, O Commander of the Faithful?" He said: "I said what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Any Muslim for whom four people testify to good, Allah will admit him into Paradise.'" He said: We said: "And three?" He said: "And three." He said: We said: "And two?" He said: "And two." Then we did not ask him about the one.

Al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i also narrated it in the same way, from the hadith of Dawud ibn Abi al-Furat.
[[Al-Musnad (1/22); Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1368); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1059); Sunan al-Nasa'i (4/50).]]

Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn 'Uthman ibn Yahya narrated to us, Abu Qilaba al-Raqashi narrated to us, Abu al-Walid narrated to me, Nafi' ibn 'Umar narrated to us, Umayya ibn Safwan narrated to me, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Zuhayr al-Thaqafi, from his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at al-Nabawa say: "Soon you will know your good from your evil." They said: "By what, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "By good praise and bad praise. You are the witnesses of Allah on earth."

Ibn Majah narrated it from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba, from Yazid ibn Harun.
[[Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4221). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/301): "Its chain is sahih, and its narrators are trustworthy."]] Imam Ahmad narrated it from Yazid ibn Harun, 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umar, and Shurayh, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, with the same wording.
[[I did not find it in the printed Musnad by this route, but al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar mentioned it in Atraf al-Musnad (6/231).]]

* *

Allah's statement: ﴿And We did not make the qiblah which you had been facing except that We might know who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels. And indeed, it was difficult except for those whom Allah has guided﴾.

Allah says: "We only prescribed for you, O Muhammad, facing Bayt al-Maqdis first, then We turned you away from it toward the Ka'bah, so that the condition of those who follow you, obey you, and face with you wherever you turn might become evident, from those who turn back on their heels," meaning, those who apostatize from their religion. ﴿And indeed, it was difficult﴾, meaning: this act, namely turning the direction away from Bayt al-Maqdis toward the Ka'bah, was a great thing in people's souls, ﴿except for those whom Allah has guided﴾, meaning, whose hearts Allah has guided, who were certain of the truth of the Messenger, and who were certain that everything he brought is the truth beyond any doubt, and that Allah does what He wills and decrees what He desires. So He may impose on His servants whatever He wishes and abrogate (naskh, meaning replacing one ruling with another) whatever He wishes, and He has complete wisdom and conclusive proof in all of that. This is unlike those in whose hearts is a disease, for whenever a matter occurs, it produces doubt in them, whereas the believers gain certainty and affirmation. As Allah says: ﴿And when a surah is revealed, among them are those who say: "Which of you has had his faith increased by this?" As for those who believed, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice. But as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it has added uncleanness to their uncleanness﴾ [al-Tawbah: 124–125]. And He says: ﴿Say: "It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing. But as for those who do not believe, there is deafness in their ears, and it is blindness for them"﴾ [Fussilat: 44]. And He says: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is healing and mercy for the believers, and it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss﴾ [al-Isra': 82].

For this reason, whoever remained firm in affirming the Messenger (ﷺ) and following him in this matter, and turned wherever Allah commanded, without doubt or suspicion, was among the leaders of the Companions. Some scholars have held that the foremost early ones among the Muhajirun and the Ansar are those who prayed toward both qiblahs.

Al-Bukhari said in his tafsir of this verse:
Musaddad narrated to us, Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: While the people were praying the dawn prayer in the Mosque of Quba', a man came and said: "A Qur'an has been revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ) tonight, and he has been commanded to face the Ka'bah, so face it." So they turned toward the Ka'bah.
[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4488).]]

Muslim narrated it through another route from Ibn 'Umar.
[[Sahih Muslim no. (526).]] Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri, and in his version they were bowing, so they turned as they were toward the Ka'bah while still bowing.
[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (341).]] Likewise, Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salama, from Thabit, from Anas, similarly.
[[Sahih Muslim no. (527).]] This indicates their complete obedience to Allah and His Messenger, and their submission to the commands of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. May Allah be pleased with them all.

* *

Allah's statement: ﴿And Allah would not have caused your faith to be lost﴾, meaning: your prayer toward Bayt al-Maqdis before that will not have its reward lost with Allah. In the Sahih, from the hadith of Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from al-Bara', he said: Some people died who had been praying toward Bayt al-Maqdis, so the people said: "What is their condition regarding that?" Then Allah revealed: ﴿And Allah would not have caused your faith to be lost﴾.
[[The hadith was cited shortly before.]]
[Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas and graded it sahih.]
[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2964).]]

Ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And Allah would not have caused your faith to be lost﴾, meaning: regarding the first qiblah, and your affirmation of your Prophet and following him toward the other qiblah; that is, He will give you the reward for both of them together. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful toward the people﴾.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: ﴿And Allah would not have caused your faith to be lost﴾, meaning: Allah would not have wasted Muhammad (ﷺ) and your turning with him wherever he turned. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful toward the people﴾.

In the Sahih, it is reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw a woman among the captives whose child had been separated from her. Whenever she found a child among the captives, she took him and pressed him to her chest, while searching for her own child. When she found him, she embraced him and put her breast in his mouth. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you think this woman would throw her child into the Fire while she is able not to throw him?" They said: "No, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "By Allah, Allah is more merciful to His servants than this woman is to her child."
[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5999); Sahih Muslim no. (2754).]]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verses 142–143 (part 1 of 2):

It has been said that the "foolish ones" (al-sufaha') here refers to the polytheists, the polytheists of the Arabs; this was said by al-Zajjaj. It has also been said that they are the rabbis of the Jews; this was said by Mujahid. It has also been said that they are the hypocrites; this was said by al-Suddi. The verse is general, encompassing all of these, and God knows best. [[Addition from ج, ط.]]

Al-Bukhari said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, having heard Zuhayr, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) for sixteen or seventeen months, and he liked that his qiblah (direction of prayer) be toward the House (the Ka'bah). The first prayer he prayed toward it was the 'Asr prayer, and a people prayed with him. Then a man who had prayed with him went out and passed by the people of the mosque while they were bowing, and he said: "I bear witness before Allah that I prayed with the Prophet ﷺ facing Makkah." So they turned around as they were, toward the House. Among those who had died upon the qiblah before it was changed toward the House were men who had been killed, and we did not know what to say about them. So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And Allah would never let your faith go to waste. Indeed, Allah is toward the people Kind and Merciful﴾. [[In ج: "إلى البيت" ("toward the House").]] [[In ط: "فخرج قوم" ("then a people went out").]] [[In ط: "فخرج قوم".]] Al-Bukhari alone narrated it through this route. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4486.]] Muslim narrated it through another route. [[Sahih Muslim, no. 525.]]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid narrated to me, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray toward Bayt al-Maqdis and would often look up to the sky, waiting for the command of Allah. So Allah revealed: ﴿We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven. We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased. So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram (the Sacred Mosque)﴾. Some men among the Muslims said: "We wish we knew the state of those among us who died before we were turned toward the qiblah, and how our prayer toward Bayt al-Maqdis will be (regarded)?" So Allah revealed: ﴿And Allah would never let your faith go to waste﴾. And the foolish among the people, who are the People of the Book, said: "What has turned them away from their qiblah that they were upon?" So Allah revealed: ﴿The foolish among the people will say...﴾, to the end of the verse. [[In أ: "حدثني المعلى" ("Al-Mu'alla narrated to me").]] [[In أ: "فقال رجل" ("a man said").]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn 'Atiyyah narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen or seventeen months, and he loved to be turned toward the Ka'bah. So Allah revealed: ﴿We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven...﴾ He said: So he was turned toward the Ka'bah. And the foolish among the people, who are the Jews, said: ﴿What has turned them away from their qiblah that they were upon?﴾ So Allah revealed: ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west. He guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ migrated to Madinah, Allah commanded him to face Bayt al-Maqdis, so the Jews rejoiced. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ faced it for some ten-odd months, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ loved the qiblah of Ibrahim (Abraham), so he would supplicate to Allah and look toward the sky. So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿So turn your faces toward it﴾, meaning: toward it. The Jews were then suspicious of this and said: "What has turned them away from their qiblah that they were upon?" So Allah revealed: ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west. He guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾.

Many hadiths have been transmitted on this topic, and the summary of the matter is that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had been commanded to face the rock of Bayt al-Maqdis. In Makkah, he would pray between the two corners (of the Ka'bah), so the Ka'bah was in front of him while he faced the rock of Bayt al-Maqdis. When he migrated to Madinah, it became impossible to combine the two, so Allah commanded him to face Bayt al-Maqdis. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and the majority. Then these scholars differed as to whether the command to do so came by the Qur'an or otherwise, into two opinions. Al-Qurtubi in his tafsir relates from Ikrimah, Abu al-'Aliyah and al-Hasan al-Basri that facing Bayt al-Maqdis was by his own ijtihad (independent reasoning), upon him be prayers and peace. The intended point is that facing Bayt al-Maqdis was after his arrival in Madinah ﷺ, and the matter continued thus for some ten-odd months. He would often supplicate and beseech that he be turned toward the Ka'bah, the qiblah of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. He was answered in this, and was commanded to face the Ancient House. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed the people and informed them of this. The first prayer he prayed toward it was the 'Asr prayer, as has preceded in the two Sahihs from the narration of al-Bara'. It occurs in al-Nasa'i's narration from Abu Sa'id ibn al-Mu'alla that it was the Zuhr prayer. [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11004.]] As for the people of Quba', the report did not reach them until the Fajr prayer of the following day, as came in the two Sahihs from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "While the people were at Quba' in the Fajr prayer, a messenger came to them and said: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has received a Qur'an tonight, and he has been commanded to face the Ka'bah, so face it.' Their faces had been toward Syria, so they turned around toward the Ka'bah." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 403, and Sahih Muslim, no. 526.]]

In this is evidence that the naskh (abrogation) of a ruling does not bind its application until one has knowledge of it, even if its revelation and conveyance came earlier, for they were not commanded to repeat the 'Asr, Maghrib and 'Isha' prayers. And God knows best.

When this occurred, doubt, deviation from guidance, confusion and uncertainty arose in some people, from among the hypocrites, the doubters, and the disbelievers among the Jews, and they said: ﴿What has turned them away from their qiblah that they were upon?﴾, meaning: What is the matter with these people, that at one time they face this and at another time they face that? So Allah revealed their answer in His saying: ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west﴾, meaning: the judgment, the disposal and the command all belong to Allah, and wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah. And (the verse): ﴿It is not righteousness that you turn your faces toward the east or the west, but righteousness is (in) one who believes in Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 177], meaning: the whole matter lies in complying with the commands of Allah. So wherever He directs us, we turn. Obedience lies in complying with His command, even if He directs us several times a day to multiple directions. We are His servants and His attendants, and wherever He directs us, we turn. He, exalted is He, has shown great care for His servant and Messenger Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, and his Ummah, for He guided them to the qiblah of Ibrahim, the Friend of the Most Merciful, and made their turning toward the Ka'bah, which was built in the name of Him alone, with no partner, the most noble of the houses of Allah on earth, since it is the building of Ibrahim the Friend, peace be upon him. For this reason He said: ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west. He guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Ali ibn 'Asim, from Husayn ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Amr [[In ط، أ، و: "عن عمرو" ("from Amr").]] ibn Qays, from Muhammad ibn al-Ash'ath, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, meaning regarding the People of the Book: "They do not envy us for anything as they envy us for Friday, which Allah guided us to, and they went astray from it, and for the qiblah which Allah guided us to, and they went astray from it, and for our saying behind the imam: Amin." [[Al-Musnad (6/134).]]

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And thus We have made you a median (wasat) nation, that you may be witnesses over the people, and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾. He, exalted is He, says: We only turned you toward the qiblah of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and We chose it for you, so that We may make you the best of nations, so that on the Day of Resurrection you may be witnesses over the nations, because all of them acknowledge your merit. Here, wasat means the best and most excellent, as one says: "Quraysh is the most noble of the Arabs in lineage and abode," meaning the best of them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was wasat among his people, meaning the most noble of them in lineage. From this comes the Salat al-Wusta (the middle prayer), which is the most excellent of the prayers, and it is the 'Asr, as is established in the Sahih collections and others. When Allah made this Ummah wasat, He singled it out with the most perfect of the laws, the most upright of the methods, and the clearest of the paths, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty; (it is) the religion of your father Ibrahim. He named you "Muslims" before (this) and in this (revelation), that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people﴾ [al-Hajj: 78].

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Nuh (Noah) will be called on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said to him: 'Did you convey (the message)?' He will say: 'Yes.' Then his people will be called and it will be said to them: 'Did he convey to you?' They will say: 'No warner came to us, and no one came to us.' Then it will be said to Nuh: 'Who will testify for you?' He will say: 'Muhammad and his Ummah.'" He said: That is His saying: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation﴾. [[Al-Musnad (3/32).]]

He (Abu Sa'id) said: The wasat is the just (al-'adl), so you will be called, and you will testify for him that he conveyed, then I will testify over you. [[In ج، ط: "قال: والوسط" ("He said: And the wasat").]] [[In ج: "بقول يشهد عليكم"; in ط: "وأشهد عليكم" ("and I will testify over you").]] It was narrated by al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah through several routes from al-A'mash, [with it] [[Addition from ج، ط، أ، و.]]. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 3339 and 4487; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2961; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11007; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4284.]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The Prophet will come on the Day of Resurrection, and with him a man, and a prophet with him two men, and more than that. Then his people will be called, and it will be said to them: 'Did this one convey to you?' They will say: 'No.' Then it will be said to him: 'Did you convey to your people?' He will say: 'Yes.' Then it will be said to him: 'Who will testify for you?' He will say: 'Muhammad and his Ummah.' Then Muhammad and his Ummah will be called, and it will be said to them: 'Did this one convey to his people?' They will say: 'Yes.' It will be said: 'And how do you know?' They will say: 'Our Prophet ﷺ came to us and informed us that the messengers had conveyed.'" That is the saying of Him, mighty and majestic: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation﴾. He said: "Just (adlan), ﴿that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾." [[Al-Musnad (3/58).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet ﷺ, regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation﴾, he said: "Just." [[Al-Musnad (3/9).]]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad, from Abu Malik al-Ashja'i, from al-Mughirah ibn 'Utaybah [[In ج: "بن عيينة" ("ibn 'Uyaynah").]] ibn Nahhas, who said: A slave of ours (muktib) narrated to me from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "I and my Ummah on the Day of Resurrection will be upon a mound, overlooking the creation. There is no one among the people but he would wish that he were of us. And there is no prophet whose people denied him but that we will bear witness that he conveyed the message of his Lord, mighty and majestic." [[It was narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir (3/147) through the route of Ibn Fudayl from Abu Malik al-Ashja'i, with it.]]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 2, verses 142–143 (part 2 of 2):

Al-Hakim narrated in his *Mustadrak*, and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it, with the wording being Ibn Mardawayh's, from the hadith of Mus'ab ibn Thabit, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) attended a funeral among Banu Salima, and I was beside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Some of them said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, what a fine man he was! He was chaste and a Muslim, and he was..." and they praised him well. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You are saying what you say." The man said: "Allah knows the hidden things; as for what appeared to us of him, that is what it is." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "It is due (wajabat)." Then he attended a funeral among Banu Haritha, and I was beside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Some of them said: "O Messenger of Allah, what a bad man he was! He was harsh in speech." They spoke ill of him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to some of them: "You are saying what you say." The man said: "Allah knows the hidden things; as for what appeared to us of him, that is what it is." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is due."

Mus'ab ibn Thabit said: Muhammad ibn Ka'b then said to us: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke the truth." Then he recited: ﴿And thus We have made you a middle nation, that you may be witnesses over the people, and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾.

Then al-Hakim said: "This is a hadith whose chain (isnad) is sahih, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not narrate it."
[[Al-Mustadrak (2/268). Al-Dhahabi criticized it with his words: "In it is Mus'ab ibn Thabit, who is not strong."]]

Imam Ahmad said: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Dawud ibn Abi al-Furat narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Buraydah, from Abu al-Aswad, that he said: I came to Medina and arrived when a disease had struck it, and they were dying in great numbers. I sat with 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and a funeral passed by him, and good was spoken of its companion. He said: "It is due, it is due." Then another passed by, and evil was spoken of its companion, and 'Umar said: "It is due." Abu al-Aswad said: "What is due, O Commander of the Faithful?" He said: "I said what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Any Muslim for whom four people testify to good, Allah will admit him into Paradise.'" He said: We said: "And three?" He said: "And three." He said: We said: "And two?" He said: "And two." Then we did not ask him about the one.

Al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i also narrated it in the same way, from the hadith of Dawud ibn Abi al-Furat.
[[Al-Musnad (1/22); Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1368); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1059); Sunan al-Nasa'i (4/50).]]

Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn 'Uthman ibn Yahya narrated to us, Abu Qilaba al-Raqashi narrated to us, Abu al-Walid narrated to me, Nafi' ibn 'Umar narrated to us, Umayya ibn Safwan narrated to me, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Zuhayr al-Thaqafi, from his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at al-Nabawa say: "Soon you will know your good from your evil." They said: "By what, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "By good praise and bad praise. You are the witnesses of Allah on earth."

Ibn Majah narrated it from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba, from Yazid ibn Harun.
[[Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4221). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/301): "Its chain is sahih, and its narrators are trustworthy."]] Imam Ahmad narrated it from Yazid ibn Harun, 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umar, and Shurayh, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, with the same wording.
[[I did not find it in the printed Musnad by this route, but al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar mentioned it in Atraf al-Musnad (6/231).]]

* *

Allah's statement: ﴿And We did not make the qiblah which you had been facing except that We might know who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels. And indeed, it was difficult except for those whom Allah has guided﴾.

Allah says: "We only prescribed for you, O Muhammad, facing Bayt al-Maqdis first, then We turned you away from it toward the Ka'bah, so that the condition of those who follow you, obey you, and face with you wherever you turn might become evident, from those who turn back on their heels," meaning, those who apostatize from their religion. ﴿And indeed, it was difficult﴾, meaning: this act, namely turning the direction away from Bayt al-Maqdis toward the Ka'bah, was a great thing in people's souls, ﴿except for those whom Allah has guided﴾, meaning, whose hearts Allah has guided, who were certain of the truth of the Messenger, and who were certain that everything he brought is the truth beyond any doubt, and that Allah does what He wills and decrees what He desires. So He may impose on His servants whatever He wishes and abrogate (naskh, meaning replacing one ruling with another) whatever He wishes, and He has complete wisdom and conclusive proof in all of that. This is unlike those in whose hearts is a disease, for whenever a matter occurs, it produces doubt in them, whereas the believers gain certainty and affirmation. As Allah says: ﴿And when a surah is revealed, among them are those who say: "Which of you has had his faith increased by this?" As for those who believed, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice. But as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it has added uncleanness to their uncleanness﴾ [al-Tawbah: 124–125]. And He says: ﴿Say: "It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing. But as for those who do not believe, there is deafness in their ears, and it is blindness for them"﴾ [Fussilat: 44]. And He says: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is healing and mercy for the believers, and it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss﴾ [al-Isra': 82].

For this reason, whoever remained firm in affirming the Messenger (ﷺ) and following him in this matter, and turned wherever Allah commanded, without doubt or suspicion, was among the leaders of the Companions. Some scholars have held that the foremost early ones among the Muhajirun and the Ansar are those who prayed toward both qiblahs.

Al-Bukhari said in his tafsir of this verse:
Musaddad narrated to us, Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: While the people were praying the dawn prayer in the Mosque of Quba', a man came and said: "A Qur'an has been revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ) tonight, and he has been commanded to face the Ka'bah, so face it." So they turned toward the Ka'bah.
[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4488).]]

Muslim narrated it through another route from Ibn 'Umar.
[[Sahih Muslim no. (526).]] Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri, and in his version they were bowing, so they turned as they were toward the Ka'bah while still bowing.
[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (341).]] Likewise, Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salama, from Thabit, from Anas, similarly.
[[Sahih Muslim no. (527).]] This indicates their complete obedience to Allah and His Messenger, and their submission to the commands of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. May Allah be pleased with them all.

* *

Allah's statement: ﴿And Allah would not have caused your faith to be lost﴾, meaning: your prayer toward Bayt al-Maqdis before that will not have its reward lost with Allah. In the Sahih, from the hadith of Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from al-Bara', he said: Some people died who had been praying toward Bayt al-Maqdis, so the people said: "What is their condition regarding that?" Then Allah revealed: ﴿And Allah would not have caused your faith to be lost﴾.
[[The hadith was cited shortly before.]]
[Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas and graded it sahih.]
[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2964).]]

Ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And Allah would not have caused your faith to be lost﴾, meaning: regarding the first qiblah, and your affirmation of your Prophet and following him toward the other qiblah; that is, He will give you the reward for both of them together. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful toward the people﴾.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: ﴿And Allah would not have caused your faith to be lost﴾, meaning: Allah would not have wasted Muhammad (ﷺ) and your turning with him wherever he turned. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful toward the people﴾.

In the Sahih, it is reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw a woman among the captives whose child had been separated from her. Whenever she found a child among the captives, she took him and pressed him to her chest, while searching for her own child. When she found him, she embraced him and put her breast in his mouth. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you think this woman would throw her child into the Fire while she is able not to throw him?" They said: "No, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "By Allah, Allah is more merciful to His servants than this woman is to her child."
[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5999); Sahih Muslim no. (2754).]]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 2, verse 144:

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: The first thing abrogated (naskh) in the Qur'an was the qiblah (the direction of prayer). When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ migrated to Madinah, most of its inhabitants were Jews, so Allah commanded him to face Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). The Jews rejoiced, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ faced it for about sixteen months. He loved the qiblah of Ibrahim (Abraham), so he would supplicate to Allah while looking up at the sky. Allah then revealed: ﴿We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the sky﴾ up to His words: ﴿so turn your faces toward it﴾. The Jews were disturbed by this and said: ﴿What has turned them away from their qiblah, which they had been on?﴾ [Allah revealed the reply:] ﴿Say, "To Allah belong the east and the west; He guides whom He wills to a straight path."﴾ [[Addition from T.]] And He said: ﴿Wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 115]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We did not make the qiblah which you were using except that We might give evidence of who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels﴾.

Ibn Mardawayh related through al-Qasim al-'Umari, from his paternal uncle 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Umar, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ finished his prayer facing Bayt al-Maqdis, he would raise his head toward the sky. So Allah revealed: ﴿So We will surely turn you to a qiblah that you will like. So turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque﴾, to the Ka'bah, to the spout (al-Mizab), with Jibra'il [[In T: "Jibril".]] (peace be upon him) leading the way.

al-Hakim related in his Mustadrak, from the narration of Shu'bah, from Ya'la ibn 'Ata', from Yahya ibn Qamtah, who said: I saw 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr [[In A: "Ibn 'Umar".]] sitting in the Sacred Mosque, opposite the spout, and he recited this verse: ﴿So We will surely turn you to a qiblah that you will like﴾, and said: "Toward the spout of the Ka'bah."

Then he said: "Its chain is sound (sahih al-isnad), though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it."[[al-Mustadrak (2/269).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim also related it from al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah, from Hushaym, from Ya'la ibn 'Ata', with the same wording.

Others have said likewise, and this is one of the two opinions of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him: that the intent is hitting the exact position of the qiblah. The other view, which the majority hold, is that what is meant is facing it (al-muwajahah) [[In T, A, and W: "al-wijhah".]], as al-Hakim related from the narration of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from 'Umayr ibn Ziyad al-Kindi, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, regarding ﴿So turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque﴾, that he said: "Shatrahu" means "its direction (qiblatahu)." Then he said: "Its chain is sound, though they did not record it."

This is the view of Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and others. As has been mentioned in another hadith: "Between the east and the west is a qiblah."

[al-Qurtubi said: Ibn Jurayj related from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Between the east and the west is a qiblah for the people of the Mosque; the Mosque is a qiblah for the people of the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram); and the Sacred Precinct is a qiblah for the people of the earth in its eastern and western regions, from my ummah."[[Related by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (2/9, 10) through 'Umar ibn Hafs, from Ibn Jurayj. al-Bayhaqi said: "'Umar ibn Hafs al-Makki alone narrated it, and he is weak and not to be used as evidence. It was also narrated by another weak chain, from 'Abd Allah ibn Habash, likewise as a marfu' report, and such a report cannot be used as evidence, and Allah knows best."]] ] [[Addition from J, T, A.]]

Abu Nu'aym al-Fadl ibn Dukayn said:

Zuhayr narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', that the Prophet ﷺ prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen or seventeen months. He liked his qiblah to be toward the House (the Ka'bah), and he prayed the 'Asr prayer, and some people prayed with him. A man who had prayed with him went out and passed by the people of the mosque while they were bowing, and he said: "I bear witness by Allah that I prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ facing Makkah." So they turned around, while still in their positions, toward the House.[[Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 4486, from Abu Nu'aym.]]

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Isra'il informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' [who said] [[Addition from J, T, W.]]: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived in Madinah, he prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen or seventeen months, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ loved to be turned toward the Ka'bah. So this was revealed: ﴿We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the sky, so We will surely turn you to a qiblah that you will like﴾ [[Addition from J.]], and he was turned toward the Ka'bah.

al-Nasa'i related from Abu Sa'id ibn al-Mu'alla, who said: "We used to go in the morning to the mosque during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we would pass by the mosque and pray in it. One day we passed by while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting on the pulpit (minbar), and I said: 'Something has happened.' So I sat down, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse: ﴿We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the sky, so We will surely turn you to a qiblah that you will like﴾, until he finished the verse. I said to my companion: 'Come, let us pray two units (rak'ahs) before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ descends, so that we will be the first to pray.' So we hid ourselves and prayed them. Then the Prophet ﷺ descended and led the people in the Dhuhr prayer that day."[[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra (11004).]]

Similarly, Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn 'Umar that the first prayer the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed toward the Ka'bah was the Dhuhr prayer, and that it is the "middle prayer" (al-salat al-wusta). But the well-known view is that the first prayer he prayed toward the Ka'bah was the 'Asr prayer, and for this reason the news reached the people of Quba' only at the Fajr prayer.

The Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Sulayman ibn Ahmad narrated to us; al-Husayn ibn Ishaq al-Tustari narrated to us; Raja' ibn Muhammad al-Saqati narrated to us; Ishaq ibn Idris narrated to us; Ibrahim ibn Ja'far narrated to us; my father narrated to me, from his grandmother, his father's mother, Umm Nuwaylah bint Muslim, who said: "We prayed the Dhuhr [or the 'Asr] [[In J: "the Dhuhr and the 'Asr".]] in the Mosque of Bani Harithah, and we faced the Mosque of Iliya' (Jerusalem) and prayed two units. Then someone came and told us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had turned to face the Sacred House. So the women moved to the place of the men, and the men to the place of the women, and we prayed the remaining two prostrations facing the Sacred House." A man from Bani Harithah told me that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Those are men who believe in the unseen."[[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (25/43). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (2/14): "In its chain is Ishaq ibn Idris al-Aswari, who is weak and abandoned."]]

Ibn Mardawayh also said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Duhaym narrated to us; Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us; Malik ibn Isma'il al-Nahdi narrated to us; Qays narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn 'Ilaqah, from 'Umarah ibn Awz, who said: "While we were praying toward Bayt al-Maqdis, bowing, a caller came to the door and announced: 'The qiblah has been changed to the Ka'bah.' So I bear witness regarding our imam that he turned, and he, along with the men and the boys, while they were bowing, turned toward the Ka'bah."[[Also related by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf (1/335) from Shababah, from Qays, from Ziyad, with the same wording.]]

* *

His words: ﴿And wherever you are, turn your faces toward it﴾ commands facing the Ka'bah from all directions of the earth, east, west, north, and south, with no exception, except for the voluntary (nafilah) prayer while travelling, for one may pray it in whatever direction one's mount faces, while the heart is oriented toward the Ka'bah. Likewise, in the state of fighting in battle, one prays in any condition. Likewise, whoever does not know the direction of the qiblah prays according to his best effort (ijtihad), even if he is mistaken in reality, because Allah the Exalted does not burden a soul beyond its capacity.

Issue: The Malikis have used this verse as evidence that the one praying should look ahead of him, not at the place of his prostration, as al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and Abu Hanifah held. The Malikis say, based on His words: ﴿So turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque﴾, that if he looked at the place of his prostration, he would have to bend in some way, and this contradicts the completeness of standing. Some have said: the one praying, while standing, looks at his chest. Shurayk al-Qadi said: he looks, while standing, at the place of his prostration, as the majority of the community said, because it is more effective in humility and more emphatic in khushu' (devotion), and a hadith has been transmitted about it. As for when bowing (ruku'), he looks at the place of his feet; when prostrating (sujud), at the place of his nose; and when sitting, at his lap.

* *

His words: ﴿And indeed, those who were given the Scripture know that it is the truth from their Lord﴾ mean: the Jews, who denied your facing the Ka'bah and your turning away from Bayt al-Maqdis, know that Allah the Exalted would direct you toward it, through what is in their books from their prophets regarding the description and attributes of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his ummah, and what Allah the Exalted singled him out with and honored him with, of the complete and great Shari'ah. But the People of the Book conceal this among themselves out of envy, disbelief, and obstinacy. For this reason, Allah the Exalted threatens them with His words: ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what they do﴾ [[In J, T: "what you do".]].

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 145:

He, exalted is He, informs about the disbelief and obstinacy of the Jews, and their opposition to what they know about the matter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and that even if he (ﷺ) were to present to them every proof of the truth of what he had brought them, they would not follow him and would abandon their desires, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justified will not believe. Even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment.﴾ [Yunus: 96, 97] And for this reason He said here: ﴿And even if you brought those who were given the Scripture every sign, they would not follow your qiblah.﴾

* *

As for His saying ﴿Nor are you one who will follow their qiblah [and some of them are not followers of each other's qiblah]﴾, it is an informing about the strength of the Messenger's ﷺ adherence to what Allah, exalted is He, commanded him, and that just as they hold firmly to their opinions and desires, he too holds firmly to the command of Allah, His obedience, and following His good pleasure. He does not follow their desires in any of his circumstances. He was not facing Bayt al-Maqdis because it is the qiblah of the Jews; rather, that was by the command of Allah, exalted is He. Then Allah, exalted is He, warned against deviating from the truth, which the scholar knows, toward desire, for the proof against the scholar is more binding than against others. For this reason He said, addressing the Messenger, while the intended meaning is the Ummah: ﴿And even if you brought those who were given the Scripture every sign, they would not follow your qiblah, nor are you one who will follow their qiblah, nor are some of them followers of the qiblah of others. And if you followed their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, indeed you would then be of the wrongdoers.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 145]

Allah, exalted is He, informs us that the scholars of the People of the Book recognize the truth of what the Messenger (ﷺ) brought them [as they recognize their sons], just as one of them recognizes his own son. The Arabs used to give this as an example of the certainty of a matter, as in the hadith that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to a man who had a young child with him: "Is this your son?" He said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah, I testify to that." He said: "Indeed, he will not commit a crime against you, nor will you against him."[[Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (2/226, 228) and Abu Dawud in al-Sunan, no. 4495.]]

[Al-Qurtubi said: It is related that Umar said to Abdullah ibn Salam: "Do you recognize Muhammad (ﷺ) as you recognize your son?" He said: "Yes, and more. The trustworthy one descended from the heaven to the trustworthy one on earth with his description, so I recognized him. As for what has happened concerning his affair, I do not know." I say: It may be that the intended meaning is ﴿they recognize him as they recognize their sons﴾ among the sons of people, for no one doubts or disputes recognizing his own son when he sees him among all the sons of people.][[Added from C, T, A.]]

Then Allah, exalted is He, informed that, despite this verification and scholarly certainty, ﴿they conceal the truth﴾, meaning: they conceal from people what is in their books regarding the description of the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿while they know﴾.

Then Allah, exalted is He, strengthened His Prophet and the believers, and informed them that what the Messenger (ﷺ) brought is the truth about which there is no doubt or uncertainty, so He said: ﴿The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.﴾

Allah, exalted is He, informs us that the scholars of the People of the Book recognize the truth of what the Messenger (ﷺ) brought them [as they recognize their sons], just as one of them recognizes his own son. The Arabs used to give this as an example of the certainty of a matter, as in the hadith that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to a man who had a young child with him: "Is this your son?" He said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah, I testify to that." He said: "Indeed, he will not commit a crime against you, nor will you against him."[[Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (2/226, 228) and Abu Dawud in al-Sunan, no. 4495.]]

[Al-Qurtubi said: It is related that Umar said to Abdullah ibn Salam: "Do you recognize Muhammad (ﷺ) as you recognize your son?" He said: "Yes, and more. The trustworthy one descended from the heaven to the trustworthy one on earth with his description, so I recognized him. As for what has happened concerning his affair, I do not know." I say: It may be that the intended meaning is ﴿they recognize him as they recognize their sons﴾ among the sons of people, for no one doubts or disputes recognizing his own son when he sees him among all the sons of people.][[Added from C, T, A.]]

Then Allah, exalted is He, informed that, despite this verification and scholarly certainty, ﴿they conceal the truth﴾, meaning: they conceal from people what is in their books regarding the description of the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿while they know﴾.

Then Allah, exalted is He, strengthened His Prophet and the believers, and informed them that what the Messenger (ﷺ) brought is the truth about which there is no doubt or uncertainty, so He said: ﴿The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.﴾

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿And for each there is a direction toward which it turns﴾: he meant by this the people of the religions. He said: each has a qibla which they are content with, and the direction of Allah is wherever the believers turn.

Abu al-'Aliyah said: for the Jew there is a direction toward which he turns, and for the Christian there is a direction toward which he turns, and He has guided you, O community [of the certain] [[addition from ج.]], to the qibla which is the qibla.

Similar to this was narrated from Mujahid, 'Ata', al-Dahhak, al-Rabi' ibn Anas and al-Suddi.

Mujahid said in another narration: rather, He commanded every people to pray toward the Ka'bah.

Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Ja'far al-Baqir and Ibn 'Amir read: "wa-li-kullin wijhatun huwa muwalaha" (and for each there is a direction, He is turning it).

This verse is similar to His saying, the Exalted: ﴿For each of you We have made a law and a way. And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one community, but [He intended] to test you in what He has given you. So race to [all that is] good. To Allah is your return, all of you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 48].

And here He said: ﴿Wherever you may be, Allah will bring you all together. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent﴾ — meaning: He is able to gather you from the earth, even if your bodies and forms have been scattered.

This is the third command from Allah, the Exalted, to face the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram) from all regions of the earth.

Scholars have differed concerning the wisdom behind this repetition three times. It has been said that it is for emphasis, because it was the first abrogation (naskh) that occurred in Islam, as stated by Ibn 'Abbas and others. It has also been said that rather, it is directed at different circumstances: the first command is for one who is witnessing the Ka'bah, the second for one who is in Makkah but absent from it, and the third for one who is in the rest of the lands. This is how Fakhr al-Din al-Razi (Fakhr al-Din al-Razi) explained it. Al-Qurtubi said: the first is for one who is in Makkah, the second for one who is in the rest of the regions, and the third for one who sets out on journeys. Al-Qurtubi favoured this answer. It has also been said that this was mentioned because of its connection to what comes before or after it in the context. He first said: ﴿We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven; so We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased﴾, up to His saying: ﴿And indeed, those who were given the Scripture know that it is the truth from their Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what they do﴾. So in this place He mentioned His granting his request and His command to the qiblah which he loved to face and was pleased with. In the second command He said: ﴿And from wherever you emerge, turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And indeed, it is the truth from your Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what you do﴾. So He stated that it is the truth from Allah, and it rose above the first position, since it was in accord with the pleasure of the Messenger ﷺ. He then made clear that it is also the truth from Allah, which He loves and approves. In the third command He mentioned the wisdom of cutting off the argument of the opposing Jews, who used to argue by the Messenger's facing their qiblah, and they knew from their books that he would be turned to the qiblah of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), that is, the Ka'bah. Likewise, the polytheists of the Arabs had their argument cut off when the Messenger ﷺ was turned away from the qiblah of the Jews to the qiblah of Ibrahim, which is more honourable. They used to venerate the Ka'bah, and the Messenger's facing it pleased them. Other answers regarding the wisdom of the repetition have been given besides these, and Fakhr al-Din and others have elaborated on them. And Allah, glory be to Him, knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿So that people will not have any argument against you﴾ means: the People of the Scripture. For they know from the description of this Ummah that it faces the Ka'bah, so if they lacked that trait in its description they might argue against the Muslims with it. Or [it means] so that they would not argue by the Muslims' agreement with them in facing Bayt al-Maqdis. And this is the more apparent.

Abu al-'Aliyah said: ﴿So that people will not have any argument against you﴾ refers to the People of the Scripture when they said: "Muhammad has been turned to the Ka'bah," and they said: "The man has yearned for the house of his father and the religion of his people." Their argument against the Prophet ﷺ regarding his turning to the Sacred House was that they said: "He will return to our religion just as he returned to our qiblah."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Similar to this has been related from Mujahid, 'Ata', al-Dahhak, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Qatadah and al-Suddi.

These said, regarding His saying: ﴿except those who wronged among them﴾, that it refers to the polytheists of Quraysh.

Some of them explained the argument of the wrongdoers, which is baseless, by saying: "This man claims that he is upon the religion of Ibrahim. If his facing Bayt al-Maqdis was upon the creed of Ibrahim, why did he turn away from it?" The answer: Allah, the Exalted, chose for him to face Bayt al-Maqdis first, due to the wisdom He has in that, so he obeyed his Lord in that. Then He turned him to the qiblah of Ibrahim, which is the Ka'bah, and he also complied with Allah's command in that. So he, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, is obedient to Allah in all his circumstances, never deviating from the command of Allah for the blink of an eye, and his community follows him.

* *

His saying: ﴿So do not fear them, but fear Me﴾ means: do not fear the doubts of the wrongdoers who seek to trouble you, and single out fear for Me, for He, the Exalted, is the One who deserves to be feared.

* *

His saying: ﴿And that I may complete My favour upon you﴾ is conjoined to ﴿So that people will not have any argument against you﴾, meaning: and that I may complete My favour upon you in what I have legislated for you of facing the Ka'bah, so that the Sharia may be perfected for you in all its aspects. ﴿And that you may be guided﴾ means: to that from which the nations went astray, We have guided you to it and singled you out with it. For this reason this Ummah is the most honoured and the most excellent of the nations.

This is the third command from Allah, the Exalted, to face the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram) from all regions of the earth.

Scholars have differed concerning the wisdom behind this repetition three times. It has been said that it is for emphasis, because it was the first abrogation (naskh) that occurred in Islam, as stated by Ibn 'Abbas and others. It has also been said that rather, it is directed at different circumstances: the first command is for one who is witnessing the Ka'bah, the second for one who is in Makkah but absent from it, and the third for one who is in the rest of the lands. This is how Fakhr al-Din al-Razi (Fakhr al-Din al-Razi) explained it. Al-Qurtubi said: the first is for one who is in Makkah, the second for one who is in the rest of the regions, and the third for one who sets out on journeys. Al-Qurtubi favoured this answer. It has also been said that this was mentioned because of its connection to what comes before or after it in the context. He first said: ﴿We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven; so We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased﴾, up to His saying: ﴿And indeed, those who were given the Scripture know that it is the truth from their Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what they do﴾. So in this place He mentioned His granting his request and His command to the qiblah which he loved to face and was pleased with. In the second command He said: ﴿And from wherever you emerge, turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And indeed, it is the truth from your Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what you do﴾. So He stated that it is the truth from Allah, and it rose above the first position, since it was in accord with the pleasure of the Messenger ﷺ. He then made clear that it is also the truth from Allah, which He loves and approves. In the third command He mentioned the wisdom of cutting off the argument of the opposing Jews, who used to argue by the Messenger's facing their qiblah, and they knew from their books that he would be turned to the qiblah of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), that is, the Ka'bah. Likewise, the polytheists of the Arabs had their argument cut off when the Messenger ﷺ was turned away from the qiblah of the Jews to the qiblah of Ibrahim, which is more honourable. They used to venerate the Ka'bah, and the Messenger's facing it pleased them. Other answers regarding the wisdom of the repetition have been given besides these, and Fakhr al-Din and others have elaborated on them. And Allah, glory be to Him, knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿So that people will not have any argument against you﴾ means: the People of the Scripture. For they know from the description of this Ummah that it faces the Ka'bah, so if they lacked that trait in its description they might argue against the Muslims with it. Or [it means] so that they would not argue by the Muslims' agreement with them in facing Bayt al-Maqdis. And this is the more apparent.

Abu al-'Aliyah said: ﴿So that people will not have any argument against you﴾ refers to the People of the Scripture when they said: "Muhammad has been turned to the Ka'bah," and they said: "The man has yearned for the house of his father and the religion of his people." Their argument against the Prophet ﷺ regarding his turning to the Sacred House was that they said: "He will return to our religion just as he returned to our qiblah."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Similar to this has been related from Mujahid, 'Ata', al-Dahhak, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Qatadah and al-Suddi.

These said, regarding His saying: ﴿except those who wronged among them﴾, that it refers to the polytheists of Quraysh.

Some of them explained the argument of the wrongdoers, which is baseless, by saying: "This man claims that he is upon the religion of Ibrahim. If his facing Bayt al-Maqdis was upon the creed of Ibrahim, why did he turn away from it?" The answer: Allah, the Exalted, chose for him to face Bayt al-Maqdis first, due to the wisdom He has in that, so he obeyed his Lord in that. Then He turned him to the qiblah of Ibrahim, which is the Ka'bah, and he also complied with Allah's command in that. So he, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, is obedient to Allah in all his circumstances, never deviating from the command of Allah for the blink of an eye, and his community follows him.

* *

His saying: ﴿So do not fear them, but fear Me﴾ means: do not fear the doubts of the wrongdoers who seek to trouble you, and single out fear for Me, for He, the Exalted, is the One who deserves to be feared.

* *

His saying: ﴿And that I may complete My favour upon you﴾ is conjoined to ﴿So that people will not have any argument against you﴾, meaning: and that I may complete My favour upon you in what I have legislated for you of facing the Ka'bah, so that the Sharia may be perfected for you in all its aspects. ﴿And that you may be guided﴾ means: to that from which the nations went astray, We have guided you to it and singled you out with it. For this reason this Ummah is the most honoured and the most excellent of the nations.

The Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 2, verses 151–152:

Allah, the Exalted, mentions to His believing servants the blessing He bestowed upon them by sending to them the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿He recites to them His verses, purifies them﴾, meaning He cleanses them from base moral qualities, the defilement of souls, and the deeds of the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance), ﴿and brings them out of darkness into light﴾, ﴿and teaches them the Book﴾, which is the Qur'an, ﴿and the wisdom﴾, which is the Sunnah (the Prophetic tradition), ﴿and teaches them what they did not know﴾. They had been in the utter ignorance of the Jahiliyyah, speaking foolishly with lies. Through the blessing of his message and the auspiciousness of his mission, they moved to the state of the friends of Allah and the character of the scholars. They became the deepest of people in knowledge, the most righteous of hearts, the least artificial, and the most truthful in speech. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Certainly did Allah confer favour upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from themselves, reciting to them His verses and purifying them﴾ [Al 'Imran: 164], to the end of the verse. He also censured those who did not recognise the worth of this blessing, saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to settle in the house of destruction?﴾ [Ibrahim: 28].

Ibn 'Abbas said: "By the favour of Allah is meant Muhammad (ﷺ)." For this reason Allah urged the believers to acknowledge this blessing and to requite it with remembrance and gratitude to Him, saying: ﴿So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not be ungrateful﴾.

Mujahid said regarding His words ﴿as We sent among you a messenger from yourselves﴾ [[In T: "fikum" which is an error.]]: "It means: as I have done, so remember Me."

'Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated from Hisham ibn Sa'id, from Zayd ibn Aslam, that Musa (peace be upon him) said: "O Lord, how shall I thank You?" His Lord said to him: "Remember Me and do not forget Me. When you remember Me, you have indeed thanked Me, and when you forget Me, you have indeed been ungrateful to Me."

Al-Hasan al-Basri, Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Suddi, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "Allah remembers whoever remembers Him, increases whoever thanks Him, and punishes whoever disbelieves in Him."

One of the early generation (al-salaf, the righteous predecessors) said regarding the verse ﴿Fear Allah as He should be feared﴾ [Al 'Imran: 102]: "It means that He is obeyed and not disobeyed, remembered and not forgotten, and thanked and not disbelieved."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun informed us, 'Umarah al-Saydalani informed us, Makhul al-Azdi narrated to us, who said: I said to Ibn 'Umar: "What do you think of one who kills a soul, drinks wine, steals, and commits adultery, yet remembers Allah? And Allah has said: ﴿So remember Me; I will remember you﴾?" He said: "When such a person remembers Allah, Allah remembers him with His curse, until he falls silent."

Al-Hasan al-Basri, regarding His words ﴿So remember Me; I will remember you﴾, said: "Remember Me in what I have made obligatory upon you, and I will remember you in what I have made binding upon Myself for you."

From Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Remember Me through your obedience to Me, and I will remember you through My forgiveness." In another narration: "through My mercy."

From Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words ﴿So remember Me; I will remember you﴾ [[In H: "udhkuruni" and the affirmed reading is from T.]]: "The remembrance of Allah for you is greater than your remembrance of Him."

In the authentic hadith: "Allah, the Exalted, says: Whoever remembers Me in his self, I remember him in My Self; and whoever remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than it."

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: O son of Adam, if you remember Me in yourself, I remember you in Myself; and if you remember Me in a gathering, I remember you in a gathering of angels, or He said: in a gathering better than them. And if you draw near to Me by a span, I draw near to you by a cubit; and if you draw near to Me by a cubit, I draw near to you by a fathom; and if you come to Me walking, I come to you running."

Its chain is sound (sahih al-isnad). Al-Bukhari transmitted it from the hadith of Qatadah [[Al-Musnad (3/138) and Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (7536).]]. In his version, Qatadah said: "Allah is nearer with mercy."

* *

As for His words ﴿and be grateful to Me and do not be ungrateful﴾: Allah commanded gratitude to Him and promised increase of good in return for it, saying: ﴿And when your Lord proclaimed: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you; but if you are ungrateful, indeed My punishment is severe﴾ [Ibrahim: 7].

Imam Ahmad said: Rawh narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Fudayl [[In A: "al-Fadl".]] ibn Fadalah, a man from Qays, who said: Abu Raja al-'Utaridi narrated to us, who said: 'Imran ibn Husayn came out to us wearing a mutraf (a striped cloak) of khazz (silk) which we had never seen him wear before or after that. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has been granted a blessing by Allah, Allah loves to see the effect of His blessing upon His creation." Rawh said on one occasion: "upon His servant" [[Al-Musnad (4/438).]].
