Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 153–154:

When Allah, exalted is He, finished explaining the command to give thanks (shukr), He began explaining patience (sabr), and guiding to seeking help through patience and prayer (salah). A servant is either in a blessing, so he gives thanks for it, or in an affliction, so he is patient through it, as came in the hadith: "How wondrous is the affair of the believer! Allah does not decree for him any decree except that it is good for him. If something pleasant befalls him and he gives thanks, it is good for him; and if something harmful befalls him and he is patient, it is good for him."

Allah, exalted is He, also made clear that the best things to seek help with in bearing calamities are patience and prayer, as was mentioned earlier in His saying: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed it is difficult except for the humble [khashi'in]﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 45]. And in the hadith: when a matter distressed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he would pray (salla).[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. (1319), from the hadith of Hudhayfah (may Allah be pleased with him).]]

Patience is of two kinds: patience in abstaining from what is forbidden and sinful, and patience in performing acts of obedience and drawing near (to Allah). The second brings greater reward, because it is the intended goal. As 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "Patience is in two matters: patience for Allah in what He loves, even if it is burdensome to the souls and bodies, and patience for Allah in what He dislikes, even if the desires strive toward it. Whoever is like this is among the patient ones to whom greetings will be given, if Allah wills."

'Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-'Abidin said: "When Allah gathers the first and the last, a caller will call out: 'Where are the patient ones, that they may enter Paradise before the reckoning?' He said: So a group of people will stand up, and the angels will meet them and say: 'Where are you going, O children of Adam?' They will say: 'To Paradise.' They will say: 'And before the reckoning?' They will say: 'Yes.' They will say: 'And who are you?' They will say: 'The patient ones.' They will say: 'And what was your patience?' They will say: 'We were patient in obedience to Allah, and we were patient in refraining from disobedience to Allah, until Allah caused us to die.' They will say: 'You are as you have said. Enter Paradise; how excellent is the reward of those who act.'"

I say: This is supported by the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿Only those who are patient will be given their reward without reckoning﴾ [Az-Zumar: 10].

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Patience is the servant's acknowledgment to Allah of what has befallen him, and his seeking reward from Allah, hoping for His recompense. A man may be distressed while appearing self-controlled, so that nothing is seen from him but patience."

* *

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not say of those who are killed in the way of Allah, "They are dead." Rather, they are alive, but you do not perceive﴾, He informs that the martyrs in their barzakh (intermediate state) are alive and provided for, as came in Sahih Muslim: "Indeed, the souls of the martyrs are in the crops of green birds that roam in Paradise wherever they wish, then they take shelter in lamps suspended beneath the Throne. Your Lord looks down upon them with a look and says: 'What do you desire?' They say: 'O our Lord, what more could we desire, when You have given us what You have not given any of Your creation?' Then He returned to them with the same question, and when they saw that they would not be left alone until they asked, they said: 'We want You to return us to the worldly abode so that we may fight in Your way and be killed in You once more,' because of what they see of the reward of martyrdom. The Lord, majestic is His majesty, says: 'I have decreed that they will not return to it.'"[[Sahih Muslim, no. (1887), from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him); its wording differs but its meaning is the same.]]

And in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad, from Imam al-Shafi'i, from Imam Malik, from al-Zuhri, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The soul of the believer is a bird that hangs from the trees of Paradise until Allah returns it to its body on the Day He resurrects it."[[Al-Musnad (3/455).]]

In it there is also an indication that it applies generally to believers, although the martyrs have been specifically mentioned in the Qur'an, as an honour, dignity and exaltation for them.

God, the Exalted, informs us that He tests His servants [the believers] [[addition from ج.]], that is, He tries and examines them, as He said: ﴿And We will surely test you until We know those of you who strive and endure, and We will test your reports﴾ [Muhammad: 31]. He tests them sometimes with ease and sometimes with hardship, such as fear and hunger, as He said: ﴿So Allah made them taste the garment of hunger and fear﴾ [al-Nahl: 112]. The hungry person and the frightened person both show it. For this reason He said, "the garment of hunger and fear." Here He said, ﴿with something of fear and hunger﴾, meaning a small amount of it, ﴿and loss of wealth﴾, meaning the loss of some of it, ﴿and lives﴾, such as the death of companions, relatives and loved ones, ﴿and fruits﴾, meaning that gardens and fields do not yield as they usually do. As some of the early generations [al-Salaf] said, some palm trees would bear fruit only once. All of this and similar things are the means by which Allah tests His servants. Whoever is patient, Allah rewards him, and whoever despairs, Allah brings His punishment upon him. For this reason He said: ﴿And give good news to the patient﴾.

Some exegetes have related that what is meant here by "fear" is the fear of Allah, by "hunger" is the fast of Ramadan, by "loss of wealth" is zakat, by "lives" is illness, and by "fruits" is children. But this requires consideration, and Allah knows best.

Then God clarified who the patient are whom He praised. He said: ﴿Those who, when a calamity afflicts them, say, "Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return"﴾. That is, by saying this they console themselves over what has befallen them, and they know that they are His possession, and that He disposes of His servants as He wills, and they know that not even the weight of an atom is lost before Him on the Day of Resurrection. So this statement brings them the acknowledgment that they are His servants and that they will return to Him in the Hereafter. For this reason God informed us of what He gave them in return, saying: ﴿Upon them are blessings from their Lord﴾, meaning praise from Allah for them and mercy.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: that is, security from punishment. ﴿And they are the guided ones﴾. Amir al-Mu'minin 'Umar ibn al-Khattab [may Allah be pleased with him] said: "What an excellent pair of portions, and what an excellent addition!" ﴿Upon them are blessings from their Lord and mercy﴾: these are the two portions, ﴿and they are the guided ones﴾: this is the addition, which is what is placed between the two loads and is an increase in the burden. Likewise these people receive their reward and are also given more.

Numerous hadiths have been transmitted concerning the reward for istirja' [saying "Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return"] at the time of calamities. Among them is what Imam Ahmad narrated:

Yunus narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, meaning Ibn Sa'd, from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Usamah ibn al-Hadi, from 'Amr ibn Abi 'Amr, from al-Muttalib, from Umm Salamah, who said: Abu Salamah came to me one day from the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "I have heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a statement that pleased me." He said: "No Muslim is afflicted by a calamity and then says the istirja' at the time of his calamity and then says: 'O Allah, reward me in my calamity and give me something better in its place,' except that it will be done for him." Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 158:

Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Hashimi narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I said: "Have you considered the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, as-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. So whoever makes pilgrimage to the House or performs 'umrah, there is no blame upon him for going back and forth between them﴾?" I said: "By Allah, there is no blame upon anyone for not going back and forth between them." Then 'A'ishah said: "What an evil thing you have said, my nephew! If it were as you interpret it, the verse would read: 'There is no blame upon him for not going back and forth between them.' Rather, it was revealed concerning the Ansar, who, before they embraced Islam, used to pronounce the talbiyah for Manat, the idol they worshipped at al-Mushallal. Whoever pronounced the talbiyah for her would feel reluctant to go back and forth between as-Safa and al-Marwah. So they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about that and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we used to feel reluctant to go back and forth between as-Safa and al-Marwah in the Jahiliyyah.' Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, as-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah﴾ up to His words: ﴿there is no blame upon him for going back and forth between them﴾." 'A'ishah said: "Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ established the going back and forth between them as a sunnah, so no one has the right to abandon going back and forth between them." Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in the Two Sahihs.

And in a narration from al-Zuhri, he said: I narrated this hadith to Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, and he said: "This knowledge, I had not heard it. But I have heard men of knowledge saying that the people – except those whom 'A'ishah mentioned – used to say: 'Our going back and forth between these two stones is from the affairs of the Jahiliyyah.' And others from the Ansar said: 'We were only commanded to circumambulate the House, and we were not commanded to go back and forth between as-Safa and al-Marwah.' So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿Indeed, as-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah﴾." Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman said: "Perhaps it was revealed concerning both of these groups."

Al-Bukhari narrated it from the hadith of Malik, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, with something similar to what preceded. Then al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Sulayman, who said: "I asked Anas about as-Safa and al-Marwah, and he said: 'We used to consider that to be from the affairs of the Jahiliyyah. When Islam came, we refrained from them, and then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, as-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah﴾."

Al-Qurtubi mentioned in his tafsir, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The devils used to separate between as-Safa and al-Marwah the whole night, and there were idols between them. When Islam came, they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about going back and forth between them, and this verse was revealed." Al-Sha'bi said: "Isaf was upon as-Safa and Na'ilah was upon al-Marwah, and they used to touch (istilam) them. After Islam, they felt reluctant to go back and forth between them, so this verse was revealed."

I say: Ibn Ishaq mentioned in the Book of the Biography (al-Sirah) that Isaf and Na'ilah were two humans who committed fornication inside the Ka'bah, so they were transformed into two stones. Quraysh set them up opposite the Ka'bah so that people might take a lesson from them. When their time passed, they were worshipped. Then they were moved to as-Safa and al-Marwah and were set up there, and whoever circumambulated as-Safa and al-Marwah would touch them. For this reason Abu Talib says in his well-known qasidah:

"And where the Ash'ariyyun kneel their mounts,
at the flowing place of the torrents, from Isaf and Na'il..."

In the Sahih of Muslim there is the lengthy hadith of Jabir, in which: when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished his circumambulation of the House, he returned to the Corner (al-Rukn) and touched it, then he went out from the Gate of as-Safa, while he was reciting: ﴿Indeed, as-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah﴾, then he said: "I begin with what Allah began with." And in the narration of al-Nasa'i: "Begin with what Allah began with."

Imam Ahmad said: Shurayh narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mu'ammal narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Safiyyah bint Shaybah, from Habibah bint Abi Tajrah, who said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ going back and forth between as-Safa and al-Marwah, with the people in front of him while he was behind them, and he was running, so that I could see his knees from the intensity of the running, his waist-wrap revolving around him, and he was saying: 'Run, for Allah has prescribed running for you.'"

Then Imam Ahmad narrated it from 'Abd al-Razzaq, who informed us, from Ma'mar, from Wasil – the freedman of Abu 'Uyaynah – from Musa ibn 'Ubaydah, from Safiyyah bint Shaybah, that a woman informed her that she heard the Prophet ﷺ between as-Safa and al-Marwah saying: "Running has been prescribed for you, so run."

This hadith has been used as evidence for the view of those who hold that running between as-Safa and al-Marwah is a pillar (rukn) of Hajj, as is the view of al-Shafi'i and whoever agrees with him, and it is a narration from Ahmad and the well-known view from Malik. It is also said that it is obligatory (wajib) and not a pillar; whoever abandons it, intentionally or by forgetfulness, compensates for it with a sacrifice (dam), and this is a narration from Ahmad, and a group holds it. It is also said that it is merely recommended (mustahabb), and this is the view of Abu Hanifah, al-Thawri, al-Sha'bi and Ibn Sirin, and it is narrated from Anas, Ibn 'Umar and Ibn 'Abbas, and it is related from Malik in al-'Utbiyyah. Al-Qurtubi said: "They argued with His words: ﴿And whoever volunteers good﴾." It is also said that it is merely recommended. The first view is more preponderant, because he ﷺ went back and forth between them and said: "Take your rites from me." So everything he did in that Hajj is obligatory and must be performed in Hajj, except what is excluded by an evidence. And Allah knows best.

Allah, the Exalted, has made clear that going back and forth between as-Safa and al-Marwah is among the symbols of Allah, meaning: among what Allah, the Exalted, prescribed for Ibrahim the Friend in the rites of Hajj. It has preceded in the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas that the origin of this is taken from the running of Hajar and her going back and forth between as-Safa and al-Marwah in search of water for her child, when her water and provisions ran out, when Ibrahim, peace be upon him, left them there with no one from the people near them. When she feared for her child's destruction there and what she had was exhausted, she set out seeking relief from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. She kept going back and forth in this blessed place between as-Safa and al-Marwah, humbled, fearful, anxious, distressed, and in need of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, until Allah relieved her distress, comforted her strangeness, relieved her hardship, and caused Zamzam to gush forth for her, whose water is food for the eater and a cure for sickness. So the one who runs between them should bring to mind his poverty, his humility and his need of Allah for the guidance of his heart, the righteousness of his condition, and the forgiveness of his sins; he should seek refuge with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to remove what he has of deficiencies and faults; he should ask Him to guide him to the Straight Path, to keep him upon it until his death, and to transform him from his state of sins and disobedience to a state of perfection, forgiveness, rectitude and steadfastness, just as He did with Hajar, peace be upon her.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And whoever volunteers good﴾, it has been said: he adds to his circumambulation between them beyond the required amount, an eighth, a ninth, and so on. It has also been said: he goes back and forth between them during a voluntary Hajj or a voluntary 'umrah. It has also been said: the meaning is that he volunteers good in all other acts of worship. Al-Razi (Fakhr al-Din) related this, and he attributed the third view to al-Hasan al-Basri. And Allah knows best. Ibn Kathir said: He, may He be exalted, informs of His singularity in divinity, and that He has no partner and no equal. Rather, He is Allah, the One, the Unique, the Single, the Eternal Refuge, ﴿there is no god but He, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾. The explanation of these two names has already preceded at the beginning of the surah. [[In manuscripts ج، ط، أ، و: "at the beginning of al-Fatihah".]]

In the hadith transmitted from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma' bint Yazid ibn al-Sakan, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "The Greatest Name of Allah is in these two verses: ﴿And your God is One God; there is no god but He, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾ and ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. Allah, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all existence﴾ [Al-Imran: 1, 2]." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. 1496, and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. 3478; al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith."]]

Then he cited the evidence for His sole divinity through His creation of the heavens and the earth, and what is in them, and what lies between them of the created beings that He brought into existence and originated, which point to His oneness. He said:

﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, and the ships that sail in the sea with what benefits mankind, and what Allah sends down from the sky of water, giving life thereby to the earth after its death, and dispersing therein every kind of moving creature, and the turning of the winds and the clouds subjected between the sky and the earth, are signs for a people who use their reason.﴾

He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾, with their subtlety [and] [[Addition from A.]] their height, their vastness, their wandering planets and fixed stars, and the revolution of their spheres. And this earth, with its [density and] [[Addition from A.]] its lowness, its mountains, its seas, its deserts, its valleys, its inhabited places, and what is in it of benefits. ﴿And the alternation of the night and the day﴾: this one comes and goes, and the other follows and succeeds it, not lagging behind it for an instant, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿The sun is not permitted to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day, but each is travelling in an orbit﴾ [Ya-Sin: 40]. Sometimes this one lengthens and that one shortens, and sometimes one takes from the other and then they exchange, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night﴾ [al-Hajj: 61], meaning: He adds from this to that and from that to this.

﴿And the ships that sail in the sea with what benefits mankind﴾

That is, in His subjugation of the sea to carry ships from one side to the other, for the livelihood of people and for benefiting from what is in the possession of the people of that region, and transporting this to those, and what is with those to these. [In C: "those for these".]

﴿And what Allah sends down from the sky of water, giving life thereby to the earth after its death﴾, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And a sign for them is the dead earth: We give it life and bring forth from it grain, and from it they eat. And We have made therein gardens of date palms and grapevines, and caused springs to gush forth therein, that they may eat of its fruit, and of what their hands have made. Will they not then be grateful? Glory be to Him who created all the pairs, of what the earth grows, and of themselves, and of what they do not know﴾ [Ya-Sin: 33–36].

﴿And He dispersed therein every kind of moving creature﴾: that is, with the differences of their forms, colours, benefits, smallness and largeness. He knows all of that, and provides for it; nothing of that is hidden from Him, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿There is no creature on the earth but that its provision is upon Allah, and He knows its place of rest and its place of storage; all is in a clear record﴾ [Hud: 6].

﴿And the turning of the winds﴾: that is, sometimes they come with mercy and sometimes they come with punishment; sometimes they come bringing good news before the clouds, sometimes they drive them, sometimes they gather them, sometimes they scatter them, and sometimes they change them. [Then sometimes they come from the south, which is the Syrian direction, and sometimes they come from the direction of Yemen, and sometimes it is a Saba wind, which is the eastern wind that strikes the face of the Ka'bah, and sometimes it is a Dabur wind, which is a western wind that blows from the direction of the back of the Ka'bah. The winds are all named according to how they pass over the Ka'bah. People have written many books on the winds, the rain and the weather-stars concerning their terminology and rulings, and to expound on that would be lengthy here; and Allah knows best.] [[Addition from C, T, A.]]

﴿And the clouds subjected between the sky and the earth﴾ [that is: moving between the sky and the earth] [[Addition from C, A, W.]] being driven to whatever lands and places Allah wills, as He directs them, exalted is He.

﴿Are signs for a people who use their reason﴾: that is, in these things there are clear proofs of the oneness of Allah, exalted is He, as He said: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of night and day, are signs for those of understanding, who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides, and reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth: "Our Lord, You did not create this in vain; glory be to You, so protect us from the punishment of the Fire"﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 190–191].

The Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim informed us, Abu Sa'id al-Dashtaki narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ash'ath ibn Ishaq, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Quraysh came to Muhammad (ﷺ) and said: "O Muhammad, we only want you to ask your Lord to make as-Safa into gold for us, so that we may buy horses and weapons with it, and then we will believe in you and fight alongside you." He said: "Make a covenant with me: if I ask my Lord and He makes as-Safa gold for you, you will surely believe in me." They made a covenant with him. He prayed to his Lord, and Jibril came to him and said: "Your Lord has given them as-Safa as gold, on the condition that if they do not believe in you, He will punish them with a punishment that He has not inflicted on anyone among the worlds." Muhammad (ﷺ) said: "My Lord, no! Leave me and my people; I will call them day by day." Then Allah revealed this verse: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of night and day, and the ships that sail in the sea with what benefits mankind﴾ until the end of the verse.

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it by another route, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, with the same chain. [Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/12) by way of Yahya al-Himmani, from Ya'qub al-Qummi, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, similar to it.] At its end he added: "And how would they ask you about as-Safa when they see signs greater than as-Safa?"

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: My father narrated to us, Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from 'Ata', who said: When ﴿And your God is one God; there is no god but He, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾ was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ) in Madinah, the disbelievers of Quraysh in Makkah said: "How can one God be enough for the people?" So Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of night and day, and the ships that sail in the sea with what benefits mankind﴾ up to His words: ﴿are signs for a people who use their reason﴾.

By this they know that He is one God, and that He is the God of everything and the Creator of everything.

Waki' said: Sufyan narrated to us, from his father, from Abu al-Duha, who said: When ﴿And your God is one God﴾ was revealed up to the end of the verse, the polytheists said: "If that is so, then let Him bring us a sign." So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of night and day﴾ up to His words: ﴿use their reason﴾.

Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated it from Abu Ja'far, who is al-Razi, from Sa'id ibn Masruq, the father of Sufyan, from Abu al-Duha, with the same.

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 165–167:

God mentions the state of the polytheists in this world and what awaits them in the Hereafter, since they set up [for Him] [[addition from manuscript J]] rivals (*andad*), that is, equals and counterparts whom they worship alongside Him and love as they love Him. He is God, there is no god but Him, He has no opposite, no rival, and no partner with Him.

In the *Sahihayn* (the two Sahih collections), it is narrated from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: I said, "O Messenger of God, what is the greatest sin?" He said: "That you set up a rival to God, when He created you." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4477), and Sahih Muslim, no. (68).]

As for His words, ﴿But those who believe are stronger in love for Allah﴾: because of their love for God, their complete knowledge of Him, their reverence for Him and their affirmation of His oneness, they do not associate anything with Him. Rather, they worship Him alone, rely upon Him, and turn to Him in all their affairs. Then God threatened the polytheists, who wronged themselves by this, saying: ﴿If only those who have wronged could see when they will see the punishment that all power belongs to Allah entirely, and that Allah is severe in punishment.﴾

Some of them said: the sense of the statement is: if they witnessed the punishment, they would then know that all power belongs to God entirely, meaning that judgment belongs to Him alone, with no partner, and that all things are under His subjugation, dominion and authority. ﴿And that Allah is severe in punishment﴾, as He said: ﴿So on that Day, none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds﴾ [al-Fajr 89:25–26]. The meaning is: if they knew what they would witness there, and the terrible, dreadful and horrifying matter that would befall them because of their polytheism and disbelief, they would desist from the error they are in.

Then He informed of their disbelief in their idols and the disavowal of the leaders by the followers, saying: ﴿When those who were followed disassociate themselves from those who followed [and they see the punishment, and their relations are cut off from them] [[addition from manuscript J]]﴾. The angels, whom they used to claim they worshipped in the worldly abode, will disassociate themselves from them. The angels will say: ﴿We disassociate ourselves before You; they never used to worship us﴾ [al-Qasas 28:63], and they will say: ﴿Glory be to You; You are our guardian, not them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them were believers in them﴾ [Saba' 34:41]. The jinn too will disassociate themselves from them and disown their worship of them, as God said: ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah, one who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they are unaware of their supplication? And when the people are gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship﴾ [al-Ahqaf 46:5–6]. He also said: ﴿And they have taken other than Allah as gods that they may be for them a source of honor. No! They will reject their worship of them and will be opponents to them﴾ [Maryam 19:81–82]. And al-Khalil (Abraham) said to his people: ﴿You have taken, other than Allah, idols only out of affection among yourselves in worldly life; then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will deny others and curse one another, and your refuge will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:25]. And God said: ﴿If only you could see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord, returning word to one another. Those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Were it not for you, we would have been believers." Those who were arrogant will say to those who were oppressed, "Did we avert you from guidance after it came to you? Rather, you were criminals." And those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Rather, it was [your] planning by night and day, when you were ordering us to disbelieve in Allah and set up rivals to Him." And they will conceal regret when they see the punishment. And We will put shackles around the necks of those who disbelieved. Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?﴾ [Saba' 34:31–33]. And God said: ﴿And Satan will say when the matter has been decided, "Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I betrayed you. And I had no authority over you, except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves. I cannot be your deliverer, nor can you be my deliverer. Indeed, I reject your association of me with Allah before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment."﴾ [Ibrahim 14:22].

As for His words, ﴿and they see the punishment, and their relations are cut off from them﴾: meaning they witnessed the punishment of God, and the means and ways of escape were cut off from them. They found no escape from the Fire and no place to turn.

'Ata' reported from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿and their relations were cut off from them﴾ that he said: "The affection (*mawaddah*)." Likewise Mujahid said, in the narration of Ibn Abi Najih.

As for His words, ﴿And those who followed will say, "If only we had another chance, we would disassociate ourselves from them as they have disassociated themselves from us."﴾: meaning, if only we had a return to the worldly abode, so that we could disown these people and their worship, and not turn to them, but rather single out God alone in worship. But they are lying in this; indeed, if they were returned, they would go back to what they had been forbidden. As God informed about them: ﴿Thus will Allah show them their deeds as regrets upon them, and they will never emerge from the Fire﴾. That is, their deeds will perish and vanish, as God said: ﴿And We will confront what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ [al-Furqan 25:23].

God also said: ﴿The example of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes which the wind blows forcefully on a stormy day﴾ [Ibrahim 14:18], the verse continuing. And God said: ﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a desert, which the thirsty one supposes to be water﴾ [al-Nur 24:39], the verse continuing. Therefore God said: ﴿And they will never emerge from the Fire﴾.

When Allah, exalted is He, showed that there is no god but Him and that He alone is the Creator, He began to show that He is the Provider of all His creation. In the context of bestowing favour, He mentioned that He permitted them to eat of what is on the earth, being lawful (halal) from Allah and good (tayyib), meaning agreeable in itself and harmful neither to the bodies nor to the minds. He forbade them to follow the footsteps (khutuwat) of Satan, which are his ways and paths, in what he led his followers astray in, such as the forbidding of the bahira (a she-camel whose ear was slit and was released), the sa'iba (a camel released freely), the wasila (a she-camel that bore female young consecutively), and the like, which he made attractive to them in their pre-Islamic ignorance (jahiliyya). This is as in the hadith of Iyad ibn Himar, which is in Sahih Muslim, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who said: "Allah, the Exalted, says: 'Indeed, all that I have given My servants is lawful for them.'" And in it: "Indeed I created My servants as ḥunafa' (upright in faith), but the devils came to them and led them away from their religion, and forbade them what I had made lawful for them." (Sahih Muslim, no. 2865).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Bakr ibn Murdawayh narrated to us: Sulayman ibn Ahmad narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Shayba al-Misri narrated to us: al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ihtiyati narrated to us: Abu Abd Allah al-Jawzajani, companion of Ibrahim ibn Adham, narrated to us: Ibn Juraij narrated to us, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas, who said: This verse was recited in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿O mankind, eat of what is on the earth, lawful and good﴾. Then Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, ask Allah to make me one whose supplication is answered." He said: "O Sa'd, purify your food and you will be one whose supplication is answered. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, indeed a man who puts a morsel of unlawful food into his stomach, his deeds will not be accepted for forty days. And any servant whose flesh has grown from what is unlawful and from usury, the Fire is more deserving of him." (al-Mu'jam al-Awsat of al-Tabarani, no. 5026, Majma' al-Bahrayn).

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy﴾ is a warning against him and a caution about him, as He said: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party that they may be among the companions of the Blaze﴾ [Fatir: 6]. And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Will you then take him and his descendants as allies instead of Me while they are an enemy to you? Wretched is the exchange for the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Kahf: 50].

Qatada and al-Suddi said concerning His saying: ﴿And do not follow the footsteps of Satan﴾: every act of disobedience to Allah is from the footsteps of Satan.

Ikrima said: they are the incitements (nazghat) of Satan. Mujahid said: his steps, or he said: his sins.

Abu Mijlaz said: they are vows made in acts of disobedience.

al-Sha'bi said: A man vowed to slaughter his son, so Masruq issued a fatwa to him to sacrifice a ram instead, and said: "This is from the footsteps of Satan."

Abu al-Duha narrated from Masruq: Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud was brought some udder (dar') with salt, and he began to eat. A man from the people withdrew, so Ibn Mas'ud said: "Give your companion something." He said: "I do not want it." He said: "Are you fasting?" He said: "No." He said: "Then what is your situation?" He said: "I have sworn never to eat udder." Ibn Mas'ud said: "This is from the footsteps of Satan. Eat, and make expiation for your oath."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated these, and he also said:

My father narrated to us: Hassan ibn Abd Allah al-Misri narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Rafi', who said: I became angry with my wife, and she said: "She is a Jewess one day and a Christian the next, and every slave she owns is free, if you do not divorce your wife." So I came to Abd Allah ibn Umar, and he said: "This is only from the footsteps of Satan." Zaynab bint Umm Salama said the same, and she was at that time the most learned woman in Madina. I also came to Asim and Ibn Umar, and they both said the same.

Abd ibn Humayd said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, from Shurayk, from Abd al-Karim, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Any oath or vow made in anger is from the footsteps of Satan, and its expiation is the expiation of an oath.

[Sa'id ibn Dawud said in his tafsir: Ubada ibn Abbad al-Muhallabi narrated to us, from Asim al-Ahwal, from Ikrima, concerning a man who said to his slave: "If I do not whip you one hundred lashes, then my wife is divorced." He said: "He should not whip his slave, and his wife is not divorced. This is from the footsteps of Satan."]

* *

His saying: ﴿He only commands you to evil and immorality and to say about Allah what you do not know﴾ means: Satan, your enemy, only commands you to bad deeds, and more severe than these is immorality (al-fahsha'), such as fornication and the like, and more severe than that is saying about Allah without knowledge. This includes every disbeliever and every innovator (mubtadi') as well.

When Allah, exalted is He, showed that there is no god but Him and that He alone is the Creator, He began to show that He is the Provider of all His creation. In the context of bestowing favour, He mentioned that He permitted them to eat of what is on the earth, being lawful (halal) from Allah and good (tayyib), meaning agreeable in itself and harmful neither to the bodies nor to the minds. He forbade them to follow the footsteps (khutuwat) of Satan, which are his ways and paths, in what he led his followers astray in, such as the forbidding of the bahira (a she-camel whose ear was slit and was released), the sa'iba (a camel released freely), the wasila (a she-camel that bore female young consecutively), and the like, which he made attractive to them in their pre-Islamic ignorance (jahiliyya). This is as in the hadith of Iyad ibn Himar, which is in Sahih Muslim, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who said: "Allah, the Exalted, says: 'Indeed, all that I have given My servants is lawful for them.'" And in it: "Indeed I created My servants as ḥunafa' (upright in faith), but the devils came to them and led them away from their religion, and forbade them what I had made lawful for them." (Sahih Muslim, no. 2865).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Bakr ibn Murdawayh narrated to us: Sulayman ibn Ahmad narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Shayba al-Misri narrated to us: al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ihtiyati narrated to us: Abu Abd Allah al-Jawzajani, companion of Ibrahim ibn Adham, narrated to us: Ibn Juraij narrated to us, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas, who said: This verse was recited in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿O mankind, eat of what is on the earth, lawful and good﴾. Then Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, ask Allah to make me one whose supplication is answered." He said: "O Sa'd, purify your food and you will be one whose supplication is answered. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, indeed a man who puts a morsel of unlawful food into his stomach, his deeds will not be accepted for forty days. And any servant whose flesh has grown from what is unlawful and from usury, the Fire is more deserving of him." (al-Mu'jam al-Awsat of al-Tabarani, no. 5026, Majma' al-Bahrayn).

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy﴾ is a warning against him and a caution about him, as He said: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party that they may be among the companions of the Blaze﴾ [Fatir: 6]. And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Will you then take him and his descendants as allies instead of Me while they are an enemy to you? Wretched is the exchange for the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Kahf: 50].

Qatada and al-Suddi said concerning His saying: ﴿And do not follow the footsteps of Satan﴾: every act of disobedience to Allah is from the footsteps of Satan.

Ikrima said: they are the incitements (nazghat) of Satan. Mujahid said: his steps, or he said: his sins.

Abu Mijlaz said: they are vows made in acts of disobedience.

al-Sha'bi said: A man vowed to slaughter his son, so Masruq issued a fatwa to him to sacrifice a ram instead, and said: "This is from the footsteps of Satan."

Abu al-Duha narrated from Masruq: Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud was brought some udder (dar') with salt, and he began to eat. A man from the people withdrew, so Ibn Mas'ud said: "Give your companion something." He said: "I do not want it." He said: "Are you fasting?" He said: "No." He said: "Then what is your situation?" He said: "I have sworn never to eat udder." Ibn Mas'ud said: "This is from the footsteps of Satan. Eat, and make expiation for your oath."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated these, and he also said:

My father narrated to us: Hassan ibn Abd Allah al-Misri narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Rafi', who said: I became angry with my wife, and she said: "She is a Jewess one day and a Christian the next, and every slave she owns is free, if you do not divorce your wife." So I came to Abd Allah ibn Umar, and he said: "This is only from the footsteps of Satan." Zaynab bint Umm Salama said the same, and she was at that time the most learned woman in Madina. I also came to Asim and Ibn Umar, and they both said the same.

Abd ibn Humayd said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, from Shurayk, from Abd al-Karim, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Any oath or vow made in anger is from the footsteps of Satan, and its expiation is the expiation of an oath.

[Sa'id ibn Dawud said in his tafsir: Ubada ibn Abbad al-Muhallabi narrated to us, from Asim al-Ahwal, from Ikrima, concerning a man who said to his slave: "If I do not whip you one hundred lashes, then my wife is divorced." He said: "He should not whip his slave, and his wife is not divorced. This is from the footsteps of Satan."]

* *

His saying: ﴿He only commands you to evil and immorality and to say about Allah what you do not know﴾ means: Satan, your enemy, only commands you to bad deeds, and more severe than these is immorality (al-fahsha'), such as fornication and the like, and more severe than that is saying about Allah without knowledge. This includes every disbeliever and every innovator (mubtadi') as well.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when it is said﴾ to these disbelievers among the polytheists: ﴿Follow what Allah has sent down﴾ upon His Messenger, and leave aside what you are upon of misguidance and ignorance, they answered: ﴿Rather, we will follow what we found﴾ — i.e., what we found ﴿our forefathers upon﴾ — i.e., worshipping idols and rivals (andad). Allah the Exalted says, rebuking them: ﴿Even though their forefathers﴾ — i.e., those whom they follow and whose footsteps they tread — ﴿did not reason at all, nor were they guided?﴾ — i.e., they had no understanding and no guidance!!

Ibn Ishaq narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: that it was revealed concerning a group of the Jews whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) invited to Islam, and they said: "Rather, we will follow what we found our forefathers upon." So Allah revealed this verse.

Then Allah the Exalted coined for them a parable, as He said: ﴿For those who do not believe in the Hereafter is the evil description﴾ [An-Nahl: 60]. So He said: ﴿And the likeness of those who disbelieve﴾ — i.e., in their state of error, misguidance and ignorance — is like the livestock that are called out to, which do not comprehend what is said to them. Rather, when their shepherd calls to them (na'aqa bihi ra'iyuhu), i.e., calls them toward what guides them, they do not comprehend what he says nor understand it; they only hear his voice.

This is what was related from Ibn Abbas, Abu al-Aliyah, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ata, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ata al-Khurasani and al-Rabi' ibn Anas, in similar wording.

It was also said: this is a parable coined for them regarding their calling upon the idols, which do not hear, nor see, nor understand anything. This was chosen by Ibn Jarir, but the first view is more preferable, because idols do not hear anything, nor understand it, nor see it, and they have no power to strike and no life in them. [In A: "Because the idols do not hear supplication or call; rather they are inanimate objects that hear nothing."] And His saying: ﴿Deaf, dumb, blind﴾ — i.e., deaf to hearing the truth, dumb, not uttering it, blind to seeing its path and way; ﴿so they do not reason﴾ — i.e., they do not understand or comprehend anything, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And those who denied Our signs are deaf and dumb in darkness. Whomever Allah wills, He leaves astray, and whomever He wills, He places on a straight path﴾ [Al-An'am: 39].

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when it is said﴾ to these disbelievers among the polytheists: ﴿Follow what Allah has sent down﴾ upon His Messenger, and leave aside what you are upon of misguidance and ignorance, they answered: ﴿Rather, we will follow what we found﴾ — i.e., what we found ﴿our forefathers upon﴾ — i.e., worshipping idols and rivals (andad). Allah the Exalted says, rebuking them: ﴿Even though their forefathers﴾ — i.e., those whom they follow and whose footsteps they tread — ﴿did not reason at all, nor were they guided?﴾ — i.e., they had no understanding and no guidance!!

So Allah revealed this verse.

Then Allah the Exalted coined for them a parable, as He said: ﴿For those who do not believe in the Hereafter is the evil description﴾ [An-Nahl: 60]. So He said: ﴿And the likeness of those who disbelieve﴾ — i.e., in their state of error, misguidance and ignorance — is like the livestock that are called out to, which do not comprehend what is said to them. Rather, when their shepherd calls to them (na'aqa bihi ra'iyuhu), i.e., calls them toward what guides them, they do not comprehend what he says nor understand it; they only hear his voice.

This is what was related from Ibn Abbas, Abu al-Aliyah, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ata, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ata al-Khurasani and al-Rabi' ibn Anas, in similar wording.

It was also said: this is a parable coined for them regarding their calling upon the idols, which do not hear, nor see, nor understand anything. This was chosen by Ibn Jarir, but the first view is more preferable, because idols do not hear anything, nor understand it, nor see it, and they have no power to strike and no life in them. [In A: "Because the idols do not hear supplication or call; rather they are inanimate objects that hear nothing."] And His saying: ﴿Deaf, dumb, blind﴾ — i.e., deaf to hearing the truth, dumb, not uttering it, blind to seeing its path and way; ﴿so they do not reason﴾ — i.e., they do not understand or comprehend anything, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And those who denied Our signs are deaf and dumb in darkness. Whomever Allah wills, He leaves astray, and whomever He wills, He places on a straight path﴾ [Al-An'am: 39].

Allah the Exalted says, commanding His believing servants to eat of the good things He has provided for them, and to be thankful to Him for that, if they are truly His servants. Eating what is lawful is a cause for the acceptance of supplication and worship, just as eating what is unlawful prevents the acceptance of supplication and worship. This is as found in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad:

Abu al-Nadr narrated to us: al-Fudayl ibn Marzuq narrated to us, from 'Adi ibn Thabit, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O people, Allah is Good and accepts only what is good. Allah commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers, so He said: ﴿O messengers, eat of the good things and do righteous deeds; indeed, I am Knowing of what you do﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 51], and He said: ﴿O you who have believed, eat of the good things We have provided for you﴾." Then he mentioned a man who travels for a long time, disheveled and dusty, who raises his hands to the sky, saying: "O Lord, O Lord," while his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothing is unlawful, and he is nourished by the unlawful. So how could his supplication be answered?

Muslim related it in his Sahih, and al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Fudayl [[added from A.]] ibn Marzuq. [[Al-Musnad (2/328), Sahih Muslim no. (1015), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2989).]]

When Allah bestowed His favour upon them with His provision, and guided them to eat of its good things, He mentioned that He had not forbidden them from that except carrion (al-maytah), which is that which dies of itself without slaughter (tadhkiyah). Whether it was strangled, beaten to death, fallen from a height, gored, or partly eaten by a predator, it is all carrion.

The majority of scholars have made an exception from this for the carrion of the sea, based on His saying: ﴿Lawful for you is the game of the sea and its food, as a provision for you and for the travelers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 96], as will come. The hadith of al-'Anbar is in the Sahih, the Musnad, the Muwatta' and the Sunan, in which he (peace be upon him) said concerning the sea: "Its water is pure, and its carrion is lawful." Al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, Ibn Majah and al-Daraqutni related from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, traced to the Prophet: "Two carrions and two bloods are lawful for us: fish and locusts, and liver and spleen." The explanation of this will come in the commentary on Surah al-Ma'idah. [[The takhrij of the two hadiths will come at the tafsir of the beginning of Surah al-Ma'idah.]]

The milk of carrion and its egg attached to it are impure according to al-Shafi'i and others, because it is a part of it. Malik said in one narration: it is pure, but it becomes impure by contact. Likewise the rennet (anfahah) of carrion is subject to difference of opinion, and the well-known view among them is that it is impure. They raised an objection against themselves regarding the Companions eating cheese of the Magians. Al-Qurtubi in his tafsir here said: a small amount of impurity mixed into a large quantity of liquid is excused. Ibn Majah related from the hadith of Sayf ibn Harun, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about ghee, cheese and furs, and he said: "The lawful is what Allah made lawful in His Book, the unlawful is what Allah made unlawful in His Book, and what He has been silent about is among what He has pardoned." [[Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3367); al-Tirmidhi related it in the Sunan no. (1726) through Sayf ibn Harun with this chain and said: "This is a gharib hadith; we do not know it as marfu' except through this route." Sufyan and others related from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu 'Uthman, from Salman, as his own statement, and the mawquf version appears more authentic. I asked al-Bukhari about this hadith and he said: "I do not consider it preserved; Sufyan related from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu 'Uthman, from Salman, as mawquf." Al-Bukhari said: "Sayf ibn Harun is close to acceptable in hadith; Sayf ibn Muhammad, from 'Asim, is abandoned in hadith."]]

Likewise He forbade them the flesh of swine, whether it was slaughtered or died of itself, and its fat is included in the ruling on its flesh, either by way of predominance, or because the term "flesh" encompasses it, or by way of analogy according to one opinion. [[In J: "and its flesh is included in the ruling on its fat."]] Likewise He forbade them that over which the name of other than Allah has been invoked, which is what is slaughtered for other than Allah's name, such as the idols (anṣāb), the rivals (andad), and the arrows (azlam), and similar things that the pre-Islamic era used to slaughter for. [Al-Qurtubi related from Ibn 'Atiyyah that he transmitted from al-Hasan al-Basri that he was asked about a woman who held a wedding feast for her idol and slaughtered a camel in it, and he said: it may not be eaten, because it was slaughtered for an idol. Al-Qurtubi also cited from 'A'ishah that she was asked about what non-Arabs slaughter at their festivals and then send some of it as a gift to the Muslims; she said: what was slaughtered for that day, do not eat it, but eat from their trees.] [[added from J, A.]]

Then Allah permitted the consumption of these prohibited things in cases of necessity and need for them, when other foods are absent, saying: ﴿But whoever is compelled, neither desiring nor transgressing﴾, meaning: without desire for sin or aggression, and transgression is exceeding the limit. ﴿Then there is no sin upon him﴾, meaning: in eating that. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Mujahid said regarding ﴿whoever is compelled, neither desiring nor transgressing﴾: one who cuts off the road, or who separates from the leaders, or who goes out in disobedience to Allah, has no permission (rukhsah), and whoever goes out rebelling, transgressing, or in disobedience to Allah, has no permission even if he is compelled to it. Similarly it was narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

Sa'id (in one narration from him) and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "neither desiring" means neither considering it lawful. Al-Suddi said: "neither desiring" means seeking his appetite in it. 'Ata' al-Khurasani said regarding His saying ﴿neither desiring﴾: he does not roast the carrion to enjoy it, nor cook it, and eats only what keeps him alive, and carries with him what will bring him to lawful food; when he reaches it, he discards the rest. And His saying ﴿nor transgressing﴾: he does not exceed in it what is lawful.

From Ibn 'Abbas: he should not eat his fill of it. Al-Suddi explained it as aggression. From Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿neither desiring nor transgressing﴾: ﴿neither desiring﴾ in the carrion, ﴿nor transgressing﴾ in eating it. Qatadah said: ﴿whoever is compelled, neither desiring nor transgressing﴾ in its eating: that he moves from the lawful to the unlawful while he has an alternative to it.

Al-Qurtubi related from Mujahid regarding His saying ﴿whoever is compelled﴾: meaning he is forced to it without his choice.

Issue: Al-Qurtubi mentioned that if the one in necessity finds carrion and another's food in a situation where there is no cutting off or harm, then it is not lawful for him to eat the carrion, but rather he eats the other's food without disagreement, so he said. Then he said: if he eats it in this state, does he have to compensate for it or not? There are two opinions, which are two narrations from Malik. Then he cited from the Sunan of Ibn Majah, from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Abu Iyas Ja'far ibn Abi Wahshiyyah: I heard 'Abbad ibn al-'Anzi say: a year of famine struck us, so I came to Medina. I came to an orchard, took some ears of grain, rubbed them and ate them, and put some in my cloak. The owner of the orchard came, beat me, and took my garment. I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him, and he said to the man: "You did not feed him when he was hungry or in need, nor did you teach him when he was ignorant." So he ordered that his garment be returned to him, and ordered for him a wasq of food or half a wasq. This is a sound, strong, good chain, and it has many corroborating reports. Among them is the hadith of 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about hanging fruit, and he said: "Whoever takes from it out of need, with his mouth, without carrying it in his garment, there is nothing upon him." [[Related by al-Tirmidhi in the Sunan no. (1289), who said: "This is a hasan hadith."]] The hadith continues.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said regarding His saying ﴿then there is no sin upon him, indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: concerning what he ate out of necessity; and it reached us, and Allah knows best, that he should not exceed three morsels.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Forgiving for what he ate of the unlawful; Merciful in that He made the unlawful lawful for him in necessity.

Waki' said: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, who said: whoever is compelled and does not eat or drink, then dies, enters the Fire.

[This implies that eating carrion for one in necessity is an obligation ('azimah), not a concession (rukhsah). Abu al-Hasan al-Tabari, known as al-Kiya al-Harrasi, companion of al-Ghazali in al-Ishtighal, said: this is the correct view according to us, like breaking the fast for the sick in Ramadan and similar cases.] [[added from J.]]

Among them is the hadith of 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about hanging fruit, and he said: "Whoever takes from it out of need, with his mouth, without carrying it in his garment, there is nothing upon him." [[Related by al-Tirmidhi in the Sunan no. (1289), who said: "This is a hasan hadith."]] The hadith continues.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said regarding His saying ﴿then there is no sin upon him, indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: concerning what he ate out of necessity; and it reached us, and Allah knows best, that he should not exceed three morsels.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Forgiving for what he ate of the unlawful; Merciful in that He made the unlawful lawful for him in necessity.

Waki' said: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, who said: whoever is compelled and does not eat or drink, then dies, enters the Fire.

[This implies that eating carrion for one in necessity is an obligation ('azimah), not a concession (rukhsah). Abu al-Hasan al-Tabari, known as al-Kiya al-Harrasi, companion of al-Ghazali in al-Ishtighal, said: this is the correct view according to us, like breaking the fast for the sick in Ramadan and similar cases.] [[added from J.]]

Ibn Kathir said: Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, those who conceal﴾ [what testifies to His messengership] [[addition from ج]] ﴿what Allah has sent down of the Book﴾. He means the Jews who concealed the description of Muhammad ﷺ in their books that were in their hands, which testify to his messengership and prophethood. They concealed this so that their leadership would not be lost, and so that the gifts and presents they took from the Arabs in honour of them would not stop. [[In A: "like the covenant".]] They feared, may Allah curse them, that if they made this known, the people would follow him and abandon them. So they concealed it in order to preserve what they received from this, which was a trifling amount. Thus they sold themselves for it and exchanged guidance, following the truth, believing the Messenger, and faith in what came from Allah, for that trifling price. So they lost and were ruined in this world and the Hereafter. As for this world, Allah made His Messenger's truthfulness manifest to His servants through the clear signs and decisive proofs He set up and placed with him. Those who had feared following him believed him, became helpers to him against their own people, and "they returned with anger upon anger." Allah condemned them in His Book in more than one place. Among that is this noble verse: ﴿Indeed, those who conceal what Allah has sent down of the Book and exchange it for a small price﴾, which is the goods of this worldly life, ﴿those eat nothing into their bellies except the Fire﴾. That is, what they eat is only fire in exchange for concealing the truth, a blazing fire in their bellies on the Day of Resurrection. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly only consume fire into their bellies, and they will [soon] burn in a Blaze﴾ [al-Nisa': 10]. In the authentic hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: "Whoever eats or drinks from vessels of gold and silver, it is only the Fire of Hell that he gulps down into his belly." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5634) and Sahih Muslim no. (2065), from the hadith of Umm Salamah رضي الله عنها.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and for them is a painful punishment﴾. This is because He is angry with them, since they concealed the truth while knowing it, and so they deserved His anger. Therefore He will not look upon them or purify them, meaning He will not praise them or commend them, but will punish them with a painful punishment.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh mention here the hadith that Muslim also narrated, from the hadith of al-A'mash, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Three whom Allah will not speak to, nor will He look at them, nor will He purify them [and for them is a painful punishment] [[addition from ج and Sahih Muslim]]: an elderly adulterer, a lying king, and an arrogant poor man." [[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih no. (107).]]

Then Allah the Exalted said, informing about them: ﴿Those are the ones who have bought error in exchange for guidance and punishment in exchange for forgiveness﴾. That is, they exchanged guidance, which is the proclaiming of what is in their books about the description of the Messenger, the mention of his mission, the good tidings of him from the books of the prophets, and following and affirming him. In place of that they took and exchanged for it error, which is denying him, disbelieving in him, and concealing his attributes in their books. ﴿And punishment in exchange for forgiveness﴾: that is, they exchanged forgiveness for punishment, which is what they engaged in through its causes mentioned above.

* *

As for His saying the Exalted: ﴿So how patient they are for the Fire!﴾ He informs that they are in a severe, great, terrifying punishment, so whoever sees them in it marvels at their endurance of it, given the intensity of the punishment, torment and shackles they are in. We seek refuge with Allah from that.

[It has also been said that the meaning of His saying ﴿So how patient they are for the Fire!﴾ is: how constant they are in doing the sins that lead them to the Fire.] [[addition from A.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿That is because Allah has sent down the Book in truth﴾: that is, they only deserve this severe punishment because Allah the Exalted sent down to His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ and to the prophets before him His books, establishing the truth and nullifying falsehood. These people took the signs of Allah in mockery. Their own book commands them to make knowledge manifest and spread it, but they opposed it and denied it. This final Messenger calls them to Allah the Exalted, commands them to do what is good and forbids them from what is evil, yet they deny him, oppose him, reject him, and conceal his description. So they mocked the signs of Allah sent down to His messengers. For this they deserve punishment and torment. Therefore He said: ﴿That is because Allah has sent down the Book in truth. And indeed, those who differ over the Book are in extreme dissension﴾.
