This final Messenger calls them to Allah the Exalted, commands them to do what is good and forbids them from what is evil, yet they deny him, oppose him, reject him, and conceal his description. So they mocked the signs of Allah sent down to His messengers. For this they deserve punishment and torment. Therefore He said: ﴿That is because Allah has sent down the Book in truth. And indeed, those who differ over the Book are in extreme dissension﴾.

This verse contains great principles, broad foundations, and a sound creed. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, ʿUbayd (in one manuscript: "ʿUbaydah") ibn Hisham al-Halabi narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, from ʿAmir ibn Shufay, from ʿAbd al-Karim, from Mujahid, from Abu Dharr: that he asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "What is faith (iman)?" He recited to him: ﴿It is not righteousness that you turn your faces [toward the east or the west]...﴾ to the end of the verse. He said: Then he asked him again, and he recited it to him again. Then he asked him (a third time). He said: "When you do a good deed, your heart loves it, and when you do a bad deed, your heart hates it."[[In manuscript ج: "recited to him", "then he asked him", "so his heart loved it", "so his heart hated it." Muhammad ibn Nasr narrated it in Taʿzim Qadr al-Salah, no. 409, through ʿAbd al-Razzaq, from Maʿmar, from ʿAbd al-Karim, from Mujahid, with the same wording.]]

This chain is disconnected (munqatiʿ, a break in the isnad), because Mujahid did not meet Abu Dharr, as Abu Dharr died early.

Al-Masʿudi said: al-Qasim ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: A man came to Abu Dharr and said: "What is faith?" He recited to him this verse until he finished it. The man said: "I did not ask you about righteousness." Abu Dharr said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and asked him what you asked me, so he recited this verse to him. He refused to be satisfied, just as you refused to be satisfied. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him, gesturing with his hand: "When the believer does a good deed, it pleases him and he hopes for its reward, and when he does a bad deed, it grieves him and he fears its punishment."[[Muhammad ibn Nasr narrated it in Taʿzim Qadr al-Salah, no. 408, through ʿAbd Allah ibn Yazid and al-Mala'i, both from al-Masʿudi, similar in meaning. al-Hakim (2/272) narrated it through Musa ibn Aʿyan, from ʿAbd al-Karim, similar in meaning, and said: "This is a sahih hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not narrate it." al-Dhahabi objected: "I say: it is disconnected (munqatiʿ)."]]

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it, and this too is disconnected, and Allah knows best.

As for explaining this verse: when Allah, Exalted is He, first commanded the believers to face Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), then turned them toward the Kaʿbah, this was difficult for some of the People of the Book and some Muslims. So Allah, Exalted is He, revealed the wisdom behind this, which is that the purpose is only obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and compliance with His commands. Facing wherever He directs, and following what He legislates, is what righteousness, piety, and complete faith are. There is no righteousness or obedience in being bound to face a particular direction, from east to west, if it is not by the command and legislation of Allah. For this reason He said: ﴿It is not righteousness that you turn your faces toward the east or the west, but righteousness is [in] one who believes in Allah and the Last Day...﴾ to the end of the verse. Similarly, He said regarding sacrificial animals and offerings: ﴿Their meat does not reach Allah, nor their blood, but piety from you reaches Him﴾ [al-Hajj: 37].

al-ʿAwfi narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding this verse: "It is not righteousness that you pray and do not act." This was when he moved from Mecca to Medina, and the obligations and limits were revealed, so Allah commanded the obligations and acting upon them.

Similar was narrated from al-Dahhak and Muqatil.

Abu al-ʿAliyah said: The Jews used to face toward the west, and the Christians used to face toward the east, so Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿It is not righteousness that you turn your faces toward the east or the west﴾, meaning: this is a statement of faith, and its reality is action. Similar was narrated from al-Hasan and al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas.

Mujahid said: "But righteousness is what is firmly established in the hearts of obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

al-Dahhak said: "But righteousness and piety is that you perform the obligations in their proper manner."

al-Thawri said regarding ﴿But righteousness is [in] one who believes in Allah...﴾ to the end of the verse: "These are all the types of righteousness." May Allah have mercy on him, he spoke the truth. Whoever embodies this verse has entered all the bonds of Islam, and grasped all the essentials of good. It is faith in Allah, which is that there is no deity except Him; and belief in the existence of the angels, who are the emissaries between Allah and His messengers; ﴿and the Book﴾, which is a collective noun encompassing the books sent down from heaven upon the prophets, until they were concluded with the most noble of them, which is the Qur'an, the one that guards over (muhaymin) the books before it, to which every good has led, and which encompasses every happiness in this world and the Hereafter, and by which Allah abrogated (naskh) every other book before it. And he believes in all of Allah's prophets, from the first of them to the last of them, Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him and upon them all.

* *

His saying: ﴿and gives wealth, in spite of love for it﴾ means: he gives it out, while he loves it and desires it. Ibn Masʿud, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, and others from the early and later generations stated this, as is established in the two Sahihs (of al-Bukhari and Muslim) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "The best charity is that you give while you are healthy and miserly, hoping for wealth and fearing poverty."

al-Hakim narrated in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of Shuʿbah and al-Thawri, from Mansur, from Zubayd, from Murrah, from Ibn Masʿud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ﴿and gives wealth in spite of love for it﴾ means that you give it while you are healthy and miserly, hoping for wealth [and] fearing poverty. Then he said: It is sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not narrate it.[[al-Mustadrak (2/272).]]

I say: Waki' narrated it from al-Aʿmash, and Sufyan from Zubayd, from Murrah, from Ibn Masʿud, as a statement of Ibn Masʿud (mawquf), and this is more authentic, and Allah knows best.

Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And they give food, in spite of love for it, to the needy, the orphan, and the captive. [We feed you only for the countenance of Allah; we do not want from you reward or thanks.]﴾ [al-Insan: 8, 9].

And He said: ﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love﴾ [Al 'Imran: 92]. His saying: ﴿and prefer [others] over themselves, though they are in need﴾ [al-Hashr: 9] is another type higher than this, which is that they gave away what they themselves needed, while these [in the previous verses] gave and fed what they themselves loved.

* *

His saying: ﴿the near of kin﴾ refers to a person's relatives, and they are the most deserving of charity, as is established in the hadith: "Charity to the poor is one charity, but to relatives there are two: charity and maintaining ties (silah)." So they are the people most deserving of your righteousness and your giving. Allah, Exalted is He, commanded kindness to them in more than one place in His Mighty Book.

﴿the orphans﴾ are those who have no earner, whose fathers have died, and who are weak, young, below puberty, and unable to earn a living. ʿAbd al-Razzaq said: Maʿmar informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, from al-Nazzal ibn Sabrah, from ʿAli, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "There is no orphanhood after reaching puberty."

﴿the needy﴾ are those who do not find what suffices them for their food, clothing, and housing, so they are given what fills their need and their lack. In the two Sahihs, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The needy person is not the one who goes around and is turned away by a date or two dates, or a morsel or two morsels, but the needy person is the one who does not find sufficient wealth to suffice him, and is not noticed so that charity is given to him."[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. 1479 and Sahih Muslim no. 1039.]]

﴿the traveler﴾ is the passing traveler whose provisions have run out, so he is given what brings him to his homeland. Likewise, one who intends a journey for an act of obedience is given what suffices him for his going and returning. This includes the guest. As ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, that he said: "Ibn al-Sabil is the guest who stays with the Muslims." Likewise said Mujahid, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Abu Jaʿfar al-Baqir, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Zuhri, al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan.

﴿the beggars﴾ are those who present themselves to ask, so they are given from the zakat and the charities. As Imam Ahmad said: Waki' and ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Musʿab ibn Muhammad, from Yaʿla ibn Abi Yahya, from Fatimah bint al-Husayn, from her father (ʿAbd al-Rahman said: Husayn ibn ʿAli), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The beggar has a right, even if he comes on a horse." Narrated by Abu Dawud.[[In manuscript ج: "Fatimah bint Husayn, from her father." In manuscript أ: "Fatimah bint Husayn ibn ʿAli, from Husayn ibn ʿAli."]]

﴿and for the captives [freeing slaves]﴾ are the mukatabun, those who are bound by a contract of manumission and cannot find what they owe for their freedom.

The discussion of many of these categories will come, if Allah wills, in the verse on charities in Surat al-Bara'ah (al-Tawbah). Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Yahya ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah, from al-Shaʿbi, who said: Fatimah bint Qays narrated to me that she asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Is there a right in wealth other than zakat?" She said: Then he recited to me ﴿and gives wealth in spite of love for it﴾.[[It is in Sahih al-Bukhari no. 33 and Sahih Muslim no. 59, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through Adam ibn Abi Iyas and Yahya ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid, both from Sharik, from Abu Hamzah, from al-Shaʿbi, from Fatimah bint Qays, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is a right in wealth other than zakat." Then he recited ﴿It is not righteousness that you turn your faces toward the east or the west...﴾ to His saying: ﴿and for the captives﴾.

[Abu Dawud? no: Ibn Majah and al-Tirmidhi narrated it.[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 659 and Sunan Ibn Majah no. 1789. al-Tirmidhi said: "This hadith does not have a strong isnad, and Abu Hamzah (Maymun al-Aʿwar) is weak in hadith, and Bayan and Ismaʿil ibn Salim narrated it from al-Shaʿbi as his own statement, and this is more authentic."]]]

* *

His saying: ﴿and established prayer and gave zakat﴾ means: and completed the acts of prayer at their appointed times, with its bowing, prostration, tranquility, and humility, in the lawful and accepted manner.

* *

His saying: ﴿and gave zakat﴾ may refer to the purification of the soul and cleansing it of base and vile character traits, as in His saying: ﴿He has succeeded who purifies it, and he has failed who corrupts it﴾ [al-Shams: 9, 10], and Musa's saying to Pharaoh: ﴿Would you like to purify yourself, and I would guide you to your Lord so you would fear Him?﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 18, 19], and His saying: ﴿And woe to the polytheists, who do not give zakat﴾ [Fussilat: 6, 7].

It may also refer to zakat on wealth, as said by Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Muqatil ibn Hayyan. In that case, the mention of giving to these categories and groups refers only to voluntary charity, righteousness, and kindness. For this reason it preceded in the hadith from Fatimah bint Qays that there is a right in wealth other than zakat. And Allah knows best.

* *

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 177 (part 2 of 2):

His saying: ﴿And those who fulfil their covenant when they make it﴾ is like His saying: ﴿Those who fulfil the covenant of Allah and do not break the pledge﴾ [al-Ra'd: 20]. The opposite of this attribute is hypocrisy (nifaq), as is authentically established in the hadith: "The sign of the hypocrite is three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays." And in another hadith: "When he speaks he lies, when he makes a covenant he betrays, and when he disputes he behaves wickedly" [Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (58), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, may Allah be pleased with him].
* *
His saying: ﴿And the patient in misfortune and adversity and in time of battle﴾ means: in the state of poverty, which is al-ba'sa' (misfortune), and in the state of illness and sickness, which is al-darra' (adversity). ﴿And in time of battle⦆ means: in the state of fighting and the meeting of enemies. This was said by Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah, Murrah al-Hamdani, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Suddi, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Abu Malik, al-Dahhak, and others.

The word ﴿al-sabirin﴾ (the patient) is in the accusative case (nasb) as a form of praise and as an encouragement to patience in these circumstances, because of their severity and difficulty. And Allah knows best; He is the One sought for help, and upon Him is reliance.
* *
His saying: ﴿Those are the ones who are true﴾ means: those who are characterized by these attributes are the ones who were truthful in their faith, because they actualized inner faith through their words and deeds. These are the ones who are true. ﴿And those are the mindful (al-muttaqun)﴾ because they guarded against the forbidden things and performed the acts of obedience.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Prescribed for you﴾ is justice in retaliation (qisas) regarding the slain, O believers: the free for the free, and your slave for your slave, and your female for your female. Do not overstep or transgress, as those before you transgressed and altered the ruling of Allah concerning them. The cause of this was the tribes of Quraydhah and [Banu] al-Nadir. Banu al-Nadir had raided Quraydhah in the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance) and subjugated them. So if a man of al-Nadir killed a man of Quraydhah, he would not be killed in retaliation for him, but would be ransomed for one hundred wasq of dates. And if a man of Quraydhah killed a man of al-Nadir, he would be killed in retaliation for him. If they paid ransom, he would pay two hundred wasq of dates, double the blood money of the Quraydhi. So Allah commanded justice in retaliation, and not to follow the path of the corrupters, the distorters, those who opposed the rulings of Allah concerning them, out of disbelief and transgression [in another manuscript: "out of play and amusement"]. Then Allah said: ﴿Retaliation is prescribed for you regarding the slain: the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female﴾.

It is related regarding the occasion of its revelation what Imam Abu Muhammad ibn Abi Hatim narrated: Abu Zur'a related to us, Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn Bukayr related to us, Abdullah ibn Lahi'a related to me, Ata' ibn Dinar related to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿O you who believe, retaliation is prescribed for you regarding the slain﴾, meaning: if it is intentional, the free for the free. This was because two Arab clans fought one another in the Jahiliyyah, shortly before Islam, and there was killing and wounding between them, until they killed the slaves and the women. Neither side would take retribution from the other until they embraced Islam. Then one of the two clans would boast over the other in numbers and wealth, and they swore that they would not be satisfied until a free man of theirs was killed for a slave of ours, and a man of theirs for a woman of ours. So this was revealed concerning them.

﴿The free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female﴾: it has been abrogated (mansukha) by ﴿a life for a life﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 45].

Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn Abbas concerning His words ﴿and the female for the female﴾: this is because they would not kill a man for a woman, but would kill a man for a man and a woman for a woman. So Allah revealed: ﴿a life for a life, and an eye for an eye﴾. He made free persons equal in retaliation among themselves for intentional killing, men and women alike, in the case of life and in lesser injuries, and He made slaves equal among themselves in intentional killing, in the case of life and in lesser injuries, men and women alike. Similarly it is narrated from Abu Malik that it was abrogated by His words: ﴿a life for a life﴾.

Issue: The position of Abu Hanifah is that a free man is killed for a slave, based on the general wording of the verse of al-Ma'idah. This was also the view of al-Thawri, Ibn Abi Layla and Dawud, and it is narrated from Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Qatadah and al-Hakam. Al-Bukhari, Ali ibn al-Madini, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and al-Thawri in one narration from him said: a master is killed for his slave, based on the general wording of the hadith of al-Hasan from Samurah: "Whoever kills his slave, we kill him; whoever castrates his slave, we castrate him; and whoever mutilates his slave, we mutilate him." [Related by Abu Dawud in al-Sunan, nos. (4515, 4516), and al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan, no. (1414), and al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith."] The majority (al-jumhur) disagreed with them and said: a free man is not killed for a slave, because the slave is property (silcah); if he were killed by mistake, no blood money (diyah) would be owed for him, only his value, and a limb of his cannot be retaliated for with a free man's limb, so a fortiori the soul cannot be. The majority also held that a Muslim is not killed for a disbeliever, as established in al-Bukhari from Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A Muslim is not killed for a disbeliever." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (111).] No hadith or interpretation that opposes this is authentic. As for Abu Hanifah, he held that a Muslim is killed for a disbeliever, based on the general wording of the verse of al-Ma'idah.

Issue: al-Hasan and Ata' said: a man is not killed for a woman, based on this verse. The majority disagreed with them on the basis of the verse of al-Ma'idah, and on the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "The Muslims' blood is equal in value." [Related by Ibn Majah in al-Sunan, no. (2683), from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him.] Al-Layth said: if a man kills his wife, he is not killed for her specifically.

Issue: The position of the four Imams and the majority is that a group is killed for one person. Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said regarding a boy whom seven people killed, that he killed them all, and said: "If the people of San'a' had conspired together against him, I would have killed them." No opponent among the Companions is known from his time, and this is like a consensus (ijma'). It is reported from Imam Ahmad a narration that a group is not killed for one person, and a soul is only taken for one soul. Ibn al-Mundhir related this from Mu'adh, Ibn al-Zubayr, Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, al-Zuhri, Muhammad ibn Sirin and Habib ibn Abi Thabit. Then Ibn al-Mundhir said: "This is more correct, and there is no proof for the one who permits killing a group for one person." What we have mentioned is established from Ibn al-Zubayr, and when the Companions differ, the way is to reason (al-nazar).

* *

His words: ﴿But whoever is pardoned by his brother in anything, then pursuit should be made in good manner, and payment made to him with good conduct﴾. Mujahid related from Ibn Abbas: ﴿whoever is pardoned by his brother in anything﴾: the pardon (al-'afw) means accepting blood money (diyah) for intentional killing. This was also narrated from Abu al-Aliyah, Abu al-Sha'tha', Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ata', al-Hasan, Qatadah and Muqatil ibn Hayyan.

Al-Dahhak related from Ibn Abbas: ﴿whoever is pardoned by his brother in anything﴾ means: whoever is left something by his brother, i.e., after taking the blood money once the right to life has become due; and that is the pardon. ﴿Then pursuit should be made in good manner﴾ means: the claimant should pursue it in a good manner when he accepts the blood money. ﴿And payment made to him with good conduct﴾ means: from the killer, without harm or delay (ma'k), i.e., without resistance.

Al-Hakim related from the hadith of Sufyan, from Amr, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas: "and the one who is owed should be paid with good conduct." Likewise said Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu al-Sha'tha' Jabir ibn Zayd, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ata' al-Khurasani, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Suddi and Muqatil ibn Hayyan.

Issue: Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, in the narration of Ibn al-Qasim from him, which is the well-known one, and Abu Hanifah and his companions, and al-Shafi'i in one of his two opinions, said: the guardian of the blood has no right to pardon in exchange for blood money unless the killer consents. The others said: he may pardon in exchange for it even if the killer does not consent. A group of the early generations (salaf) held that women have no right to pardon, among them al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Zuhri, Ibn Shubrumah, al-Layth and al-Awza'i, but the others disagreed with them.

* *

As Sa'id ibn Mansur said:

Sufyan related to us, from Amr ibn Dinar; Mujahid informed me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Retaliation for the slain was prescribed for the Children of Israel, and there was no pardon among them. So Allah said to this nation: ﴿Retaliation is prescribed for you regarding the slain: the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female. But whoever is pardoned by his brother in anything, then pursuit should be made in good manner, and payment made to him with good conduct﴾. The pardon is accepting blood money for intentional killing. Qatadah said: ﴿That is an alleviation from your Lord﴾: May Allah have mercy on this nation and make blood money food for them, which was not lawful for anyone before them. The People of the Torah had only retaliation or pardon with no compensation (arsh) between them. The People of the Gospel had only pardon, which they were commanded to observe, while for this nation Allah made retaliation, pardon and compensation.

Similar to this was narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Muqatil ibn Hayyan and al-Rabi' ibn Anas.

* *

Similar was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ata', Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Suddi and Muqatil ibn Hayyan: that it refers to the one who is killed after taking the blood money. If he desires a fourth, then restrain him. Whoever transgresses after that, for him is the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever." Related by Ahmad [al-Musnad (4/31)].

I mean: I do not accept blood money from him, but kill him." [Al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur (1/421) and attributed it to Sumawayh in his Fawa'id. Al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (8/54) related from the route of Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah, from Mutar, from al-Hasan, as a mursal narration with similar wording. Abu Dawud in al-Sunan, no. (4507), related from the route of Hammad, from Mutar, from al-Hasan, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him, as a marfu' narration with similar wording.]

This noble verse includes the command to make a bequest (wasiyyah) to parents and close relatives. According to the more correct of the two opinions, this was obligatory before the verse of inheritance (ayat al-mawarith) was revealed. When the verses of the prescribed shares (ayat al-fara'id) were revealed, they abrogated (nasakhat) this ruling, and the prescribed inheritances became an obligation from Allah, which their rightful heirs take as a binding right without any bequest and without it being a favour from the testator. For this reason, the hadith in the Sunan and elsewhere is reported from 'Amr ibn Kharijah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ delivering a sermon, saying: "Indeed Allah has given every rightful person his right, so there is no bequest for an heir" [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2121; Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/247); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2712].

It was also narrated by another route as marfu' (traced to the Prophet), but its raising is weak."]]

Regarding its being raised (to the Prophet), there is also a point of scrutiny here.[[In manuscript C: "Regarding its being raised as well, there is scrutiny."]] The best that has been reported on this subject is what 'Abd al-Razzaq said:

Ma'mar narrated to us, from Ash'ath ibn 'Abd Allah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed a man may work the deeds of the people of goodness for seventy years, then when he makes a bequest he deviates in his bequest, so his life is closed with the worst of his deeds, and he enters the Fire. And indeed a man may work the deeds of the people of evil for seventy years, then he is just in his bequest, so his life is closed with the best of his deeds, and he enters Paradise."[[In manuscript C: "The two phrases are transposed (presented in reverse order)."]] Abu Hurayra said: Recite, if you wish: ﴿These are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 229].

This noble verse includes the command to make a bequest (wasiyyah) to parents and close relatives. According to the more correct of the two opinions, this was obligatory before the verse of inheritance (ayat al-mawarith) was revealed. When the verses of the prescribed shares (ayat al-fara'id) were revealed, they abrogated (nasakhat) this ruling, and the prescribed inheritances became an obligation from Allah, which their rightful heirs take as a binding right without any bequest and without it being a favour from the testator. For this reason, the hadith in the Sunan and elsewhere is reported from 'Amr ibn Kharijah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ delivering a sermon, saying: "Indeed Allah has given every rightful person his right, so there is no bequest for an heir" [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2121; Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/247); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2712].

Imam Ahmad said: Ismail ibn Ibrahim ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: Ibn 'Abbas sat and recited Surat al-Baqarah until he reached this verse: ﴿If he leaves wealth, the bequest is for the parents and the relatives﴾, and he said: "This verse has been abrogated."

Similarly, Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated it from Hushaym, from Yunus, with the same chain. Al-Hakim also narrated it in his Mustadrak and said: "Sahih according to the conditions of both of them" [Sunan Sa'id ibn Mansur, no. 252, edited by al-Duktur al-Humaid; al-Mustadrak (2/273)].

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿The bequest for the parents and the relatives﴾: "No one inherited alongside the two parents except those [relatives] for whom there was a bequest. Then Allah revealed the verse of inheritance (ayat al-mirath), explaining the inheritance of the parents, and confirmed the bequest to the relatives within one-third of the deceased's property."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Ibn Juraij informed us, and 'Uthman ibn 'Ata' [narrated], from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿The bequest for the parents and the relatives﴾: "This verse abrogated it: ﴿For men there is a share of what the parents and relatives leave, and for women there is a share of what the parents and relatives leave, whether it is little or much, a share ordained﴾ [al-Nisa': 7]."

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: It is also narrated from Ibn 'Umar, Abu Musa, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Hasan, Mujahid, 'Ata', Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Muhammad ibn Sirin, 'Ikrimah, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Tawus, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Shurayh, al-Dahhak, and al-Zuhri that this verse is abrogated, abrogated by the verse of inheritance.

It is strange that Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Umar al-Razi, may Allah have mercy on him, in his great tafsir (al-Tafsir al-Kabir), reported from Abu Muslim al-Isfahani that this verse is not abrogated, but rather it is explained by the verse of inheritance, and its meaning is: "It has been prescribed for you what Allah has commanded concerning the inheritance of the parents and relatives," from His saying: ﴿Allah enjoins you concerning your children﴾ [al-Nisa': 11]. He said: "This is the view of most of the exegetes and of the scholars among the jurists." He said: "Some of them said: it is abrogated concerning those who inherit, and established concerning those who do not inherit. This is the position of Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, Masruq, Tawus, al-Dahhak, Muslim ibn Yasar, and al-'Ala' ibn Ziyad."

I say: Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Qatadah, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan also held this view. However, according to the view of these scholars, this is not called abrogation (naskh) in our later terminology, because the verse of inheritance only removed the ruling for some of the individuals covered by the general wording of the verse of bequest, since "the relatives" (al-aqrabin) is more general, including both those who inherit and those who do not. So the ruling for those who inherit was lifted by what was specified for them, and the other category remained under what the first verse indicated. This applies only according to the view of some of them that the bequest at the beginning of Islam was merely recommended (nadb) until it was abrogated. As for the one who says that it was obligatory, which is the apparent meaning of the context of the verse, then it must be that it was abrogated by the verse of inheritance, as most of the exegetes and the scholars among the jurists have said. The obligation of a bequest to parents and relatives who are heirs (al-warithin) is abrogated by consensus (ijma'). Indeed, it is even forbidden, due to the earlier hadith: "Indeed Allah has given every rightful person his right, so there is no bequest for an heir." Thus the verse of inheritance is an independent ruling and an obligation from Allah for those entitled to fixed shares (ahl al-furud) and for the agnatic heirs (al-'asabat), and by it the ruling of this verse was completely lifted. The relatives who have no inheritance remain, and it is recommended for the testator to make a bequest to them from one-third, drawing on the verse of bequest and its comprehensiveness, and because of what is established in the two Sahihs from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "It is not right for a Muslim who has something to bequeath to spend two nights without his bequest being written and kept with him." Ibn 'Umar said: "No night has passed over me since I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say that without my bequest being with me" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2738; Sahih Muslim, no. 1627].

The verses and hadiths commanding kindness to relatives and good treatment of them are very numerous.

'Abd ibn Humayd said in his Musnad: 'Ubayd Allah informed us, from Mubarak ibn Hassan, from Nafi', who said: 'Abd Allah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah the Exalted says: O son of Adam, there are two things of which you have none: I have given you a share of your wealth when I seized your throat, to purify you and cleanse you by it; and the prayers of My servants upon you after the end of your term."

* *

His saying: ﴿If he leaves wealth﴾ means: property. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ata', Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu al-'Aliyah, 'Ata' al-'Awfi, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Qatadah, and others.

Then among them, some said: the bequest is prescribed whether the property is small or large, just like inheritance. Others said: one makes a bequest only if he leaves a substantial amount of property. Then they differed over its amount. Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri' narrated to us, Sufyan informed us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, who said: It was said to 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: "A man from Quraysh has died, leaving three hundred dinars or four hundred, and he made no bequest." He said: "It is nothing; Allah only said: ﴿If he leaves wealth﴾."

He said: Harun ibn Ishaq al-Hamdani narrated to us, 'Abdah, that is, Ibn Sulayman, narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father: that 'Ali entered upon a man from his people to visit him, and the man said to him: "Shall I make a bequest?" 'Ali said to him: "Allah the Exalted only said: ﴿If he leaves wealth, the bequest﴾. You have only left a little, so leave it for your child."

al-Hakam ibn Aban said: He narrated to me from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿If he leaves wealth﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Whoever does not leave sixty dinars has not left wealth." Al-Hakam said: Tawus said: "Whoever does not leave eighty dinars has not left wealth." Qatadah said: "It used to be said: a thousand or more."

* *

His saying: ﴿According to what is fair﴾ means: with kindness and goodness, as Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Ahmad narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yasar narrated to us, Surur ibn al-Mughirah narrated to me, from 'Abbad ibn Mansur, from al-Hasan, concerning his saying: ﴿It is prescribed for you when death approaches one of you﴾, he said: "Yes, the bequest is a right; every Muslim must make a bequest when death approaches him, according to what is fair, not what is reprehensible."

What is meant by "what is fair" is that he bequeaths to his relatives a bequest that does not harm his heirs, neither extravagant nor stingy. As established in the two Sahihs, Sa'd said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have wealth and no one inherits from me except a daughter of mine. Shall I bequeath two-thirds of my wealth?" He said: "No." He said: "Then half?" He said: "No." He said: "Then one-third?" He said: "One-third, and one-third is much. Indeed, that you leave your heirs wealthy is better than that you leave them in need, begging from people" [Sahih al-Bukhari; Sahih Muslim].

In Sahih al-Bukhari: Ibn 'Abbas said: "If only people would reduce the bequest from one-third to one-quarter, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'One-third, and one-third is much.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2743].

Imam Ahmad narrated from Abu Sa'id, client of Bani Hashim, from Dhayyal ibn 'Ubayd ibn Handhalah, who said: I heard Handhalah ibn Hidhim ibn Hanifah: that his grandfather Hanifah made a bequest to an orphan under his guardianship of one hundred camels. This was hard on his sons, so they brought the matter to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Hanifah said: "I bequeathed to an orphan of mine one hundred camels; we used to call them al-Mutayyabah." The Prophet ﷺ said: "No, no, no. Charity is five; otherwise ten; otherwise fifteen; otherwise twenty; otherwise twenty-five; otherwise thirty; otherwise thirty-five; and if you exceed that, then forty."

He mentioned the hadith in full [al-Musnad (5/67)].

* *

His saying: ﴿Then whoever alters it after he has heard it, indeed its sin is upon those who alter it﴾. He, the Exalted, says: whoever alters the bequest and distorts it, changing its ruling, adding to it or subtracting from it, and concealing it is included in this by greater reason, then ﴿indeed its sin is upon those who alter it﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and others said: The reward of the deceased has fallen upon Allah, and the sin has attached to those who altered it. ﴿Indeed Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾, meaning: He has knowledge of what the deceased bequeathed, and He knows what the appointed executors altered.

* *

His saying: ﴿Then whoever fears from a testator injustice (janafan) or sin﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and al-Suddi said: "Janaf" means error. This includes all kinds of error, such as when he gives an heir a benefit through an intermediary or a means, like when he bequeaths the sale of a particular item at a discount, or bequeaths to his daughter's son in order to increase her share, or similar means. This may be done unintentionally, out of his natural inclination and the strength of his affection without careful consideration, or deliberately and sinfully. In that case, the executor may, in such a situation, correct the matter and act justly with the bequest according to the legal manner, turning away from what the deceased bequeathed toward what is closest to it and most like what was commanded, combining the testator's intention with the legal path. This correction and reconciliation is not alteration at all. Therefore He linked this, explaining it, to the prohibition of that, so it would be known that this is not of that kind at all. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-'Abbas ibn al-Walid ibn Yazid narrated to us by reading, my father informed me, from al-Awza'i, who said: al-Zuhri said: 'Urwah narrated to me, from 'A'ishah, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "What is returned of a sick person's charity during his life is what is returned of the bequest of one who oppresses at his death" [Abu Dawud in al-Marasil, no. 194, by way of al-'Abbas ibn al-Walid ibn Yazid, from his father, from al-Awza'i, with it. Al-'Abbas said: "I narrated it once from 'Urwah, and once from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, from the Prophet ﷺ." Then Abu Dawud narrated it (no. 195) from 'Urwah as a mursal, and (no. 196) from al-Zuhri as a mursal].

Likewise Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of al-'Abbas ibn al-Walid, with it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Walid ibn Mazyad has erred in this. This statement is only from 'Urwa alone. Al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated it from al-Awza'i, and did not extend its chain beyond 'Urwa.

Ibn Mardawayh also said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, 'Umar ibn al-Mughira narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Deviating in a bequest is among the major sins."[[Al-Daraqutni in al-Sunan (4/151), al-'Uqayli in al-Du'afa' (3/189) and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (6/271) narrated it through 'Umar ibn al-Mughira with similar wording. Al-Bayhaqi (6/271) also narrated it through Hushaym from Dawud as a mawquf (ending with a companion) report, and said: "This is the correct version, a mawquf report; likewise Ibn 'Uyayna and others narrated it from Dawud as mawquf. It was also narrated by another route as marfu' (traced to the Prophet), but its raising is weak."]]

Regarding its being raised (to the Prophet), there is also a point of scrutiny here.[[In manuscript C: "Regarding its being raised as well, there is scrutiny."]] The best that has been reported on this subject is what 'Abd al-Razzaq said:

Ma'mar narrated to us, from Ash'ath ibn 'Abd Allah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed a man may work the deeds of the people of goodness for seventy years, then when he makes a bequest he deviates in his bequest, so his life is closed with the worst of his deeds, and he enters the Fire. And indeed a man may work the deeds of the people of evil for seventy years, then he is just in his bequest, so his life is closed with the best of his deeds, and he enters Paradise."[[In manuscript C: "The two phrases are transposed (presented in reverse order)."]] Abu Hurayra said: Recite, if you wish: ﴿These are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 229].

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 183–184 (part 1 of 2):

Allah, the Exalted, addresses the believers of this Ummah and commands them to fast (al-siyam), which is abstaining from food, drink, and marital relations, with a sincere intention for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic [[In C: "sincerely for the Face of Allah, the Exalted."]], because of what it contains of purifying the soul, cleansing it, and purging it of corrupt humours and base character traits. He mentions that just as He made it obligatory upon them, He made it obligatory upon those before them, so they have in it a precedent, and these should strive to perform this obligation more perfectly than those did, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿For each of you We have made a law and a way. And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one community, but [He intended] to test you in what He has given you. So race to [all] good deeds.﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 48]. For this reason He said here: ﴿O you who have believed, fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you, that you may become righteous.﴾ Because fasting contains purification of the body and constriction of the pathways of Satan. For this reason it is established in the Two Sahihs: "O assembly of youth, whoever among you is able to marry, let him marry, and whoever is not able, let him fast, for it is a shield for him" [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5066) and Sahih Muslim no. (1400), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. Then He explained the quantity of fasting, and that it is not every day, lest it burden souls so that they become too weak to bear it and perform it, but rather on specific numbered days. This was at the beginning of Islam: they would fast three days of every month, then this was abrogated by the fasting of the month of Ramadan, as its explanation will come. It has been narrated that fasting was initially as it was for the nations before us, three days of every month, from Mu'adh, Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ata', Qatadah, and al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim. He added: "This remained prescribed from the time of Nuh until Allah abrogated it with the fasting of the month of Ramadan."

'Abbad ibn Mansur related from al-Hasan al-Basri regarding ﴿O you who have believed, fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you, that you may become righteous. [For] a limited number of days﴾ that he said: "Yes, by Allah, fasting was prescribed for every nation that passed before us, just as it was prescribed for us, a full month and numbered days, a known count." It is also narrated from al-Suddi something similar.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri', from Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Walid, from Abu al-Rabi', a man from the people of Madinah, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The fasting of Ramadan, Allah prescribed it upon the nations before you..." in a lengthy hadith from which this was abridged [[Ibn Hajar cited it in al-Fath (8/178) from Ibn Abi Hatim and said: "Its chain contains an unknown narrator."]].

Abu Ja'far al-Razi related from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from one who narrated to him from Ibn 'Umar, who said: It was revealed: ﴿Fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you [that you may become righteous]﴾ — it was prescribed for them that when one of them prayed the 'atamah (night prayer) and slept, Allah made food, drink, and women forbidden to him until the same time [the next night].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Something similar has been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and 'Ata' al-Khurasani.

'Ata' al-Khurasani related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿as it was prescribed for those before you﴾ that by this is meant the People of the Book. It is also narrated from al-Sha'bi and al-Suddi and 'Ata' al-Khurasani something similar.

Then He explained the ruling on fasting as it stood at the beginning of Islam, saying: ﴿So whoever among you is ill or on a journey [should fast] an equal number of other days﴾, meaning: the sick person and the traveller do not fast during illness and travel, because of the hardship upon them; rather they break the fast and make up the same number of days later. As for the healthy resident who is able to fast, he had the choice between fasting and feeding: if he wished, he fasted, and if he wished, he broke the fast and fed one poor person for each day. If he fed more than one poor person for each day, it is better. And if he fasted, it is better than feeding. This was said by Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Tawus, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and others of the predecessors. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And for those who are able to fast [but with difficulty], there is a ransom: feeding a poor person. And whoever volunteers good, it is better for him. And to fast is better for you, if you only knew.﴾

Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr related to us, al-Mas'udi related to us, 'Amr ibn Murrah related to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Prayer was altered in three stages, and fasting was altered in three stages. As for the stages of prayer: when the Prophet (ﷺ) arrived in Madinah, he prayed seventeen months toward Bayt al-Maqdis. Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed to him: ﴿We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven, so We will surely turn you to a qiblah You will be pleased with﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 144], and He turned him toward Makkah. That is one stage.

He said: They used to gather for prayer and one would call others to it until they were almost exhausted. Then a man from the Ansar, called 'Abdullah ibn Zayd, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I saw in what the sleeper sees — and if I said I was not asleep, I would be telling the truth — that while I was between sleep and wakefulness, I saw a person wearing two green garments, who faced the qiblah and said: 'Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah' — twice — until he finished the adhan. Then he waited a while and said the same, but added: 'Qad qamat al-salah' — twice." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Teach it to Bilal, so that he may call the adhan with it." So Bilal was the first to call the adhan with it. He said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I was visited in a dream by the same thing that visited him, except that he preceded me." So these are two stages.

He said: They used to come to the prayer after the Prophet (ﷺ) had already prayed some of it, so a man would signal to another man asking how much he had prayed, and he would say: "One or two," and he would pray those, then join the people in their prayer. He said: Then Mu'adh came and said: "I will never find myself in any state except that I will be in it; then I will make up what I missed." He said: He came when the Prophet (ﷺ) had already prayed part of it, and he joined him. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished, he stood and completed his prayer. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Mu'adh has established a sunnah for you, so do likewise." These are three stages.

As for the stages of fasting: when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived in Madinah, he began fasting three days of every month and fasted 'Ashura'. Then Allah made fasting obligatory upon him, and Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you﴾,

up to His words: ﴿And for those who are able to fast, there is a ransom: feeding a poor person﴾. So whoever wished fasted, and whoever wished fed a poor person, and that sufficed for him. Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed the other verse: ﴿The month of Ramadan is that in which the Qur'an was sent down﴾ up to His words: ﴿So whoever witnesses the month, let him fast it﴾. Thus Allah established fasting for the resident who is healthy, granted concession for the sick and the traveller, and the feeding was retained for the elderly person who cannot fast. These are two stages.

He said: They used to eat, drink, and approach their wives as long as they had not slept; but if they slept, they refrained. Then a man from the Ansar called Sirmah worked while fasting until evening, came to his family, prayed the 'Isha', then slept without eating or drinking, and so he woke up fasting. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw him, greatly exhausted, and said: "What is wrong with you, that I see you so exhausted?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I worked yesterday, and when I came back I threw myself down and slept, and I awoke fasting." 'Umar had approached his wife after he had slept, so he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿It is made lawful for you, the night of fasting, to go to your wives﴾ up to His words: ﴿Then complete the fast until the night﴾.

Abu Dawud related it in his Sunan, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of al-Mas'udi, with this chain [[Sunan Abi Dawud nos. (506, 507)]].

Al-Bukhari and Muslim related from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah that she said: 'Ashura' was fasted, and when the obligation of Ramadan was revealed, whoever wished fasted and whoever wished broke the fast [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4502) and Sahih Muslim no. (1125)]]. Al-Bukhari also narrated something similar from Ibn 'Umar and Ibn Mas'ud [[The hadith of Ibn 'Umar is in Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4501) and the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud is in Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4503)]].

* *

As for His words: ﴿And for those who are able to fast, there is a ransom: feeding a poor person﴾, as Mu'adh said: "At the beginning of the matter, whoever wished fasted and whoever wished broke the fast and fed one poor person for each day." Likewise al-Bukhari narrated from Salamah ibn al-Akwa' that he said: When this was revealed: ﴿And for those who are able to fast, there is a ransom: feeding a poor person﴾, whoever wanted to break the fast would pay a ransom, until the verse that follows it came and abrogated it [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4507)]].

It was also narrated from the hadith of 'Ubaydullah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: It is abrogated.

Al-Suddi said, from Murrah, from 'Abdullah: When this verse was revealed: ﴿And for those who are able to fast, there is a ransom: feeding a poor person﴾, he said: It says: ﴿And for those who are able to fast﴾, meaning: those who strain to do it. 'Abdullah said: Whoever wished fasted, and whoever wished broke the fast and fed a poor person. ﴿And whoever volunteers good﴾ — he said: he feeds another poor person ﴿it is better for him. And to fast is better for you﴾. They continued like this until it was abrogated by: ﴿So whoever witnesses the month among you, let him fast it﴾.

Al-Bukhari also said: Ishaq related to us, Rawh informed us, Zakariyya ibn Ishaq related to us, 'Amr ibn Dinar related to us, from 'Ata', who heard Ibn 'Abbas reading: "wa 'ala alladhina yutawwaqunahu fidyatun ta'amu miskin" [[Read as yutawwaqunahu, a variant reading.]]. Ibn 'Abbas said: It is not abrogated; it is for the elderly man and the elderly woman who cannot fast, so they feed a poor person for each day instead [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4505)]].

Likewise, others related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, something similar.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah said: 'Abd al-Rahim related to us, from Ash'ath ibn Sawwar, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, [who said]: This verse: ﴿And for those who are able to fast, there is a ransom: feeding a poor person﴾ was revealed concerning the elderly man who cannot bear fasting, and then became weak, so he was granted concession to feed a poor person for each day instead.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated to us; al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Bihram al-Mahrami narrated to us; Wahb ibn Baqiyya narrated to us; Khalid ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, who said: I entered upon Ata' during Ramadan while he was eating, and he said: Ibn Abbas said: "This verse was revealed: ﴿And for those who are able to fast [it is] a ransom: the feeding of a poor person﴾, so whoever wished would fast and whoever wished would break the fast and feed a poor person. Then this verse was revealed and abrogated the first, except for the elderly person who is unable [to fast], who may break the fast and feed a poor person for each day."

The conclusion of the matter is that abrogation applies to the healthy resident, through the obligation of fasting upon him by His saying: ﴿So whoever of you witnesses the month, let him fast it﴾. As for the aged old man (al-shaykh al-fani [al-harim]) who is unable to fast, he may break the fast and there is no make-up (qada') upon him, because he has no condition to which he will return in which he can make up the fast. But is it obligatory upon him, when he breaks the fast, to feed a poor person for each day if he is well-off? On this there are two opinions among the scholars. One: no feeding is obligatory upon him, because he is weak due to his age, so no ransom is obligatory upon him, like a child, because Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. This is one of the two opinions of al-Shafi'i. The second, which is the sound one and the view of most scholars, is that a ransom is obligatory upon him for each day, as Ibn Abbas and others among the early generation explained it, according to the reading of the one who reads: ﴿And for those who are able to fast﴾, meaning: those who strain to do it (yatajashshamunahu), as Ibn Mas'ud and others said. This is also the choice of al-Bukhari, for he said: "As for the elderly man who is unable to fast, Anas, after he became old for a year or two, fed a poor person each day with bread and meat, and broke his fast."

What al-Bukhari suspended (ta'liq) has been connected by al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili in his Musnad. He said: Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Imran narrated to us, from Ayyub ibn Abi Tamima, who said: Anas [ibn Malik] became weak with regard to fasting, so he prepared a bowl of thareed and invited thirty poor people and fed them.

Abd ibn Humayd also narrated it from Rawh ibn Ubada, from Imran—he is Ibn Hudayr—from Ayyub, with the same wording.

Abd also narrated it through six of Anas's companions, from Anas, with a similar meaning.

Among what is attached to this meaning: the pregnant woman and the nursing woman, if they fear for themselves or for their children. There is much disagreement among the scholars concerning them. Some said: they break the fast, pay the ransom, and make up the fast. It was said: they pay the ransom only, with no make-up. It was said: make-up is obligatory without ransom. It was said: they break the fast with neither ransom nor make-up. We have expounded this issue fully in the book on fasting that we devoted to it. And to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 183–184 (part 1 of 2):

Allah, the Exalted, addresses the believers of this Ummah and commands them to fast (al-siyam), which is abstaining from food, drink, and marital relations, with a sincere intention for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic [[In C: "sincerely for the Face of Allah, the Exalted."]], because of what it contains of purifying the soul, cleansing it, and purging it of corrupt humours and base character traits. He mentions that just as He made it obligatory upon them, He made it obligatory upon those before them, so they have in it a precedent, and these should strive to perform this obligation more perfectly than those did, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿For each of you We have made a law and a way. And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one community, but [He intended] to test you in what He has given you. So race to [all] good deeds.﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 48]. For this reason He said here: ﴿O you who have believed, fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you, that you may become righteous.﴾ Because fasting contains purification of the body and constriction of the pathways of Satan. For this reason it is established in the Two Sahihs: "O assembly of youth, whoever among you is able to marry, let him marry, and whoever is not able, let him fast, for it is a shield for him" [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5066) and Sahih Muslim no. (1400), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. Then He explained the quantity of fasting, and that it is not every day, lest it burden souls so that they become too weak to bear it and perform it, but rather on specific numbered days. This was at the beginning of Islam: they would fast three days of every month, then this was abrogated by the fasting of the month of Ramadan, as its explanation will come. It has been narrated that fasting was initially as it was for the nations before us, three days of every month, from Mu'adh, Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ata', Qatadah, and al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim. He added: "This remained prescribed from the time of Nuh until Allah abrogated it with the fasting of the month of Ramadan."

'Abbad ibn Mansur related from al-Hasan al-Basri regarding ﴿O you who have believed, fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you, that you may become righteous. [For] a limited number of days﴾ that he said: "Yes, by Allah, fasting was prescribed for every nation that passed before us, just as it was prescribed for us, a full month and numbered days, a known count." It is also narrated from al-Suddi something similar.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri', from Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Walid, from Abu al-Rabi', a man from the people of Madinah, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The fasting of Ramadan, Allah prescribed it upon the nations before you..." in a lengthy hadith from which this was abridged [[Ibn Hajar cited it in al-Fath (8/178) from Ibn Abi Hatim and said: "Its chain contains an unknown narrator."]].

Abu Ja'far al-Razi related from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from one who narrated to him from Ibn 'Umar, who said: It was revealed: ﴿Fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you [that you may become righteous]﴾ — it was prescribed for them that when one of them prayed the 'atamah (night prayer) and slept, Allah made food, drink, and women forbidden to him until the same time [the next night].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Something similar has been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and 'Ata' al-Khurasani.

'Ata' al-Khurasani related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿as it was prescribed for those before you﴾ that by this is meant the People of the Book. It is also narrated from al-Sha'bi and al-Suddi and 'Ata' al-Khurasani something similar.

Then He explained the ruling on fasting as it stood at the beginning of Islam, saying: ﴿So whoever among you is ill or on a journey [should fast] an equal number of other days﴾, meaning: the sick person and the traveller do not fast during illness and travel, because of the hardship upon them; rather they break the fast and make up the same number of days later. As for the healthy resident who is able to fast, he had the choice between fasting and feeding: if he wished, he fasted, and if he wished, he broke the fast and fed one poor person for each day. If he fed more than one poor person for each day, it is better. And if he fasted, it is better than feeding. This was said by Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Tawus, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and others of the predecessors. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And for those who are able to fast [but with difficulty], there is a ransom: feeding a poor person. And whoever volunteers good, it is better for him. And to fast is better for you, if you only knew.﴾

Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr related to us, al-Mas'udi related to us, 'Amr ibn Murrah related to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Prayer was altered in three stages, and fasting was altered in three stages. As for the stages of prayer: when the Prophet (ﷺ) arrived in Madinah, he prayed seventeen months toward Bayt al-Maqdis. Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed to him: ﴿We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven, so We will surely turn you to a qiblah You will be pleased with﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 144], and He turned him toward Makkah. That is one stage.

He said: They used to gather for prayer and one would call others to it until they were almost exhausted. Then a man from the Ansar, called 'Abdullah ibn Zayd, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I saw in what the sleeper sees — and if I said I was not asleep, I would be telling the truth — that while I was between sleep and wakefulness, I saw a person wearing two green garments, who faced the qiblah and said: 'Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah' — twice — until he finished the adhan. Then he waited a while and said the same, but added: 'Qad qamat al-salah' — twice." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Teach it to Bilal, so that he may call the adhan with it." So Bilal was the first to call the adhan with it. He said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I was visited in a dream by the same thing that visited him, except that he preceded me." So these are two stages.

He said: They used to come to the prayer after the Prophet (ﷺ) had already prayed some of it, so a man would signal to another man asking how much he had prayed, and he would say: "One or two," and he would pray those, then join the people in their prayer. He said: Then Mu'adh came and said: "I will never find myself in any state except that I will be in it; then I will make up what I missed." He said: He came when the Prophet (ﷺ) had already prayed part of it, and he joined him. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished, he stood and completed his prayer. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Mu'adh has established a sunnah for you, so do likewise." These are three stages.

As for the stages of fasting: when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived in Madinah, he began fasting three days of every month and fasted 'Ashura'. Then Allah made fasting obligatory upon him, and Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you﴾,

up to His words: ﴿And for those who are able to fast, there is a ransom: feeding a poor person﴾. So whoever wished fasted, and whoever wished fed a poor person, and that sufficed for him. Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed the other verse: ﴿The month of Ramadan is that in which the Qur'an was sent down﴾ up to His words: ﴿So whoever witnesses the month, let him fast it﴾. Thus Allah established fasting for the resident who is healthy, granted concession for the sick and the traveller, and the feeding was retained for the elderly person who cannot fast. These are two stages.

He said: They used to eat, drink, and approach their wives as long as they had not slept; but if they slept, they refrained. Then a man from the Ansar called Sirmah worked while fasting until evening, came to his family, prayed the 'Isha', then slept without eating or drinking, and so he woke up fasting. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw him, greatly exhausted, and said: "What is wrong with you, that I see you so exhausted?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I worked yesterday, and when I came back I threw myself down and slept, and I awoke fasting." 'Umar had approached his wife after he had slept, so he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿It is made lawful for you, the night of fasting, to go to your wives﴾ up to His words: ﴿Then complete the fast until the night﴾.

Abu Dawud related it in his Sunan, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of al-Mas'udi, with this chain [[Sunan Abi Dawud nos. (506, 507)]].

Al-Bukhari and Muslim related from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah that she said: 'Ashura' was fasted, and when the obligation of Ramadan was revealed, whoever wished fasted and whoever wished broke the fast [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4502) and Sahih Muslim no. (1125)]]. Al-Bukhari also narrated something similar from Ibn 'Umar and Ibn Mas'ud [[The hadith of Ibn 'Umar is in Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4501) and the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud is in Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4503)]].
