Abu 'Abdullah Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Majah said in his Sunan: Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim informed us, from Ishaq ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Madani,[[In (ه): "Abd Allah", the correct form being what we have recorded.]] from 'Abd Allah[[In (و): "Ubayd Allah".]] ibn Abi Mulaykah, from[[In (ج): "I heard".]] 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The fasting person has a supplication at the time of his breaking the fast that is not rejected." 'Abd Allah[[In (و): "Ubayd Allah".]] ibn Abi Mulaykah said: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr say, when he broke his fast: "O Allah, I ask You by Your mercy, which encompasses all things, that You forgive me."[[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (1753). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (2/38): "This chain is sound, and its narrators are trustworthy," and al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar graded it hasan in Nata'ij al-Afkar.]]

In the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, the Sunan of al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Three whose supplication is not rejected: the just ruler, the fasting person until he breaks his fast, and the supplication of the oppressed, which Allah raises above the clouds on the Day of Resurrection, and the gates of heaven are opened for it, and He says: 'By My might, I will surely help you, even if after a while.'"[[Musnad (2/445), Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3598), and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (1752).]]

This is a concession (*rukhsah*) from Allah the Exalted to the Muslims, and a lifting of what the ruling had been at the beginning of Islam. Then, if one of them broke his fast, eating, drinking and intercourse were permitted to him only until the 'Isha' prayer, or until he slept before it. Once he slept or prayed 'Isha', eating, drinking and intercourse became forbidden to him until the following night. They found this to be a great hardship. Here *al-rafath* means intercourse. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ata', Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Tawus, Salim ibn 'Abd Allah, 'Amr ibn Dinar, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Zuhri, al-Dahhak, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Suddi, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan.

* *

As for His words, ﴿They are a garment for you and you are a garment for them﴾: Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Suddi and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: it means they are a comfort (*sakan*) for you, and you are a comfort for them.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: they are a covering (*lihaf*) for you, and you are a covering for them.

The essence of this is that the man and the woman each mix with the other, touch and lie together, so it was fitting that they be granted leave to have intercourse during the nights of Ramadan, so that this would not burden them or cause them distress. The poet said:

*When the bedfellow bends her neck,*
*they cling together and she becomes a garment for him...*

The occasion of the revelation of this verse was as previously mentioned in the lengthy hadith of Mu'adh. Abu Ishaq narrated from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: When a man among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) was fasting and slept before breaking his fast, he would not eat until the following night. Qays ibn Sirmah al-Ansari was fasting, and that day he worked on his land. When the time of iftar came, he came to his wife and said: "Do you have any food?" She said: "No, but I will go and look for some for you." He was overcome by sleep and fell asleep. When his wife came back and saw him asleep, she said: "What a disappointment for you! Have you gone to sleep?" When midday came, he fainted. He mentioned this to the Prophet (ﷺ), and this verse was revealed: ﴿It has been made lawful for you, on the night of the fast, to go to your wives...﴾ up to His words: ﴿and eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread of the dawn﴾. They rejoiced at it with great joy.

[The wording of al-Tabari in his tafsir (3/495) is this.]

The wording of al-Bukhari here, from the route of Abu Ishaq, is: I heard al-Bara' say: "When the fasting of Ramadan was prescribed, they did not approach their women the whole of Ramadan, and some men were betraying themselves. So Allah revealed: ﴿Allah knew that you were deceiving yourselves, so He turned to you in forgiveness and pardoned you﴾."

[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4508.]

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: In the month of Ramadan, when Muslims prayed 'Isha', women and food became forbidden to them until the same time the next day. Then some Muslims had relations with women and ate after 'Isha' in Ramadan, among them 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. They complained of this to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Allah knew that you were deceiving yourselves, so He turned to you in forgiveness and pardoned you. So now, lie with them﴾. Al-'Awfi also narrated similarly from Ibn 'Abbas.

Musa ibn 'Uqbah narrated from Kurayb, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Before the ruling on fasting was revealed, people would eat and drink and have relations with their wives. When one of them slept, he would not eat or drink, nor approach his wife, until he broke his fast the next day. It has reached us that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, after he had slept and the fast had become obligatory for him, had relations with his wife. Then he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "I complain to Allah and to you about what I have done." He said: "And what have you done?" He said: "My self beguiled me, and I had relations with my wife after I had slept, though I intended to fast." They said that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You were not fit to do that." Then the Book was revealed: ﴿It has been made lawful for you, on the night of the fast, to go to your wives﴾.

Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated from Qays ibn Sa'd, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Abu Hurayrah, concerning Allah's words ﴿It has been made lawful for you, on the night of the fast, to go to your wives﴾ up to His words ﴿Then complete the fast until the night﴾. He said: Before this verse was revealed, when Muslims prayed 'Isha' al-Akhirah, food, drink and women became forbidden to them until they broke their fast. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab had relations with his wife after the 'Isha' prayer, and Sirmah ibn Qays al-Ansari was overcome by sleep after the Maghrib prayer, so he slept without having eaten enough, and did not wake until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had prayed 'Isha'. Then he got up and ate and drank. When morning came, he went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and told him about this. Then Allah revealed at that time: ﴿It has been made lawful for you, on the night of the fast, to go to your wives﴾, meaning by *al-rafath* sexual intercourse with women, ﴿they are a garment for you and you are a garment for them. Allah knew that you were deceiving yourselves﴾, meaning: you were having intercourse with women and eating and drinking after 'Isha', ﴿so He turned to you in forgiveness and pardoned you. So now, lie with them﴾, meaning: have intercourse with them, ﴿and seek what Allah has prescribed for you﴾, meaning: offspring, ﴿and eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread of the dawn; then complete the fast until the night﴾. So that was a pardon from Allah and a mercy.

Hushaym narrated from Husayn ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, last night I desired my wife as a man desires his wife, and she said: 'I have already slept.' I thought she was making an excuse, so I had relations with her." Then this was revealed concerning 'Umar: ﴿It has been made lawful for you, on the night of the fast, to go to your wives﴾.

Shu'bah narrated it in the same way from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Ibn Abi Layla, with the same chain.

[Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his tafsir through 'Amr ibn 'Awn, from Hushaym. The Hafiz Ibn Kathir said in *Musnad al-Faruq* (2/566): "This is a good chain, though Ibn Abi Layla is disputed as to whether he heard from 'Umar, but it has been related by another route from Ibn Abi Layla, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, that 'Umar did the like of this." Al-Tabari narrated it in his tafsir (3/493) through Shu'bah from 'Amr ibn Murrah.]

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: al-Muthanna narrated to me, Suwayd narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ibn Lahi'ah, who narrated to me, from Musa ibn Jubayr, client of Banu Salamah, that he heard 'Abd Allah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik narrate from his father, who said: During Ramadan, when a man fasted and then in the evening fell asleep, food, drink and women became forbidden to him until he broke his fast the next day. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab returned from the Prophet (ﷺ) one night after he had been talking with him late, and found his wife had gone to sleep. He wanted her, but she said: "I have already slept!" He said: "You have not slept!" Then he had relations with her. Ka'b ibn Malik did the same. In the morning 'Umar went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and told him, and Allah revealed: ﴿Allah knew that you were deceiving yourselves, so He turned to you in forgiveness and pardoned you. So now lie with them﴾ [up to the verse].

[Tafsir al-Tabari (3/496).]

The same was related from Mujahid, 'Ata', 'Ikrimah, al-Suddi, Qatadah and others concerning the occasion of the revelation of this verse, that it concerned 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and whoever acted as he did, and Sirmah ibn Qays. Thus Allah permitted intercourse, eating and drinking throughout the night, as mercy, leniency and kindness.

* *

As for His words, ﴿and seek what Allah has prescribed for you﴾: Abu Hurayrah, Ibn 'Abbas, Anas, Shurayh al-Qadi, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ata', al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Suddi, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Hakam ibn 'Utbah, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Hasan al-Basri, al-Dahhak, Qatadah and others said: it means the child.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: it means intercourse.

'Amr ibn Malik al-Nakri narrated from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas: "*and seek what Allah has prescribed for you*" means the Night of Power (*Laylat al-Qadr*). Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, saying: Qatadah said: "*and seek the concession that Allah has prescribed for you*." Sa'id narrated from Qatadah: "*and seek what Allah has prescribed for you*" means what Allah has made lawful for you.

'Abd al-Razzaq also said: Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, who said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: "How do you read this verse: *wa-btaghu* (seek) or *wa-ttabi'u* (follow)?" He said: "Whichever you wish; keep to the first reading."

Ibn Jarir preferred the view that the verse is more general than all of these.

* *

As for His words, ﴿and eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread of the dawn; then complete the fast until the night﴾: Allah the Exalted permitted eating and drinking, along with what has preceded of the permission of intercourse at any part of the night the fasting person wishes, until the light of morning becomes distinct from the darkness of night. He expressed this by "the white thread from the black thread," and removed ambiguity by His words ﴿of the dawn﴾, as came in the hadith narrated by the Imam Abu 'Abd Allah al-Bukhari: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, Abu Ghassan Muhammad ibn Mutarrif narrated to us, Abu Hazim narrated to me, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: When the verse ﴿and eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread﴾ was revealed, the words ﴿of the dawn﴾ had not yet been revealed. Some men, when they wanted to fast, would tie a white thread and a black thread to their feet, and they would keep eating until they could distinguish the two. Then Allah revealed afterwards ﴿of the dawn﴾, and they understood that it meant night and day.

[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4511.]

Imam Ahmad said: Hushaym narrated to us, Husayn informed us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: 'Adi ibn Hatim informed me, saying: When this verse was revealed, ﴿and eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread﴾, I took two cords, one black and one white, and put them under my pillow. I kept looking at them, but the black did not become distinct to me from the white, nor the white from the black. When morning came, I went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and told him what I had done. He said: "Your pillow must be wide indeed! That is only the whiteness of day and the blackness of night."

[*al-Musnad* (4/377).]

Both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in their two Sahihs through several routes from 'Adi.

[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 1916 and 4509; Sahih Muslim, no. 1090.]

The meaning of his words, "Your pillow must be wide indeed," is: if it is wide enough to place under it the black thread and the white thread that are intended in this verse, then they are the whiteness of day and the blackness of night. This would imply that the pillow would have to be as wide as the east and the west.

And this is how it occurs in the narration of al-Bukhari, explained by this: Musa ibn Isma'il informed us, Abu 'Awana narrated to us, from Husayn, from al-Sha'bi, from 'Adi, who said: "'Adi took a white thread and a black thread, and when part of the night had passed he looked but could not distinguish them." [[In A and B: "could not make them out."]] When morning came he said: "O Messenger of Allah, I put them under my pillow." He said: "Then your pillow must be broad, if the white thread and the black thread are under your pillow" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4509.]].

In some wordings it occurs: "Indeed, you have a broad nape." Some interpreted this as dullness, but this is weak. Rather, it returns to the same meaning, because if his pillow was broad, his nape is also broad, and Allah knows best. Al-Bukhari's narration also explains it:

Qutayba narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Mutarrif, from al-Sha'bi, from 'Adi ibn Hatim, who said: "I said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the white thread from the black thread? Are they two threads?" He said: "You have a broad nape if you can see the two threads." Then he said: "No, rather it is the blackness of the night and the whiteness of the day" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4510.]].

The permission Allah gives to eat until the break of dawn is evidence for the recommendation (istihbab) of suhur (the pre-dawn meal), because it falls under the category of concession (rukhsah), and taking advantage of a concession is beloved. For this reason the established Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came urging suhur. In the Two Sahihs, from Anas, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Take suhur, for in suhur there is blessing" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1923; Sahih Muslim, no. 1095.]]. In Sahih Muslim, from 'Amr ibn al-'As, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The greatest difference between our fasting and the fasting of the People of the Book is the meal of suhur" [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1096.]].

Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq ibn 'Isa, that is Ibn al-Tabba', narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd narrated to us, from his father, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Suhur is a blessing, so do not forgo it. Even if one of you swallows a mouthful of water, Allah and His angels send blessings upon those who take suhur" [[Al-Musnad, 3/44.]].

Many hadiths encourage suhur, even if it is only a mouthful of water, in imitation of those who eat. It is recommended to delay it until close to the appearance of dawn, as came in the Two Sahihs, from Anas ibn Malik, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "We took suhur with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then we stood up for the prayer." Anas said: "I asked Zayd: how long was between the adhan and the suhur?" He said: "About the length of fifty verses" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1921; Sahih Muslim, no. 1097.]].

Imam Ahmad said: Musa ibn Dawud narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'a narrated to us, from Salim ibn Ghaylan, from Sulayman ibn Abi 'Uthman, from 'Adi ibn Hatim al-Himsi, from Abu Dhar, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "My community will remain in good as long as they hasten the iftar and delay the suhur" [[Al-Musnad, 5/172.]].

Many hadiths state that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called suhur "the blessed morning meal." In the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, through the narration of Hammad ibn Salama, from 'Asim ibn Bahdala, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman, who said: "We took suhur with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and it was daytime except that the sun had not risen" [[Al-Musnad, 5/396; Sunan al-Nasa'i, 4/142; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 1695.]]. This is a hadith in which 'Asim ibn Abi al-Nujud stands alone, as al-Nasa'i said. He interpreted it to mean that the daytime was near, as Allah says: ﴿Then when they reach their term, either retain them in kindness or release them in kindness﴾ [al-Talaq: 2], meaning: they have come close to the end of the waiting period, so either retain or leave. This interpretation is the one that is necessarily the correct meaning of the hadith: that they took suhur without being certain of the appearance of dawn, so that some of them thought it had appeared and some were not sure of it. It has been related from a large group of the early generations (salaf) that they were lenient about suhur when dawn was approaching. The like of this was narrated from Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, Hudhayfa, Abu Hurayra, Ibn 'Umar, Ibn 'Abbas and Zayd ibn Thabit, and from a large group of the Successors (tabi'un), among them Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, Abu Mijlaz, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Abu al-Duha, Abu Wa'il and others among the companions of Ibn Mas'ud, 'Ata', al-Hasan, al-Hakam ibn 'Uyayna, Mujahid, 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, and Abu al-Sha'tha' Jabir ibn Zayd. To this view al-A'mash and Ma'mar ibn Rashid also went. We have verified the chains of these reports in the book al-Siyam al-Mufrad, and to Allah belongs all praise.

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir related in his Tafsir, from some of them, that abstention is only obligatory from the rising of the sun, just as breaking the fast is permitted at its setting.

I say: I do not think any scholar would stand firm on this view, because it contradicts the explicit text of the Qur'an in His saying: ﴿And eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread of dawn; then complete the fast until night﴾. It has been established in the Two Sahihs, from the hadith of al-Qasim, from 'A'isha, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Let not Bilal's call to prayer keep you from your suhur, for he calls at night, so eat and drink until you hear the call of Ibn Umm Maktum, for he does not call until dawn has come." This is the wording of al-Bukhari [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 1918, 622; Sahih Muslim, no. 1092. The phrase "Let not Bilal's call to prayer keep you from your suhur" does not occur in al-Bukhari from the hadith of 'A'isha but from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud; this is what appeared to me after research, and Allah knows best.]].

Imam Ahmad said: Musa ibn Dawud narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Jabir narrated to us, from Qays ibn Talq, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The dawn is not the one that spreads lengthwise across the horizon, but the one that stretches across, red" [[Al-Musnad, 4/23.]]. Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated it, and their wording is: "Eat and drink, and do not let the rising, ascending light deceive you. Eat and drink until the red stretches across for you" [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2348; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 705.]].

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Shu'ba narrated to us, from a shaykh of Banu Qushayr: I heard Samura ibn Jundab say: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Let not the call of Bilal and this whiteness deceive you, until the dawn bursts forth, or the dawn rises."

Then he narrated it through another route, from the hadith of Shu'ba and others, from Sawada ibn Handhala, from Samura, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Let not Bilal's call to prayer keep you from your suhur, nor the lengthwise dawn, but the dawn that spreads across the horizon" [[I have not found this hadith in the printed Tafsir of al-Tabari.]].

He said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sawada al-Qushayri, from his father, from Samura ibn Jundab, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Let not the call of Bilal or this whiteness deceive you; aim for the dawn when it spreads across."

Muslim narrated it in his Sahih from Zuhayr ibn Harb, from Isma'il ibn Ibrahim, that is Ibn 'Ulayya, the same wording exactly [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1094.]].

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Let not Bilal's call to prayer keep any one of you from his suhur, or he said, Bilal's call, for Bilal calls, or he said, cries out, to wake your sleeper and to return your one who is standing [in prayer]. The dawn is not that it says this and this, but until it says this." [The Prophet (ﷺ) indicated it with his hands.]

He narrated it by another route from al-Taymi, with the same chain [[I have not found this hadith in the printed Tafsir of al-Tabari. It is narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, nos. 621, 5298, and Muslim in his Sahih, no. 1093, through the route of Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi.]].

Al-Hasan ibn al-Zibriqan al-Nakha'i narrated to me, Abu Usama narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Dhi'b, from al-Harith ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Thawban, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Dawn is of two kinds: the one that is like the tail of a wolf does not make anything unlawful, but the one that spreads and covers the horizon makes prayer lawful and makes food unlawful" [[Tafsir al-Tabari, 3/514.]]. This is a good mursal (a report in which the Companion's name is omitted from the chain).

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, from 'Ata', who said: I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: "There are two dawns. As for the one that shines in the sky, it neither makes lawful nor unlawful anything. But the dawn that becomes clear over the mountaintops is the one that makes drinking unlawful." 'Ata' said: "As for when it shines brightly in the sky, and its shining is that it stretches upward in the sky lengthwise, it does not make drink unlawful for the fast, nor does it cause the Hajj to be missed. But when it spreads over the mountaintops, it makes drink unlawful for the fast and causes the Hajj to be missed."

This is a sound chain to Ibn 'Abbas and 'Ata', and the like of this has been related from more than one of the early generations, may Allah have mercy on them.

Issue: From Allah's making the dawn the limit for the permission of intercourse, eating and drinking for one who intends to fast, it is deduced that whoever enters the morning in a state of major ritual impurity (janabah) should perform ghusl, complete his fast, and there is no fault upon him. This is the position of the four Imams and the majority of scholars, both earlier and later, based on what al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated from the hadith of 'A'isha and Umm Salama, may Allah be pleased with them both, that they both said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would enter the morning in a state of janabah from intercourse, not from a wet dream, then he would perform ghusl and fast" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 1925, 1926; Sahih Muslim, no. 1109.]]. In the version of Umm Salama in both of them: "Then he would not break the fast nor make it up." In Sahih Muslim, from 'A'isha: a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, the prayer reaches me while I am junub, and I fast?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The prayer reaches me too while I am junub, and I fast." He said: "You are not like us, O Messenger of Allah; Allah has forgiven you what came before of your sins and what came after." He said: "By Allah, I truly hope that I am the most fearful of Allah among you and the most knowing of what I should guard against" [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1109.]]. As for the hadith which Imam Ahmad narrated:

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 187 (part 3 of 4):

'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "If the call to prayer is made for the prayer, the dawn prayer, and one of you is in a state of janabah, then he should not fast that day." [Al-Musnad (2/314).] This is a hadith whose chain is sound (jayyid al-isnad) according to the criteria of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), as you can see. It is also in the two Sahihs, from Abu Hurayrah, from al-Fadl ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ). [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1925) and Sahih Muslim no. (1109).] In Sunan al-Nasa'i, from him, from Usamah ibn Zayd and al-Fadl ibn 'Abbas, and it was not traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ) [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra nos. (2933, 2934)]. Some scholars gave this hadith a defect (ʿillah) on this basis, and others adopted it. This view is reported from Abu Hurayrah, Salim, 'Ata', Hisham ibn 'Urwah, and al-Hasan al-Basri. Others made a distinction between one who becomes junub while asleep, who is not at fault, based on the hadith of 'A'ishah and Umm Salamah, and one who does so deliberately, whose fast is not valid, based on the hadith of Abu Hurayrah. This is reported from 'Urwah, Tawus, and al-Hasan. Others distinguished between the obligatory fast, which one must complete and make up, and the voluntary fast, which is not harmful to him. This was narrated by al-Thawri, from Mansur, from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and it is also a narration from al-Hasan al-Basri. Others claimed that the hadith of Abu Hurayrah was abrogated by the hadiths of 'A'ishah and Umm Salamah, but there is no known chronology for this.

Ibn Hazm claimed that it was abrogated by this noble verse, but this is also far-fetched, and even more so, since there is no chronology; rather, the apparent chronology indicates the opposite. Others interpreted the hadith of Abu Hurayrah as negating perfection ("then he has no fast"), in light of the hadiths of 'A'ishah and Umm Salamah which indicate permissibility. This approach is the closest of the opinions and the most comprehensive, and Allah knows best.

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then complete the fast until the night﴾ requires breaking the fast at sunset as a legal ruling, as came in the two Sahihs, from the Commander of the Faithful 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the night approaches from here and the day recedes from here, the fasting person has broken his fast." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1954) and Sahih Muslim no. (1100).]

And from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "People will remain in good as long as they hasten to break the fast." Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) also narrated it. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1957) and Sahih Muslim no. (1098).]

Imam Ahmad said: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, al-Awza'i narrated to us, Qurrah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: Indeed, the most beloved of My servants to Me are those who hasten to break their fast."

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi through more than one chain, from al-Awza'i, with it. He said: This is a hadith that is hasan gharib.

Ahmad also said: 'Affan narrated to us, 'Ubayd Allah ibn Iyad narrated to us, I heard Iyad ibn Laqit say: I heard Layla, the wife of Bashir ibn al-Khasasiyah, say: I wanted to fast two days continuously (wisal), but Bashir prevented me and said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade it. And he said: "The Christians do that, but fast as Allah has commanded you, and complete the fast until the night, and when night comes, break your fast." [Al-Musnad (5/225).]

[The Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir narrated: Bakr ibn Sahl narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Yahya ibn Hamzah narrated to us, from Thawr ibn Yazid, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Dharr, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fasted continuously for two days and a night; then Jibril came to him and said: Indeed Allah has accepted your continuous fasting, and it is not permissible for anyone after you. That is because Allah said: ﴿Then complete the fast until the night﴾, so there is no fasting after the night, and He commanded me to pray the witr before dawn. This chain is not objectionable; he cited it in the biography of 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Dharr in his History.] [Addition from manuscripts ج, أ, و.] [See: Mukhtasar Tarikh Dimashq by Ibn Manzur (15/192).]

For this reason, the authentic hadiths report the prohibition of wisal, which is joining the fast of one day to another without eating anything between them. Imam Ahmad said:

'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not practise wisal." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, you practise wisal." He said: "I am not like you; I spend the night while my Lord feeds me and gives me drink." He said: They did not desist from wisal, so the Prophet (ﷺ) joined with them for two days and two nights; then they saw the new moon, and he said: "If the moon had been delayed, I would have increased it for you," as a punishment for them.

Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) also narrated it in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of al-Zuhri with it. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6851) and Sahih Muslim no. (1105).] Likewise, both narrated the prohibition of wisal from the hadiths of Anas and Ibn 'Umar. [The hadith of Anas is in Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1961) and Sahih Muslim no. (1104); the hadith of Ibn 'Umar is in Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1962) and Sahih Muslim no. (1102).]

And from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade wisal, out of mercy for them. They said: "You practise wisal." He said: "I am not like your state; my Lord feeds me and gives me drink." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1964) and Sahih Muslim no. (1105).]

Thus the prohibition is established through more than one chain, and it is established that it is among the special characteristics of the Prophet (ﷺ), and that he was strengthened for it and assisted in it. The most apparent view is that this food and drink, in his case, was spiritual, not physical; otherwise he would not be described as practising wisal with physical food. Rather, as the poet said:

She has stories of your remembrance that occupy her
away from drink, and distract her from food...

As for one who wishes to abstain after sunset until the time of suhur, he may do so, as in the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not practise wisal. Whichever of you wishes to practise wisal, let him continue until suhur." They said: "But you practise wisal, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "I am not like your state; I spend the night while there is one who feeds me, and one who gives me drink." Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it in the two Sahihs as well. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1963); I have not located it in Sahih Muslim.]

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Abu Isra'il al-'Absi narrated to us, from Abu Bakr ibn Hafs, from the mother of a child of Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah: that she passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was taking suhur, and he invited her to the food. She said: "I am fasting." He said: "How do you fast?" She mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "How far are you from the wisal of the family of Muhammad, from suhur to suhur?" [Tafsir al-Tabari (3/537, 538).]

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from 'Abd al-A'la, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali, from 'Ali: that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to practise wisal from suhur to suhur. [Al-Musnad (1/91, 141).]

Ibn Jarir narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr and others among the early generations that they used to practise wisal for several days. He understood this from them as a discipline for themselves, not as worship. And Allah knows best. It is also possible that they understood the prohibition as guidance, out of compassion, as came in the hadith of 'A'ishah: "out of mercy for them." So Ibn al-Zubayr, his son 'Amir, and whoever followed their path, would undertake and practise it, because they found strength in it. It is mentioned of them that they would break their fast first with ghee and aloe, so that the intestines would not be torn by food at first. It is narrated from Ibn al-Zubayr that he would practise wisal for seven days and would be the strongest and most robust of them on the seventh day. Abu al-'Aliyah said: Allah only obligated fasting during the day; when night comes, whoever wishes eats, and whoever wishes does not eat.

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And do not have intercourse with them while you are devoting yourselves to worship in the mosques﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: This refers to a man who observes i'tikaf in the mosque, whether in Ramadan or otherwise. Allah forbade him to have relations with women, by night or by day, until he completes his i'tikaf.

Al-Dahhak said: When a man performed i'tikaf and went out of the mosque, he would have intercourse if he wished. So Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And do not have intercourse with them while you are devoting yourselves to worship in the mosques﴾, meaning: do not approach them as long as you are in i'tikaf in the mosque, nor elsewhere. Likewise Mujahid, Qatadah, and others said that they used to do that until this verse was revealed.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, Muhammad ibn Ka'b, Mujahid, 'Ata', al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and Muqatil, that they said: He does not approach them while he is in i'tikaf. What he related from these is the matter agreed upon among the scholars: that the one in i'tikaf is forbidden from women as long as he is in i'tikaf in his mosque. If he goes to his home for a necessary need, it is not permissible for him to remain there except for the time needed to finish that need, such as relieving himself or eating. He may not kiss his wife, embrace her, or occupy himself with anything other than his i'tikaf, and he should not visit the sick, but he may inquire about them while passing on his way.

Rulings on i'tikaf are detailed in its own chapter; some are agreed upon among the scholars, and some are disputed. We have mentioned a good portion of that at the end of the Book of Fasting, and to Allah belongs all praise.

Accordingly, the jurists who compiled their works follow the Book of Fasting with the Book of I'tikaf (seclusion in the mosque for worship), following the example of the Mighty Qur'an, which drew attention to mentioning i'tikaf after mentioning fasting. Mentioning i'tikaf after fasting by the Exalted is a guidance and an indication of i'tikaf during the fast, or in the last part of the month of fasting, as the Sunnah was established from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he used to observe i'tikaf in the last ten nights of Ramadan until Allah took him. Then his wives observed i'tikaf after him. Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated it from the hadith of 'A'ishah, the Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2033) and Sahih Muslim no. (1172), the wording being Muslim's.]

In the two Sahihs it is reported that Safiyyah bint Huyayy used to visit the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was in seclusion in the mosque. She talked with him for a while, then rose to return to her home, and that was at night. The Prophet (ﷺ) stood up to walk with her until she reached her dwelling, and her house was in the residence of Usamah ibn Zayd, on the outskirts of Madinah. When they were part of the way, two men of the Ansar met him. When they saw the Prophet (ﷺ), they hastened, and in another narration, they hid themselves, out of modesty before the Prophet (ﷺ) because his wife was with him. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to them: "Take it easy, she is Safiyyah bint Huyayy," meaning: do not hasten, and know that she is Safiyyah bint Huyayy, that is, my wife. They said: "Glory be to Allah, O Messenger of Allah!" He, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed, Satan flows through the son of Adam as the blood flows, and I feared that he might cast something into your hearts," or he said: "evil." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2035, 6219) and Sahih Muslim no. (2175), from the hadith of Safiyyah, may Allah be pleased with her.]

Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: He, peace be upon him, wished to teach his Ummah to clear themselves of suspicion in its proper place, lest they fall into what is forbidden, although those two were too God-fearing to suspect the Prophet (ﷺ) of anything. And Allah knows best.

Then, the intended meaning of mubashara (intimate contact) is indeed intercourse and its preliminaries, such as kissing, embracing and the like. As for handing something over and similar acts, there is no harm in them. It is established in the two Sahihs, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to bring his head close to me and I would comb it while I was menstruating, and he would not enter the house except for the needs of a human being. 'A'ishah said: The sick person would be in the house, and I would not ask about him except while passing by. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2029) and Sahih Muslim no. (297).]

* *

As for His saying ﴿تِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ﴾ ("These are the limits set by Allah"), meaning: this which We have explained, prescribed and defined regarding fasting and its rulings, what We have permitted in it and what We have forbidden, and We mentioned its time limits, its concessions and its firm obligations, these are the limits of Allah, that is, Allah legislated them and explained them Himself. ﴿فَلا تَقْرَبُوهَا﴾ ("so do not approach them"), that is, do not transgress them or exceed them.

Al-Dahhak and Muqatil said, concerning His saying ﴿تِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ﴾, that it refers to intimate contact during i'tikaf.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: He means these four limits. He recited ﴿أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ لَيْلَةَ الصِّيَامِ الرَّفَثُ إِلَى نِسَائِكُمْ﴾ ("It is made lawful for you on the night of fasting to go to your wives") until he reached ﴿ثُمَّ أَتِمُّوا الصِّيَامَ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ﴾ ("Then complete the fast until nightfall"). He said: My father and others of our shaykhs used to say this and recite it to us.

﴿كَذَلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ آيَاتِهِ لِلنَّاسِ﴾ ("Thus Allah makes clear His signs to mankind"), that is, just as He explained fasting, its rulings, its laws and its details, so He explains all the other rulings through His servant and Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ﴾ ("so that they may be mindful of Him"), that is, so that they may know how to be guided and how to obey, as the Exalted said: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي يُنزلُ عَلَى عَبْدِهِ آيَاتٍ بَيِّنَاتٍ لِيُخْرِجَكُمْ مِنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى النُّورِ وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُمْ لَرَءُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ ("It is He who sends down to His servant clear signs that He may bring you out of darknesses into light. Indeed, Allah is to you Kind and Merciful"). [Al-Hadid: 9.]

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: This refers to a man who owes money, but has no evidence against him for it. So he denies the debt and brings his case before the judges, although he knows that the right is upon him, and he knows that he is sinful, one who consumes what is unlawful.

Similarly it has been related from Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, that they said: Do not dispute while you know that you are a wrongdoer. It has also been related in the two Sahihs (al-Sahihayn) from Umm Salamah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed I am only a human being, and disputants come to me. Perhaps one of you is more eloquent in his argument than another, so I decide in his favour. Whomever I decide in favour of, taking away the right of a Muslim, it is only a piece of Fire, so let him take it or leave it." (Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 2458, 6967, and Sahih Muslim, no. 1713, from the hadith of Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her.)

This noble verse and this hadith indicate that the ruling of a judge does not change the reality of the matter. Thus it does not make lawful in reality what is unlawful, nor make unlawful what is lawful. Rather, it is binding only outwardly (fi'l-zahir). If it conforms to the reality of the matter, then well and good; otherwise the judge has his reward, and the one who deceived bears the burden. For this reason Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And do not consume one another's wealth by false means, nor send it [as bribes] to the judges so that you may consume a portion [i.e., a part]﴾ ﴿of the wealth of the people in sin, while you know [it]﴾, meaning: while you know the falsehood of what you claim, and you pass it off in your speech.

Qatadah said: Know, O son of Adam, that the judge's decision does not make lawful for you what is unlawful, nor make right for you what is false. The judge only decides according to what he sees and what the witnesses testify to, and the judge is a human being who errs and is correct. Know that whoever is decided in his favour in falsehood, his dispute is not ended until Allah gathers them both on the Day of Resurrection, and He judges between the one who is in the wrong and the one who is in the right with something better than what was decided in this world in favour of the wrongdoer against the one who is right.

Abu Hanifah said: The ruling of a judge concerning the divorce of a wife, when two false witnesses testify before him, while they are upright in his estimation, makes her lawful to other husbands, even to the two witnesses, and makes her unlawful to her husband from whom he has ruled her divorced. They said: This is like the li'an of a woman: it separates her from her husband and makes her unlawful to him, even if she is lying in reality. And if the judge knew of her lying, he would have punished her with the hadd and would not have made her unlawful (to him). This view is more correct (awla).

Issue: al-Qurtubi said: The People of the Sunnah agree that whoever consumes unlawful wealth, even if it is not something that is truly called wealth, is a sinner (yafsuq). Bishr ibn al-Mu'tamir, among a group of the Mu'tazilah, said: One becomes a sinner only by consuming two hundred dirhams or more, and is not a sinner by less than that. Al-Jubba'i said: One becomes a sinner by consuming a single dirham or more, but not by less than that.

Ibn Abbas said, as narrated by al-Awfi: The people asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the crescent moons, and this verse was revealed: ﴿They ask you about the new moons. Say: They are timings for the people [and for the Hajj]﴾ [[Addition from manuscript A.]], by which they know the terms of their debts, the waiting periods of their wives, and the time of their Hajj.

Abu Ja'far narrated from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliyah: "It reached us that they said: O Messenger of Allah, why were the crescent moons created?" So Allah revealed: ﴿They ask you about the new moons. Say: They are timings for the people﴾, meaning: Allah made them timings for the fasting and breaking of the fast of the Muslims, the waiting periods of their wives, and the due dates of their debts.

Similar things have been related from Ata', al-Dahhak, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas.

Abd al-Razzaq said, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Rawwad, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah made the new moons timings for the people. So fast when you see it, and break your fast when you see it. If it is cloudy over you, then count thirty days."

Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak through the hadith of Ibn Abi Rawwad, with the same chain [[al-Mustadrak (1/423).]]. He said: "He was trustworthy, devout, diligent, and of noble lineage, so its chain is sound, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it."

Muhammad ibn Jabir narrated from Qays ibn Talq, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah made the new moons. When you see the crescent, fast; and when you see it, break your fast. If it is hidden from you, then complete the count to thirty" [[Related by Ahmad in al-Musnad (4/23) through Muhammad ibn Jabir.]]. Similarly it has been related from the hadith of Abu Hurairah and from the words of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him [[In manuscript C: "them".]] [[The hadith of Abu Hurairah is related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (1909), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (1081).]].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter the houses from their backs, but righteousness is [in] one who fears Allah. So enter houses through their doors﴾. Al-Bukhari said: Ubayd Allah [[In manuscript A: "Abd Allah".]] ibn Musa narrated to us, from Israil, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: When they entered ihram in the Jahiliyyah, they would enter the house from its back. So Allah revealed: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter the houses from their backs, but righteousness is [in] one who fears Allah. So enter houses through their doors﴾ [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4512).]].

Similarly, Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated from Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: When the Ansar returned from a journey, a man would not enter from the door of his house, so this verse was revealed.

Al-A'mash said, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir: Quraysh were called al-Hums, and they would enter through the doors while in ihram, whereas the Ansar and the rest of the Arabs would not enter through a door while in ihram. While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in a garden, he came out through its door, and Qutbah ibn Amir al-Ansari came out with him. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, Qutbah ibn Amir is a merchant (in manuscript C: 'wicked'), and he came out with you through the door." He said to him: "What led you to do what you did?" He said: "I saw you do it, so I did as you did." He said: "I am a man of Hums." He said: "Then my religion is your religion." So Allah revealed: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter the houses from their backs, but righteousness is [in] one who fears Allah. So enter houses through their doors﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim related it. Al-Awfi related it from Ibn Abbas with similar wording. Similarly it has been related from Mujahid, al-Zuhri, Qatadah, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Suddi, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Some people of the Jahiliyyah, when one of them wanted to travel and went out of his house intending his journey, then after he had gone out it occurred to him to stay and abandon his journey, he would not enter the house through its door, but would climb over it from its back. So Allah the Exalted said: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter the houses from their backs [but righteousness is in one who fears Allah]﴾, to the end of the verse.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: When a man performed i'tikaf, he would not enter his home through the door of the house, so Allah revealed this verse.

Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: The people of Yathrib, when they returned from their festival, would enter their homes from their backs, considering that closer to righteousness. So Allah the Exalted said: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter the houses from their backs﴾.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And fear Allah that you may be successful﴾, meaning: fear Allah by doing what He has commanded you and leaving what He has forbidden you, ﴿that you may be successful﴾ tomorrow when you stand before Him, and He will repay you for your deeds in full and complete measure.

Abu Ja'far al-Razi related from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you﴾. He said: "This is the first verse revealed about fighting in Medina. When it was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would fight whoever fought him and refrain from whoever refrained from him, until Surah Bara'ah (At-Tawbah) was revealed." 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said the same, and went on to say: "It was abrogated (mansukh) by His words: ﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [At-Tawbah: 5]." But this view requires consideration, because His words ﴿who fight you﴾ are only an incitement and an urging against the enemies whose aim is to fight Islam and its people. That is, "Just as they fight you, fight them." He said similarly: ﴿And fight the polytheists all together as they fight you all together﴾ [At-Tawbah: 36]. For this reason He said in this verse: ﴿And kill them wherever you overtake them, and expel them from where they have expelled you﴾, meaning: let your resolve be roused to fight them, just as their resolve is roused to fight you, and to expel them from the lands from which they expelled you, as retribution.

It is related from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, that the first verse revealed about fighting after the Hijrah was ﴿Permission is given to those who are being fought, because they have been wronged﴾ [Al-Hajj: 39], and this is the most well-known view, and the hadith also came with it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And do not transgress; indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors﴾, meaning: fight in the way of Allah, and do not transgress in that. This includes committing what is forbidden, as al-Hasan al-Basri said, such as mutilation (muthlah), embezzlement from the spoils (ghulul), killing women, children, and elderly people who have no opinion and do not fight, monks and those in monasteries, burning trees, and killing animals without benefit. Ibn 'Abbas, 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and others said the same. For this reason it came in Sahih Muslim, from Buraydah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: "Go out to fight in the way of Allah; fight those who disbelieve in Allah. Go forth and do not embezzle, do not betray, do not mutilate, and do not kill a child, nor the people of the monasteries." Imam Ahmad narrated it. [Sahih Muslim no. (1731) and al-Musnad (5/352).]

And from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent out his armies, he would say: "Set out in the name of Allah. Fight in the way of Allah those who disbelieve in Allah. Do not betray, do not embezzle, do not mutilate, and do not kill children or the people of the monasteries." Imam Ahmad narrated it. [al-Musnad (1/300).]

Abu Dawud related a similar report from Anas, traced to the Prophet ﷺ. [Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2614).] In the Two Sahihs, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: A woman was found killed during one of the military expeditions of the Prophet ﷺ, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disapproved of the killing of women and children. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3015) and Sahih Muslim no. (1744).]

Imam Ahmad said: Musab ibn Sallam narrated to us, al-Ajlah narrated to us, from Qays ibn Abi Muslim, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, who said: I heard Huthayfah say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck for us parables of one, three, five, seven, nine, and eleven, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck for us one of them and left the rest. He said: "There was a people who were weak and humble, and they were fought by a people who were oppressive and hostile. Allah gave the weak people victory over them, but they went to their enemy and enslaved them and dominated them, so they angered Allah against themselves until the day they meet Him." [al-Musnad (5/407).]

This is a hadith whose chain is fine (hasan al-isnad). Its meaning is that these weak people, when they gained power over the strong, transgressed against them and put them to work in ways that were not fitting for them, and so they brought Allah's anger upon themselves because of this transgression. The hadiths and reports on this subject are very numerous.

Since jihad involves the destruction of souls and the killing of men, Allah, Exalted is He, drew attention to the fact that what they persist in, namely disbelief in Allah, associating partners with Him, and barring others from His path, is more severe, more grievous, and more monstrous than killing. For this reason He said: ﴿And fitnah is worse than killing﴾. Abu Malik said: That is, what you persist in is greater than killing.

Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said regarding His words ﴿and fitnah is worse than killing﴾: "It means shirk is worse than killing."

* *

As for His words: ﴿And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram﴾, as came in the Two Sahihs: "This city, Allah made it sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth. It is sacred by Allah's sanctity until the Day of Resurrection. Fighting in it was not permitted to me except for an hour of a day, and it is sacred by Allah's sanctity until the Day of Resurrection. Its trees are not to be cut and its grass is not to be uprooted. If anyone takes the concession of fighting in it because of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, say: Allah permitted His Messenger, but He did not permit you." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1834) and Sahih Muslim no. (1353), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.]

By this, peace and blessings be upon him, he meant his fighting its people on the day of the Conquest of Mecca. He conquered it by force (‘anwah), and some men were killed at al-Khandamah. It was also said that it was taken by treaty (sulh), based on his saying: "Whoever closes his door is safe, whoever enters the Masjid is safe, and whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan is safe."

[Al-Qurtubi relates that the prohibition of fighting at al-Masjid al-Haram has been abrogated (mansukh). Qatadah said: It was abrogated by His words: ﴿Then when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them and seize them﴾ [At-Tawbah: 5]. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It was abrogated by His words: ﴿Then when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾. But this view requires consideration.]

* *

As for His words: ﴿Until they fight you there. But if they fight you, then kill them. Such is the recompense of the disbelievers﴾, Allah, Exalted is He, says: Do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram unless they begin fighting you there. Then you have the right to fight and kill them, to repel their aggression, just as the Prophet ﷺ pledged his companions at al-Hudaybiyah beneath the tree to fight, when the tribes of Quraysh and those allied with them from the clans of Thaqif and the Ahabish gathered against him that year. Then Allah withheld the fighting between them, and He said: ﴿And it is He who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them within Mecca after He had given you victory over them﴾ [Al-Fath: 24]. And He said: ﴿And if not for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, you might have trampled them, and harm would have come upon you from them without knowledge, so that Allah would admit into His mercy whom He wills. If they had been separated, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with painful punishment﴾ [Al-Fath: 25].

* *

As for His words: ﴿But if they desist, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning: if they abandon fighting in the sanctuary and turn back to Islam and repentance, then indeed Allah [is Forgiving and Merciful], He forgives their sins, even if they had killed Muslims in the sanctuary of Allah, for no sin is too great for Him to forgive to one who repents to Him from it.

Then Allah, Exalted is He, commanded the fighting of the disbelievers: ﴿Until there is no fitnah﴾, meaning: no shirk. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Rabi', Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Suddi, and Zayd ibn Aslam.

﴿And religion is for Allah﴾, meaning: the religion of Allah becomes dominant (al-'Aali) over all other religions, as was established in the Two Sahihs from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about a man who fights out of bravery, fights out of zeal, and fights to be seen, "Which of these is in the way of Allah?" He said: "Whoever fights so that the word of Allah is supreme, he is in the way of Allah." [Sahih al-Bukhari nos. (2810, 3126) and Sahih Muslim no. (1904).] And in the Two Sahihs: "I have been commanded to fight people until they say: There is no god but Allah. When they say it, they have protected their blood and property from me, except by its right, and their reckoning is with Allah." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (25) and Sahih Muslim no. (22), from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both.]

As for His words: ﴿But if they desist, then there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers﴾, meaning: if they desist from what they are engaged in of shirk and fighting the believers, then leave them alone. Whoever fights them after that is a wrongdoer, and there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers. This is the meaning of Mujahid's statement: "One is only fought if he fights." Or its meaning may be: "If they desist, then they have been freed from wrongdoing, which is shirk, and there is no aggression against them after that." Here the word "aggression" (‘udwan) means punishment and fighting, like His words: ﴿So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 194], and His words: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it﴾ [Ash-Shura: 40], and ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the same as you were punished with﴾ [An-Nahl: 126]. For this reason 'Ikrimah and Qatadah said: The wrongdoer is the one who refused to say: There is no god but Allah.

Al-Bukhari said: His words ﴿And fight them until there is no fitnah [and religion is for Allah]﴾, the verse: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: Two men came to him during the fitnah of Ibn al-Zubayr and said: "The people have ruined things, and you are the son of 'Umar and the companion of the Prophet ﷺ. What prevents you from going out?" He said: "What prevents me is that Allah has forbidden the blood of my brother." They said: "Did Allah not say: ﴿And fight them until there is no fitnah﴾?" He said: "We fought until there was no fitnah and the religion was for Allah, but you want to fight until there is fitnah and the religion is for other than Allah." It is related from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, that the first verse revealed about fighting after the Hijrah was ﴿Permission is given to those who are being fought, because they have been wronged﴾ [Al-Hajj: 39], and this is the most well-known view, and the hadith also came with it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And do not transgress; indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors﴾, meaning: fight in the way of Allah, and do not transgress in that. This includes committing what is forbidden, as al-Hasan al-Basri said, such as mutilation (muthlah), embezzlement from the spoils (ghulul), killing women, children, and elderly people who have no opinion and do not fight, monks and those in monasteries, burning trees, and killing animals without benefit. Ibn 'Abbas, 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and others said the same. For this reason it came in Sahih Muslim, from Buraydah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: "Go out to fight in the way of Allah; fight those who disbelieve in Allah. Go forth and do not embezzle, do not betray, do not mutilate, and do not kill a child, nor the people of the monasteries." Imam Ahmad narrated it. [Sahih Muslim no. (1731) and al-Musnad (5/352).]

And from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent out his armies, he would say: "Set out in the name of Allah. Fight in the way of Allah those who disbelieve in Allah. Do not betray, do not embezzle, do not mutilate, and do not kill children or the people of the monasteries." Imam Ahmad narrated it. [al-Musnad (1/300).]

Abu Dawud related a similar report from Anas, traced to the Prophet ﷺ. [Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2614).] In the Two Sahihs, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: A woman was found killed during one of the military expeditions of the Prophet ﷺ, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disapproved of the killing of women and children. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3015) and Sahih Muslim no. (1744).]

Imam Ahmad said: Musab ibn Sallam narrated to us, al-Ajlah narrated to us, from Qays ibn Abi Muslim, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, who said: I heard Huthayfah say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck for us parables of one, three, five, seven, nine, and eleven, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck for us one of them and left the rest. He said: "There was a people who were weak and humble, and they were fought by a people who were oppressive and hostile. Allah gave the weak people victory over them, but they went to their enemy and enslaved them and dominated them, so they angered Allah against themselves until the day they meet Him." [al-Musnad (5/407).]

This is a hadith whose chain is fine (hasan al-isnad). Its meaning is that these weak people, when they gained power over the strong, transgressed against them and put them to work in ways that were not fitting for them, and so they brought Allah's anger upon themselves because of this transgression. The hadiths and reports on this subject are very numerous.

Since jihad involves the destruction of souls and the killing of men, Allah, Exalted is He, drew attention to the fact that what they persist in, namely disbelief in Allah, associating partners with Him, and barring others from His path, is more severe, more grievous, and more monstrous than killing. For this reason He said: ﴿And fitnah is worse than killing﴾. Abu Malik said: That is, what you persist in is greater than killing.

Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said regarding His words ﴿and fitnah is worse than killing﴾: "It means shirk is worse than killing."

* *

As for His words: ﴿And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram﴾, as came in the Two Sahihs: "This city, Allah made it sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth. It is sacred by Allah's sanctity until the Day of Resurrection. Fighting in it was not permitted to me except for an hour of a day, and it is sacred by Allah's sanctity until the Day of Resurrection. Its trees are not to be cut and its grass is not to be uprooted. If anyone takes the concession of fighting in it because of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, say: Allah permitted His Messenger, but He did not permit you." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1834) and Sahih Muslim no. (1353), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.]

By this, peace and blessings be upon him, he meant his fighting its people on the day of the Conquest of Mecca. He conquered it by force (‘anwah), and some men were killed at al-Khandamah. It was also said that it was taken by treaty (sulh), based on his saying: "Whoever closes his door is safe, whoever enters the Masjid is safe, and whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan is safe."

[Al-Qurtubi relates that the prohibition of fighting at al-Masjid al-Haram has been abrogated (mansukh). Qatadah said: It was abrogated by His words: ﴿Then when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them and seize them﴾ [At-Tawbah: 5]. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It was abrogated by His words: ﴿Then when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾. But this view requires consideration.]

* *

As for His words: ﴿Until they fight you there. But if they fight you, then kill them. Such is the recompense of the disbelievers﴾, Allah, Exalted is He, says: Do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram unless they begin fighting you there. Then you have the right to fight and kill them, to repel their aggression, just as the Prophet ﷺ pledged his companions at al-Hudaybiyah beneath the tree to fight, when the tribes of Quraysh and those allied with them from the clans of Thaqif and the Ahabish gathered against him that year. Then Allah withheld the fighting between them, and He said: ﴿And it is He who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them within Mecca after He had given you victory over them﴾ [Al-Fath: 24]. And He said: ﴿And if not for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, you might have trampled them, and harm would have come upon you from them without knowledge, so that Allah would admit into His mercy whom He wills. If they had been separated, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with painful punishment﴾ [Al-Fath: 25].

* *

As for His words: ﴿But if they desist, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning: if they abandon fighting in the sanctuary and turn back to Islam and repentance, then indeed Allah [is Forgiving and Merciful], He forgives their sins, even if they had killed Muslims in the sanctuary of Allah, for no sin is too great for Him to forgive to one who repents to Him from it.

Then Allah, Exalted is He, commanded the fighting of the disbelievers: ﴿Until there is no fitnah﴾, meaning: no shirk. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Rabi', Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Suddi, and Zayd ibn Aslam.

﴿And religion is for Allah﴾, meaning: the religion of Allah becomes dominant (al-'Aali) over all other religions, as was established in the Two Sahihs from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about a man who fights out of bravery, fights out of zeal, and fights to be seen, "Which of these is in the way of Allah?" He said: "Whoever fights so that the word of Allah is supreme, he is in the way of Allah." [Sahih al-Bukhari nos. (2810, 3126) and Sahih Muslim no. (1904).] And in the Two Sahihs: "I have been commanded to fight people until they say: There is no god but Allah. When they say it, they have protected their blood and property from me, except by its right, and their reckoning is with Allah." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (25) and Sahih Muslim no. (22), from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both.]

As for His words: ﴿But if they desist, then there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers﴾, meaning: if they desist from what they are engaged in of shirk and fighting the believers, then leave them alone. Whoever fights them after that is a wrongdoer, and there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers. This is the meaning of Mujahid's statement: "One is only fought if he fights." Or its meaning may be: "If they desist, then they have been freed from wrongdoing, which is shirk, and there is no aggression against them after that." Here the word "aggression" (‘udwan) means punishment and fighting, like His words: ﴿So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 194], and His words: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it﴾ [Ash-Shura: 40], and ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the same as you were punished with﴾ [An-Nahl: 126]. For this reason 'Ikrimah and Qatadah said: The wrongdoer is the one who refused to say: There is no god but Allah.

Al-Bukhari said: His words ﴿And fight them until there is no fitnah [and religion is for Allah]﴾, the verse: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: Two men came to him during the fitnah of Ibn al-Zubayr and said: "The people have ruined things, and you are the son of 'Umar and the companion of the Prophet ﷺ. What prevents you from going out?" He said: "What prevents me is that Allah has forbidden the blood of my brother." They said: "Did Allah not say: ﴿And fight them until there is no fitnah﴾?" He said: "We fought until there was no fitnah and the religion was for Allah, but you want to fight until there is fitnah and the religion is for other than Allah." 'Uthman ibn Salih added, from Ibn Wahb, who said: Such-and-such informed me, and Haywah ibn Shurayh narrated to me, from Bakr ibn 'Amr al-Mu'afiri, that Bukayr ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to him, from Nafi', that a man came to Ibn 'Umar and said: "O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, what made you perform Hajj one year and 'Umrah the next, and abandon jihad in the way of Allah, although you know what Allah has encouraged in it?" He said: "O my nephew, Islam was built on five: faith in Allah and His Messenger, the five prayers, fasting in Ramadan, giving zakat, and pilgrimage to the House." He said: "O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, do you not hear what Allah mentioned in His Book: ﴿And if two groups of believers fight each other, then make peace between them. But if one of them oppresses the other, then fight the one that oppresses until it returns to the command of Allah﴾ [Al-Hujurat: 9], and ﴿And fight them until there is no fitnah﴾?" He said: "We did that during the time of the Prophet ﷺ when Islam was few, and a man would be tried in his religion: either they would kill him or torture him, until Islam became widespread and there was no fitnah." He said: "What then is your view about 'Ali and 'Uthman?" He said: "As for 'Uthman, Allah pardoned him, but you disliked that he be pardoned. As for 'Ali, he is the cousin of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his son-in-law," and he pointed with his hand and said: "This is his house, as you see." [Sahih al-Bukhari nos. (4513-4515).]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 194:

Ikrimah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, and al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, Miqsam, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, 'Ata' and others said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out performing 'umrah in the sixth year after the Hijrah, the polytheists prevented him from entering and reaching the House, and they barred him and those Muslims with him in Dhu al-Qa'dah, which is a sacred month, until he made a treaty with them that he would enter the following year. He entered it in the coming year, he and those Muslims who were with him, and Allah took retribution from them for it. So this verse was revealed concerning that: ﴿The sacred month for the sacred month, and violations are subject to retaliation﴾.

Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq ibn 'Isa narrated to us, Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not fight in a sacred month unless he was attacked, or they fought him; but if it came upon him, he would remain until it had passed. [[al-Musnad (3/345).]]

This is a sound chain of narration. For this reason, when the Prophet ﷺ, while camped at al-Hudaybiyah, received word that 'Uthman had been killed, and he had sent him on a message to the polytheists, he took the pledge from his companions, who numbered one thousand four hundred, under the tree, to fight the polytheists. When he learned that 'Uthman had not been killed, he refrained from that and inclined toward peace and reconciliation, and what happened happened.

Likewise, when he finished fighting the Hawazin on the day of Hunayn and their remnants took refuge in al-Ta'if, he turned toward it, besieged it, and Dhu al-Qa'dah came while he was besieging it with the catapult, and he continued against it for a full forty days, as is established in the two Sahihs from Anas. [[The hadith with this meaning is in Sahih Muslim, no. (1059).]] When many of his companions were killed, he withdrew from it without its being conquered. Then he turned back toward Makkah and performed 'umrah from al-Ji'ranah, where he divided the spoils of Hunayn. And this 'umrah of his was also in Dhu al-Qa'dah, in the year eight, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you﴾, it is a command to justice even toward the polytheists, as He said: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were afflicted﴾ [al-Nahl: 126]. And He said: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it﴾ [al-Shura: 40].

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that His saying: ﴿So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you﴾ was revealed in Makkah, where there was no power and no jihad, and then it was abrogated (naskh) by the verse of jihad in Madinah. Ibn Jarir rejected this view and said: rather, this verse is Madani, after the 'Umrat al-Qada', and he attributed that to Mujahid, may Allah have mercy on him.

Here the term "transgression" (i'tida') is applied to retaliation (iqtisas) by way of correspondence, as 'Amr ibn Umm Kulthum said:

Ala la yajhalanna ahadun 'alayna ... fanajhal fawqa jahli al-jahilina ...

Ibn Durayd said: For me there is equanimity, if my clients are equanimous ... For me there is twisting, if those who oppose me twist ...

And another said:

For me there is a steed of forbearance bridled with forbearance ... and for me there is a steed of ignorance saddled with ignorance ...

Whoever seeks to straighten me, I am straight ... and whoever seeks to bend me, I am bent ...

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And fear Allah and know that Allah is with the righteous﴾, it is a command to them to obey Allah and be mindful of Him, and an information that He, exalted is He, is with those who are mindful of Him, with support and aid in this world and the Hereafter.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 195:

Al-Bukhari said: Ishaq narrated to us, al-Nadr informed us, Shu'bah informed us, from Sulayman, who said: I heard Abu Wa'il, from Hudhayfah, regarding ﴿And spend in the way of Allah, and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction﴾, that he said: It was revealed concerning spending (in charity) [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4516.]].

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah, from Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, with the same wording. He said: It is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ata', al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan, something similar to this.

Al-Layth ibn Sa'd said, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Aslam Abu 'Imran, who said: A man from the Muhajirun (the Emigrants who came from Makkah to Madinah) charged into the enemy's line at Constantinople until he broke through it. With us was Abu Ayyub al-Ansari. People said: He has thrown himself with his own hand into destruction. Abu Ayyub said: We know best about this verse; it was revealed concerning us, the Ansar (the Helpers of Madinah). We accompanied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, witnessed the battles with him, and supported him. When Islam spread and became dominant, we, the Ansar, gathered together in private consultation and said: Allah has honoured us with the companionship of His Prophet ﷺ and with supporting him, until Islam has spread and its adherents have multiplied. We had preferred him over our families, our wealth, and our children, and now the war has laid down its burdens. So let us return to our families and children and settle among them. Then there was revealed concerning us: ﴿And spend in the way of Allah, and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction﴾. So the destruction was in remaining with our families and property and abandoning jihad.

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, 'Abd ibn Humayd in his Tafsir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh, the hafiz Abu Ya'la in his Musnad, Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak all narrated it, all from the hadith of Yazid ibn Abi Habib, with the same wording [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2512; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2972; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11029; Tafsir al-Tabari (3/590); Sahih Ibn Hibban, no. 1667 (Mawarid edition); al-Mustadrak (2/275).]].

Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan sahih gharib (a hadith rated sound and good, but with a single chain). Al-Hakim said: It meets the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), but they did not record it.

The wording of Abu Dawud from Aslam Abu 'Imran is: "We were at Constantinople, and over the people of Egypt was 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, and over the people of Syria was a man, Yazid ibn Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd. A great line of the Romans came out from the city, and we lined up against them. A man from the Muslims charged into the Romans until he entered among them. Then he came back out to us, and the people shouted at him, saying: Subhan Allah! He has thrown himself with his own hand into destruction. Abu Ayyub said: O people, you interpret this verse in a way other than its proper interpretation. It was revealed only concerning us, the company of the Ansar, when Allah made His religion mighty and its helpers increased. We said to one another: If we turn back to our wealth and tend to it, it will be set right. So Allah revealed this verse."

Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrated from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, who said: A man said to al-Bara' ibn 'Azib: If I charge alone against the enemy and they kill me, have I thrown myself with my own hand into destruction? He said: No. Allah said to His Messenger: ﴿So fight in the way of Allah; you are not burdened except with yourself﴾ [al-Nisa': 84]. This verse concerns only spending. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it, and al-Hakim recorded it in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, with the same wording, and said: Sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it [[al-Mustadrak (2/275).]]. Al-Thawri and Qays ibn al-Rabi' also narrated it from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', and mentioned it. After his words ﴿you are not burdened except with yourself﴾, al-Bara' added: But the destruction is that a man commits a sin, then throws himself with his own hand into destruction and does not repent.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Salih, the scribe of al-Layth, narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to me, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid ibn Musafir narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, that 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad ibn 'Abd Yaghuth informed him that they besieged Damascus, and a man from the tribe of Azd Shanu'ah set out and rushed alone toward the enemy to confront them. The Muslims disapproved of this and reported his action to 'Amr ibn al-'As. 'Amr sent for him and turned him back, and said: Allah says: ﴿And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction﴾.

'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And spend in the way of Allah, and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction﴾, that this does not refer to fighting; it refers only to spending: that you withhold your hand from spending in the way of Allah. And do not throw your hand into destruction.

Hammad ibn Salamah narrated from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, from al-Dahhak ibn Abi Jubayrah, who said: The Ansar used to give charity and spend from their wealth, but then a year of drought struck them, so they withheld from spending in the way of Allah, and then there was revealed: ﴿and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction﴾.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said regarding ﴿and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction﴾: It is stinginess.
