Simak ibn Harb narrated, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, regarding His words ﴿and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction﴾: that a man commits a sin and then says: I will not be forgiven. So Allah revealed: ﴿and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction, and do good; indeed Allah loves the doers of good﴾. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It is also narrated from 'Ubaydah al-Salmani, al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, and Abu Qilabah something similar; that is, similar to the saying of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir: it refers to the man who commits a sin and believes he will not be forgiven, so he throws himself with his own hand into destruction; that is, he multiplies sins and so perishes. For this reason 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "Destruction" means the punishment of Allah.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir both said together: Yunus narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Abu Sakhr informed me, from al-Qurazi, that he used to say concerning this verse: ﴿and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction﴾: The people were in the way of Allah, and a man would take provisions, and one would have better provisions than another. The needy one would spend from his provisions until nothing of his provisions remained, wishing to share with his companion. So Allah revealed: ﴿And spend in the way of Allah, and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction﴾ [[Tafsir al-Tabari (3/584).]].

Ibn Wahb also said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ayyash informed me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, regarding the word of Allah: ﴿And spend in the way of Allah, and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction﴾. The reason was that men would go out in expeditions which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent out without provision; either they would be cut off, or they would become dependents. So Allah commanded them to spend from what Allah had provided them, and not to throw their hands into destruction. The destruction is that men perish from hunger, thirst, or exhaustion from walking. And He said to those who had surplus: ﴿and do good; indeed Allah loves the doers of good﴾.

The meaning of the verse: it commands spending in the way of Allah in all the various forms of nearness to Allah and all the forms of obedience, and especially directing wealth to fighting the enemies and expending it in what makes the Muslims strong against their enemy. It also informs that abandoning this act is destruction and ruin for whoever persists in it and becomes accustomed to it. Then it links to the command of ihsan (excellence in doing good), which is the highest station of obedience, saying: ﴿and do good; indeed Allah loves the doers of good﴾.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 196 (part 1 of 3):

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the rulings of fasting and joined them with the mention of jihad, He began explaining the rites (manasik). He commanded the completion of the Hajj (pilgrimage) and the 'Umrah (lesser pilgrimage). The apparent context is that their acts should be completed once one has begun them [[In Ṭ: "فيها" (feminine, referring to the two acts)]]. Therefore He said after it: ﴿But if you are prevented﴾, meaning: if you are kept from reaching the House and are hindered from completing them. For this reason the scholars agreed that beginning the Hajj and 'Umrah is binding, whether it is said that 'Umrah is obligatory or recommended, as these are two opinions among the scholars. We have mentioned both opinions with their evidences in our book "al-Aḥkām" in full, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

Shu'bah related from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from ʿAbdullah ibn Salamah, from ʿAlī that he said concerning this verse, ﴿And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah﴾: "It is that you enter ihram (the state of consecration) from the dwelling of your family."

Likewise said Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and Ṭāwūs. And it is reported from Sufyān al-Thawrī that he said concerning this verse: "Completing them is that you enter ihram from your family, intending only the Hajj and the 'Umrah, and that you pronounce the talbiyah from the miqāt (the prescribed place of entering ihram). It is not that you go out for trade or for some need. Then, when you are near Makkah, you say: 'If only I had performed Hajj or 'Umrah.' That would suffice, but the completion is that you set out for it alone and do not set out for anything else."

Makhūl said: "Completing them is initiating both of them together from the miqāt."

ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: "It reached us that ʿUmar said concerning the words of Allah: ﴿And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah﴾: Among their completion is that you separate each of them from the other, and that you perform 'Umrah outside the months of Hajj, for Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿The Hajj is in well-known months﴾."

Hushaym related from Ibn ʿAwn, who said: "I heard al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad say: Indeed, 'Umrah during the months of Hajj is not complete." It was said to him: "What about 'Umrah in Muḥarram?" He said: "They used to consider it complete." It is similarly narrated from Qatādah ibn Diʿāmah, may Allah have mercy on them both.

This view is open to scrutiny, because it is established that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed four 'Umrahs, all of them in Dhū al-Qaʿdah: the 'Umrah of al-Ḥudaybiyah in Dhū al-Qaʿdah in the sixth year, the 'Umrah of the making-up (al-Qaḍāʾ) in Dhū al-Qaʿdah in the seventh year, the 'Umrah of al-Ji'rānah in Dhū al-Qaʿdah in the eighth year, and his 'Umrah that was with his Hajj, which he entered into together with it in Dhū al-Qaʿdah in the tenth year. He never performed 'Umrah at any other time after his migration. However, he said to Umm Hāni' [[In J, Ṭ, A: "to that woman"]] "An 'Umrah in Ramadan is equal to a Hajj with me." [[It is written here as Umm Hāni', which is an error; the correct name is Umm Sinān, and the hadith is in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, number (1863).]] That was only because she had resolved to perform Hajj with him, peace be upon him, but was prevented from it by a reason related to purity, as is explained at length in the hadith in al-Bukhārī. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr stated explicitly that this was one of her particular privileges. And Allah knows best.

Al-Suddī said concerning His words: ﴿And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah﴾: meaning, establish the Hajj and the 'Umrah.

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah related from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His words: ﴿And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah﴾, that he said: "Whoever enters ihram for Hajj or for 'Umrah is not permitted to exit the state until he completes them. The completion of the Hajj is on the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Naḥr), when he throws the Jamrat al-ʿAqabah, circumambulates the House, and performs the sa'y between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, then he has exited the state." [[In J, Ṭ, W: "and visited"]]

Qatādah related, from Zurārah, from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: "The Hajj is ʿArafah, and the 'Umrah is the circumambulation (ṭawāf)." Likewise al-Aʿmash related from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, concerning His words: ﴿And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah﴾, that he said: "In the recitation of ʿAbdullah it is: 'And establish (aqīmū) the Hajj and the 'Umrah to the House,' so that the 'Umrah does not go beyond the House." Ibrāhīm said: "I mentioned that to Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and he said: 'Thus Ibn ʿAbbās said.'"

Sufyān related from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah that he said: "Establish (aqīmū) the Hajj and the 'Umrah to the House." Likewise al-Thawrī related from Ibrāhīm, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, that he recited: "Establish the Hajj and the 'Umrah to the House."

Al-Shaʿbī recited: "Complete (wa-atammū) the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah," with the 'Umrah in the nominative case, and he said: "It is not obligatory." It is also narrated from him the opposite of that. [[In J: "Establish"]]

Many hadiths have come through multiple chains from Anas and a group of the Companions, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ combined the Hajj and the 'Umrah in one ihram. And it is established in the Ṣaḥīḥ from him that he said to his companions: "Whoever has the sacrificial animal with him, let him pronounce the talbiyah for Hajj and 'Umrah together." [[Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, number (1236), from the hadith of Asmāʾ, may Allah be pleased with her.]]

He also said in the Ṣaḥīḥ: "The 'Umrah has entered into the Hajj until the Day of Resurrection."

Imam Abū Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated a strange hadith concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse. He said: "ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn related to us: Abū ʿAbdullah al-Harawī related to us: Ghassān al-Harawī related to us: Ibrāhīm ibn Ṭahmān related to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah, that he said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ smeared with saffron, wearing a robe, and said: 'How do you command me, O Messenger of Allah, concerning my 'Umrah?' He said: Then Allah revealed: ﴿And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah﴾. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Where is the one who asked about the 'Umrah?' He said: 'Here I am.' He said to him: 'Take off your clothes, then perform ghusl, and inhale water into your nose as much as you can. Then whatever you would do in your Hajj, do it in your 'Umrah.'" [[Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, number (1218), from the hadith of Jābir, may Allah be pleased with him.]] This is a strange hadith with an unusual context. What is found in the two Ṣaḥīḥs is from Yaʿlā ibn Umayyah, in the story of the man who asked the Prophet ﷺ while he was at al-Jiʿrānah: "What is your view on a man who entered ihram for 'Umrah while wearing a robe and perfume?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was silent, then the revelation came to him. Then he raised his head and said: "Where is the questioner?" He said: "Here I am." He said: "As for the robe, take it off; and as for the perfume that is on you, wash it off; then whatever you would do in your Hajj, do it in your 'Umrah." [[Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr narrated it in al-Tamhīd (2/251) through Muḥammad ibn Sābiq, from Ibrāhīm ibn Ṭahmān, from Abū al-Zubayr, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah.]] It does not mention the ghusl or the inhalation of water, nor does it mention the revelation of the verse [[In Ṭ: "the revelation of the truth"]]. And it is from Yaʿlā ibn Umayyah, not from Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His words: ﴿But if you are prevented, then [send] what is easy of the sacrificial animal﴾, they mention that this verse was revealed in the sixth year, which was the year of al-Ḥudaybiyah, when the polytheists stood between the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and reaching the House. Allah revealed in that Sūrat al-Fatḥ in full, and He granted them a concession: that they slaughter what they had with them of the sacrificial animals, which were seventy camels, and that they exit from their ihram. Then the Prophet, peace be upon him, commanded them to shave their heads and exit the state. They did not do so, waiting for abrogation (naskh) [[Naskh: abrogation, the cancellation of a ruling by a later revealed text.]], until he went out and shaved his head. Then the people did so, though some of them shortened their hair and did not shave it. Therefore he ﷺ said: "May Allah have mercy on those who shave." They said: "And those who shorten, O Messenger of Allah?" He said a third time: "And those who shorten." [[Narrated by Muslim in his Ṣaḥīḥ, number (1301), from the hadith of ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him.]] They had shared in that sacrifice, seven in each camel, and they were fourteen hundred. Their place was al-Ḥudaybiyah, outside the Ḥaram. It was also said that they were at the edge of the Ḥaram. And Allah knows best.

For this reason the scholars differed on whether restraint (iḥṣār) is specific to the enemy, so that one exits the state only if an enemy has restrained him, and not illness or anything else? There are two opinions.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdullah ibn Yazīd al-Muqrī related to us: Sufyān related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, and from Ibn Abī Najīḥ [and Mujāhid] [[Added from J, Ṭ.]], from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: "There is no restraint except the restraint of the enemy. As for one who is afflicted by illness, pain, or going astray, there is nothing upon him. Allah, exalted is He, only said: ﴿But when you are secure﴾, and security is not restraint."

He said: "It is also narrated from Ibn ʿUmar, Ṭāwūs, al-Zuhrī, and Zayd ibn Aslam something similar to that."

The second opinion: restraint is more general than being by an enemy, illness, or going astray, which is losing one's way or the like. Imam Aḥmad said: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd related to us: Ḥajjāj ibn al-Ṣawwāf related to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from ʿIkrimah, from al-Ḥajjāj ibn ʿAmr [[In A: "ibn ʿUmar"]] al-Anṣārī, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Whoever is broken or lame has exited the state, and upon him is another Hajj.'"

He said: "I mentioned that to Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Hurayrah, and they both said: 'He spoke the truth.'"

The compilers of the four books [of Sunan] narrated it [[In J: "And it was narrated by"]] through Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, with the same chain. [[Musnad (3/450), Sunan Abī Dāwūd, number (1862), Sunan al-Tirmidhī, number (940), Sunan al-Nasāʾī (5/198), Sunan Ibn Mājah, number (3078).]] In one narration of Abū Dāwūd and Ibn Mājah: "Whoever is lame, or broken, or ill," and he mentioned its meaning. Ibn Abī Ḥātim related it from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿArafah, from Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUlayyah, from al-Ḥajjāj ibn Abī ʿUthmān al-Ṣawwāf, with the same. Then he said: "It is also narrated from Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn al-Zubayr, ʿAlqamah, Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, Mujāhid, al-Nakhaʿī, ʿAṭāʾ, and Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān, that they said: 'Restraint is by an enemy, or illness, or breaking.'"

Al-Thawrī said: "Restraint is by anything that harms him."

It is established in the two Ṣaḥīḥs from ʿĀʾishah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon Ḍubāʿah bint al-Zubayr ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, and she said: "O Messenger of Allah, I wish to perform Hajj, but I am ill." He said: "Perform Hajj and stipulate: 'My exit from the state is wherever You hold me back.'" [[Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, number (5089), and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, number (1207).]] Muslim also narrated it from Ibn ʿAbbās with the same meaning. [[Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, number (1208).]] So some of the scholars went to the validity of making such a stipulation in Hajj on the basis of this hadith. Imam Muḥammad ibn Idrīs al-Shāfiʿī made the validity of this position depend on the authenticity of this hadith. Al-Bayhaqī and other hadith masters said: "It is authentic, and to Allah belongs all praise."

* *

As for His words: ﴿then [send] what is easy of the sacrificial animal﴾: Imam Mālik related from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib that he used to say: ﴿what is easy of the sacrificial animal﴾ is a sheep. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "The sacrificial animal is from the eight pairs: from the camels, the cattle, the goats, and the sheep."

Al-Thawrī related from Ḥabīb, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His words: ﴿what is easy of the sacrificial animal﴾, that he said: "A sheep." Likewise said ʿAṭāʾ, Mujāhid, Ṭāwūs, Abū al-ʿĀliyah, Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim, al-Shaʿbī, al-Nakhaʿī, al-Ḥasan, Qatādah, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān, and others similar to that. This is the position of the four Imams.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: Abū Saʿīd al-Ashajj related to us: Abū Khālid al-Aḥmar related to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim, from ʿĀʾishah and Ibn ʿUmar, that they both did not consider what is easy of the sacrificial animal to be anything except camels and cattle.

He said: It is also narrated from Salim, al-Qasim, 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and Sa'id ibn Jubayr something similar to this.

I (Ibn Kathir) say: The apparent basis for what these scholars held is the incident of al-Hudaybiyah, for none of them is reported to have slaughtered a sheep upon his release (from ihram) on that occasion; rather, they slaughtered camels and cows. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Jabir, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to share in camels and cows, seven of us for each cow." [Sahih Muslim, no. 1318]

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: ﴿so what is feasible of the offering﴾, he said: "According to one's means."

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "If he is well-off, then from camels; otherwise from cows; otherwise from sheep."

Hisham ibn 'Urwah narrated from his father regarding ﴿so what is feasible of the offering﴾: "That applies only in the range between cheapness and scarcity."

The evidence for the correctness of the view of the majority, regarding the validity of slaughtering a sheep in the case of being prevented (ihsar), is that Allah made obligatory the slaughter of what is feasible of the offering, i.e., whatever is easily available of what is called an offering (hady). The hady is from the grazing livestock, namely camels, cows and sheep, as stated by the scholar of the sea (al-Hibr al-Bahr), the interpreter of the Qur'an and the cousin of the Messenger ﷺ. It is firmly established in the two Sahihs, on the authority of 'A'ishah, Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "The Prophet ﷺ once offered sheep as an offering."  [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1701, and Sahih Muslim, no. 1321]

* *

As for His words: ﴿And do not shave your heads until the offering reaches its place of sacrifice﴾, it is coordinated with His words: ﴿And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah﴾, and it is not coordinated with His words: ﴿But if you are prevented, then what is feasible of the offering﴾, as Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, claimed. This is because when the Prophet ﷺ and his companions in the year of al-Hudaybiyah were prevented by the disbelievers of Quraysh from entering the Haram, they shaved their heads and slaughtered their offerings outside the Haram. But in a state of security and access to the Haram, shaving is not permissible ﴿until the offering reaches its place of sacrifice﴾,

and the pilgrim completes the acts of Hajj and 'Umrah, if he is a qarin (combining both), or the acts of one of them if he is a mufrid (performing Hajj alone) or a mutamatti' (performing 'Umrah then Hajj). This is established in the two Sahihs on the authority of Hafsah, who said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the matter with the people? They have exited ihram from the 'Umrah, but you have not exited from your 'Umrah?" He said: "I have locked my hair and garlanded my offering, so I will not exit ihram until I have sacrificed." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1725, and Sahih Muslim, no. 1229]

* *

As for His words: ﴿So whoever among you is ill or has an injury of his head, then a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice﴾, al-Bukhari said: Adam narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Asbahani: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn Ma'qil say: I went back to Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah in this mosque — meaning the Mosque of Kufah — and asked him about ﴿then a ransom of fasting﴾. He said: "I was brought to the Prophet ﷺ while lice were falling from my face." He said: "I did not think the hardship had reached you to this extent! Do you not find a sheep?" I said: "No." He said: "Fast three days, or feed six poor people, half a sa' of food for each poor person, and shave your head." So it was revealed concerning me specifically, and it is general for you.  [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4517]

Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us, from Mujahid, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah, who said: The Prophet ﷺ came upon me while I was lighting a fire under a cooking pot, and lice were falling on my face — or he said: my eyebrows — and he said: "Do the vermin of your head harm you?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Then shave it, and fast three days, or feed six poor people, or offer a sacrifice (nusuk)." Ayyub said: "I do not know which of them he started with."  [Musnad (4/241)]

Ahmad also said: Hushaym narrated to us, Abu Bishr informed us, from Mujahid, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-Hudaybiyah, and we were in ihram, and the polytheists had prevented him (the enemy), and I had a full head of hair, so the vermin began to fall on my face. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by me and said: "Do the vermin of your head harm you?" So he ordered me to shave. He said: "And this verse was revealed: ﴿So whoever among you is ill or has an injury of his head, then a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice﴾."  [Musnad (4/241)]

Similarly, 'Affan narrated it from Shu'bah, from Abu Bishr, who is Ja'far ibn Iyas, with the same chain. And from Shu'bah, from al-Hakam, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, with the same.  [Ahmad in al-Musnad, as in Ibn Hajar's Atraf (5/219)] And from Shu'bah, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, from Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah, something similar.

Malik narrated it from Humayd ibn Qays, from Mujahid, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah, and mentioned something similar.  [Muwatta' (1/417)]

Sa'd ibn Ishaq ibn Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah narrated from Aban ibn Salih, from al-Hasan al-Basri, that he heard Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah say: "So I slaughtered a sheep." Ibn Mardawayh narrated it. It is also narrated from the hadith of 'Umar ibn Qays, Sandal — and he is weak — from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The sacrifice is a sheep, the fasting is three days, and the feeding is between six (persons)."  [Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (1/515), attributing it to Ibn Mardawayh and al-Wahidi.]

Similarly it is reported from 'Ali, Muhammad ibn Ka'b, 'Ikrimah, Ibrahim [al-Nakha'i], Mujahid, 'Ata', al-Suddi, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la informed us, 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb informed us: that Malik ibn Anas narrated to him, from 'Abd al-Karim ibn Malik al-Jazari, from Mujahid, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah: that he was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and lice harmed him in his head, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered him to shave his head, and said: "Fast three days, or feed six poor people, two mudd for each person, or sacrifice a sheep; whichever of these you do, it suffices you."  [The hadith in al-Muwatta' (1/417)]

Likewise, Layth ibn Abi Sulaym narrated from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿then a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice﴾, he said: "When it is 'aw (or), whichever you take suffices you."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It is also narrated from Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, 'Ata', Tawus, al-Hasan, Humayd al-A'raj, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and al-Dahhak, something similar.

I (Ibn Kathir) say: This is the position of the Four Imams and the general body of scholars: that one is given the choice in this situation. If he wishes, he fasts; if he wishes, he gives charity of a faraq, which is three a'sa', half a sa' for each poor person, which is two mudd; and if he wishes, he slaughters a sheep and gives it to the poor. Whichever he does suffices him. And since the wording of the Qur'an, in stating the concession, came with the easiest then the easier: ﴿then a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice﴾. And when the Prophet ﷺ commanded Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah with this, he guided him to the best then the better, and said: "Sacrifice a sheep, or feed six poor people, or fast three days." Each is good in its place. And to Allah belong praise and grace.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, who said: al-A'mash mentioned: Ibrahim asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about this verse: ﴿then a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice﴾, and he answered him saying: "A food is imposed upon him. If he has it, he buys a sheep; if not, the sheep is valued in dirhams, and food is substituted for it, and he gives it in charity; otherwise he fasts a day for each half sa'." Ibrahim said: "Thus I heard 'Alqamah mention." He said: "When Sa'id ibn Jubayr said to me: 'Who is this? How witty he is!' I said: 'This is Ibrahim.' He said: 'How witty he is! He used to sit with us.'" He said: "I mentioned that to Ibrahim, and when I said: 'He used to sit with us,' he shook (with the words)."  [Tafsir al-Tabari (4/74)]

Ibn Jarir also said: Ibn Abi 'Imran narrated to us, 'Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, from his father, from Ash'ath, from al-Hasan regarding His words: ﴿then a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice﴾, he said: "If the muhrim has an injury to his head, he shaves and pays a ransom with whichever of these three he wishes: fasting is ten days, charity is to ten poor people, each poor person receiving two makkuk — a makkuk of dates and a makkuk of wheat — and the sacrifice is a sheep."

Qatadah, from al-Hasan and 'Ikrimah, regarding His words: ﴿then a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice﴾, said: "It is feeding ten poor people."

These two statements from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Alqamah, al-Hasan and 'Ikrimah are strange views and are open to scrutiny, because the Sunnah has been established in the hadith of Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah for fasting three days, not ten, nor six, or feeding six poor people, or a sheep as a sacrifice, and that this is by choice, as the context of the Qur'an indicates. As for this ordering, it is known only in the case of killing game, as the text of the Qur'an states, and the jurists there agreed upon it, unlike this. And Allah knows best.

Hushaym said: Layth informed us, from Tawus, that he used to say: "Whatever is of blood or food is in Makkah, and whatever is of fasting is wherever one wishes." Similarly said 'Ata', Mujahid and al-Hasan.

Hushaym said: Hajjaj, 'Abd al-Malik and others informed us, from 'Ata', that he used to say: "Whatever is of blood is in Makkah, and whatever is of food or fasting is wherever one wishes."

Hushaym said: Yahya ibn Sa'id informed us, from Ya'qub ibn Khalid, Abu Asma', mawla of Ibn Ja'far, informed us, who said: 'Uthman ibn 'Affan performed Hajj, and with him were 'Ali and al-Husayn ibn 'Ali. 'Uthman set out (ritual departure). Abu Asma' said: I was with Ibn Ja'far, and suddenly we came upon a man sleeping with his camel at his head. I said: "O sleeper!" He woke up, and it was al-Husayn ibn 'Ali. Ibn Ja'far carried him until we brought him to al-Suqya. He said: 'Ali sent for (physicians), and Asma' bint 'Umays was with him. We treated him for about twenty nights. 'Ali said to al-Husayn: "What do you feel?" He pointed with his hand to his head. 'Ali ordered him to be shaved, then called for a camel and slaughtered it. If this camel was for the shaving, then it shows that he slaughtered it outside Makkah. And if it was for exiting ihram, then it is clear.

* *

As for His words: ﴿So when you are secure, whoever performs 'Umrah then Hajj, then what is feasible of the offering﴾, meaning: when you are able to perform the rites, then whoever among you is a mutamatti' by 'Umrah then Hajj — and this includes one who entered ihram for both together, or who entered ihram for 'Umrah first and, when he finished it, entered ihram for Hajj. This is the specific tamattu', and it is what is known in the language of the jurists. The general tamattu' includes both types, as the authentic hadiths indicate, for some narrators say: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed tamattu'," and another says: "He performed qiran." And there is no disagreement that he brought the offering (hady) with him.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 196 (part 3 of 3):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Whoever performs the tamattu' (enjoyment) by combining the 'umrah with the hajj, let him give whatever sacrificial animal (hady) is feasible.﴾ That is, he should slaughter whatever sacrificial animal he is able to, and the least of it is a sheep, and he may slaughter a cow, because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ slaughtered a cow on behalf of his wives. Al-Awza'i said, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah [[In H: "Abu Muslim", and the correct version is what we have recorded from J and A.]], from Abu Hurayrah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ slaughtered a cow on behalf of his wives, and they were performing tamattu'. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated it [[Abu Dawud also narrated it in his Sunan, no. (1751), through al-Walid, from al-Awza'i with this chain.]].

In this is evidence for the legitimacy (shar'iyyah) of tamattu', as came in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) from 'Imran ibn Husayn, who said: The verse of tamattu' (mut'ah) was revealed in the Book of Allah, and we performed it with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then no Qur'an was revealed prohibiting it, and he did not forbid it until he died. [Then] a man said his opinion whatever he wished [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4518), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1226).]]. Al-Bukhari said: It is said that he was 'Umar. What al-Bukhari said has come explicitly: that 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to forbid people from tamattu' and say: "If we follow the Book of Allah, then indeed Allah commands completion (tamam)." He meant His saying: ﴿And complete the hajj and the 'umrah for Allah﴾. In reality, 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, did not forbid it as one who declares it unlawful; he only forbade it so that people's pilgrimage and 'umrah visits to the House would increase, as he himself stated, may Allah be pleased with him.

* *

His saying: ﴿So whoever cannot find [an animal], then fasting three days during the hajj and seven when you return; those are ten complete.﴾ Allah the Exalted says: whoever does not find a sacrificial animal, let him fast three days during the hajj, that is, during the days of the rites. The scholars said: The preferable time is to fast them before the Day of 'Arafah, within the first ten days (of Dhu al-Hijjah), as said by 'Ata'. Or from the time he enters the state of ihram, as said by Ibn 'Abbas and others, based on His saying: ﴿during the hajj﴾. Among them are those who permit fasting them from the beginning of Shawwal, as said by Tawus, Mujahid and others. Al-Sha'bi permitted fasting the Day of 'Arafah and the two days before it, and Mujahid said likewise, as did Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Suddi, 'Ata', Tawus, al-Hakam, al-Hasan, Hammad, Ibrahim, Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, al-Rabi' and Muqatil ibn Hayyan. Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: If he does not find a sacrificial animal, then upon him is fasting three days during the hajj before the Day of 'Arafah; when the third day, the Day of 'Arafah, comes, his fasting is complete; and seven when he returns to his family. Likewise Abu Ishaq narrated from Wabarah, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: He fasts one day before the Day of Tarwiyah, the Day of Tarwiyah, and the Day of 'Arafah. Likewise it was narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from 'Ali as well.

If he did not fast them, or some of them, before the day of the 'Id, is it permissible for him to fast them during the Days of Tashriq? On this there are two opinions of the scholars, and both are also attributed to Imam al-Shafi'i. The older of the two is that it is permissible for him to fast them, based on the saying of 'A'ishah and Ibn 'Umar in Sahih al-Bukhari: "He was not granted permission to fast during the Days of Tashriq except for one who cannot find a sacrificial animal" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (1997).]]. Likewise Malik narrated it from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, and from Salim, from Ibn 'Umar [They said this only because of the generality of His saying: ﴿three days during the hajj and seven﴾] [[Added from J, A.]]. [[Al-Muwatta': (1/426).]] It has been narrated through more than one chain from both of them. Sufyan narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from 'Ali that he used to say: Whoever misses fasting the three days during the hajj, let him fast them during the Days of Tashriq. This is also the view of 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr al-Laythi, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan al-Basri and 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr; and they said this only because of the generality of His saying: ﴿So fasting three days during the hajj﴾. The newer of the two opinions is that it is not permissible to fast them on the Days of Tashriq, because of what Muslim narrated from Nubaishah al-Hudhali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The Days of Tashriq are days of eating, drinking, and remembrance of Allah" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1141).]].

* *

His saying: ﴿and seven when you return﴾ has two opinions:
The first: when you return on the road. For this reason Mujahid said: it is a concession; if he wishes, he fasts them on the road. Likewise 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said.
The second opinion: when you return to your homelands. 'Abd al-Razzaq said: al-Thawri informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Salim, I heard Ibn 'Umar say: ﴿So whoever cannot find [an animal], then fasting three days during the hajj and seven when you return﴾ — he said: when he returns to his family. Likewise it was narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, 'Ata', 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Zuhri and al-Rabi' ibn Anas. Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir related a consensus (ijma') on this.

Al-Bukhari said: Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to us, from 'Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim ibn 'Abd Allah that Ibn 'Umar said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed tamattu' in the Farewell Hajj, combining the 'umrah with the hajj, and he brought a sacrificial animal, driving it with him from Dhu al-Hulayfah; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began by entering ihram for 'umrah, then entered ihram for hajj, and the people performed tamattu' with the Prophet ﷺ, combining the 'umrah with the hajj. Among the people were those who brought sacrificial animals and drove them, and among them were those who did not bring them. When the Prophet ﷺ arrived in Makkah, he said to the people: "Whoever among you has brought a sacrificial animal, he may not lawfully take anything that was forbidden to him until he completes his hajj. Whoever among you has not brought a sacrificial animal, let him circumambulate the House and (perform the sa'y) between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and let him shorten (his hair) and exit the state of ihram, then enter ihram for hajj. Whoever does not find a sacrificial animal, let him fast three days during the hajj and seven when he returns to his family." He mentioned the rest of the hadith [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (1691).]].

Al-Zuhri said: 'Urwah informed me, from 'A'ishah, the same as Salim informed me from his father. The hadith is recorded in the two Sahihs through al-Zuhri with this chain [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (1692), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1228).]].

* *

His saying: ﴿those are ten complete﴾ it was said: it is an emphasis, as the Arabs say: "I saw with my own eye, I heard with my own ear, and I wrote with my own hand." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿nor a bird that flies with its two wings﴾ [al-An'am: 38], and He said: ﴿nor do you write it with your right hand﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 48], and He said: ﴿And We appointed for Moses thirty nights and completed them with ten, so the appointed time of his Lord was complete forty nights﴾ [al-A'raf: 142].

It was also said: the meaning of ﴿complete﴾ is the command to complete and perfect them, chosen by Ibn Jarir. And it was said: the meaning of ﴿complete﴾ is that they suffice in place of the sacrificial animal. Hushaym narrated from 'Abbad ibn Rashid, from al-Hasan al-Basri, regarding His saying: ﴿those are ten complete﴾, he said: "in place of the sacrificial animal."

* *

His saying: ﴿That is for one whose family is not present at the Sacred Mosque﴾. Ibn Jarir said: The people of interpretation differed concerning whom is meant by His saying: ﴿for one whose family is not present at the Sacred Mosque﴾, after all of them agreed that the people of the Haram are meant by it and that they have no tamattu'. Some of them said: it refers specifically to the people of the Haram, to the exclusion of others.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us — that is al-Thawri — who said: Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid said: they are the people of the Haram. Likewise Ibn al-Mubarak narrated from al-Thawri, and added: "the community agrees on this."

Qatadah said: It was mentioned to us that Ibn 'Abbas used to say: "O people of Makkah, you have no tamattu'. It was made lawful for the people of the outlying regions and forbidden to you. Indeed one of you crosses a valley — or he said: places a valley between himself and the Haram — then enters ihram for 'umrah."

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, who said: The tamattu' is for the people — not for the people of Makkah — whose family is not from the Haram. That is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿That is for one whose family is not present at the Sacred Mosque﴾. He said: and it reached me from Ibn 'Abbas a statement like Tawus's.

Others said: they are the people of the Haram and those between it and the miqat (boundary points), as 'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from a man, from 'Ata', who said: whoever's family is within the miqat is like the people of Makkah; he does not perform tamattu'.

'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak said, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir, from Makhul, regarding His saying: ﴿That is for one whose family is not present at the Sacred Mosque﴾, he said: whoever is within the miqat.

Ibn Jurayj said, from 'Ata': ﴿That is for one whose family is not present at the Sacred Mosque﴾, he said: 'Arafah, Marr, 'Urnah, Dajnan and al-Raji' [[In W: "al-Dajee'".]].

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, I heard al-Zuhri say: whoever's family is a day's journey or near it may perform tamattu'. In another narration from him: a day or two days.

Ibn Jarir chose, in this matter, the view of al-Shafi'i that they are the people of the Haram, and whoever is at a distance from it where prayer is not shortened; because whoever is like that is considered present, not a traveller. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿And fear Allah﴾, that is, in what He has commanded you and what He has forbidden you, ﴿and know that Allah is severe in punishment﴾, that is, for whoever opposes His command and commits what He has forbidden.

The grammarians disagreed about His words, ﴿The Hajj is in well-known months﴾. Some of them said: [its implied meaning is] [[Addition from manuscripts ج, أ, و.]] "The Hajj is the Hajj of well-known months." On this reading, beginning the ihram for Hajj during those months is more complete than beginning it at other times, although that other ihram is also valid. The view that the ihram for Hajj is valid at any time of the year is the position of Malik, Abu Hanifah, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Thawri, and al-Layth ibn Sa'd also held it. They argued from His words, ﴿They ask you about the new moons. Say: They are timings for the people and for the Hajj﴾ [al-Baqarah: 189], and because Hajj is one of the two rites of pilgrimage ('umrah being the other), so beginning its ihram at any time of the year is valid, just like 'umrah.

Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, held that the ihram for Hajj is not valid except in its months. So if one begins Hajj ihram before them, it is not concluded. As for whether it becomes 'umrah, there are two opinions from him. The view that the ihram for Hajj is valid only in its months is related from Ibn 'Abbas and Jabir, and Ata', Tawus, and Mujahid also said it, may Allah have mercy on them all. The evidence for it is His words, ﴿The Hajj is in well-known months﴾. Its apparent meaning is the other reading that the grammarians adopted, namely that "the time of Hajj is well-known months," so the months are specified from among all the other months of the year. This indicates that it is not valid before them, like the prescribed times of prayer.

Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Muslim ibn Khalid informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Umar ibn 'Ata' informed me, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: "It is not right for anyone to begin ihram for Hajj except in the months of Hajj, because of Allah's words, ﴿The Hajj is in well-known months﴾." Ibn Abi Hatim also related it in the same way, from Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Malik al-Susi, from Hajjaj ibn Muhammad al-A'war, from Ibn Jurayj, with the same chain. Ibn Mardawayh related it in his tafsir by two routes, from Hajjaj ibn Arta'ah, from al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah [[In manuscripts أ and و: "ibn 'Uyaynah."]], from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: "It is from the Sunnah that one should not begin ihram for Hajj except in the months of Hajj."

Ibn Khuzaymah said in his Sahih: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "One should not begin ihram for Hajj except in the months of Hajj, for it is part of the Sunnah of Hajj that one begins ihram for it in its months." [[Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah, no. (2596).]] This is a sound chain. A companion's statement, "It is from the Sunnah," has the status of a marfu' report according to most scholars, especially when it is Ibn 'Abbas's statement as an interpretation of the Qur'an, and he is its interpreter (tarjuman).

A marfu' hadith has also come on this matter. Ibn Mardawayh said: 'Abd al-Baqi ibn Qani' narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "It is not right for anyone to begin ihram for Hajj except in the months of Hajj."

Its chain is acceptable. However, al-Shafi'i and al-Bayhaqi related it through several routes from Ibn Jurayj, from Abu al-Zubayr, that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah being asked: "Does one begin ihram for Hajj before the months of Hajj?" He said: "No." [[Al-Umm of al-Shafi'i (2/136) and al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Bayhaqi (4/343).]]

This statement attributed to Jabir (mawquf) is more sound and more firmly established than the marfu' report. In that case, what remains is the view of a companion, which is strengthened by Ibn 'Abbas's statement: "It is from the Sunnah that one should not begin ihram for Hajj except in its months." And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His words, ﴿well-known months﴾, al-Bukhari said: Ibn 'Umar said: "They are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and the first ten [days] of Dhu al-Hijjah." [[Sahih al-Bukhari (3/419), Fath.]] What al-Bukhari reported from him in the form of a firm assertion (ta'liq bi-sighat al-jazm) was related by Ibn Jarir with a connected chain: Ahmad ibn Hazim ibn Abi Gharzah [[In manuscript ج: "ibn Abi 'Azrah."]] narrated to us, Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Warqa' narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Umar, regarding ﴿The Hajj is in well-known months﴾: "Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and ten [days] of Dhu al-Hijjah." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (4/116).]]

This chain is sound. Al-Hakim also related it in his Mustadrak, from al-Asamm, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn 'Affan, from 'Abd Allah ibn Numayr, from 'Ubayd Allah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, and he mentioned it and said: "It meets the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim)." [[Al-Mustadrak (2/276).]] [[In manuscripts هـ and أ: "'Abd Allah," but the correct reading is what we have recorded from ج, ط, و.]]

I say: This view is also related from 'Umar, 'Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, Ibn 'Abbas, Ata', Tawus, Mujahid, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Makhul, Qatadah, al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan. It is also the position of al-Shafi'i, Abu Hanifah, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Abu Yusuf, and Abu Thawr, may Allah have mercy on them all. Ibn Jarir chose this view and said: "It is valid to apply the plural to two months and part of a third, by way of predominance (taghlib), just as the Arabs say: 'I visited him this year' and 'I saw him today,' when that happened only in part of the year or part of the day." Allah says, ﴿Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him﴾ [al-Baqarah: 203], though he hastened only in a day and a half.

Imam Malik ibn Anas [and al-Shafi'i in his old view (al-qadim)] [[Addition from manuscripts ج, ط, أ, و.]] said: They are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and all of Dhu al-Hijjah. This is also a report from Ibn 'Umar. Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and Dhu al-Hijjah."

Ibn Abi Hatim said in his tafsir: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed me, who said: I asked Nafi': "Did you hear 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar name the months of Hajj?" He said: "Yes. 'Abd Allah used to name them: 'Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and Dhu al-Hijjah.'" Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Shihab, Ata', and Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, the Companion of the Prophet (ﷺ), also said the same. This chain to Ibn Jurayj is sound. This view has also been related from Tawus, Mujahid, 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and Qatadah. A marfu' hadith has also come on this, but it is fabricated (mawdu'). It was related by the hafiz Ibn Mardawayh, through Husayn ibn Mukhariq, who is accused of fabricating hadith, from Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Hajj is in well-known months: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and Dhu al-Hijjah." [[Also related by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. (1693), Majma' al-Bahrayn, through Muhammad ibn Thawwab, from Husayn ibn Mukhariq, with the same chain.]]

As you have seen, this report does not have a sound attribution to the Prophet (ﷺ). And Allah knows best.

The practical consequence of Malik's view is that the months extend to the end of Dhu al-Hijjah, in the sense that they are specific to Hajj. Thus 'umrah is disliked in the rest of Dhu al-Hijjah. It does not mean that Hajj is valid after the night of sacrifice (laylat al-nahr).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab, who said: 'Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud) said: "Hajj is in well-known months, in which there is no 'umrah." This is a sound chain.

Ibn Jarir said: Those who held that the months of Hajj are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and Dhu al-Hijjah only meant that these months are not the months of 'umrah. They are for Hajj, even though the rites of Hajj end with the end of the days of Mina. As Muhammad ibn Sirin said: "None of the people of knowledge doubts that 'umrah outside the months of Hajj is more excellent than 'umrah within the months of Hajj."

Ibn 'Awn said: I asked al-Qasim ibn Muhammad about 'umrah in the months of Hajj, and he said: "They did not consider it complete."

I say: It is established from 'Umar and 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with them both, that they used to encourage 'umrah outside the months of Hajj and forbade it during the months of Hajj. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His words, ﴿Whoever undertakes Hajj therein﴾, meaning: whoever makes Hajj obligatory upon himself by entering ihram for it. This indicates that one must maintain the ihram for Hajj and continue with it. Ibn Jarir said: They agreed that the meaning of "obligation" (fard) here is requirement and binding upon oneself.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿Whoever undertakes Hajj therein﴾: "He means: whoever enters ihram for Hajj or 'umrah." Ata' said: "Fard is ihram." Ibrahim, al-Dahhak, and others said the same.

Ibn Jurayj said: 'Umar ibn 'Ata' informed me, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding ﴿Whoever undertakes Hajj therein﴾: "One should not pronounce the talbiyah for Hajj and then stay in a land [without going on]." Ibn Abi Hatim said: The same was related from Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn al-Zubayr, Mujahid, Ata', Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, Sufyan al-Thawri, al-Zuhri, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan, something similar to that.

Tawus and al-Qasim ibn Muhammad said: "It is the talbiyah."

* *

As for His words, ﴿there shall be no obscenity﴾, meaning: whoever has entered ihram for Hajj or 'umrah must avoid obscenity (rafath), which is sexual intercourse, as Allah said: ﴿It is made lawful for you on the night of fasting to go in unto your wives﴾ [al-Baqarah: 187]. Likewise, it is forbidden to engage in its preliminaries, such as touching and kissing and the like, and also to speak of it in the presence of women.

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to me. Ibn Wahb informed us, Yunus informed me, that Nafi' informed him that 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar used to say: "Rafath is having sexual relations with women. Speaking about it means that men and women mention it with their mouths."

Ibn Wahb said: Abu Sakhr also informed me, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, with the same meaning.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from a man, from Abu al-'Aliyah al-Riyahi, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he used to drive the camels chanting while he was in ihram, and he would say:

"And they walk with us in whispers... if the bird speaks truly, we will attain the beauty."

Abu al-'Aliyah said: "I said: 'Do you speak of rafath while you are in ihram?' He said: 'Rafath is only what is said in the presence of women.'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (4/126).]]

It was also related by al-A'mash, from Ziyad ibn Husayn, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ibn 'Abbas, and he mentioned it.

Ibn Jarir also said: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from 'Awn, [he said]: Ziyad ibn Husayn narrated to me, my father Husayn ibn Qays narrated to me, who said: "I accompanied Ibn 'Abbas on the Hajj, and I was his close friend. When we had entered ihram, Ibn 'Abbas took hold of the tail of his camel and began to twist it, reciting rajaz and saying:

'And they walk with us in whispers... if the bird speaks truly, we will attain the beauty.'"

He said: "I said: 'Do you engage in rafath while you are in ihram?' He said: 'Rafath is only what is said in the presence of women.'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (4/126).]]

'Abd Allah ibn Tawus related from his father: "I asked Ibn 'Abbas about the words of Allah, ﴿there shall be no obscenity nor wickedness﴾." He said: "Rafath is alluding to sexual intercourse by hinting at it (al-ta'ridh), and it is called al-'arabah in the speech of the Arabs, and that is the least degree of rafath."

Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: "Rafath is intercourse and what falls short of it, such as obscene speech." Amr ibn Dinar said the same. Ata' also said: "They disliked al-'arabah, which is alluding to intercourse, while one is in ihram."

Tawus said: "It is that you say to a woman: 'When you exit the state of ihram, I will have you.'" Abu al-'Aliyah said the same.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: "Ar-rafath (obscenity, sexual misconduct) means having intercourse with women, kissing, fondling, and making suggestive remarks to them with obscene speech, and the like."[[In C: "yu'arrid laha bil-fuhsha'" ("making lewd remarks to her").]]

Ibn Abbas and Ibn Umar also said: "Ar-rafath means having intercourse with women." Likewise said Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Ibrahim (al-Nakha'i), Abu al-Aliyah, Ata, Makhul, Ata ibn Yasar, Atiyyah, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Rabi', al-Zuhri, al-Suddi, Malik ibn Anas, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Abd al-Karim ibn Malik, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and others.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿And there is no wickedness﴾, Miqsam and others narrated from Ibn Abbas that it means sins (al-ma'asi). Likewise said Ata, Mujahid, Tawus, Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Muhammad ibn Ka'b, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Zuhri, Makhul, Ibn Aban, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Ata ibn Yasar, Ata al-Khurasani, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: "Al-fusuq is whatever is committed of the disobedience of Allah through hunting game or otherwise." Similarly, Ibn Wahb narrated from Yunus, from Nafi', that Abdullah ibn Umar used to say: "Al-fusuq is committing acts of disobedience to Allah within the sacred precinct (al-haram)."

Others said: "Al-fusuq here is cursing (al-sibab)." This was said by Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, Ibn al-Zubayr, Mujahid, al-Suddi, Ibrahim, and al-Hasan. Those who hold this view may rely on what is established in the Sahih: "Insulting a Muslim is fusuq, and fighting him is kufr."

For this reason, the great scholar Abu Muhammad ibn Abi Hatim, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated it here from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri, from Yazid,[[In A: "from Zayd"; in W: "from Zubayd".]] from Abu Wa'il, from Abdullah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Insulting a Muslim is fusuq, and fighting him is kufr."[[Al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (6044), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (63), via the route of Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir from Abu Wa'il with the same wording.]] It has also been narrated from the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, from his father,[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (2634), and al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (7/122).]] and from the hadith of Abu Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Sa'd, from his father.[[Narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan, no. (3941).]]

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "Al-fusuq here is slaughtering for idols." Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿or a sacrifice dedicated to other than Allah﴾ [Al-An'am: 145].

Al-Dahhak said: "Al-fusuq is mutual insulting by nicknames."

Those who said that al-fusuq here means all sins are upheld by correctness, just as Allah forbade wrongdoing in the sacred months, though it is forbidden throughout the year; but in the sacred months it is more emphatic. For this reason He said: ﴿Of them, four are sacred. That is the upright religion, so do not wrong yourselves therein﴾ [At-Tawbah: 36], and He said regarding the sacred precinct: ﴿And whoever intends therein deviation by wrongdoing – We will make him taste a painful punishment﴾ [Al-Hajj: 25].

Ibn Jarir chose that al-fusuq here means committing what is forbidden during the state of ihram (the sacred state of pilgrimage), such as killing game, shaving the hair, cutting the nails, and the like, as was previously mentioned from Ibn Umar. What we have mentioned is more preferable, and Allah knows best. It is established in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever performs this House's pilgrimage and does not commit rafath or fusuq will return from his sins as on the day his mother bore him."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (1521), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1350).]]

* *

As for His saying, ﴿nor is there disputing during the pilgrimage﴾, there are two views:

The first: there is to be no arguing regarding the time of the pilgrimage or its rites. Allah has explained this in the most complete explanation and clarified it in the most perfect manner. As Waki' narrated from al-Ala' ibn Abd al-Karim: I heard Mujahid say: "Regarding ﴿nor is there disputing during the pilgrimage﴾: Allah has explained the months of Hajj, so there is no disputing among people about it."

Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid: "﴿nor is there disputing during the pilgrimage﴾ – he said: There is no postponing of a month (nasi'), and no disputing during the pilgrimage, now that it has been made clear." Then he mentioned the manner in which the polytheists used to perform the nasi' (intercalation) for which Allah censured them.

Al-Thawri narrated from Abd al-Aziz ibn Rufay', from Mujahid regarding His saying, ﴿nor is there disputing during the pilgrimage﴾: "The pilgrimage has been set in order, so there is no disputing in it." Al-Suddi said likewise.

Hushaym said: Hajjaj informed us, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿nor is there disputing during the pilgrimage﴾: "Al-mira' (contention) during the pilgrimage."

Abdullah ibn Wahb said: Malik said: Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿nor is there disputing during the pilgrimage﴾. The disputing during the pilgrimage – and Allah knows best – is that the Quraysh used to stand at the sacred landmark (al-mash'ar al-haram) at Muzdalifah, while the Arabs and others would stand at Arafat. They would argue, saying: "We are more correct," and the others would say: "We are more correct." This is what we think, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Wahb narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam: "They would stand at various positions, disputing, each claiming that his position was the position of Ibrahim. So Allah ended it when He informed His Prophet about the rites."

Ibn Wahb narrated from Abu Sakhr, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: "When the Quraysh gathered at Mina, one group would say: 'Our pilgrimage is more complete than your pilgrimage,' and the other would say: 'Our pilgrimage is more complete than yours.'"

Hammad ibn Salamah narrated from Jabr[[In J: "from Husayn"; in A: "from Jubayr".]] ibn Habib, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, that he said: "Disputing during the pilgrimage is for one of them to say: 'The pilgrimage is tomorrow,' and another to say: 'Today.'"

Ibn Jarir chose the substance of these views, which is ending disagreement regarding the rites of the pilgrimage.

The second view: the intended meaning of disputing here is quarreling (al-khusumah).

Ibn Jarir said: Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan narrated to us, Ishaq narrated to us, from Sharik, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abdullah – that is Ibn Mas'ud – regarding His saying, ﴿nor is there disputing during the pilgrimage﴾: "That you argue with your companion until you anger him."

With this chain to Abu Ishaq, from al-Taymi: "I asked Ibn Abbas about 'al-jidal' (disputing)." He said: "Al-mira' (contention): you argue with your companion until you anger him." Likewise narrated Miqsam and al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas. Likewise said Abu al-Aliyah, Ata, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ikrimah, Jabir ibn Zayd, Ata al-Khurasani, Makhul, Amr ibn Dinar, al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Ata ibn Yasar, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Zuhri, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: "﴿nor is there disputing during the pilgrimage﴾: al-jidal is al-mira' and al-mulahah (wrangling), until you anger your brother and companion, so Allah forbade that."

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: "﴿nor is there disputing during the pilgrimage﴾: they used to dislike disputing." Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: "Al-jidal is cursing (al-sibab) and quarreling (al-munazarah)." Ibn Wahb likewise narrated from Yunus, from Nafi', that Ibn Umar used to say: "Disputing during the pilgrimage is cursing, contention, and disputes."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was narrated from Ibn al-Zubayr, al-Hasan, Ibrahim, Tawus, and Muhammad ibn Ka'b that they said: "Al-jidal is al-mira'."

Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated from Yahya ibn Bishr[[In A: "ibn Bashir".]] from Ikrimah: "﴿nor is there disputing during the pilgrimage﴾. Al-jidal is anger: that you make a Muslim angry with you, unless you are asking a slave to make amends, and you anger him without striking him; then there is no harm upon you, if Allah wills."

I say: If he struck him, it would be permissible and acceptable. The evidence for this is what Imam Ahmad narrated: Abdullah ibn Idris narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abbad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, that Asma' bint Abi Bakr said: "We set out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as pilgrims, until when we were at al-Araj, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) dismounted. Aisha sat beside the Messenger of Allah, and I sat beside my father. The baggage of Abu Bakr and the baggage of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was one, with the servant of Abu Bakr. Abu Bakr sat waiting for him until he would appear, but he appeared without his camel. Abu Bakr said: 'Where is your camel?' He said: 'I lost it last night.' Abu Bakr said: 'One camel and you lost it?' So he began to strike him, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) smiled and said: 'Look at this muhrim (one in the state of ihram), what is he doing?'"

Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah likewise narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Ishaq.[[Al-Musnad (6/344), Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (1818), and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (2933).]] From this hadith, some have related from some of the early scholars that he said: "Striking the camels is part of completing the pilgrimage." However, from the statement of the Prophet (ﷺ) about Abu Bakr, "Look at this muhrim, what is he doing?" – in the manner of a gentle disapproval – it is derived that the better course is to avoid that, and Allah knows best.

Imam Abd ibn Humayd said in his Musnad: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Musa ibn Ubaydah, from his brother Abdullah ibn Ubaydah, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever completes his rites and the Muslims are safe from his tongue and his hand, his previous sin will be forgiven."[[Al-Muntakhab of Abd ibn Humayd, no. (1148); Musa ibn Ubaydah is weak.]]

* *

As for His saying, ﴿And whatever good you do, Allah knows it﴾: when He forbade them from committing ugly acts, in speech and in deed, He urged them to do what is good, and informed them that He knows it, and that He will reward them for it with the fullest reward on the Day of Resurrection.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿And take provision, for the best provision is taqwa (God-consciousness)﴾: Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas: "There were people who would leave their families without provisions, saying: 'We will perform the pilgrimage to the House of Allah, and He will not feed us.' So Allah said: 'Take provision, which will keep your faces from people.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Muqri narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ikrimah, who said: "Some people used to perform the pilgrimage without provisions, so Allah revealed: ﴿And take provision, for the best provision is taqwa﴾."

Likewise Ibn Jarir narrated it from Amr – who is al-Fallas – from Ibn Uyaynah.[[In J: "and he is Ibn al-Ala'"; in A: "Abu al-Fallas".]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: This hadith was also narrated by Warqa', from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas. He said: "What is narrated from Ibn Uyaynah is more authentic (asahh)."

I say: al-Nasa'i narrated it from Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Makhzumi, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas [who said]:[[Addition from J.]] "Some people used to perform the pilgrimage without provisions, so Allah revealed: ﴿And take provision, for the best provision is taqwa﴾."[[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11033).]] As for the hadith of Warqa', al-Bukhari narrated it from Yahya ibn Bishr, from Shababah.[[In T: "Yahya ibn Bishr narrated to us"; in A: "from Ibn Bashir, Naba' (informed us), from Shababah"; in T: "Shababah said".]] Abu Dawud narrated it from Abu Mas'ud Ahmad ibn al-Furat al-Razi and Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Mukhrami, from Shababah, from Warqa', from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The people of Yemen used to perform the pilgrimage without taking provisions, and they would say: 'We are the reliant ones (al-mutawakkilun).' So Allah revealed: ﴿And take provision, for the best provision is taqwa﴾."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (1523), and Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (1730).]]

He also related it in his Tafsir, from Shababah [with it]. Ibn Hibban related it in his Sahih from the hadith of Shababah, with it.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh related from the hadith of Amr ibn Abd al-Ghaffar [from Muhammad ibn Suqah], from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: "When they entered the state of ihram, they would have their provisions with them, and they would throw them away and take other provisions." So Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And take provisions, for the best provision is piety﴾, and they were forbidden from that and commanded to take dried bread (al-ka'k), flour, and roasted barley flour (sawiq). Likewise said Ibn al-Zubayr, Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, Ikrimah, al-Sha'bi, al-Nakha'i, Salim ibn Abd Allah, Ata al-Khurasani, Qatadah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "So take provisions of flour, roasted barley flour, and al-ka'k." Waki' [ibn al-Jarrah] said in his Tafsir: Sufyan related to us, from Muhammad ibn Suqah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding ﴿And take provisions﴾: "Al-khushkanaj and sawiq." Waki' also said: Ibrahim al-Makki related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn Umar, who said: "Indeed, among a man's generosity is the goodness of his provisions on a journey." Hammad ibn Salamah added in it, from Abu Rayhanah, that Ibn Umar used to stipulate to whoever accompanied him: the good quality (al-jawzah).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿For the best provision is piety﴾: when He commanded them to take provisions for the journey in this world, He guided them to the provision for the Hereafter, which is to carry piety with them to it, as He said: ﴿And raiment of piety — that is best﴾ [al-A'raf: 26]. When He mentioned the material clothing, He drew attention to the spiritual clothing, which is humility, obedience, and piety, and He stated that it is better than this and more beneficial.

Ata al-Khurasani said regarding His saying: ﴿For the best provision is piety﴾, meaning: the provision of the Hereafter.

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Abdan related to us, Hisham ibn Ammar related to us, Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah related to us, from Isma'il, from Qays, from Jarir ibn Abd Allah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever takes provision in this world, it will benefit him in the Hereafter." (al-Mu'jam al-Kabir; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/311): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih.")

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿And take provisions﴾, a man from the poor Muslims stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we find no provision to take with us." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Take as provision that which keeps your face from people, and the best of what you take as provision is piety." Ibn Abi Hatim related it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And fear Me, O people of understanding﴾: it means: fear My punishment, My retribution, and My torment, for whoever opposes Me and does not comply with My command, O possessors of intellects and understanding.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 198 (part 1 of 2):

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad narrated to us, Ibn 'Uyaynah informed me, from 'Amr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "'Ukaz, Majanna and Dhu al-Majaz were the markets of the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance). So they considered it sinful to trade during the seasons (of Hajj), and then this was revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord﴾ during the seasons of Hajj." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4519.]

In another version, it was also related by 'Abd al-Razzaq, Sa'id ibn Mansur and others, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, with the same wording. [Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (1/65) and Sunan Sa'id ibn Mansur, no. 347.]

For some of them the wording is: "When Islam came, they considered it sinful to trade, so they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about that, and Allah revealed this verse." Likewise, Ibn Jurayj related it from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The trading place of the people in the Jahiliyyah was 'Ukaz, Majanna and Dhu al-Majaz. When Islam came, it was as if they disliked that, until this verse was revealed."

Abu Dawud and others related, through Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "They used to avoid buying and selling and trade during the season of Hajj, saying: 'These are days of remembrance.' So Allah revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord﴾." [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1731.]

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Hushaym narrated to us, Hajjaj informed us, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: "There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord during the seasons of Hajj."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning this verse: "There is no harm upon you in buying and selling before the Ihram and after it." Likewise al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas.

Waki' said: Talhah ibn 'Amr al-Hadrami narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, that he used to recite: "There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord during the seasons of Hajj." [And 'Abd al-Razzaq said: from his father 'Uyaynah, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid: I heard Ibn al-Zubayr say: "There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord during the seasons of Hajj."] [Addition from J, T, and W.]

'Abd ibn Humayd related it from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid: I heard Ibn al-Zubayr reciting—and he mentioned the same, identically. Likewise Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir, Qatadah, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Rabi' ibn Anas and others interpreted it.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah narrated to us, Shababah ibn Sawwar narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Umayah, who said: I heard Ibn 'Umar—and he was asked about a man who performs Hajj while he has merchandise with him—so Ibn 'Umar recited: ﴿There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord﴾.

This is a mawquf (companion's statement), and it is strong and good. It has also been related marfu' (traced to the Prophet ﷺ). Ahmad said: Ahmad ibn Asbat narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn 'Amr al-Fuqaymi narrated to us, from Abu Umamah al-Taymi, who said: I said to Ibn 'Umar: "We are hired (as transport), so is there Hajj for us?" He said: "Do you not circumambulate the House, come to 'Arafat, throw the pebbles, and shave your heads?" We said: "Yes." Ibn 'Umar said: "A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him about what you have asked me, and he did not answer him, until Jibril descended to him with this verse: ﴿There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord﴾. The Prophet ﷺ called him and said: 'You are pilgrims (hujjaj).'" [Al-Musnad (2/155).]

'Abd al-Razzaq said: al-Thawri informed us, from al-'Ala' ibn al-Musayyab, from a man of Banu Taym Allah, who said: A man came to 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar and said: "O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, we are a people who are hired, and they claim that we have no Hajj." He said: "Do you not enter the state of ihram as they enter it, circumambulate as they circumambulate, and throw as they throw?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then you are a pilgrim (hajj)." [In J: "Then you are pilgrims."] Then Ibn 'Umar said: "A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him about what you asked about, and then this verse was revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord﴾." [Also related by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (4/169) through 'Abd al-Razzaq.]

'Abd [ibn Humayd in his Tafsir] [Addition from W.] related it from 'Abd al-Razzaq with the same chain. Similarly, Ibn Hudhayfah related this hadith from al-Thawri, marfu'. It has also been related marfu' through other routes. [See the mention of these routes in the marginal notes of Shaykh Sa'd al-Humayd on Sunan Sa'id ibn Mansur, no. 352, where he excelled and benefited, and were it not for fear of lengthiness I would have quoted it here.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah narrated to us, 'Abbad ibn al-'Awwam narrated to us, from al-'Ala' ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Umamah al-Taymi, who said: I said to Ibn 'Umar: "We are people who are hired on this route to Makkah, and some people claim that we have no Hajj. Do you consider that we have Hajj?" He said: "Do you not enter ihram, circumambulate the House, and perform the rites?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Then you are pilgrims." Then he said: "A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him about [the same as] what you asked, and he did not know what to reply to him—or he said: he did not return anything to him—until this verse was revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord﴾. So he called the man, recited it to him, and said: 'You are pilgrims.'" [Also related by Ibn Khuzaymah in his Sahih, no. 3051, through Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah from al-'Ala' ibn al-Musayyab; and by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. 1733, through 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad from al-'Ala' ibn al-Musayyab.]

Likewise, Mas'ud ibn Sa'd, 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad, and Shurayk al-Qadi related it from al-'Ala' ibn al-Musayyab, marfu'.

Ibn Jarir said: Tulayq ibn Muhammad al-Wasiti narrated to me, Asbat—that is, Ibn Muhammad—narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn 'Amr—that is, al-Fuqaymi—informed us, from Abu Umamah al-Taymi, who said: I said to Ibn 'Umar: "We are a people who are hired, so is there Hajj for us?" He said: "Do you not circumambulate the House, come to 'Arafat, throw the pebbles, and shave your heads?" We said: "Yes." He said: "A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him about what you asked me, and he did not know what to say to him, until Jibril, upon him be peace, descended with this verse: ﴿There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord﴾ to the end of the verse, and the Prophet ﷺ said: 'You are pilgrims.'" [Tafsir al-Tabari (4/164).]

Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, Mandal narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Muhajir, from Abu Salih, the freedman of 'Umar, who said: I said: "O Commander of the Faithful, did you used to trade during Hajj?" He said: "And were their livelihoods anything other than during Hajj?"

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So when you pour forth from 'Arafat, remember Allah at al-Mash'ar al-Haram﴾.

The word "'Arafat" is declined (ṣarf) even though it is a proper noun for a feminine entity, because in origin it is a plural like Muslimat and Mu'minat. It was named for a specific place, so the original form was preserved and it was declined. This was chosen by Ibn Jarir.

'Arafah is the place of standing (al-mawqif) in Hajj, and it is the principal of the rites of Hajj. For this reason, Imam Ahmad and the compilers of the Sunan related, with a sound chain, from al-Thawri, from Bukayr ibn 'Ata', from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya'mar al-Dili, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Hajj is 'Arafat"—three times—"whoever reaches 'Arafah before the dawn breaks, has indeed reached (the Hajj). The days of Mina are three, so whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him." [Al-Musnad (4/335); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1949; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2975; Sunan al-Nasa'i (5/264); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3015.]

The time of standing is from the decline of the sun on the day of 'Arafah until the dawn of the second day of sacrifice (Yawm al-Nahr), because the Prophet ﷺ stood during the Farewell Hajj after he had prayed Zuhr, until the sun set, and said: "Take your rites from me." [Related by Muslim in his Sahih, no. 1297, from the hadith of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him.]

In this hadith he said: "Whoever reaches 'Arafah before the dawn breaks has indeed reached (the Hajj)." This is the view of Malik, Abu Hanifah and al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on them. Imam Ahmad, however, held that the time of standing begins from the first day of 'Arafah. They used as evidence the hadith of al-Sha'bi, from 'Urwah ibn Mudarris ibn Harithah ibn Lam al-Ta'i, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Muzdalifah when he came out to the prayer, and I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have come from the mountains of Tayy; I have tired out my mount and exhausted myself. By Allah, I did not leave a mountain without standing upon it. Is there Hajj for me?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever witnesses this prayer of ours, and stands with us until we depart, having stood at 'Arafah before that by night or by day, his Hajj is complete and he has fulfilled his obligations (taffah)."

Related by Imam Ahmad and the compilers of the Sunan, and al-Tirmidhi declared it sahih. [Al-Musnad (4/15); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1950; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 891; Sunan al-Nasa'i (5/263); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3016.]

Then it was said: 'Arafat was so named because of what 'Abd al-Razzaq related: Ibn Jurayj informed me, he said: Ibn al-Musayyib said: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib said: Allah sent Jibril, upon him be peace, to Ibrahim, upon him be peace, and he performed Hajj with him, until when he came to 'Arafah, he said: "You have recognized ('araft)," and he had come to it once before that, so for this reason it was named 'Arafah.

Ibn al-Mubarak said, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, from 'Ata', who said: 'Arafah was named because Jibril used to show Ibrahim the rites, and would say: "I have recognized, I have recognized." So it was named "'Arafat." A similar report is related from Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Umar and Abu Mijlaz. And Allah knows best.

'Arafat is also called al-Mash'ar al-Halal, al-Mash'ar al-Aqsa, and Ilal (on the pattern of Hilal). The mountain in its middle is called Jabal al-Rahmah (the Mount of Mercy). Abu Talib said in his famous qasidah:

And at the farthest Mash'ar, when they aim for it,
Ilal, toward those flowing valleys (al-shiraj al-qawabil).

[The verse is in Ibn Hisham's Sirah (1/274).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Hammad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Anbasah narrated to us, Abu 'Amir narrated to us, from Zam'ah—that is, Ibn Salih—from Salamah—that is, Ibn Wahram [In J: "that is, Ibn Hisham"]—from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The people of the Jahiliyyah used to stand at 'Arafah until, when the sun was upon the mountaintops like turbans upon the heads of men, they would depart. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ delayed the departure from 'Arafah until the sun had set.

Ibn Mardawayh related it through the hadith of Zam'ah ibn Salih, and added: "Then he stood at Muzdalifah and prayed the dawn prayer in the dim light, and when everything became clear, and it was the appointed time, he departed." This is a hasan chain.

Ibn Juraij said, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed us while he was at 'Arafat. He praised Allah and extolled Him. Then he said: "Amma ba'd" (And now, to proceed), for when he gave a sermon he would say, "Amma ba'd." "Indeed, this day is al-Hajj al-Akbar (the greatest Hajj). Beware! The people of polytheism and idols used to depart from this day before the sun set, when the sun was on the mountaintops, like the turbans of men on their faces. We depart after the sun sets. And they used to depart from al-Mash'ar al-Haram after the sun rose, when the sun was on the mountaintops like the turbans of men on their faces. We depart before the sun rises, differing from the guidance of the people of polytheism."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in this way, and this is his wording, and al-Hakim in his al-Mustadrak. Both are from the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Mubarak al-'Aishi, from 'Abd al-Warith ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Juraij, with it. Al-Hakim said: "Sahih according to the condition of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it." He said: "The hearing of al-Miswar from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has been established and confirmed by what we have mentioned, not as the vulgar among our companions imagine, that he was among those who had a sighting (ru'yah) without hearing."[[In C: "ممن له رواية" (one who had a narration).]] [[Al-Mustadrak (2/277).]]

Waki' said, from Shu'bah, from Isma'il ibn Raja' [al-Zubaidi],[[Addition from W.]] from al-Ma'rur ibn Suwaid, who said: "I saw 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, when he departed from 'Arafat, as if I am looking at him, a bald man on his camel, urging it on (yuwda'), and he was saying: 'Indeed we have found that al-ifadah is al-ida'."
