In the lengthy hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, which is in Sahih Muslim, he said in it: "He remained standing—meaning at 'Arafat—until the sun set and the yellowness had gone somewhat, until the disc disappeared. He took Usamah behind him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ departed, having drawn tight the rein of al-Qaswa' (his camel), so that her head was touching the saddle-frame of his riding-saddle, and he was saying with his right hand: 'O people, tranquility, tranquility!' Whenever he came to a mountain, he would loosen it a little for her until she ascended, until he came to Muzdalifah. There he prayed Maghrib and 'Isha' with one adhan and two iqamahs, and he did not perform any voluntary prayer between them. Then he lay down until the dawn rose, and he prayed Fajr when the dawn became clear to him, with one adhan and one iqamah. Then he rode al-Qaswa' until he came to al-Mash'ar al-Haram, and he faced the qiblah, and he supplicated Allah, glorified Him, declared His greatness (tahlil) and affirmed His oneness. He remained standing until it became very bright, then he departed before the sun rose."[[Sahih Muslim, no. (1218).]]

In the Sahih (of al-Bukhari and Muslim) from Usamah ibn Zayd, that he was asked how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ traveled when he departed. He said: "He would travel at an 'anaq (a moderate, steady pace), and when he found an open space he would go at a nass (a fast pace)."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (1666, 4413) and Sahih Muslim, no. (1286).]] Al-'Anaq is an extended pace of travel, and al-nass is above it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Muhammad, the son of the daughter of al-Shafi'i, informed us, in what he wrote to me, from his father or his paternal uncle, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, his statement: ﴿Then when you depart from 'Arafat, remember Allah at al-Mash'ar al-Haram﴾, and it is both prayers (Maghrib and 'Isha') together.[[In C and T: "الصلاتين" (the two prayers). This is an error; the correct form is "الصلاتان" (the two prayers).]]

Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i said, from 'Amr ibn Maymun: "I asked 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr about al-Mash'ar al-Haram, and he was silent until, when the forelegs of our mounts descended at Muzdalifah, he said: 'Where is the one who asked about al-Mash'ar al-Haram? This is al-Mash'ar al-Haram.'"

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, who said: Ibn 'Umar said: "al-Mash'ar al-Haram is all of Muzdalifah."[[Al-Tabari narrated it in his Tafsir (4/176) through 'Abd al-Razzaq with it.]]

Hushaym said, from Hajjaj,[[In C: "عن الحجاج" (from al-Hajjaj).]] from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar: that he was asked about His statement: ﴿Remember Allah at al-Mash'ar al-Haram﴾, and he said: "It is the mountain and what is around it."

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: "Ibn 'Umar saw them crowding at Quzah, and he said: 'Why are these people crowding? Everything here is a mash'ar.'"[[Al-Tabari narrated it in his Tafsir (4/177, 178) through 'Abd al-Razzaq with it.]]

It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, al-Suddi, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Hasan, and Qatadah that they said: It is what is between the two mountains.

Ibn Juraij said: I asked 'Ata': "Where is Muzdalifah?" He said: "When you depart from the two narrow passes of 'Arafat, that is up to Muhassir." He said: "The two narrow passes are not of 'Arafat nor of Muzdalifah, but they are between them (their meeting point)." He said: "So stand between them if you wish." He said: "And I like that you stand short of Quzah. Come to us for the sake of the people's path."

I say: The mash'ar are the apparent landmarks. Muzdalifah was named al-Mash'ar al-Haram because it is within the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram). As for whether standing there is a pillar (rukn) of Hajj, without which it is not valid, as some of the early scholars and some of al-Shafi'i's companions, including al-Qaffal and Ibn Khuzaymah, have held, based on the hadith of 'Urwah ibn Mudarris?[[In C: "أو" appears as a question mark-type; the source poses the question.]] Or is it an obligation (wajib), which can be compensated for with a sacrifice, as is one of al-Shafi'i's two opinions? Or is it recommended (mustahabb), such that neglecting it incurs nothing, as is the other opinion? There are three opinions among the scholars on this, and its full discussion belongs in another place. And Allah knows best.

'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak said, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Zayd ibn Aslam, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "All of 'Arafat is a place of standing (mawqif), and lift up from 'Uranah,[[In A and W: "عن عرفة" (from 'Arafah).]] and all of Jam' (Muzdalifah) is a place of standing except Muhassir."[[Al-Tabari narrated it in the Tafsir (4/179). It has come connected (mawsul) through a hadith of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him. Ibn Majah narrated it in his Sunan, no. (3012), and its origin is in Sahih Muslim, no. (1218). Taken from the footnote of Shaykh Ahmad Shakir on Tafsir al-Tabari.]]

This is a mursal hadith (one in which the Companion is omitted from the chain). Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Musa narrated to me, from Jubayr ibn Mut'im,[[In T: "from Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from his father."]] from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "All of 'Arafat is a place of standing, and lift up from 'Uranah. All of Muzdalifah is a place of standing, and lift up from Muhassir. All the paths of Makkah are places of sacrifice, and all the days of Tashriq are days of slaughter."[[Al-Musnad (4/82).]]

This too is munqati' (a chain with a break), for Sulayman ibn Musa here, who is al-Ashdaq, did not meet Jubayr ibn Mut'im. However, al-Walid ibn Muslim and Suwayd ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated it from Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, from Sulayman. Al-Walid said: "from a son of Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from his father," while Suwayd said: "from Nafi' ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ," and he mentioned it. And Allah knows best.

* *

His statement: ﴿And remember Him as He has guided you, though before this you were certainly among the astray﴾ is a reminder to them of what He has bestowed upon them: guidance, clarification, and direction to the rites of Hajj, according to what Abraham the Friend (al-Khalil), upon him be peace, was upon. For this reason He said: ﴿And indeed you were before it among the astray.﴾ It was said: before this guidance, and before the Qur'an, and before the Messenger. All of these are close in meaning, interrelated, and sound.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 199:

"Thumma" (then) here is used to conjoin one report to another and to place it in sequence after it, as if the Exalted instructed the one standing at 'Arafat to proceed (depart) to Muzdalifah, so that he may remember Allah at al-Mash'ar al-Haram, and instructed him that his standing should be together with the majority of people at 'Arafat, as the majority of people used to do: they stand there, except the Quraysh, for they would not leave the Haram; they would stand at the edge of the Haram, at the nearest point of the lawful area [[In A: "al-jabal" (the mountain).]], and say: "We are the people of Allah, in His city and the custodians of His House."

Al-Bukhari said: Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Hazim narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Quraysh and those who followed their religion used to stand at Muzdalifah, and they were called al-Hums (the Hums, the zealous ones), while the rest of the Arabs used to stand at 'Arafat. When Islam came, Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to go to 'Arafat, stand there, and then depart from it. That is His saying: ﴿Then depart from where the people depart﴾ [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4520).]].

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ata', Qatadah, al-Suddi and others said likewise. Ibn Jarir chose this view and related consensus upon it, may Allah have mercy on them.

Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from his father, who said: "I lost a camel of mine at 'Arafat, so I went to search for it, and there was the Prophet (ﷺ) standing. I said: 'This is one of the Hums; what is he doing here?'"

Both al-Bukhari and Muslim related it in their Sahihs [[Musnad (4/80), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1664), Sahih Muslim no. (1220).]]. Then al-Bukhari related, from the hadith of Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from Kurayb, from Ibn 'Abbas, what implies that the intended meaning of "al-ifadah" here is the departure from Muzdalifah to Mina for the stoning of the pillars [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4521).]]. Allah knows best. Ibn Jarir related this only from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, and said: "The intended meaning of 'the people' is Ibrahim, peace be upon him." And in another narration from him: "the Imam." Ibn Jarir said: "Were it not for the consensus of the scholars against it, it would have been the more preferred view."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And seek forgiveness from Allah; indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, Allah often commands remembrance of Him after the completion of acts of worship. For this reason it is established in Sahih Muslim that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he finished the prayer, would seek forgiveness three times. And in the two Sahihs, he recommended glorifying (tasbih), praising (tahmid) and magnifying (takbir) Allah thirty-three times each, thirty-three times each.

Ibn Jarir has related here the hadith of al-'Abbas ibn Mirdas al-Sulami concerning the Prophet's (peace be upon him) seeking forgiveness for his Ummah on the evening of 'Arafat. We have cited it in a separate section that we compiled on the virtue of the Day of 'Arafat [[Al-Tabari said in his tafsir (4/192): "Ismail ibn Sayf al-Ajli related to me, saying: Abd al-Qahir ibn al-Sari al-Sulami narrated to us, saying: Ibn Kinanah - and his kunyah is Abu Kinanah - narrated to us, from his father, from al-Abbas ibn Mirdas al-Sulami, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'I supplicated Allah on the Day of 'Arafat to forgive the sins of my Ummah, and He answered me: I have forgiven, except what is between them and My creatures. I repeated the supplication that day, but I was not answered in anything. When it was the morning at Muzdalifah, I said: O Lord, You are able to compensate this wronged one for his injustice and forgive this wrongdoer, and He answered me: I have forgiven.' He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed. We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we saw you laugh on a day you did not used to laugh!' He said: 'I laughed at the enemy of Allah, Iblis, when he heard what had happened, for he was calling out for destruction and ruin and putting dust on his head.'"]].

Ibn Mardawayh also cited here the hadith that al-Bukhari related from Shaddad ibn Aws, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best form of seeking forgiveness is that the servant says: 'O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I am upon Your covenant and Your promise as far as I am able. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge before You Your favour upon me, and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins except You.' Whoever says it at night and dies that night will enter Paradise, and whoever says it during the day and dies will enter Paradise" [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6306).]].

In the two Sahihs, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr: Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, teach me a supplication that I may make in my prayer." He said: "Say: 'O Allah, I have wronged myself greatly, and none forgives sins except You. So forgive me with forgiveness from You and have mercy upon me; indeed You are the Forgiving, the Merciful'" [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (7378); Sahih Muslim no. (2705).]].

The narrations concerning seeking forgiveness are many.

Allah commands remembering Him and increasing in His remembrance after completing the rites of pilgrimage and finishing them.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿As you remember your fathers﴾, the scholars differed over its meaning. Ibn Jurayj said, from ʿAṭāʾ: it is like the saying of a child, "Abah, ummah" (Daddy, Mummy), meaning: just as a child constantly calls upon his father and mother, so should you constantly call upon Allah after completing the rite. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas said likewise. Ibn Jarir transmitted through al-ʿAwfī, from Ibn ʿAbbas, something similar.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said, from Ibn ʿAbbas: The people of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic period) used to stand at the season (of pilgrimage), and a man among them would say, "My father used to feed people and bear the burdens of blood-money (diyat)." Their remembrance was only of their fathers' deeds. So Allah revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿So remember Allah as you remember your fathers, or with even greater remembrance﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It has been narrated from Anas ibn Malik, Abu Wa'il, ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abi Rabah in one of his two opinions, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ʿIkrimah in one of his narrations, Mujahid, al-Suddi, ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurasani, al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas, al-Ḥasan, Qatadah, Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, and Muqatil ibn Ḥayyan, something similar. Ibn Jarir also related it in this manner from a group (of scholars). And Allah knows best.

The purpose of this is to urge increasing the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. For this reason, the expression ﴿or with even greater remembrance﴾ is in the accusative of specification (tamyiz); its implied meaning is: "as you remember your fathers, or with greater remembrance than that." The word "or" here serves to affirm the equivalence in the statement, as in His saying: ﴿Then they are like stones, or even harder in hardness﴾ [al-Baqarah: 74]; His saying: ﴿They fear people as they fear Allah, or even more intensely﴾ [al-Nisa': 77]; ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more﴾ [al-Saffat: 147]; ﴿So he was (as close as) two bow-lengths or nearer﴾ [al-Najm: 9]. Therefore it is definitely not expressing doubt here; rather it is to affirm the report that it is so, or more than that.

Then Allah guided (people) to supplicate after increasing His remembrance, for that is a likely time for an answer. He also censured those who ask Him only for the affairs of this world while turning away from the Hereafter. He said: ﴿Among the people is he who says, "Our Lord, give us in this world," and he will have no share in the Hereafter﴾, meaning: no portion or benefit. This censure also includes a warning against imitating those who are like that. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said, from Ibn ʿAbbas: Some Bedouins used to come to the place of standing (ʿArafat) and say, "O Allah, make it a year of rain, a year of plenty, and a year of good offspring," mentioning nothing of the affairs of the Hereafter. So Allah revealed concerning them: ﴿Among the people is he who says, "Our Lord, give us in this world," and he will have no share in the Hereafter﴾. Then others among the believers would come after them and say: ﴿Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾. So Allah revealed: ﴿Those will have a share of what they have earned, and Allah is swift in reckoning﴾.

For this reason He praised the one who asks for both the world and the Hereafter, saying: ﴿And among them is he who says, "Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire"﴾. This supplication gathers every good in this world and averts every evil. Good in this world includes every worldly desire: good health, a spacious home, a good wife, abundant provision, beneficial knowledge, righteous deeds, a pleasant mount, a fine reputation, and other things that the words of the exegetes have included, and there is no contradiction between them, for all of them fall under "good in this world." As for good in the Hereafter, the highest of it is entry into Paradise and its consequences, including safety from the greatest terror on the Plain of Judgment, the ease of reckoning, and other good matters of the Hereafter. As for being saved from the Fire, it requires facilitating its causes in this world, by avoiding the prohibitions and sins, and abandoning doubtful matters and what is unlawful.

Al-Qasim ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman said: Whoever is given a grateful heart, a remembering tongue, and an enduring body has been given good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and has been protected from the punishment of the Fire.

For this reason the Sunnah (the Prophetic tradition) came with encouragement to this supplication. Al-Bukhari said: Abu Maʿmar narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Warith narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-ʿAziz, from Anas ibn Malik who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "O Allah, our Lord, give us in this world good and in the Hereafter good, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4522.]

Imam Ahmad said: Ismaʿil ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Suhayb narrated to us, from Anas, [who said: Qatadah asked Anas, "Which supplication did the Prophet (ﷺ) make most often?" He said: The most frequent supplication the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made was: "O Allah, our Lord, give us in this world good, and in the Hereafter good, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire."] [Musnad (3/101).]

[Whenever Anas wanted to supplicate with a supplication, he would supplicate with it, and whenever he wanted to supplicate with a supplication, he would supplicate with that which is in it.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Nuʿaym narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Salam ibn Shaddad (i.e., Abu Talut) narrated to us, who said: I was with Anas ibn Malik, and Thabit said to him: "Your brothers love that you supplicate for them." So he said: "O Allah, give us in this world good, and in the Hereafter good, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire." They spoke for a while, and when they wanted to rise, they said: "O Abu Hamzah, your brothers want to rise, so supplicate for them." He said: "Do you want me to make matters difficult for you? If Allah has given you good in this world, and good in the Hereafter, and protected you from the punishment of the Fire, then He has given you all good."

Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn Abi ʿAdi narrated to us, from Humayd, [and ʿAbd Allah ibn Bakr al-Sahmi narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us,] from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) visited a Muslim man who had become like a young bird (so emaciated). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Did you use to supplicate Allah for anything, or ask Him for something?" He said: "Yes, I used to say: 'O Allah, whatever You were going to punish me with in the Hereafter, hasten it for me in this world.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Subhan Allah! You cannot bear it, or you cannot endure it. Why did you not say: ﴿Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾?" He said: So he supplicated to Allah, and He healed him.

Muslim alone transmitted it, narrating it from the hadith of Ibn Abi ʿAdi with this chain.

Al-Shafiʿi said: Saʿid ibn Salim al-Qaddah informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Yahya ibn ʿUbayd, the client of al-Sa'ib, from his father, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib: that he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say, between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone: ﴿Our Lord, give us in this world good, and in the Hereafter good, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾. [Al-Baghawi related it in Sharh al-Sunnah (7/128) through al-Shafiʿi with this chain, and Ibn Hibban related it in his Sahih, no. 1001 (Mawarid), through Yahya al-Qattan from Ibn Jurayj, with something similar.] Al-Thawri also narrated it from Ibn Jurayj in the same way.

Ibn Majah related, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar. Its chain contains weakness [Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2957]. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Mardawayh said: ʿAbd al-Baqi narrated to us, Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn Musawir informed us, Saʿid ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Sulayman, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Hurmuz, from Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have never passed by the (Yemeni) Corner without seeing an angel upon it saying: Amin. So when you pass by it, say: ﴿Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾."

Al-Hakim said in his Mustadrak: Abu Zakariyya al-ʿAnbari informed us, Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Salam narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Jarir informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim al-Bitin, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr who said: A man came to Ibn ʿAbbas and said: "I hired myself out to a people on condition that they carry me, and I reduced from my wage on condition that they allow me to perform Hajj with them. Is that permissible?" He said: "You are of those about whom Allah said: ﴿Those will have a share of what they have earned, and Allah is swift in reckoning﴾." Then al-Hakim said: It is sound according to the criteria of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not include it [Mustadrak (2/277)].

[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4522.]

He said: The most frequent supplication the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made was: "O Allah, our Lord, give us in this world good, and in the Hereafter good, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire."] [Musnad (3/101).]

[Whenever Anas wanted to supplicate with a supplication, he would supplicate with it, and whenever he wanted to supplicate with a supplication, he would supplicate with that which is in it.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Nuʿaym narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Salam ibn Shaddad (i.e., Abu Talut) narrated to us, who said: I was with Anas ibn Malik, and Thabit said to him: "Your brothers love that you supplicate for them." So he said: "O Allah, give us in this world good, and in the Hereafter good, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire." They spoke for a while, and when they wanted to rise, they said: "O Abu Hamzah, your brothers want to rise, so supplicate for them." He said: "Do you want me to make matters difficult for you? If Allah has given you good in this world, and good in the Hereafter, and protected you from the punishment of the Fire, then He has given you all good."

Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn Abi ʿAdi narrated to us, from Humayd, [and ʿAbd Allah ibn Bakr al-Sahmi narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us,] from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) visited a Muslim man who had become like a young bird (so emaciated). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Did you use to supplicate Allah for anything, or ask Him for something?" He said: "Yes, I used to say: 'O Allah, whatever You were going to punish me with in the Hereafter, hasten it for me in this world.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Subhan Allah! You cannot bear it, or you cannot endure it. Why did you not say: ﴿Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾?" He said: So he supplicated to Allah, and He healed him.

Muslim alone transmitted it, narrating it from the hadith of Ibn Abi ʿAdi with this chain.

Al-Shafiʿi said: Saʿid ibn Salim al-Qaddah informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Yahya ibn ʿUbayd, the client of al-Sa'ib, from his father, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib: that he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say, between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone: ﴿Our Lord, give us in this world good, and in the Hereafter good, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾. [Al-Baghawi related it in Sharh al-Sunnah (7/128) through al-Shafiʿi with this chain, and Ibn Hibban related it in his Sahih, no. 1001 (Mawarid), through Yahya al-Qattan from Ibn Jurayj, with something similar.] Al-Thawri also narrated it from Ibn Jurayj in the same way.

Ibn Majah related, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar. Its chain contains weakness [Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2957]. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Mardawayh said: ʿAbd al-Baqi narrated to us, Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn Musawir informed us, Saʿid ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Sulayman, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Hurmuz, from Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have never passed by the (Yemeni) Corner without seeing an angel upon it saying: Amin. So when you pass by it, say: ﴿Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾."

Al-Hakim said in his Mustadrak: Abu Zakariyya al-ʿAnbari informed us, Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Salam narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Jarir informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim al-Bitin, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr who said: A man came to Ibn ʿAbbas and said: "I hired myself out to a people on condition that they carry me, and I reduced from my wage on condition that they allow me to perform Hajj with them. Is that permissible?" He said: "You are of those about whom Allah said: ﴿Those will have a share of what they have earned, and Allah is swift in reckoning﴾." Then al-Hakim said: It is sound according to the criteria of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not include it [Mustadrak (2/277)].

Allah commands remembering Him and increasing in His remembrance after completing the rites of pilgrimage and finishing them.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿As you remember your fathers﴾, the scholars differed over its meaning. Ibn Jurayj said, from ʿAṭāʾ: it is like the saying of a child, "Abah, ummah" (Daddy, Mummy), meaning: just as a child constantly calls upon his father and mother, so should you constantly call upon Allah after completing the rite. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas said likewise. Ibn Jarir transmitted through al-ʿAwfī, from Ibn ʿAbbas, something similar.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said, from Ibn ʿAbbas: The people of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic period) used to stand at the season (of pilgrimage), and a man among them would say, "My father used to feed people and bear the burdens of blood-money (diyat)." Their remembrance was only of their fathers' deeds. So Allah revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿So remember Allah as you remember your fathers, or with even greater remembrance﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It has been narrated from Anas ibn Malik, Abu Wa'il, ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abi Rabah in one of his two opinions, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ʿIkrimah in one of his narrations, Mujahid, al-Suddi, ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurasani, al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas, al-Ḥasan, Qatadah, Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, and Muqatil ibn Ḥayyan, something similar. Ibn Jarir also related it in this manner from a group (of scholars). And Allah knows best.

The purpose of this is to urge increasing the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. For this reason, the expression ﴿or with even greater remembrance﴾ is in the accusative of specification (tamyiz); its implied meaning is: "as you remember your fathers, or with greater remembrance than that." The word "or" here serves to affirm the equivalence in the statement, as in His saying: ﴿Then they are like stones, or even harder in hardness﴾ [al-Baqarah: 74]; His saying: ﴿They fear people as they fear Allah, or even more intensely﴾ [al-Nisa': 77]; ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more﴾ [al-Saffat: 147]; ﴿So he was (as close as) two bow-lengths or nearer﴾ [al-Najm: 9]. Therefore it is definitely not expressing doubt here; rather it is to affirm the report that it is so, or more than that.

Then Allah guided (people) to supplicate after increasing His remembrance, for that is a likely time for an answer. He also censured those who ask Him only for the affairs of this world while turning away from the Hereafter. He said: ﴿Among the people is he who says, "Our Lord, give us in this world," and he will have no share in the Hereafter﴾, meaning: no portion or benefit. This censure also includes a warning against imitating those who are like that. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said, from Ibn ʿAbbas: Some Bedouins used to come to the place of standing (ʿArafat) and say, "O Allah, make it a year of rain, a year of plenty, and a year of good offspring," mentioning nothing of the affairs of the Hereafter. So Allah revealed concerning them: ﴿Among the people is he who says, "Our Lord, give us in this world," and he will have no share in the Hereafter﴾. Then others among the believers would come after them and say: ﴿Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾. So Allah revealed: ﴿Those will have a share of what they have earned, and Allah is swift in reckoning﴾.

For this reason He praised the one who asks for both the world and the Hereafter, saying: ﴿And among them is he who says, "Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire"﴾. This supplication gathers every good in this world and averts every evil. Good in this world includes every worldly desire: good health, a spacious home, a good wife, abundant provision, beneficial knowledge, righteous deeds, a pleasant mount, a fine reputation, and other things that the words of the exegetes have included, and there is no contradiction between them, for all of them fall under "good in this world." As for good in the Hereafter, the highest of it is entry into Paradise and its consequences, including safety from the greatest terror on the Plain of Judgment, the ease of reckoning, and other good matters of the Hereafter. As for being saved from the Fire, it requires facilitating its causes in this world, by avoiding the prohibitions and sins, and abandoning doubtful matters and what is unlawful.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "The numbered days" (al-ayyam al-maʿdudat) are the days of tashriq (the days after ʿId al-Adha on which the pilgrims remain in Mina), and "the known days" (al-ayyam al-maʿlumat) are the ten days (of Dhu al-Hijjah). ʿIkrimah said concerning ﴿And remember Allah during numbered days﴾: it means the takbir (saying "Allahu akbar") on the days of tashriq after the obligatory prayers: "Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar."

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' related to us, Musa ibn ʿAli related to us, from his father, who said: I heard ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmir say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The day of ʿArafah, the day of an-Nahr (sacrifice), and the days of tashriq are our festival, the people of Islam, and they are days of eating and drinking." [[al-Musnad (4/153).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Hushaym related to us, Khalid informed us, from Abu al-Malih, from Nubaysha al-Hudhali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The days of tashriq are days of eating, drinking, and remembrance of Allah." It was also related by Muslim. [[al-Musnad (5/75) and Sahih Muslim, no. (1141).]] The hadith of Jubayr ibn Mut'im has already been mentioned: "All of ʿArafah is a place of standing, and all the days of tashriq are days of slaughter." And the hadith of ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Yaʿmar al-Dili has already been mentioned [[in one copy: "Muʿammar al-Daylami".]]: "The days of Mina are three; whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him."

Ibn Jarir said: Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim and Khallad ibn Aslam related to us, both saying: Hushaym related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Abi Salamah, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The days of tashriq are days of food and remembrance." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (4/211).]]

Khallad ibn Aslam related to us: Rawh related to us, Salih related to us, Ibn Shihab related to me, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent ʿAbd Allah ibn Hudhafah to go around in Mina: "Do not fast these days, for they are days of eating, drinking, and the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (4/211).]]

Yaʿqub related to us: Hushaym related to us, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from al-Zuhri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent ʿAbd Allah ibn Hudhafah, and he proclaimed during the days of tashriq: "Indeed these days are days of eating, drinking, and the remembrance of Allah, except for one who has an obligation of fasting due to a sacrificial offering." This addition is good but mursal.

Hushaym also related, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, from ʿAmr ibn Dinar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Bishr ibn Suhaym, and he proclaimed during the days of tashriq: "Indeed these days are days of eating, drinking, and the remembrance of Allah."

Hushaym said, from Ibn Abi Layla, from ʿAta', from ʿA'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade fasting on the days of tashriq and said: "They are days of eating, drinking, and the remembrance of Allah."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Hakim ibn Hakim, from Mas'ud ibn al-Hakim al-Zuraqi, from his mother, who said: "It is as if I am looking at ʿAli on the white mule of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), until he stopped at the mountain pass of the Ansar, and he was saying: 'O people, these are not days of fasting; they are only days of eating, drinking, and remembrance.'" [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (4/213) through the route of Ibn ʿUlayyah from Ibn Ishaq.]]

Miqsam said, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "The numbered days" are the days of tashriq, four days: the day of an-Nahr and three days after it. It is also narrated from Ibn ʿUmar, Ibn al-Zubayr, Abu Musa, ʿAta', Mujahid, ʿIkrimah, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Abu Malik, Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Suddi, al-Zuhri, al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, al-Dahhak, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, ʿAta' al-Khurasani, Malik ibn Anas, and others, the same.

ʿAli ibn Abi Talib said: They are three days: the day of an-Nahr and two days after it. Slaughter on whichever of them you wish, and the best of them is the first.

The first view is the well-known one, and the noble verse indicates it apparently, where He says: ﴿Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him﴾, which indicates three days after the day of an-Nahr.

Related to His saying: ﴿And remember Allah during numbered days﴾ is the remembrance of Allah over the sacrificial animals, which has already been mentioned, and that the preferred position on this is the school of al-Shafiʿi, may Allah have mercy on him, that the time of the udhiyah (sacrifice) is from the day of an-Nahr until the end of the days of tashriq. Also related to it is the remembrance at fixed times after the prayers, and the unrestricted remembrance in all other circumstances. Concerning its time, the scholars have several opinions, and the most famous, on which practice rests, is that it begins from the Fajr prayer on the day of ʿArafah until the ʿAsr prayer on the last of the days of tashriq, which is the end of the second departure. A hadith has come concerning this, narrated by al-Daraqutni, but it is not authentically traced to the Prophet (ﷺ) as a marfuʿ report. [[Sunan al-Daraqutni (2/49, 50) through several routes from Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him).]] And Allah knows best. It is established that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) used to glorify Allah in his tent, and the people of the market would glorify Allah along with his glorification, until Mina would resound with takbir.

Related to this also is the takbir and remembrance of Allah at the time of throwing the jamarat every day of the days of tashriq. There has come in the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud and others: "The circumambulation of the House, the running between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and the throwing of the pebbles were only prescribed to establish the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (1888).]]

When Allah the Exalted mentioned the first and second departures, which is the dispersal of people from the season of Hajj to all the regions and horizons after their gathering at the sacred sites and places of standing, He said: ﴿And fear Allah and know that you will be gathered to Him﴾ [i.e., you will be assembled on the Day of Resurrection], as He said: ﴿And it is He who multiplied you upon the earth, and to Him you will be gathered﴾ [al-Muminun: 79].

Al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning al-Akhnas ibn Shariq al-Thaqafi. He came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and displayed Islam, while inwardly holding the opposite.

From Ibn Abbas: It was revealed concerning a group of hypocrites who spoke against Khubayb and his companions, who were killed at al-Raji'. They disparaged them. So Allah revealed, condemning the hypocrites and praising Khubayb and his companions: ﴿And among mankind is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾.

It was also said: Rather, it is general, applying to all the hypocrites and to all the believers. This is the view of Qatadah, Mujahid, al-Rabi' ibn Anas and others, and it is the sound view.

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, al-Laith ibn Sa'd informed me, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from al-Qurazi, from Nawf, who was al-Bikali and one of those who read the scriptures. He said: "Indeed I find the description of some people of this Ummah in the Book of Allah that was revealed: a people who use religion to gain worldly ends. Their tongues are sweeter than honey, and their hearts are more bitter than aloes. They wear sheep's wool before people (the sheepskin) while their hearts are the hearts of wolves. Allah says: 'Upon Me they are bold! And by Me they are deceived! I swear by Myself that I will send upon them a trial that will leave the forbearing among them bewildered.'" Al-Qurazi said: "I reflected on it in the Qur'an, and behold, they are the hypocrites. I found it: ﴿And among mankind is he whose speech about the life of this world impresses you, and he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart﴾, to the end of the verse."

Muhammad ibn Abi Ma'shar narrated to me: my father, Abu Ma'shar Najih, informed me, saying: I heard Sa'id al-Maqburi discussing with Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi. Sa'id said: "In some of the books it is said: Indeed, there are servants of Allah whose tongues are sweeter than honey, and whose hearts are more bitter than aloes. They wear sheep's wool of softness before people, they chew the world with religion. Allah says: 'Upon Me you are bold! And by Me you are deceived! By My might, I will send upon them a trial that will leave the forbearing among them bewildered.'" Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: "This is in the Book of Allah." Sa'id said: "And where is it in the Book of Allah?" He said: "The saying of Allah: ﴿And among mankind is he whose speech about the life of this world impresses you﴾, to the end of the verse." Sa'id said: "I know for whom this verse was revealed." Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: "The verse may be revealed concerning a particular man, and then it becomes general thereafter." What al-Qurazi said is good and sound.

As for His words ﴿and he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart﴾: Ibn Muhaysin read it as "wayashhadu Allahu" with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the name of Allah (Allah being the subject). Its meaning is: even if this one displays to you fine words, Allah knows from his heart its ugliness, like His saying: ﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say, "We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah." And Allah knows that you are His Messenger, and Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are liars﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 1].

The reading of the majority is with a damma on the ya' and a fatha on the name of Allah: ﴿and he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart﴾. Its meaning is that he displays Islam to the people while defying Allah with what is in his heart of disbelief and hypocrisy, like His saying: ﴿They hide from people, yet they cannot hide from Allah﴾ [al-Nisa': 108], to the end of the verse. This is the meaning of what Ibn Ishaq narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from Ikrimah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas.

It was also said: the meaning is that when he displays Islam to the people, he swears and calls Allah to witness for them that what is in his heart agrees with his tongue. This meaning is sound. It was said by Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, Ibn Jarir chose it, attributed it to Ibn Abbas, and related it from Mujahid. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And he is the most stubborn of opponents﴾. Al-Alladd in the language means the crooked. ﴿And to warn with it a people who are stubbornly contentious﴾ [Maryam: 97], meaning crooked. Likewise the hypocrite, in his state of contention, lies, turns away from the truth, and does not remain upright with it. Rather, he fabricates and transgresses, as is established in the Sahih from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "The sign of the hypocrite is three: when he speaks he lies, when he makes a promise he breaks it, and when he disputes he transgresses."

Al-Bukhari said: Qabisah narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Aishah, raising it (to the Prophet ﷺ), who said: "The most hated of men to Allah is the most stubborn opponent." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4523.]

He said: Abd Allah ibn Yazid also said: Sufyan narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to me, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Aishah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Indeed the most hated of men to Allah is the most stubborn opponent." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4523.]

Likewise Abd al-Razzaq narrated it from Ma'mar, regarding His saying ﴿And he is the most stubborn of opponents﴾, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Aishah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Indeed the most hated of men to Allah is the most stubborn opponent." [Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq (1/97).]

* *

As for His words: ﴿And when he turns away, he strives in the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and animals. And Allah does not like corruption﴾. * *

As for His words: ﴿And when it is said to him, "Fear Allah," he is seized by arrogance to [commit] sin﴾. This verse resembles His saying: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, you can recognize denial on the faces of those who disbelieve. They nearly assault those who recite Our verses to them. Say, "Shall I inform you of something worse than that? For this reason He said in this verse: ﴿Sufficient for him is Hell, and wretched is the resting place﴾, meaning: it suffices him as punishment for this.

* *

When he embraced Islam in Makkah and wished to emigrate (hijrah), the people prevented him from emigrating with his wealth. He said that if they wanted, he would leave it all behind and emigrate. So he freed himself from them by giving them his wealth, and Allah revealed this verse concerning him. Umar ibn al-Khattab and a group met him at the edge of al-Harrah (a lava field near Madinah). They said: "The trade has profited." He said: "And you, may Allah not make your trade a loss. What is this?" They informed him that Allah had revealed this verse concerning him. It is related that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Suhayb has profited in the trade, Suhayb has profited in the trade."

Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Rustah narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Dawud narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Sulayman al-Da'bi narrated to us, Awf narrated to us, from Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, from Suhayb, who said: "When I wished to emigrate from Makkah to the Prophet ﷺ, the Quraysh said to me: 'O Suhayb, you came to us with no wealth, and now you leave with your wealth! I departed until I reached Madinah. The Prophet ﷺ was informed of this and said: 'Suhayb has profited, Suhayb has profited,' twice." [Ibn Sa'd related it in al-Tabaqat (2/227) from Hawdhah, from Awf, from Abu Uthman, who said: "It reached me that Suhayb…" and similar; Ibn Sa'd (2/228) and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (1/151) also related it through Ali ibn Zayd from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, with a similar account of the story.]

He dismounted from his mount, emptied his quiver, and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, you know that I am among the best of you at archery, and by Allah you will not reach me until I shoot every arrow in my quiver, then strike with my sword as long as anything remains in my hand. When he came to the Prophet ﷺ, he said: "The trade has profited, the trade has profited." He said: And this verse was revealed: ﴿And among mankind is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of Allah. And Allah is Kind to the servants﴾.

As for the majority, they understood it to mean that it was revealed concerning every fighter in the cause of Allah, as He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for that they will have Paradise. And Allah is Kind to the servants﴾.

Al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning al-Akhnas ibn Shariq al-Thaqafi. He came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and displayed Islam, while inwardly holding the opposite.

From Ibn Abbas: It was revealed concerning a group of hypocrites who spoke against Khubayb and his companions, who were killed at al-Raji'. They disparaged them. So Allah revealed, condemning the hypocrites and praising Khubayb and his companions: ﴿And among mankind is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾.

It was also said: Rather, it is general, applying to all the hypocrites and to all the believers. This is the view of Qatadah, Mujahid, al-Rabi' ibn Anas and others, and it is the sound view.

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, al-Laith ibn Sa'd informed me, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from al-Qurazi, from Nawf, who was al-Bikali and one of those who read the scriptures. He said: "Indeed I find the description of some people of this Ummah in the Book of Allah that was revealed: a people who use religion to gain worldly ends. Al-Qurazi said: "I reflected on it in the Qur'an, and behold, they are the hypocrites. He dismounted from his mount, emptied his quiver, and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, you know that I am among the best of you at archery, and by Allah you will not reach me until I shoot every arrow in my quiver, then strike with my sword as long as anything remains in my hand. Then do what you wish. Or, if you wish, I will show you my wealth and my property in Makkah and you will let my way be." They said: "Yes." When he came to the Prophet ﷺ, he said: "The trade has profited, the trade has profited." He said: And this verse was revealed: ﴿And among mankind is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of Allah. And Allah is Kind to the servants﴾.

As for the majority, they understood it to mean that it was revealed concerning every fighter in the cause of Allah, as He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for that they will have Paradise. They fight in the cause of Allah, so they kill and are killed. It is a true promise from Him in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an. And who is more faithful to his covenant than Allah? So rejoice in the transaction which you have contracted. And that is the great attainment﴾ [al-Tawbah: 111]. When Hisham ibn Amir was carried between the two lines (in battle), some people objected to it, and Umar ibn al-Khattab, Abu Hurayrah and others responded to them, reciting this verse: ﴿And among mankind is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of Allah. And Allah is Kind to the servants﴾.

Al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning al-Akhnas ibn Shariq al-Thaqafi. He came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and displayed Islam, while inwardly holding the opposite.

From Ibn Abbas: It was revealed concerning a group of hypocrites who spoke against Khubayb and his companions, who were killed at al-Raji'. They disparaged them. So Allah revealed, condemning the hypocrites and praising Khubayb and his companions: ﴿And among mankind is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾.

It was also said: Rather, it is general, applying to all the hypocrites and to all the believers. This is the view of Qatadah, Mujahid, al-Rabi' ibn Anas and others, and it is the sound view.

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, al-Laith ibn Sa'd informed me, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from al-Qurazi, from Nawf, who was al-Bikali and one of those who read the scriptures. He said: "Indeed I find the description of some people of this Ummah in the Book of Allah that was revealed: a people who use religion to gain worldly ends. Their tongues are sweeter than honey, and their hearts are more bitter than aloes. They wear sheep's wool before people (the sheepskin) while their hearts are the hearts of wolves. Allah says: 'Upon Me they are bold! And by Me they are deceived! I swear by Myself that I will send upon them a trial that will leave the forbearing among them bewildered.'" Al-Qurazi said: "I reflected on it in the Qur'an, and behold, they are the hypocrites. I found it: ﴿And among mankind is he whose speech about the life of this world impresses you, and he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart﴾, to the end of the verse."

Muhammad ibn Abi Ma'shar narrated to me: my father, Abu Ma'shar Najih, informed me, saying: I heard Sa'id al-Maqburi discussing with Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi. Sa'id said: "In some of the books it is said: Indeed, there are servants of Allah whose tongues are sweeter than honey, and whose hearts are more bitter than aloes. They wear sheep's wool of softness before people, they chew the world with religion. Allah says: 'Upon Me you are bold! And by Me you are deceived! By My might, I will send upon them a trial that will leave the forbearing among them bewildered.'" Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: "This is in the Book of Allah." Sa'id said: "And where is it in the Book of Allah?" He said: "The saying of Allah: ﴿And among mankind is he whose speech about the life of this world impresses you﴾, to the end of the verse." Sa'id said: "I know for whom this verse was revealed." Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: "The verse may be revealed concerning a particular man, and then it becomes general thereafter." What al-Qurazi said is good and sound.

As for His words ﴿and he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart﴾: Ibn Muhaysin read it as "wayashhadu Allahu" with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the name of Allah (Allah being the subject). Its meaning is: even if this one displays to you fine words, Allah knows from his heart its ugliness, like His saying: ﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say, "We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah." And Allah knows that you are His Messenger, and Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are liars﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 1].

The reading of the majority is with a damma on the ya' and a fatha on the name of Allah: ﴿and he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart﴾. Its meaning is that he displays Islam to the people while defying Allah with what is in his heart of disbelief and hypocrisy, like His saying: ﴿They hide from people, yet they cannot hide from Allah﴾ [al-Nisa': 108], to the end of the verse. This is the meaning of what Ibn Ishaq narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from Ikrimah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas.

It was also said: the meaning is that when he displays Islam to the people, he swears and calls Allah to witness for them that what is in his heart agrees with his tongue. This meaning is sound. It was said by Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, Ibn Jarir chose it, attributed it to Ibn Abbas, and related it from Mujahid. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And he is the most stubborn of opponents﴾. Al-Alladd in the language means the crooked. ﴿And to warn with it a people who are stubbornly contentious﴾ [Maryam: 97], meaning crooked. Likewise the hypocrite, in his state of contention, lies, turns away from the truth, and does not remain upright with it. Rather, he fabricates and transgresses, as is established in the Sahih from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "The sign of the hypocrite is three: when he speaks he lies, when he makes a promise he breaks it, and when he disputes he transgresses."

Al-Bukhari said: Qabisah narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Aishah, raising it (to the Prophet ﷺ), who said: "The most hated of men to Allah is the most stubborn opponent." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4523.]

He said: Abd Allah ibn Yazid also said: Sufyan narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to me, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Aishah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Indeed the most hated of men to Allah is the most stubborn opponent." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4523.]

Likewise Abd al-Razzaq narrated it from Ma'mar, regarding His saying ﴿And he is the most stubborn of opponents﴾, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Aishah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Indeed the most hated of men to Allah is the most stubborn opponent." [Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq (1/97).]

* *

As for His words: ﴿And when he turns away, he strives in the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and animals. And Allah does not like corruption﴾. That is: his speech is crooked and his actions are evil. That is His saying, and this is his deed: his speech is false, his belief is corrupt, and his actions are ugly.

Al-Sa'y (striving) here means intending, as He said, reporting about Pharaoh: ﴿Then he turned away, striving. And he gathered [his people] and called out, and said, "I am your lord, the most high." So Allah seized him in the punishment of the Hereafter and the first [life]. Indeed in that is a lesson for whoever fears﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 22–26]. And He said: ﴿O you who have believed, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Jumu'ah, then hasten to the remembrance of Allah﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 9], meaning: intend and resolve upon it, intending the Friday prayer. For the physical running toward the prayer is forbidden by the Prophetic Sunnah: "When you come to the prayer, do not come running, but come walking with tranquility and dignity."

This hypocrite has no aspiration except corruption in the land and the destruction of the crops, which is the place of the growth of plants, fruits and offspring, that is, the young of animals, on which people's livelihood depends.

Mujahid said: When he strives in the land for corruption, Allah withholds the rain, and the crops and animals perish. ﴿And Allah does not like corruption﴾, meaning He does not love one who has this characteristic, nor one from whom such things proceed.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And when it is said to him, "Fear Allah," he is seized by arrogance to [commit] sin﴾. That is: when this wicked one is admonished in his speech and actions, and it is said to him, "Fear Allah, desist from your words and deeds, and return to the truth," he refuses and rejects, and zeal and anger seize him for sin, meaning because of what the sins contain. This verse resembles His saying: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, you can recognize denial on the faces of those who disbelieve. They nearly assault those who recite Our verses to them. Say, "Shall I inform you of something worse than that? The Fire, which Allah has promised to those who disbelieve, and wretched is the destination"﴾ [al-Hajj: 72]. For this reason He said in this verse: ﴿Sufficient for him is Hell, and wretched is the resting place﴾, meaning: it suffices him as punishment for this.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And among mankind is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾. When He informed about the hypocrites with their blameworthy characteristics, He mentioned the praiseworthy characteristics of the believers, saying: ﴿And among mankind is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾.

Ibn Abbas, Anas, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, Ikrimah and a group said: It was revealed concerning Suhayb ibn Sinan al-Rumi. When he embraced Islam in Makkah and wished to emigrate (hijrah), the people prevented him from emigrating with his wealth. He said that if they wanted, he would leave it all behind and emigrate. So he freed himself from them by giving them his wealth, and Allah revealed this verse concerning him. Umar ibn al-Khattab and a group met him at the edge of al-Harrah (a lava field near Madinah). They said: "The trade has profited." He said: "And you, may Allah not make your trade a loss. What is this?" They informed him that Allah had revealed this verse concerning him. It is related that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Suhayb has profited in the trade, Suhayb has profited in the trade."

Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Rustah narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Dawud narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Sulayman al-Da'bi narrated to us, Awf narrated to us, from Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, from Suhayb, who said: "When I wished to emigrate from Makkah to the Prophet ﷺ, the Quraysh said to me: 'O Suhayb, you came to us with no wealth, and now you leave with your wealth! By Allah, that will never happen.' I said to them: 'Do you see, if I hand over my wealth to you, will you let me go?' They said: 'Yes.' So I handed over my wealth to them, and they let me go. I departed until I reached Madinah. The Prophet ﷺ was informed of this and said: 'Suhayb has profited, Suhayb has profited,' twice." [Ibn Sa'd related it in al-Tabaqat (2/227) from Hawdhah, from Awf, from Abu Uthman, who said: "It reached me that Suhayb…" and similar; Ibn Sa'd (2/228) and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (1/151) also related it through Ali ibn Zayd from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, with a similar account of the story.]

He dismounted from his mount, emptied his quiver, and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, you know that I am among the best of you at archery, and by Allah you will not reach me until I shoot every arrow in my quiver, then strike with my sword as long as anything remains in my hand. Then do what you wish. Or, if you wish, I will show you my wealth and my property in Makkah and you will let my way be." They said: "Yes." When he came to the Prophet ﷺ, he said: "The trade has profited, the trade has profited." He said: And this verse was revealed: ﴿And among mankind is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of Allah. And Allah is Kind to the servants﴾.

They fight in the cause of Allah, so they kill and are killed. It is a true promise from Him in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an. And who is more faithful to his covenant than Allah? So rejoice in the transaction which you have contracted. And that is the great attainment﴾ [al-Tawbah: 111]. When Hisham ibn Amir was carried between the two lines (in battle), some people objected to it, and Umar ibn al-Khattab, Abu Hurayrah and others responded to them, reciting this verse: ﴿And among mankind is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of Allah. And Allah is Kind to the servants﴾.

Allah the Exalted says, commanding His servants who believe in Him and affirm His Messenger: that they should take hold of all the handholds (ʿurā) of Islam and its laws, act upon all of its commands, and abstain from all of its prohibitions, to the extent they are able.

Al-ʿAwfi related from Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, Tawus, al-Dahhak, ʿIkrimah, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd, regarding His saying: ﴿Enter into peace (al-silm)﴾ that it means Islam.

Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn ʿAbbas, as did Abu al-ʿAliyah and al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas: ﴿Enter into peace﴾ means obedience. Qatadah also said: it means reconciliation (al-muwada'ah).

* *

His saying: ﴿kaffah﴾ (entirely, all of you). Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, Abu al-ʿAliyah, ʿIkrimah, al-Rabiʿ, al-Suddi, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Qatadah, and al-Dahhak said: "jamiʿan" (all together). Mujahid said: that is, act upon all deeds and all forms of righteousness.

ʿIkrimah claimed that it was revealed concerning a group of those among the Jews and others who had embraced Islam, such as ʿAbdullah ibn Salam, Thaʿlabah, Asad ibn ʿUbayd, and a group who asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for permission to observe the Sabbath and to stand in prayer through the night with the Torah. So Allah commanded them to establish the rites of Islam and to occupy themselves with them to the exclusion of anything else. However, there is scrutiny in mentioning ʿAbdullah ibn Salam among these people, for it is far-fetched that he would seek permission to observe the Sabbath while, with the completeness of his faith, he knew of its abrogation, its removal, and its invalidity, and that the festivals of Islam had replaced it.

Among the exegetes are those who make His saying ﴿kaffah﴾ a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring to those who enter, meaning: enter into Islam all of you. The correct view is the first, namely that they were commanded, all of them [[addition from manuscripts Jim, Ta, Alif, Waw]], to act upon all the branches of faith (shuʿab al-iman) and the laws of Islam, which are very numerous, to the extent they are able to do so. Ibn Abi Hatim said: ʿAli ibn al-Husayn related to us, Ahmad ibn al-Sabbah related to us, al-Haytham ibn Yaman related to me, Ismaʿil ibn Zakariyya related to us, Muhammad ibn ʿAwn related to me, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿O you who have believed, enter into peace entirely﴾ — thus he recited it with the accusative (kaffatan) — meaning the believers among the People of the Book, for they, along with their belief in Allah, were holding fast to some of the commands of the Torah and the laws that had been revealed to them. So Allah said: ﴿Enter into peace entirely﴾, meaning: enter into the laws of the religion of Muhammad ﷺ and do not leave any part of it, and let belief in the Torah and what is in it suffice for you [not as a substitute].

* *

His saying: ﴿And do not follow the footsteps of Satan﴾, meaning: perform the acts of obedience and avoid what Satan commands you. ﴿Indeed, he only commands you to evil and immorality and to say about Allah that which you do not know﴾ [al-Baqarah: 169], and ﴿He only invites his party to be among the companions of the Blaze﴾ [Fatir: 6]. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy﴾. Mutarrif said: the most deceitful of Allah's servants toward Allah's servants is Satan.

* *

His saying: ﴿And if you slip after clear evidence has come to you﴾, meaning: you deviate from the truth after the proofs have been established against you, then know that Allah is Mighty in His retribution, none who flees escapes Him and none who overpowers can overcome Him, and Wise in His rulings, His annulling and His affirming. For this reason Abu al-ʿAliyah, Qatadah, and al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas said: "Mighty in His vengeance, Wise in His command." Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: "al-ʿAziz" means He is mighty in His victory over whoever disbelieves in Him when He wills, and "al-Hakim" means He is wise in His excuse and His proof addressed to His servants.
