Ibn Kathir says, addressing the disbelievers regarding Muhammad (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), as a warning: ﴿Do they await only that Allah should come to them in canopies of clouds, and the angels?﴾ That is, on the Day of Resurrection, to settle the judgment between the first and the last, and He will recompense every doer for his deed: if good, then good; if evil, then evil. For this reason He said: ﴿And the matter is decided, and to Allah all matters are returned.﴾ As He said: ﴿Nay, when the earth is pounded to powder, pounded to powder, and your Lord comes, and the angels, rank upon rank, and Hellfire is brought near that day—on that day man will remember, but how will remembrance benefit him?﴾ [al-Fajr: 21-23]. And He said: ﴿Do they await only that the angels should come to them, or that your Lord should come, or that some of the signs of your Lord should come? On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come...﴾ [al-An'am: 158], to the end of the verse.

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) has mentioned here the long hadith of the Trumpet (al-Sur) from its beginning, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. It is a well-known hadith, related by more than one of the compilers of the Musnads and others, and in it: "When the people become anxious about their standing in the open plains, they seek intercession with their Lord through the prophets, one by one, from Adam onward. Each of them shrinks back from it until they reach Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. When they come to him, he says: 'I am for it, I am for it.' He goes and prostrates before Allah beneath the Throne, and intercedes with Allah that He come to settle the judgment among the servants. Allah grants his intercession, and He comes in canopies of clouds after the lowest heaven has been split open. Those in it of the angels descend, then the second, then the third, up to the seventh. The bearers of the Throne and the Karubiyyun (the cherubim) descend. [He] said: The Almighty, the Majestic, descends in canopies of clouds, with the angels, and they have a thunderous sound of their glorification, saying: 'Glory to the Possessor of the Dominion and the Kingdom of the heavens; glory to the Lord of the Throne, the Possessor of Majesty; glory to the Living who does not die; glory to the One who causes creatures to die and does not die; Most Holy, Most Pure, Lord of the angels and the Spirit; Holy, Holy; glory to our Lord the Most High; glory to the Possessor of Authority and Greatness; glory to Him forever and ever.'" [Tafsir al-Tabari (4/266). The full hadith will come under the commentary on verse 73 of al-An'am.]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh has cited here hadiths that contain strangeness, and Allah knows best. Among them is what he narrated from the hadith of al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abu Ubaydah ibn Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, from Masruq, from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "Allah gathers the first and the last for an appointed day, standing with their eyes fixed upon the sky, awaiting the decisive judgment. And Allah descends in canopies of clouds, from the Throne to the Kursi." [Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (9/416, 417) by two routes from al-Minhal ibn Amr, at greater length; al-Dhahabi said: "Its isnad is hasan."]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Ata ibn Muqaddam narrated to us, Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, I heard Abd al-Jalil al-Qaysi narrating from Abdullah ibn Amr concerning: ﴿Do they await only that Allah should come to them in canopies of clouds﴾ to the end of the verse, that he said: "He descends when He descends, and between Him and His creation are seventy thousand veils, among them light, darkness, and water. The water will make a sound in that darkness, a sound by which hearts will be torn from their places."

He said: My father narrated to us: Muhammad ibn al-Wazir al-Dimashqi narrated to us, al-Walid narrated to us, who said: I asked Zuhayr ibn Muhammad concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿Do they await only that Allah should come to them in canopies of clouds﴾, and he said: "Canopies of clouds, strung with rubies, adorned with pearls and emeralds."

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿in canopies of clouds﴾: "It is other than the ordinary clouds, and it never appeared except to the Children of Israel in their wandering when they lost their way."

Abu Ja'far al-Razi said, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliyah, concerning: ﴿Do they await only that Allah should come to them in canopies of clouds, and the angels﴾ [He] said: "It means: the angels come in canopies of clouds, and Allah, the Exalted, comes as He wills." In some readings it is: "Do they await only that Allah should come to them, and the angels, in canopies of clouds," and it is like His saying: ﴿And the day the sky is split open with clouds, and the angels are sent down, a sending down.﴾ [al-Furqan: 25].

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says, informing about the Children of Israel: How many signs did they witness with Musa (Moses), ﴿a clear sign﴾, i.e., a decisive proof of his truthfulness in what he brought them: his hand, his staff, his splitting of the sea, his striking of the rock, the shading of the clouds over them in the intense heat, the sending down of the manna and quail, and other signs that point to the existence of the Doer who chooses, and to the truthfulness of the one through whose hands these extraordinary events occurred. Yet despite this, many of them turned away from them, and ﴿they exchanged the favour of Allah [for disbelief]﴾ [[Addition from manuscripts ج, ط, أ, و.]], i.e., they substituted disbelief in them and turning away from them for belief in them.

﴿And whoever exchanges the favour of Allah after it has come to him, then indeed Allah is severe in punishment﴾, as He said, reporting about the disbelievers of Quraysh: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin? [Into] Hell, which they will enter, and wretched is the settling place﴾ [Ibrahim: 28–29].

Then Allah, exalted is He, informed about His making the worldly life appealing to the disbelievers, who were content with it and found rest in it, gathered wealth and withheld it from the channels in which they were commanded to spend it, which would please Allah with them. They mocked those who believed, who turned away from it, and spent what they had obtained from it in obedience to their Lord, giving seeking the Face of Allah. For this reason they attained the most felicitous station and the greatest portion on the Day of their return. They were above those others in their gathering, their resurrection, their journey and their abode; they settled in the ranks, in the highest of ʿIlliyyin, while those others were made to abide in the lowest of the lowest depths. For this reason Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning﴾, i.e., He provides for whom He wills of His creation and gives them abundant, great bounty without limit or counting, in this world and the Hereafter [[In ط: "in the world and not in the Hereafter".]], as came in the hadith: "Son of Adam, spend and I will spend upon you." The Prophet ﷺ also said: "Spend, Bilal, and do not fear from the Lord of the Throne any poverty." [[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/192) through Yahya ibn Wathhab, from Masruq, from ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud (may Allah be pleased with him), as a marfu' report; al-Mundhiri graded it hasan in al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib (2/51).]] Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whatever you spend, He will replace it﴾ [Saba: 39]. In the Sahih it is reported that two angels descend from the sky every morning; one of them says: "O Allah, give the one who spends a replacement," and the other says: "O Allah, give the one who withholds destruction." And in the Sahih [[In أ: "And in the two Sahihs."]]: "The son of Adam says: 'My wealth, my wealth!' Do you have from your wealth anything but what you have eaten and so consumed, what you have worn and so worn out, and what you have given in charity and so let it pass on? Everything else will go and he will leave it for people."

And in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: "The world is the abode of one who has no abode, and the wealth of one who has no wealth, and for it gathers one who has no intellect."

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says, informing about the Children of Israel: How many signs did they witness with Musa (Moses), ﴿a clear sign﴾, i.e., a decisive proof of his truthfulness in what he brought them: his hand, his staff, his splitting of the sea, his striking of the rock, the shading of the clouds over them in the intense heat, the sending down of the manna and quail, and other signs that point to the existence of the Doer who chooses, and to the truthfulness of the one through whose hands these extraordinary events occurred. Yet despite this, many of them turned away from them, and ﴿they exchanged the favour of Allah [for disbelief]﴾ [[Addition from manuscripts ج, ط, أ, و.]], i.e., they substituted disbelief in them and turning away from them for belief in them.

﴿And whoever exchanges the favour of Allah after it has come to him, then indeed Allah is severe in punishment﴾, as He said, reporting about the disbelievers of Quraysh: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin? [Into] Hell, which they will enter, and wretched is the settling place﴾ [Ibrahim: 28–29].

Then Allah, exalted is He, informed about His making the worldly life appealing to the disbelievers, who were content with it and found rest in it, gathered wealth and withheld it from the channels in which they were commanded to spend it, which would please Allah with them. They mocked those who believed, who turned away from it, and spent what they had obtained from it in obedience to their Lord, giving seeking the Face of Allah. For this reason they attained the most felicitous station and the greatest portion on the Day of their return. They were above those others in their gathering, their resurrection, their journey and their abode; they settled in the ranks, in the highest of ʿIlliyyin, while those others were made to abide in the lowest of the lowest depths. For this reason Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning﴾, i.e., He provides for whom He wills of His creation and gives them abundant, great bounty without limit or counting, in this world and the Hereafter [[In ط: "in the world and not in the Hereafter".]], as came in the hadith: "Son of Adam, spend and I will spend upon you." The Prophet ﷺ also said: "Spend, Bilal, and do not fear from the Lord of the Throne any poverty." [[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/192) through Yahya ibn Wathhab, from Masruq, from ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud (may Allah be pleased with him), as a marfu' report; al-Mundhiri graded it hasan in al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib (2/51).]] Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whatever you spend, He will replace it﴾ [Saba: 39]. In the Sahih it is reported that two angels descend from the sky every morning; one of them says: "O Allah, give the one who spends a replacement," and the other says: "O Allah, give the one who withholds destruction." And in the Sahih [[In أ: "And in the two Sahihs."]]: "The son of Adam says: 'My wealth, my wealth!' Do you have from your wealth anything but what you have eaten and so consumed, what you have worn and so worn out, and what you have given in charity and so let it pass on? Everything else will go and he will leave it for people."

And in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: "The world is the abode of one who has no abode, and the wealth of one who has no wealth, and for it gathers one who has no intellect."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 213:

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Abu Dawud narrated to us, Hammam informed us, from Qatadah, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Between Nuh (Noah) and Adam there were ten generations, all of them upon the Shari'ah (religious law) of the Truth. Then they differed, so Allah sent the Prophets as bearers of glad tidings and as warners." He said: "And thus it is in the recitation of 'Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud): 'The people were one nation, then they differed.'"

Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of Bundar, from Muhammad ibn Bashshar. Then he said: "Sahih (authentic), but the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not narrate it." [Tafsir al-Tabari (4/275) and al-Mustadrak (2/546).]

Similarly, Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that he used to recite it: "The people were one nation, then they differed, so Allah sent the Prophets as bearers of glad tidings and as warners."

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿The people were one nation﴾, he said: "They were all upon guidance, then they differed, so Allah sent the Prophets as bearers of glad tidings and as warners." The first Prophet sent was Nuh. Mujahid said the same, as Ibn 'Abbas had said first.

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿The people were one nation﴾: "They were disbelievers, so Allah sent the Prophets as bearers of glad tidings and as warners."

The first statement from Ibn 'Abbas is more sound in its chain and in its meaning, because the people were upon the religion of Adam, peace be upon him, until they worshipped idols. So Allah sent to them Nuh, peace be upon him, who was the first Messenger that Allah sent to the people of the earth.

Hence He said: ﴿And He sent down with them the Book in truth, to judge between the people concerning that over which they differed. And none differed concerning it except those who were given it, after clear proofs had come to them, out of animosity among themselves.﴾

That is: after the proofs had been established against them. What led them to it was nothing but transgression of some of them against others. ﴿So Allah guided those who believed to the truth concerning that over which they differed, by His permission. And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.﴾

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Sulayman al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, regarding His saying: ﴿So Allah guided those who believed to the truth concerning that over which they differed, by His permission﴾, he said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "We are the last (in coming) but the first on the Day of Resurrection; we are the first of the people to enter Paradise, except that they were given the Book before us and we were given it after them. Then Allah guided us to the truth concerning that over which they differed. This is the day about which they differed, and Allah guided us to it. So the people follow us in it: tomorrow is for the Jews, and the day after tomorrow is for the Christians."

Then 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated it from Ma'mar, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah. [Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (1/99), and the hadith is recorded in the two Sahihs.]

Ibn Wahb said, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, regarding His saying: ﴿So Allah guided those who believed to the truth concerning that over which they differed, by His permission﴾: They differed concerning the day of Friday, so the Jews took Saturday and the Christians took Sunday, and Allah guided the Ummah of Muhammad to Friday. They differed concerning the qiblah: the Christians faced the east and the Jews faced Bayt al-Maqdis, and Allah guided the Ummah of Muhammad to the qiblah. They differed concerning the prayer: some of them bow without prostrating, some prostrate without bowing, some pray while speaking, and some pray while walking, and Allah guided the Ummah of Muhammad to the truth in that. They differed concerning fasting: some of them fast part of the day, and some abstain from some foods, and Allah guided the Ummah of Muhammad to the truth in that. They differed concerning Ibrahim, peace be upon him: the Jews said he was a Jew, and the Christians said he was a Christian, and Allah made him a hanif, a Muslim, and Allah guided the Ummah of Muhammad to the truth in that. They differed concerning 'Isa, peace be upon him: the Jews denied him and uttered a great slander against his mother, and the Christians made him a god and a son, while Allah made him His spirit and His word, and Allah guided the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ to the truth in that.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said regarding His saying: ﴿So Allah guided those who believed to the truth concerning that over which they differed, by His permission﴾: meaning, at the time of differing, they held to what the Messengers had brought before the differing, they persisted in sincerity to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, alone, in worshipping Him without partner, in establishing the prayer and giving the zakah. So they remained upon the first matter that was before the differing, and they kept away from the differing. And they were witnesses over the people on the Day of Resurrection, witnesses against the people of Nuh, the people of Hud, the people of Salih, the people of Shu'ayb, and the family of Pharaoh, that their Messengers had conveyed to them, and that they had denied their Messengers.

In the recitation of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "And that they may be witnesses over the people on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path." Abu al-'Aliyah used to say: in this verse is the way out of doubts, misguidance and trials.

* *

His saying: ﴿by His permission﴾ means: by His knowledge, by what He guided them to. This was stated by Ibn Jarir. ﴿And Allah guides whom He wills﴾: i.e., from His creation, ﴿to a straight path﴾, meaning that to Him belong the judgment and the conclusive proof. In the Sahih of al-Bukhari and Muslim, from 'A'ishah: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, whenever he rose at night to pray, would say: "O Allah, Lord of Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, You judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ. Guide me to the truth concerning that over which they differed, by Your permission, for You guide whom You will to a straight path." [Sahih Muslim, no. 770.] And in the transmitted supplication: "O Allah, show us the truth as truth and grant us the ability to follow it, and show us falsehood as falsehood and grant us the ability to avoid it, and do not make it confused for us so that we go astray, and make us an imam for the righteous."

Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Or did you think that you would enter Paradise before you were tried, tested and examined, as those nations before you were?﴾ For this reason He said: ﴿Or have you thought that you would enter Paradise without there having come to you the example of those who passed away before you? Adversity and hardship touched them, and they were shaken﴾. [The adversity and hardship] are: sicknesses, ailments, pains, calamities and misfortunes.

Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Murrah al-Hamdani, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi' (ibn Anas), al-Suddi and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: ﴿al-ba'sa'* (adversity)﴾ is poverty. Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿al-darra'* (hardship)﴾ is illness.

﴿Wa zulzilu* (and they were shaken)﴾ means they were shaken by fear of the enemies, with a severe shaking, and they were tested with a great testing. This is as mentioned in the authentic hadith from Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, who said: "We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, will you not seek victory for us? Will you not supplicate Allah for us?' He said: 'Among those who came before you, a man would have a saw placed on the middle of his head and it would split him down to his feet, and that would not turn him away from his religion. And iron combs would be drawn over his flesh and bones, and that would not turn him away from his religion.'" Then he said: "By Allah, Allah will surely complete this matter, until a rider travels from Sana'a to Hadramawt fearing none but Allah and the wolf concerning his sheep, but you are a people who are hasty."

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. Do people think that they will be left alone because they say, "We believe," and they will not be tested? And We had certainly tested those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful and will surely make evident the liars﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 1-3].

A great portion of this occurred to the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, on the day of the Confederates (al-Ahzab), as Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿When they came at you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes shifted and the hearts reached the throats, and you assumed about Allah assumptions. There the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking. And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said, "Allah and His Messenger promised us only delusion."﴾ [al-Ahzab: 10-12], and the verses that follow.

When Heraclius asked Abu Sufyan: "Did you fight him?" He said: "Yes." He said: "So how was the war between you?" He said: "Its outcome was alternating: sometimes he prevails over us and sometimes we prevail over him." He said: "Thus are the messengers tested, and then the final outcome is theirs." [The hadith of Heraclius is narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (7).]

* *

His saying: ﴿The example of those who passed away before you﴾ means: their way (sunnah). As Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿So We destroyed those who were stronger than them in might, and the example of the former peoples has passed﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 8].

* *

His saying: ﴿And they were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of Allah?"﴾ means: they sought victory over their enemies and supplicated for the nearness of relief and a way out, at the narrowness of the situation and the severity of hardship. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near﴾, and as He says: ﴿For indeed, with hardship is ease. Indeed, with hardship is ease﴾ [al-Sharh: 5-6].

Just as hardship intensifies, the help that descends with it intensifies too. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near﴾. In the hadith of Abu Razin: "Your Lord marvels at the despair of His servants while His relief is near. He looks at them despairing, and so He keeps laughing, knowing that their relief is near," and so on. [Ibn Majah narrated it in al-Sunan, no. (181), through Ya'la ibn 'Ata', from Waki' ibn 'Udus, from Abu Razin. al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (1/85): "This chain has some weakness."]

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: This verse concerns voluntary charity (nafaqat al-tatawwu'). Al-Suddi said: It was abrogated (nasakhaha) by zakat (the obligatory alms). But this is open to question (wa-fihi nazar). The meaning of the verse: "They ask you what they should spend." This was said by Ibn Abbas and Mujahid. So Allah the Exalted clarified this for them, saying: ﴿Say: Whatever wealth you spend should go to parents and near relatives, orphans, the needy and the wayfarer﴾. That is, direct it to these categories. As has come in the hadith: "Your mother and your father, your sister and your brother, then the nearest and then the nearest." Maymun ibn Mihran recited this verse and then said: These are the proper places of expenditure; nothing is mentioned in them of drums or flutes, nor of wooden images, nor of decorating walls.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whatever good you do, indeed Allah is Knowing of it﴾. That is: whatever act of goodness proceeds from you, Allah knows it, and He will reward you for it with the fullest reward, for He does not wrong anyone even by the weight of an atom.

This is an obligation from Allah the Exalted upon the Muslims to fight (jihad), so that they repel the evil of the enemies from the territory of Islam.

Al-Zuhri said: Jihad is obligatory upon everyone, whether he goes out to fight or sits at home. So the one who sits at home, when he is asked for help, must help; when he is sought for aid, he must aid; and when he is called to go forth, he must go forth. And if he is not needed, he may remain seated.

I say: For this reason it is established in the Sahih that "Whoever dies without having fought, or having never resolved in his soul to fight, dies a death of Jahiliyyah." (Sahih Muslim, no. 1910, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.) And the Prophet (ﷺ) said on the day of the Conquest: "There is no hijrah, but there is jihad and intention. When you are called to go forth, then go forth." (Reported by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, nos. 1834, 2783, 2825, and by Muslim in his Sahih, no. 1353, from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.)

* *

His saying: ﴿And it is hateful to you﴾ means: it is difficult and burdensome for you. And so it is, for one either is killed or wounded, along with the hardship of travel and the struggle against the enemies.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿But perhaps you hate a thing while it is good for you﴾, meaning: because fighting is followed by victory and triumph over the enemies, and the seizure of their lands, their wealth, their offspring, and their children.

﴿And perhaps you love a thing while it is bad for you﴾. This is general across all matters: a person may love something in which he has no good and no benefit. Among this is sitting back from fighting, which may be followed by the enemy's seizure of the lands and the rule.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And Allah knows, while you do not know﴾, meaning: He is more knowing of the outcomes of affairs than you, and more aware of what is good for you in your worldly life and your Hereafter. So respond to Him, and submit to His command, ﴿that you may be guided﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami narrated to us, al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from his father, al-Hadrami narrated to me, from Abu al-Sawwar, from Jundab ibn Abdullah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a detachment (rahṭ) and appointed over them Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah [or Ubaydah ibn al-Harith] [addition from Ṭ, A, W]. When he set off to depart, he wept out of longing (ṣabābah) for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so he sat down. He then appointed in his place Abdullah ibn Jahsh, wrote a letter for him, and instructed him not to read the letter until he reached such-and-such a place. He said: "Do not compel anyone among your companions to march with you." When he read the letter, he said, "We hear and obey Allah and His Messenger." He informed them of the matter and read the letter to them. Two men turned back, and the rest remained. They encountered Ibn al-Hadrami and killed him, not realising whether that day was in Rajab or Jumada. The polytheists said to the Muslims: "You have killed in the sacred month!" So Allah revealed: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it. Say: Fighting in it is grave.﴾ to the end of the verse.

Al-Suddi narrated, from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it. Say: Fighting in it is grave.﴾ The reason was that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a sariyyah (a small military expedition), and they were seven men, under the command of Abdullah ibn Jahsh al-Asadi. Among them were Ammar ibn Yasir, Abu Hudhayfah ibn Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Utbah ibn Ghazwan al-Sulami (an ally of the Banu Nawfal), Suhayl ibn Bayda', Amir ibn Fuhayrah, and Waqid ibn Abdullah al-Yarbu'i (an ally of Umar ibn al-Khattab). He wrote a letter for Ibn Jahsh and instructed him not to read it until he had reached Batn Malal. When he reached Batn Malal, he opened the letter, and in it was: "Proceed until you reach Batn Nakhlah." He said to his companions: "Whoever desires death, let him advance and make his will, for I will make my will and proceed to fulfil the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He marched on, but Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and Utbah fell behind, for they had lost a riding camel of theirs, and they went searching for it in Bahran. Ibn Jahsh proceeded to Batn Nakhlah, where he came upon al-Hakam ibn Kaysan, al-Mughirah ibn Uthman, Amr ibn al-Hadrami, and Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah. Ibn al-Mughirah escaped, while they captured al-Hakam ibn Kaysan and al-Mughirah. Amr was killed by Waqid ibn Abdullah. This was the first spoil (ghanimah) that the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ acquired.

When they returned to Madinah with the two captives and the wealth they had taken, the people of Makkah wished to ransom the two captives. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Not until we see what has become of our two companions." Then Sa'd and his companion returned, and he ransomed the two captives. The polytheists became indignant and said: "Muhammad claims that he follows the obedience of Allah, yet he is the first to make lawful the sacred month, and he killed our companion in Rajab." The Muslims said: "We only killed him in Jumada," and it was also said: "at the beginning of Rajab and the last night of Jumada." The Muslims had sheathed their swords when the month of Rajab began. So Allah revealed, rebuking the people of Makkah: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it. Say: Fighting in it is grave﴾, but it is not lawful. What you have done, O polytheists, is greater than killing in the sacred month: when you disbelieved in Allah, and barred Muhammad ﷺ and his Companions from Him, and expelled the people of the Sacred Mosque from it when they expelled Muhammad ﷺ, is greater in the sight of Allah than killing.

Al-Awfi narrated, from Ibn Abbas, regarding: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it. Say: Fighting in it is grave.﴾ The reason was that the polytheists barred the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and turned him back from the [Sacred] Mosque in a sacred month, then Allah granted victory to His Prophet in a sacred month of the following year. The polytheists then criticised the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for fighting in a sacred month. So Allah said: ﴿And barring from the way of Allah, disbelief in Him, and the Sacred Mosque, and expelling its people from it, is greater [than fighting] in it.﴾ Also, Muhammad ﷺ sent a sariyyah, and they encountered Amr ibn al-Hadrami as he was coming from al-Ta'if in the last night of Jumada and the first night of Rajab. The Companions of Muhammad ﷺ thought that night was in Jumada, but it was the first of Rajab, and they did not realise it. A man among them killed him and they took what he had with him. The polytheists sent word rebuking him for this, so Allah said: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it. Say: Fighting in it is grave,﴾ and what is other than that is greater than it: barring from the way of Allah, disbelief in Him and the Sacred Mosque, and expelling its people from it. The expulsion of the people of the Sacred Mosque is greater than what the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ did, and shirk is worse than that.

Similarly, Abu Sa'd al-Baqqal narrated from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that it was revealed concerning the sariyyah of Abdullah ibn Jahsh and the killing of Amr ibn al-Hadrami.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib al-Kalbi narrated to me, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Regarding what happened to Amr ibn al-Hadrami, there was revealed: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it﴾ to the end of the verse.

Abd al-Malik ibn Hisham, the transmitter of the biography (al-Sirah), narrated from Ziyad ibn Abdullah al-Bakka'i, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar al-Madani, may Allah have mercy on him, in his book on the Sirah, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Abdullah ibn Jahsh ibn Ri'ab al-Asadi in Rajab, at the time of his return from the first Badr [expedition], and sent with him eight men from the Emigrants (Muhajirun), none of the Helpers (Ansar) being among them. He wrote him a letter and instructed him not to look into it until he had travelled for two days, and then to look into it and carry out what he had been commanded, and not to compel any of his companions. The companions of Abdullah ibn Jahsh were from the Emigrants: then from the Banu Abd Shams ibn Abd Manaf: Abu Hudhayfah ibn Utbah ibn Rabi'ah ibn Abd Shams ibn Abd Manaf; and from their allies: Abdullah ibn Jahsh, who was the commander of the people, and Ukkashah ibn Mihsan ibn Hurthan, of the Banu Asad ibn Khuzaymah, an ally of theirs. From the Banu Nawfal ibn Abd Manaf: Utbah ibn Ghazwan ibn Jabir, an ally of theirs. From the Banu Zuhrah ibn Kilab: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. From the Banu Adi ibn Ka'b: Amir ibn Rabi'ah, an ally of theirs from the Anz ibn Wa'il, and Waqid ibn Abdullah ibn Abd Manaf ibn Arin ibn Tha'labah ibn Yarbu', one of the Banu Tamim, an ally of theirs; and Khalid ibn al-Bukayr, one of the Banu Sa'd ibn Layth, an ally of theirs. From the Banu al-Harith ibn Fihr: Suhayl ibn Bayda'.

When Abdullah ibn Jahsh had marched for two days, he opened the letter and looked into it, and in it was: "When you have looked into this letter of mine, proceed until you reach Nakhlah, between Makkah and al-Ta'if, and watch the Quraysh there, and learn for us some of their news." When Abdullah ibn Jahsh looked into the letter, he said: "We hear and obey." Then he said to his companions: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has commanded me to proceed to Nakhlah to watch the Quraysh there, until I bring him news of them, and he has forbidden me to compel any of you. So whoever among you desires martyrdom and is eager for it, let him go forward, and whoever dislikes that, let him return. As for me, I will proceed to fulfil the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He proceeded, and his companions proceeded with him; not one of them turned back.

He took the road into the Hijaz until, when he was at a mine (ma'dan) above al-Fur', called Bahran, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and Utbah ibn Ghazwan lost a camel of theirs, which they had been riding in turns. They stayed behind to search for it, while Abdullah ibn Jahsh and the rest of his companions went on until they reached Nakhlah. A caravan of the Quraysh passed by them carrying raisins, leather, and merchandise of the Quraysh's trade, among them Amr ibn al-Hadrami, Uthman ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, his brother Nawfal ibn Abdullah al-Makhzumiyyan, and al-Hakam ibn Kaysan, the client (mawla) of Hisham ibn al-Mughirah.

When the people saw them, they were afraid of them, since they had camped near them. Ukkashah ibn Mihsan went up to them, having shaved his head. When they saw him they felt secure and said: "They are Umrah pilgrims; there is no harm to you from them." The people consulted about them, and that was on the last day of Rajab. The people said: "By Allah, if you leave these people tonight, they will enter the Sacred Area (Haram) and be protected by it from you. And if you kill them, you will be killing them in the sacred month." So they hesitated and were reluctant to advance against them, then they encouraged themselves against them and resolved to kill whoever they could of them and seize what they had. Waqid ibn Abdullah al-Tamimi [in A: al-Sahmi] shot Amr ibn al-Hadrami with an arrow and killed him, and they captured Uthman ibn Abdullah and al-Hakam ibn Kaysan, while Nawfal ibn Abdullah escaped from the people and eluded them. Abdullah ibn Jahsh and his companions came back with the caravan and the two captives, until they arrived before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Madinah.

Ibn Ishaq said: Some of the family of Abdullah ibn Jahsh mentioned that Abdullah said to his companions: "Indeed, one-fifth (khums) of what we have taken is due to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and that was before Allah made the khums obligatory on booty." So he set aside one-fifth of the caravan for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and divided the rest among his companions.

Ibn Ishaq said: When they arrived before the Messenger of Allah, he said: "I did not command you to fight in the sacred month." He held back the caravan and the two captives, and refused to take anything from that. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said this, the people were dismayed and thought they had been destroyed, and their brothers among the Muslims rebuked them for what they had done. The Quraysh said: "Muhammad and his companions have made lawful the sacred month: they shed blood in it, took wealth in it, and took men captive in it." And those Muslims in Makkah who would answer them said: "They only obtained what they obtained in Sha'ban."

The Jews also made an omen of it against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Amr ibn al-Hadrami, whom Waqid ibn Abdullah killed; "Amr" (ʿAmr) means "the war has grown (ʿamarat)", "al-Hadrami" means "the war has come (ḥaḍarat)", and "Waqid ibn Abdullah" means "the war has blazed (waqadat)." So Allah turned that omen against them and not in their favour.

When the people had much to say about this, Allah revealed to His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it. Say: Fighting in it is grave, but barring from the way of Allah, disbelief in Him and the Sacred Mosque, and expelling its people from it, is greater in the sight of Allah, and fitnah (persecution/tumult) is greater than killing.﴾ That is: if you killed in the sacred month, they have barred you from the way of Allah while disbelieving in Him, and from the Sacred Mosque, and expelled you from it although you are its people. That is greater in the sight of Allah than the killing of those of them whom you killed. ﴿And fitnah is greater than killing﴾: that is, they used to test the Muslim in his religion until they turned him back to disbelief after his faith. That is greater in the sight of Allah than killing. ﴿And they will not cease fighting you until they turn you back from your religion, if they are able﴾: that is, they remain persistent in the worst and gravest of that, neither repenting nor desisting.

Ibn Ishaq said: When the Qur'an was revealed concerning this matter, and God relieved the Muslims of the distress they had been in, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) took possession of the caravan and the two captives. Quraysh sent to him to ransom 'Uthman ibn 'Abd Allah and al-Hakam ibn Kaysan. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "We will not ransom them to you until our two companions return," meaning Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and 'Utba ibn Ghazwan, "for we fear for them at your hands. If you kill them, we will kill your two companions." Then Sa'd and 'Utba returned, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) ransomed the two captives to them.

As for al-Hakam ibn Kaysan, he embraced Islam, and his Islam was good. He remained with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) until he was killed as a martyr (shahid, one who dies in the cause of God) on the day of Bi'r Ma'una. As for 'Uthman ibn 'Abd Allah, he joined Mecca and died there as a disbeliever.

Ibn Ishaq said: When the situation that 'Abd Allah ibn Jahsh and his companions had been in when the Qur'an was revealed was made clear to them, they hoped for reward and said: "O Messenger of God, do we hope that there will be a military expedition for us in which we will be given the reward of the mujahidun [the emigrants]?" Then God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who emigrated and strove in the way of God, these hope for the mercy of God, and God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. Thus God placed them at the highest level of hope.

Ibn Ishaq said: The report on this matter comes from al-Zuhri and Yazid ibn Ruman, from 'Urwa.

Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn Ruman, from 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, something close to this account. Musa ibn 'Uqba also narrated from al-Zuhri himself something similar.

Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamza narrated from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, something similar to this as well, and in it: Ibn al-Hadrami was the first person killed between the Muslims and the polytheists. A delegation of the disbelieving Quraysh set out until they came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in Medina and said: "Is fighting in the sacred month permitted?" Then God revealed: ﴿They ask you about fighting in the sacred month [concerning it]﴾ [[Addition from manuscript ج، ط.]], the verse. The Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi has thoroughly covered this in his book "Dala'il al-Nubuwwa" (Evidences of Prophethood).

Then Ibn Hisham said, citing Ziyad, from Ibn Ishaq: It has been mentioned that some of the family of 'Abd Allah [ibn Jahsh] [[Addition from manuscript أ.]] said that God divided the fay' (booty taken without fighting) when He made it lawful, assigning four-fifths to those who obtained it and one-fifth to God and His Messenger. This coincided with what 'Abd Allah ibn Jahsh had done in that caravan [[Al-Sira al-Nabawiyya of Ibn Hisham (1/605).]].

Ibn Hisham said: It was the first ghanima (spoils of war) that the Muslims acquired. 'Amr ibn al-Hadrami was the first person whom the Muslims killed, and 'Uthman ibn 'Abd Allah and al-Hakam ibn Kaysan were the first people the Muslims captured [[Al-Sira al-Nabawiyya of Ibn Hisham (1/605).]].

Ibn Ishaq said: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, said concerning the expedition of 'Abd Allah ibn Jahsh, and it is said that 'Abd Allah ibn Jahsh himself said it, when Quraysh said: "Muhammad and his companions have made the sacred month lawful. They shed blood in it, took property in it, and captured men in it." Ibn Hisham said: The following poem is by 'Abd Allah ibn Jahsh:

You count the killing in the sacred month a great offence,
but a greater offence than it is that of one who sees right guidance and does not follow it.
Your turning away from what Muhammad says, and your disbelief in him, while God is watching and witnessing,
and your expulsion of its people from the Sacred Mosque, so that none might be seen prostrating to God in the House.
Even if you reproach us for killing him,
and the envious and the transgressor spread lies about Islam,
we gave Ibn al-Hadrami a drink of our spears at Nakhla, when the one who kindled war had lit its fire.
Blood, and 'Uthman ibn 'Abd Allah is between us, struggling with him is a shackle of leather, rebellious and stubborn.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami narrated to us, al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from his father, al-Hadrami narrated to me, from Abu al-Sawwar, from Jundab ibn Abdullah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a detachment (rahṭ) and appointed over them Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah [or Ubaydah ibn al-Harith] [addition from Ṭ, A, W]. When he set off to depart, he wept out of longing (ṣabābah) for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so he sat down. He then appointed in his place Abdullah ibn Jahsh, wrote a letter for him, and instructed him not to read the letter until he reached such-and-such a place. He said: "Do not compel anyone among your companions to march with you." When he read the letter, he said, "We hear and obey Allah and His Messenger." He informed them of the matter and read the letter to them. Two men turned back, and the rest remained. They encountered Ibn al-Hadrami and killed him, not realising whether that day was in Rajab or Jumada. The polytheists said to the Muslims: "You have killed in the sacred month!" So Allah revealed: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it. Say: Fighting in it is grave.﴾ to the end of the verse.

Al-Suddi narrated, from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it. Say: Fighting in it is grave.﴾ The reason was that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a sariyyah (a small military expedition), and they were seven men, under the command of Abdullah ibn Jahsh al-Asadi. Among them were Ammar ibn Yasir, Abu Hudhayfah ibn Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Utbah ibn Ghazwan al-Sulami (an ally of the Banu Nawfal), Suhayl ibn Bayda', Amir ibn Fuhayrah, and Waqid ibn Abdullah al-Yarbu'i (an ally of Umar ibn al-Khattab). He wrote a letter for Ibn Jahsh and instructed him not to read it until he had reached Batn Malal. When he reached Batn Malal, he opened the letter, and in it was: "Proceed until you reach Batn Nakhlah." He said to his companions: "Whoever desires death, let him advance and make his will, for I will make my will and proceed to fulfil the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He marched on, but Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and Utbah fell behind, for they had lost a riding camel of theirs, and they went searching for it in Bahran. Ibn Jahsh proceeded to Batn Nakhlah, where he came upon al-Hakam ibn Kaysan, al-Mughirah ibn Uthman, Amr ibn al-Hadrami, and Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah. Ibn al-Mughirah escaped, while they captured al-Hakam ibn Kaysan and al-Mughirah. Amr was killed by Waqid ibn Abdullah. This was the first spoil (ghanimah) that the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ acquired.

When they returned to Madinah with the two captives and the wealth they had taken, the people of Makkah wished to ransom the two captives. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Not until we see what has become of our two companions." Then Sa'd and his companion returned, and he ransomed the two captives. The polytheists became indignant and said: "Muhammad claims that he follows the obedience of Allah, yet he is the first to make lawful the sacred month, and he killed our companion in Rajab." The Muslims said: "We only killed him in Jumada," and it was also said: "at the beginning of Rajab and the last night of Jumada." The Muslims had sheathed their swords when the month of Rajab began. So Allah revealed, rebuking the people of Makkah: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it. Say: Fighting in it is grave﴾, but it is not lawful. What you have done, O polytheists, is greater than killing in the sacred month: when you disbelieved in Allah, and barred Muhammad ﷺ and his Companions from Him, and expelled the people of the Sacred Mosque from it when they expelled Muhammad ﷺ, is greater in the sight of Allah than killing.

Al-Awfi narrated, from Ibn Abbas, regarding: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it. Say: Fighting in it is grave.﴾ The reason was that the polytheists barred the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and turned him back from the [Sacred] Mosque in a sacred month, then Allah granted victory to His Prophet in a sacred month of the following year. The polytheists then criticised the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for fighting in a sacred month. So Allah said: ﴿And barring from the way of Allah, disbelief in Him, and the Sacred Mosque, and expelling its people from it, is greater [than fighting] in it.﴾ Also, Muhammad ﷺ sent a sariyyah, and they encountered Amr ibn al-Hadrami as he was coming from al-Ta'if in the last night of Jumada and the first night of Rajab. The Companions of Muhammad ﷺ thought that night was in Jumada, but it was the first of Rajab, and they did not realise it. A man among them killed him and they took what he had with him. The polytheists sent word rebuking him for this, so Allah said: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it. Say: Fighting in it is grave,﴾ and what is other than that is greater than it: barring from the way of Allah, disbelief in Him and the Sacred Mosque, and expelling its people from it. The expulsion of the people of the Sacred Mosque is greater than what the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ did, and shirk is worse than that.

Similarly, Abu Sa'd al-Baqqal narrated from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that it was revealed concerning the sariyyah of Abdullah ibn Jahsh and the killing of Amr ibn al-Hadrami.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib al-Kalbi narrated to me, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Regarding what happened to Amr ibn al-Hadrami, there was revealed: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it﴾ to the end of the verse.

Abd al-Malik ibn Hisham, the transmitter of the biography (al-Sirah), narrated from Ziyad ibn Abdullah al-Bakka'i, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar al-Madani, may Allah have mercy on him, in his book on the Sirah, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Abdullah ibn Jahsh ibn Ri'ab al-Asadi in Rajab, at the time of his return from the first Badr [expedition], and sent with him eight men from the Emigrants (Muhajirun), none of the Helpers (Ansar) being among them. He wrote him a letter and instructed him not to look into it until he had travelled for two days, and then to look into it and carry out what he had been commanded, and not to compel any of his companions. The companions of Abdullah ibn Jahsh were from the Emigrants: then from the Banu Abd Shams ibn Abd Manaf: Abu Hudhayfah ibn Utbah ibn Rabi'ah ibn Abd Shams ibn Abd Manaf; and from their allies: Abdullah ibn Jahsh, who was the commander of the people, and Ukkashah ibn Mihsan ibn Hurthan, of the Banu Asad ibn Khuzaymah, an ally of theirs. From the Banu Nawfal ibn Abd Manaf: Utbah ibn Ghazwan ibn Jabir, an ally of theirs. From the Banu Zuhrah ibn Kilab: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. From the Banu Adi ibn Ka'b: Amir ibn Rabi'ah, an ally of theirs from the Anz ibn Wa'il, and Waqid ibn Abdullah ibn Abd Manaf ibn Arin ibn Tha'labah ibn Yarbu', one of the Banu Tamim, an ally of theirs; and Khalid ibn al-Bukayr, one of the Banu Sa'd ibn Layth, an ally of theirs. From the Banu al-Harith ibn Fihr: Suhayl ibn Bayda'.

When Abdullah ibn Jahsh had marched for two days, he opened the letter and looked into it, and in it was: "When you have looked into this letter of mine, proceed until you reach Nakhlah, between Makkah and al-Ta'if, and watch the Quraysh there, and learn for us some of their news." When Abdullah ibn Jahsh looked into the letter, he said: "We hear and obey." Then he said to his companions: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has commanded me to proceed to Nakhlah to watch the Quraysh there, until I bring him news of them, and he has forbidden me to compel any of you. So whoever among you desires martyrdom and is eager for it, let him go forward, and whoever dislikes that, let him return. As for me, I will proceed to fulfil the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He proceeded, and his companions proceeded with him; not one of them turned back.

He took the road into the Hijaz until, when he was at a mine (ma'dan) above al-Fur', called Bahran, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and Utbah ibn Ghazwan lost a camel of theirs, which they had been riding in turns. Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 219–220 (part 1 of 2):

Imam Ahmad said: Khalaf ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Maysara, from Umar that he said: When the prohibition of wine (khamr) was revealed, he said: "O Allah, make for us a clear and healing explanation regarding wine." So this verse in al-Baqarah was revealed: ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: In them is great sin and [some benefit for people]﴾ [[Addition from manuscript Jim.]]. Umar was called and it was recited to him, and he said: "O Allah, make for us a clear and healing explanation regarding wine." Then the verse in an-Nisa' was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated﴾ [an-Nisa': 43]. The herald of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whenever he called the prayer, would call out: "No intoxicated person should approach the prayer." Umar was called and it was recited to him, and he said: "O Allah, make for us a clear and healing explanation regarding wine." Then the verse in al-Ma'idah was revealed. Umar was called, and it was recited to him, and when it reached ﴿So will you not desist?﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 91], Umar said: "We have desisted, we have desisted." [[Al-Musnad (1/53).]]

Likewise, Abu Dawud, at-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa'i narrated it through various chains from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq. [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3670), Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. (3049) and Sunan an-Nasa'i (8/286).]] Likewise, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through the route of ath-Thawri, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Maysara, whose name is Amr ibn Shurahbil al-Hamdani al-Kufi, from Umar. He has no other narration from him, but Abu Zur'ah said: "He did not hear from him." And Allah knows best. Ali ibn al-Madini said: "This is a sound chain," and at-Tirmidhi authenticated it. Ibn Abi Hatim added, after his saying "We have desisted": "It removes wealth and removes the intellect." This hadith will also come, together with what Ahmad narrated through the route of Abu Hurayrah as well [[In manuscript Jim: "from him".]], at the words in Surat al-Ma'idah: ﴿Indeed, wine, gambling, idols, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 90], and the verses that follow.

As for His saying: ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling﴾, as for wine, it is as the Commander of the Faithful Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "It is everything that clouds the intellect," as will be explained in Surat al-Ma'idah. Likewise gambling, which is maysir (games of chance).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Say: In them is great sin and benefits for people﴾, as for their sin, it is in religion; and as for the benefits, they are worldly, in that there is in them benefit for the body, aid in digesting food, expelling waste, sharpening some minds, and the pleasure of the intoxicating strength that is in them, as Hassan ibn Thabit said in his pre-Islamic days:

"We drink it, and it leaves us as kings,
and lions that the encounter does not repel..."

Likewise its sale and benefiting from its price, and what some of them would gather from gambling and spend on themselves or their dependents. But these benefits do not balance its harm and its dominant corruption, because it relates to the intellect and religion. Therefore He said: ﴿And their sin is greater than their benefit﴾. For this reason this verse was a preparation for the absolute prohibition of wine, and it was not explicit but rather indirect. Imam Ahmad said: Khalaf ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Maysara, from Umar that he said: When the prohibition of wine (khamr) was revealed, he said: "O Allah, make for us a clear and healing explanation regarding wine." Umar was called, and it was recited to him, and when it reached ﴿So will you not desist?﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 91], Umar said: "We have desisted, we have desisted." [[Al-Musnad (1/53).]]

(3049) and Sunan an-Nasa'i (8/286).]] Likewise, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through the route of ath-Thawri, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Maysara, whose name is Amr ibn Shurahbil al-Hamdani al-Kufi, from Umar. He has no other narration from him, but Abu Zur'ah said: "He did not hear from him." And Allah knows best. Ali ibn al-Madini said: "This is a sound chain," and at-Tirmidhi authenticated it. And in Allah is the trust.

This is a prohibition from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon the believers against marrying idolatrous women who worship idols.

Then, if its generality is intended, and it includes every idolatrous woman, whether from the People of the Book or from the idolaters, then He has specified from this the women of the People of the Book with His saying: ﴿And [lawful to you are] the chaste women from among the believers and the chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, when you have given them their due compensation, desiring chastity, not unlawful intercourse or taking [secret] lovers [[An addition from manuscript ج.]]﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 5].

ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe﴾, that Allah excepted from this the women of the People of the Book. Likewise said Mujahid, ʿIkrimah, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Makhul, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, and others.

It has also been said: rather, what is meant by this is the idolaters who worship idols, and the People of the Book are not intended at all. The meaning is close to the first, and Allah knows best.

As for what Ibn Jarir narrated: "ʿUbayd ibn Adam ibn Abi Iyas al-ʿAsqalani told me, my father told us, ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Bahram al-Fazari told us, Shahr ibn Hawshab told us, who said: I heard ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAbbas say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade [marrying] categories of women, except for the believing emigrant women, and he prohibited every woman of a religion other than Islam. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in faith, his deeds have become worthless﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 5]. Talhah ibn ʿUbaydullah married a Jewish woman, and Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman married a Christian woman, and ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab became extremely angry, to the point that he intended to attack them both. They said: 'We will divorce them, O Commander of the Believers, so do not be angry!' He said: 'If their divorce is permitted, then their marriage is permitted, but I will take them from you as a humiliating, disgraceful [act]'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (4/364).]] — this is a very strange hadith, and this report from ʿUmar is also strange.

Abu Jaʿfar ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, said after relating the consensus (ijma', scholarly agreement) on the permissibility of marrying women of the People of the Book: "ʿUmar only disliked that so that people would not become averse to Muslim women, or for other meanings," as Abu Kurayb told us, Ibn Idris told us, al-Saltt ibn Bahram told us, from Shaqiq, who said: Hudhayfah married a Jewish woman, so ʿUmar wrote to him: "Release her," and he wrote back: "Do you consider her unlawful so that I should release her?" He said: "I do not consider her unlawful, but I fear that they [the Muslim men] may take up prostitutes from among them" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (4/366).]].

This is a sound chain (isnad). al-Khallal narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Waki', from al-Saltt [[In manuscript ج: "from al-Fadl."]] something similar.

Ibn Jarir also said: "Musa ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Masruqi told me, Muhammad ibn Bishr told us, Sufyan ibn Saʿid told us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Zayd ibn Wahb, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab [said] to me [[An addition from manuscript ج.]]: 'A Muslim may marry a Christian woman, but a Christian man may not marry a Muslim woman.'"

He said: "This is a more authentic chain than the first" [[In manuscript ج: "This is a more authentic chain than the first."]] [[Tafsir al-Tabari (4/367).]].

Then he said: "Tamim ibn al-Muntasir told us, Ishaq al-Azraq told us [[In manuscript أ: "Tamim ibn al-Muntasir told us, ʿUthman ibn al-Muntasir told us, Ishaq al-Azraq told us."]], from Sharik, from Ashʿath ibn Sawwar, from al-Hasan, from Jabir ibn ʿAbdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'We marry the women of the People of the Book, but they do not marry our women.'"

Then he said: "This report, although there is something [weak] in its chain, the acceptance of it is based on the consensus of the entire Ummah upon the validity of acting according to it" [[In manuscripts ج, أ, و: "the consensus of the entire Ummah upon it."]] [[Tafsir al-Tabari (4/367).]].

Thus said Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: "Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi told us, Waki' told us, from Jaʿfar ibn Burqan, from Maymun ibn Mihran, from Ibn ʿUmar: that he disliked marrying the People of the Book, and he interpreted [it as applying to them] with ﴿And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe﴾."

Al-Bukhari said: "Ibn ʿUmar said: 'I do not know of any polytheism greater than saying that her lord is ʿIsa.'" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5285), and it is here connected to Ibn ʿUmar.]]

Abu Bakr al-Khallal al-Hanbali said: "Muhammad ibn Harun [[In manuscripts أ, و: "Muhammad ibn Abi Harun."]] told us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim told us (ḥ) and Muhammad ibn ʿAli informed me, Salih ibn Ahmad told us, that both of them asked Abu ʿAbdullah Ahmad ibn Hanbal about the saying of Allah: ﴿And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe﴾. He said: 'The polytheistic women of the Arabs who worship idols [[In manuscripts ج, أ, و: "the idols."]].'"

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And a believing slave woman is better than a polytheist woman, even though she might please you﴾, al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning ʿAbdullah ibn Rawahah. He had a black slave woman, and he became angry with her and slapped her, then he regretted it and went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him of her matter. He said to him: "What is she like?" He said: "She fasts, prays, performs wudu' well, and testifies that there is no god but Allah and that you are the Messenger of Allah." He said: "O Abu ʿAbdullah, she is a believer." He said: "By the One who sent you with the truth, I will free her and marry her." He did so, and some Muslims criticized him, saying: "He married a slave woman." They wanted to marry [their women] to polytheists, and to marry [polytheists] for the sake of their lineages. So Allah revealed: ﴿And a believing slave woman is better than a polytheist woman, even though she might please you﴾ and ﴿And a believing slave is better than a polytheist, even though he might please you﴾.

ʿAbd ibn Humayd said: Jaʿfar ibn ʿAwn told us, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad al-Ifriqi told us, from ʿAbdullah ibn Yazid, from ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Do not marry women for their beauty, for their beauty may ruin them; and do not marry them for their wealth, for their wealth may make them rebellious; but marry them for religion. A black, split-eared slave woman who is religious is better." [[Al-Muntakhab of ʿAbd ibn Humayd, no. (328).]] Al-Ifriqi is weak.

It is established in the two Sahihs from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "A woman is married for four [things]: for her wealth, for her lineage, for her beauty, and for her religion. So win the one with religion; may your hands be rubbed with dust." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5090), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1466).]] Muslim has, from Jabir, something similar [[Sahih Muslim, no. (715).]]. And he has, from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The world is a provision, and the best provision of the world is a righteous woman." [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1457).]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And do not marry polytheist men [to your women] until they believe﴾, that is: do not marry believing women to polytheist men.

As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿They are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them﴾ [Al-Mumtahanah: 10].

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And a believing slave is better than a polytheist, even though he might please you﴾, that is: a believing man, even if he is an Abyssinian slave, is better than a polytheist, even if the latter is a chief or a nobleman. ﴿Those invite to the Fire﴾, that is: their company and association prompt love of the world, acquiring it, and preferring it over the Hereafter, and the consequence of that is grievous. ﴿But Allah invites to Paradise and forgiveness by His permission﴾, that is: by His legislation and what He commanded and what He forbade. ﴿And He makes clear His verses to the people that they may remember﴾.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 222–223 (part 1 of 5):

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas: The Jews, when a woman among them menstruated, would not eat with her, nor would they stay with her in the houses. The Companions of the Prophet [the Prophet] (the words in brackets are added from manuscripts A and W) ﷺ asked about this, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿They ask you about menstruation. Say: It is an harm, so keep away from women during menstruation, and do not approach them until they are purified. But when they have purified themselves﴾, until he finished the verse. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do everything except sexual intercourse (nikah)." This reached the Jews, and they said: "This man does not want to leave any of our affairs without opposing us in it!" Then Usayd ibn Hudayr and Abbad ibn Bishr came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the Jews have said such and such. Shall we not have intercourse with them?" The face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ changed until we thought that he was displeased with them both. So they left, and a gift of milk was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and met them. He sent after them and gave them to drink, and they understood that he was not displeased with them.

Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salama (al-Musnad 3/132 and Sahih Muslim no. 302).

So His saying ﴿keep away from women during menstruation﴾ means the vagina (al-farj), in accordance with his saying: "Do everything except sexual intercourse (al-nikah)." For this reason many of the scholars, or most of them, held that it is permissible to have physical contact with a menstruating woman in other than the vagina.

Abu Dawud said: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Ikrimah, from one of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ that the Prophet ﷺ, when he wanted something from a menstruating woman, would place a cloth over her vagina (Sunan Abi Dawud no. 272).

Abu Dawud also said: al-Qa'nabi narrated to us, Abd Allah, meaning ibn Umar ibn Ghanim, narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman, meaning ibn Ziyad, from Umara ibn Ghurab: that a paternal aunt of his told him that she asked Aisha, saying: "One of us menstruates, and she and her husband have only one bed?" She said: "I will tell you what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did: he came in and went to his place of prayer" — Abu Dawud said: she means the prayer place of her house — "and he did not leave until my eyes were overcome by sleep, and the cold troubled him, so he said: 'Come close to me.' I said: 'I am menstruating.' He said: 'Uncover your thighs.' So I uncovered my thighs, and he placed his cheek and chest on my thigh, and I warmed him until he was warm and slept ﷺ (Sunan Abi Dawud no. 270)."

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us, from the book of Abu Qilaba: that Masruq rode to Aisha and said: "Peace be upon the Prophet and upon his family." Aisha said: "Abu Aisha! Welcome, welcome." They gave him permission and he entered and said: "I wish to ask you about something, and I am shy." She said: "I am only your mother, and you are my son." He said: "What is lawful for a man from his wife when she is menstruating?" She said: "For him everything except her vagina (farj)" (Tafsir al-Tabari 4/378).

He also narrated it from Humayd ibn Mas'ada, from Yazid ibn Zuray', from Uyayna ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Jawshan, from Marwan al-Asfar, from Masruq who said: I said to Aisha: "What is lawful for a man from his wife when she is menstruating?" She said: "Everything except intercourse (al-jima')."

This is the view of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan and Ikrimah.

Ibn Jarir also narrated, from Abu Kurayb, from Ibn Abi Za'ida, from Hajjaj, from Maymun ibn Mihran, from Aisha who said: "For him is what is above the waist-wrapper (izar)."

I say: Lying beside her and eating with her is permitted without disagreement. Aisha said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to ask me to wash his head while I was menstruating, and he would recline in my lap while I was menstruating, and he would recite the Qur'an" (narrated by Muslim in his Sahih no. 297). In the Sahih, from her, she said: "I used to bite the meat from the bone while I was menstruating, and I would give it to the Prophet ﷺ, and he would put his mouth on the same place where I had put my mouth. I would drink the drink and pass it to him, and he would put his mouth on the same place from which I had drunk" (Sahih Muslim no. 300).

Abu Dawud said: Musaddad narrated to us, Yahya narrated to us, from Jabir ibn Subh (in manuscripts J, A and W: Sabih), I heard Khilas al-Hajari say: I heard Aisha say: "I and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would sleep in one garment, and I was menstruating, and if anything of mine touched him, he would wash that place and not go beyond it, and if anything (meaning his garment) touched him, he would wash that place and not go beyond it, and he would pray in it" (Sunan Abi Dawud no. 269).

As for what Abu Dawud narrated: Sa'id ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us, Abd al-Aziz (meaning ibn Muhammad) narrated to us, from Abu al-Yaman, from Umm Dharra, from Aisha: that she said: "When I menstruated, I would descend from the raised bed onto the mat, and we would not approach the Messenger of Allah ﷺ nor draw near to him until we were purified" (Sunan Abi Dawud no. 271) — this is to be understood as a matter of cleanliness and caution.

Others said: Only physical contact with her other than what is beneath the waist-wrapper is lawful for him, as established in the two Sahihs, from Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyyah who said: "When the Prophet ﷺ wanted to have physical contact with one of his wives, he would order her to tie on her waist-wrapper, while she was menstruating." This is the wording of al-Bukhari, and both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated similar from Aisha (Sahih al-Bukhari no. 303 and Sahih Muslim no. 294; and Sahih al-Bukhari no. 300 and Sahih Muslim no. 293).

Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of al-Ala' ibn al-Harith, from Hizam ibn Hakim, from his paternal uncle Abd Allah ibn Sa'd al-Ansari: that he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "What is lawful for me from my wife when she is menstruating?" He said: "What is above the waist-wrapper" (al-Musnad 4/342; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 212; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 133; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 651).

Abu Dawud also narrated, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about what is lawful for me from my wife when she is menstruating (Sunan Abi Dawud no. 213). He said: "What is above the waist-wrapper, and abstaining from that is better." This is also a narration from Aisha, as previously mentioned, and from Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, and Shurayh.

These hadiths and what resembles them are the evidence of those who hold that what is above the waist-wrapper is lawful from her. This is one of the two opinions in the school of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, which many of the Iraqis and others preferred. Their basis is that the area near the vagina is its protected surroundings (harim), so it is forbidden, lest one come to commit what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden, which the scholars have unanimously agreed is forbidden, namely physical contact in the vagina. Then whoever does that has sinned, so he should seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him. Is he then obliged to make expiation (kaffarah) along with that or not? On this there are two opinions:

The first: Yes, based on what Imam Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan narrated from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning one who comes to his wife while she is menstruating: "Let him give charity of a dinar or half a dinar" (al-Musnad 1/230; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 266; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 136; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 282). In a wording of al-Tirmidhi: "If it is red blood, then a dinar; and if it is yellow blood, then half a dinar." Also in Imam Ahmad, from him: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prescribed for a menstruating woman who is touched, a dinar; if he came to her when the blood had withdrawn from her and she had not yet washed, then half a dinar.

The second opinion, which is the correct and newer view of the school of al-Shafi'i and the view of the majority: there is nothing for this; rather he should seek forgiveness from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because this hadith was not established as attributed to the Prophet in their view, for it was narrated as marfu' as previously mentioned and also as mawquf, and this is the sound view according to many of the imams of hadith.

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿and do not approach them until they are purified﴾ explains His saying: ﴿keep away from women during menstruation﴾, and it is a prohibition on approaching them for intercourse as long as menstruation exists. Its implication is that it becomes lawful when it has ceased. Some of the early scholars also held this. Al-Qurtubi said: Mujahid, Ikrimah and Tawus said: the cessation of the blood makes her lawful for her husband, but only once she performs ablution (wudu').

* *

His saying: ﴿So when they have purified themselves, come to them from where Allah has commanded you﴾ contains a recommendation and guidance to having intercourse with them after bathing (ghusl). Ibn Hazm held that intercourse becomes obligatory after every menstrual period, based on His saying: ﴿So when they have purified themselves, come to them from where Allah has commanded you﴾. He has no evidence for this, because this is a command after a prohibition. Among the scholars of legal theory (usul) there are several views: some say it indicates obligation like an absolute command; those must answer Ibn Hazm. Others say it indicates permissibility, and they take the prior prohibition as a contextual indicator diverting it from obligation; this is open to scrutiny. What the evidence supports is that the ruling is returned to what it was before the prohibition: if it was obligatory, it is obligatory, like His saying: ﴿Then when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists﴾ [al-Tawbah: 5]; or permissible, it is permissible, like His saying: ﴿And when you are released from the state of ihram, then hunt﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 2], and ﴿Then when the prayer has been concluded, disperse in the land﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 10]. On this view the evidences are reconciled. Al-Ghazali and others related it, and some later imams chose it, and it is the sound view.

The scholars have agreed that when a woman's menstruation has ceased, she is not lawful until she performs ghusl with water, or tayammum if that is impossible for her under its conditions. [Except Yahya ibn Bukayr of the Malikis, who is one of the teachers of al-Bukhari, for he held the permissibility of intercourse with a woman merely upon the cessation of menstrual blood. Some attribute this also to Ibn Abd al-Hakam, and al-Qurtubi related it from Mujahid and Ikrimah from Tawus, as previously mentioned.] However, Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, says concerning the case where her blood ceases at the maximum period of menstruation, which in his view is ten days: she becomes lawful merely by the cessation, without needing ghusl; and for less than that, further lawfulness depends on ghusl, and the time of a prayer enters upon her, unless she is of a dimah type (with weak flow), in which case it enters by the mere cessation of it. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿until they are purified﴾, i.e. from the blood; ﴿when they have purified themselves﴾, i.e. with water. Likewise said Mujahid, Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Layth ibn Sa'd, and others.

* *

His saying: ﴿from where Allah has commanded you﴾. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said: it means the vagina. Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn Abbas: ﴿come to them from where Allah has commanded you﴾ means in the vagina, and do not go beyond it to anything else; whoever does any of that has transgressed.

Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Ikrimah said: ﴿come to them from where Allah has commanded you﴾ means: that you keep away from them. And there is in this then an indication of the prohibition of intercourse in the anus, as will be established shortly.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verses 222–223 (part 2 of 5):

Abu Razin, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak and others said: ﴿So go to them from where Allah has commanded you﴾ means: when they are pure, not menstruating. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are constantly repentant﴾, meaning, from sin, even if their intercourse is repeated, ﴿and He loves those who purify themselves﴾, meaning, those who keep themselves far from filth and harm, which includes what they were forbidden from, namely having intercourse with a menstruating woman, or in other than the place of sowing.[[In manuscript ج, "and if it happens repeatedly"; in ج, أ: "from".]]
* *
As for His saying: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you﴾, Ibn 'Abbas said: "The tilth is the place of the child." ﴿So come to your tilth as you wish﴾, meaning: however you wish, facing forward or from behind, in one orifice, as hadiths have established regarding this.
Al-Bukhari said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn al-Munkadir, who said: I heard Jabir say: The Jews used to say: "If a man has intercourse with his wife from behind, the child will be cross-eyed." So this was revealed: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth as you wish﴾. Dawud [and in manuscripts ج, أ, و: "Muslim and Abu Dawud"] also related it from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri with this chain.[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4528).]]
Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Malik ibn Anas, Ibn Jurayj and Sufyan ibn Sa'id al-Thawri informed me that Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to them that Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah informed him that the Jews said to the Muslims: "Whoever has intercourse with a woman while she is facing away, the child will be cross-eyed." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth as you wish﴾.
Ibn Jurayj said in the hadith: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Facing forward or from behind, provided it is in the vagina."
In the hadith of Bahz ibn Hakim ibn Mu'awiyah ibn Haydah al-Qushayri, from his father, from his grandfather, that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, of our wives, what may we approach and what must we leave?" He said: "Your tilth. Come to your tilth as you wish, except that you do not strike the face, nor revile, nor forsake except in the sleeping place [in manuscripts ج, أ, و: 'in the house']." The hadith [continues]. Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan related it.[[Musnad (5/3), Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2143), and al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Nasa'i, no. (9160).]]
Another hadith: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus narrated to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Ibn Lahi'ah informed me, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from 'Amir ibn Yahya, from Hanash ibn 'Abd Allah, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, who said: Some people from Himyar came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him about several matters. A man said to him: "I practise jabb with women (a manner of intercourse), so what is your view on this?" So Allah revealed: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you﴾.[[Also related by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (4/413) and al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/237), through Ibn Lahi'ah with this chain.]]
Another hadith: Abu Ja'far al-Tahawi said in his book "Mushkil al-Hadith": Ahmad ibn Dawud ibn Musa narrated to us, Ya'qub ibn Kasib narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Nafi' narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Sa'd, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: that a man had intercourse with his wife in her rear, and the people denounced him for this, so Allah revealed: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth as you wish﴾. Ibn Jarir also related it from Yunus and from Ya'qub, with this chain.[[Mushkil al-Athar, no. (6118).]]
Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: 'Affan narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khuthaym narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, who said: I entered upon Hafsah, daughter of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, and I said: "I am going to ask you about a matter, and I am shy to ask you." She said: "Do not be shy, nephew." He said: "Concerning intercourse with women in their rears?"
