She said: Umm Salamah narrated to me that the Ansar used not to practise jabb with women, and the Jews used to say: "Whoever practises jabb with his wife, the child will be cross-eyed." When the Muhajirun came to Madinah, they married women of the Ansar and practised jabb with them. A woman of the Ansar refused to obey her husband and said: "You will not do this until I go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." She entered upon Umm Salamah and mentioned this to her. Umm Salamah said: "Sit until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ comes." When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came, the Ansari woman was too shy to ask him, so she went out, and Umm Salamah informed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: "Call the Ansari woman." She was called, and he recited to her this verse: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth as you wish﴾, [and said:] "one orifice".
It was also related by al-Tirmidhi, from Bundar, from Ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan, from Ibn Khuthaym, with this chain.[[Musnad (6/304) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2979).]] He said: "Hasan" (good).
I say: It has also been related through the route of Hammad ibn Abi Hanifah, from his father, from Ibn Khuthaym, from Yusuf ibn Mahak, from Hafsah, Mother of the Believers: that a woman came to her and said: "My husband comes to me from the side and from the front, and I dislike that." This reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "There is no harm if it is in one orifice."[[Musnad Abi Hanifah, no. (102).]]
Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Ya'qub, that is al-Qummi, narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am ruined!" He said: "What has ruined you?" He said: "I turned my mount last night!" He said: The Prophet did not answer him at all. Then Allah revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ this verse: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth as you wish﴾, "approach from the front or from behind, but beware of the rear and of menstruation."
Al-Tirmidhi related it from 'Abd ibn Humayd, from Hasan ibn Musa al-Ashyab, with this chain.[[Musnad (1/297) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2980).]] He said: "Hasan gharib" (good, strange).
Imam Ahmad also said: Yahya ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, Rishdin narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Thawban narrated to me, from 'Amir ibn Yahya al-Ma'afiri, from Hanash, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: This verse was revealed: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you﴾ concerning some people of the Ansar who came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "Go to her in any state, provided it is in the vagina."[[Musnad (1/268).]]
Abu Ya'la al-Hafiz said: al-Harith ibn Suraij [in manuscript هـ: "Shurayh"] narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Nafi' narrated to us, Hisham ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id, who said: A man sodomised his wife during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they said: "So-and-so has sodomised his wife." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth as you wish﴾.[[Musnad Abi Ya'la (2/354). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (6/319): "His shaykh al-Harith ibn Suraij is weak and a liar, but he has been corroborated: Ya'qub ibn Humayd related it from 'Abd Allah ibn Nafi', from Hisham, from Zayd ibn Aslam with this chain, al-Tahawi related it in Mushkil al-Athar, no. (6118), and it has already been mentioned."]]
Abu Dawud said: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya Abu al-Asbagh narrated to us, saying: Muhammad, that is Ibn Salamah, narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Aban ibn Salih, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Indeed Ibn 'Umar, and Allah forgives him, made a mistake. The people of this clan of the Ansar, who were idolaters, were with the people of this clan of the Jews, who were People of the Book, and they regarded them as having superiority over them in knowledge, so they imitated many of their actions. Among the practices of the People of the Book was that they would not approach women except on one side, since that is the most concealing position for a woman. This clan of the Ansar adopted this practice from them. And this clan of Quraysh would approach women in a reprehensible manner and would enjoy them facing forward, from behind and lying on their backs. When the Muhajirun came to Madinah, a man of them married a woman of the Ansar and went to do that with her, and she objected to him and said: "We were only approached from one side. Do it that way, or else keep away from me." Their affair spread, and it reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so Allah revealed: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth as you wish﴾, that is: facing forward, from behind, and lying on the back, meaning by this the place of the child.[[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2164).]]
Abu Dawud alone related it, and what has preceded of the hadiths testifies to its soundness, especially the narration of Umm Salamah, for it resembles this context.
Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani also related this hadith through the route of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Aban ibn Salih, from Mujahid, who said: I presented the Mushaf to Ibn 'Abbas from its opening to its end, stopping at every verse and asking him about it, until I reached this verse: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth as you wish﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "This clan of Quraysh used to approach their women in Makkah and enjoy them..." and he mentioned the story in its full context.[[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/77).]]
As for Ibn 'Abbas's saying: "Indeed Ibn 'Umar, and Allah forgives him, made a mistake," it seems to refer to what al-Bukhari related:
Ishaq narrated to us, al-Nadr ibn Shumayl narrated to us, Ibn 'Awn informed us, from Nafi', who said: When Ibn 'Umar recited the Qur'an, he would not speak until he had finished it. One day I was with him, and he recited Surah al-Baqarah until he reached a place, and he said: "Do you know concerning what it was revealed?" I said: "No." He said: "It was revealed concerning such and such." Then he continued. And from 'Abd al-Samad, who said: My father narrated to me, Ayyub narrated to me, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, concerning ﴿So come to your tilth as you wish﴾, he said: "He comes to her in..." [There is a blank space in all manuscripts. In Fath al-Bari (8/130): "This is how it occurs in all the manuscripts; it does not mention what follows the adverbial phrase, which is the prepositional object. What appears in al-Jam' bayn al-Sahihayn of al-Humaydi is: 'He comes to her in the vagina,' and this is from his own understanding." Also taken from the margin of the Shu'ayb edition.]]
Thus al-Bukhari related it, and he alone transmitted it through these routes.[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4526).]]
Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, Ibn 'Awn narrated to us, from Nafi', who said: One day I recited: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth as you wish﴾, and Ibn 'Umar said: "Do you know concerning what it was revealed?" I said: "No." He said: "It was revealed concerning intercourse with women in their rears."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (4/404).]]
Abu Qilabah also narrated to me: 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Ayyub, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar: ﴿So come to your tilth as you wish﴾, he said: "In the rear."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (4/406).]]
It has also been related from the hadith of Malik, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, but it is not authentic.
Al-Nasa'i related, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Uways, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ibn 'Umar: that a man came to his wife in her rear, and he felt great remorse over that, so Allah revealed: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth as you wish﴾.[[Al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Nasa'i, no. (8981).]]
Abu Hatim al-Razi said: If this were with Zayd ibn Aslam from Ibn 'Umar, people would not have been so fond of Nafi'. This is his criticism of this hadith.
'Abd Allah ibn Nafi' related it from Dawud ibn Qays, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Ibn 'Umar, and so he mentioned it.

This is upon what came before, namely that he comes to her in her front passage from behind her, based on what al-Nasa'i also narrated from ʿAli ibn ʿUthman al-Nufayli, from Saʿid ibn ʿIsa, from al-Mufaddal[[In all the manuscripts: "al-Fadl," and the correct form is what we have adopted.]] ibn Fadala, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Sulayman al-Tawil, from Kaʿb ibn ʿAlqama, from Abu al-Nadr: that he told him that he said to Nafi', the freed slave of Ibn ʿUmar: "Indeed, it has been said much against you, that you say on the authority of Ibn ʿUmar that he issued a legal ruling that women may be approached in their rear passages." He said: "They have lied about me. But I will tell you how the matter actually was: Ibn ʿUmar once presented the Mushaf (the written codex of the Qur'an) while I was with him, until he reached: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so approach your tilth however you wish﴾. Then he said: 'O Nafi', do you know the context of this verse?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'We, the company of Quraysh, used to have intercourse with women in a dominating manner (lit. we used to lay women down). When we entered Medina and married women of the Ansar, we wanted from them the same as we used to want, but they disliked that and found it grave. The women of the Ansar had adopted the custom of the Jews, who only approached women on their sides. So Allah revealed: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so approach your tilth however you wish﴾.'" [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (8978).]]

This is a sound chain (isnad). It has also been narrated by Ibn Mardawayh, from al-Tabarani, from al-Husayn ibn Ishaq, from Zakariyya[[In manuscript A: "from Abu Zakariyya."]] ibn Yahya al-Katib al-ʿUmari, from Mufaddal ibn Fadala, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAyyash[[In manuscript A: "ʿAbbas."]] from Kaʿb ibn ʿAlqama, and so on. We have also related from Ibn ʿUmar explicit reports to the contrary, and that it is neither permissible nor lawful, as will come. Although this view has been attributed to a group of the jurists of Medina and others, some have attributed it to Imam Malik in the book Kitab al-Sirr[[In manuscript A: "al-Sayr."]], but most people deny that this is authentically from Imam Malik, may Allah have mercy on him.

Hadiths reported through many routes have come prohibiting this act and engaging in it. Al-Hasan ibn ʿArafa said:
"Ismaʿil ibn ʿAyyash[[In manuscript A: "ʿAbbas."]] narrated to us, from Suhayl[[In manuscripts J and A: "from Sahl."]] ibn Abi Salih, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Be modest, for Allah is not shy of the truth. It is not lawful to approach women in their anuses.'" [[Also narrated by al-Daraqutni in al-Sunan (3/288) by way of al-Hasan ibn ʿArafa.]]

Imam Ahmad said: "ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from ʿAbd[[In manuscripts J and A: "from ʿAbd Allah."]] ibn Shaddad, from a man, from Khuzayma ibn Thabit: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade a man to approach his wife in her rear." [[al-Musnad (5/215); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, nos. (8985, 8986); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (1924). See the variant readings in it in Sunan al-Nasa'i (5/316-319).]]

Another route: Ahmad said: "Yaʿqub narrated to us, I heard my father narrate, from Yazid ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Usama ibn al-Had: that ʿUbayd Allah ibn al-Husayn al-Walibi narrated to him that Harami ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Waqifi narrated to him that Khuzayma ibn Thabit al-Khatmi narrated to him that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Allah is not shy of the truth; Allah is not shy of the truth' (three times), 'Do not approach women in their backsides.'"

al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated it through several routes, from Khuzayma ibn Thabit, and its chain contains much disagreement.

Another hadith: Abu ʿIsa al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i said: "Abu Saʿid al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, from al-Dahhak ibn ʿUthman, from Makhrama ibn Sulayman, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Allah does not look at a man who approaches a man or a woman in the rear.'" Then al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hadith that is hasan (good) and gharib (singular)." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (1165); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (9001).]] Ibn Hibban also narrated it in his Sahih in this way [[Sahih Ibn Hibban, no. (1302), "Mawarid" edition.]]. Ibn Hazm also authenticated it. However, al-Nasa'i narrated it from Hannad, from Waki', from al-Dahhak, with the same wording, as a mawquf (a report ending at a Companion, not traced to the Prophet).

ʿAbd said: "ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, Maʿmar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father: that a man asked Ibn ʿAbbas about approaching a woman in her rear. He said: 'You ask me about disbelief!'" [Sound chain] [[Addition from manuscripts J, A, and H.]]

Likewise al-Nasa'i narrated it through the route of Ibn al-Mubarak, from Maʿmar, with a similar wording.[[In manuscript H: "from ʿIkrima," which is an error.]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: "ʿAbd al-Samad narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us, Qatada narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'The one who approaches his wife in her rear is the lesser Lut (sodomite).'" [[al-Musnad (2/210).]]

ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad said: "Hudba narrated to me, Hammam narrated to us, he said: Qatada was asked about the one who approaches his wife in her rear. Qatada said: 'ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "It is the lesser Lut."'"
Qatada said: "ʿUqba ibn Wassaj also narrated to me, from Abu al-Darda', who said: 'Does anyone do that except a disbeliever?'" [[Zawa'id al-Musnad (2/210).]]

This hadith was also narrated by Yahya ibn Saʿid al-Qattan, from Saʿid ibn Abi ʿArouba, from Qatada, from Abu Ayyub, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs, as his own statement (qawl). This is more authentic, and Allah knows best.

Likewise, ʿAbd ibn Humayd narrated it from Yazid ibn Harun, from Humayd al-Aʿraj, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, as a mawquf report, from his own statement.

Another route: Jaʿfar al-Firyabi said: "Qutayba narrated to us, Ibn Lahiʿa narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad ibn al-ʿAm, from Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Seven are those whom Allah will not look at on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and He will say: Enter the Fire with those who enter: the one who does and the one to whom it is done, the one who masturbates, the one who has intercourse with an animal, the one who has intercourse with a woman in her rear, the one who has intercourse with a woman and her daughter, the one who commits adultery with his neighbor's wife, and the one who harms his neighbor until he curses him.'" [[Narrated by Abu al-Shaykh in Majlis min Hadithih (62/1, 2), and Ibn Bishran in al-Amali (86/1, 2), through several routes from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad al-Afriqi. End of quote, drawn from Irwa' al-Ghalil by al-Albani (8/59).]]

Ibn Lahiʿa and his shaykh are both weak.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: "ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Sufyan informed us, from ʿAsim, from ʿIsa ibn Hittan, from Muslim ibn Salam, from ʿAli ibn Talq, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade that women be approached in their rear passages, for Allah is not shy of the truth." [[Ibn Hajar mentioned it in Atraf al-Musnad (4/384), but I did not find it in the printed edition.]]

Ahmad also narrated it from Abu Muʿawiya, and Abu ʿIsa al-Tirmidhi narrated it by way of Abu Muʿawiya, from ʿAsim al-Ahwal [[Addition from manuscripts J and A.]], with an addition in it, and said: "This is a hadith that is hasan." [[Mentioned by al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar in Atraf al-Musnad (4/384); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (1164).]]

Some people cite this hadith in the Musnad of ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, as it appears in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal [[al-Musnad (1/86).]], but the correct attribution is that it is from ʿAli ibn Talq.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: "ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from al-Harith ibn Mukhalled, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed, the one who approaches his wife in her rear, Allah does not look at him.'"

ʿAffan narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Suhayl narrated to us, from al-Harith ibn Makhlad, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: [[In manuscripts A and H: "from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet."]] "Allah does not look at a man who has intercourse with his wife in her rear."

Ibn Majah also narrated it through the route of Suhayl. [[al-Musnad (2/344); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (1923).]]

Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from al-Harith ibn Makhlad, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Cursed is the one who approaches a woman in her rear."

In this same way Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated it through the route of Waki'. [[al-Musnad (2/444); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2162); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (9015).]]

Another route: al-Hafiz Abu Nuʿaym al-Isfahani said: "Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Rayyan informed us, Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Nasa'i narrated to us, Hannad and Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, and the wording is his, they said: Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Cursed is the one who approaches a woman in her rear.'" [[Narrated by Abu Nuʿaym in a part of his, ʿAli (high-chain), from Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Rayyan. Al-Dhahabi said: "There is in it what is objectionable."]]

This hadith is not worded this way in the Sunan of al-Nasa'i. What is in it is from Suhayl, from al-Harith ibn Makhlad, as already mentioned.

Our shaykh, al-Hafiz Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Dhahabi, said: "The narration of Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Rayyan of this hadith with this chain is an error on his part, and they have declared him weak."

Another route: Muslim ibn Khalid al-Zanji narrated it, from al-ʿAla' ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Cursed is the one who approaches women in their rear passages."

There is some discussion about Muslim ibn Khalid, and Allah knows best.

Another route: Imam Ahmad and the compilers of the Sunan narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salama, from Hakim al-Athram, from Abu Tamima al-Hujaymi, from Abu Hurayra: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever comes to a menstruating woman, or to a woman in her rear, or to a soothsayer and believes him, has disbelieved in what was revealed to Muhammad." [[al-Musnad (2/408); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (3904); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (135); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (9016); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (639).]]

al-Tirmidhi said: "al-Bukhari declared this hadith weak." What al-Bukhari said about the hadith of Hakim [al-Athram][[Addition from manuscripts J and A; in manuscript W: "Hakim al-Tirmidhi."]] from Abu Tamima is: "It is not corroborated in his hadith." [[al-Tarikh al-Kabir (3/17).]]

Another route: al-Nasa'i said: "ʿUthman ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, Sulayman ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us from his book, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Muhammad al-San'ani, from Saʿid ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: 'Be shy before Allah with true shyness; do not approach women in their rear passages.'" [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (9010).]]

Al-Nasa'i alone narrated it through this route.

Hamza ibn Muhammad al-Kinani, the hafiz, said: "This is a munkar (rejected) and batil (false) hadith, from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from the hadith of Abu Salama, and from the hadith of Saʿid. If ʿAbd al-Malik heard it from Saʿid, then he heard it after his confusion (ikhtilat). Al-Zuhri narrated from Abu Salama that he used to forbid this; but as for [the attribution] from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), no." End of his statement.

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 222–223 (part 4 of 5):

He (the critic) did well and made an excellent critique. However, 'Abd al-Malik [ibn Muhammad] [[Addition from manuscripts ج, أ, و.]] al-San'ani is not known to have become confused (ikhtilat, loss of memory). No one mentioned this except Hamzah al-Kinani, and he is trustworthy. Yet Duhaym, Abu Hatim, and Ibn Hibban criticized him, and Ibn Hibban said: "It is not permissible to use him as evidence." Allah knows best. Zayd ibn Yahya ibn [[In manuscript ج: "'an" (from).]] 'Ubayd followed him, from Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz. It was also narrated by two other chains from Abu Salamah, but nothing from them is authentic.

Another chain: al-Nasa'i said: Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Mujahid, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "A man having intercourse with women in their anuses is disbelief (kufr)."

Then he narrated it from Bundar, from 'Abd al-Rahman, with the same chain, and said: "Whoever has intercourse with his wife in her anus has committed disbelief." Thus al-Nasa'i narrated it through al-Thawri, from Layth, from Mujahid, from Abu Hurayrah, as a mawquf (a report ending with a Companion, not traced to the Prophet). Likewise he narrated it through 'Ali ibn Badhimah, from Mujahid, from Abu Hurayrah, as a mawquf. Bakr ibn Khunays narrated it from Layth, from Mujahid, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever has intercourse with any man or woman in the anus has disbelieved." The mawquf version is more authentic. Bakr ibn Khunays was declared weak by several imams, and others abandoned him. [[Narrated by al-'Uqayli in al-Du'afa' al-Kabir (1/149).]]

Another hadith: Muhammad ibn Aban al-Balkhi said: Waki' narrated to us, Zam'ah ibn Salih narrated to us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, and from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid ibn al-Hadi, both of whom said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah is not shy of the truth. Do not approach women in their anuses." [[Mentioned by al-Daraqutni in al-'Ilal (2/167). He said: "He did not mention Tawus in the hadith of 'Amr ibn Dinar, and the saying of 'Uthman ibn al-Yaman is the most authentic."]]

Al-Nasa'i also narrated it: Sa'id ibn Ya'qub al-Taliqani narrated to us, from 'Uthman ibn al-Yaman, from Zam'ah ibn Salih, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn al-Hadi, from 'Umar, who said: "Do not approach women in their anuses." [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (9008).]]

And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Yazid ibn Abi Hakim narrated to us, from Zam'ah ibn Salih, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Tawus, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Hadi al-Laythi, who said: 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Be shy before Allah, for Allah is not shy of the truth. Do not approach women in their anuses." [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (9009).]] The mawquf version is more authentic.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ghundar and Mu'adh ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, both saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from 'Isa ibn Hittan, from Muslim ibn Salam, from Talq ibn Yazid, or Yazid ibn Talq, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed Allah is not shy of the truth. Do not approach women in their buttocks." [[Ibn Hajar mentioned it in Atraf al-Musnad (4/384) through Ghundar's chain in the Musnad of 'Ali ibn Talq. I do not know how "Yazid ibn Talq" came about here, and Ibn Hajar clarified the correct version, Allah knows best.]]

It was similarly narrated by more than one person from Shu'bah. 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated it from Ma'mar, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from 'Isa ibn Hittan, from Muslim ibn Salam, from Talq ibn 'Ali, but the most likely is that it is 'Ali ibn Talq, as mentioned earlier. Allah knows best.

Another hadith: Abu Bakr al-Athram said in his Sunan: Abu Muslim al-Harami narrated to us, my brother Unays ibn Ibrahim narrated to us [[In manuscript أ: "my brother Unays ibn Abi Tamim".]] that his father Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qa'qa' informed him, from his father Abu al-Qa'qa', from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The private parts of women are forbidden." [[Also narrated by al-Dulabi in al-Kuna (2/85).]]

It was also narrated by Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah, Sufyan al-Thawri, Shu'bah, and others, from Abu 'Abd Allah al-Shaqiri, whose name is Salamah ibn Tamam, who is trustworthy, from Abu al-Qa'qa', from Ibn Mas'ud as a mawquf. This is more authentic.

Another chain: Ibn 'Adi said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Muhamili narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Hamzah narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Rufay', from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not approach women in their rear parts." [[Al-Kamil li-Ibn 'Adi (3/206).]] Muhammad ibn Hamzah is al-Jazari, and his teacher has been criticized in both cases.

It has also been narrated from the hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, Abu Dharr, and others. [[The hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka'b was narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman (no. 5457) through Abu Qilabah, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b. The hadith of 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir was narrated by Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil (4/148) through Ibn Lahi'ah, from Mishrah ibn Ha'an, from 'Uqbah.]] Each of them has criticism that prevents the hadith from being authenticated. Allah knows best.

Al-Thawri said, from al-Salt ibn Bahram, from Abu al-Mu'tamir, from Abu Juwayriyah [[In manuscript ج: "from Abu Jurayr"; in manuscript أ: "from Abu Juwayrah".]]: A man asked 'Ali about having intercourse with a woman in her anus. He said: "You have fallen low, may Allah cause you to fall! Have you not heard the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Do you commit such an abomination as no one in the worlds has committed before you?﴾ [al-A'raf: 80]."

The sayings of Ibn Mas'ud, Abu al-Darda', Abu Hurayrah, Ibn 'Abbas, and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr regarding the prohibition of this have already been mentioned. It is also established without doubt from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) that he prohibited it.

Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi said in his Musnad: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to us, from al-Harith ibn Ya'qub, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, Abu al-Hubab, who said: I said to Ibn 'Umar: "What do you say about slave girls? Do we make them 'tahmid' (a term for anal intercourse) for them?" He said: "What is tahmid?" Then he mentioned the rear. He said: "Does anyone among the Muslims do that?"

Ibn Wahb and Qutaybah also narrated it from al-Layth with the same chain. This is a sound chain and an explicit text prohibiting it. Thus, whatever is reported from him that could be interpreted in more than one way is referred back to this clear (muhkam) ruling.

Ibn Jarir said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, Abu Zayd 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad ibn Abi al-Ghamr narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim narrated to me, from Malik ibn Anas that it was said to him: "O Abu 'Abd Allah, people narrate from Salim ibn 'Abd Allah that he said: 'The slave, or the uncouth one, lied about my father [['Abd Allah]].'" [[Addition from manuscript ج.]] Malik said: "I testify about Yazid ibn Ruman that he told me, from Salim ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ibn 'Umar, the same as what Nafi' said." He was asked: "Al-Harith ibn Ya'qub narrates from Abu al-Hubab Sa'id ibn Yasar that he asked Ibn 'Umar, and he said to him: 'O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, we buy slave girls, do we make tahmid for them?' He said: 'What is tahmid?' So he mentioned the rear to him. Ibn 'Umar said: 'Uff! Uff! Would a believer (or he said: a Muslim) do that?'" Malik said: "I testify about Rabi'ah that he told me, from Abu al-Hubab, from Ibn 'Umar, the same as what Nafi' said." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (4/405).]]

Al-Nasa'i narrated, from al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman, from Asbagh ibn al-Faraj al-Faqih, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: I said to Malik: "Among us in Egypt is al-Layth ibn Sa'd, who narrates from al-Harith ibn Ya'qub, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said: I said to Ibn 'Umar: 'We buy slave girls, do we make tahmid for them?' He said: 'What is tahmid?' I said: 'We approach them in their rear parts.' He said: 'Uff! Uff! Does a Muslim do this?'" Malik said to me: "I testify about Rabi'ah that he narrated to me from Sa'id ibn Yasar that he asked Ibn 'Umar, and he said: 'There is no harm in it.'" [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (8979).]]

Al-Nasa'i also narrated through Yazid ibn Ruman, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, that Ibn 'Umar did not see any harm in a man approaching his wife in her rear. [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (8980).]]

Ma'n ibn 'Isa narrated from Malik that this is forbidden.

Abu Bakr ibn Ziyad al-Naysaburi said: Isma'il ibn Husayn narrated to me, and Isra'il ibn Rawh narrated to me: I asked Malik ibn Anas: "What do you say about having intercourse with women in their anuses?" He said: "Are you not an Arab people? Is tilth anything other than the place of sowing? Do not go beyond the vagina." I said: "O Abu 'Abd Allah, they say that you say this?!" He said: "They lie about me, they lie about me."

This is what is established from him, and it is the view of Abu Hanifah, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and all their companions. It is also the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Abu Salamah, 'Ikrimah, Tawus, 'Ata', Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Mujahid ibn Jabr, al-Hasan, and others among the early generations (al-salaf). They denounced it most strongly, and some of them applied the term disbelief to the one who does it. This is the position of the majority of scholars (jumhur al-'ulama').

Something has been reported on this from some jurists of Madinah, to the extent that they attributed it to Imam Malik, but its authenticity from him is questionable.

[Ibn Jarir, in his book on marriage, which he compiled, narrated from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la, from Ibn Wahb, its permissibility.] [[Addition from manuscripts ج, أ, و.]]

al-Tahawi said: Asbagh ibn al-Faraj narrated from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, who said: "I have not found anyone whom I follow in my religion who doubts that it is permissible." He meant intercourse with a woman in her anus. Then he recited: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 223], and then said: "What could be clearer than this?" This is al-Tahawi's report.

Al-Hakim, al-Daraqutni, and al-Khatib al-Baghdadi narrated from Imam Malik, through various chains, what suggests permissibility. But there is severe weakness in the chains, and our shaykh, the hafiz Abu 'Abd Allah al-Dhahabi, thoroughly examined them in a juz' (booklet) he compiled on this subject. Allah knows best.

al-Tahawi said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam told us that he heard al-Shafi'i say: "Nothing has been authentically reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding its permissibility or its prohibition. Analogy (qiyas) indicates that it is permissible." This was also narrated by Abu Bakr al-Khatib, from Abu Sa'id al-Sayrafi, from Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam say: I heard al-Shafi'i say ... and he mentioned it. Abu Nasr al-Sabbagh said: al-Rabi' used to swear by Allah, there is no god but He: "Ibn 'Abd al-Hakam lied about al-Shafi'i regarding this, for al-Shafi'i explicitly stated its prohibition in six of his books." Allah knows best.

Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir: Among those to whom this opinion is attributed, namely the permissibility of intercourse with a woman in her rear passage, are Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Nafi', Ibn 'Umar, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Majishun. This opinion is found in al-'Utbiyya. It is also reported from Malik in a book of his called Kitab al-Sirr (the Book of the Secret), but the leading scholars and shaykhs of Malik's companions deny that this book is his, and Malik is too exalted to have a book called Kitab al-Sirr. This opinion occurs in al-'Utbiyya. Ibn al-'Arabi mentioned that Ibn Sha'ban attributed this opinion to a large group of the Companions and the Successors, and to Malik through many narrations, from the book Jima' al-Nisa' and Ahkam al-Quran. This is his wording. He said: al-Kiya al-Harrasi al-Tabari reported from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi that he used as evidence for its permissibility the verse: ﴿Do you approach males from among the worlds, and leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses? Rather, you are a transgressing people﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 26:165-166].

That is, it is like the permissible things. Then he refuted it by saying that what is meant by what Allah created for them is the private parts of women, not their rear passages. I say: This is the correct view, and what al-Qurazi said, if it is indeed reported from him, is an error. People have written many works on this issue, among them Abu al-'Abbas al-Qurtubi, who named his book Ithhar Idbar man Ajaza al-Wat' fi al-Adbar (Exposing the Backs of Those Who Permitted Intercourse in the Rear Passages).

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And send ahead for yourselves﴾ means: through performing acts of obedience, along with complying with what He has forbidden you of abandoning the prohibited things. For this reason He said: ﴿And fear Allah, and know that you will meet Him﴾, meaning: He will hold you accountable for all your deeds.

﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾, meaning: those who obey Allah in what He has commanded them and who abandon what He has warned them against.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Qasim narrated to us, Husayn narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to me, from 'Abd Allah ibn Waqid, from 'Ata' — he said: I think he reported it from Ibn 'Abbas — regarding ﴿And send ahead for yourselves﴾, he said: it means saying "In the name of Allah," the basmala at intercourse.

It is established in Sahih al-Bukhari, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If one of them, when he intends to approach his wife, says: 'In the name of Allah. O Allah, keep Satan away from us, and keep Satan away from what You provide us,' then if a child is decreed for them from that union, Satan will never harm it." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 141].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 222–223 (part 1 of 5):

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas: The Jews, when a woman among them menstruated, would not eat with her, nor would they stay with her in the houses. The Companions of the Prophet [the Prophet] (the words in brackets are added from manuscripts A and W) ﷺ asked about this, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿They ask you about menstruation. Say: It is an harm, so keep away from women during menstruation, and do not approach them until they are purified. But when they have purified themselves﴾, until he finished the verse. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do everything except sexual intercourse (nikah)." This reached the Jews, and they said: "This man does not want to leave any of our affairs without opposing us in it!" Then Usayd ibn Hudayr and Abbad ibn Bishr came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the Jews have said such and such. Shall we not have intercourse with them?" The face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ changed until we thought that he was displeased with them both. So they left, and a gift of milk was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and met them. He sent after them and gave them to drink, and they understood that he was not displeased with them.

Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salama (al-Musnad 3/132 and Sahih Muslim no. 302).

So His saying ﴿keep away from women during menstruation﴾ means the vagina (al-farj), in accordance with his saying: "Do everything except sexual intercourse (al-nikah)." For this reason many of the scholars, or most of them, held that it is permissible to have physical contact with a menstruating woman in other than the vagina.

Abu Dawud said: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Ikrimah, from one of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ that the Prophet ﷺ, when he wanted something from a menstruating woman, would place a cloth over her vagina (Sunan Abi Dawud no. 272).

Abu Dawud also said: al-Qa'nabi narrated to us, Abd Allah, meaning ibn Umar ibn Ghanim, narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman, meaning ibn Ziyad, from Umara ibn Ghurab: that a paternal aunt of his told him that she asked Aisha, saying: "One of us menstruates, and she and her husband have only one bed?" She said: "I will tell you what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did: he came in and went to his place of prayer" — Abu Dawud said: she means the prayer place of her house — "and he did not leave until my eyes were overcome by sleep, and the cold troubled him, so he said: 'Come close to me.' I said: 'I am menstruating.' He said: 'Uncover your thighs.' So I uncovered my thighs, and he placed his cheek and chest on my thigh, and I warmed him until he was warm and slept ﷺ (Sunan Abi Dawud no. 270)."

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us, from the book of Abu Qilaba: that Masruq rode to Aisha and said: "Peace be upon the Prophet and upon his family." Aisha said: "Abu Aisha! Welcome, welcome." They gave him permission and he entered and said: "I wish to ask you about something, and I am shy." She said: "I am only your mother, and you are my son." He said: "What is lawful for a man from his wife when she is menstruating?" She said: "For him everything except her vagina (farj)" (Tafsir al-Tabari 4/378).

He also narrated it from Humayd ibn Mas'ada, from Yazid ibn Zuray', from Uyayna ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Jawshan, from Marwan al-Asfar, from Masruq who said: I said to Aisha: "What is lawful for a man from his wife when she is menstruating?" She said: "Everything except intercourse (al-jima')."

This is the view of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan and Ikrimah.

Ibn Jarir also narrated, from Abu Kurayb, from Ibn Abi Za'ida, from Hajjaj, from Maymun ibn Mihran, from Aisha who said: "For him is what is above the waist-wrapper (izar)."

I say: Lying beside her and eating with her is permitted without disagreement. Aisha said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to ask me to wash his head while I was menstruating, and he would recline in my lap while I was menstruating, and he would recite the Qur'an" (narrated by Muslim in his Sahih no. 297). In the Sahih, from her, she said: "I used to bite the meat from the bone while I was menstruating, and I would give it to the Prophet ﷺ, and he would put his mouth on the same place where I had put my mouth. I would drink the drink and pass it to him, and he would put his mouth on the same place from which I had drunk" (Sahih Muslim no. 300).

Abu Dawud said: Musaddad narrated to us, Yahya narrated to us, from Jabir ibn Subh (in manuscripts J, A and W: Sabih), I heard Khilas al-Hajari say: I heard Aisha say: "I and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would sleep in one garment, and I was menstruating, and if anything of mine touched him, he would wash that place and not go beyond it, and if anything (meaning his garment) touched him, he would wash that place and not go beyond it, and he would pray in it" (Sunan Abi Dawud no. 269).

As for what Abu Dawud narrated: Sa'id ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us, Abd al-Aziz (meaning ibn Muhammad) narrated to us, from Abu al-Yaman, from Umm Dharra, from Aisha: that she said: "When I menstruated, I would descend from the raised bed onto the mat, and we would not approach the Messenger of Allah ﷺ nor draw near to him until we were purified" (Sunan Abi Dawud no. 271) — this is to be understood as a matter of cleanliness and caution.

Others said: Only physical contact with her other than what is beneath the waist-wrapper is lawful for him, as established in the two Sahihs, from Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyyah who said: "When the Prophet ﷺ wanted to have physical contact with one of his wives, he would order her to tie on her waist-wrapper, while she was menstruating." This is the wording of al-Bukhari, and both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated similar from Aisha (Sahih al-Bukhari no. 303 and Sahih Muslim no. 294; and Sahih al-Bukhari no. 300 and Sahih Muslim no. 293).

Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of al-Ala' ibn al-Harith, from Hizam ibn Hakim, from his paternal uncle Abd Allah ibn Sa'd al-Ansari: that he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "What is lawful for me from my wife when she is menstruating?" He said: "What is above the waist-wrapper" (al-Musnad 4/342; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 212; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 133; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 651).

Abu Dawud also narrated, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about what is lawful for me from my wife when she is menstruating (Sunan Abi Dawud no. 213). He said: "What is above the waist-wrapper, and abstaining from that is better." This is also a narration from Aisha, as previously mentioned, and from Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, and Shurayh.

These hadiths and what resembles them are the evidence of those who hold that what is above the waist-wrapper is lawful from her. This is one of the two opinions in the school of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, which many of the Iraqis and others preferred. Their basis is that the area near the vagina is its protected surroundings (harim), so it is forbidden, lest one come to commit what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden, which the scholars have unanimously agreed is forbidden, namely physical contact in the vagina. Then whoever does that has sinned, so he should seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him. Is he then obliged to make expiation (kaffarah) along with that or not? On this there are two opinions:

The first: Yes, based on what Imam Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan narrated from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning one who comes to his wife while she is menstruating: "Let him give charity of a dinar or half a dinar" (al-Musnad 1/230; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 266; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 136; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 282). In a wording of al-Tirmidhi: "If it is red blood, then a dinar; and if it is yellow blood, then half a dinar." Also in Imam Ahmad, from him: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prescribed for a menstruating woman who is touched, a dinar; if he came to her when the blood had withdrawn from her and she had not yet washed, then half a dinar.

The second opinion, which is the correct and newer view of the school of al-Shafi'i and the view of the majority: there is nothing for this; rather he should seek forgiveness from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because this hadith was not established as attributed to the Prophet in their view, for it was narrated as marfu' as previously mentioned and also as mawquf, and this is the sound view according to many of the imams of hadith.

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿and do not approach them until they are purified﴾ explains His saying: ﴿keep away from women during menstruation﴾, and it is a prohibition on approaching them for intercourse as long as menstruation exists. Its implication is that it becomes lawful when it has ceased. Some of the early scholars also held this. Al-Qurtubi said: Mujahid, Ikrimah and Tawus said: the cessation of the blood makes her lawful for her husband, but only once she performs ablution (wudu').

* *

His saying: ﴿So when they have purified themselves, come to them from where Allah has commanded you﴾ contains a recommendation and guidance to having intercourse with them after bathing (ghusl). Ibn Hazm held that intercourse becomes obligatory after every menstrual period, based on His saying: ﴿So when they have purified themselves, come to them from where Allah has commanded you﴾. He has no evidence for this, because this is a command after a prohibition. Among the scholars of legal theory (usul) there are several views: some say it indicates obligation like an absolute command; those must answer Ibn Hazm. Others say it indicates permissibility, and they take the prior prohibition as a contextual indicator diverting it from obligation; this is open to scrutiny. What the evidence supports is that the ruling is returned to what it was before the prohibition: if it was obligatory, it is obligatory, like His saying: ﴿Then when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists﴾ [al-Tawbah: 5]; or permissible, it is permissible, like His saying: ﴿And when you are released from the state of ihram, then hunt﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 2], and ﴿Then when the prayer has been concluded, disperse in the land﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 10]. On this view the evidences are reconciled. Al-Ghazali and others related it, and some later imams chose it, and it is the sound view.

The scholars have agreed that when a woman's menstruation has ceased, she is not lawful until she performs ghusl with water, or tayammum if that is impossible for her under its conditions. [Except Yahya ibn Bukayr of the Malikis, who is one of the teachers of al-Bukhari, for he held the permissibility of intercourse with a woman merely upon the cessation of menstrual blood. Some attribute this also to Ibn Abd al-Hakam, and al-Qurtubi related it from Mujahid and Ikrimah from Tawus, as previously mentioned.] However, Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, says concerning the case where her blood ceases at the maximum period of menstruation, which in his view is ten days: she becomes lawful merely by the cessation, without needing ghusl; and for less than that, further lawfulness depends on ghusl, and the time of a prayer enters upon her, unless she is of a dimah type (with weak flow), in which case it enters by the mere cessation of it. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿until they are purified﴾, i.e. from the blood; ﴿when they have purified themselves﴾, i.e. with water. Likewise said Mujahid, Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Layth ibn Sa'd, and others.

* *

His saying: ﴿from where Allah has commanded you﴾. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said: it means the vagina. Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn Abbas: ﴿come to them from where Allah has commanded you﴾ means in the vagina, and do not go beyond it to anything else; whoever does any of that has transgressed.

Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Ikrimah said: ﴿come to them from where Allah has commanded you﴾ means: that you keep away from them. And there is in this then an indication of the prohibition of intercourse in the anus, as will be established shortly.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verses 222–223 (part 2 of 5):

Abu Razin, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak and others said: ﴿So go to them from where Allah has commanded you﴾ means: when they are pure, not menstruating. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are constantly repentant﴾, meaning, from sin, even if their intercourse is repeated, ﴿and He loves those who purify themselves﴾, meaning, those who keep themselves far from filth and harm, which includes what they were forbidden from, namely having intercourse with a menstruating woman, or in other than the place of sowing.[[In manuscript ج, "and if it happens repeatedly"; in ج, أ: "from".]]
* *
As for His saying: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you﴾, Ibn 'Abbas said: "The tilth is the place of the child." ﴿So come to your tilth as you wish﴾, meaning: however you wish, facing forward or from behind, in one orifice, as hadiths have established regarding this.
Al-Bukhari said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn al-Munkadir, who said: I heard Jabir say: The Jews used to say: "If a man has intercourse with his wife from behind, the child will be cross-eyed." So this was revealed: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth as you wish﴾. Dawud [and in manuscripts ج, أ, و: "Muslim and Abu Dawud"] also related it from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri with this chain.[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4528).]]
Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Malik ibn Anas, Ibn Jurayj and Sufyan ibn Sa'id al-Thawri informed me that Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to them that Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah informed him that the Jews said to the Muslims: "Whoever has intercourse with a woman while she is facing away, the child will be cross-eyed." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth as you wish﴾.
Ibn Jurayj said in the hadith: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Facing forward or from behind, provided it is in the vagina."
In the hadith of Bahz ibn Hakim ibn Mu'awiyah ibn Haydah al-Qushayri, from his father, from his grandfather, that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, of our wives, what may we approach and what must we leave?" He said: "Your tilth. Come to your tilth as you wish, except that you do not strike the face, nor revile, nor forsake except in the sleeping place [in manuscripts ج, أ, و: 'in the house']." The hadith [continues]. Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan related it.[[Musnad (5/3), Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2143), and al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Nasa'i, no. (9160).]]
Another hadith: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus narrated to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Ibn Lahi'ah informed me, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from 'Amir ibn Yahya, from Hanash ibn 'Abd Allah, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, who said: Some people from Himyar came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him about several matters. A man said to him: "I practise jabb with women (a manner of intercourse), so what is your view on this?" So Allah revealed: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you﴾.[[Also related by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (4/413) and al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/237), through Ibn Lahi'ah with this chain.]]
Another hadith: Abu Ja'far al-Tahawi said in his book "Mushkil al-Hadith": Ahmad ibn Dawud ibn Musa narrated to us, Ya'qub ibn Kasib narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Nafi' narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Sa'd, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: that a man had intercourse with his wife in her rear, and the people denounced him for this, so Allah revealed: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth as you wish﴾. Ibn Jarir also related it from Yunus and from Ya'qub, with this chain.[[Mushkil al-Athar, no. (6118).]]
Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: 'Affan narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khuthaym narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, who said: I entered upon Hafsah, daughter of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, and I said: "I am going to ask you about a matter, and I am shy to ask you." She said: "Do not be shy, nephew." He said: "Concerning intercourse with women in their rears?" She said: Umm Salamah narrated to me that the Ansar used not to practise jabb with women, and the Jews used to say: "Whoever practises jabb with his wife, the child will be cross-eyed." When the Muhajirun came to Madinah, they married women of the Ansar and practised jabb with them. A woman of the Ansar refused to obey her husband and said: "You will not do this until I go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." She entered upon Umm Salamah and mentioned this to her. Umm Salamah said: "Sit until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ comes." When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came, the Ansari woman was too shy to ask him, so she went out, and Umm Salamah informed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: "Call the Ansari woman." She was called, and he recited to her this verse: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth as you wish﴾, [and said:] "one orifice".
It was also related by al-Tirmidhi, from Bundar, from Ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan, from Ibn Khuthaym, with this chain.[[Musnad (6/304) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2979).]] He said: "Hasan" (good).
I say: It has also been related through the route of Hammad ibn Abi Hanifah, from his father, from Ibn Khuthaym, from Yusuf ibn Mahak, from Hafsah, Mother of the Believers: that a woman came to her and said: "My husband comes to me from the side and from the front, and I dislike that." This reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "There is no harm if it is in one orifice."[[Musnad Abi Hanifah, no. (102).]]
Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Ya'qub, that is al-Qummi, narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am ruined!" He said: "What has ruined you?" He said: "I turned my mount last night!" He said: The Prophet did not answer him at all. Then Allah revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ this verse: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth as you wish﴾, "approach from the front or from behind, but beware of the rear and of menstruation."
Al-Tirmidhi related it from 'Abd ibn Humayd, from Hasan ibn Musa al-Ashyab, with this chain.[[Musnad (1/297) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2980).]] He said: "Hasan gharib" (good, strange).
Imam Ahmad also said: Yahya ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, Rishdin narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Thawban narrated to me, from 'Amir ibn Yahya al-Ma'afiri, from Hanash, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: This verse was revealed: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you﴾ concerning some people of the Ansar who came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "Go to her in any state, provided it is in the vagina."[[Musnad (1/268).]]
Abu Ya'la al-Hafiz said: al-Harith ibn Suraij [in manuscript هـ: "Shurayh"] narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Nafi' narrated to us, Hisham ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id, who said: A man sodomised his wife during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they said: "So-and-so has sodomised his wife." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth as you wish﴾.[[Musnad Abi Ya'la (2/354). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (6/319): "His shaykh al-Harith ibn Suraij is weak and a liar, but he has been corroborated: Ya'qub ibn Humayd related it from 'Abd Allah ibn Nafi', from Hisham, from Zayd ibn Aslam with this chain, al-Tahawi related it in Mushkil al-Athar, no. (6118), and it has already been mentioned."]]
Abu Dawud said: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya Abu al-Asbagh narrated to us, saying: Muhammad, that is Ibn Salamah, narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Aban ibn Salih, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Indeed Ibn 'Umar, and Allah forgives him, made a mistake. The people of this clan of the Ansar, who were idolaters, were with the people of this clan of the Jews, who were People of the Book, and they regarded them as having superiority over them in knowledge, so they imitated many of their actions. Among the practices of the People of the Book was that they would not approach women except on one side, since that is the most concealing position for a woman. This clan of the Ansar adopted this practice from them. And this clan of Quraysh would approach women in a reprehensible manner and would enjoy them facing forward, from behind and lying on their backs. When the Muhajirun came to Madinah, a man of them married a woman of the Ansar and went to do that with her, and she objected to him and said: "We were only approached from one side. Do it that way, or else keep away from me." Their affair spread, and it reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so Allah revealed: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth as you wish﴾, that is: facing forward, from behind, and lying on the back, meaning by this the place of the child.[[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2164).]]
Abu Dawud alone related it, and what has preceded of the hadiths testifies to its soundness, especially the narration of Umm Salamah, for it resembles this context.
Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani also related this hadith through the route of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Aban ibn Salih, from Mujahid, who said: I presented the Mushaf to Ibn 'Abbas from its opening to its end, stopping at every verse and asking him about it, until I reached this verse: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth as you wish﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "This clan of Quraysh used to approach their women in Makkah and enjoy them..." and he mentioned the story in its full context.[[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/77).]]
As for Ibn 'Abbas's saying: "Indeed Ibn 'Umar, and Allah forgives him, made a mistake," it seems to refer to what al-Bukhari related:
Ishaq narrated to us, al-Nadr ibn Shumayl narrated to us, Ibn 'Awn informed us, from Nafi', who said: When Ibn 'Umar recited the Qur'an, he would not speak until he had finished it. One day I was with him, and he recited Surah al-Baqarah until he reached a place, and he said: "Do you know concerning what it was revealed?" I said: "No." He said: "It was revealed concerning such and such." Then he continued. And from 'Abd al-Samad, who said: My father narrated to me, Ayyub narrated to me, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, concerning ﴿So come to your tilth as you wish﴾, he said: "He comes to her in..." [There is a blank space in all manuscripts. In Fath al-Bari (8/130): "This is how it occurs in all the manuscripts; it does not mention what follows the adverbial phrase, which is the prepositional object. What appears in al-Jam' bayn al-Sahihayn of al-Humaydi is: 'He comes to her in the vagina,' and this is from his own understanding." Also taken from the margin of the Shu'ayb edition.]]
Thus al-Bukhari related it, and he alone transmitted it through these routes.[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4526).]]
Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, Ibn 'Awn narrated to us, from Nafi', who said: One day I recited: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth as you wish﴾, and Ibn 'Umar said: "Do you know concerning what it was revealed?" I said: "No." He said: "It was revealed concerning intercourse with women in their rears."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (4/404).]]
Abu Qilabah also narrated to me: 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Ayyub, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar: ﴿So come to your tilth as you wish﴾, he said: "In the rear."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (4/406).]]
It has also been related from the hadith of Malik, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, but it is not authentic.
Al-Nasa'i related, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Uways, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ibn 'Umar: that a man came to his wife in her rear, and he felt great remorse over that, so Allah revealed: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth as you wish﴾.[[Al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Nasa'i, no. (8981).]]
Abu Hatim al-Razi said: If this were with Zayd ibn Aslam from Ibn 'Umar, people would not have been so fond of Nafi'. This is his criticism of this hadith.
'Abd Allah ibn Nafi' related it from Dawud ibn Qays, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Ibn 'Umar, and so he mentioned it.

This is upon what came before, namely that he comes to her in her front passage from behind her, based on what al-Nasa'i also narrated from ʿAli ibn ʿUthman al-Nufayli, from Saʿid ibn ʿIsa, from al-Mufaddal[[In all the manuscripts: "al-Fadl," and the correct form is what we have adopted.]] ibn Fadala, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Sulayman al-Tawil, from Kaʿb ibn ʿAlqama, from Abu al-Nadr: that he told him that he said to Nafi', the freed slave of Ibn ʿUmar: "Indeed, it has been said much against you, that you say on the authority of Ibn ʿUmar that he issued a legal ruling that women may be approached in their rear passages." He said: "They have lied about me. But I will tell you how the matter actually was: Ibn ʿUmar once presented the Mushaf (the written codex of the Qur'an) while I was with him, until he reached: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so approach your tilth however you wish﴾. Then he said: 'O Nafi', do you know the context of this verse?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'We, the company of Quraysh, used to have intercourse with women in a dominating manner (lit. we used to lay women down). When we entered Medina and married women of the Ansar, we wanted from them the same as we used to want, but they disliked that and found it grave. The women of the Ansar had adopted the custom of the Jews, who only approached women on their sides. So Allah revealed: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so approach your tilth however you wish﴾.'" [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (8978).]]

This is a sound chain (isnad). It has also been narrated by Ibn Mardawayh, from al-Tabarani, from al-Husayn ibn Ishaq, from Zakariyya[[In manuscript A: "from Abu Zakariyya."]] ibn Yahya al-Katib al-ʿUmari, from Mufaddal ibn Fadala, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAyyash[[In manuscript A: "ʿAbbas."]] from Kaʿb ibn ʿAlqama, and so on. We have also related from Ibn ʿUmar explicit reports to the contrary, and that it is neither permissible nor lawful, as will come. Although this view has been attributed to a group of the jurists of Medina and others, some have attributed it to Imam Malik in the book Kitab al-Sirr[[In manuscript A: "al-Sayr."]], but most people deny that this is authentically from Imam Malik, may Allah have mercy on him.

Hadiths reported through many routes have come prohibiting this act and engaging in it. Al-Hasan ibn ʿArafa said:
"Ismaʿil ibn ʿAyyash[[In manuscript A: "ʿAbbas."]] narrated to us, from Suhayl[[In manuscripts J and A: "from Sahl."]] ibn Abi Salih, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Be modest, for Allah is not shy of the truth. It is not lawful to approach women in their anuses.'" [[Also narrated by al-Daraqutni in al-Sunan (3/288) by way of al-Hasan ibn ʿArafa.]]

Imam Ahmad said: "ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from ʿAbd[[In manuscripts J and A: "from ʿAbd Allah."]] ibn Shaddad, from a man, from Khuzayma ibn Thabit: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade a man to approach his wife in her rear." [[al-Musnad (5/215); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, nos. (8985, 8986); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (1924). See the variant readings in it in Sunan al-Nasa'i (5/316-319).]]

Another route: Ahmad said: "Yaʿqub narrated to us, I heard my father narrate, from Yazid ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Usama ibn al-Had: that ʿUbayd Allah ibn al-Husayn al-Walibi narrated to him that Harami ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Waqifi narrated to him that Khuzayma ibn Thabit al-Khatmi narrated to him that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Allah is not shy of the truth; Allah is not shy of the truth' (three times), 'Do not approach women in their backsides.'"

al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated it through several routes, from Khuzayma ibn Thabit, and its chain contains much disagreement.

Another hadith: Abu ʿIsa al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i said: "Abu Saʿid al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, from al-Dahhak ibn ʿUthman, from Makhrama ibn Sulayman, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Allah does not look at a man who approaches a man or a woman in the rear.'" Then al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hadith that is hasan (good) and gharib (singular)." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (1165); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (9001).]] Ibn Hibban also narrated it in his Sahih in this way [[Sahih Ibn Hibban, no. (1302), "Mawarid" edition.]]. Ibn Hazm also authenticated it. However, al-Nasa'i narrated it from Hannad, from Waki', from al-Dahhak, with the same wording, as a mawquf (a report ending at a Companion, not traced to the Prophet).

ʿAbd said: "ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, Maʿmar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father: that a man asked Ibn ʿAbbas about approaching a woman in her rear. He said: 'You ask me about disbelief!'" [Sound chain] [[Addition from manuscripts J, A, and H.]]

Likewise al-Nasa'i narrated it through the route of Ibn al-Mubarak, from Maʿmar, with a similar wording.[[In manuscript H: "from ʿIkrima," which is an error.]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: "ʿAbd al-Samad narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us, Qatada narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'The one who approaches his wife in her rear is the lesser Lut (sodomite).'" [[al-Musnad (2/210).]]

ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad said: "Hudba narrated to me, Hammam narrated to us, he said: Qatada was asked about the one who approaches his wife in her rear. Qatada said: 'ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "It is the lesser Lut."'"
Qatada said: "ʿUqba ibn Wassaj also narrated to me, from Abu al-Darda', who said: 'Does anyone do that except a disbeliever?'" [[Zawa'id al-Musnad (2/210).]]

This hadith was also narrated by Yahya ibn Saʿid al-Qattan, from Saʿid ibn Abi ʿArouba, from Qatada, from Abu Ayyub, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs, as his own statement (qawl). This is more authentic, and Allah knows best.

Likewise, ʿAbd ibn Humayd narrated it from Yazid ibn Harun, from Humayd al-Aʿraj, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, as a mawquf report, from his own statement.

Another route: Jaʿfar al-Firyabi said: "Qutayba narrated to us, Ibn Lahiʿa narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad ibn al-ʿAm, from Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Seven are those whom Allah will not look at on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and He will say: Enter the Fire with those who enter: the one who does and the one to whom it is done, the one who masturbates, the one who has intercourse with an animal, the one who has intercourse with a woman in her rear, the one who has intercourse with a woman and her daughter, the one who commits adultery with his neighbor's wife, and the one who harms his neighbor until he curses him.'" [[Narrated by Abu al-Shaykh in Majlis min Hadithih (62/1, 2), and Ibn Bishran in al-Amali (86/1, 2), through several routes from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad al-Afriqi. End of quote, drawn from Irwa' al-Ghalil by al-Albani (8/59).]]

Ibn Lahiʿa and his shaykh are both weak.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: "ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Sufyan informed us, from ʿAsim, from ʿIsa ibn Hittan, from Muslim ibn Salam, from ʿAli ibn Talq, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade that women be approached in their rear passages, for Allah is not shy of the truth." [[Ibn Hajar mentioned it in Atraf al-Musnad (4/384), but I did not find it in the printed edition.]]

Ahmad also narrated it from Abu Muʿawiya, and Abu ʿIsa al-Tirmidhi narrated it by way of Abu Muʿawiya, from ʿAsim al-Ahwal [[Addition from manuscripts J and A.]], with an addition in it, and said: "This is a hadith that is hasan." [[Mentioned by al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar in Atraf al-Musnad (4/384); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (1164).]]

Some people cite this hadith in the Musnad of ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, as it appears in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal [[al-Musnad (1/86).]], but the correct attribution is that it is from ʿAli ibn Talq.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: "ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from al-Harith ibn Mukhalled, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed, the one who approaches his wife in her rear, Allah does not look at him.'"

ʿAffan narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Suhayl narrated to us, from al-Harith ibn Makhlad, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: [[In manuscripts A and H: "from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet."]] "Allah does not look at a man who has intercourse with his wife in her rear."

Ibn Majah also narrated it through the route of Suhayl. [[al-Musnad (2/344); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (1923).]]

Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from al-Harith ibn Makhlad, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Cursed is the one who approaches a woman in her rear."

In this same way Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated it through the route of Waki'. [[al-Musnad (2/444); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2162); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (9015).]]

Another route: al-Hafiz Abu Nuʿaym al-Isfahani said: "Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Rayyan informed us, Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Nasa'i narrated to us, Hannad and Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, and the wording is his, they said: Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Cursed is the one who approaches a woman in her rear.'" [[Narrated by Abu Nuʿaym in a part of his, ʿAli (high-chain), from Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Rayyan. Al-Dhahabi said: "There is in it what is objectionable."]]

This hadith is not worded this way in the Sunan of al-Nasa'i. What is in it is from Suhayl, from al-Harith ibn Makhlad, as already mentioned.

Our shaykh, al-Hafiz Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Dhahabi, said: "The narration of Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Rayyan of this hadith with this chain is an error on his part, and they have declared him weak."

Another route: Muslim ibn Khalid al-Zanji narrated it, from al-ʿAla' ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Cursed is the one who approaches women in their rear passages."

There is some discussion about Muslim ibn Khalid, and Allah knows best.

Another route: Imam Ahmad and the compilers of the Sunan narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salama, from Hakim al-Athram, from Abu Tamima al-Hujaymi, from Abu Hurayra: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever comes to a menstruating woman, or to a woman in her rear, or to a soothsayer and believes him, has disbelieved in what was revealed to Muhammad." [[al-Musnad (2/408); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (3904); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (135); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (9016); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (639).]]

al-Tirmidhi said: "al-Bukhari declared this hadith weak." What al-Bukhari said about the hadith of Hakim [al-Athram][[Addition from manuscripts J and A; in manuscript W: "Hakim al-Tirmidhi."]] from Abu Tamima is: "It is not corroborated in his hadith." [[al-Tarikh al-Kabir (3/17).]]

Another route: al-Nasa'i said: "ʿUthman ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, Sulayman ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us from his book, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Muhammad al-San'ani, from Saʿid ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: 'Be shy before Allah with true shyness; do not approach women in their rear passages.'" [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (9010).]]

Al-Nasa'i alone narrated it through this route.

Hamza ibn Muhammad al-Kinani, the hafiz, said: "This is a munkar (rejected) and batil (false) hadith, from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from the hadith of Abu Salama, and from the hadith of Saʿid. If ʿAbd al-Malik heard it from Saʿid, then he heard it after his confusion (ikhtilat). Al-Zuhri narrated from Abu Salama that he used to forbid this; but as for [the attribution] from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), no." End of his statement.

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 222–223 (part 4 of 5):

He (the critic) did well and made an excellent critique. However, 'Abd al-Malik [ibn Muhammad] [[Addition from manuscripts ج, أ, و.]] al-San'ani is not known to have become confused (ikhtilat, loss of memory). No one mentioned this except Hamzah al-Kinani, and he is trustworthy. Yet Duhaym, Abu Hatim, and Ibn Hibban criticized him, and Ibn Hibban said: "It is not permissible to use him as evidence." Allah knows best. Zayd ibn Yahya ibn [[In manuscript ج: "'an" (from).]] 'Ubayd followed him, from Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz. It was also narrated by two other chains from Abu Salamah, but nothing from them is authentic.

Another chain: al-Nasa'i said: Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Mujahid, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "A man having intercourse with women in their anuses is disbelief (kufr)."

Then he narrated it from Bundar, from 'Abd al-Rahman, with the same chain, and said: "Whoever has intercourse with his wife in her anus has committed disbelief." Thus al-Nasa'i narrated it through al-Thawri, from Layth, from Mujahid, from Abu Hurayrah, as a mawquf (a report ending with a Companion, not traced to the Prophet). Likewise he narrated it through 'Ali ibn Badhimah, from Mujahid, from Abu Hurayrah, as a mawquf. Bakr ibn Khunays narrated it from Layth, from Mujahid, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever has intercourse with any man or woman in the anus has disbelieved." The mawquf version is more authentic. Bakr ibn Khunays was declared weak by several imams, and others abandoned him. [[Narrated by al-'Uqayli in al-Du'afa' al-Kabir (1/149).]]

Another hadith: Muhammad ibn Aban al-Balkhi said: Waki' narrated to us, Zam'ah ibn Salih narrated to us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, and from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid ibn al-Hadi, both of whom said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah is not shy of the truth. Do not approach women in their anuses." [[Mentioned by al-Daraqutni in al-'Ilal (2/167). He said: "He did not mention Tawus in the hadith of 'Amr ibn Dinar, and the saying of 'Uthman ibn al-Yaman is the most authentic."]]

Al-Nasa'i also narrated it: Sa'id ibn Ya'qub al-Taliqani narrated to us, from 'Uthman ibn al-Yaman, from Zam'ah ibn Salih, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn al-Hadi, from 'Umar, who said: "Do not approach women in their anuses." [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (9008).]]

And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Yazid ibn Abi Hakim narrated to us, from Zam'ah ibn Salih, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Tawus, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Hadi al-Laythi, who said: 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Be shy before Allah, for Allah is not shy of the truth. Do not approach women in their anuses." [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (9009).]] The mawquf version is more authentic.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ghundar and Mu'adh ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, both saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from 'Isa ibn Hittan, from Muslim ibn Salam, from Talq ibn Yazid, or Yazid ibn Talq, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed Allah is not shy of the truth. Do not approach women in their buttocks." [[Ibn Hajar mentioned it in Atraf al-Musnad (4/384) through Ghundar's chain in the Musnad of 'Ali ibn Talq. I do not know how "Yazid ibn Talq" came about here, and Ibn Hajar clarified the correct version, Allah knows best.]]

It was similarly narrated by more than one person from Shu'bah. 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated it from Ma'mar, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from 'Isa ibn Hittan, from Muslim ibn Salam, from Talq ibn 'Ali, but the most likely is that it is 'Ali ibn Talq, as mentioned earlier. Allah knows best.

Another hadith: Abu Bakr al-Athram said in his Sunan: Abu Muslim al-Harami narrated to us, my brother Unays ibn Ibrahim narrated to us [[In manuscript أ: "my brother Unays ibn Abi Tamim".]] that his father Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qa'qa' informed him, from his father Abu al-Qa'qa', from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The private parts of women are forbidden." [[Also narrated by al-Dulabi in al-Kuna (2/85).]]

It was also narrated by Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah, Sufyan al-Thawri, Shu'bah, and others, from Abu 'Abd Allah al-Shaqiri, whose name is Salamah ibn Tamam, who is trustworthy, from Abu al-Qa'qa', from Ibn Mas'ud as a mawquf. This is more authentic.

Another chain: Ibn 'Adi said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Muhamili narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Hamzah narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Rufay', from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not approach women in their rear parts." [[Al-Kamil li-Ibn 'Adi (3/206).]] Muhammad ibn Hamzah is al-Jazari, and his teacher has been criticized in both cases.

It has also been narrated from the hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, Abu Dharr, and others. [[The hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka'b was narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman (no. 5457) through Abu Qilabah, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b. The hadith of 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir was narrated by Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil (4/148) through Ibn Lahi'ah, from Mishrah ibn Ha'an, from 'Uqbah.]] Each of them has criticism that prevents the hadith from being authenticated. Allah knows best.

Al-Thawri said, from al-Salt ibn Bahram, from Abu al-Mu'tamir, from Abu Juwayriyah [[In manuscript ج: "from Abu Jurayr"; in manuscript أ: "from Abu Juwayrah".]]: A man asked 'Ali about having intercourse with a woman in her anus. He said: "You have fallen low, may Allah cause you to fall! Have you not heard the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Do you commit such an abomination as no one in the worlds has committed before you?﴾ [al-A'raf: 80]."

The sayings of Ibn Mas'ud, Abu al-Darda', Abu Hurayrah, Ibn 'Abbas, and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr regarding the prohibition of this have already been mentioned. It is also established without doubt from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) that he prohibited it.

Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi said in his Musnad: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to us, from al-Harith ibn Ya'qub, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, Abu al-Hubab, who said: I said to Ibn 'Umar: "What do you say about slave girls? Do we make them 'tahmid' (a term for anal intercourse) for them?" He said: "What is tahmid?" Then he mentioned the rear. He said: "Does anyone among the Muslims do that?"

Ibn Wahb and Qutaybah also narrated it from al-Layth with the same chain. This is a sound chain and an explicit text prohibiting it. Thus, whatever is reported from him that could be interpreted in more than one way is referred back to this clear (muhkam) ruling.

Ibn Jarir said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, Abu Zayd 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad ibn Abi al-Ghamr narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim narrated to me, from Malik ibn Anas that it was said to him: "O Abu 'Abd Allah, people narrate from Salim ibn 'Abd Allah that he said: 'The slave, or the uncouth one, lied about my father [['Abd Allah]].'" [[Addition from manuscript ج.]] Malik said: "I testify about Yazid ibn Ruman that he told me, from Salim ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ibn 'Umar, the same as what Nafi' said." He was asked: "Al-Harith ibn Ya'qub narrates from Abu al-Hubab Sa'id ibn Yasar that he asked Ibn 'Umar, and he said to him: 'O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, we buy slave girls, do we make tahmid for them?' He said: 'What is tahmid?' So he mentioned the rear to him. Ibn 'Umar said: 'Uff! Uff! Would a believer (or he said: a Muslim) do that?'" Malik said: "I testify about Rabi'ah that he told me, from Abu al-Hubab, from Ibn 'Umar, the same as what Nafi' said." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (4/405).]]

Al-Nasa'i narrated, from al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman, from Asbagh ibn al-Faraj al-Faqih, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: I said to Malik: "Among us in Egypt is al-Layth ibn Sa'd, who narrates from al-Harith ibn Ya'qub, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said: I said to Ibn 'Umar: 'We buy slave girls, do we make tahmid for them?' He said: 'What is tahmid?' I said: 'We approach them in their rear parts.' He said: 'Uff! Uff! Does a Muslim do this?'"
