Malik said to me: "I testify about Rabi'ah that he narrated to me from Sa'id ibn Yasar that he asked Ibn 'Umar, and he said: 'There is no harm in it.'" [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (8979).]]

Al-Nasa'i also narrated through Yazid ibn Ruman, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, that Ibn 'Umar did not see any harm in a man approaching his wife in her rear. [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (8980).]]

Ma'n ibn 'Isa narrated from Malik that this is forbidden.

Abu Bakr ibn Ziyad al-Naysaburi said: Isma'il ibn Husayn narrated to me, and Isra'il ibn Rawh narrated to me: I asked Malik ibn Anas: "What do you say about having intercourse with women in their anuses?" He said: "Are you not an Arab people? Is tilth anything other than the place of sowing? Do not go beyond the vagina." I said: "O Abu 'Abd Allah, they say that you say this?!" He said: "They lie about me, they lie about me."

This is what is established from him, and it is the view of Abu Hanifah, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and all their companions. It is also the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Abu Salamah, 'Ikrimah, Tawus, 'Ata', Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Mujahid ibn Jabr, al-Hasan, and others among the early generations (al-salaf). They denounced it most strongly, and some of them applied the term disbelief to the one who does it. This is the position of the majority of scholars (jumhur al-'ulama').

Something has been reported on this from some jurists of Madinah, to the extent that they attributed it to Imam Malik, but its authenticity from him is questionable.

[Ibn Jarir, in his book on marriage, which he compiled, narrated from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la, from Ibn Wahb, its permissibility.] [[Addition from manuscripts ج, أ, و.]]

al-Tahawi said: Asbagh ibn al-Faraj narrated from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, who said: "I have not found anyone whom I follow in my religion who doubts that it is permissible." He meant intercourse with a woman in her anus. Then he recited: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 223], and then said: "What could be clearer than this?" This is al-Tahawi's report.

Al-Hakim, al-Daraqutni, and al-Khatib al-Baghdadi narrated from Imam Malik, through various chains, what suggests permissibility. But there is severe weakness in the chains, and our shaykh, the hafiz Abu 'Abd Allah al-Dhahabi, thoroughly examined them in a juz' (booklet) he compiled on this subject. Allah knows best.

al-Tahawi said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam told us that he heard al-Shafi'i say: "Nothing has been authentically reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding its permissibility or its prohibition. Analogy (qiyas) indicates that it is permissible." This was also narrated by Abu Bakr al-Khatib, from Abu Sa'id al-Sayrafi, from Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam say: I heard al-Shafi'i say ... and he mentioned it. Abu Nasr al-Sabbagh said: al-Rabi' used to swear by Allah, there is no god but He: "Ibn 'Abd al-Hakam lied about al-Shafi'i regarding this, for al-Shafi'i explicitly stated its prohibition in six of his books." Allah knows best.

Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir: Among those to whom this opinion is attributed, namely the permissibility of intercourse with a woman in her rear passage, are Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Nafi', Ibn 'Umar, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Majishun. This opinion is found in al-'Utbiyya. It is also reported from Malik in a book of his called Kitab al-Sirr (the Book of the Secret), but the leading scholars and shaykhs of Malik's companions deny that this book is his, and Malik is too exalted to have a book called Kitab al-Sirr. This opinion occurs in al-'Utbiyya. Ibn al-'Arabi mentioned that Ibn Sha'ban attributed this opinion to a large group of the Companions and the Successors, and to Malik through many narrations, from the book Jima' al-Nisa' and Ahkam al-Quran. This is his wording. He said: al-Kiya al-Harrasi al-Tabari reported from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi that he used as evidence for its permissibility the verse: ﴿Do you approach males from among the worlds, and leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses? Rather, you are a transgressing people﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 26:165-166].

That is, it is like the permissible things. Then he refuted it by saying that what is meant by what Allah created for them is the private parts of women, not their rear passages. I say: This is the correct view, and what al-Qurazi said, if it is indeed reported from him, is an error. People have written many works on this issue, among them Abu al-'Abbas al-Qurtubi, who named his book Ithhar Idbar man Ajaza al-Wat' fi al-Adbar (Exposing the Backs of Those Who Permitted Intercourse in the Rear Passages).

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And send ahead for yourselves﴾ means: through performing acts of obedience, along with complying with what He has forbidden you of abandoning the prohibited things. For this reason He said: ﴿And fear Allah, and know that you will meet Him﴾, meaning: He will hold you accountable for all your deeds.

﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾, meaning: those who obey Allah in what He has commanded them and who abandon what He has warned them against.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Qasim narrated to us, Husayn narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to me, from 'Abd Allah ibn Waqid, from 'Ata' — he said: I think he reported it from Ibn 'Abbas — regarding ﴿And send ahead for yourselves﴾, he said: it means saying "In the name of Allah," the basmala at intercourse.

It is established in Sahih al-Bukhari, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If one of them, when he intends to approach his wife, says: 'In the name of Allah. O Allah, keep Satan away from us, and keep Satan away from what You provide us,' then if a child is decreed for them from that union, Satan will never harm it." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 141].

Allah the Exalted says: Do not make your oaths by Allah a barrier preventing you from righteousness and maintaining the ties of kinship when you swear to abandon them. This is like His saying: ﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give to the near of kin, the needy, and the emigrants in the way of Allah. Let them pardon and overlook. Do you not love that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Nur: 22]. Therefore, persisting in an oath is more sinful for its swearer than breaking it through expiation (kaffarah, the atonement required for breaking an oath). Al-Bukhari said:

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: "This is what Abu Hurairah narrated to us from the Prophet (ﷺ)," and he said: "We are the last but the foremost on the Day of Resurrection." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) also said: "By Allah, for one of you to persist in his oath concerning his family is a greater sin before Allah than to give the expiation which Allah has enjoined upon him."

Muslim narrated it likewise, from Muhammad ibn Rafi', from 'Abd al-Razzaq, with the same chain. Ahmad also narrated it from him, with the same chain.

Then al-Bukhari said: Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to us: Yahya ibn Salih narrated to us: Mu'awiyah, namely Ibn Sallam, narrated to us, from Yahya, namely Ibn Abi Kathir, from Ikrimah, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever persists in an oath concerning his family, he is greater in sin; expiation does not suffice him."

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths﴾, that he said: "Do not make your oath an obstacle to doing good, but make expiation for your oath and do good."

Likewise said Masruq, al-Sha'bi, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Mujahid, Tawus, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ata', Ikrimah, Makhul, al-Zuhri, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Dahhak, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, and al-Suddi. The majority (al-jumhur) view is supported by what is established in the two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim) from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Allah, if Allah wills, I will not swear an oath and then see something else better than it, except that I do what is better and make expiation for my oath." It is also established in both Sahihs that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah: "O 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah, do not ask for leadership, for if you are given it without asking, you will be aided in it, but if you are given it upon asking, you will be left to it. And if you swear an oath and then see something better than it, then do what is better and make expiation for your oath."

Muslim narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever swears an oath and then sees something other than it to be better, let him make expiation for his oath and do what is better."

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Sa'id, the client of Bani Hashim, narrated to us: Khalifah ibn Khayyat narrated to us: 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever swears an oath and then sees something other than it to be better, abandoning it is its expiation."

Abu Dawud narrated it through the route of 'Ubayd Allah ibn al-Akhnas, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no vow or oath concerning what the son of Adam does not possess, nor in disobedience to Allah, nor in severing the ties of kinship. Whoever swears an oath and then sees something other than it to be better, let him abandon it and do what is better, for abandoning it is its expiation."

Then Abu Dawud said: All the hadiths from the Prophet (ﷺ) are: "let him make expiation for his oath," and these are the authentic (sihah) ones.

Ibn Jarir said: 'Ali ibn Sa'id al-Kindi narrated to us: 'Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from Harithah ibn Muhammad, from 'Amrah, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever swears an oath concerning severing the ties of kinship or disobedience, then his righteousness is to break it and return from his oath."

This is a weak hadith, because this Harithah is Ibn Abi al-Rijal, Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, matruk al-hadith (abandoned in narration), weak according to all.

Then Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Jubayr, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Masruq and al-Sha'bi that they said: There is no oath in disobedience, and no expiation for it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths﴾, meaning: He will not punish you or obligate you for the idle oaths (al-aiman al-laghiyah) that proceed from you, which are those the swearer does not intend, but which flow over his tongue out of habit without deliberation or emphasis. This is established in the two Sahihs from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever swears and says in his oath, 'By al-Lat and al-'Uzza,' let him say, 'There is no god but Allah.'" He said this to a people recently converted from the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic ignorance), who had accepted Islam while their tongues had become accustomed to what they used to do, swearing by al-Lat without intention. So they were commanded to utter the word of sincerity (kalimat al-ikhlas) just as they had uttered that word without intention, so that this would be in place of that. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned. And Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing﴾, just as He said in another verse in al-Ma'idah: ﴿But He will hold you accountable for oaths you have deliberately sworn﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 89].

Abu Dawud said: Chapter on the idle oath: Humayd ibn Mas'adah al-Shami narrated to us: Hassan, namely Ibn Ibrahim, narrated to us: Ibrahim, namely al-Sayigh, narrated to us, from 'Ata', concerning the idle oath: 'A'ishah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is the speech of a man in his house: 'No, by Allah,' and 'Yes, by Allah.'"

Then Abu Dawud said: Dawud ibn Abi al-Furat narrated it from Ibrahim al-Sayigh, from 'Ata', from 'A'ishah, as a mawquf (a report ending with a Companion, not attributed to the Prophet (ﷺ)). Al-Zuhri, 'Abd al-Malik and Malik ibn Mi'wal all narrated it from 'Ata', from 'A'ishah, also as mawquf.

I say: Likewise Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Abi Layla narrated it from 'Ata', from 'A'ishah, as mawquf.

Ibn Jarir narrated, from Hannad, from Waki', 'Abdah and Abu Mu'awiyah, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, concerning His saying: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 89], that she said: "No, by Allah; yes, by Allah."

Then he narrated it from Muhammad ibn Humayd, from Salamah, from Ibn Ishaq, from Hisham, from his father, from her. And also from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, from al-Qasim, from her. And also from Salamah, from Ibn Abi Najih, from 'Ata', from her.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah concerning His saying: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths﴾, that she said: "They are the people who dispute about a matter, and one of them says: 'No, by Allah,' 'Yes, by Allah,' and 'No, by Allah,' disputing over the matter. Their hearts do not bind themselves to it."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Harun ibn Ishaq al-Hamdani informed us: 'Abdah, namely Ibn Sulayman, narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths﴾, that she said: "It is the saying of a man: 'No, by Allah,' and 'Yes, by Allah.'"

And my father narrated to us: Abu Salih, scribe of al-Layth, narrated to us: Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me, from Abu al-Aswad, from 'Urwah, who said: 'A'ishah used to say: "The idle oath is only in jesting and joking, and it is the saying of a man: 'No, by Allah,' and 'Yes, by Allah.' There is no expiation for that. Expiation is only for what the heart has bound itself to do, and then does not do."

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: It has been related from Ibn 'Umar, and Ibn 'Abbas in one of his opinions, al-Sha'bi, Ikrimah in one of his two opinions, 'Ata', al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, Mujahid in one of his two opinions, 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Abu Salih, al-Dahhak in one of his two opinions, Abu Qilabah, and al-Zuhri, something similar.

The second aspect: It was read to Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la: Ibn Wahb informed us: a trustworthy transmitter (al-thiqah) informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, that she used to interpret this verse, meaning His saying: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths﴾, and she would say: "It is a thing one of you swears about, intending nothing from it but truth, yet it turns out to be other than what he swore."

Then he said: It has been related from Abu Hurairah, Ibn 'Abbas in one of his two opinions, Sulayman ibn Yasar, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid in one of his two opinions, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i in one of his two opinions, al-Hasan, Zurarah ibn Awfa, Abu Malik, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah, one of Ikrimah's two opinions, Habib ibn Abi Thabit, al-Suddi, Makhul, Muqatil, Tawus, Qatadah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Yahya ibn Sa'id, and Rabi'ah, something similar.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi narrated to us: 'Abd Allah ibn Maymun al-Mirali narrated to us: 'Awf al-A'rabi narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by a people shooting arrows (yantadilun, meaning throwing), and with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was a man from his Companions. A man from the people shot and said: "By Allah, I hit it! By Allah, I missed!" The one who was with the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The man has broken his oath, O Messenger of Allah!" He said: "No! The oaths of archers are idle (laghw); there is no expiation for them and no punishment." This is a mursal (a report omitting a Companion from its chain) hasan (good) narration from al-Hasan.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It has been related from 'A'ishah both opinions together.

Isam ibn Rawwad narrated to us: Adam informed us: Shaybah informed us, from Jabir, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from 'A'ishah, who said: It is his saying: "No, by Allah," and "Yes, by Allah," while he thinks he is truthful, and it is not so.

Other opinions: 'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Hushaym, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim: It is a man who swears about something and then forgets it.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: It is the saying of a man: "May Allah blind my sight if I did not do such and such, may Allah remove me from my wealth if I do not come to you tomorrow." This is that.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us: Musaddad narrated to us: Khalid narrated to us: 'Ata' informed us, from Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The idle oath is that you swear while you are angry.

My father informed me: Abu al-Jamahir informed us: Sa'id ibn Bashir narrated to us: Abu Bishr narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The idle oath is that you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you; that is what carries no expiation for you. And it is similarly related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

Abu Dawud said, in the chapter "The oath in anger": Muhammad ibn al-Minhal narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zuray' informed us: Habib al-Mu'allim narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: that two brothers from the Ansar had an inheritance between them. One of them asked the other for the division, and he said: "If you ask me about the division again, then all my wealth is in the curtain of the Ka'bah." 'Umar said to him: "The Ka'bah is free of need for your wealth. Make expiation for your oath and speak to your brother. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'There is no oath upon you, and no vow in disobedience to the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, nor in severing the ties of kinship, nor in what you do not possess.'"

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths﴾, meaning: He will not punish you or obligate you for the idle oaths (al-aiman al-laghiyah) that proceed from you, which are those the swearer does not intend, but which flow over his tongue out of habit without deliberation or emphasis. This is established in the two Sahihs from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever swears and says in his oath, 'By al-Lat and al-'Uzza,' let him say, 'There is no god but Allah.'" He said this to a people recently converted from the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic ignorance), who had accepted Islam while their tongues had become accustomed to what they used to do, swearing by al-Lat without intention. So they were commanded to utter the word of sincerity (kalimat al-ikhlas) just as they had uttered that word without intention, so that this would be in place of that. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned. And Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing﴾, just as He said in another verse in al-Ma'idah: ﴿But He will hold you accountable for oaths you have deliberately sworn﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 89].

Abu Dawud said: Chapter on the idle oath: Humayd ibn Mas'adah al-Shami narrated to us: Hassan, namely Ibn Ibrahim, narrated to us: Ibrahim, namely al-Sayigh, narrated to us, from 'Ata', concerning the idle oath: 'A'ishah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is the speech of a man in his house: 'No, by Allah,' and 'Yes, by Allah.'"

Then Abu Dawud said: Dawud ibn Abi al-Furat narrated it from Ibrahim al-Sayigh, from 'Ata', from 'A'ishah, as a mawquf (a report ending with a Companion, not attributed to the Prophet (ﷺ)). Al-Zuhri, 'Abd al-Malik and Malik ibn Mi'wal all narrated it from 'Ata', from 'A'ishah, also as mawquf.

I say: Likewise Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Abi Layla narrated it from 'Ata', from 'A'ishah, as mawquf.

Ibn Jarir narrated, from Hannad, from Waki', 'Abdah and Abu Mu'awiyah, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, concerning His saying: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 89], that she said: "No, by Allah; yes, by Allah."

Then he narrated it from Muhammad ibn Humayd, from Salamah, from Ibn Ishaq, from Hisham, from his father, from her. And also from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, from al-Qasim, from her. And also from Salamah, from Ibn Abi Najih, from 'Ata', from her.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah concerning His saying: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths﴾, that she said: "They are the people who dispute about a matter, and one of them says: 'No, by Allah,' 'Yes, by Allah,' and 'No, by Allah,' disputing over the matter. Their hearts do not bind themselves to it."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Harun ibn Ishaq al-Hamdani informed us: 'Abdah, namely Ibn Sulayman, narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths﴾, that she said: "It is the saying of a man: 'No, by Allah,' and 'Yes, by Allah.'"

And my father narrated to us: Abu Salih, scribe of al-Layth, narrated to us: Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me, from Abu al-Aswad, from 'Urwah, who said: 'A'ishah used to say: "The idle oath is only in jesting and joking, and it is the saying of a man: 'No, by Allah,' and 'Yes, by Allah.' There is no expiation for that. Expiation is only for what the heart has bound itself to do, and then does not do."

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: It has been related from Ibn 'Umar, and Ibn 'Abbas in one of his opinions, al-Sha'bi, Ikrimah in one of his two opinions, 'Ata', al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, Mujahid in one of his two opinions, 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Abu Salih, al-Dahhak in one of his two opinions, Abu Qilabah, and al-Zuhri, something similar.

The second aspect: It was read to Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la: Ibn Wahb informed us: a trustworthy transmitter (al-thiqah) informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, that she used to interpret this verse, meaning His saying: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths﴾, and she would say: "It is a thing one of you swears about, intending nothing from it but truth, yet it turns out to be other than what he swore."

Then he said: It has been related from Abu Hurairah, Ibn 'Abbas in one of his two opinions, Sulayman ibn Yasar, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid in one of his two opinions, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i in one of his two opinions, al-Hasan, Zurarah ibn Awfa, Abu Malik, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah, one of Ikrimah's two opinions, Habib ibn Abi Thabit, al-Suddi, Makhul, Muqatil, Tawus, Qatadah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Yahya ibn Sa'id, and Rabi'ah, something similar.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi narrated to us: 'Abd Allah ibn Maymun al-Mirali narrated to us: 'Awf al-A'rabi narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by a people shooting arrows (yantadilun, meaning throwing), and with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was a man from his Companions. A man from the people shot and said: "By Allah, I hit it! By Allah, I missed!" The one who was with the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The man has broken his oath, O Messenger of Allah!" He said: "No! The oaths of archers are idle (laghw); there is no expiation for them and no punishment." This is a mursal (a report omitting a Companion from its chain) hasan (good) narration from al-Hasan.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It has been related from 'A'ishah both opinions together.

Isam ibn Rawwad narrated to us: Adam informed us: Shaybah informed us, from Jabir, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from 'A'ishah, who said: It is his saying: "No, by Allah," and "Yes, by Allah," while he thinks he is truthful, and it is not so.

Other opinions: 'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Hushaym, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim: It is a man who swears about something and then forgets it.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: It is the saying of a man: "May Allah blind my sight if I did not do such and such, may Allah remove me from my wealth if I do not come to you tomorrow." This is that.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us: Musaddad narrated to us: Khalid narrated to us: 'Ata' informed us, from Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The idle oath is that you swear while you are angry.

My father informed me: Abu al-Jamahir informed us: Sa'id ibn Bashir narrated to us: Abu Bishr narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The idle oath is that you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you; that is what carries no expiation for you. And it is similarly related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

Abu Dawud said, in the chapter "The oath in anger": Muhammad ibn al-Minhal narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zuray' informed us: Habib al-Mu'allim narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: that two brothers from the Ansar had an inheritance between them. One of them asked the other for the division, and he said: "If you ask me about the division again, then all my wealth is in the curtain of the Ka'bah." 'Umar said to him: "The Ka'bah is free of need for your wealth. Make expiation for your oath and speak to your brother. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'There is no oath upon you, and no vow in disobedience to the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, nor in severing the ties of kinship, nor in what you do not possess.'"

* *

"And His saying: ﴿But Allah will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid and others said: this refers to one who swears to something while knowing that it is false. Mujahid and others said: it is like His saying: ﴿But He will hold you accountable for the oaths you have sworn in earnest﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:89], and so on. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing﴾, meaning: Forgiving toward His servants, Forbearing with them."

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 226–227:

*Al-Iylā'* (the oath of abstention) means taking an oath. When a man swears that he will not have intercourse with his wife for a period, the situation has only two possibilities: either the period is less than four months, or it is more than four months. If it is less than four months, he may wait until the period ends and then have intercourse with his wife, and she must be patient. She has no right to demand that he return to her during this period. This is as established in the two *Ṣaḥīḥs* (Bukhari and Muslim) from ʿĀʾishah: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took an oath of abstention from his wives for a month, and he came down (from his chamber) on the twenty-ninth day, and said: "The month is twenty-nine days." Both (Bukhari and Muslim) also narrated something similar from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. As for when the period exceeds four months, the wife may demand that the husband, when the four months have passed, either return to her (*fayʾ*, i.e., have intercourse) or divorce her, and the judge compels him to do one or the other, so that he does not harm her. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those who take an oath of abstention from their wives﴾, meaning those who swear to abstain from intercourse with their wives. This indicates that *al-iylā'* applies only to wives and not to slave-women, as is the position of the majority (*jumhur*). ﴿A waiting period of four months﴾, meaning the husband waits four months from the time of the oath, after which he is held in suspense and is required either to return (*fayʾ*) or to divorce. For this reason He said: ﴿And if they return﴾, meaning they revert to what they were before, and this is a metaphor for intercourse, as stated by Ibn ʿAbbās, Masrūq, al-Shaʿbī, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and others, including Ibn Jarīr, may Allah have mercy on him. ﴿Then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning for the shortcoming toward them that occurred because of the oath.

* *

His saying: ﴿And if they return, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ contains an indication for one of the two opinions of the scholars, which is the earlier (*qadīm*) opinion of al-Shāfiʿī: that if the one who took the oath returns after the four months, there is no expiation (*kaffārah*) upon him. This is reinforced by what preceded in the verse before it, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever swears an oath and then sees something else as better than it, leaving it is its expiation," as narrated by Aḥmad and Abū Dāwūd. However, what the majority hold, and what is the later (*jadīd*) opinion of al-Shāfiʿī's school, is that he must pay expiation, due to the general obligation of expiation upon every one who swears, as was also mentioned earlier in the authentic hadiths. And Allah knows best.

The jurists and others, in discussing the reason for postponing the one who takes the oath of abstention by four months, have mentioned the report that Imam Mālik ibn Anas, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated in the *Muwaṭṭaʾ*, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb went out at night and heard a woman saying:

*The night has grown long and its sides have darkened,*
*And my restlessness is that I have no beloved to play with.*

*By Allah, were it not for Allah, of whom I am mindful,*
*The sides of this couch would be shaken from its sides.*

So ʿUmar asked his daughter Ḥafṣah, may Allah be pleased with her: "What is the longest a woman can endure without her husband?" She said: "Six months, or four months." So ʿUmar said: "I will not hold back any of the soldiers from (returning to their wives) for longer than that."

And Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq said, from al-Sāʾib ibn Jubayr, the freed slave of Ibn ʿAbbās, who had met the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ): "I kept hearing the account of ʿUmar, that he went out one night circling around Madinah, as he used to do often. He passed by a woman from among the women of the Arabs, who had closed her door, [and] she was saying:

*This night has grown long and its sides have turned dark,*
*And my restlessness is that there is no bedfellow to play with.*

*I play with him at times, and at times it is as if*
*A moon has appeared in the darkness of night, its crescent.*

*He is pleasing to the one who amuses himself by his nearness,*
*Gentle in the waist, whom his relatives cannot contain.*

*By Allah, were it not for Allah, and nothing else,*
*The sides of this couch would be broken from its sides.*

*But I fear a watchful guardian appointed*
*Over our selves, whose scribe never tires through the ages.*"

Then he mentioned the rest of that account as it preceded, or similar to it. This has been narrated by many chains, and it is among the well-known reports.

* *

His saying: ﴿And if they resolve upon divorce﴾ contains an indication that divorce does not take effect merely by the passing of the four months, as is the view of the majority. Others held that it takes effect as one (revocable) divorce upon the passing of the four months, and this is narrated through authentic chains from ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn ʿUmar, and Zayd ibn Thābit, and this is the view of Ibn Sīrīn, [Masrūq], al-Qāsim, Sālim, al-Ḥasan, Abū Salamah, Qatādah, Shurayḥ the judge, Qabīṣah ibn Dhuʾayb, ʿAṭāʾ, Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Sulaymān ibn Ṭarkhān al-Taymī, Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas, and al-Suddī.

Then it was said that she is divorced by one revocable divorce upon the passing of the four months; this was said by Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām, Makḥūl, Rabīʿah, al-Zuhrī, and Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam. And it was said that she is divorced by one irrevocable (*bāʾin*) divorce; this was narrated from ʿAlī, Ibn Masʿūd, ʿUthmān, Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn ʿUmar, and Zayd ibn Thābit, and this is the view of ʿAṭāʾ, Jābir ibn Zayd, Masrūq, ʿIkrimah, al-Ḥasan, Ibn Sīrīn, Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah, Ibrāhīm, Qabīṣah ibn Dhuʾayb, Abū Ḥanīfah, al-Thawrī, and al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ. Everyone who said that she is divorced upon the passing of the four months made the waiting period (*ʿiddah*) obligatory for her, except what was narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ: that if she had menstruated three times, then there is no waiting period for her. This is the view of al-Shāfiʿī. However, what the majority hold is that he is held in suspense and is required either to do this or that, and no divorce takes effect upon her merely by the passing of the period.

Mālik narrated from Nāfiʿ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, that he said: "If a man takes an oath of abstention from his wife, no divorce takes effect upon him even if four months pass, until he is held in suspense, and then either he divorces or he returns." This was narrated by al-Bukhari.

Al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah informed us, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from Sulaymān ibn Yasār, who said: "I met more than ten of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), all of whom would hold the one who took the oath of abstention in suspense." Al-Shāfiʿī said: "The least of that is thirteen." Al-Shāfiʿī also narrated from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, that he held the one who took the oath in suspense. Then he said: "And this is what we say, and it agrees with what we have narrated from ʿUmar, Ibn ʿUmar, ʿĀʾishah, ʿUthmān, Zayd ibn Thābit, and more than ten of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ)." Thus said al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him.

Ibn Jarīr said: Ibn Abī Maryam narrated to us, Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb narrated to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, from Suhayl ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ, from his father, who said: "I asked twelve men from among the Companions about a man who takes an oath of abstention from his wife, and all of them said: 'Nothing is upon him until four months pass, then he is held in suspense: if he returns, (well and good), and otherwise he divorces.'"

Al-Dāraquṭnī narrated it through the chain of Suhayl.

I say: This is also narrated from ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, Abū al-Dardāʾ, ʿĀʾishah the Mother of the Believers, Ibn ʿUmar, and Ibn ʿAbbās. Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, Mujāhid, Ṭāwūs, Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb, and al-Qāsim held this view. It is the position of Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, and their companions, may Allah have mercy on them all. It is also the view chosen by Ibn Jarīr, and it is the opinion of al-Layth ibn Saʿd, Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh, Abū ʿUbayd, Abū Thawr, and Dāwūd. All of these said: If he does not return, he is compelled to divorce; if he does not divorce, the judge divorces on his behalf, and the divorce is revocable, so he has the right to revoke it during the waiting period.

Mālik alone held that it is not permissible for him to revoke it until he has intercourse with her during the waiting period, and this is extremely rare (*gharīb jiddan*).

Then he said: "And this is what we say, and it agrees with what we have narrated from ʿUmar, Ibn ʿUmar, ʿĀʾishah, ʿUthmān, Zayd ibn Thābit, and more than ten of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ)." Thus said al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him.

Ibn Jarīr said: Ibn Abī Maryam narrated to us, Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb narrated to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, from Suhayl ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ, from his father, who said: "I asked twelve men from among the Companions about a man who takes an oath of abstention from his wife, and all of them said: 'Nothing is upon him until four months pass, then he is held in suspense: if he returns, (well and good), and otherwise he divorces.'"

Al-Dāraquṭnī narrated it through the chain of Suhayl.

I say: This is also narrated from ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, Abū al-Dardāʾ, ʿĀʾishah the Mother of the Believers, Ibn ʿUmar, and Ibn ʿAbbās. Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, Mujāhid, Ṭāwūs, Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb, and al-Qāsim held this view. It is the position of Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, and their companions, may Allah have mercy on them all. It is also the view chosen by Ibn Jarīr, and it is the opinion of al-Layth ibn Saʿd, Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh, Abū ʿUbayd, Abū Thawr, and Dāwūd. All of these said: If he does not return, he is compelled to divorce; if he does not divorce, the judge divorces on his behalf, and the divorce is revocable, so he has the right to revoke it during the waiting period.

Mālik alone held that it is not permissible for him to revoke it until he has intercourse with her during the waiting period, and this is extremely rare (*gharīb jiddan*).

This is the command from Allah, exalted is He, concerning divorced women who have been consummated with and who menstruate: ﴿they shall wait by themselves for three periods﴾. That is, one of them remains (in the waiting period, 'iddah) for three periods after her husband divorces her, and then she may remarry if she wishes. The four Imams (Abu Hanifah, Malik, al-Shafi'i and Ahmad) excluded from this general ruling the slave woman (amah) when she is divorced. According to them, her waiting period is two periods, because she is half of a free woman, and a period (qur') cannot be divided, so she is given two complete periods. This is based on what Ibn Jurayj narrated from Muzahir ibn Aslam al-Makhzumi al-Madani, from al-Qasim, from 'A'ishah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The divorce of a slave woman is two divorces, and her waiting period is two menstrual periods."

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it. However, this Muzahir is completely weak. The Hafiz al-Daraqutni and others said: "The correct view is that it is from the statement of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad himself."

Ibn Majah also narrated it through 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Umar, traced to the Prophet ﷺ. Al-Daraqutni said: "The correct version is what Salim and Nafi' narrated from Ibn 'Umar, as his own statement." The same is narrated from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. They said: "No disagreement is known among the Companions." Some of the earlier scholars said: "Rather, her waiting period is like that of a free woman, because of the generality of the verse; and because this is a natural matter, so slave women and free women are equal in it." Allah knows best. Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr related this view from Muhammad ibn Sirin and some of the people of the Zahiri school (Ahl al-Zahir), and he declared it weak.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: We were told by my father, who was told by Abu al-Yaman, who was told by Isma'il (i.e., Ibn 'Ayyash), from 'Amr ibn Muhajir, from his father, that Asma' bint Yazid ibn al-Sakan al-Ansariyyah said: "I was divorced during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and a divorced woman had no waiting period. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed when Asma' was divorced the waiting period for divorce. She was the first woman for whom the waiting period of divorce was revealed," meaning: ﴿And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three periods﴾.

This is a strange narration through this chain.

The scholars of the earlier generations, the later generations and the Imams differed about what is meant by "qur'" (period). There are two views:

The first: it means the states of purity (tuhr). Malik said in al-Muwatta', from Ibn Shihab, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, that she said: "Hafsah bint 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr moved (out of the marital home) when she entered the bleeding of the third menstruation." Al-Zuhri said: "I mentioned that to 'Amrah bint 'Abd al-Rahman, and she said: ''Urwah spoke the truth.'" Some people argued with her about this, saying: "Allah, the Exalted, says in His Book: 'three periods'." Then 'A'ishah said: "You have spoken the truth. Do you know what the periods are? The periods are only the states of purity (al-atuhar)."

Malik also said, from Ibn Shihab: "I heard Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman say: 'I did not meet any of our jurists except that he would say this,' meaning the statement of 'A'ishah." Malik also said, from Nafi', from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, that he used to say: "If a man divorces his wife and she enters the bleeding of the third menstruation, then she has separated from him and he from her." Malik said: "This is the position among us." The same is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Zayd ibn Thabit, Salim, al-Qasim, 'Urwah, Sulayman ibn Yasar, Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, Aban ibn 'Uthman, 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, Qatadah, al-Zuhri, the rest of the seven jurists of Madinah, and it is the school of Malik, al-Shafi'i, [and others, and Dawud and Abu Thawr, and it is a narration from Ahmad]. They used as evidence Allah's statement: ﴿So divorce them at their waiting period﴾ (al-Talaq 65:1), meaning during the states of purity. Since the purity in which one divorces is counted, this shows it is one of the three periods commanded. For this reason, these scholars said: the woman's waiting period ends and she is separated from her husband upon the stabbing (i.e., the beginning) of the third menstruation. The shortest period in which a woman is believed about the completion of her waiting period is thirty-two days and two moments [of time].

Abu 'Ubayd and others cited as evidence the verse of the poet, al-A'sha:

"Every year you undertake a raid,
whose far end tightens the resolve of your determination,
You are absent for a whole year, and in the tribe there is a loss
for the periods of your women that were lost in it."

He is praising a commander among the Arab commanders who preferred raiding over staying at home, so that the days of purity of his wives were lost, during which he did not have intercourse with them.

The second view: the periods mean menstruation (hayd). So the waiting period does not end until she becomes pure from the third menstruation. Others added: and she performs the ritual bath (ghusl) from it. The shortest time in which a woman is believed about the completion of her waiting period is thirty-three days and a moment. Al-Thawri said, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, who said: "We were with 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, when a woman came to him and said: 'My husband separated from me with one or two (divorces), then he came to me [and I had already released my water] and I had taken off my clothes and closed my door.' 'Umar said to 'Abd Allah (i.e., Ibn Mas'ud): [What do you think?] He said: 'I think she is still his wife, as long as she is not permitted to pray.' [Umar said:] 'I also think so.'"

The same is narrated from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, Abu al-Darda', 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, Anas ibn Malik, Ibn Mas'ud, Mu'adh, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, 'Alqamah, al-Aswad, Ibrahim, Mujahid, 'Ata', Tawus, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, Muhammad ibn Sirin, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Sha'bi, al-Rabi', Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Suddi, Makhul, al-Dahhak, and 'Ata' al-Khurasani, that they said: "The periods are the menstruations."

This is the school of Abu Hanifah and his companions, and the more authentic of the two narrations from Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal. Al-Athram related from him that he said: "The senior Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'The periods are the menstruations.'" It is also the school of al-Thawri, al-Awza'i, Ibn Abi Layla, Ibn Shubrumah, al-Hasan ibn Salih ibn Hayy, Abu 'Ubayd, and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh.

This is supported by what came in the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i, through the chain of al-Mundhir ibn al-Mughirah, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Fatimah bint Abi Hubaysh, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: "Leave the prayer during the days of your periods (aqra')." If this were authentic, it would be explicit that the qur' is menstruation. However, Abu Hatim said of this al-Mundhir: "Unknown, not well known." Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat (the reliable narrators).

Ibn Jarir said: "The origin of the word qur' in the speech of the Arabs is: 'the time for the arrival of a thing that customarily arrives at a known time, and for the departure of a thing that customarily departs at a known time.'" This expression implies that it is shared (mushtarak) between these two meanings. Some of the usul scholars (scholars of legal theory) took this view, and Allah knows best. This is also the statement of al-Asma'i, that the qur' is the time. Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' said: "The Arabs call menstruation qur', they call purity qur', and they call menstruation together with purity qur'." Al-Sheikh Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: "The people of knowledge of the Arabic language and the jurists do not disagree that qur' is used to mean menstruation and used to mean purity. They only differed about what is meant in the verse, and that is the two views."

* *

His statement: ﴿And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs﴾, meaning: of pregnancy or menstruation. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Umar, Mujahid, al-Sha'bi, al-Hakam ibn 'Uyaynah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Dahhak, and others.

* *

His statement: ﴿if they believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾ is a warning to them against saying what is contrary to the truth. This indicates that the reference in this matter is to them, because it is a matter that cannot be known except from them, and it is generally impossible to establish evidence for it. So the matter was returned to them, and they were warned about it, lest they report other than the truth, either out of haste to end the waiting period, or out of desire to prolong it, due to the aims they have in that. So they were commanded to report the truth in this matter without addition or subtraction.

* *

His statement: ﴿And their husbands have more right to take them back during that period, if they desire reconciliation﴾, meaning: their husband who divorced her has more right to take her back as long as she is in her waiting period, if his intention in taking her back is reconciliation and good. This applies to revocable divorces (raj'iyyat). As for irrevocably divorced women (bawa'in), there was no irrevocable divorce at the time this verse was revealed. Rather, that came about when divorces were limited to three. At the time this verse was revealed, a man had more right to take back his wife even if he had divorced her a hundred times. When the next verse limited it to three divorces, there came to be irrevocable and non-irrevocable divorce among people. If you reflect on this, the weakness of the method taken by some of the usul scholars becomes clear, when they cite this noble verse as evidence for the issue of whether the return of a pronoun (dhamir) specifies a general term that precedes it. The use of this verse as an example does not correspond to what they mentioned, and Allah knows best.

* *

His statement: ﴿And they have rights similar to their obligations, according to what is fair﴾, meaning: they have from men a right similar to what men have from them. Each of them should fulfil to the other what is obligatory on him or her in a fair manner. As is established in Sahih Muslim, from Jabir, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said in his sermon at the Farewell Pilgrimage: "Fear Allah concerning women, for you have taken them under the trust of Allah, and you have made their private parts lawful by the word of Allah. And you have a right over them that they do not let anyone you dislike tread upon your bedding. If they do that, then strike them with a non-severe strike. And they have their provision and their clothing according to what is fair."

And in the hadith of Bahz ibn Hakim, from Mu'awiyah ibn Haydah al-Qushayri, from his father, from his grandfather, that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the right of the wife of one of us?" He said: "That you feed her when you eat, and clothe her when you dress, and do not strike the face, and do not revile, and do not abandon her except within the house."

Waki' said, from Bashir ibn Sulayman, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: "Indeed I love to adorn myself for the woman just as I love that the woman adorns herself for me, because Allah says: ﴿And they have rights similar to their obligations, according to what is fair﴾." Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

* *

His statement: ﴿But the men have a degree over them﴾, meaning: in virtue, in character, in standing, in obedience to command, in spending, in managing affairs, and in merit in this world and the Hereafter, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Men are in charge of women by what Allah has given one over the other and what they spend from their wealth﴾ (al-Nisa' 4:34).

* *

His statement: ﴿And Allah is Mighty and Wise﴾, meaning: Mighty in His retribution against those who disobey Him and oppose His command, Wise in His command, His law and His decree.

This noble verse abrogates what was the practice at the beginning of Islam, namely that a man had more right to take back his wife (raj'ah, return to the marriage) even if he had divorced her a hundred times, so long as she was in the 'iddah (waiting period). Because this caused harm to wives, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, limited them to three divorces. He permitted return after the first and second divorce, and made the separation complete with the third. He said: ﴿Divorce is twice; then either keep (them) in an acceptable manner or release (them) with kindness﴾.

Abu Dawud, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his Sunan, under the chapter "Chapter on the abrogation of return after the three divorces": Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi narrated to us: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to me, from his father, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿The divorced women shall wait by themselves for three periods; and it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs﴾, to the end of the verse. The reason for this was that when a man divorced his wife, he had more right to take her back, even if he had divorced her three times. So this was abrogated, and He said: ﴿Divorce is twice﴾, to the end of the verse.

An–Nasa'i narrated it from Zakariya ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, with the same chain.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Harun ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Abdah (i.e., Ibn Sulayman) narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, that a man said to his wife: "I will never divorce you, nor will I ever give you shelter." She said: "How so?" He said: "I will divorce you, and when your term is about to end, I will take you back." She came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned that, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Divorce is twice﴾.

Ibn Jarir narrated it likewise in his Tafsir through the route of Jarir ibn Abd al-Hamid and Ibn Idris, and Abd ibn Humayd narrated it in his Tafsir from Ja'far ibn Awn; all of them from Hisham, from his father, who said: A man had more right to take back his wife, even if he divorced her as many times as he wished, so long as she was in the 'iddah. A man from the Ansar became angry with his wife and said: "By Allah, I will neither give you shelter nor separate from you." She said: "How so?" He said: "I will divorce you, and when your term is about to end, I will take you back; then I will divorce you again, and when your term is about to end, I will take you back." She mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Divorce is twice﴾. He said: So people began the divorce anew, both those who had divorced and those who had not.

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh also narrated it through the route of Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from Ya'la ibn Shabib, the client of al-Zubayr, from Hisham, from his father, from Aisha, mentioning it in a similar manner to what preceded. At-Tirmidhi narrated it from Qutaybah, from Ya'la ibn Shabib, with the same chain. Then he narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Ibn Idris, from Hisham, from his father, as a mursal (a report in which the Companion is omitted from the chain). He said: "This is more sound (asahh)." Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak through the route of Ya'qub ibn Humayd ibn Kasib, from Ya'la ibn Shabib, with the same chain, and said: "Its chain is sound."

Then Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to us, Salamah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Aisha, who said: "There was no set limit for divorce. A man would divorce his wife and then take her back as long as the 'iddah had not ended. Between a man from the Ansar and his family there was some of what happens between people, so he said: 'By Allah, I will leave you neither a widow nor a married woman.' So he kept divorcing her, and when her 'iddah was about to end, he would take her back. He did this several times, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning it: ﴿Divorce is twice, then either keep (them) in an acceptable manner or release (them) with kindness﴾. So He fixed divorce at three, with no return after the third, until she marries another husband." Something similar was narrated from Qatadah as a mursal. As-Suddi, Ibn Zayd and Ibn Jarir also mentioned it in this way, and he chose that this is the explanation of this verse.

* *

His saying: ﴿then either keep (them) in an acceptable manner or release (them) with kindness﴾ means: if you have divorced her once or twice, you have the choice regarding her as long as her 'iddah remains: between taking her back to you, intending reconciliation with her and kindness towards her, and between leaving her until her 'iddah ends, so that she becomes separated from you, and releasing her kindly, not wronging her in any of her rights and not harming her.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "If a man divorces his wife with two divorces, let him fear Allah regarding the third. Either he keeps her in an acceptable manner, treating her companionship well, or he releases her [with kindness], not wronging her in any of her rights."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la informed us by reading, Ibn Wahb informed us, Sufyan al-Thawri informed me, Isma'il ibn Sumay' narrated to me, who said: I heard Abu Razin say: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿then either keep (them) in an acceptable manner or release (them) with kindness﴾? Where is the third?" He said: "The release with kindness."

Abd ibn Humayd narrated it in his Tafsir, and its wording: Yazid ibn Abi Hakim informed us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il ibn Sumay', that Abu Razin al-Asadi said: A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about the saying of Allah: 'Divorce is twice'? Then where is the third?" He said: "The release with kindness is the third."

Imam Ahmad also narrated it. Likewise Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated it from Khalid ibn Abd Allah, from Isma'il ibn Zakariya and Abu Mu'awiyah, from Isma'il ibn Sumay', from Abu Razin, with the same. Qays ibn al-Rabi' also narrated it likewise from Isma'il ibn Sumay', from Abu Razin, as a mursal. Ibn Mardawayh [also] narrated it through the route of Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad, from Isma'il ibn Sumay', from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet ﷺ, and mentioned it. Then he said: Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahim narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated to us, Ubayd Allah ibn Jarir ibn Jabalah narrated to us, Ibn Aisha narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, Allah mentioned divorce twice, so where is the third?" He said: "Either keep (them) in an acceptable manner or release (them) with kindness."

* *

His saying: ﴿It is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them, [except when both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah]﴾ means: it is not lawful for you to harass them and constrict them so that they will ransom themselves from you with what you have given them of dowries, or with part of it, as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And do not treat them harshly that you may take back part of what you have given them, unless they commit a clear immorality﴾ [An-Nisa: 19]. As for when a woman gives something of it willingly from her own soul, Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿But if they give you something of it willingly, then consume it with satisfaction and ease﴾ [An-Nisa: 4]. As for when the spouses are in discord, and the woman does not fulfil the rights of the man, and she hates him and is unable to live with him, then she may ransom herself from him with what he gave her, and there is no blame upon her in paying it, nor upon him in accepting that from her. For this reason Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿It is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them, except when both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah. And if you fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah, then there is no blame upon either of them concerning that by which she ransoms herself﴾, to the end of the verse.

As for when she has no excuse and asks for ransom from him, Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, and Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us; they both said: Ayyub narrated to us, from Abu Qilabah, from one who narrated to him, from Thawban, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Any woman who asks her husband for divorce without any harm, the fragrance of Paradise is forbidden to her."

Likewise at-Tirmidhi narrated it from Bundar, from Abd al-Wahhab ibn Abd al-Majid al-Thaqafi, with the same. And Hasan said: he said: "It is also narrated from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu Asma, from Thawban." Some of them narrated it from Ayyub with this chain, but did not raise it (to the Prophet ﷺ).

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, he said: and he mentioned Abu Asma and mentioned Thawban, and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Any woman who asks her husband for divorce without any harm, the fragrance of Paradise is forbidden to her."

Likewise Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah and Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Zayd, with the same.

Another route: Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Layth, from Abu Idris, from Thawban, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Any woman who asks her husband for divorce without any harm, Allah has forbidden her the fragrance of Paradise." And he said: "Those women who seek khul' (divorce by ransom) are the hypocrites."

Then Ibn Jarir and at-Tirmidhi both narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Muzahim ibn Dhawwad ibn Ulbah, from his father, from Layth, that is Ibn Abi Sulaym, from Abu al-Khattab, from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Idris, from Thawban, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Those women who seek khul' are the hypocrites." Then at-Tirmidhi said: "Gharib (strange) from this route, and its chain is not strong."

Another hadith: Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Hafs ibn Bishr narrated to us, Qays ibn al-Rabi' narrated to us, from Ash'ath ibn Sawwar, from al-Hasan, from Thabit ibn Yazid, from Uqbah ibn Amir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, the women who seek khul' and those who are removed (by ransom) are the hypocrites." Gharib from this route, weak.

Another hadith: Ibn Majah said: Bakr ibn Khalaf Abu Bishr narrated to us, Abu Asim narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Yahya ibn Thawban, from his paternal uncle Umarah ibn Thawban, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A woman should not ask her husband for divorce without a (valid) reason, for she would then not smell the fragrance of Paradise, though its fragrance can be detected from a distance of forty years."

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ: "Those who seek khul' and those who are removed (by ransom) are the hypocrites."

Then a great many of the early scholars (salaf) and imams of later generations have said: khul' (divorce initiated by the wife through compensation) is not permissible except when the discord (shiqaq) and disobedience (nushuz) come from the wife's side. In that case it is permissible for the husband to accept the ransom (fidyah). They argued with His words: ﴿And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them, [unless both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah]﴾. They said: So He only prescribed khul' in this situation, and it is not permissible in any other case without evidence, and the original state is its absence. Among those who held this view were Ibn 'Abbas, Tawus, Ibrahim, 'Ata', [al-Hasan] and the majority. So much so that Malik and al-Awza'i said: If he took something from her while harming her, it must be returned to her, and the divorce is revocable (raj'i). Malik said: This is the matter upon which I found the people.

Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, held that khul' is permissible in a state of discord, and, by way of greater priority and more certainty, when there is agreement, and this is the view of all his companions without exception. The Shaykh Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr related in his book "al-Istidhkar" from Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani that he held that khul' is abrogated (mansukh) by His words: ﴿But if you have given one of them a great amount, do not take from it anything﴾ [An-Nisa': 20]. Ibn Jarir narrated it from him, but this is a weak view and a rejected basis on the part of its proponent.

Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas and his wife Habibah bint 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. Let us mention the chains of its narration and the variation in its wording:

Imam Malik said in his Muwatta': From Yahya ibn Sa'id, from 'Amrah bint 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'd ibn Zurarah, that she informed him from Habibah bint Sahl al-Ansariyyah, that she was married to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, and that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out for the dawn prayer and found Habibah bint Sahl at his door in the darkness. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Who is this?" She said: "I am Habibah bint Sahl." He said: "What is your matter?" She said: "I am not [able to live with] him, nor is Thabit ibn Qays" (referring to her husband). When her husband Thabit ibn Qays came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "This is Habibah bint Sahl, who has mentioned what Allah willed her to mention." Habibah said: "O Messenger of Allah, all that he gave me is with me." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Take from her." So he took from her, and she sat in her family's house.

Likewise Imam Ahmad narrated it from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Malik, with its chain, the same. Abu Dawud narrated it from al-Qa'nabi, from Malik. And al-Nasa'i from Muhammad ibn Maslamah, from Ibn al-Qasim, from Malik, with it.

Another hadith: from 'A'ishah. Abu Dawud and Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Ma'mar narrated to us, Abu 'Amir narrated to us, Abu 'Amr al-Sadusi narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah [ibn Abi Bakr], from 'Amrah, from 'A'ishah, that Habibah bint Sahl was married to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, and he struck her and broke her arm (nughd), so she came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ after the dawn prayer and complained about him to him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called Thabit and said: "Take some of her property and separate from her." He said: "Would that be permissible, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then I have given her two gardens, and they are in her hand." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Take them both and separate from her." So he did.

This is the wording of Ibn Jarir. Abu 'Amr al-Sadusi is Sa'id ibn Salamah ibn Abi al-Husam.

Another hadith in this regard: from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him:
Al-Bukhari said: Azhar ibn Jamil narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi informed us, Khalid narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: that the wife of Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I do not blame him regarding character or religion, but I dislike disbelief (kufr) in Islam." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Will you return his garden to him?" She said: "Yes." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Accept the garden and divorce her with one divorce."

Likewise al-Nasa'i narrated it from Azhar ibn Jamil with its chain, the same. Al-Bukhari also narrated it from Ishaq al-Wasiti, from Khalid, that is Ibn 'Abd Allah al-Tahhan, from Khalid, that is Ibn Mihran al-Hadhdha', from 'Ikrimah, with it, similarly.

Likewise al-Bukhari also narrated it through several chains, from Ayyub, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, with it. In some of them she said: "I cannot bear him," meaning out of hatred. This hadith is one that al-Bukhari alone narrated through this route.

Then he said: Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ayyub, from 'Ikrimah, that Jamilah, may Allah be pleased with her. Thus he said, but the well-known name is Habibah [as mentioned before].

The Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said in his tafsir: Musa ibn Harun narrated to us, Azhar ibn Marwan al-Raqqashi narrated to us, 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that Jamilah bint Salul came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "By Allah, I do not blame Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas regarding religion or character, but I dislike disbelief after Islam; I cannot bear him out of hatred." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Will you return his garden to him?" She said: "Yes." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded him to take back his garden from her and not to exceed it.

Likewise Ibn Majah narrated it from Azhar ibn Marwan, with its chain, the same. It is a good, sound chain. Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi also narrated it from 'Ubayd Allah al-Qawariri, from 'Abd al-A'la, the same. But Ibn Jarir said:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Thabit, from 'Abd Allah ibn Rabah, from Jamilah bint Ubayy ibn Salul: that she was married to Thabit ibn Qays, and she rebelled against him (nashazat), so the Prophet ﷺ sent for her and said: "O Jamilah, what did you dislike about Thabit?" She said: "By Allah, I did not dislike in him any religion or character, but I disliked his ugliness!" He said to her: "Will you return the garden?" She said: "Yes." So she returned the garden, and he separated them.

Ibn Jarir also said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, he said: I read to Fudayl, from Abu Jarir, that he asked 'Ikrimah: Was there a precedent for khul'? He said: Ibn 'Abbas used to say: The first khul' in Islam was in the case of the sister of 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy: she came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, nothing will ever join my head and his." I lifted the side of the tent and saw him coming among a group, and he was the blackest of them, the shortest in stature, and the ugliest of face. Her husband said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have given her my best property, a garden of mine. Will she return my garden to me?" He said: "What do you say?" She said: "Yes, and if he wishes I will increase it." He said: So he separated them.

Another hadith: Ibn Majah said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, from Hajjaj, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: Habibah bint Sahl was married to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, and he was an ugly man. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, were it not for fear of Allah, when he enters upon me I would spit in his face!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Will you return his garden to him?" She said: "Yes." So she returned his garden to him. He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ separated them.

The imams, may Allah have mercy on them, differed as to whether it is permissible for a man to take from her more than what he gave her. The majority held that this is permissible, by the generality of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿There is no blame upon them for what she gives up therein﴾. Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, Ayyub informed us, from Kathir, the client of Samurah: that 'Umar was brought a rebellious woman, so he ordered her to a house full of dung, then summoned her and said: "How did you find it?" She said: "I have found no ease since I was with him, except this night in which you kept me." He said to her husband: "Divorce her, even if it be for her earring." And 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated it from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from Kathir, client of Samurah, mentioning the like, and he added: So he kept her in it for three days.

Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated from Qatadah, from Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman: that a woman came to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and complained of her husband, so he kept her overnight in a house of dung. When she awoke he said to her: "How did you find your place?" She said: "I have never spent a night with him that was more pleasing to my eye than this night." He said: "Take [from him] even her hair-braids."

Al-Bukhari said: 'Uthman permitted khul' without [taking] the braids of her head.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil: that al-Rubayyi' bint Mu'awwidh ibn 'Afra' narrated to him, she said: I had a husband who used to lavish good upon me when he was present, and deprive me when he was absent from me. She said: One day a lapse came from me, so I said to him: "I will seek khul' from you with everything I possess?" He said: "Yes." She said: So I did. She said: My uncle Mu'adh ibn 'Afra' brought a dispute to 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, so he permitted the khul', and commanded him to take the braids of my head and what is less than them, or she said: what is less than the braids of the head.

The meaning of this is that it is permissible for him to take from her all that is in her hand, whether little or much, leaving her nothing but the braids of her hair. This is also the view of Ibn 'Umar, Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Qabisah ibn Dhu'ayb, al-Hasan ibn Salih, and 'Uthman al-Batti. This is the school of Malik, al-Layth, al-Shafi'i, and Abu Thawr, and Ibn Jarir chose it.

The companions of Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on them, said: If the harm came from her side, it is permissible for him to take from her what he gave her, and exceeding it is not permitted; if he takes more, it is valid in the judgment (al-qada'). If the harm came from his side, he is not permitted to take anything from her, and if he takes, it is valid in the judgment.

Imam Ahmad, Abu 'Ubayd, and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh said: It is not permissible for him to take from her more than what he gave her. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, 'Ata', 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, al-Zuhri, Tawus, al-Hasan, al-Sha'bi, Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas.

Ma'mar and al-Hakam said: 'Ali used to say: He shall not take from the woman who seeks khul' more than what he gave her. Al-Awza'i said: The judges do not permit him to take from her more than what he paid to her as dowry.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 229–230 (part 3 of 5):

I say: This view is supported by what has preceded from the narration of Qatadah, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, concerning the story of Thabit ibn Qays, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered him to take back the garden from her and not to take more. It is also supported by what Abd ibn Humayd narrated, saying: Qabisah informed us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Juraij, from Ata': that the Prophet (ﷺ) disliked that he (the husband) should take from her more than he had given her, meaning the woman who seeks khul' (divorce initiated by the wife through compensation). They interpreted the meaning of the verse according to the meaning of ﴿there is no blame on either of them for what she gives up to be released﴾, i.e., from what he had given her, because of the preceding statement: ﴿And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them, except when both fear that they will not be able to keep the limits of Allah. But if you fear that they will not keep the limits of Allah, there is no blame on either of them for what she gives up to be released﴾, i.e., from that. Thus Ar-Rabi' ibn Anas used to recite it: "there is no blame on either of them for what she gives up to be released from him." Ibn Jarir narrated it. For this reason he said after it: ﴿These are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah, it is those who are the wrongdoers.﴾

Section

Ash-Shafi'i said: Our companions differed concerning khul'. Sufyan informed us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Tawus, from Ibn Abbas, concerning a man who divorced his wife twice and then she sought khul' from him afterwards: he may marry her if he wishes, because Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Divorce is twice﴾, and he recited up to: ﴿that they both return to one another﴾. Ash-Shafi'i said: Sufyan also informed us, from Amr [ibn Dinar], from Ikrimah, who said: Everything that the wealth permits is not a divorce.

And other than ash-Shafi'i narrated, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Tawus, from Ibn Abbas: that Ibrahim ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas asked him, saying: A man divorced his wife twice and then she sought khul' from him; may he marry her? He said: Yes. Khul' is not a divorce. Allah mentioned divorce at the beginning of the verse and at its end, and khul' is between them; so khul' is nothing. Then he recited: ﴿Divorce is twice; then either keep them in an acceptable manner or release them with good treatment﴾, and he recited: ﴿And if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him afterwards until she marries another husband﴾.

This is the view that Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with both of them) took, that khul' is not a divorce but is only a faskh (annulment of the marriage). It is also a narration from the Commander of the Faithful Uthman ibn Affan and from Ibn Umar. It is the view of Tawus and Ikrimah, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, Abu Thawr and Dawud ibn Ali al-Zahiri hold it. It is the school of ash-Shafi'i in his earlier view (al-qadim), and it is the apparent meaning of the noble verse.

The second view concerning khul' is that it is a irrevocable divorce (talaq ba'in), except that he intends more than that. Malik narrated, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Jumhan, mawla of the Aslam tribe, from Umm Bakr al-Aslamiyyah: that she sought khul' from her husband Abd Allah ibn Khalid ibn Usayd, so they both came to Uthman ibn Affan about that. He said: It is one divorce, unless you had specified something, in which case it is what you specified. Ash-Shafi'i said: I do not know Jumhan. Likewise Ahmad ibn Hanbal weakened this report. And Allah knows best.

It has been narrated similarly from Umar, Ali, Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Umar. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Hasan, Ata', Shurayh, ash-Sha'bi, Ibrahim and Jabir ibn Zayd also hold it. Malik, Abu Hanifah and his companions, ath-Thawri, al-Awza'i, Uthman al-Batti, and ash-Shafi'i in his later view (al-jadid) went to it. However, the Hanafis hold that whenever the one who seeks khul' intends by his khul' one or two divorces, or gives no specification, it is one irrevocable divorce; and if he intends three, it is three. Ash-Shafi'i has another view concerning khul', namely that whenever it is not with the wording of divorce and is without intention, it is nothing at all.

Issue:

Malik, Abu Hanifah, ash-Shafi'i, and Ahmad and Ishaq in one narration from them (which is the well-known one) went to the view that the woman who has sought khul' has the waiting period (iddah) of a divorced woman, three menstrual cycles (quru'), if she is one who menstruates. This was narrated from Umar, Ali and Ibn Umar. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Sulayman ibn Yasar, Urwah, Salim, Abu Salamah, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, Ibn Shihab, al-Hasan, ash-Sha'bi, Ibrahim an-Nakha'i, Abu Iyad, Julas ibn Amr, Qatadah, Sufyan ath-Thawri, al-Awza'i, Layth ibn Sa'd and Abu Ubayd also hold it. At-Tirmidhi said: This is the view of most of the people of knowledge among the Companions and others. Their basis in this is that khul' is a divorce, so she observes the iddah like all divorced women.

The second view: she observes the iddah of one menstrual cycle, by which she cleanses her womb. Ibn Abi Shaybah said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Ubayd Allah ibn Umar, from Nafi': that al-Rubayyi' sought khul' from her husband, so her paternal uncle came to Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him), and he said: She observes one menstrual cycle. He said: Ibn Umar used to say: She observes three menstrual cycles, until Uthman said this; so Ibn Umar would issue legal rulings according to it, saying: Uthman is better than us and more knowledgeable than us.

And Abdah narrated to us, from Ubayd Allah, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: The iddah of the woman who seeks khul' is one menstrual cycle.

And Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Layth, from Tawus, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Her iddah is one menstrual cycle. Ikrimah, Aban ibn Uthman, and everyone previously mentioned who says that khul' is faskh (annulment) must hold this view. They argued for it with what Abu Dawud and at-Tirmidhi narrated, for each of them said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Baghdadi narrated to us, Ali ibn Bahr narrated to us, Hisham ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Amr ibn Muslim, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: that the wife of Thabit ibn Qays sought khul' from her husband in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered her to observe the iddah of one menstrual cycle. Then at-Tirmidhi said: Hasan gharib (a good report with an unusual chain). Abd al-Razzaq narrated it from Ma'mar, from Amr ibn Muslim, from Ikrimah, as a mursal (a report lacking the Companion's name).

Another hadith: At-Tirmidhi said: Mahmud ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, al-Fadl ibn Musa narrated to us, from Sufyan, Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, who is the mawla of the family of Talhah, from Sulayman ibn Yasar, from ar-Rubayyi' bint Mu'awwidh ibn Afra': that she sought khul' in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered her, or she was ordered, to observe the iddah of one menstrual cycle. At-Tirmidhi said: The correct version is that she was ordered to observe the iddah of one menstrual cycle.

Another route: Ibn Majah said: Ali ibn Salamah al-Naysaburi narrated to us, Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Ubadah ibn al-Walid ibn Ubadah ibn al-Samit informed me, from ar-Rubayyi' bint Mu'awwidh ibn Afra', who said: I said to her: Tell me your story. She said: I sought khul' from my husband, then I came to Uthman and asked: What iddah is due upon me? He said: There is no iddah upon you, except that if it is recent with you, you stay with him until you menstruate once. She said: He only followed in this the judgment of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning Maryam al-Mughaliyyah, who was married to Thabit ibn Qays, and she sought khul' from him.

Ibn Lahi'ah narrated from Abu al-Aswad, from Abu Salamah and Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Thawban, from ar-Rubayyi' bint Mu'awwidh, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordering the wife of Thabit ibn Qays, when she sought khul' from him, to observe the iddah of one menstrual cycle.

Issue:
