The seventh hadith: from Ibn Umar. al-Hakim said in his Mustadrak: Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Saghani narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, Abu Ghassan Muhammad ibn Mutarrif al-Madani narrated to us, from Umar ibn Nafi', from his father, that he said: A man came to Ibn Umar and asked him about a man who divorced his wife thrice, and then his brother married her without his consultation, in order to make her lawful for his brother: "Is she lawful to the first?" He said: "No, except a marriage of desire. We used to count this as fornication (sifah) during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." Then he said: "This is a hadith with a sahih chain, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not narrate it."

Al-Thawri also narrated it from Abdullah ibn Nafi', from his father, from Ibn Umar, with it. This wording indicates that it is marfu' (traced to the Prophet). Similarly, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Jawzajani, Harb al-Karmani and Abu Bakr al-Athram narrated, from the hadith of al-A'mash, from al-Musayyab ibn Rafi', from Qabisah ibn Jabir, from Umar, that he said: "I will not be brought a muhallil or a muhallal lahu except that I stone them both."

Al-Bayhaqi narrated from the hadith of Ibn Lahi'ah, from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj, from Sulayman ibn Yasar, that a man was brought before Uthman ibn Affan who had married a woman in order to make her lawful for her husband, so he separated them. Similarly, it was narrated from Ali, Ibn Abbas and a number of other Companions, may Allah be pleased with them.

* *

His saying: ﴿So if he divorces her﴾, i.e., the second husband after consummating with her, ﴿there is no blame upon them both for returning to one another﴾, i.e., the woman and the first husband, ﴿if they think that they can keep within the limits of Allah﴾, i.e., that they will live together in kindness [Mujahid said: "if they think that their marriage is not for deception"] ﴿And these are the limits of Allah﴾, i.e., His laws and rulings, ﴿which He makes clear﴾, i.e., explains, ﴿for a people who know.﴾

The imams, may Allah have mercy on them, differed regarding the case where a man divorces his wife with one or two pronouncements and leaves her until her waiting period ends, then she marries another man who consummates with her, then he divorces her and her waiting period ends, and then the first husband marries her again: Does she return to him with the remaining three (pronouncements), as is the position of Malik, al-Shafi'i and Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and it is the view of a group of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them? Or does the second husband annul what came before of divorce, so that when she returns to the first she returns with the whole three, as is the position of Abu Hanifah and his companions, may Allah have mercy on them? Their proof is that if the second husband annuls the three, then he annuls what is less than them all the more so, and Allah knows best.

This is a command from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to men: when one of them divorces his wife with a divorce that allows him to take her back, he should deal well with her affair when her waiting period (ʿiddah) has ended and only as much time remains in which he can take her back. Then either he retains her, that is, he takes her back into the bond of marriage (ʿişmat nikah) in a fair manner, which means he calls witnesses to her return and intends to live with her kindly; or he releases her, that is, leaves her until her waiting period ends, and lets her go from his home in the best manner, without discord, quarrelling or foul speech. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And do not keep them in marriage to harm them, to transgress against them.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, Masruq, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Rabiʿ, Muqatil ibn Hayyan and others said: A man would divorce his wife, and when she neared the end of her waiting period he would take her back, not to keep her but to harm her, so that she would not go to another man. Then he would divorce her again, and she would observe the waiting period anew. When she was about to complete it, he would divorce her so that the waiting period would be prolonged for her. So Allah forbade them from that and warned them against it, saying: ﴿And whoever does that has certainly wronged himself﴾, that is, by opposing the command of Allah the Exalted.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And do not take the verses of Allah in jest﴾, Ibn Jarir said concerning this verse:

Abu Kurayb informed us, Ishaq ibn Mansur informed us, from ʿAbd al-Salam ibn Harb, from Yazid ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from Abu al-ʿAlaa al-Awdi, from Humayd ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from Abu Musa: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) became angry with the Ashʿaris, so Abu Musa came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, are you angry with the Ashʿaris?" He said: "One of you says: 'I have divorced, I have taken back,' this is not the divorce of the Muslims. Divorce the woman at the time of her waiting period [[Tafsir al-Tabari (5/14).]]."

Then he narrated it by another route [[In manuscript C: "Then Ibn Majah narrated it by another route."]] from Abu Khalid al-Dallani, who is Yazid ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, and there is discussion concerning him.

Masruq said: it is the one who divorces at other than the proper time, and harms his wife by divorcing her and taking her back, so that the waiting period is prolonged for her.

Al-Hasan, Qatadah, ʿAta al-Khurasani, al-Rabiʿ and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: it is the man who divorces and says, "I was only joking," or who frees a slave and says, "I was only joking," or who marries and says, "I was only joking." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not take the verses of Allah in jest﴾, and by that He obligated them.

Ibn Mardawayh said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Abu Ahmad al-Sayrafi narrated to us, Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad al-Simsar narrated to me, from Ismaʿil ibn Yahya, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: A man divorced his wife while playing, not intending divorce; so Allah revealed: ﴿And do not take the verses of Allah in jest﴾, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) obligated him to the divorce.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: ʿIsam ibn Rawwad narrated to us, Adam narrated to us, al-Mubarak ibn Fadalah narrated to us, from al-Hasan, that is al-Basri, who said: A man would divorce and say, "I was only joking," or free a slave and say, "I was only joking," or marry and say, "I was only joking." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not take the verses of Allah in jest﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever divorces, frees, marries, or arranges a marriage, whether in earnest or in jest, it takes effect against him."

Similarly, Ibn Jarir narrated it through al-Zuhri, from Sulayman ibn Arqam, from al-Hasan, the like of it. This is a mursal report [[Tafsir al-Tabari (5/13). Ibn Abi Shaybah also narrated it in al-Musannaf (5/106) by another route, from ʿIsa ibn Yunus, from ʿAmr, from al-Hasan.]]. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it through ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd, from al-Hasan, from Abu al-Darda, as a statement of his (mawquf). He also said:

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan [[In manuscript C: "ibn al-Husayn."]] ibn Ayyub narrated to us, Yaʿqub ibn Abi Yaʿqub narrated to us, Yahya ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid narrated to us, Abu Muʿawiyah narrated to us, from Ismaʿil ibn Salamah, from al-Hasan, from ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit, regarding Allah's saying: ﴿And do not take the verses of Allah in jest﴾. He said: In the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) a man would say to another, "I have married you my daughter," and then say, "I was only joking." And he would say, "I have freed," and then say, "I was only joking." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not take the verses of Allah in jest﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Three things, whoever says them in jest or in earnest, they are binding upon him: divorce, emancipation, and marriage [[Al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah narrated it in his Musnad, no. 501 (Zawa'id), by another route: from Ibn Lahi'ah, from ʿUbayd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far, from ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit, as a marfu' report.]]."

The well-known hadith in this matter is the one narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, by way of ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Habib ibn Ardak, from ʿAta, from Ibn Mahak, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Three things, whether done in earnest or in jest, are binding: marriage, divorce, and taking back [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2194), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1184), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (2039).]]." Al-Tirmidhi said: it is hasan gharib.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And remember the favour of Allah upon you﴾, that is, in His sending the Messenger to you with guidance and clear proofs, ﴿and what He has sent down to you of the Book and wisdom﴾, that is, the Sunnah, ﴿He instructs you thereby﴾, that is, He commands you, forbids you, and warns you against committing the prohibited things, ﴿and fear Allah﴾, that is, in what you do and what you leave undone, ﴿and know that Allah is Knowing of all things﴾, that is, nothing of your affairs, whether secret or open, is hidden from Him, and He will recompense you for that.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 232:

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: This verse was revealed concerning a man who divorces his wife with one or two divorces, and her waiting period (iddah) ends, then it occurs to him to marry her again and to take her back (raji'ah), and the woman wants that, but her guardians (awliya') prevent her from it. So Allah forbade them from preventing her. Al-Awfi also related it from him, and Masruq, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Zuhri and al-Dahhak said likewise, that it was revealed concerning that. What they said is apparent from the verse, and in it is an indication that a woman does not have the right to marry herself, and that a guardian (wali) is necessary in her marriage (nikah), as al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Jarir said regarding this verse, as has come in the hadith: "A woman should not marry a woman, nor should a woman marry herself, for it is the adulteress who marries herself." [[Narrated by Ibn Majah in al-Sunan, no. (1882), through Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, as a marfu' report. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (2/84): "This chain is disputed."]] And in another report: "There is no nikah except with a guardian who is upright (murshid), and two just witnesses." On this matter there is a dispute among the scholars, which is discussed in its place in the books of jurisprudence (furu'). We have established this in our book "al-Ahkam," and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

It has been related that this verse was revealed concerning Ma'qil ibn Yasar al-Muzani and his sister. Al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his Sahih at the explanation of this verse:

Ubayd Allah ibn Sa'id related to us: Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi related to us: 'Abbad ibn Rashid related to us: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Ma'qil ibn Yasar related to me, saying: I had a sister who was being proposed for (in marriage) to me. — Al-Bukhari said: And Ibrahim said, from Yunus, from al-Hasan: Ma'qil ibn Yasar related to me. And Abu Ma'mar related to us: 'Abd al-Warith related to us: Yunus related to us, from al-Hasan: that the sister of Ma'qil ibn Yasar was divorced by her husband, and he left her until her waiting period ended, then he proposed to her, and Ma'qil refused, so this verse was revealed: "Do not prevent them from marrying their husbands." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4529).]]

Likewise it was narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh through multiple chains, from al-Hasan, from Ma'qil ibn Yasar, with it. [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2087); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2981); Tafsir al-Tabari (5/17, 18). al-Mizzi did not attribute it in Tuhfat al-Ashraf to Sunan Ibn Majah.]] Al-Tirmidhi also authenticated it, and its wording from Ma'qil ibn Yasar is: that he married his sister to a man from the Muslims during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and she remained with him for a time, then he divorced her with one divorce, and did not take her back until her waiting period ended. Then he (the husband) desired her and she desired him, so he proposed to her again along with the other suitors, and he (Ma'qil) said to him: "O you base one! I honoured you by her and married her to you, but you divorced her! By Allah, she will never return to you, the last of what is upon you." He said: So Allah knew his need for her and her need for her husband, and Allah revealed: "And when you divorce women and they reach their term..." up to His words: "And you do not know." When Ma'qil heard it he said: "Hearing and obedience to my Lord." Then he called him and said: "I will marry you and honour you." Ibn Mardawayh added: "And I expiated for my oath."

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn Jurayj, who said: she was Jumal bint Yasar, who was under Abu al-Baddah. Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, who said: she was Fatimah bint Yasar. Thus more than one of the early scholars (salaf) mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning Ma'qil ibn Yasar and his sister. Al-Suddi said: it was revealed concerning Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah and a cousin (paternal) of his. The first is the sound one, and Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: "That is admonished by it whoever among you believes in Allah and the Last Day." That is: this which We have forbidden you from, namely preventing the guardians from letting them marry their husbands when they agree among themselves in a fair manner, is what one is commanded by, is admonished by, and is moved by. "Whoever among you," O people, "believes in Allah and the Last Day": that is, believes in the Law of Allah, and fears the threat and punishment of Allah in the Hereafter and what is in it of recompense. "That is purer for you and more pure": that is, your following the Law of Allah in returning the divorced women to their husbands, and abandoning zealous pride in that, is more pure (azka) for you and more purifying (athar) for your hearts. "And Allah knows": that is, the benefits in what He commands and forbids. "And you do not know": that is, the good in what you do and what you leave undone.

This is a directive from Allah, the Exalted, to mothers: they should breastfeed their children for the full period of nursing, which is two years. Nursing after that period carries no legal weight. For this reason He said: ﴿for those who wish to complete the nursing﴾. Most of the imams held that only nursing that takes place before the two years (al-hawlayn) establishes marriage prohibitions (tahrim). So if a child nurses when he is over two years old, no prohibition is established.

At-Tirmidhi said: "Chapter: What has been reported that nursing establishes prohibition only in infancy, before the two years." Qutaybah narrated to us: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from Fatimah bint al-Mundhir, from Umm Salamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Nursing establishes no prohibition except what breaks open the intestines at the breast and occurs before weaning." He said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith. The practice of most of the people of knowledge among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and others is in accordance with this: that nursing establishes no prohibition except what occurs before the two years, and whatever occurs after the two complete years establishes no prohibition at all." Fatimah bint al-Mundhir ibn al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam was the wife of Hisham ibn 'Urwah. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1152.]

I say: At-Tirmidhi alone narrated this hadith, and its narrators meet the conditions of the two Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim). The meaning of his words "except what was in the breast" is: in the place of nursing, before the two years, as in the hadith narrated by Ahmad, from Waki' and Ghundar, from Shu'bah, from 'Adi ibn Thabit, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: When Ibrahim, the son of the Prophet ﷺ, died, he said: "Indeed he has a wet-nurse in Paradise." Al-Bukhari also narrated it in this form from the hadith of Shu'bah. [Musnad Ahmad (4/300) and Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1382.] He, peace be upon him, said this because his son Ibrahim, peace be upon him, died when he was one year and ten months old. So he said: "Indeed he has a wet-nurse in Paradise," meaning: one who will complete his nursing. This is supported by what al-Daraqutni narrated through al-Haytham ibn Jamil, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Nursing establishes no prohibition except what occurs within the two years." Then he said: No one narrated it from Ibn 'Uyaynah except al-Haytham ibn Jamil, and he is trustworthy and a memoriser (thiqah hafiz). [Sunan al-Daraqutni (4/174).]

I say: Imam Malik narrated it in al-Muwatta', from Thawr ibn Zayd, from Ibn 'Abbas, as a statement of Ibn 'Abbas (mawquf) [in ha: "marfu'" (raised to the Prophet), but the correct reading is what we have recorded from jim, alif, waw, as Shaykh Ahmad Shakir, may Allah have mercy on him, pointed out]. [Al-Muwatta' (2/602).] Al-Darawardi narrated it from Thawr, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, and added: "Whatever occurs after the two years is nothing," and this is more sound.

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no nursing after weaning, and no orphanhood after reaching puberty." The full evidence from this hadith is found in His words: ﴿and his weaning is in two years﴾ [Luqman: 14], and His words: ﴿his bearing and his weaning are thirty months﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15]. The view that nursing does not establish prohibition after the two years is reported from 'Ali, Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud, Jabir, Abu Hurayrah, Ibn 'Umar, Umm Salamah, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, 'Ata', and the majority (al-jumhur). It is the position of al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, Ishaq, al-Thawri, Abu Yusuf, Muhammad, and Malik in one narration. Another narration from Malik is that its period is two years and two months, and in another narration three months. Abu Hanifah said: two years and six months. Zufar ibn al-Hudhayl said: as long as he is being nursed, it is up to three years, and this is a narration from al-Awza'i. Malik said: If the child was weaned before the two years and then a woman nursed him after his weaning, no prohibition is established, because he has by then become like food. This is also a narration from al-Awza'i. It has been reported from 'Umar and 'Ali that they both said: "There is no nursing after weaning." It is possible that they meant the two years, as the majority say, whether or not he was weaned; and it is possible that they meant the act (of weaning), as Malik says. And Allah knows best.

It has been reported in the Sahih, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that she used to hold that nursing an adult affects prohibition. This is the view of 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah and al-Layth ibn Sa'd. 'A'ishah used to instruct whichever men she chose to come in to some of her women, so that they would nurse, and she argued for this from the hadith of Salim, the freedman of Abu Hudhayfah, when the Prophet ﷺ commanded Abu Hudhayfah's wife to nurse him, and he was an adult; so he would enter upon her by that nursing. All the other wives of the Prophet ﷺ rejected this, and they regarded it as one of the special privileges (khasa'is). This is the view of the majority. The evidence of the majority, including the four imams, the seven jurists, the senior Companions, and all the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ other than 'A'ishah, is what is established in the two Sahihs from 'A'ishah: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Look carefully at who your brothers are, for nursing is only what establishes relationship through hunger (al-majā'ah)." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2647, and Sahih Muslim, no. 1455.] The discussion of the rulings on nursing, and what relates to the nursing of an adult, will come under His words, may He be exalted: ﴿and your mothers who have nursed you﴾ [al-Nisa': 23].

* *

His words: ﴿And upon the father of the child is their provision and their clothing according to what is reasonable﴾: that is, upon the father of the child is the maintenance of the mothers and their clothing according to what is reasonable, meaning according to what is customary for women like them in their land, without extravagance or stinginess, in accordance with his ability, whether he is wealthy, of moderate means, or straitened. As He said, may He be exalted: ﴿Let the one of wealth spend from his wealth, and he whose provision is restricted, let him spend from what Allah has given him. Allah does not burden a soul except with what He has given it. Allah will bring about ease after hardship﴾ [al-Talaq: 7]. Al-Dahhak said: If a man divorces his wife and she has a child from him, and she nurses his child for him, then the father is obligated to provide for her maintenance and clothing according to what is reasonable.

* *

His words: ﴿No mother should be harmed through her child﴾: that is, she should not withhold him from the father to harm the father through his upbringing. But she does not have the right to withhold him after she has given birth, until she has given him the colostrum (al-liba'), without which he generally cannot survive. After that she may remove him from her if she wishes. However, if she intends to harm his father, it is not lawful for her to do so, just as it is not lawful for him to take the child from her merely to harm her. For this reason He said: ﴿nor a father through his child﴾: that is, by intending to take the child from her in order to harm her. This was said by Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Zuhri, al-Suddi, al-Thawri, Ibn Zayd, and others.

* *

His words: ﴿And upon the heir is the like of that﴾. It was said: it means not harming his relative; this was said by Mujahid, al-Sha'bi, and al-Dahhak. It was also said: upon him is the like of what is upon the father of the child in terms of maintaining the child's mother, fulfilling her rights, and not harming her. This is the view of the majority. Ibn Jarir thoroughly examined this in his tafsir. The Hanafis and Hanbalis who held that the maintenance of relatives is obligatory upon one another used this verse as evidence. This is also reported from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and the majority of the early generations (al-salaf). It is supported by the hadith of al-Hasan, from Samurah, raised to the Prophet: "Whoever owns a close relative within the prohibited degrees, he is freed by it (i.e., manumitted)." [Narrated by Abu Dawud, Sunan, no. 3949, and al-Tirmidhi, Sunan, no. 1365, by way of 'Asim al-Ahwal from al-Hasan. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hadith we do not know as musnad except from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, and some of them narrated this hadith from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from 'Umar something of this." Its wording in both is: "Whoever owns a close relative within the prohibited degrees, he is free."]

It has been mentioned that nursing after the two years may sometimes harm the child, either in his body or his mind. Sufyan al-Thawri narrated, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, that he saw a woman nursing after the two years, and said: "Do not nurse him."

* *

His words: ﴿But if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation, there is no blame upon them﴾: that is, if the two parents of the child agree on weaning him before the two years, and see benefit for him in it, and consult about it, and both agree upon it, then there is no blame upon them for it. From this it is taken that one of them acting alone without the other is not sufficient, and neither of them may decide it on his own without consulting the other. This was said by al-Thawri and others. This contains caution for the child and obliges careful consideration of his matter. It is among the mercy of Allah toward His servants, in that He restrained the parents in raising their child and guided them to what benefits him and benefits them, as He said in Surah al-Talaq: ﴿And if they breastfeed for you, give them their payment, and confer among yourselves in kindness; but if you are in difficulty, then another woman may nurse for him﴾ [al-Talaq: 6].

* *

His words: ﴿And if you wish to have your children nursed by a wet-nurse, there is no blame upon you, provided you pay what you give according to what is reasonable﴾: that is, if the mother and father agree that the child be handed over to a wet-nurse from her, either for an excuse from her or an excuse from him, then there is no blame upon them in handing him over, nor upon him in accepting him from her, provided he pays her the wages owed for past service in the best manner, and hires another woman to nurse his child for a fee according to what is reasonable. This was said by more than one scholar.

* *

His words: ﴿And fear Allah﴾: that is, in all your circumstances. ﴿And know that Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾: that is, nothing of your states or your words is hidden from Him.

This is a command from Allah to the women whose husbands die: they shall observe a waiting period of four months and ten nights [[In J (Ghayn?) and the other manuscript: "ليالي" (nights)]]. This ruling includes wives who have been consummated with and those who have not, by consensus (ijma', scholarly agreement). The evidence for the case of the unconsummated wife is the general wording of the noble verse, and this hadith, which Imam Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan collections narrated, and which al-Tirmidhi declared sound: Ibn Mas'ud was asked about a man who married a woman, then died before consummating the marriage and without setting a dower for her. The people went back to him repeatedly about this, so he said: "I will give my opinion on it. If it is correct, it is from Allah, and if it is wrong, it is from me and from Shaytan, and Allah and His Messenger are free of it: I judge that she is owed the full dower." In another wording: "She is owed the dower of her equals, neither less nor excessive, and she must observe the 'iddah (waiting period), and she inherits." Then Ma'qil ibn Sinan al-Ashja'i stood up and said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rule on this in the case of Barwa' bint Washiq." Ibn Mas'ud was greatly delighted by this. In another narration: "Men from Ashja' stood up and said: 'We testify that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ruled on this in the case of Barwa' bint Washiq.'" [[Musnad (4/280); Sunan Abi Dawud, nos. 2114, 2115; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1145; Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/121); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 1891.]]

The only exception to this is the woman whose husband dies while she is pregnant. Her waiting period ends with giving birth, even if she remains only a moment after it, based on the general statement of Allah: ﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth to their load﴾ [al-Talaq: 4]. Ibn 'Abbas held that she must wait for the longer of two periods: either giving birth or four months and ten days, in order to combine the two verses. This is a good line of reasoning and a strong approach, were it not that the Sunnah has established otherwise in the hadith of Subay'a al-Aslamiyya, recorded in the two Sahihs through multiple chains: her husband Sa'd ibn Khawla died while she was pregnant, and she gave birth shortly after his death. In another narration: "She gave birth to her child a few nights after him. When she became clean from her postnatal bleeding, she adorned herself for suitors. Abu al-Sanabil ibn Ba'kak entered upon her and said to her: 'Why do I see you adorned? Perhaps you hope to marry. By Allah, you will not marry until four months and ten days have passed over you.' Subay'a said: 'When he said that to me, I gathered my clothes around me in the evening, and I went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and asked him about it. He gave me a ruling that I had become free (from the waiting period) when I gave birth, and he commanded me to marry if I wished.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5319; Sahih Muslim, no. 1484.]

Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: It has been narrated that Ibn 'Abbas returned to the hadith of Subay'a when it was used as an argument against him. He said: "What confirms this from him is that his companions gave fatwas according to the hadith of Subay'a, and this is the view of all the people of knowledge."

Likewise, the slave wife is excepted from this ruling. Her waiting period is half that of a free woman: two months and five nights, according to the majority of scholars. This is because, since her legal punishment is half that of a free woman, her waiting period should likewise be half. Some scholars, such as Muhammad ibn Sirin and some of the Zahiriyya, hold that slave and free wives are equal in this matter, based on the general wording of the verse, and because the waiting period is one of the natural matters in which all creatures are equal. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Abu al-'Aliya and others mentioned that the wisdom behind making the waiting period for death four months and ten days is the possibility that the womb contains a child. If she waits this period, it becomes clear whether there is a child, as came in the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud recorded in the two Sahihs and elsewhere: "Indeed, the creation of each of you is gathered in his mother's belly for forty days as a drop, then it becomes a clot of similar length, then a lump of similar length, then the angel is sent to it and breathes the soul into it." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3208; Sahih Muslim, no. 2643.] So these are three periods of forty, totaling four months, and the ten days after them are added as a precaution, because some months may be short, and then for the appearance of movement after the soul is breathed into the child. And Allah knows best.

Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated from Qatada: "I asked Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: 'What about the ten (days)?' He said: 'In them the soul is breathed.'" Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "I asked Abu al-'Aliya: 'Why did these ten (days) come together with the four months?' He said: 'Because the soul is breathed in them.'" Ibn Jarir narrated both. From this point, Imam Ahmad, in one narration from him, held that the waiting period of the umm al-walad (a slave woman who bore her master's child) is the same as that of a free woman in this case, because she became a bed-partner like free women. He also relied on the hadith that Imam Ahmad narrated from Yazid ibn Harun, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatada, from Raja' ibn Haywa, from Qabisa ibn Dhu'ayb, from 'Amr ibn al-'As, that he said: "Do not confuse us about the Sunnah of our Prophet: the waiting period of the umm al-walad, when her master dies, is four months and ten (days)." [Musnad (4/203).] Abu Dawud narrated it from Qutayba, from Ghundar; and from Ibn al-Muthanna, from 'Abd al-A'la; and Ibn Majah from 'Ali ibn Muhammad, from Waki'. All three narrated it from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Matar al-Warraq, from Raja' ibn Haywa, from Qabisa, from 'Amr ibn al-'As, and mentioned it. [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2308; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2083.]

It has been narrated from Imam Ahmad that he rejected this hadith, and it was said that Qabisa did not hear from 'Amr. A group of the early scholars (salaf) took the position of this hadith, among them: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Abu 'Iyad, al-Zuhri, and 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz. Yazid ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, who was Commander of the Believers, used to order this. Al-Awza'i, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal in one narration from him also say this. Tawus and Qatada said: The waiting period of the umm al-walad when her master dies is half the waiting period of a free woman: two months and five nights. Abu Hanifa and his companions, al-Thawri, and al-Hasan ibn Salih ibn Hayy said: She observes three menstrual cycles. This is the view of 'Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, 'Ata', and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i. Malik, al-Shafi'i, and Ahmad in his well-known position said: Her waiting period is one menstrual cycle. This is the view of Ibn 'Umar, al-Sha'bi, Makhul, al-Layth, Abu 'Ubayd, Abu Thawr, and the majority.

Al-Layth said: If she dies while menstruating, it suffices her. Malik said: If she is one who does not menstruate, then it is three months. Al-Shafi'i and the majority said: One month, but three is more beloved to me. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿Then when they have reached their term, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an appropriate manner. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾. From this is derived the obligation of mourning (ihdad) for the widow during her waiting period, based on what is established in the two Sahihs through multiple chains from Umm Habiba and Zaynab bint Jahsh, the Mothers of the Believers, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn over a dead person for more than three days, except for a husband, for four months and ten (days)." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5337; Sahih Muslim, no. 1486, from the hadith of Zaynab bint Jahsh (may Allah be pleased with her); Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5334; Sahih Muslim, no. 1486, from the hadith of Umm Habiba (may Allah be pleased with her).] Also in the two Sahihs, from Umm Salama: a woman said: "O Messenger of Allah, my daughter's husband has died, and her eye has become inflamed. Shall we apply kohl to it?" He said: "No." He said this each time, twice or three times. Then he said: "It is only four months and ten (days). In the Jahiliyya, one of you would remain for a full year." Zaynab bint Umm Salama said: "When a woman's husband died, she would enter a hut, wear her worst clothes, and not touch perfume or anything else until a year had passed over her. Then she would come out and be given a piece of animal dung, which she would throw, then a beast—a donkey, sheep, or bird—would be brought, and she would rub herself against it. She would rarely rub against anything without it dying." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5336; Sahih Muslim, no. 1488.]

From this point, many scholars held that this verse abrogates (naskh, the lifting of a ruling by a later one) the verse after it, which is His saying: ﴿And those who die among you and leave wives behind—a bequest for their wives: provision for a year without eviction﴾ [al-Baqara: 240], as Ibn 'Abbas and others said. But this requires examination, as will be explained.

The point is that ihdad is the abandonment of adornment, including perfume, and wearing what would attract men, such as clothing, jewelry, and the like. It is obligatory during the waiting period for death without any disagreement. It is not obligatory during the waiting period for a revocable divorce, without any disagreement. As for the waiting period for an irrevocable divorce (ba'in), is it obligatory? There are two opinions on this.

Ihdad is obligatory for all wives whose husbands have died, whether young or old, free or slave, Muslim or non-Muslim, because of the general wording of the verse. Al-Thawri, Abu Hanifa, and his companions said: There is no ihdad for a non-Muslim woman. Ashhab and Ibn Nafi', from the companions of Malik, also say this. The argument of those who hold this view is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn over a dead person for more than three days, except for a husband, for four months and ten (days)." They said: So he made it an act of worship (ta'abbud). Abu Hanifa, his companions, and al-Thawri considered the young girl to be included in this ruling, because she is not legally accountable. Abu Hanifa and his companions also included the Muslim slave woman, because of her deficiency. The full discussion of all this is in the books of legal rulings and jurisprudence (furu'). And Allah is the One who grants success in what is correct.

* *

His saying: ﴿Then when they have reached their term﴾, meaning: when their waiting periods have ended. This was said by al-Dahhak and al-Rabi' ibn Anas. ﴿There is no blame upon you﴾: al-Zuhri said: meaning, upon their guardians. ﴿For what they do﴾: meaning, the women whose waiting periods have ended. Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "When a woman is divorced or her husband dies, and when her waiting period has ended, there is no blame on her if she adorns herself, beautifies herself, and makes herself available for marriage. That is the appropriate (ma'ruf) conduct." A similar report was narrated from Muqatil ibn Hayyan. Ibn Jurayj said, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿There is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an appropriate manner﴾: "It is lawful, good marriage." Similar things were narrated from al-Hasan, al-Zuhri, and al-Suddi.

Ibn Kathir said, may God Most High: "There is no blame upon you" (﴿وَلا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾) for making an indirect proposal of marriage (taʿrid, an allusion) to women during their 'iddah (waiting period) after the death of their husbands, without explicit declaration. Al-Thawri, Shuʿbah, Jarir and others related, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: "There is no blame upon you for what you allude to of the proposal to women" (﴿وَلا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيمَا عَرَّضْتُمْ بِهِ مِنْ خِطْبَةِ النِّسَاءِ﴾), that he said: The allusion (taʿrid) is that you say: "I want to marry, and I love a woman of her qualities, and of her qualities," - he alludes to her with words of good meaning - and in another narration: "I wish that God would provide me with a woman," and similar to this. And he does not set up for the proposal. And in another narration: "I do not wish to marry anyone other than you, God willing, and I would love to find a righteous woman," and he does not set up for her as long as she is in her 'iddah.

Al-Bukhari related it in suspended form (taʿliq), saying: Talq ibn Ghannam said to me, from Za'idah, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas: "There is no blame upon you for what you allude to of the proposal to women" (﴿وَلا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيمَا عَرَّضْتُمْ بِهِ مِنْ خِطْبَةِ النِّسَاءِ﴾) is that he says: "I want to marry, and women are among my needs, and I would love that a righteous woman be made easy for me." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5124).]]

Likewise said Mujahid, Tawus, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Zuhri, Yazid ibn Qusayt, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, and many others among the early generations (salaf) and imams, regarding allusion: that it is permissible for a woman whose husband has died to be approached indirectly, without explicit proposal to her. Likewise the ruling for a woman irrevocably divorced (mabtutah) is that allusion to her is permissible, as the Prophet ﷺ said to Fatimah bint Qays, when her husband Abu 'Amr ibn Hafs divorced her with the final of three pronouncements: "Observe your 'iddah in the house of Ibn Umm Maktum," and he said to her: "When you have finished your waiting period, inform me." When she had completed it, he proposed on her behalf to Usamah ibn Zayd, his freedman, and she was married to him. [[Related by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (1480).]]

As for the revocably divorced woman (al-mutallaqah al-raj'iyyah): there is no disagreement that it is not permissible for anyone other than her husband to propose to her explicitly or to allude to her. And God knows best.

* *

His saying: "Or you conceal it within yourselves" (﴿أَوْ أَكْنَنْتُمْ فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾), i.e., you harbor within yourselves the intention of proposing to them. This is like His saying: "And your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they disclose" [al-Qasas: 69], and like His saying: "And I know best what you conceal and what you disclose" [al-Mumtahanah: 1]. Therefore He said: "God knows that you will remember them" (﴿عَلِمَ اللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ سَتَذْكُرُونَهُنَّ﴾), i.e., in your hearts, so He lifted the blame from you in that matter. Then He said: "But do not promise them secretly" (﴿وَلَكِنْ لَا تُوَاعِدُوهُنَّ سِرًّا﴾). Abu Mijlaz, Abu al-Sha'tha' (Jabir ibn Zayd), al-Hasan al-Basri, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Sulayman al-Taymi, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and al-Suddi said: it means fornication (zina). This is the meaning of the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas, and it is what Ibn Jarir chose.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: "But do not promise them secretly" means: do not say to her, "I am infatuated with you," and make her promise, "Do not marry anyone other than me," and similar. Likewise it is reported from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Sha'bi, 'Ikrimah, Abu al-Duha, al-Dahhak, al-Zuhri, Mujahid, and al-Thawri: it is that he takes her pledge not to marry anyone other than him. And from Mujahid: it is a man's saying to a woman, "Do not get away from me by yourself, for I will marry you."

Qatadah said: it is that he takes the woman's pledge, while she is in her 'iddah, that she will not marry anyone other than him; so God forbade that and made it a matter of precedence, and permitted the proposal and speaking in a fitting manner.

Ibn Zayd said: "But do not promise them secretly" means that he marries her secretly during the 'iddah; then when she is free, he makes it public.

It may be that the verse is general over all of this; therefore He said: "except that you say a fitting word" (﴿إلا أَنْ تَقُولُوا قَوْلا مَعْرُوفًا﴾). Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Suddi, al-Thawri, and Ibn Zayd said: it means what has preceded, namely the permission of allusion, like saying: "I am truly interested in you," and similar.

Muhammad ibn Sirin said: I said to 'Abidah: What is the meaning of His saying: "except that you say a fitting word"? He said: He says to her guardian (waliyy): "Do not outrun me with her," meaning: do not marry her off until you inform me. Related by Ibn Abi Hatim.

* *

His saying: "And do not determine the bond of marriage until the decreed term reaches its end" (﴿وَلا تَعْزِمُوا عُقْدَةَ النِّكَاحِ حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ الْكِتَابُ أَجَلَهُ﴾), meaning: do not conclude the marriage contract until the 'iddah has ended. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Sha'bi, Qatadah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Abu Malik, Zayd ibn Aslam, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Zuhri, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, al-Suddi, al-Thawri, and al-Dahhak said: "until the decreed term reaches its end" (﴿حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ الْكِتَابُ أَجَلَهُ﴾) means until the 'iddah is over.

The scholars have agreed that a marriage contract concluded during the 'iddah is not valid. They differed regarding a man who marries a woman during her 'iddah and then consummates the marriage: he is to be separated from her, but is she forbidden to him permanently? There are two opinions. The majority hold that she is not forbidden to him; rather he may propose to her once her 'iddah has ended. Imam Malik held that she is forbidden to him permanently. He argued with what he related from Ibn Shihab and Sulayman ibn Yasar: that 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: "Whatever woman is married during her 'iddah, if her husband has not consummated with her, he is separated from her, and she completes the remainder of her 'iddah from her first husband, then the second is one of the suitors; and if he had consummated with her, they are separated, and she completes the remainder of her 'iddah from the first, then observes 'iddah from the second, and he shall never marry her." [[Al-Muwatta' (2/535).]]

They said: The basis of this is that the husband, since he hastened what God had deferred, is punished with the opposite of his aim, so she becomes forbidden to him permanently, like the killer who is deprived of inheritance. Al-Shafi'i related this report from Malik. Al-Bayhaqi said: He held this view in his earlier (qadim) opinion and retracted it in his later (jadid) opinion, due to the saying of 'Ali: "She is lawful to him."

I say: Moreover, it is disconnected (munqati') from 'Umar. Al-Thawri related from Ash'ath, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, that 'Umar retracted this and gave her her dower, and had them reunite.

* *

His saying: "And know that God knows what is in your selves, so beware of Him" (﴿وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ فَاحْذَرُوهُ﴾): He warns them about what occurs in their hearts concerning matters of women, and guides them to harbor good rather than evil. Then He did not despair them of His mercy, nor did He make them lose hope of His bounty, so He said: "And know that God is Forgiving, Forbearing" (﴿وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌ﴾).

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 236:

Allah, blessed and exalted is He, permitted the divorce of a woman after the marriage contract and before consummation with her. Ibn 'Abbas, Tawus, Ibrahim and al-Hasan al-Basri said: "al-massu" means marriage (nikah). Moreover, it is permissible for him to divorce her before consummating the marriage, and to assign her a dowry if she was one for whom no dowry had been fixed (mufawwadah), even though this may break her heart. For this reason Allah commanded that she be given a provision (imta'), which is compensation for what she has lost, in the form of something she is given by her husband according to his means: "upon the wealthy according to his means, and upon the poor according to his means."

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Isma'il ibn Umayyah, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "The best of the provision of divorce is a servant; below that is silver; below that is clothing."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "If he is wealthy, he gives her a provision of a servant or the like; and if he is poor, he gives her a provision of three garments."

al-Sha'bi said: "The middle level of that is: a shirt, a headscarf, a wrapper and an outer garment." He said: "Shurayh used to give a provision of five hundred." 'Abd al-Razzaq said: "Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin who said: 'He would give a provision of a servant, or of maintenance, or of clothing.' He said: 'al-Hasan ibn 'Ali gave a provision of ten thousand.'" (al-Tabari narrated it in his Tafsir (5/123) through the chain of 'Abd al-Razzaq.) It is also narrated that the woman said:

"A small provision from a beloved who parts from you..."

Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, held that whenever the spouses dispute the amount of the provision, she is owed half of her equivalent dowry (mahr mithlihā) from him. al-Shafi'i, in his later view (al-Jadid), said: the husband is not compelled to a specific amount, except the least that falls under the name of provision (mut'ah); and the amount I most prefer is that its least be that with which prayer is valid. In his earlier view (al-Qadim) he said: "I know of no fixed amount for the provision, except that I consider thirty dirhams commendable, based on what is narrated from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with both of them."

The scholars also differed: is the provision obligatory for every divorced woman, or is it obligatory only for the woman who was not consummated and for whom no dowry was fixed? There are several opinions:

The first: the provision is obligatory for every divorced woman, based on the generality of Allah's saying: ﴿And for divorced women is a provision according to what is reasonable, as a duty upon the righteous﴾ [al-Baqarah: 241], and on Allah's saying: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you in a graceful release﴾ [al-Ahzab: 28]. They had been assigned dowries and had been consummated with. This is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu al-'Aliyah and al-Hasan al-Basri. It is one of the two views of al-Shafi'i, and some of them considered it his correct later view (al-Jadid al-Sahih), and Allah knows best.

The second opinion: it is obligatory for a divorced woman if she is divorced before touching (consummation), even if a dowry had been fixed for her, based on Allah's saying: ﴿O you who believe, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, you have no waiting period for them to count; so provide for them and release them in a graceful release﴾ [al-Ahzab: 49]. Shu'bah and others narrated from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: "This verse in al-Ahzab abrogated the verse in al-Baqarah."

It is narrated in the Sahih of al-Bukhari, from Sahl ibn Sa'd and Abu Usayd, that they both said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Umaymah bint Sharahil. When she was brought in to him, he extended his hand toward her, and it seemed she disliked that, so he commanded Abu Usayd to equip her and give her two garments of raziqi cloth." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5226.]

The third opinion: the provision is obligatory only for a divorced woman who has not been consummated with and for whom no dowry was fixed. If he has consummated with her, then she is owed the equivalent dowry if she was mufawwadah; and if a dowry was fixed for her and he divorced her before consummation, then half of it is owed to her from him; and if he consummates with her, the whole becomes due, and that serves as her compensation in place of the provision. The one who is actually in need of a provision is the one for whom no dowry was fixed and who was not consummated with, and it is this one whom this noble verse indicates is owed the provision. This is the view of Ibn 'Umar and Mujahid. Among the scholars is one who considered it recommended (mustahabb) for every divorced woman other than the mufawwadah who is divorced before consummation; and this is not unknown, and the verse of choice in al-Ahzab is interpreted in this light. For this reason Allah said: ﴿And for divorced women is a provision according to what is reasonable, as a duty upon the righteous﴾ [al-Baqarah: 241].

Among the scholars is one who says it is recommended absolutely. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Kathir ibn Shihab al-Qazwini narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Sabiq narrated to us, 'Amr - meaning Ibn Abi Qays - narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Sha'bi who said: They mentioned to him the provision, "Is one to be detained for it?" So he recited: ﴿upon the wealthy according to his means, and upon the poor according to his means﴾. al-Sha'bi said: "By Allah, I have not seen anyone detained for it. By Allah, if it were obligatory, the judges would have detained people for it."

This verse indicates, along with the first verse, that the provision of mut'ah (consolation gift) is restricted to the case it addresses, since in this verse he only obligates half of the stipulated dower. And if the husband divorces before consummation, had there been another obligation of mut'ah, it would have been stated, especially since it has been joined to what precedes it, the restriction of mut'ah to that situation. And Allah knows best.

The halving of the dower in this situation is agreed upon among the scholars, with no disagreement among them on this. Whenever a dower has been specified for her and he then separates from her before consummating with her, half of what was specified as dower becomes due to her. However, according to the three (Imams), the entire dower becomes due if the husband has been alone with her (khalwah), even if he has not consummated with her. This is the view of al-Shafi'i in his old opinion (qawl qadim), and the rightly guided caliphs ruled accordingly. But al-Shafi'i said: Muslim ibn Khalid informed us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas that he said, concerning a man who marries a woman, is alone with her, does not touch her, and then divorces her: she is entitled to only half the dower, because Allah says: ﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them, and you have already specified for them a dower, then half of what you have specified﴾. Al-Shafi'i said: This is stronger, and it is the apparent meaning of the Book.

Al-Bayhaqi said: Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, although he is not relied upon as a proof, has been narrated to us through the chain of Ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn 'Abbas, and so it is his saying.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿unless they forgo﴾, that is, the women forgo what was due to them from their husbands of the half, so nothing is due to them from him.

As-Suddi narrated from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿unless they forgo﴾, he said: Unless the previously married woman (thayyib) forgoes and leaves her right.

Abu Muhammad ibn Abi Hatim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: It has been related from Shurayh, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, ash-Sha'bi, al-Hasan, Nafi', Qatadah, Jabir ibn Zayd, 'Ata al-Khurasani, ad-Dahhak, az-Zuhri, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Ibn Sirin, ar-Rabi' ibn Anas, and as-Suddi, something similar to that. He said: Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi disagreed with them and said: ﴿unless they forgo﴾ means the men, and this is an anomalous view that was not followed. End of his words.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿or he in whose hand is the marriage tie forgoes﴾, Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned from Ibn Lahi'ah: Amr ibn Shu'ayb related to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet (ﷺ) [who said]: "The guardian of the marriage tie is the husband."

Similarly, Ibn Mardawayh traced it through 'Abdullah ibn Lahi'ah, with the same chain. [ad-Daraqutni narrated it in as-Sunan (3/279) through Qutaybah from Ibn Lahi'ah with the same, and al-Bayhaqi mentioned it in as-Sunan al-Kubra (7/251) and said: "This is not preserved, and Ibn Lahi'ah is not relied upon as a proof, and Allah knows best."] Ibn Jarir traced it from Ibn Lahi'ah, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, and mentioned it, but he did not say "from his father, from his grandfather." And Allah knows best.

Then Ibn Abi Hatim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Yunus ibn Habib related to us, Abu Dawud related to us, Jarir, that is Ibn Hazim, related to us, from 'Isa, that is Ibn 'Asim, who said: I heard Shurayh say: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib asked me about the one in whose hand is the marriage tie. I said to him: It is the woman's guardian. 'Ali said: No, rather it is the husband.

Then he said: In one of the narrations from Ibn 'Abbas, Jubayr ibn Mut'im, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Shurayh in one of his two opinions, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, ash-Sha'bi, 'Ikrimah, Nafi', Muhammad ibn Sirin, ad-Dahhak, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, Jabir ibn Zayd, Abu Mijlaz, ar-Rabi' ibn Anas, Iyas ibn Mu'awiyah, Makhul, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan: that it is the husband.

I say: This is the new opinion (al-jadid) of al-Shafi'i's two opinions, and the view of Abu Hanifah and his companions, ath-Thawri, Ibn Shubrumah, al-Awza'i, and Ibn Jarir chose it. The basis of this view is that the one in whose hand is the marriage tie in reality is the husband, for in his hand is its contracting and its binding, its dissolution and its ending. And just as it is not permissible for the guardian to give any of the property of the woman under his care to another, so too with the dower.

He said: The second view: My father related to us, Ibn Abi Maryam related to us, Muhammad ibn Muslim related to us, 'Amr ibn Dinar related to us, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning the one whom Allah mentioned, in whose hand is the marriage tie, he said: That is her father or her brother, or whoever her marriage cannot be contracted without his permission. It is related from 'Alqamah, al-Hasan, 'Ata, Tawus, az-Zuhri, Rabi'ah, Zayd ibn Aslam, Ibrahim an-Nakha'i, 'Ikrimah in one of his two opinions, and Muhammad ibn Sirin in one of his two opinions: that it is the guardian. This is the view of Malik, and the old view (qawl qadim) of al-Shafi'i; its basis is that the guardian is the one who acquired her for him, so he has the right to dispose of it, unlike the rest of her property.

Ibn Jarir said: Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' ar-Razi related to us, Sufyan related to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Ikrimah who said: Allah permitted forgiveness and commanded it, so whatever woman forgives, her forgiveness is valid; but if she is stingy and withholds, her guardian may forgive and his forgiveness is valid.

This implies the validity of the guardian's forgiveness even if she is mature and of sound judgment, and this is related from Shurayh. However, ash-Sha'bi disputed this with him, so he retracted that and adopted the view that it is the husband, and he used to call down a curse (mubahalah) upon it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And that you forgo is nearer to righteousness﴾, Ibn Jarir said: Some of them said: It is addressed to both men and women. Yunus related to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, I heard Ibn Jurayj narrate from 'Ata ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And that you forgo is nearer to righteousness﴾, he said: The nearer of the two to righteousness is the one who forgoes.

Similarly it is related from ash-Sha'bi and others. Mujahid, ad-Dahhak, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, ar-Rabi' ibn Anas, and ath-Thawri said: "The favour (al-fadl) here" is that the woman forgoes her half, or that the man completes the dower for her. For this reason He said: ﴿And do not forget favour among yourselves﴾, that is, kindness, as Sa'id said. Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, as-Suddi, and Abu Wa'il said: the good (al-ma'ruf), meaning: do not neglect it, but practise it among yourselves.

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim related to us, Musa ibn Ishaq related to us, 'Uqbah ibn Mukram related to us, Yunus ibn Bukayr related to us, 'Ubaydullah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi related to us, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Ubayd, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There will come upon people a time of biting, when the believer bites on what is in his hands and forgets the favour. Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And do not forget favour among yourselves﴾. Evil people will deal with everyone in need, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade selling to the one in necessity and the sale of gharar. So if you have good, return it to your brother, and do not add to his ruin upon his ruin, for the Muslim is the brother of the Muslim: he does not disgrace him nor deprive him." [This has come through another route, narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (1/116) and Abu Dawud in as-Sunan, no. 3382, through Abu 'Amir al-Muzani from a shaykh of Banu Tamim from 'Ali, as a mawquf report, with similar wording.]

Sufyan said, from Abu Harun, who said: I saw 'Awn ibn 'Abdullah in the gathering of al-Qurazi, and 'Awn would narrate to us while his beard was wet from weeping, and he would say: I kept company with the wealthy and I was among the most anxious of them, when I saw them with finer clothes, sweeter scent, and finer mounts than mine. And I sat with the poor and found rest with them. And he said: ﴿And do not forget favour among yourselves﴾: when the beggar comes to him and he has nothing, let him at least supplicate for him. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾, that is: nothing of your affairs and conditions is hidden from Him, and He will recompense every doer for his deed.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verses 238–239 (part 1 of 4):

Allah, exalted is He, commands the observance of the prayers at their proper times, the preservation of their limits, and their performance at their appointed times. This is as established in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Which deed is best?" He said: "Prayer at its proper time." I said: "Then which?" He said: "Jihad in the way of Allah." I said: "Then which?" He said: "Kindness to one's parents." He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) related these to me, and had I asked him for more, he would have increased them for me." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (527, 5970) and Sahih Muslim, no. (85).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Yunus narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar ibn Hafs ibn 'Asim, from al-Qasim ibn Ghannam, from his grandmother Umm Abihi al-Dunya, from his grandmother Umm Farwa, who was among those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that she heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mention the deeds, and he said: "Indeed, the most beloved of deeds to Allah is hastening the prayer to its first time."

Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated it similarly. Al-Tirmidhi said: "We do not know it except through the route of al-'Umari, and he is not strong according to the scholars of hadith." [[al-Musnad (6/274), Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (426), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (170).]]

Allah, exalted is He, singled out from among them the middle prayer (al-Salat al-Wusta) for additional emphasis. The early and later scholars (al-Salaf wa al-Khalaf) differed concerning which prayer it is. It was said that it is the Dawn prayer (Subh). Malik related this in al-Muwatta as a mursal report (balaghan) from 'Ali and Ibn 'Abbas [Malik said: "and that is my opinion"]. [[Addition from copy ج.]]

Hushaym, Ibn 'Ulayyah, Ghundar, Ibn Abi 'Adiyy, 'Abd al-Wahhab, Shurayk and others narrated from 'Awf al-A'rabi, from Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi, who said: "I prayed the Dawn prayer behind Ibn 'Abbas, and he performed the qunut (supplication) in it and raised his hands, then said: 'This is the middle prayer which we were commanded to stand in devoutly (qanitin).'" Ibn Jarir narrated it. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (5/215, 216).]] He also narrated it from the hadith of 'Awf, from Khilas ibn 'Amr, from Ibn 'Abbas, the same in substance. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (5/218).]]

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, 'Awf narrated to us, from Abu al-Minhal, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he prayed the morning prayer (al-Ghadat) in the mosque of Basra, and performed the qunut before the bowing (ruku'), and said: "This is the middle prayer which Allah mentioned in His Book when He said: ﴿Observe the prayers, and the middle prayer, and stand before Allah in devotion﴾."

He also said: Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Damghani narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, al-Rabi' ibn Anas informed us, from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: "I prayed the morning prayer behind 'Abd Allah ibn Qays in Basra, and when I had finished, I asked a man from the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) beside me: 'What is the middle prayer?' He said: 'This prayer.'"

It was also narrated by another route from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, that he prayed the morning prayer with the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and when they had finished, he said: "I asked them: 'Which of the prayers is the middle prayer?' They said: 'The one you have just prayed.'"

He also said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Ibn 'Atamah narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Qatadah, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: "The middle prayer is the Dawn prayer."

Ibn Abi Hatim related it from Ibn 'Umar, Abu Umamah, Anas, Abu al-'Aliyah, 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, 'Ata', Mujahid, Jabir ibn Zayd, 'Ikrimah, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas. Ibn Jarir also narrated it from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Hadi, and this is what al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, explicitly stated, arguing from the verse ﴿and stand before Allah in devotion﴾, and for him the qunut is in the Dawn prayer. [Al-Damyati related it from 'Umar, Mu'adh, Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Umar, and 'A'ishah, with differing reports from them, and from Abu Musa, Jabir, Anas, Abu al-Sha'tha', Tawus, 'Ata', 'Ikrimah, and Mujahid.] [[Addition from copies ج and أ.]]

Some said it is the middle prayer on the basis that it is not shortened, and it lies between two four-unit prayers which are shortened (the Dhuhr and the 'Asr when travelling) and it is preceded by the Maghrib prayer [which is not shortened]. It was also said: it is so called because it lies between two loud night prayers (Maghrib and 'Isha') and two silent day prayers (Dhuhr and 'Asr). [[In copies أ and و: "between two nocturnal loud prayers, and two diurnal silent prayers."]]

It was said that it is the Dhuhr prayer. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said in his Musnad: Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to us, from al-Zubayriq, meaning Ibn 'Amr, from Zuhrah, meaning Ibn Ma'bad, who said: "We were sitting with Zayd ibn Thabit, and they sent for Usamah, and asked him about the middle prayer, and he said: 'It is the Dhuhr; the Prophet (ﷺ) used to pray it at the time of the midday heat (al-Hajir).'" [[Musnad al-Tayalisi, no. (628).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Abi Hakim narrated to me, I heard al-Zubayriq narrating from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pray the Dhuhr at the time of the noon heat (al-Hajirah), and he did not pray any prayer more difficult for the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) than it. So the verse was revealed: ﴿Observe the prayers, and the middle prayer﴾, and he said: 'Before it are two prayers and after it are two prayers.'" Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan from the hadith of Shu'bah, with the same chain. [[al-Musnad (5/183) and Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (411).]]

Ahmad also said: Yazid narrated to us, Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to us, from al-Zubayriq, that a group of Quraysh were gathered when Zayd ibn Thabit passed by them. They sent two of their boys to him to ask him about the middle prayer. He said: "It is the 'Asr." Then two men from among them approached him and asked him, and he said: "It is the Dhuhr." Then they returned to Usamah ibn Zayd and asked him, and he said: "It is the Dhuhr; the Prophet (ﷺ) used to pray the Dhuhr at the time of the midday heat, and behind him there would be only one or two rows, while people were at their midday rest and in their trade. So Allah revealed: ﴿Observe the prayers, and the middle prayer, and stand before Allah in devotion﴾." He said: "Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Let men desist, or I will burn their houses.'" [[al-Musnad (5/206).]]

Al-Zubayriq is Ibn 'Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri, who did not meet any of the Companions. The correct report is what preceded from his narration from Zuhrah ibn Ma'bad and 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr.

Shu'bah and Hammam narrated from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Ibn 'Umar, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "The middle prayer is the Dhuhr prayer."

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi and others narrated from Shu'bah: "'Umar ibn Sulayman, from the descendants of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, informed me: I heard 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Aban ibn 'Uthman narrating from his father, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: 'The middle prayer is the Dhuhr.'"

Ibn Jarir narrated it from Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah, from 'Abd al-Samad, from Shu'bah, from 'Umar ibn Sulayman, with the same chain, from Zayd ibn Thabit, in a hadith he traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ): "The middle prayer is the Dhuhr prayer."

Among those from whom it is reported that it is the Dhuhr: Ibn 'Umar, Abu Sa'id, and 'A'ishah, with differing reports from them. This is also the view of 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Hadi, and a report from Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on them all.

It was said that it is the 'Asr prayer. Al-Tirmidhi and al-Baghawi, may Allah have mercy on them both, said: "This is the view of most of the scholars among the Companions and others." Al-Qadi al-Mawardi said: "It is the view of the majority of the Successors (Tabi'un)." The Hafiz Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: "It is the view of most people of transmitted reports (ahl al-athar)." Abu Muhammad ibn 'Atiyyah said in his tafsir: "It is the view of the majority of people." The Hafiz Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Mu'min ibn Khalaf al-Damyati said in his book titled Kashf al-Mughatta fi Tabyin al-Salat al-Wusta: "In it he supported that it is the 'Asr, and he related it from 'Umar, 'Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Ayyub, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, Samurah ibn Jundub, Abu Hurayrah, Abu Sa'id, Hafsah, Umm Habibah, and Umm Salamah. And from Ibn 'Umar, Ibn 'Abbas, and 'A'ishah, according to the sound report from them. This is also the view of 'Abidah, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Zirr ibn Hubaysh, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ibn Sirin, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Kalbi, Muqatil, 'Ubayd ibn Abi Maryam, and others, and it is the school of Ahmad ibn Hanbal." Al-Qadi al-Mawardi said: "And al-Shafi'i." Ibn al-Mundhir said: "It is the sound view from Abu Hanifah, Abu Yusuf, and Muhammad, and Ibn Habib al-Maliki chose it, may Allah have mercy on them all."

The evidence for this:

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Muslim, from Shutayr ibn Shakal, from 'Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said on the day of the Confederates (al-Ahzab): "They preoccupied us from the middle prayer, the 'Asr prayer; may Allah fill their hearts and their houses with fire." Then he prayed it between the two evening prayers, the Maghrib and the 'Isha'. [[al-Musnad (1/81).]]

Similarly, Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Abu Mu'awiyah Muhammad ibn Hazim al-Darir, and al-Nasa'i from the route of 'Isa ibn Yunus; both from al-A'mash, from Muslim ibn Subayh, from Abu al-Duha, from Shutayr ibn Shakal ibn Humayd, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the same. [[Sahih Muslim, no. (627) and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11045).]]

Muslim also narrated it from the route of Shu'bah, from al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah, from Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, from 'Ali, with the same. [[Sahih Muslim, no. (627).]]

It was also narrated by al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim), Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, and many compilers of musnads, sunans and sahihs, through many routes whose mention would be lengthy, from 'Abidah al-Salmani, from 'Ali, with the same. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (2931, 4111), Sahih Muslim, no. (627), Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (409), Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2984), and Sunan al-Nasa'i (1/236).]]

al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the route of al-Hasan al-Basri, from 'Ali, with the same. [[I have not come across this route, and al-Mizzi did not mention it in Tuhfat al-Ashraf.]] Al-Tirmidhi said: "His hearing from him is not known."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Asim, from Zirr, who said: I said to 'Abidah: "Ask 'Ali about the middle prayer." So he asked him, and he said: "We used to consider it the Dawn prayer, until I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say on the day of the Confederates: 'They preoccupied us from the middle prayer, the 'Asr prayer; may Allah fill their graves and their bellies (or their houses) with fire.'" Ibn Jarir narrated it from Bundar, from Ibn Mahdi, with the same. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (5/184).]]

The hadith of the day of the Confederates, and the polytheists' preoccupying the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions from performing the 'Asr prayer that day, is narrated from a group of Companions whose mention would be lengthy. What is intended is the narration of those who explicitly stated in their reports that the middle prayer is the 'Asr prayer. Muslim also narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud and al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, may Allah be pleased with them both. [[Sahih Muslim, no. (628) from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, and no. (630) from the hadith of al-Bara', may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: 'Affan narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Samurah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The middle prayer is the 'Asr prayer." [[al-Musnad (5/22).]]

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 238–239 (part 2 of 4):

Bahz and Affan narrated to us, both saying: Aban narrated to us, Qatada narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Samura, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ﴿Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer﴾, and he named it for us: that it is the Asr prayer [[Al-Musnad (5/8).]].

Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Rawh narrated to us, both saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, from Samura ibn Jundub, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is the Asr." Ibn Ja'far said: He was asked about the middle prayer [[Al-Musnad (5/7, 12, 13).]].

And al-Tirmidhi narrated it through the hadith of Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, from Samura [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, nos. (182, 2983).]]. He said: "Hasan sahih (good and authentic); and al-Hasan is known to have heard from him."

[Another hadith] [[Addition from the manuscripts J and A.]]: Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Mani' narrated to us, Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata' narrated to us, from al-Taymi, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The middle prayer is the Asr prayer" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (5/189).]].

Another chain, or rather another hadith: Ibn Jarir said: al-Muthanna narrated to me, Sulayman ibn Ahmad al-Jurashi al-Wasiti narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us. He said: Sadaqa ibn Khalid informed me, Khalid ibn Dihqan narrated to me, from Khalid ibn Sabalan, from Kuhayl ibn Harmala, who said: Abu Hurayra was asked about the middle prayer, and he said: "We disagreed about it just as you have disagreed about it, while we were in the courtyard of the house of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and among us was the righteous man, Abu Hashim ibn Utba ibn Rabi'a ibn Abd Shams. He said: 'I will find out for you about that.' So he got up, sought permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and entered upon him. Then he came out to us and said: 'He informed us that it is the Asr prayer'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (5/191).]]. This chain is very strange (gharib) indeed.

Another hadith: Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, Abd al-Salam narrated to us, from Salim, mawla (freed slave) of Abu Basir [[In A: "Abi Nusayr".]], Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Dimashqi narrated to me, who said: I was sitting with Abd al-Aziz ibn Marwan, and he said: "O so-and-so, go to so-and-so and say to him: What did you hear from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the middle prayer?" A man who was sitting there said: "Abu Bakr and Umar sent me, while I was a small boy, to ask him about the middle prayer. He took my little finger and said: 'This is Fajr.' Then he gripped the one next to it and said: 'This is Zuhr.' Then he gripped the thumb and said: 'This is Maghrib.' Then he gripped the one next to it and said: 'This is Isha.' Then he said: 'Which of your fingers remains?' I said: 'The middle one.' He said: 'Which prayer remains?' I said: 'Asr.' He said: 'It is Asr'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (5/196).]]. This too is gharib.

Another hadith: Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Awf al-Ta'i narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Damdam ibn Zur'a narrated to me, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The middle prayer is the Asr prayer" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (5/198). The Hafiz's statement: "Its chain is not objectionable" is open to challenge, for its chain contains weakness and a break in continuity; this version is well-known and was transmitted by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir.]]. Its chain is not objectionable [[In A: "Ibn Abbas".]].

Another hadith: Abu Hatim ibn Hibban said in his Sahih: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zuhayr narrated to us, al-Jarrah ibn Makhlad narrated to us, Amr ibn Asim narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us, from Qatada, from Muwarriq [[In H: "Hammam ibn Muwarriq", the correction being from al-Ihsan.]] al-Ijli, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The middle prayer is the Asr prayer" [[Sahih Ibn Hibban (3/121), al-Ihsan edition.]].

Al-Tirmidhi also narrated, through the hadith of Muhammad ibn Talha ibn Musarrif, from Zubayd al-Yami, from Murra al-Hamdani, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The middle prayer is the Asr prayer" [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (181).]]. Then he said: "Hasan sahih."

Muslim also narrated it in his Sahih through the chain of Muhammad ibn Talha, with the same content, and its wording is: "They preoccupied us from the middle prayer, the Asr prayer," the hadith in full.

These are texts on the matter which admit of no other interpretation. This is confirmed by the command to guard it, and by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) in the sound hadith, from the narration of al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever misses the Asr prayer, it is as if he has lost his family and his wealth" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (626).]]. And in the Sahih also, through the hadith of al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Qilaba, from Abu al-Muhajir [[In J: "from Abu al-Muhajir, from Abu al-Malih".]], from Buraydah ibn al-Husayb, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Hasten to the prayer on a cloudy day, for whoever abandons the Asr prayer, his deed has been nullified" [[What is in the Sahih is only from Hisham, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Qilaba, from Abu al-Malih, from Buraydah, may Allah be pleased with him, and it is in Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (553). This second version is in Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (694). The first is the preserved one. Its inclusion in manuscript J was correct, as I have explained, but there was confusion in this, for he wrote the phrase "and in the Sahih" and then corrected it.]] [[Found in J: "Thus Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of al-Awza'i, and al-Bukhari and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Hisham al-Dastuwa'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Qilaba, from Abu al-Malih ibn Usama, from Buraydah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): 'Whoever abandons the Asr prayer, his deed has been nullified.'"]].

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'a informed us, from Abd Allah ibn Hubayra, from Abu Tamim, from Abu Basra [[In J: "from Abu Nadra".]] al-Ghifari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) led us in prayer in a valley of their valleys called al-Makhammas, the Asr prayer. He said: "Indeed, this prayer, the Asr prayer, was presented to those before you, and they neglected it. Beware! Whoever prays it will have his reward doubled. Beware! There is no prayer after it until you see the witness (the sun's setting)" [[In A: "until it sets".]].

Then he said: It was narrated by Yahya ibn Ishaq, from al-Layth, from Khayr [[In J: "from Hasan".]] ibn Nu'aym, from Abd Allah ibn Hubayra, with the same content [[Al-Musnad (6/397).]].

Thus Muslim and al-Nasa'i both narrated it, through Qutayba, from al-Layth [[Sahih Muslim, no. (830), and Sunan al-Nasa'i (1/259).]]. Muslim also narrated it through the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid ibn Abi Habib narrated to me, both of them from Khayr ibn Nu'aym al-Hadrami, from Abd Allah ibn Hubayra al-Sabai [[In A: "al-Shaybani".]] [[Sahih Muslim, no. (830).]].

As for the hadith which Imam Ahmad also narrated: Ishaq narrated to us, Malik informed me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from al-Qa'qa' ibn Hakim, from Abu Yunus, mawla of Aisha, who said: Aisha ordered me to write a mushaf (copy of the Qur'an) for her, and she said: "When you reach this verse, ﴿Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer﴾, inform me." When I reached it, I informed her, and she dictated to me: "Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer, and the Asr prayer, and stand before Allah in devotion (qanitin)." She said: "I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." Thus Muslim also narrated it, from Yahya ibn Yahya, from Malik, with the same content [[Al-Musnad (6/73) and Sahih Muslim, no. (629).]].

Ibn Jarir said: al-Muthanna narrated to me, al-Hajjaj narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Urwa, from his father, who said: In the mushaf of Aisha was: "Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer, and it is the Asr prayer" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (5/175).]]. He also narrated it through the chain of al-Hasan al-Basri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited it in this way.
