Imam Malik also narrated, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Amr ibn Rafi', who said: I used to write a mushaf for Hafsa, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), and she said: "When you reach this verse, inform me: ﴿Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer﴾." When I reached it, I informed her, and she dictated to me: "Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer, and the Asr prayer, and stand before Allah in devotion" [[Al-Muwatta' (1/139).]].

Thus Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated it, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to me, and Nafi', mawla of Ibn Umar [[In J: "ibn Bashshar".]]: that Umar ibn Nafi' said ... and he mentioned the like of it, and added: "As I memorised it from the Prophet (ﷺ)."

Another chain from Hafsa: Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'ba narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Azdi, from Salim ibn Abd Allah, that Hafsa ordered a person to write a mushaf for her, and she said: "When you reach this verse, ﴿Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer﴾, inform me." When he reached it, he informed her, and she said: "Write: 'Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer, and the Asr prayer'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (5/208, 209).]].

Another chain: Ibn Jarir said: Ibn al-Muthanna Abd al-Wahhab narrated to me, Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Nafi', that Hafsa ordered a freed slave of hers to write a mushaf for her, and she said: "When you reach this verse, ' Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer ', do not write it until I dictate it to you as I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite it." When he reached it, she ordered him, and he wrote it: "Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer, and the Asr prayer, and stand before Allah in devotion." Nafi' said: "I read that mushaf and I saw in it the letter 'waw' (and)" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (5/209).]].

Likewise Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas and Ubayd ibn Umayr that they both recited it in this way.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abda narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, Abu Salama narrated to me, from Amr ibn Rafi', mawla of Umar, who said: In the mushaf of Hafsa was: "Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer, and the Asr prayer, and stand before Allah in devotion" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (5/211).]].

The statement of the objection is this: the verse links "the Asr prayer" to "the middle prayer" with the conjunction "and" (waw), which requires difference, and so this indicates that the Asr prayer is other than the middle prayer. This has been answered in several ways. First: if this is narrated as a report, then the hadith of Ali is sounder and more explicit than it. Moreover, the "and" may be superfluous, as in His words: ﴿And thus We detail the verses, that the way of the criminals may become clear﴾ [al-An'am: 55], and ﴿And thus We showed Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth, that he might be among the certain﴾ [al-An'am: 75]. Or the "and" may be for coordinating attributes, not essences, as in His words: ﴿But (he is) the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets﴾ [al-Ahzab: 40], and His words: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, who created and proportioned, and who determined and guided, and who brought forth the pasture﴾ [al-A'la: 1–4], and there are many similar examples. The poet said:

*To the lordly king and the son of the valiant,*
*and the lion of the battle in the crush...*

And Abu Du'ad al-Iyadi said:

*He let death and the fates (al-manun) loose upon them,*
*so for them in the echo of the graves is a skull.*

And death is al-manun. The poet Adi ibn Zayd al-Ibadi said:

*I presented the hide to his wrists,*
*so he found her words false and a lie (mayna).*

And mayna means falsehood. Sibawayh, the master of the grammarians, has explicitly affirmed the permissibility of the saying of one who says: "I passed by your brother and your companion," where the companion is the brother himself. And Allah knows best.

As for it being narrated as Qur'an, it is not transmitted by mass transmission (tawatur, a report so widely transmitted that its reliability is certain), so no Qur'an can be established by a single-narrator report (khabar al-wahid). For this reason, the Commander of the Faithful, 'Uthman ibn 'Affan (may Allah be pleased with him), did not include it in the Imam Mushaf (the standard codex), and none of the reciters whose recitation establishes proof read it in this way, neither among the Seven nor among others.

Then, a report has indicated the abrogation (naskh, the cancellation of a ruling or recitation by a later revelation) of this recitation mentioned in this hadith. Muslim said: Ishaq ibn Rahawayh narrated to us, Yahya ibn Adam informed us, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from Shaqiq ibn 'Uqbah, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: "The following was revealed: 'Guard the prayers and the middle prayer, the 'Asr prayer,' [[In J and A: "And the middle prayer is the 'Asr prayer."]] and we recited it before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for as long as Allah willed. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, abrogated it and revealed: ﴿Guard the prayers and the middle prayer﴾." Zahir, a man who was with Shaqiq, said to him: "Is it the 'Asr?" He said: "I have told you how it was revealed and how Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, abrogated it."

Muslim said: al-Ash'ari also narrated it from al-Thawri, from al-Aswad, from Shaqiq.

I say: Muslim did not narrate from this Shaqiq anything except this single hadith, and Allah knows best. Accordingly, this recitation, which is the recitation of the mainstream (al-jaddah), abrogates the wording of the narration of 'Aishah and Hafsah, and its meaning as well, if the conjunction "and" indicates difference; otherwise it abrogates only its wording. And Allah knows best.

It has been said that the middle prayer is the Maghrib prayer. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this from Ibn 'Abbas, but its chain (isnad) is problematic, for he narrated it from his father, from Abu al-Jumahir [[In A: "from Abu al-Jamahir."]], from Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Khalil, from his paternal uncle, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The middle prayer is the Maghrib." Ibn Jarir transmitted this view from Qabisah ibn Dhu'ayb, and it is also reported from Qatadah with variation in his account. Some have justified this view on the grounds that it is the middle in number between the four-unit and two-unit prayers, that it is the odd (witr) of the obligatory prayers, and by the virtue reported concerning it. And Allah knows best.

It has been said that it is the 'Isha' prayer (the night prayer), which was chosen by 'Ali ibn Ahmad al-Wahidi in his well-known tafsir. It has also been said that it is one of the five, unspecified, and it was left undetermined among them, just as the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr) is undetermined within the year, the month, or the last ten [nights]. This view is attributed to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Shurayh al-Qadi, Nafi' the client of Ibn 'Umar, and al-Rabi' ibn Khaytham, and it is also reported from Zayd ibn Thabit. Imam al-Haramayn al-Juwayni chose it in his book al-Nihayah.

It has also been said: rather, the middle prayer is the totality of the five prayers. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this from Ibn 'Umar, but its authenticity is also questionable. It is strange that this view was chosen by Shaykh Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr al-Namari, the imam of the lands beyond the sea, and indeed it is one of the greatest [errors], for he chose it, despite his knowledge and memorization, though no proof from the Book, the Sunnah, or a transmitted report supports it. It has been said: it is the 'Isha' and the Fajr prayers. It has been said: rather, it is the congregational prayer. It has been said: the Friday prayer. It has been said: the prayer of fear (salat al-khawf). It has been said: rather, the 'Id al-Fitr prayer. It has been said: rather, the 'Id al-Adha prayer. It has been said: the witr prayer. It has been said: the Duha prayer. Others suspended judgment on it when the evidences conflicted with them, and the basis for preferring one view did not become clear to them. No consensus (ijma', scholarly agreement) was reached on a single view; rather, the dispute over it has continued to exist from the time of the Companions until now.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar and Ibn Muthanna narrated to me, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, who said: I heard Qatadah narrating from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: "The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) differed concerning the middle prayer in this way," and he interlaced his fingers.

[Fakhr al-Din al-Razi, in his tafsir, related a view from a group of scholars, among them Zayd ibn Thabit and Rabi' ibn Khaytham: that its explanation was not intended, rather its indefiniteness was intended, just as the Night of Decree is undetermined in Ramadan, the hour of answered supplication on Friday, the Greatest Name among the names of Allah, and the time of death for the responsible person, so that he may be ready at every time. Likewise, the night in which a plague descends from the sky was left undetermined so that people might beware of it and always be prepared; likewise, the time of the Hour is something Allah has kept for Himself, so it will come only suddenly.]

All these views are weak in comparison to the one before them, and the axis and the arena of dispute is really between the Fajr and the 'Asr. The Sunnah has established that it is the 'Asr, so it is necessary to adopt this view.

Imam Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim al-Razi narrated in his book "Fada'il al-Shafi'i" (may Allah have mercy on him): My father narrated to us, I heard Harmalah ibn Yahya al-Tujibi say: al-Shafi'i said: "Whatever I have said, if there is a report from the Prophet (ﷺ) that is authentic and contrary to my statement, then the hadith of the Prophet (ﷺ) takes priority, and do not follow me blindly." Similarly, al-Rabi', al-Za'farani, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated from al-Shafi'i. Musa Abu al-Walid, son of Abu al-Jarud, said on the authority of al-Shafi'i: "When a hadith is authentic and I have stated a view, I retract my view and act upon that [hadith]." This is from his nobility and trustworthiness, and this is the same as that of his fellow imams, may Allah have mercy on them, be pleased with them all, amen. From here, al-Qadi al-Mawardi firmly stated that the school of al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) holds that the middle prayer is the 'Asr prayer, although it is explicitly stated in the New (al-Jadid) and other works that it is the Fajr, because the hadiths that it is the 'Asr are authentic. A group of the school's hadith scholars has agreed with this approach, and all praise and grace belong to Allah. Among the jurists of the school are those who deny that the 'Asr is the school's position of al-Shafi'i, and they insist that it is the Fajr, with a single view. Al-Mawardi said: "Among them are those who report two opinions on the matter, and the presentation of objections and responses has another place other than this, which we have compiled separately, and all praise and grace belong to Allah."

* *

And His Exalted saying: ﴿And stand before Allah in devotion﴾, meaning: humble, submissive, and meek before Him. This command necessarily entails abstaining from speech during the prayer, as speech contradicts it. For this reason, when the Prophet (ﷺ) refrained from returning the greeting to Ibn Mas'ud when he greeted him while he was praying, he apologized to him for that and said: "Indeed, there is preoccupation in the prayer." In Sahih Muslim, he (peace be upon him) said to Mu'awiyah ibn al-Hakam al-[Sulami] [[Addition from J, A, and W.]] when he spoke during the prayer: "Indeed, this prayer does not allow any of the speech of people; it is only glorification, magnification, and the remembrance of Allah."

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Isma'il, Harith ibn Shubayl narrated to me, from Abu 'Amr al-Shaybani, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: "A man used to speak to his companion during the prayer in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) about a need, until this verse was revealed: ﴿And stand before Allah in devotion﴾, and we were commanded to be silent." This was narrated by the group [of compilers] except Ibn Majah, through several chains from Isma'il.

This hadith has troubled a group of scholars, since it was established for them that the prohibition of speech in the prayer occurred in Mecca, before the migration to Medina and after the migration to the land of Abyssinia, as indicated by the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud in the Sahih, who said: "We used to greet the Prophet (ﷺ) before we migrated to Abyssinia while he was praying, and he would return our greeting. When we returned, I greeted him, but he did not return my greeting, and I was struck by anxiety. When he finished the prayer, he said: 'I did not return your greeting except that I was in prayer, and indeed Allah brings about from His command what He wills, and among what He has newly commanded is that you not speak during the prayer.'"

Ibn Mas'ud was among those who embraced Islam early and migrated to Abyssinia, then returned from it to Mecca with those who returned, then migrated to Medina. This verse ﴿And stand before Allah in devotion﴾ was revealed in Medina without any disagreement. Some said that Zayd ibn Arqam, in his saying "A man used to speak to his brother about his need during the prayer," intended to inform about the general class of people, and he derived the prohibition of that from this verse according to what he understood from it, and Allah knows best.

Others said: he intended that this occurred in Medina after the migration to it, and that it would have been permitted twice and prohibited twice, as some of our companions and others chose. The first is more evident. And Allah also knows best.

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Bishr ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Yahya narrated to us, from al-Musayyab, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Some of us used to greet one another during the prayer. I passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and greeted him, but he did not return my greeting, and it occurred to my mind that something had been revealed concerning me. When the Prophet (ﷺ) finished his prayer, he said: 'And upon you be peace, O greeter, and the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, brings about from His command what He wills. So when you are in prayer, be devoutly obedient (qunut) and do not speak.'" [[Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/137) through a chain from 'Asim, from al-Musayyab, from Ibn Mas'ud, similarly.]]

* *

And His saying: ﴿So if you fear, then [pray] on foot or riding; and when you are safe, remember Allah as He has taught you that which you did not know﴾. When Allah, the Exalted, commanded His servants to guard the prayers, to uphold their limits, and emphasized the matter with its confirmation, He mentioned the state in which a person is preoccupied from performing them in the most complete manner, which is the state of fighting and the clash of battle. So He said: ﴿So if you fear, then [pray] on foot or riding﴾ [[In J: "And if" which is an error.]], meaning: then pray in whatever state you are, on foot or riding, that is: facing the qiblah or not facing it. As Malik narrated from Nafi', that Ibn 'Umar, whenever he was asked about the prayer of fear, described it, then said: "If the fear is greater than that, pray on foot or riding, facing the qiblah or not facing it." Nafi' said: "I do not think Ibn 'Umar mentioned that except from the Prophet (ﷺ)." Al-Bukhari narrated it, and this wording is his [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4535).]], and Muslim [narrated it]. Al-Bukhari also narrated it through another route, from Ibn Jurayj, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), similarly or close to it [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (943).]]. Muslim also has from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "If the fear is greater than that, then pray riding or standing, signaling with gestures" [[Sahih Muslim no. (839).]].

In the hadith of Abdullah ibn Unays al-Juhani, when the Prophet ﷺ sent him to Khalid ibn Sufyan al-Hudhali to kill him, and he was near 'Arafa (or 'Arafat), when he met him, the time of the 'Asr prayer came. He said: "I feared that it would pass me, so I began to pray while signaling with my head (*ima'*)." The full hadith was narrated by Ahmad and Abu Dawud with a sound chain.[[al-Musnad (3/496) and Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (1249).]] This is one of the concessions (*rukhas*) that Allah granted to His servants, and one of the burdens and shackles He lifted from them.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through Shabib ibn Bishr, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said regarding this verse: the rider prays on his mount and the one on foot prays on his feet. He said: similar views were reported from al-Hasan, Mujahid, Makhul, al-Suddi, al-Hakam, Malik, al-Awza'i, al-Thawri and al-Hasan ibn Salih, and they added: he signals with his head wherever he faces.[[In A: "signaling with the face."]]

Then he said: My father narrated to us, Abu Ghassan narrated to us, Dawud (i.e., Ibn 'Ulayya) narrated to us, from Mutarrif, from 'Atiyya, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: "When there is close fighting (*al-musayafa*), let him signal with his head [signaling] wherever his face is directed." That is the meaning of Allah's words: ﴿on foot or riding﴾.[[Addition from the manuscript.]]

Similar views were reported from al-Hasan, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ata', 'Atiyya, al-Hakam, Hammad and Qatada. Imam Ahmad, as explicitly stated by him, held that the prayer of fear (*salat al-khawf*) may in some cases be performed with one rak'a when the two armies are locked in combat. On this view is the hadith narrated by Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah and Ibn Jarir, through Abu 'Awana al-Wadday ibn 'Abd Allah al-Yashkuri (Muslim and al-Nasa'i add: and Ayyub ibn 'A'idh), both from Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas al-Kufi, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Allah prescribed the prayer through the tongue of your Prophet ﷺ: four rak'as when residing, two rak'as when traveling, and one rak'a in fear."[[Sahih Muslim, no. (687); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (1247); Sunan al-Nasa'i (1/226, 3/118, 119, 169); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (1068); and Tafsir al-Tabari (5/247).]] This was also the view of al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatada, al-Dahhak and others.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Shu'ba, who said: "I asked al-Hakam, Hammad and Qatada about the prayer during close fighting, and they said: one rak'a." Al-Thawri narrated the same from them, identically.

Ibn Jarir also said: Sa'id ibn 'Amr al-Sukuni narrated to me, Baqiyya ibn al-Walid narrated to us, al-Mas'udi narrated to us, Yazid al-Faqir narrated to us, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: "The prayer of fear is one rak'a." Ibn Jarir chose this view.

Al-Bukhari said: "Chapter: Prayer when storming fortresses and meeting the enemy." Al-Awza'i said: If conquest has become imminent and they are unable to pray, they pray by signaling, each person for himself. If they cannot signal, they delay the prayer until the fighting subsides or they feel safe, then pray two rak'as. If they cannot, they pray one rak'a and two prostrations. If they cannot even do that, the takbir does not suffice for them, and they postpone it until they are safe. Makhul also held this view. Anas ibn Malik said: "I witnessed the storming of the fortress of Tustar at dawn, when the fighting intensified and they could not pray. We did not pray until the sun had risen high, and then we prayed it with Abu Musa, and the city was conquered for us. Anas said: I would not be pleased to have this prayer in exchange for the world and all that is in it."

This is the wording of al-Bukhari.[[Sahih al-Bukhari (2/434).]] He then cited as evidence the hadith of the Prophet ﷺ delaying the 'Asr prayer on the day of the Trench (al-Khandaq) due to the excuse of battle until after the sun had set, and his words ﷺ to his companions after that, when he sent them to Banu Qurayza: "None of you should pray 'Asr except in Banu Qurayza." Some of them were overtaken by the prayer on the road, so they prayed and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only intended for us to hasten our journey. Others were overtaken by the time and did not pray until the sun set in Banu Qurayza, and he did not rebuke either group. This indicates al-Bukhari's preference for this view. The majority disagree with it and rely on the fact that the prayer of fear, in the form described in Surat al-Nisa' and in the hadiths, was not prescribed at the Battle of the Trench, but was prescribed only afterward. This has been explicitly stated in the hadith of Abu Sa'id and others. As for Makhul, al-Awza'i and al-Bukhari, they reply that the prescription of the prayer of fear after that does not negate the permissibility of that (earlier practice), because this is a rare, specific circumstance, so what we have mentioned is permissible in it, based on the practice of the Companions in the conquest of Tustar during the time of 'Umar, which became well known and was not denied. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And when you are secure, remember Allah﴾, meaning: establish your prayer as you were commanded, completing its bowing, prostration, standing, sitting, humility and night vigil. ﴿As He taught you what you did not know﴾, meaning: like the blessing He bestowed upon you, guided you to faith, and taught you what benefits you in this world and the Hereafter. So respond to that with gratitude and remembrance, as in His words after mentioning the prayer of fear: ﴿And when you are secure, establish the prayer. Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers at specified times﴾ [An-Nisa': 103]. The hadiths related to the prayer of fear and its forms will come in Surat al-Nisa' at His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And when you are among them and lead them in prayer...﴾ [An-Nisa': 102].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verses 238–239 (part 1 of 4):

Allah, exalted is He, commands the observance of the prayers at their proper times, the preservation of their limits, and their performance at their appointed times. This is as established in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Which deed is best?" He said: "Prayer at its proper time." I said: "Then which?" He said: "Jihad in the way of Allah." I said: "Then which?" He said: "Kindness to one's parents." He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) related these to me, and had I asked him for more, he would have increased them for me." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (527, 5970) and Sahih Muslim, no. (85).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Yunus narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar ibn Hafs ibn 'Asim, from al-Qasim ibn Ghannam, from his grandmother Umm Abihi al-Dunya, from his grandmother Umm Farwa, who was among those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that she heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mention the deeds, and he said: "Indeed, the most beloved of deeds to Allah is hastening the prayer to its first time."

Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated it similarly. Al-Tirmidhi said: "We do not know it except through the route of al-'Umari, and he is not strong according to the scholars of hadith." [[al-Musnad (6/274), Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (426), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (170).]]

Allah, exalted is He, singled out from among them the middle prayer (al-Salat al-Wusta) for additional emphasis. The early and later scholars (al-Salaf wa al-Khalaf) differed concerning which prayer it is. It was said that it is the Dawn prayer (Subh). Malik related this in al-Muwatta as a mursal report (balaghan) from 'Ali and Ibn 'Abbas [Malik said: "and that is my opinion"]. [[Addition from copy ج.]]

Hushaym, Ibn 'Ulayyah, Ghundar, Ibn Abi 'Adiyy, 'Abd al-Wahhab, Shurayk and others narrated from 'Awf al-A'rabi, from Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi, who said: "I prayed the Dawn prayer behind Ibn 'Abbas, and he performed the qunut (supplication) in it and raised his hands, then said: 'This is the middle prayer which we were commanded to stand in devoutly (qanitin).'" Ibn Jarir narrated it. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (5/215, 216).]] He also narrated it from the hadith of 'Awf, from Khilas ibn 'Amr, from Ibn 'Abbas, the same in substance. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (5/218).]]

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, 'Awf narrated to us, from Abu al-Minhal, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he prayed the morning prayer (al-Ghadat) in the mosque of Basra, and performed the qunut before the bowing (ruku'), and said: "This is the middle prayer which Allah mentioned in His Book when He said: ﴿Observe the prayers, and the middle prayer, and stand before Allah in devotion﴾."

He also said: Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Damghani narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, al-Rabi' ibn Anas informed us, from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: "I prayed the morning prayer behind 'Abd Allah ibn Qays in Basra, and when I had finished, I asked a man from the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) beside me: 'What is the middle prayer?' He said: 'This prayer.'"

It was also narrated by another route from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, that he prayed the morning prayer with the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and when they had finished, he said: "I asked them: 'Which of the prayers is the middle prayer?' They said: 'The one you have just prayed.'"

He also said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Ibn 'Atamah narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Qatadah, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: "The middle prayer is the Dawn prayer."

Ibn Abi Hatim related it from Ibn 'Umar, Abu Umamah, Anas, Abu al-'Aliyah, 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, 'Ata', Mujahid, Jabir ibn Zayd, 'Ikrimah, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas. Ibn Jarir also narrated it from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Hadi, and this is what al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, explicitly stated, arguing from the verse ﴿and stand before Allah in devotion﴾, and for him the qunut is in the Dawn prayer. [Al-Damyati related it from 'Umar, Mu'adh, Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Umar, and 'A'ishah, with differing reports from them, and from Abu Musa, Jabir, Anas, Abu al-Sha'tha', Tawus, 'Ata', 'Ikrimah, and Mujahid.] [[Addition from copies ج and أ.]]

Some said it is the middle prayer on the basis that it is not shortened, and it lies between two four-unit prayers which are shortened (the Dhuhr and the 'Asr when travelling) and it is preceded by the Maghrib prayer [which is not shortened]. It was also said: it is so called because it lies between two loud night prayers (Maghrib and 'Isha') and two silent day prayers (Dhuhr and 'Asr). [[In copies أ and و: "between two nocturnal loud prayers, and two diurnal silent prayers."]]

It was said that it is the Dhuhr prayer. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said in his Musnad: Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to us, from al-Zubayriq, meaning Ibn 'Amr, from Zuhrah, meaning Ibn Ma'bad, who said: "We were sitting with Zayd ibn Thabit, and they sent for Usamah, and asked him about the middle prayer, and he said: 'It is the Dhuhr; the Prophet (ﷺ) used to pray it at the time of the midday heat (al-Hajir).'" [[Musnad al-Tayalisi, no. (628).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Abi Hakim narrated to me, I heard al-Zubayriq narrating from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pray the Dhuhr at the time of the noon heat (al-Hajirah), and he did not pray any prayer more difficult for the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) than it. So the verse was revealed: ﴿Observe the prayers, and the middle prayer﴾, and he said: 'Before it are two prayers and after it are two prayers.'" Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan from the hadith of Shu'bah, with the same chain. [[al-Musnad (5/183) and Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (411).]]

Ahmad also said: Yazid narrated to us, Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to us, from al-Zubayriq, that a group of Quraysh were gathered when Zayd ibn Thabit passed by them. They sent two of their boys to him to ask him about the middle prayer. He said: "It is the 'Asr." Then two men from among them approached him and asked him, and he said: "It is the Dhuhr." Then they returned to Usamah ibn Zayd and asked him, and he said: "It is the Dhuhr; the Prophet (ﷺ) used to pray the Dhuhr at the time of the midday heat, and behind him there would be only one or two rows, while people were at their midday rest and in their trade. So Allah revealed: ﴿Observe the prayers, and the middle prayer, and stand before Allah in devotion﴾." He said: "Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Let men desist, or I will burn their houses.'" [[al-Musnad (5/206).]]

Al-Zubayriq is Ibn 'Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri, who did not meet any of the Companions. The correct report is what preceded from his narration from Zuhrah ibn Ma'bad and 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr.

Shu'bah and Hammam narrated from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Ibn 'Umar, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "The middle prayer is the Dhuhr prayer."

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi and others narrated from Shu'bah: "'Umar ibn Sulayman, from the descendants of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, informed me: I heard 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Aban ibn 'Uthman narrating from his father, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: 'The middle prayer is the Dhuhr.'"

Ibn Jarir narrated it from Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah, from 'Abd al-Samad, from Shu'bah, from 'Umar ibn Sulayman, with the same chain, from Zayd ibn Thabit, in a hadith he traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ): "The middle prayer is the Dhuhr prayer."

Among those from whom it is reported that it is the Dhuhr: Ibn 'Umar, Abu Sa'id, and 'A'ishah, with differing reports from them. This is also the view of 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Hadi, and a report from Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on them all.

It was said that it is the 'Asr prayer. Al-Tirmidhi and al-Baghawi, may Allah have mercy on them both, said: "This is the view of most of the scholars among the Companions and others." Al-Qadi al-Mawardi said: "It is the view of the majority of the Successors (Tabi'un)." The Hafiz Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: "It is the view of most people of transmitted reports (ahl al-athar)." Abu Muhammad ibn 'Atiyyah said in his tafsir: "It is the view of the majority of people." The Hafiz Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Mu'min ibn Khalaf al-Damyati said in his book titled Kashf al-Mughatta fi Tabyin al-Salat al-Wusta: "In it he supported that it is the 'Asr, and he related it from 'Umar, 'Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Ayyub, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, Samurah ibn Jundub, Abu Hurayrah, Abu Sa'id, Hafsah, Umm Habibah, and Umm Salamah. And from Ibn 'Umar, Ibn 'Abbas, and 'A'ishah, according to the sound report from them. This is also the view of 'Abidah, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Zirr ibn Hubaysh, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ibn Sirin, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Kalbi, Muqatil, 'Ubayd ibn Abi Maryam, and others, and it is the school of Ahmad ibn Hanbal." Al-Qadi al-Mawardi said: "And al-Shafi'i." Ibn al-Mundhir said: "It is the sound view from Abu Hanifah, Abu Yusuf, and Muhammad, and Ibn Habib al-Maliki chose it, may Allah have mercy on them all."

The evidence for this:

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Muslim, from Shutayr ibn Shakal, from 'Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said on the day of the Confederates (al-Ahzab): "They preoccupied us from the middle prayer, the 'Asr prayer; may Allah fill their hearts and their houses with fire." Then he prayed it between the two evening prayers, the Maghrib and the 'Isha'. [[al-Musnad (1/81).]]

Similarly, Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Abu Mu'awiyah Muhammad ibn Hazim al-Darir, and al-Nasa'i from the route of 'Isa ibn Yunus; both from al-A'mash, from Muslim ibn Subayh, from Abu al-Duha, from Shutayr ibn Shakal ibn Humayd, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the same. [[Sahih Muslim, no. (627) and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11045).]]

Muslim also narrated it from the route of Shu'bah, from al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah, from Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, from 'Ali, with the same. [[Sahih Muslim, no. (627).]]

It was also narrated by al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim), Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, and many compilers of musnads, sunans and sahihs, through many routes whose mention would be lengthy, from 'Abidah al-Salmani, from 'Ali, with the same. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (2931, 4111), Sahih Muslim, no. (627), Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (409), Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2984), and Sunan al-Nasa'i (1/236).]]

al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the route of al-Hasan al-Basri, from 'Ali, with the same. [[I have not come across this route, and al-Mizzi did not mention it in Tuhfat al-Ashraf.]] Al-Tirmidhi said: "His hearing from him is not known."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Asim, from Zirr, who said: I said to 'Abidah: "Ask 'Ali about the middle prayer." So he asked him, and he said: "We used to consider it the Dawn prayer, until I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say on the day of the Confederates: 'They preoccupied us from the middle prayer, the 'Asr prayer; may Allah fill their graves and their bellies (or their houses) with fire.'" Ibn Jarir narrated it from Bundar, from Ibn Mahdi, with the same. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (5/184).]]

The hadith of the day of the Confederates, and the polytheists' preoccupying the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions from performing the 'Asr prayer that day, is narrated from a group of Companions whose mention would be lengthy. What is intended is the narration of those who explicitly stated in their reports that the middle prayer is the 'Asr prayer. Muslim also narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud and al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, may Allah be pleased with them both. [[Sahih Muslim, no. (628) from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, and no. (630) from the hadith of al-Bara', may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: 'Affan narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Samurah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The middle prayer is the 'Asr prayer." [[al-Musnad (5/22).]]

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 238–239 (part 2 of 4):

Bahz and Affan narrated to us, both saying: Aban narrated to us, Qatada narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Samura, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ﴿Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer﴾, and he named it for us: that it is the Asr prayer [[Al-Musnad (5/8).]].

Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Rawh narrated to us, both saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, from Samura ibn Jundub, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is the Asr." Ibn Ja'far said: He was asked about the middle prayer [[Al-Musnad (5/7, 12, 13).]].

And al-Tirmidhi narrated it through the hadith of Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, from Samura [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, nos. (182, 2983).]]. He said: "Hasan sahih (good and authentic); and al-Hasan is known to have heard from him."

[Another hadith] [[Addition from the manuscripts J and A.]]: Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Mani' narrated to us, Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata' narrated to us, from al-Taymi, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The middle prayer is the Asr prayer" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (5/189).]].

Another chain, or rather another hadith: Ibn Jarir said: al-Muthanna narrated to me, Sulayman ibn Ahmad al-Jurashi al-Wasiti narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us. He said: Sadaqa ibn Khalid informed me, Khalid ibn Dihqan narrated to me, from Khalid ibn Sabalan, from Kuhayl ibn Harmala, who said: Abu Hurayra was asked about the middle prayer, and he said: "We disagreed about it just as you have disagreed about it, while we were in the courtyard of the house of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and among us was the righteous man, Abu Hashim ibn Utba ibn Rabi'a ibn Abd Shams. He said: 'I will find out for you about that.' So he got up, sought permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and entered upon him. Then he came out to us and said: 'He informed us that it is the Asr prayer'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (5/191).]]. This chain is very strange (gharib) indeed.

Another hadith: Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, Abd al-Salam narrated to us, from Salim, mawla (freed slave) of Abu Basir [[In A: "Abi Nusayr".]], Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Dimashqi narrated to me, who said: I was sitting with Abd al-Aziz ibn Marwan, and he said: "O so-and-so, go to so-and-so and say to him: What did you hear from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the middle prayer?" A man who was sitting there said: "Abu Bakr and Umar sent me, while I was a small boy, to ask him about the middle prayer. He took my little finger and said: 'This is Fajr.' Then he gripped the one next to it and said: 'This is Zuhr.' Then he gripped the thumb and said: 'This is Maghrib.' Then he gripped the one next to it and said: 'This is Isha.' Then he said: 'Which of your fingers remains?' I said: 'The middle one.' He said: 'Which prayer remains?' I said: 'Asr.' He said: 'It is Asr'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (5/196).]]. This too is gharib.

Another hadith: Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Awf al-Ta'i narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Damdam ibn Zur'a narrated to me, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The middle prayer is the Asr prayer" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (5/198). The Hafiz's statement: "Its chain is not objectionable" is open to challenge, for its chain contains weakness and a break in continuity; this version is well-known and was transmitted by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir.]]. Its chain is not objectionable [[In A: "Ibn Abbas".]].

Another hadith: Abu Hatim ibn Hibban said in his Sahih: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zuhayr narrated to us, al-Jarrah ibn Makhlad narrated to us, Amr ibn Asim narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us, from Qatada, from Muwarriq [[In H: "Hammam ibn Muwarriq", the correction being from al-Ihsan.]] al-Ijli, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The middle prayer is the Asr prayer" [[Sahih Ibn Hibban (3/121), al-Ihsan edition.]].

Al-Tirmidhi also narrated, through the hadith of Muhammad ibn Talha ibn Musarrif, from Zubayd al-Yami, from Murra al-Hamdani, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The middle prayer is the Asr prayer" [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (181).]]. Then he said: "Hasan sahih."

Muslim also narrated it in his Sahih through the chain of Muhammad ibn Talha, with the same content, and its wording is: "They preoccupied us from the middle prayer, the Asr prayer," the hadith in full.

These are texts on the matter which admit of no other interpretation. This is confirmed by the command to guard it, and by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) in the sound hadith, from the narration of al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever misses the Asr prayer, it is as if he has lost his family and his wealth" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (626).]]. And in the Sahih also, through the hadith of al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Qilaba, from Abu al-Muhajir [[In J: "from Abu al-Muhajir, from Abu al-Malih".]], from Buraydah ibn al-Husayb, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Hasten to the prayer on a cloudy day, for whoever abandons the Asr prayer, his deed has been nullified" [[What is in the Sahih is only from Hisham, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Qilaba, from Abu al-Malih, from Buraydah, may Allah be pleased with him, and it is in Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (553). This second version is in Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (694). The first is the preserved one. Its inclusion in manuscript J was correct, as I have explained, but there was confusion in this, for he wrote the phrase "and in the Sahih" and then corrected it.]] [[Found in J: "Thus Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of al-Awza'i, and al-Bukhari and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Hisham al-Dastuwa'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Qilaba, from Abu al-Malih ibn Usama, from Buraydah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): 'Whoever abandons the Asr prayer, his deed has been nullified.'"]].

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'a informed us, from Abd Allah ibn Hubayra, from Abu Tamim, from Abu Basra [[In J: "from Abu Nadra".]] al-Ghifari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) led us in prayer in a valley of their valleys called al-Makhammas, the Asr prayer. He said: "Indeed, this prayer, the Asr prayer, was presented to those before you, and they neglected it. Beware! Whoever prays it will have his reward doubled. Beware! There is no prayer after it until you see the witness (the sun's setting)" [[In A: "until it sets".]].

Then he said: It was narrated by Yahya ibn Ishaq, from al-Layth, from Khayr [[In J: "from Hasan".]] ibn Nu'aym, from Abd Allah ibn Hubayra, with the same content [[Al-Musnad (6/397).]].

Thus Muslim and al-Nasa'i both narrated it, through Qutayba, from al-Layth [[Sahih Muslim, no. (830), and Sunan al-Nasa'i (1/259).]]. Muslim also narrated it through the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid ibn Abi Habib narrated to me, both of them from Khayr ibn Nu'aym al-Hadrami, from Abd Allah ibn Hubayra al-Sabai [[In A: "al-Shaybani".]] [[Sahih Muslim, no. (830).]].

As for the hadith which Imam Ahmad also narrated: Ishaq narrated to us, Malik informed me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from al-Qa'qa' ibn Hakim, from Abu Yunus, mawla of Aisha, who said: Aisha ordered me to write a mushaf (copy of the Qur'an) for her, and she said: "When you reach this verse, ﴿Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer﴾, inform me." When I reached it, I informed her, and she dictated to me: "Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer, and the Asr prayer, and stand before Allah in devotion (qanitin)." She said: "I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." Thus Muslim also narrated it, from Yahya ibn Yahya, from Malik, with the same content [[Al-Musnad (6/73) and Sahih Muslim, no. (629).]].

Ibn Jarir said: al-Muthanna narrated to me, al-Hajjaj narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Urwa, from his father, who said: In the mushaf of Aisha was: "Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer, and it is the Asr prayer" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (5/175).]]. He also narrated it through the chain of al-Hasan al-Basri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited it in this way.

Imam Malik also narrated, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Amr ibn Rafi', who said: I used to write a mushaf for Hafsa, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), and she said: "When you reach this verse, inform me: ﴿Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer﴾." When I reached it, I informed her, and she dictated to me: "Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer, and the Asr prayer, and stand before Allah in devotion" [[Al-Muwatta' (1/139).]].

Thus Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated it, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to me, and Nafi', mawla of Ibn Umar [[In J: "ibn Bashshar".]]: that Umar ibn Nafi' said ... and he mentioned the like of it, and added: "As I memorised it from the Prophet (ﷺ)."

Another chain from Hafsa: Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'ba narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Azdi, from Salim ibn Abd Allah, that Hafsa ordered a person to write a mushaf for her, and she said: "When you reach this verse, ﴿Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer﴾, inform me." When he reached it, he informed her, and she said: "Write: 'Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer, and the Asr prayer'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (5/208, 209).]].

Another chain: Ibn Jarir said: Ibn al-Muthanna Abd al-Wahhab narrated to me, Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Nafi', that Hafsa ordered a freed slave of hers to write a mushaf for her, and she said: "When you reach this verse, ' Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer ', do not write it until I dictate it to you as I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite it." When he reached it, she ordered him, and he wrote it: "Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer, and the Asr prayer, and stand before Allah in devotion." Nafi' said: "I read that mushaf and I saw in it the letter 'waw' (and)" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (5/209).]].

Likewise Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas and Ubayd ibn Umayr that they both recited it in this way.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abda narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, Abu Salama narrated to me, from Amr ibn Rafi', mawla of Umar, who said: In the mushaf of Hafsa was: "Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer, and the Asr prayer, and stand before Allah in devotion" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (5/211).]].

The statement of the objection is this: the verse links "the Asr prayer" to "the middle prayer" with the conjunction "and" (waw), which requires difference, and so this indicates that the Asr prayer is other than the middle prayer. This has been answered in several ways. First: if this is narrated as a report, then the hadith of Ali is sounder and more explicit than it. Moreover, the "and" may be superfluous, as in His words: ﴿And thus We detail the verses, that the way of the criminals may become clear﴾ [al-An'am: 55], and ﴿And thus We showed Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth, that he might be among the certain﴾ [al-An'am: 75]. Or the "and" may be for coordinating attributes, not essences, as in His words: ﴿But (he is) the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets﴾ [al-Ahzab: 40], and His words: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, who created and proportioned, and who determined and guided, and who brought forth the pasture﴾ [al-A'la: 1–4], and there are many similar examples. The poet said:

*To the lordly king and the son of the valiant,*
*and the lion of the battle in the crush...*

And Abu Du'ad al-Iyadi said:

*He let death and the fates (al-manun) loose upon them,*
*so for them in the echo of the graves is a skull.*

And death is al-manun. The poet Adi ibn Zayd al-Ibadi said:

*I presented the hide to his wrists,*
*so he found her words false and a lie (mayna).*

And mayna means falsehood. Sibawayh, the master of the grammarians, has explicitly affirmed the permissibility of the saying of one who says: "I passed by your brother and your companion," where the companion is the brother himself. And Allah knows best.

As for it being narrated as Qur'an, it is not transmitted by mass transmission (tawatur, a report so widely transmitted that its reliability is certain), so no Qur'an can be established by a single-narrator report (khabar al-wahid). For this reason, the Commander of the Faithful, 'Uthman ibn 'Affan (may Allah be pleased with him), did not include it in the Imam Mushaf (the standard codex), and none of the reciters whose recitation establishes proof read it in this way, neither among the Seven nor among others.

Then, a report has indicated the abrogation (naskh, the cancellation of a ruling or recitation by a later revelation) of this recitation mentioned in this hadith. Muslim said: Ishaq ibn Rahawayh narrated to us, Yahya ibn Adam informed us, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from Shaqiq ibn 'Uqbah, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: "The following was revealed: 'Guard the prayers and the middle prayer, the 'Asr prayer,' [[In J and A: "And the middle prayer is the 'Asr prayer."]] and we recited it before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for as long as Allah willed. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, abrogated it and revealed: ﴿Guard the prayers and the middle prayer﴾." Zahir, a man who was with Shaqiq, said to him: "Is it the 'Asr?" He said: "I have told you how it was revealed and how Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, abrogated it."

Muslim said: al-Ash'ari also narrated it from al-Thawri, from al-Aswad, from Shaqiq.

I say: Muslim did not narrate from this Shaqiq anything except this single hadith, and Allah knows best. Accordingly, this recitation, which is the recitation of the mainstream (al-jaddah), abrogates the wording of the narration of 'Aishah and Hafsah, and its meaning as well, if the conjunction "and" indicates difference; otherwise it abrogates only its wording. And Allah knows best.

It has been said that the middle prayer is the Maghrib prayer. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this from Ibn 'Abbas, but its chain (isnad) is problematic, for he narrated it from his father, from Abu al-Jumahir [[In A: "from Abu al-Jamahir."]], from Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Khalil, from his paternal uncle, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The middle prayer is the Maghrib." Ibn Jarir transmitted this view from Qabisah ibn Dhu'ayb, and it is also reported from Qatadah with variation in his account. Some have justified this view on the grounds that it is the middle in number between the four-unit and two-unit prayers, that it is the odd (witr) of the obligatory prayers, and by the virtue reported concerning it. And Allah knows best.

It has been said that it is the 'Isha' prayer (the night prayer), which was chosen by 'Ali ibn Ahmad al-Wahidi in his well-known tafsir. It has also been said that it is one of the five, unspecified, and it was left undetermined among them, just as the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr) is undetermined within the year, the month, or the last ten [nights]. This view is attributed to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Shurayh al-Qadi, Nafi' the client of Ibn 'Umar, and al-Rabi' ibn Khaytham, and it is also reported from Zayd ibn Thabit. Imam al-Haramayn al-Juwayni chose it in his book al-Nihayah.

It has also been said: rather, the middle prayer is the totality of the five prayers. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this from Ibn 'Umar, but its authenticity is also questionable. It is strange that this view was chosen by Shaykh Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr al-Namari, the imam of the lands beyond the sea, and indeed it is one of the greatest [errors], for he chose it, despite his knowledge and memorization, though no proof from the Book, the Sunnah, or a transmitted report supports it. It has been said: it is the 'Isha' and the Fajr prayers. It has been said: rather, it is the congregational prayer. It has been said: the Friday prayer. It has been said: the prayer of fear (salat al-khawf). It has been said: rather, the 'Id al-Fitr prayer. It has been said: rather, the 'Id al-Adha prayer. It has been said: the witr prayer. It has been said: the Duha prayer. Others suspended judgment on it when the evidences conflicted with them, and the basis for preferring one view did not become clear to them. No consensus (ijma', scholarly agreement) was reached on a single view; rather, the dispute over it has continued to exist from the time of the Companions until now.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar and Ibn Muthanna narrated to me, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, who said: I heard Qatadah narrating from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: "The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) differed concerning the middle prayer in this way," and he interlaced his fingers.

[Fakhr al-Din al-Razi, in his tafsir, related a view from a group of scholars, among them Zayd ibn Thabit and Rabi' ibn Khaytham: that its explanation was not intended, rather its indefiniteness was intended, just as the Night of Decree is undetermined in Ramadan, the hour of answered supplication on Friday, the Greatest Name among the names of Allah, and the time of death for the responsible person, so that he may be ready at every time. Likewise, the night in which a plague descends from the sky was left undetermined so that people might beware of it and always be prepared; likewise, the time of the Hour is something Allah has kept for Himself, so it will come only suddenly.]

All these views are weak in comparison to the one before them, and the axis and the arena of dispute is really between the Fajr and the 'Asr. The Sunnah has established that it is the 'Asr, so it is necessary to adopt this view.

Imam Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim al-Razi narrated in his book "Fada'il al-Shafi'i" (may Allah have mercy on him): My father narrated to us, I heard Harmalah ibn Yahya al-Tujibi say: al-Shafi'i said: "Whatever I have said, if there is a report from the Prophet (ﷺ) that is authentic and contrary to my statement, then the hadith of the Prophet (ﷺ) takes priority, and do not follow me blindly." Similarly, al-Rabi', al-Za'farani, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated from al-Shafi'i. Musa Abu al-Walid, son of Abu al-Jarud, said on the authority of al-Shafi'i: "When a hadith is authentic and I have stated a view, I retract my view and act upon that [hadith]." This is from his nobility and trustworthiness, and this is the same as that of his fellow imams, may Allah have mercy on them, be pleased with them all, amen. From here, al-Qadi al-Mawardi firmly stated that the school of al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) holds that the middle prayer is the 'Asr prayer, although it is explicitly stated in the New (al-Jadid) and other works that it is the Fajr, because the hadiths that it is the 'Asr are authentic. A group of the school's hadith scholars has agreed with this approach, and all praise and grace belong to Allah. Among the jurists of the school are those who deny that the 'Asr is the school's position of al-Shafi'i, and they insist that it is the Fajr, with a single view. Al-Mawardi said: "Among them are those who report two opinions on the matter, and the presentation of objections and responses has another place other than this, which we have compiled separately, and all praise and grace belong to Allah."

* *

And His Exalted saying: ﴿And stand before Allah in devotion﴾, meaning: humble, submissive, and meek before Him. This command necessarily entails abstaining from speech during the prayer, as speech contradicts it. For this reason, when the Prophet (ﷺ) refrained from returning the greeting to Ibn Mas'ud when he greeted him while he was praying, he apologized to him for that and said: "Indeed, there is preoccupation in the prayer." In Sahih Muslim, he (peace be upon him) said to Mu'awiyah ibn al-Hakam al-[Sulami] [[Addition from J, A, and W.]] when he spoke during the prayer: "Indeed, this prayer does not allow any of the speech of people; it is only glorification, magnification, and the remembrance of Allah."

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Isma'il, Harith ibn Shubayl narrated to me, from Abu 'Amr al-Shaybani, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: "A man used to speak to his companion during the prayer in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) about a need, until this verse was revealed: ﴿And stand before Allah in devotion﴾, and we were commanded to be silent." This was narrated by the group [of compilers] except Ibn Majah, through several chains from Isma'il.

This hadith has troubled a group of scholars, since it was established for them that the prohibition of speech in the prayer occurred in Mecca, before the migration to Medina and after the migration to the land of Abyssinia, as indicated by the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud in the Sahih, who said: "We used to greet the Prophet (ﷺ) before we migrated to Abyssinia while he was praying, and he would return our greeting. When we returned, I greeted him, but he did not return my greeting, and I was struck by anxiety. When he finished the prayer, he said: 'I did not return your greeting except that I was in prayer, and indeed Allah brings about from His command what He wills, and among what He has newly commanded is that you not speak during the prayer.'"

Ibn Mas'ud was among those who embraced Islam early and migrated to Abyssinia, then returned from it to Mecca with those who returned, then migrated to Medina. This verse ﴿And stand before Allah in devotion﴾ was revealed in Medina without any disagreement. Some said that Zayd ibn Arqam, in his saying "A man used to speak to his brother about his need during the prayer," intended to inform about the general class of people, and he derived the prohibition of that from this verse according to what he understood from it, and Allah knows best.

Others said: he intended that this occurred in Medina after the migration to it, and that it would have been permitted twice and prohibited twice, as some of our companions and others chose. The first is more evident. And Allah also knows best.

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Bishr ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Yahya narrated to us, from al-Musayyab, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Some of us used to greet one another during the prayer. I passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and greeted him, but he did not return my greeting, and it occurred to my mind that something had been revealed concerning me. When the Prophet (ﷺ) finished his prayer, he said: 'And upon you be peace, O greeter, and the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, brings about from His command what He wills. So when you are in prayer, be devoutly obedient (qunut) and do not speak.'" [[Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/137) through a chain from 'Asim, from al-Musayyab, from Ibn Mas'ud, similarly.]]

* *

And His saying: ﴿So if you fear, then [pray] on foot or riding; and when you are safe, remember Allah as He has taught you that which you did not know﴾. When Allah, the Exalted, commanded His servants to guard the prayers, to uphold their limits, and emphasized the matter with its confirmation, He mentioned the state in which a person is preoccupied from performing them in the most complete manner, which is the state of fighting and the clash of battle. So He said: ﴿So if you fear, then [pray] on foot or riding﴾ [[In J: "And if" which is an error.]], meaning: then pray in whatever state you are, on foot or riding, that is: facing the qiblah or not facing it. As Malik narrated from Nafi', that Ibn 'Umar, whenever he was asked about the prayer of fear, described it, then said: "If the fear is greater than that, pray on foot or riding, facing the qiblah or not facing it." Nafi' said: "I do not think Ibn 'Umar mentioned that except from the Prophet (ﷺ)." Al-Bukhari narrated it, and this wording is his [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4535).]], and Muslim [narrated it]. Al-Bukhari also narrated it through another route, from Ibn Jurayj, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), similarly or close to it [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (943).]]. Muslim also has from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "If the fear is greater than that, then pray riding or standing, signaling with gestures" [[Sahih Muslim no. (839).]].

In the hadith of Abdullah ibn Unays al-Juhani, when the Prophet ﷺ sent him to Khalid ibn Sufyan al-Hudhali to kill him, and he was near 'Arafa (or 'Arafat), when he met him, the time of the 'Asr prayer came. He said: "I feared that it would pass me, so I began to pray while signaling with my head (*ima'*)." The full hadith was narrated by Ahmad and Abu Dawud with a sound chain.[[al-Musnad (3/496) and Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (1249).]] This is one of the concessions (*rukhas*) that Allah granted to His servants, and one of the burdens and shackles He lifted from them.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through Shabib ibn Bishr, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said regarding this verse: the rider prays on his mount and the one on foot prays on his feet. He said: similar views were reported from al-Hasan, Mujahid, Makhul, al-Suddi, al-Hakam, Malik, al-Awza'i, al-Thawri and al-Hasan ibn Salih, and they added: he signals with his head wherever he faces.[[In A: "signaling with the face."]]

Then he said: My father narrated to us, Abu Ghassan narrated to us, Dawud (i.e., Ibn 'Ulayya) narrated to us, from Mutarrif, from 'Atiyya, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: "When there is close fighting (*al-musayafa*), let him signal with his head [signaling] wherever his face is directed." That is the meaning of Allah's words: ﴿on foot or riding﴾.[[Addition from the manuscript.]]

Similar views were reported from al-Hasan, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ata', 'Atiyya, al-Hakam, Hammad and Qatada. Imam Ahmad, as explicitly stated by him, held that the prayer of fear (*salat al-khawf*) may in some cases be performed with one rak'a when the two armies are locked in combat. On this view is the hadith narrated by Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah and Ibn Jarir, through Abu 'Awana al-Wadday ibn 'Abd Allah al-Yashkuri (Muslim and al-Nasa'i add: and Ayyub ibn 'A'idh), both from Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas al-Kufi, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Allah prescribed the prayer through the tongue of your Prophet ﷺ: four rak'as when residing, two rak'as when traveling, and one rak'a in fear."[[Sahih Muslim, no. (687); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (1247); Sunan al-Nasa'i (1/226, 3/118, 119, 169); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (1068); and Tafsir al-Tabari (5/247).]] This was also the view of al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatada, al-Dahhak and others.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Shu'ba, who said: "I asked al-Hakam, Hammad and Qatada about the prayer during close fighting, and they said: one rak'a." Al-Thawri narrated the same from them, identically.

Ibn Jarir also said: Sa'id ibn 'Amr al-Sukuni narrated to me, Baqiyya ibn al-Walid narrated to us, al-Mas'udi narrated to us, Yazid al-Faqir narrated to us, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: "The prayer of fear is one rak'a." Ibn Jarir chose this view.

Al-Bukhari said: "Chapter: Prayer when storming fortresses and meeting the enemy." Al-Awza'i said: If conquest has become imminent and they are unable to pray, they pray by signaling, each person for himself. If they cannot signal, they delay the prayer until the fighting subsides or they feel safe, then pray two rak'as. If they cannot, they pray one rak'a and two prostrations. If they cannot even do that, the takbir does not suffice for them, and they postpone it until they are safe. Makhul also held this view. Anas ibn Malik said: "I witnessed the storming of the fortress of Tustar at dawn, when the fighting intensified and they could not pray. We did not pray until the sun had risen high, and then we prayed it with Abu Musa, and the city was conquered for us. Anas said: I would not be pleased to have this prayer in exchange for the world and all that is in it."

This is the wording of al-Bukhari.[[Sahih al-Bukhari (2/434).]] He then cited as evidence the hadith of the Prophet ﷺ delaying the 'Asr prayer on the day of the Trench (al-Khandaq) due to the excuse of battle until after the sun had set, and his words ﷺ to his companions after that, when he sent them to Banu Qurayza: "None of you should pray 'Asr except in Banu Qurayza." Some of them were overtaken by the prayer on the road, so they prayed and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only intended for us to hasten our journey. Others were overtaken by the time and did not pray until the sun set in Banu Qurayza, and he did not rebuke either group. This indicates al-Bukhari's preference for this view. The majority disagree with it and rely on the fact that the prayer of fear, in the form described in Surat al-Nisa' and in the hadiths, was not prescribed at the Battle of the Trench, but was prescribed only afterward. This has been explicitly stated in the hadith of Abu Sa'id and others. As for Makhul, al-Awza'i and al-Bukhari, they reply that the prescription of the prayer of fear after that does not negate the permissibility of that (earlier practice), because this is a rare, specific circumstance, so what we have mentioned is permissible in it, based on the practice of the Companions in the conquest of Tustar during the time of 'Umar, which became well known and was not denied. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And when you are secure, remember Allah﴾, meaning: establish your prayer as you were commanded, completing its bowing, prostration, standing, sitting, humility and night vigil. ﴿As He taught you what you did not know﴾, meaning: like the blessing He bestowed upon you, guided you to faith, and taught you what benefits you in this world and the Hereafter. So respond to that with gratitude and remembrance, as in His words after mentioning the prayer of fear: ﴿And when you are secure, establish the prayer. Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers at specified times﴾ [An-Nisa': 103]. The hadiths related to the prayer of fear and its forms will come in Surat al-Nisa' at His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And when you are among them and lead them in prayer...﴾ [An-Nisa': 102].

The majority of scholars said: this verse has been abrogated (*mansukh*, abrogated by *naskh*, the divine removal of a ruling) by the one before it, which is His saying: ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days﴾.

Al-Bukhari said: Umayyah narrated to us, Yazid ibn Zurai' narrated to us, from Habib, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: Ibn al-Zubayr said: I said to Uthman ibn Affan: ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind﴾ has been abrogated by the other verse, so why do you write it down, or leave it [in the Mushaf]? He said: O nephew, I will not change anything of it from its place.

The difficulty that Ibn al-Zubayr raised to Uthman was this: if its ruling has been abrogated by the four months, what is the wisdom in keeping its text when its ruling has ceased? And if its text remains after the verse that abrogated it, that suggests its ruling still applies. The Commander of the Believers replied that this is a matter of divine revelation (*tawqifi*, fixed by revelation and not by personal choice), and that he had found it established in the Mushaf in that position after it, so he kept it where he found it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj and Uthman ibn Ata', from Ata', from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind, a bequest for their wives: maintenance for a year without being driven out﴾. The widow used to have her maintenance and residence in the house for a year, and then the verses of inheritance abrogated this, so the wives were given a quarter or an eighth of what the husband left.

He then said: It is also reported from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, Ibn al-Zubayr, Mujahid, Ibrahim, Ata', al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Suddi, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Ata' al-Khurasani and al-Rabi' ibn Anas that it has been abrogated.

It is also reported through the chain of Ali ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn Abbas, who said: When a man died and left his wife, she would observe a waiting period of a year in his house, and he would provide for her from his property. Then Allah revealed afterwards: ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days﴾.

This is the waiting period of a widow, except if she is pregnant, in which case her waiting period is until she gives birth to what is in her womb. And He said: ﴿For them is a quarter of what you leave, if you have no child; but if you have a child, then for them is an eighth of what you leave﴾ [al-Nisa': 12]. So He specified the inheritance of the woman and left out the bequest and maintenance.

He said: It is reported from Mujahid, al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi' and Muqatil ibn Hayyan that they said: it was abrogated by ﴿four months and ten days﴾.

He said: It is reported from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab that he said: it was abrogated by the verse in al-Ahzab: ﴿O you who believe, when you marry believing women and then divorce them﴾ [al-Ahzab: 49].

I say: It is also reported from [Muqatil and] Qatadah that it was abrogated by the verse of inheritance.

Al-Bukhari said: Ishaq ibn Rahawayh narrated to us, Rawh narrated to us, Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind﴾, he said: This waiting period was obligatory, that she observe it in the house of her husband's family. Then Allah revealed: ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind, a bequest for their wives: maintenance for a year without being driven out. But if they leave, there is no blame on you for what they do with themselves of what is reasonable﴾. He said: Allah made for her the completion of the year, seven months and twenty nights, a bequest; if she wishes she may stay in her bequest, and if she wishes she may leave. This is the saying of Allah: ﴿without being driven out. But if they leave, there is no blame on you﴾. So the waiting period remains as it is, obligatory for her. This is what was reported from Mujahid, may Allah have mercy on him. Ata' said, and Ibn Abbas said: This verse abrogated her waiting period in her family's house, so she may observe it wherever she wishes. This is the saying of Allah: ﴿without being driven out﴾. Ata' said: If she wishes, she may observe the waiting period in her family's house and stay in her bequest, and if she wishes, she may leave, due to the saying of Allah: ﴿there is no blame on you for what they do with themselves﴾. Ata' said: Then the inheritance came and abrogated the residence, so she observes the waiting period wherever she wishes, and she has no residence right. Then al-Bukhari transmitted from Ibn Abbas the same as what was mentioned before from him [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4531].

So this is the view on which Mujahid and Ata' relied, that this verse did not establish the obligation of a year's waiting period, as the majority claimed, such that it would be abrogated by the four months and ten days. Rather, it indicates that this was a matter of the injunction concerning wives, that they be allowed residence in their husbands' houses after their death for a full year, if they choose that. For this reason He said: ﴿a bequest for their wives﴾, meaning: Allah enjoins you concerning them as a bequest, like His saying: ﴿Allah enjoins you concerning your children﴾ [al-Nisa': 11], and His saying: ﴿a bequest from Allah﴾ [al-Nisa': 12]. It is also said that it is in the accusative (*nasb*) in the sense of: "let them bequeath for them a bequest." Others read it in the nominative, "wasiyyatun" (a bequest), in the sense of: "a bequest has been prescribed for you," and Ibn Jarir preferred this reading. They are not prevented from this, due to His saying: ﴿without being driven out﴾. As for when their waiting period has ended, by the four months and ten days or by giving birth, and they choose to leave and move from that dwelling, they are not prevented from doing so, due to His saying: ﴿But if they leave, there is no blame on you for what they do with themselves of what is reasonable﴾. This view has its force, and the wording supports it. A group of scholars chose it, among them the Imam Abu al-Abbas Ibn Taymiyyah [in Jim: "Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him"]. Others rejected it, among them the Shaykh Abu Umar Ibn Abd al-Barr.

As for the saying of Ata' and those who follow him, that this was abrogated by the verse of inheritance: if they mean what exceeds the four months and ten days, this is accepted; but if they mean that the residence during the four months and ten days is not owed from the estate of the deceased, this is a matter of disagreement among the scholars, and there are two views of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him. They have used as evidence for the obligation of residence in the husband's house what Malik narrated in his Muwatta', from Sa'd ibn Ishaq ibn Ka'b ibn Ujrah, from his paternal aunt Zaynab bint Ka'b ibn Ujrah: that al-Furay'ah bint Malik ibn Sinan, who was the sister of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with them both, informed her that she came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking him to allow her to return to her family in Banu Khudrah, for her husband had gone out in pursuit of runaway slaves of his, and they caught up with him at a place called al-Qadum and killed him. She said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to let me return to my family in Banu Khudrah, for my husband did not leave me in a house he owned nor with maintenance. She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Yes." She said: So I turned to leave, and when I was in the chamber, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called me, or had me called, and said: "How did you say it?" So I repeated to him the story I had told him about my husband. He said: "Stay in your house until the prescribed term reaches its end." She said: So I observed the waiting period there for four months and ten days. She said: When Uthman ibn Affan was caliph, he sent for me and asked me about this, and I told him, so he followed it and gave judgment accordingly [Muwatta', 2/591].

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i also transmitted it in the same way from the hadith of Malik [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2300; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1204; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11044]. Al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah also transmitted it through various chains from Sa'd ibn Ishaq [Sunan al-Nasa'i, 6/199, 200; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2031]. Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih (good and authentic).

* *

His saying: ﴿For divorced women there is provision in a reasonable manner, a duty upon the God-conscious﴾. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: When His saying was revealed: ﴿provision in a reasonable manner, a duty upon the doers of good﴾ [al-Baqarah: 236], a man said: If I wish, I will do good and act; and if I wish, I will not act. So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿For divorced women there is provision in a reasonable manner, a duty upon the God-conscious﴾. Scholars who held that the provision (*mut'ah*) is obligatory for every divorced woman, whether she was one for whom no dowry had been specified, or one for whom a dowry had been set, or one divorced before consummation, or one who had been consummated with, have used this verse as evidence. This is a view attributed to al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and other early scholars also held it, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Those who do not make it obligatory in every case restrict this general statement by the implication of His saying: ﴿There is no blame on you if you divorce women before you have touched them or specified for them a dowry; but provide for them, the wealthy according to his means and the straitened according to his means, a provision in a reasonable manner, a duty upon the doers of good﴾. The earlier scholars answered that this is a case of mentioning some individual instances of the general category, so there is no restriction according to the well-known and preferred view. And Allah knows best.

* *
