They have used as evidence for the obligation of residence in the husband's house what Malik narrated in his Muwatta', from Sa'd ibn Ishaq ibn Ka'b ibn Ujrah, from his paternal aunt Zaynab bint Ka'b ibn Ujrah: that al-Furay'ah bint Malik ibn Sinan, who was the sister of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with them both, informed her that she came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking him to allow her to return to her family in Banu Khudrah, for her husband had gone out in pursuit of runaway slaves of his, and they caught up with him at a place called al-Qadum and killed him. She said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to let me return to my family in Banu Khudrah, for my husband did not leave me in a house he owned nor with maintenance. She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Yes." She said: So I turned to leave, and when I was in the chamber, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called me, or had me called, and said: "How did you say it?" So I repeated to him the story I had told him about my husband. He said: "Stay in your house until the prescribed term reaches its end." She said: So I observed the waiting period there for four months and ten days. She said: When Uthman ibn Affan was caliph, he sent for me and asked me about this, and I told him, so he followed it and gave judgment accordingly [Muwatta', 2/591].

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i also transmitted it in the same way from the hadith of Malik [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2300; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1204; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11044]. Al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah also transmitted it through various chains from Sa'd ibn Ishaq [Sunan al-Nasa'i, 6/199, 200; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2031]. Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih (good and authentic).

* *

His saying: ﴿For divorced women there is provision in a reasonable manner, a duty upon the God-conscious﴾. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: When His saying was revealed: ﴿provision in a reasonable manner, a duty upon the doers of good﴾ [al-Baqarah: 236], a man said: If I wish, I will do good and act; and if I wish, I will not act. So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿For divorced women there is provision in a reasonable manner, a duty upon the God-conscious﴾. Scholars who held that the provision (*mut'ah*) is obligatory for every divorced woman, whether she was one for whom no dowry had been specified, or one for whom a dowry had been set, or one divorced before consummation, or one who had been consummated with, have used this verse as evidence. This is a view attributed to al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and other early scholars also held it, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Those who do not make it obligatory in every case restrict this general statement by the implication of His saying: ﴿There is no blame on you if you divorce women before you have touched them or specified for them a dowry; but provide for them, the wealthy according to his means and the straitened according to his means, a provision in a reasonable manner, a duty upon the doers of good﴾. The earlier scholars answered that this is a case of mentioning some individual instances of the general category, so there is no restriction according to the well-known and preferred view. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you His verses﴾, meaning: in His permitting and forbidding, His obligations and His limits, in what He has commanded you and forbidden you, He has explained them, clarified them, and expounded them, and did not leave them unclear at the time you need them, ﴿so that you may understand﴾, meaning: that you may comprehend and reflect.

The majority of scholars said: this verse has been abrogated (*mansukh*, abrogated by *naskh*, the divine removal of a ruling) by the one before it, which is His saying: ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days﴾.

Al-Bukhari said: Umayyah narrated to us, Yazid ibn Zurai' narrated to us, from Habib, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: Ibn al-Zubayr said: I said to Uthman ibn Affan: ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind﴾ has been abrogated by the other verse, so why do you write it down, or leave it [in the Mushaf]? He said: O nephew, I will not change anything of it from its place.

The difficulty that Ibn al-Zubayr raised to Uthman was this: if its ruling has been abrogated by the four months, what is the wisdom in keeping its text when its ruling has ceased? And if its text remains after the verse that abrogated it, that suggests its ruling still applies. The Commander of the Believers replied that this is a matter of divine revelation (*tawqifi*, fixed by revelation and not by personal choice), and that he had found it established in the Mushaf in that position after it, so he kept it where he found it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj and Uthman ibn Ata', from Ata', from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind, a bequest for their wives: maintenance for a year without being driven out﴾. The widow used to have her maintenance and residence in the house for a year, and then the verses of inheritance abrogated this, so the wives were given a quarter or an eighth of what the husband left.

He then said: It is also reported from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, Ibn al-Zubayr, Mujahid, Ibrahim, Ata', al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Suddi, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Ata' al-Khurasani and al-Rabi' ibn Anas that it has been abrogated.

It is also reported through the chain of Ali ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn Abbas, who said: When a man died and left his wife, she would observe a waiting period of a year in his house, and he would provide for her from his property. Then Allah revealed afterwards: ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days﴾.

This is the waiting period of a widow, except if she is pregnant, in which case her waiting period is until she gives birth to what is in her womb. And He said: ﴿For them is a quarter of what you leave, if you have no child; but if you have a child, then for them is an eighth of what you leave﴾ [al-Nisa': 12]. So He specified the inheritance of the woman and left out the bequest and maintenance.

He said: It is reported from Mujahid, al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi' and Muqatil ibn Hayyan that they said: it was abrogated by ﴿four months and ten days﴾.

He said: It is reported from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab that he said: it was abrogated by the verse in al-Ahzab: ﴿O you who believe, when you marry believing women and then divorce them﴾ [al-Ahzab: 49].

I say: It is also reported from [Muqatil and] Qatadah that it was abrogated by the verse of inheritance.

Al-Bukhari said: Ishaq ibn Rahawayh narrated to us, Rawh narrated to us, Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind﴾, he said: This waiting period was obligatory, that she observe it in the house of her husband's family. Then Allah revealed: ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind, a bequest for their wives: maintenance for a year without being driven out. But if they leave, there is no blame on you for what they do with themselves of what is reasonable﴾. He said: Allah made for her the completion of the year, seven months and twenty nights, a bequest; if she wishes she may stay in her bequest, and if she wishes she may leave. This is the saying of Allah: ﴿without being driven out. But if they leave, there is no blame on you﴾. So the waiting period remains as it is, obligatory for her. This is what was reported from Mujahid, may Allah have mercy on him. Ata' said, and Ibn Abbas said: This verse abrogated her waiting period in her family's house, so she may observe it wherever she wishes. This is the saying of Allah: ﴿without being driven out﴾. Ata' said: If she wishes, she may observe the waiting period in her family's house and stay in her bequest, and if she wishes, she may leave, due to the saying of Allah: ﴿there is no blame on you for what they do with themselves﴾. Ata' said: Then the inheritance came and abrogated the residence, so she observes the waiting period wherever she wishes, and she has no residence right. Then al-Bukhari transmitted from Ibn Abbas the same as what was mentioned before from him [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4531].

So this is the view on which Mujahid and Ata' relied, that this verse did not establish the obligation of a year's waiting period, as the majority claimed, such that it would be abrogated by the four months and ten days. Rather, it indicates that this was a matter of the injunction concerning wives, that they be allowed residence in their husbands' houses after their death for a full year, if they choose that. For this reason He said: ﴿a bequest for their wives﴾, meaning: Allah enjoins you concerning them as a bequest, like His saying: ﴿Allah enjoins you concerning your children﴾ [al-Nisa': 11], and His saying: ﴿a bequest from Allah﴾ [al-Nisa': 12]. It is also said that it is in the accusative (*nasb*) in the sense of: "let them bequeath for them a bequest." Others read it in the nominative, "wasiyyatun" (a bequest), in the sense of: "a bequest has been prescribed for you," and Ibn Jarir preferred this reading. They are not prevented from this, due to His saying: ﴿without being driven out﴾. As for when their waiting period has ended, by the four months and ten days or by giving birth, and they choose to leave and move from that dwelling, they are not prevented from doing so, due to His saying: ﴿But if they leave, there is no blame on you for what they do with themselves of what is reasonable﴾. This view has its force, and the wording supports it. A group of scholars chose it, among them the Imam Abu al-Abbas Ibn Taymiyyah [in Jim: "Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him"]. Others rejected it, among them the Shaykh Abu Umar Ibn Abd al-Barr.

As for the saying of Ata' and those who follow him, that this was abrogated by the verse of inheritance: if they mean what exceeds the four months and ten days, this is accepted; but if they mean that the residence during the four months and ten days is not owed from the estate of the deceased, this is a matter of disagreement among the scholars, and there are two views of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him. They have used as evidence for the obligation of residence in the husband's house what Malik narrated in his Muwatta', from Sa'd ibn Ishaq ibn Ka'b ibn Ujrah, from his paternal aunt Zaynab bint Ka'b ibn Ujrah: that al-Furay'ah bint Malik ibn Sinan, who was the sister of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with them both, informed her that she came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking him to allow her to return to her family in Banu Khudrah, for her husband had gone out in pursuit of runaway slaves of his, and they caught up with him at a place called al-Qadum and killed him. She said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to let me return to my family in Banu Khudrah, for my husband did not leave me in a house he owned nor with maintenance. She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Yes." She said: So I turned to leave, and when I was in the chamber, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called me, or had me called, and said: "How did you say it?" So I repeated to him the story I had told him about my husband. He said: "Stay in your house until the prescribed term reaches its end." She said: So I observed the waiting period there for four months and ten days. She said: When Uthman ibn Affan was caliph, he sent for me and asked me about this, and I told him, so he followed it and gave judgment accordingly [Muwatta', 2/591].

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i also transmitted it in the same way from the hadith of Malik [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2300; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1204; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11044]. Al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah also transmitted it through various chains from Sa'd ibn Ishaq [Sunan al-Nasa'i, 6/199, 200; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2031]. Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih (good and authentic).

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verses 243–245 (part 1 of 2):

It is narrated from Ibn Abbas that they were four thousand. And from him: they were eight thousand. Abu Salih said: nine thousand. And from Ibn Abbas: forty thousand. Wahb ibn Munabbih and Abu Malik said: they were a few more than thirty thousand. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: they were people of a village called Dawardan. Al-Suddi and Abu Salih said likewise, and Abu Salih added: "from the direction of Wasit." Sa'id ibn Abd al-Aziz said: they were from the people of Adhri'at. Ibn Jurayj narrated from Ata, who said: "This is a parable." Ali ibn Asim said: they were from the people of Dawardan, a village one farsakh from Wasit.

Waki' ibn al-Jarrah said in his Tafsir: Sufyan narrated to us from Maysara ibn Habib al-Nahdi, from al-Minhal ibn Amr al-Asadi, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse ﴿Have you not seen those who went out of their homes, and they were thousands, fearing death?﴾. He said: They were four thousand who left, fleeing from the plague. They said: "We will go to a land where there is no death." When they reached a certain place, Allah said to them: "Die," and they died. Then a prophet passed by them and supplicated his Lord to revive them, and He revived them. That is the meaning of His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Have you not seen those who went out of their homes, and they were thousands, fearing death?﴾ to the end of the verse.

Many of the early generations (al-Salaf) mentioned that these people were the inhabitants of a town in the time of the Children of Israel. They found their land unwholesome, and a severe pestilence afflicted them there, so they went out into the wilderness fleeing from death. They settled in a vast valley and filled the space between its two slopes. Allah sent to them two angels, one from the lower part of the valley and the other from its upper part, and they cried out to them with a single cry, and they all died together, as one man dies. They were gathered into enclosures, walls were built around them, and they became graves. They decayed and were scattered. After a long time, a prophet of the Children of Israel named Hizqil passed by them, and he asked Allah to revive them at his hands. He was granted this, and he was commanded to say: "O bones, decayed, Allah commands you to come together." The bones of each body came together, one to another. Then he was commanded to call out: "O bones, Allah commands you to be clothed with flesh, sinews and skin." That came to pass while he was witnessing it. Then he was commanded to call out: "O souls, Allah commands you that each soul return to the body it used to inhabit." They rose up alive, looking around, for Allah had revived them after their long sleep, and they were saying: "Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You. There is no god but You."

In their revival there was a lesson and a decisive proof of the occurrence of the bodily resurrection (al-ma'ad al-jismani) on the Day of Resurrection. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward mankind﴾, that is, in what He shows them of striking signs, conclusive proofs and decisive indications. ﴿But most of mankind do not give thanks﴾, that is, they do not perform the thanks due for what Allah has bestowed upon them in their religion and their worldly life.

In this story there is a lesson and an indication that caution does not avail against decree, and that there is no refuge from Allah except in Him. These people fled from the plague seeking a long life, so they were treated contrary to their intention, and death came upon them swiftly, all at once.

Of this kind is the authentic hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Ishaq ibn Isa narrated to us, Malik and Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar informed us, both of them from al-Zuhri, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn al-Khattab, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal, from Abdullah ibn Abbas: that Umar ibn al-Khattab set out for Syria, and when he reached Sargh, the commanders of the armies, Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah and his companions, met him and informed him that the plague had broken out in Syria. He then mentioned the hadith. Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf came to him, having been absent on some errand, and said: "I have knowledge of this. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'If it breaks out in a land while you are in it, do not leave fleeing from it, and if you hear of it in a land, do not enter upon it.'" Umar praised Allah and then turned back.

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it in their Sahihs through the hadith of al-Zuhri with the same chain.

Another route for part of it: Ahmad said: Hajjaj and Yazid al-Ammi narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Abi Dhi'b informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from Abdullah ibn Amir ibn Rabi'a, that Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf informed Umar, while he was in Syria, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "This affliction was a punishment with which earlier nations were tormented. So when you hear of it in a land, do not enter it, and when it breaks out in a land while you are in it, do not leave fleeing from it." He said: Umar then returned from Syria.

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it in their Sahihs through the hadith of Malik, from al-Zuhri, with similar wording.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And fight in the way of Allah, and know that Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾, that is: just as caution does not avail against decree, likewise fleeing from jihad and avoiding it does not bring a term nearer nor push it further away. Rather, the appointed term and the apportioned provision are decreed and fixed, neither increased nor decreased, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Those who said of their brothers while they sat [at home], "If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed." Say: "Then avert from yourselves death, if you should be truthful."﴾ [Al 'Imran: 168] And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they say, "Our Lord, why have You decreed upon us fighting? Why did You not delay us to a near term?" Say: "The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah, and you will not be wronged a whit. Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you should be in fortified towers."﴾ [An-Nisa': 77–78]

And we have related from the commander of the armies, the leader of the troops, the defender of the frontier of Islam, the drawn sword of Allah against His enemies, Abu Sulayman Khalid ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said, while in the throes of death: "I have witnessed such-and-such a number of battles, and there is not a single limb of my body without a mark of an arrow, a stab or a blow. And here I am, dying on my bed as a camel dies! May the eyes of cowards not sleep!" [Note: see Mukhtasar Tarikh Dimashq by Ibn Manzur (8/26).] He means that he was pained that he did not die a martyr in battle, and he grieved over it, feeling anguish that he should die on his bed.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan so He will multiply it for him many times over?﴾ He, the Exalted, urges His servants to spend in His way, and He has repeated this verse in His Mighty Book in more than one place. In the hadith of the descent [of the Lord], it is said: "He, the Exalted, says: 'Whoever lends to one who is neither poor nor unjust...'" Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan ibn Arafa narrated to us, Khalaf ibn Khalifa narrated to us, from Humayd al-A'raj, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: When the verse ﴿Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan so He will multiply it for him﴾ was revealed, Abu al-Dahdah al-Ansari said: "O Messenger of Allah, does Allah really want a loan from us?" He said: "Yes, O Abu al-Dahdah." He said: "Show me your hand, O Messenger of Allah." So he gave him his hand. He said: "I have lent my orchard to my Lord." He had an orchard in which there were six hundred palm trees, and Umm al-Dahdah and her children lived in it. He said: Abu al-Dahdah came and called out: "O Umm al-Dahdah!" She said: "At your service." He said: "Leave, for I have lent it to my Lord, Mighty and Majestic." Ibn Marduwayh also narrated it from the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Umar, in a marfu' form, with similar wording. [Note: Juz' al-Hasan ibn Arafa, no. (87); Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated it in his Sunan, no. (417), ed. Dr. al-Hamid; and al-Tabarani narrated it through Khalaf in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (22/301) with similar wording. Humayd al-A'raj is weak, but the hadith has corroborating reports from the hadith of Anas and Umar, may Allah be pleased with them.]

* *

As for His words: ﴿a goodly loan﴾, it has been related from Umar and others among the early generations that it means spending in the way of Allah. It has also been said that it means spending on one's dependents. And it has been said that it means glorifying and sanctifying (Allah). As for His words: ﴿so He will multiply it for him many times over﴾, this is like His saying: ﴿The parable of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a seed that grows seven spikes, in each spike a hundred grains﴾ to the end of the verse [Al-Baqarah: 261]. Its discussion will come later.

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid [ibn Harun] narrated to us, Mubarak ibn Fadala informed us, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, who said: I came to Abu Hurayra and said to him: "It has reached me that you say that a good deed is multiplied a thousand thousand times." He said: "And what amazes you about that? I heard it from the Prophet (ﷺ) saying: 'Allah multiplies a good deed two thousand thousand times.'" [Note: al-Musnad (2/296).]

This is a gharib hadith, and Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an has munkar reports. However, Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through another route, saying:

Abu Khallad Sulayman ibn Khallad al-Mu'addib narrated to us, Yunus ibn Muhammad al-Mu'addib narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Uqba al-Ruba'i [note: thus in manuscripts A, W and H. In al-Jarh of Ibn Abi Hatim (4/1/36): "Muhammad ibn Uqba, narrated from Ziyad al-Jassas, and Yunus ibn Muhammad al-Mu'addib narrated from him. Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: I asked my father about him, and he said: 'A shaykh.' I said: 'Yunus ibn Muhammad says: al-Rifa'i.' He said: 'He is not al-Rifa'i; he is from another tribe.'" Taken from the margin of the Shu'ayb edition.], from Ziyad al-Jassas, from Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, who said: No one sat with Abu Hurayra more than I did. He travelled to Hajj before me, and I came after him, and I found the people of Basra relating from him that he said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Allah multiplies a good deed a thousand thousand good deeds.'" I said: "Woe to you! By Allah, no one sat with Abu Hurayra more than I did, and I did not hear this hadith." He said: So I prepared myself, wanting to catch up with him. I found that he had set out for Hajj, so I set out for Hajj to meet him about this hadith. I met him and said: "O Abu Hurayra, what is this hadith that I heard the people of Basra relating from you?" He said: "What is it?" I said: "They claim that you say: 'Allah multiplies a good deed a thousand thousand good deeds.'" He said: "O Abu Uthman, why are you surprised at this? Allah says: ﴿Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan so He will multiply it for him many times over﴾, and He says: ﴿Then the enjoyment of worldly life, compared to the Hereafter, is but little﴾ [At-Tawbah: 38]. By the One in whose hand is my soul, I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Allah multiplies a good deed two thousand thousand good deeds.'" [Note: also narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (5/521) through Ali ibn Zayd, from Abu Uthman, with the same wording.]

In the meaning of this hadith is what al-Tirmidhi and others narrated through the route of Amr ibn Dinar, from Salim, from Abdullah ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever enters one of the markets and says: 'There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. To Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs all praise, and He is over all things capable,' Allah writes for him a thousand thousand good deeds and erases from him a thousand thousand sins..." and the hadith continues. [Note: Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3429). He said: "Amr ibn Dinar here is a Basran shaykh, and some people of hadith have spoken about him from other than this route."]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'a narrated to us: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim ibn Bassam narrated to us: Abu Isma'il al-Mu'addib narrated to us, from Isa ibn al-Musayyab, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: When the verse ﴿The likeness of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that grows seven spikes﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:261] was revealed, to its end, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "My Lord, increase my ummah." Then this was revealed: ﴿Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan so that He multiplies it for him many times over?﴾ He said: "My Lord, increase my ummah." Then this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account﴾ [az-Zumar 39:10]. [[Ibn Hibban also narrated it in his Sahih, no. (1648) in al-Mawarid, through the route of Hafs al-Muqri', from Abu Isma'il al-Mu'addib with the same chain.]]

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from Ka'b al-Ahbar that a man came to him and said: "I heard a man say: whoever recites ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ [al-Ikhlas 112:1] once, Allah will build for him ten thousand thousand [[In (ج) it reads: "ten"]] chambers of pearls and rubies in Paradise. [Note: Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3429). He said: "Amr ibn Dinar here is a Basran shaykh, and some people of hadith have spoken about him from other than this route."]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'a narrated to us: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim ibn Bassam narrated to us: Abu Isma'il al-Mu'addib narrated to us, from Isa ibn al-Musayyab, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: When the verse ﴿The likeness of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that grows seven spikes﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:261] was revealed, to its end, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "My Lord, increase my ummah." Then this was revealed: ﴿Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan so that He multiplies it for him many times over?﴾ He said: "My Lord, increase my ummah." Then this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account﴾ [az-Zumar 39:10]. [[Ibn Hibban also narrated it in his Sahih, no. (1648) in al-Mawarid, through the route of Hafs al-Muqri', from Abu Isma'il al-Mu'addib with the same chain.]]

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from Ka'b al-Ahbar that a man came to him and said: "I heard a man say: whoever recites ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ [al-Ikhlas 112:1] once, Allah will build for him ten thousand thousand [[In (ج) it reads: "ten"]] chambers of pearls and rubies in Paradise. Shall I believe that?" He said: "Yes, or are you amazed at that?" He said: "Yes." Ka'b said: "Twenty thousand thousand and thirty thousand thousand, and none can count that except Allah." Then he recited ﴿Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan so that He multiplies it for him many times over?﴾ and said: "The abundance from Allah cannot be counted."

* *

As for His saying ﴿And Allah withholds and extends﴾, meaning: spend and do not worry, for Allah is the Provider. He restricts the provision of whom He wills of His servants and expands it for others, and He has perfect wisdom in that. ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 246:

'Abd al-Razzaq related from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: "This prophet is Yusha' ibn Nun (Joshua son of Nun)." Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: "That is, Ibn Afra'thim [[In manuscript ج: "Ifra'thim"; in manuscript أ: "Ibrahim".]] ibn Yusuf ibn Ya'qub." This opinion is far-fetched, because this occurred a long time after Musa (Moses), and it took place in the time of Dawud (David), peace be upon him, as is stated explicitly in the story. Between Dawud and Musa there was a span of more than a thousand years, and Allah knows best.

Al-Suddi said: "He is Sham'un [[In manuscript و: "Shamwil".]]." Mujahid said: "He is Shamwil, peace be upon him." Muhammad ibn Ishaq likewise related from Wahb ibn Munabbih, and he is: Shamwil ibn Bali ibn 'Alqamah ibn Yarkham [[In manuscript ج: "Ham"; in manuscript و: "Nazkham".]] ibn Ilihu ibn Tahu ibn Suf [[In manuscript ج: "Qahuas"; in manuscript أ: "Qahras"; in manuscript و: "Bahras".]] ibn 'Alqamah ibn Mahith [[In manuscript أ: "Ibn Mahib".]] ibn 'Amarsa ibn 'Izriya ibn Safniyah [[In manuscripts ج and و: "ibn Safiyah".]] ibn 'Alqamah ibn Abi Yasif ibn Qarun ibn Yasahar ibn Qahath ibn Lawi ibn Ya'qub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Khalil (Abraham the Friend of Allah), peace be upon him.

Wahb ibn Munabbih and others said: After Musa, peace be upon him, the Children of Israel remained on the path of uprightness for a period of time. Then they introduced innovations, and some of them worshipped idols. Among them there continued to be prophets who commanded them to do good and forbade them from evil, and who kept them upon the methods of the Tawrah (the Torah), until they did what they did. Then Allah empowered their enemies over them, and they killed a great slaughter among them, captured a multitude of people, and seized many of their lands. No one fought against them without defeating him, because they had the Tawrah and the Tabut (the Ark) that had been handed down from ancient times, passed from their successors to their predecessors, going back to Musa al-Kalim (Moses the one who spoke with Allah), upon him be the best of prayers and peace. Their persistence in misguidance continued until some of the kings seized it from them during some of the wars, took the Tawrah from their hands, and none remained among them who could preserve it except a few. Prophethood ceased among their tribes, and none remained of the tribe of Lawi, in which the prophets were, except a pregnant woman whose husband had been killed. They took her and imprisoned her in a house and guarded her, hoping that Allah would grant her a boy who would become a prophet for them. The woman continued to call upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to grant her a boy, and Allah heard her and gave her a boy. She named him Shamwil, meaning: Allah heard. Some say Sham'un, which has the same meaning. That boy grew up and was raised among them, and Allah caused him to grow well. When he reached the age of prophets, Allah revealed to him and commanded him to call to Him and to His Oneness. He called the Children of Israel, and they asked him to appoint for them a king under whose leadership they could fight their enemies, for kingship had also been lost among them [[In manuscript ج: "from them".]]. The prophet said to them: "Would you perhaps, if Allah appoints a king for you, refrain from fulfilling the obligation to fight alongside him?" ﴿They said: "What is the matter with us that we should not fight in the way of Allah, when we have been expelled from our homes and our children?"﴾ That is, our lands have been taken from us and our children have been taken captive. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Then when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, except for a few of them. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾ That is, they did not fulfil what they had promised. Rather, most of them shrank back from jihad, and Allah knows them well.

Namely: when they asked their prophet to appoint a king over them from among them, he appointed Talut (Saul) for them. He was a man from their soldiers, and he was not from the royal house among them, because kingship among them was in the tribe of Judah (Yahudha), and he was not from that tribe. Therefore they said: ﴿How can he have kingship over us?﴾ That is, how can he be a king over us? ﴿While we have more right to kingship than he, and he has not been given abundance of wealth.﴾ That is, moreover, despite this he is poor and has no wealth with which to sustain kingship. Some of them mentioned that he was a water-carrier, and it was said he was a tanner. This was an objection from them to their prophet and a stubborn challenge, whereas it would have been more fitting for them to show obedience and speak in a good manner. Then the Prophet answered them, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you﴾, that is, He selected him for you from among you, and Allah knows better than you who is worthy of it. He means: it is not I who appointed him of my own accord; rather Allah commanded me concerning him when you asked me for that. ﴿And He has increased him broadly in knowledge and stature.﴾ That is, despite this he is more knowledgeable than you, and more noble and more handsome than you, and stronger and more patient in war, and more knowledgeable in it; that is, more complete in knowledge and bearing than you. From here it follows that the king should possess knowledge, good appearance, and great strength in his body and soul. Then He said: ﴿And Allah gives His kingship to whom He wills.﴾ That is, He is the Judge who does whatever He wills, and He is not questioned about what He does, whereas they will be questioned, owing to His knowledge [and His wisdom] and His compassion toward His creation. Therefore He said: ﴿And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.﴾ That is, He is vast in bounty, bestowing His mercy specially on whom He wills, and He is All-Knowing of who deserves kingship and who does not.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 248:

Their prophet said to them: The sign of the blessing of Talut's (Saul's) kingship over you is that Allah will return to you the Ark (al-tabut) that was taken from you.

﴿In it is tranquillity (sakinah) from your Lord.﴾ It was said: its meaning is in it is dignity (waqar) and majesty (jalalah).

ʿAbd al-Razzaq related from Ma'mar from Qatadah: ﴿In it is tranquillity﴾ means dignity (waqar). Al-Rabi' said: mercy (rahmah). The same was related from al-ʿAwfi from Ibn ʿAbbas. Ibn Jurayj said: I asked ʿAta' about His saying: ﴿In it is tranquillity [from your Lord]﴾, and he said: what they recognize of the signs of Allah, so that they find rest in it.

It was also said: the sakinah is a golden basin in which the hearts of the prophets were washed. Allah gave it to Musa, peace be upon him, and he placed the tablets in it. al-Suddi related it from Abu Malik from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Sufyan al-Thawri said: from Salamah ibn Kuhayl from Abu al-Ahwas from ʿAli, who said: the sakinah has a face like the face of a human, and then it is a light, gentle wind (ruh haffafah).

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, Abu Dawud narrated to us, Shu'bah and Hammad ibn Salamah, and Abu al-Ahwas, all of them from Simak from Khalid ibn ʿUrʿurah from ʿAli, who said: the sakinah is a wind that is ... (khajuj) and it has two heads.

Mujahid said: it has two wings and a tail. Muhammad ibn Ishaq related from Wahb ibn Munabbih: the sakinah is the head of a dead cat which, when it cries out inside the ark with the cry of a cat, they were certain of victory and the conquest came to them.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq said: Bakkar ibn ʿAbd Allah informed us that he heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: the sakinah is a spirit from Allah that speaks; when they disagreed about something, it spoke and informed them of the clarification of what they wanted.

* *

His saying: ﴿And the remnant of what the family of Musa and the family of Harun left behind﴾. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn al-Muthanna informed us, Abu al-Walid narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us from Dawud ibn Abi Hind from ʿIkrimah from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding this verse: ﴿And the remnant of what the family of Musa and the family of Harun left behind﴾, he said: his staff and the shattered pieces of the tablets. Qatadah, al-Suddi, al-Rabi' ibn Anas and ʿIkrimah said likewise, and ʿIkrimah added: and the Torah.

Abu Salih said: ﴿The remnant﴾ means: the staff of Musa, the staff of Harun, two tablets of the Torah, and the manna.

ʿAtiyyah ibn Sa'd said: the staff of Musa, the staff of Harun, the garments of Musa, the garments of Harun, and the shattered pieces of the tablets.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq said: I asked al-Thawri about His saying: ﴿And the remnant of what the family of Musa and the family of Harun left behind﴾, and he said: among them are those who say a qafiz of manna, and the shattered pieces of the tablets; and among them are those who say: the staff and the two sandals.

* *

His saying: ﴿Carried by the angels﴾. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: the angels came carrying the ark between heaven and earth until they placed it before Talut, while the people were watching.

al-Suddi said: the ark appeared in the house of Talut, and they believed in the prophethood of Shamʿun and obeyed Talut.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq related from al-Thawri from some of his shaykhs: the angels brought it driving it on a cart drawn by a cow; it was also said: by two cows.

Others mentioned that the ark had been at Jericho (Ariha), and when the polytheists took it, they placed it in the house of their gods beneath their great idol. The ark was then found atop the idol, so they took it down and placed it beneath it, and it was so again; they nailed it beneath it, and the idol was found with its legs broken, cast far away. They knew that this was a matter from Allah against which they had no power, so they removed the ark from their land and placed it in one of the villages. Its people were afflicted with a disease in their necks, and a slave girl from the captives of the Children of Israel instructed them to return it to the Children of Israel so that they would be freed from this disease. They loaded it onto two cows, and the two cows set off with it; no one came near it without dying, until they drew near the land of the Children of Israel, whereupon the two cows broke their yokes and returned. The Children of Israel came and took it. It was said: Dawud, peace be upon him, received it, and when he rose toward the two of them, he leapt with joy at this. It was also said: two young men from among them; Allah knows best. It was also said: the ark was in a village of the villages of Palestine called Azdurd.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for you﴾, that is: a proof of my truthfulness in what I have brought you of prophethood, and in what I have commanded you of obedience to Talut: ﴿if you are believers﴾, that is, in Allah and the Last Day.

Allah, the Exalted, says, reporting about Talut (Saul), king of the Children of Israel, when he went out with his armies and those of the notables of the Children of Israel who obeyed him. His army on that day, according to what as-Suddi mentioned, was eighty thousand, but Allah knows best. He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is going to test you with a river﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and others said: it is a river between Jordan and Palestine, namely the well-known River Shari'ah (the Jordan River). ﴿Whoever drinks from it is not of me﴾, meaning: he shall not accompany me today on this expedition. ﴿And whoever does not taste it is of me, except one who scoops up a handful with his hand﴾, meaning: there is no blame upon him. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So they drank from it, except a few of them﴾. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said: whoever scooped from it with his hand was satisfied, and whoever drank from it directly was not satisfied. Likewise, as-Suddi narrated it from Abu Malik, from Ibn 'Abbas. Qatadah and Ibn Shawdhab also said the same.

As-Suddi said: the army was eighty thousand, and seventy-six thousand of them drank, and four thousand remained with him. So he said, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Jarir narrated through the chains of Israel, Sufyan ath-Thawri and Mis'ar ibn Kidam, from Abu Ishaq as-Sabi'i, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: "We used to say that the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ) who were at Badr were three hundred and some ten, equal to the number of the companions of Talut who crossed the river with him, and none crossed with him except a believer."

Al-Bukhari narrated it from 'Abdullah ibn Raja', from Isra'il ibn Yunus, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: "We, the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), used to say that the number of the companions of Badr was equal to the number of the companions of Talut who crossed the river with him, and none crossed with him except a believer: ten and three hundred."

Then he narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ath-Thawri and Zuhayr, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', with similar wording.

For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So when he and those who believed with him had crossed it, they said, "We have no power today against Goliath and his soldiers"﴾, meaning: they considered themselves too few to face their enemy because of their numbers. Their scholars, who knew that Allah's promise is true, encouraged them, for victory is from Allah, not by the abundance of numbers nor by the quantity of equipment. For this reason they said: ﴿How many a small company has overcome a large company by the permission of Allah. And Allah is with the patient﴾.

Namely: when the party of faith, who were few, from the companions of Talut, confronted their enemy, the companions of Jalut, who were a great host, they said: ﴿Our Lord, pour upon us patience﴾, that is, send down upon us patience from You; ﴿and make our feet firm﴾, that is, in meeting the enemy, and keep us from fleeing and weakness; ﴿and help us against the disbelieving people﴾.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So they routed them by Allah's permission﴾, that is, they overcame and subdued them by Allah's help for them. ﴿And Dawud killed Jalut﴾. They mention in the Isra'iliyyat (narrations from the Israelites) that he killed him with a sling (miqla') that was in his hand; he threw it at him, it struck him, and he killed him. Talut had promised him that if he killed Jalut he would marry him to his daughter, share his wealth with him, and make him a partner in his affairs. He fulfilled this for him. Then the kingship passed to Dawud, peace be upon him, together with what Allah granted him of great prophethood. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah gave him the kingship﴾, which had been in the hand of Talut, ﴿and the wisdom﴾, that is, prophethood after Shmuel (Samuel), ﴿and taught him of what He willed﴾, that is, of the knowledge which Allah willed and which He singled him out with (ﷺ). Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And were it not that Allah repels some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted﴾, that is, were it not that He repels from one people by means of another, as He repelled from the Children of Israel by the fighting of Talut and the bravery of Dawud, they would have been destroyed, as He said: ﴿And were it not that Allah repels some people by means of others, there would have been demolished monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques in which the name of Allah is much mentioned﴾ [al-Hajj: 40].

Ibn Jarir said, may Allah have mercy on him: Abu Humayd al-Himsi Ahmad ibn al-Mughira narrated to me, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Hafs ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Suqa, from Wabara ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah repels by means of a righteous Muslim the calamity from a hundred households of his neighbours." Then Ibn Umar recited: ﴿And were it not that Allah repels some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted﴾. [Tafsir al-Tabari (5/374)]. This chain is weak, for Yahya ibn Sa'id [here] [addition from A and W] is Abu Zakariyya al-Attar al-Himsi, and he is extremely weak.

Then Ibn Jarir said: Abu Humayd al-Himsi narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Uthman ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah sets right through the righteousness of a Muslim man his child, the child of his child, the people of his dwelling and the dwellings around him, and they will continue in the protection of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as long as he is among them." [Tafsir al-Tabari (5/375)].

This too is strange and weak, for the same reason as before. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim informed us, Ali ibn Isma'il ibn Hammad informed us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id informed us, Zayd ibn al-Hubab informed us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilaba, from Abu Asma' [in C: "Ibn Abi Usama"], from Thawban, raising the hadith, who said: "There will always remain among you seven by whom you are helped, by whom you are given rain, and by whom you are provided for, until the command of Allah comes." [It was also narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf (no. 20457) from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilaba, as a mursal report.]

Ibn Mardawayh also said: And Muhammad ibn Ahmad [in C: "and Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated to us"] narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Jarir ibn Yazid narrated to us, Abu Mu'adh Nahar ibn Uthman al-Laythi narrated to us, Zayd ibn al-Hubab informed us, Umar al-Bazzar informed me, from Anbasa al-Khawass, from Qatada, from Abu Qilaba, from Abu al-Ash'ath al-San'ani, from Ubada ibn al-Samit, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Abdal (substitutes) in my Ummah are thirty; by them the earth stands, by them you are given rain, and by them you are helped." Qatada said: "I indeed hope that al-Hasan is among them." [It was narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir through the route of Muhammad ibn al-Faraj from Zayd ibn al-Hubab with it. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/63): "al-Tabarani narrated it through Amr al-Bazzar from Anbasa al-Khawass, and both of them I do not know; the rest of its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]

Benefit: Imam Ibn al-Qayyim said in al-Manar al-Munif (p. 136): "The hadiths about the Abdal, the Aqtab, the Aghwath, the Nuqaba', the Nujaba' and the Awtad are all false upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The closest of them is: 'Do not revile the people of Sham, for among them are the Abdal; whenever a man among them dies, Allah replaces him with another man.' Ahmad mentioned it, but it is not authentic either, for it is disconnected (munqati')."

* *

His saying: ﴿But Allah is full of bounty to the worlds﴾, that is, He is gracious to them and merciful to them, repelling by means of some of them the harm of others; to Him belong the command, the wisdom, and the proof over His creation in all His actions and sayings.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿These are the verses of Allah, which We recite to you in truth, and indeed you are among the messengers﴾, that is, these are the verses of Allah which We have related to you concerning the matter of those We have mentioned, in truth, that is, in accordance with the reality of the matter, matching what the People of the Book possess of the truth which the scholars of the Children of Israel know. ﴿And indeed you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿are among the messengers﴾. This is an emphasis and a preface to an oath.

His saying: ﴿But Allah is full of bounty to the worlds﴾, that is, He is gracious to them and merciful to them, repelling by means of some of them the harm of others; to Him belong the command, the wisdom, and the proof over His creation in all His actions and sayings.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿These are the verses of Allah, which We recite to you in truth, and indeed you are among the messengers﴾, that is, these are the verses of Allah which We have related to you concerning the matter of those We have mentioned, in truth, that is, in accordance with the reality of the matter, matching what the People of the Book possess of the truth which the scholars of the Children of Israel know. ﴿And indeed you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿are among the messengers﴾. This is an emphasis and a preface to an oath.

Namely: when the party of faith, who were few, from the companions of Talut, confronted their enemy, the companions of Jalut, who were a great host, they said: ﴿Our Lord, pour upon us patience﴾, that is, send down upon us patience from You; ﴿and make our feet firm﴾, that is, in meeting the enemy, and keep us from fleeing and weakness; ﴿and help us against the disbelieving people﴾.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So they routed them by Allah's permission﴾, that is, they overcame and subdued them by Allah's help for them. ﴿And Dawud killed Jalut﴾. They mention in the Isra'iliyyat (narrations from the Israelites) that he killed him with a sling (miqla') that was in his hand; he threw it at him, it struck him, and he killed him. Talut had promised him that if he killed Jalut he would marry him to his daughter, share his wealth with him, and make him a partner in his affairs. He fulfilled this for him. Then the kingship passed to Dawud, peace be upon him, together with what Allah granted him of great prophethood. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah gave him the kingship﴾, which had been in the hand of Talut, ﴿and the wisdom﴾, that is, prophethood after Shmuel (Samuel), ﴿and taught him of what He willed﴾, that is, of the knowledge which Allah willed and which He singled him out with (ﷺ). Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And were it not that Allah repels some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted﴾, that is, were it not that He repels from one people by means of another, as He repelled from the Children of Israel by the fighting of Talut and the bravery of Dawud, they would have been destroyed, as He said: ﴿And were it not that Allah repels some people by means of others, there would have been demolished monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques in which the name of Allah is much mentioned﴾ [al-Hajj: 40].

Ibn Jarir said, may Allah have mercy on him: Abu Humayd al-Himsi Ahmad ibn al-Mughira narrated to me, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Hafs ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Suqa, from Wabara ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah repels by means of a righteous Muslim the calamity from a hundred households of his neighbours." Then Ibn Umar recited: ﴿And were it not that Allah repels some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted﴾. [Tafsir al-Tabari (5/374)]. This chain is weak, for Yahya ibn Sa'id [here] [addition from A and W] is Abu Zakariyya al-Attar al-Himsi, and he is extremely weak.

Then Ibn Jarir said: Abu Humayd al-Himsi narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Uthman ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah sets right through the righteousness of a Muslim man his child, the child of his child, the people of his dwelling and the dwellings around him, and they will continue in the protection of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as long as he is among them." [Tafsir al-Tabari (5/375)].

This too is strange and weak, for the same reason as before. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim informed us, Ali ibn Isma'il ibn Hammad informed us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id informed us, Zayd ibn al-Hubab informed us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilaba, from Abu Asma' [in C: "Ibn Abi Usama"], from Thawban, raising the hadith, who said: "There will always remain among you seven by whom you are helped, by whom you are given rain, and by whom you are provided for, until the command of Allah comes." [It was also narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf (no. 20457) from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilaba, as a mursal report.]

Ibn Mardawayh also said: And Muhammad ibn Ahmad [in C: "and Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated to us"] narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Jarir ibn Yazid narrated to us, Abu Mu'adh Nahar ibn Uthman al-Laythi narrated to us, Zayd ibn al-Hubab informed us, Umar al-Bazzar informed me, from Anbasa al-Khawass, from Qatada, from Abu Qilaba, from Abu al-Ash'ath al-San'ani, from Ubada ibn al-Samit, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Abdal (substitutes) in my Ummah are thirty; by them the earth stands, by them you are given rain, and by them you are helped." Qatada said: "I indeed hope that al-Hasan is among them." [It was narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir through the route of Muhammad ibn al-Faraj from Zayd ibn al-Hubab with it. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/63): "al-Tabarani narrated it through Amr al-Bazzar from Anbasa al-Khawass, and both of them I do not know; the rest of its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]

Benefit: Imam Ibn al-Qayyim said in al-Manar al-Munif (p. 136): "The hadiths about the Abdal, the Aqtab, the Aghwath, the Nuqaba', the Nujaba' and the Awtad are all false upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The closest of them is: 'Do not revile the people of Sham, for among them are the Abdal; whenever a man among them dies, Allah replaces him with another man.' Ahmad mentioned it, but it is not authentic either, for it is disconnected (munqati')."

* *

His saying: ﴿But Allah is full of bounty to the worlds﴾, that is, He is gracious to them and merciful to them, repelling by means of some of them the harm of others; to Him belong the command, the wisdom, and the proof over His creation in all His actions and sayings.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿These are the verses of Allah, which We recite to you in truth, and indeed you are among the messengers﴾, that is, these are the verses of Allah which We have related to you concerning the matter of those We have mentioned, in truth, that is, in accordance with the reality of the matter, matching what the People of the Book possess of the truth which the scholars of the Children of Israel know. ﴿And indeed you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿are among the messengers﴾. This is an emphasis and a preface to an oath.

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 253:

He, exalted is He, informs that He preferred some of the Messengers over others, as He said: ﴿And We have certainly preferred some of the prophets over others, and We gave David the Zabur [Psalms]﴾ [al-Isra' 17:55]. And here He said: ﴿Those messengers, We preferred some of them over others. Among them are those to whom Allah spoke﴾, meaning Musa (Moses) and Muhammad (ﷺ). Likewise Adam, as is reported in the hadith narrated in Sahih Ibn Hibban from Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him). ﴿And He raised some of them in rank﴾, as is established in the hadith of the Isra' (Night Journey), when the Prophet (ﷺ) saw the prophets in the heavens, according to the differences in their ranks with Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

If it is said: what is the reconciliation between this verse and the hadith established in the two Sahihs from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A man from the Muslims and a man from the Jews quarrelled. The Jew said, in an oath he was swearing: "No, by the One who chose Musa above the worlds." The Muslim raised his hand and slapped the Jew's face, and said: "You wicked one! And [chose] Muhammad (ﷺ)!" The Jew came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and complained about the Muslim. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not prefer me over the prophets, for the people will be struck senseless on the Day of Resurrection, and I will be the first to regain consciousness, and I will find Musa grasping one of the pillars of the Throne. I will not know whether he regained consciousness before me or was recompensed with the swoon of Mount Sinai. So do not prefer me over the prophets." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3408) and Sahih Muslim no. (2373)]. And in another narration: "Do not make distinctions between the prophets."

The answer has several aspects:

First: that this was before he was informed of the preference. But in this there is scrutiny.

Second: that he said this out of humility and modesty.

Third: that this is a prohibition of preference in such a situation, in which they went to judgment during the dispute and the quarrel.

Fourth: do not prefer by mere opinions and partisanship.

Fifth: the station of preference is not up to you; it belongs to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and upon you is submission, surrender to Him, and belief in Him.

* *

His saying: ﴿And We gave Isa (Jesus), son of Maryam, the clear proofs﴾, meaning the decisive proofs and evidences for the truth of what he brought to the Children of Israel, that he is the servant of Allah and His Messenger to them. ﴿And We supported him with the Holy Spirit﴾, meaning that Allah strengthened him with Jibril (Gabriel), peace be upon him. Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if Allah had willed, those after them would not have fought one another after the clear proofs had come to them; but they differed, so some of them believed and some of them disbelieved. And if Allah had willed, they would not have fought one another; but Allah does what He intends﴾. That is: all of that is by the decree and destiny of Allah. Therefore He said: ﴿But Allah does what He intends﴾.

Allah commands His servants to spend from what He has provided them, in His way, the way of goodness, so that they may store up the reward of that with their Lord and Sovereign, and that they hasten to do so in this worldly life, ﴿before there comes a Day﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection, ﴿in which there is no trade, nor friendship, nor intercession﴾. That is: no one will be able to ransom himself, nor be redeemed by wealth even if he were to offer it, even if he came with the earth filled with gold; nor will anyone's friendship benefit him, meaning his friendship, nor even his kinship, as He said: ﴿And when the Trumpet is blown, there will be no kinship among them that Day, nor will they ask of one another﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 101]. ﴿Nor intercession﴾: that is, the intercession of intercessors will not benefit them.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And the disbelievers, they are the wrongdoers﴾, the subject (mubtada') here is restricted to its predicate (khabar), meaning: there is no one more wrongful than the one who meets Allah on that Day as a disbeliever. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from 'Ata' ibn Dinar that he said: "Praise be to Allah, who said: ﴿And the disbelievers, they are the wrongdoers﴾, and did not say: 'And the wrongdoers, they are the disbelievers.'"

This is the Verse of the Throne, and it has a great status. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has been authentically reported to have said that it is the best verse in the Book of Allah. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Sa'id al-Jurayri, from Abu al-Salil, from Abd Allah ibn Rabah, from Ubayy, that is Ibn Ka'b, that the Prophet ﷺ asked him: "Which verse in the Book of Allah is the greatest?" He said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He repeated the question several times, then Ubayy said: "The Verse of the Throne." He said: "May knowledge be pleasant for you, Abu al-Mundhir. By Him in whose hand my soul is, it has a tongue and two lips with which it sanctifies the King at the foot of the Throne." Muslim also narrated it from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Abd al-Ala ibn Abd al-Ala, from al-Jurayri with the same chain [[Al-Musnad (5/141) and Sahih Muslim, no. (810).]], but he does not have the addition: "By Him in whose hand my soul is..." etc.

Another narration from Ubayy also concerning the virtue of the Verse of the Throne. The hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi narrated to us, Mubashshir narrated to us, from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abdah ibn Abi Lubabah [[In manuscript C: "ibn Abi Kinanah".]], from Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that his father informed him that he had a storehouse containing dates. He said: Ubayy would check on it, and he found it decreasing. He said: So he kept watch over it one night, and suddenly there was a creature resembling a grown youth. He said: I greeted it and it returned the greeting. He said: I said: "What are you, a jinn or a human?" It said: "A jinn." I said: "Give me your hand." He said: It gave me its hand, and behold, its hand was the hand of a dog and its hair was dog's hair. I said: "Is this how the jinn are created?" It said: "The jinn know well that among them there is none stronger than me." I said: "What led you to do what you did?" It said: "I have heard that you are a man who loves giving charity, so we wanted to partake of your food." He said: Then he [[In manuscript A and W: "Then my father said to him."]] said: "What then protects us from you?" It said: "This verse: the Verse of the Throne." Then he went in the morning to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "The wicked one has spoken the truth."

This has also been narrated by al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, from Harb ibn Shaddad, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from al-Hadrami ibn Lahiq, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from his grandfather with the same [[Al-Mustadrak (1/562), and it contains a break in the chain. It has come through another route: Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih, no. (1724) "Mawarid", through al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from the son of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from his father Ka'b, that he informed him, and mentioned something similar.]]. He said: "Its chain is sound, but they did not record it."

Another route: Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Uthman ibn Ghiyath [[In manuscript A: "ibn Attab".]] narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu al-Salil say: "A man from the companions of the Prophet ﷺ used to narrate to people until they became numerous around him, and then he would climb onto the roof of a house and narrate to the people." He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Which verse in the Qur'an is the greatest?" A man said: ﴿Allah, there is no deity except Him﴾. He said: So he placed his hand between my shoulders, and I felt its coolness between my breasts, or he said: he placed his hand between my breasts and I felt its coolness between my shoulders, and he said: "May knowledge be pleasant for you, Abu al-Mundhir" [[Al-Musnad (5/58).]].

Another hadith: from al-Asfa' al-Bakri. The hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Abu Yazid al-Qaratisi narrated to us, Ya'qub ibn Abi Abbad al-Makki narrated to us, Muslim ibn Khalid narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj: Umar ibn Ata informed me that the client of Ibn al-Asfa', a truthful man, informed him, from al-Asfa' al-Bakri, that he heard him say: The Prophet ﷺ came to them in the Suffah of the Emigrants [[The Suffah was a shaded area of the Prophet's mosque where poor emigrants lived.]], and a man asked him: "Which verse in the Qur'an is the greatest?" The Prophet ﷺ said: ﴿Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Living, the Self-Subsisting. Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him﴾, until the end of the verse [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (1/334). Al-Haythami said in Al-Majma' (6/321): "It contains a narrator who was not named but was declared trustworthy, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy."]].

Another hadith: from Anas. Imam Ahmad said: Abd Allah ibn al-Harith narrated to us, Salamah ibn Wardan narrated to me, that Anas ibn Malik narrated to him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked a man from among his companions: "O so-and-so, have you married?" He said: "No, and I do not have what I could marry with." He said: "Do you not have: ﴿Say, He is Allah, One﴾?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an. Do you not have: ﴿Say, O disbelievers﴾?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an. Do you not have ﴿When the earth is shaken﴾?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an. Do you not have: ﴿When the help of Allah [and the victory] comes﴾?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an. Do you not have the Verse of the Throne: ﴿Allah, there is no deity except Him [the Living, the Self-Subsisting]﴾?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an" [[Al-Musnad (3/221).]].

Another hadith: from Abu Dharr Jundub ibn Junadah. Imam Ahmad said: Waki' ibn al-Jarrah narrated to us, al-Mas'udi narrated to us, Abu Umar al-Dimashqi informed me, from Ubayd ibn al-Khashkhash, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was in the mosque, and I sat down. He said: "O Abu Dharr, have you prayed?" I said: "No." He said: "Stand and pray." So I stood and prayed, then I sat. He said: "O Abu Dharr, seek refuge in Allah from the evil of the devils of mankind and the jinn." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, are there devils among mankind?" He said: "Yes." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about prayer?" He said: "The best matter: whoever wishes may do little, and whoever wishes may do much." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about fasting?" He said: "An obligation that suffices, and with Allah there is more." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about charity?" He said: "Multiplied many times over." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of these is best?" He said: "The effort of one who has little, or secret giving to a poor person." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of the prophets was first?" He said: "Adam." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, was he a prophet?" He said: "Yes, a prophet to whom Allah spoke directly." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, how many were the messengers?" He said: "Three hundred and some dozen, a great multitude," and once he said: "and fifteen." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of what was revealed to you is the greatest?" He said: "The Verse of the Throne: ﴿Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Living, the Self-Subsisting﴾." It was also narrated by al-Nasa'i [[Al-Musnad (5/178) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi (8/275).]].

Another hadith: from Abu Ayyub Khalid ibn Zayd al-Ansari, may Allah be pleased with him and satisfy him. Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us from Ibn Abi Layla, from his brother Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Abu Ayyub: that he spent the night in a storeroom [[In manuscript C: "that he spent the night".]] of his, and the ghul [[A ghul is a monstrous jinn-like creature that preys on people and travellers.]] used to come and take things, so he complained about it to the Prophet ﷺ. He said: "When you see it, say: 'In the name of Allah, answer the Messenger of Allah.'" He said: So it came, and he [the Prophet] said to it [Abu Ayyub]: So he seized it, and it said: "I will not return." So he released it. Then he came back, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "What did your prisoner do?" He said: "I seized it, and it said to me: 'I will not return, I will not return.' So I released it." The Prophet said: "It will return." He seized it two or three times, and each time it said: "I will not return." And I would come to the Prophet ﷺ, and he would say: "What did your prisoner do?" I would say: "I seized it, and it says: 'I will not return.'" He would say: "It will return." Then I seized it, and it said: "Release me, and I will teach you something to say, and nothing will come near you: the Verse of the Throne." So he came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him, and he said: "It has spoken the truth, though it is a liar" [[Al-Musnad (5/423).]].

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in the Virtues of the Qur'an from Bundar, from Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri, with the same, and said: "Hasan gharib" [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2880).]].

Al-Bukhari also mentioned this story from Abu Hurayrah. He mentioned it in the Book of "Virtues of the Qur'an," in the Book of "Agency," and in "The Description of Iblis" of his Sahih: Uthman ibn al-Haytham Abu Amr narrated to us, Awf narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entrusted me with guarding the zakat of Ramadan. A visitor came and began scooping food. I seized him and said: "I will certainly take you to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said: "I am needy, I have dependants, and I have a severe need." He said: So I let him go. In the morning the Prophet ﷺ said: "O Abu Hurayrah, what did your prisoner do last night?" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, he complained of a severe need and dependants, so I had mercy on him and let him go." He said: "As for him, he has lied to you, and he will return." So I knew he would return, because of the words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "He will return." So I watched for him, and he came scooping food. I seized him and said: "I will certainly take you to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said: "Leave me, for I am needy, I have dependants, and I will not return." So I had mercy on him and let him go. In the morning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "O Abu Hurayrah, what did your prisoner do last night?" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, he complained of need and dependants, so I had mercy on him and let him go." He said: "As for him, he has lied to you, and he will return." So I watched for him the third time, and he came scooping food. I seized him and said: "I will certainly take you to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. This is the third time, you claim you will not return, then you return." He said: "Leave me, and I will teach you words by which Allah will benefit you." I said: "What are they?" He said: "When you go to your bed, recite the Verse of the Throne: ﴿Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Living, the Self-Subsisting﴾ until you finish the verse, for there will always be a guardian from Allah over you, and no devil will come near you until morning." So I let him go. In the morning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "What did your prisoner do last night?" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, he claimed he would teach me words by which Allah would benefit me, so I let him go." He said: "What are they?" He said: "He said to me: 'When you go to your bed, recite the Verse of the Throne from its beginning until you finish the verse: ﴿Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Living, the Self-Subsisting﴾.' And he said to me: 'There will always be a guardian from Allah over you, and no devil will come near you until morning.'" They were the most eager of people for good. The Prophet ﷺ said: "He has indeed told you the truth, though he is a liar. Do you know who you have been addressing these three nights, O Abu Hurayrah?" I said: "No." He said: "That was a devil."

Thus al-Bukhari narrated it as a suspended narration [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (2311, 3275).]] in the form of a definite statement. Al-Nasa'i also narrated it in "Al-Yawm wa al-Laylah" from Ibrahim ibn Ya'qub, from Uthman ibn al-Haytham, and mentioned it [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (10795).]]. It has also been narrated through another route from Abu Hurayrah with a different wording close to this. The hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said in his Tafsir:

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 2, verse 255 (part 2 of 4):

Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Amrawayh al-Saffar narrated to us: Ahmad ibn Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Muslim ibn Ibrahim informed us: Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Abdi informed us: Abu al-Mutawakkil al-Naji informed us that Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) had the key to the storehouse of the charity (sadaqah), and in it there were dates. One day he went and opened the door and found that a handful of dates had been taken from it. He entered on another day and found that a handful had been taken. Then he entered on a third day and found that the same amount had been taken. Abu Hurayrah complained of this to the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Would you like to catch this companion of yours?" He said: "Yes." He said: "When you open the door, say: 'Glory be to the One who subjected you to Muhammad.'" So he went, opened the door, and said: "Glory be to the One who subjected you to Muhammad." Then, behold, the thief was standing before him. He said: "O enemy of Allah, are you the companion of this?" He said: "Yes. Leave me, for I will not return. I was only taking for a family among the jinn who are poor." So he released him, then he came back a second time, then a third time. I said: "Did you not promise me that you would not return?" He said: "I will not leave you today until I take you to the Prophet (ﷺ)." The jinn said: "Do not do that, for if you leave me I will teach you words which, when you say them, no one among the jinn, small or great, male or female, will come near you." He said to him: "Will you truly do it?" He said: "Yes." He said: "What are they?" He said: "Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence." He recited Ayat al-Kursi until he finished it. So he let him go, and he went off and kept away. Abu Hurayrah mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Did you not know that it was so?"

Al-Nasa'i also narrated it from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ubayd Allah, from Shu'ayb ibn Harb, from Isma'il ibn Muslim, from Abu al-Mutawakkil, from Abu Hurayrah, with this same wording. [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 10794.] A similar incident had already been related about Ubayy ibn Ka'b, so these are three incidents.

Another story: Abu Ubayd said in his book "al-Gharib": Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Abu Asim al-Thaqafi, from al-Sha'bi, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: A man from mankind went out and met a man from the jinn. The jinn said: "Would you wrestle with me? If you throw me down, I will teach you a verse which, when you recite it upon entering your house, no devil will enter." So he wrestled with him and threw him down. [In one version: "threw him down, Umar."] The jinn said: "I see you are slight and thin, as if your forearms were the forearms of a dog. Is this how you are, O jinn, all of you, or are you one of them?" The jinn said: "I am among them, and I am strong. Wrestle with me again." So he wrestled with him, and the human threw him down again. The jinn said: "Recite Ayat al-Kursi, for no one recites it upon entering his house except that the devil departs with a fart like the braying of a donkey."

It was said to Ibn Mas'ud: "Was it Umar?" He said: "Who else could it be but Umar?"

Abu Ubayd said: al-Dani'l (slight) means thin of body. Khabaj (with a dotted kha) is also said with an undotted ha, and it means flatulence.

Another hadith from Abu Hurayrah: Al-Hakim Abu Abd Allah said in his "al-Mustadrak": Ali ibn Hamshad narrated to us: Bishr ibn Musa narrated to us: al-Humaydi narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us: Hakim ibn Jubayr al-Asadi narrated to me, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Surat al-Baqarah contains a verse which is the chief of the verses of the Qur'an. It is not recited in a house in which there is a devil except that it leaves: it is Ayat al-Kursi."

He narrated it by another route from Za'idah, from Hakim ibn Jubayr, and then said: "Its isnad is sahih, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it." Thus he said. Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from the hadith of Za'idah, and its wording is: "Everything has a summit, and the summit of the Qur'an is Surat al-Baqarah, and in it is a verse which is the chief of the verses of the Qur'an: Ayat al-Kursi." Then he said: "Gharib (a hadith transmitted through a single narrator at some point in its chain), which we do not know except through the hadith of Hakim ibn Jubayr. Shu'bah spoke about it and weakened it." [Al-Mustadrak 2/259.]

I say: Ahmad, Yahya ibn Ma'in and many other imams likewise weakened it. Ibn Mahdi abandoned it, and al-Sa'di called him a liar.

Another hadith: Ibn Mardawayh said: Abd al-Baqi ibn Nafi narrated to us: Isa ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi informed us: Umar ibn Muhammad al-Bukhari informed us: my father informed us: Isa ibn Musa Ghunjar informed us, from Abd Allah ibn Kaysan: Yahya ibn Aqil informed us, from Yahya ibn Ya'mar, from Ibn Umar, from Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), that he went out one day to the people, and they were in circles. He said: "Which of you can tell me of the greatest verse in the Qur'an?" Ibn Mas'ud said: "You have fallen upon one who knows. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The greatest verse in the Qur'an is: Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence.'" [Al-Jawraqani narrated it in "al-Abatil", no. 712, by way of Isa ibn Musa Ghunjar.]

Another hadith concerning its containing the Greatest Name of Allah: Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us: Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad informed us: Shahr ibn Hawshab narrated to us, from Asma bint Yazid ibn al-Sakan, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say concerning these two verses: "Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence" and "Alif, Lam, Mim. Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence" (Aal Imran 3:1-2): "Indeed in them is the Greatest Name of Allah." [Al-Musnad 6/461.]

Likewise Abu Dawud narrated it from Musaddad, al-Tirmidhi from Ali ibn Khashram, and Ibn Majah from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, all three from Isa ibn Yunus, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad, with it. [Sunan Abi Dawud no. 1496; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3478; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 3855.] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih."

Another hadith with the same meaning, from Abu Umamah (may Allah be pleased with him): Ibn Mardawayh said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Numayr informed us: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Isma'il informed us: Hisham ibn Ammar informed us: al-Walid ibn Muslim informed us: Abd Allah ibn al-Ala ibn Zayd informed us that he heard al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman narrate from Abu Umamah, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "The Greatest Name of Allah, which when He is called upon by it, He answers, is in three surahs: Surat al-Baqarah, Aal Imran, and Ta-Ha." Hisham, who is Ibn Ammar, the preacher of Damascus, said: "As for al-Baqarah, it is: 'Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence.' In Aal Imran it is: 'Alif, Lam, Mim. Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence.' And in Ta-Ha it is: 'And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence' (Ta-Ha 20:111)."

Another hadith from Abu Umamah concerning its merit when recited after the obligatory prayer: Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Muharriz ibn Musawir al-Udami narrated to us: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed us: al-Husayn ibn Bishr in Tarsus informed us: Muhammad ibn Himyar informed us: Muhammad ibn Ziyad informed us, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi after every obligatory prayer, nothing will prevent him from entering Paradise except death."

Al-Nasa'i narrated it likewise in "al-Yawm wa al-Laylah" from al-Husayn ibn Bishr. [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 9928.] Ibn Hibban recorded it in his Sahih from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Himyar, who is al-Himsi and also among the narrators of al-Bukhari. So its isnad meets the conditions of al-Bukhari. Abu al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzi claimed that it is a fabricated hadith (mawdu'). Allah knows best.

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated, from the hadith of Ali [the hadith of Ali was also narrated by al-Bayhaqi in "Shu'ab al-Iman", no. 2395, by way of Nahshal, from Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani, from Habbah al-Urani, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him)], and al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah [the hadith of al-Mughirah was narrated by Abu Nu'aym in "al-Hilyah" 3/221, by way of Umar ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah (may Allah be pleased with him)], and Jabir ibn Abd Allah, something similar to this hadith. But in the isnad of each of them there is weakness.
