[Sahih Muslim, no. 106.]

Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn 'Uthman ibn Yahya narrated to us, 'Uthman ibn Muhammad al-Duri informed us, Hushaym ibn Kharijah informed us, Sulayman ibn 'Uqbah informed us, from Yunus ibn Maysarah, from Abu Idris, from Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "No disobedient child (of parents), no one who reminds of favours, and no habitual drinker of wine, nor one who denies divine decree, will enter Paradise." Ahmad and Ibn Majah narrated similarly from the narration of Yunus ibn Maysarah. [Musnad Ahmad (6/441) and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3376. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/103): "This chain is good; Sulayman ibn 'Utbah is disputed, and the rest of the narrators are trustworthy."]

Then Ibn Mardawayh, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim in his al-Mustadrak, and al-Nasa'i narrated from the narration of 'Abdullah ibn Yasar al-A'raj, from Salim ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Three, Allah will not look at them on the Day of Resurrection: the one who is disobedient to his parents, the habitual drinker of wine, and the one who reminds of what he has given." [al-Mustadrak (4/146) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (5/80).]

Al-Nasa'i narrated, from Malik ibn Sa'd, from his paternal uncle Rawh ibn 'Ubadah, from 'Attab ibn Bashir, from Khusayf al-Jazari, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "No habitual drinker of wine, no disobedient child, and no one who reminds of favours will enter Paradise." [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 4921.]

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this from al-Hasan ibn al-Minhal, from Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Ammar al-Mawsili, from 'Attab, from Khusayf, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas.

Al-Nasa'i narrated it from the narration of 'Abd al-Karim ibn Malik al-Jazari, from Mujahid, as his own statement. It has also been reported from Mujahid, from Abu Sa'id [al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 4920], and from Mujahid, from Abu Hurayrah, similarly [al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 4922].

For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not invalidate your charities with reminders and injury﴾. So He informed us that charity is nullified by what follows it of reminder and injury, for the reward of charity cannot withstand the sin of reminder and injury.

Then Almighty Allah said: ﴿like one who spends his wealth to be seen by the people﴾, meaning: do not nullify your charities with reminders and injury, just as the charity of one who does it to show off to people is nullified. He displays to them that he seeks the Face of Allah, while his real aim is the people's praise of him, or his fame for beautiful qualities, so that he is thanked among the people, or so it is said that he is generous, and similar worldly aims, while disregarding dealing with Allah the Exalted and seeking His pleasure and great reward. For this reason He said: ﴿and does not believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾.

Then Almighty Allah struck a parable for that showy person in his spending. [Al-Dahhak said: "And the one who follows his spending with reminder or injury."] He said: ﴿So his example is like that of a smooth rock﴾. Safwan is the plural of safwanah, and some say that safwan is also used in the singular, meaning a flat stone, which is a smooth rock. ﴿Upon it is dust, and then a heavy rain strikes it﴾, which is a violent downpour, ﴿and leaves it bare﴾, meaning the heavy rain leaves that rock bare, that is, smooth and dry, with nothing on it of that dust. Rather, all of it has gone. Likewise, the deeds of those who show off are lost and vanish in the sight of Allah, even if they appear to the people like dust. For this reason He said: ﴿They are unable to obtain anything of what they have earned. And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.﴾

And the example of those who spend their wealth seeking the approval of Allah (﷾) and as a firm affirmation from themselves [[ ... ]]

Here is the translation:

And the example of those who spend their wealth seeking the approval of Allah and as a firm affirmation from themselves (﴿وَتَثْبِيتًا مِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾): that is, they are certain and firmly convinced that Allah will reward them for it with the fullest reward. A parallel to this in meaning is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) in the hadith agreed upon as authentic: "Whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward..." That is, he believes that Allah has prescribed it, and seeks its reward from Allah.

Ash-Sha'bi said: "Tathbiten min anfusihim" means affirmation (tasdiq) and certainty (yaqin). Qatadah, Abu Salih and Ibn Zayd said likewise, and Ibn Jarir chose this view. Mujahid and al-Hasan said: it means they are careful about where they place their charity.

* *

His saying: "Like a garden on a height" (﴿كَمَثَلِ جَنَّةٍ بِرَبْوَةٍ﴾): that is, like a garden on a height. According to the majority, a "rabwah" is an elevated, level place of land. Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak added: "with rivers flowing through it."

Ibn Jarir said: For "rabwah" there are three dialectal forms, which are three recitations: with a dammah on the ra', which is the reading of the majority of the people of Madinah, the Hijaz and Iraq; with a fathah, which is the reading of some people of Syria and Kufa, and it is said to be the dialect of Tamim; and with a kasrah, which is reported to be the reading of Ibn Abbas.

* *

His saying: "It is struck by a heavy rain" (﴿أَصَابَهَا وَابِلٌ﴾): "wabil" is heavy rain, as mentioned earlier. "So it yields its produce" (﴿فَآتَتْ أُكُلَهَا﴾): that is, its fruit, "doubled" (﴿ضِعْفَيْنِ﴾): in comparison with other gardens. "But if heavy rain does not strike it, then a light rain" (﴿فَإِنْ لَمْ يُصِبْهَا وَابِلٌ فَطَلٌّ﴾). Al-Dahhak said: "tall" is "al-radhadh," which is the gentle kind of rain. That is: this garden on this height never becomes barren, for if heavy rain does not strike it, then a light rain does, and in either case it is sufficient for it. Likewise, the work of the believer never perishes; rather, Allah accepts it, multiplies it and makes it grow, each worker according to his measure. For this reason He said: "And Allah is Seeing of what you do" (﴿وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ﴾): that is, nothing of the deeds of His servants is hidden from Him.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on surah 2, verse 266:

Al-Bukhari said, in explaining this verse: Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Hisham (ibn Yusuf) narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I heard Abdullah [[In ج, أ, و: "Ubayd Allah".]] ibn Abi Mulaykah narrating from Ibn Abbas, and I heard his brother Abu Bakr ibn Abi Mulaykah narrating from Ubayd ibn Umayr, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab once said to the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ: "Concerning whom do you think this verse was revealed: ﴿Would any of you like to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines﴾?" They said: "God knows best." Umar became angry and said: "Say: 'We know' or 'We do not know'." [[In ج: "They said: Do you know or do you not know?"]] Ibn Abbas said: "In my heart there is something about it, O Commander of the Faithful." Umar said: "O son of my brother, speak, and do not belittle yourself." Ibn Abbas said: "It was struck as a parable for a deed." Umar said: "What deed?" Ibn Abbas said: "For a deed." Umar said: "For a rich man who works in obedience to God. Then God sent the devil to him, and he worked in acts of disobedience until he burned up [[In ج: "until he drowned"]] his deeds."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4538).]]

Then al-Bukhari narrated it again, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Za'farani, from Hajjaj ibn Muhammad al-A'war, from Ibn Jurayj, and mentioned it [[I have not found this chain in Sahih al-Bukhari, and al-Mizzi did not mention it in Tuhfat al-Ashraf.]]. This narration is one that al-Bukhari alone reported, may God have mercy on him.

In this hadith there is sufficiency for explaining this verse and clarifying the parable it contains: it is the likeness of a person who first did good deeds and then reversed his course, exchanging good deeds for bad ones, God forbid. By his second deed he nullified what he had previously sent forward of righteousness, and he came to need something from the first in the most straitened circumstances, but nothing of it was available to him, and it failed him at the time he was most in need of it. For this reason God, the Exalted, said: ﴿And he has weak offspring, and a whirlwind strikes it﴾, which is a fierce wind, ﴿in which is fire, and it is burned﴾, meaning: it burned its fruits and destroyed its trees. So what would his condition be?

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated, through al-Awfi, from Ibn Abbas, who said: God struck for him a good parable, and all His parables are good. He said: ﴿Would any of you like to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines, with rivers flowing beneath it, having in it every kind of fruit﴾, meaning: he wasted it in his old age, ﴿and old age has overtaken him﴾, while his children and offspring are weak at the end of his life. Then a whirlwind with fire in it strikes and burns his orchard, and he has no strength to plant the like of it, and his offspring have no good to return to him. Likewise the disbeliever on the Day of Resurrection, when he is returned to God, the Mighty and Majestic, has no good thing that would be given in exchange for him to make amends, just as this man has no strength to plant the like of his orchard, and does not find that he sent forward for himself any good that would benefit him. Just as his offspring could not avail him, and his reward was withheld from him at the time he was most in need of it, so too this man is deprived of the garden of God at the time he is most in need of it, in his old age and when his offspring are weak.

Similarly, al-Hakim narrated in his Mustadrak that the Messenger of God ﷺ used to say in his supplication: "O God, make the widest of Your provision mine at the time of my old age and the end of my life."[[Al-Mustadrak (1/542), through Sa'id ibn Sulayman, from Isa ibn Maymun, from al-Qasim, from Aisha, may God be pleased with her, as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) narration. Al-Hakim said: "This is a hadith with a sound chain, and the text is strange; supplication of this kind is recommended for the elderly, but Isa ibn Maymun was not relied upon by the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim)." Al-Dhahabi said: "I say: Isa is accused (of lying)."]]

For this reason God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Thus God makes clear to you the verses, that you may reflect﴾, meaning: that you may take heed, understand the parables and meanings, and apply them to their intended sense, as God, the Exalted, said: ﴿And these parables We strike for the people, but none understands them except those who have knowledge﴾ [al-Ankabut: 43].

Allah commands His believing servants to spend (and here the word means charity, as Ibn 'Abbas said) from the good things of the wealth they have earned which He has provided for them. Mujahid said: this means trade, by Him making it easy for them.

'Ali and al-Suddi said: "From the good things of what you have earned" means gold and silver, and from the fruits and crops which He has caused to grow for them from the earth.

Ibn 'Abbas said: He commanded them to spend from the best, finest and most precious wealth, and He forbade them to give in charity from the worst and most despicable wealth, which is its bad part. For Allah is Good and accepts only what is good. For this reason He said: ﴿And do not aim at the bad part of it to spend from, while you would not accept it yourselves⦆ meaning: even if it were given to you, you would not take it, unless you overlook it. Allah is more Self-Sufficient than you, so do not assign to Allah what you dislike.

It was also said that the meaning is: ﴿And do not aim at the bad part of it to spend from﴾ meaning: do not turn away from lawful wealth and aim at the unlawful, making your spending from it.

Here is mentioned the hadith which Imam Ahmad narrated: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, Aban ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from as-Sabbah ibn Muhammad, from Murrah al-Hamdani, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah has distributed among you your characters just as He has distributed among you your provisions. Allah gives the world to whomever He loves and whomever He does not love, but He gives religion only to those whom He loves. Whoever Allah gives religion to, He has loved him. By the One in whose hand is my soul, a servant does not submit (become Muslim) until his heart and tongue submit, and he does not believe until his neighbour is safe from his evils." They said: "What are his evils, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "His oppression and his injustice. A servant does not earn wealth from unlawful means and then spend from it, and it be blessed for him in it; nor does he give charity from it, and it be accepted from him; nor does he leave it behind his back except that it becomes his provision to the Fire. Indeed Allah does not erase evil with evil, but He erases evil with good. Indeed the bad does not erase the bad."

The correct view is the first one. Ibn Jarir said: al-Husayn ibn 'Amr al-'Anqazi narrated to me, my father narrated to me, from Asbat, from as-Suddi, from 'Adi ibn Thabit, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib concerning the words of Allah: ﴿O you who believe, spend from the good things you have earned and from what We have brought forth for you from the earth. And do not aim at the bad part of it to spend from﴾ to the end of the verse. He said: It was revealed concerning the Ansar. The Ansar, when the time of harvesting the palm dates came, would bring out bunches of unripe dates from their gardens and hang them on a rope between the two pillars in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the poor of the Muhajirun would eat from it. A man among them would go to the dry and worthless dates and put them in with the bunches of unripe dates, thinking that this was permissible. So Allah revealed concerning those who did that: ﴿And do not aim at the bad part of it to spend from﴾.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Majah, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak narrated it, by way of as-Suddi, from 'Adi ibn Thabit, from al-Bara', in similar words. Al-Hakim said: "Sahih according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it." [Tafsir al-Tabari (5/559, 560), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (1822), al-Mustadrak (2/285). al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (2/58): "This is a sahih chain, its narrators are trustworthy, and it has a witness from the hadith of 'Awf ibn Malik, narrated by the authors of the four Sunan."]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Israil, from as-Suddi, from Abu Malik, from al-Bara': ﴿And do not aim at the bad part of it to spend from, while you would not accept it yourselves unless you overlook it﴾. He said: It was revealed about us. We were people of palm trees, and a man would bring from his palm trees according to how much or little he had. A man would bring a bunch and hang it in the mosque, and the People of the Suffah had no food. When one of them became hungry he would come and strike it with his stick, and the unripe and ripe dates would fall from it, and he would eat. But some people who did not desire good would bring a bunch in which there was dry and worthless dates, or a broken bunch, and hang it up. So it was revealed: ﴿And do not aim at the bad part of it to spend from, while you would not accept it yourselves unless you overlook it﴾. He said: If one of you were given a gift like what he gave, he would not take it except with overlooking and shame. So after that, one of us would bring the best of what he had.

At-Tirmidhi narrated it likewise, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi, from 'Ubayd Allah, who is Ibn Musa al-'Absi, from Israil, from as-Suddi, who is Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Malik al-Ghifari, whose name is Ghazwan, from al-Bara', and he mentioned something similar.

Then he said: This is a hasan gharib hadith.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu al-Walid narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Kathir narrated to us, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, from his father: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade two kinds of dates: al-Ju'rur and the variety called al-Hubayq. The people used to aim at the worst of their fruit and then bring it out in charity, so this was revealed: ﴿And do not aim at the bad part of it to spend from﴾. [al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (1/402), and al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (6/76) by way of Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi with this chain, and al-Hakim said: "A hadith sahih according to the condition of al-Bukhari."]

Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Husayn, from az-Zuhri [with this chain]. Then he said: Abu al-Walid traced it back from Sulayman ibn Kathir, from az-Zuhri, and its wording is: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade al-Ju'rur and the variety called al-Hubayq to be taken in charity. [Sunan Abi Dawud no. (1607).]

An-Nasa'i narrated this hadith by way of 'Abd al-Jalil ibn Humayd al-Yahsubi, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Umamah, and he did not say "from his father," and he mentioned something similar. Ibn Wahb likewise narrated it from 'Abd al-Jalil.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Yahya ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn as-Sa'ib, from 'Abdullah ibn Ma'qil, concerning this verse: ﴿And do not aim at the bad part of it to spend from﴾. He said: The earnings of a Muslim are not bad, but he should not give in charity dry and worthless dates, a counterfeit dirham, or anything that has no good in it.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Sa'id narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Hammad, who is Ibn Abi Sulayman, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from 'A'ishah who said: A dabb lizard was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he did not eat it, nor did he forbid it. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, should we feed it to the poor?" He said: "Do not feed them what you do not eat." [Musnad (6/105).]

He then narrated it from 'Affan, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same chain, and in it: "Shall I feed it to the poor?" He said: "Do not feed them what you do not eat."

Ath-Thawri said: from as-Suddi, from Abu Malik, from al-Bara', concerning ﴿while you would not accept it yourselves unless you overlook it﴾: it means that if a man were owed something by another man, and the debtor gave him that, he would not take it unless he saw that it had been reduced from his right. Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿while you would not accept it yourselves unless you overlook it﴾ means: if you were owed something by someone, and he came to you with less than your right, you would not accept it at full value until you reduced it. He said: That is His saying: ﴿unless you overlook it﴾. "So how do you accept for Me what you do not accept for yourselves, when My right over you is from the best and finest of your wealth!?"

Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir, and he added: This is His saying: ﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love﴾ [Al 'Imran: 92]. Then he narrated by way of al-'Awfi and others, from Ibn 'Abbas, something similar, and likewise many others mentioned it.

His saying: ﴿And know that Allah is Ever Free of need, Praiseworthy﴾ means: even though He commands you to give charity and to give the good part of it, He is free of need of it. He only does this so that the wealthy and the poor may be equal, like His saying: ﴿It is not their meat nor their blood that reaches Allah, but piety from you reaches Him﴾ [al-Hajj: 37]. He is free of need of all His creation, and all His creation is in need of Him. He is vast in bounty, and what is with Him does not run out. Whoever gives charity from good earnings should know that Allah is free of need, of wide giving, generous and bountiful; He will reward him for it and multiply it for him many times over, for He lends to one who is not poor and not unjust. He is al-Hamid, meaning the Praised in all His actions, sayings, legislation and decree. There is no god but Him, and no lord besides Him.

* *

His saying: ﴿The Shaytan threatens you with poverty and commands you to immorality, while Allah promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty, and Allah is All-Encompassing and Knowing﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us, Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn as-Sa'ib, from Murrah al-Hamdani, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The Shaytan has an inspiration (lamma) upon the son of Adam, and the angel has an inspiration. As for the inspiration of the Shaytan, it is a promise of evil and a denial of the truth; as for the inspiration of the angel, it is a promise of good and an affirmation of the truth. Whoever finds that, let him know it is from Allah, and let him praise Allah; and whoever finds the other, let him seek refuge in Allah from the Shaytan." Then he recited: ﴿The Shaytan threatens you with poverty and commands you to immorality, while Allah promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty﴾ to the end of the verse.

Likewise at-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa'i narrated it in the books of tafsir of their Sunans, both from Hannad ibn al-Sari. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2988), Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11051).]

Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih, from Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, from Hannad, with the same chain. [Sahih Ibn Hibban no. (40), Mawarid.] At-Tirmidhi said: Hasan gharib; it is the hadith of Abu al-Ahwas, meaning Sallam ibn Sulaym, and we do not know it as marfu' except from his narration. Thus he said. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh also narrated it in his tafsir, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Rustah, from Harun al-Farwi, from Abu Damrah, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abdullah, from Ibn Mas'ud, as marfu', similar to it.

However, Mis'ar narrated it from 'Ata' ibn as-Sa'ib, from Abu al-Ahwas 'Awf ibn Malik ibn Nadhlah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and he made it his own saying (mawquf). And Allah knows best.

The meaning of His saying: ﴿The Shaytan threatens you with poverty﴾ is: he frightens you with poverty, so that you hold back what is in your hands and do not spend it seeking Allah's pleasure. ﴿And commands you to immorality﴾ means: alongside his forbidding you to spend out of fear of destitution, he commands you to sins, offences, prohibitions, and opposing what is good (al-khalaq). Allah said: ﴿And Allah promises you forgiveness from Him﴾, meaning in exchange for what the Shaytan commands you of immorality; ﴿and bounty﴾, meaning in exchange for what the Shaytan frightens you of poverty. ﴿And Allah is All-Encompassing and Knowing.﴾

* *

His saying: ﴿He gives wisdom to whom He wills﴾. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: it means knowledge of the Qur'an, its abrogating and abrogated (nasikh and mansukh) parts, its clear (muhkam) and allegorical (mutashabih) parts, its earlier and later parts, its lawful and unlawful parts, and its parables.

Juwaybir related, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, in a marfu' report: "Al-hikmah is the Qur'an." That is, its tafsir (exegesis). Ibn 'Abbas said: "For indeed the righteous and the wicked have recited it." Ibn Mardawayh narrated it. (al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (2/66) to Ibn Mardawayh in his tafsir, and its isnad is very weak.)

Ibn Abi Najih related, from Mujahid: "By al-hikmah is meant accuracy in speech."

Layth ibn Abi Sulaym related, from Mujahid: "﴿He gives wisdom to whom He wills﴾ is not prophethood, rather it is knowledge, understanding (fiqh) and the Qur'an."

Abu al-'Aliyah said: "Al-hikmah is the fear of Allah, for the fear of Allah is the head of all wisdom."

Ibn Mardawayh related, through the route of Baqiyyah, from 'Uthman ibn Zufar al-Juhani, from Abu 'Ammar al-Asadi, from Ibn Mas'ud, in a marfu' report: "The head of wisdom is the fear of Allah." (Al-Bayhaqi narrated it and declared it weak in Shu'ab al-Iman, no. 744, through Muhammad ibn Wasifi from Baqiyyah; al-Bayhaqi also narrated it by another route as a mawquf report from Ibn Mas'ud.)

Abu al-'Aliyah, in another narration from him, said: "Al-hikmah is the Book and understanding." Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: "Al-hikmah is understanding." Abu Malik said: "Al-hikmah is the Sunnah." Ibn Wahb related, from Malik, that Zayd ibn Aslam said: "Al-hikmah is reason (al-'aql)." Malik said: "It occurs to my heart that al-hikmah is fiqh (deep understanding) in the religion of Allah, and a matter that Allah places in the hearts from His mercy and bounty. What clarifies this is that you find a man intelligent in worldly affairs, with insight into them, and you find another weak in his worldly affairs but knowledgeable in his religion and perceptive about it, whom Allah grants that and withholds this. So al-hikmah is fiqh in the religion of Allah."

Al-Suddi said: "Al-hikmah is prophethood."

The sound view, as the majority (al-jumhur) held, is that al-hikmah is not restricted to prophethood; rather it is more general than that, and its highest level is prophethood. Risalah (messengerhood) is more specific. However, the followers of the prophets have a share of good by way of following, as occurs in some hadiths: "Whoever memorizes the Qur'an has had prophethood placed between his two shoulders, except that it is not revealed to him." (Its isnad includes Isma'il ibn Rafi' al-Madani, whom Ahmad, Ibn Ma'in and al-Nasa'i declared weak, and Ibn 'Adi said: his narrations are all subject to scrutiny.) Waki' ibn al-Jarrah related it in his tafsir from Isma'il ibn Rafi', from a man he did not name, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, and his statement.

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' and Yazid related to us, both saying: Isma'il (meaning Ibn Abi Khalid) related to us, from Qays (that is, Ibn Abi Hazim), from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "There is no envy except in two: a man whom Allah has given wealth and has empowered him to spend it in the right way, and a man whom Allah has given wisdom, so he judges by it and teaches it." (Musnad, 1/432.)

Al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated it in the same way, through multiple routes, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid. (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 73; Sahih Muslim, no. 816; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 5840; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4208.)

* *

As for His statement: ﴿And none will be reminded except the people of understanding﴾, meaning: none benefits from the admonition and remembrance except one who has intellect and reason by which he comprehends the address, and the meaning of the speech.

Allah commands His believing servants to spend (and here the word means charity, as Ibn 'Abbas said) from the good things of the wealth they have earned which He has provided for them. Mujahid said: this means trade, by Him making it easy for them.

'Ali and al-Suddi said: "From the good things of what you have earned" means gold and silver, and from the fruits and crops which He has caused to grow for them from the earth.

Ibn 'Abbas said: He commanded them to spend from the best, finest and most precious wealth, and He forbade them to give in charity from the worst and most despicable wealth, which is its bad part. For Allah is Good and accepts only what is good. For this reason He said: ﴿And do not aim at the bad part of it to spend from, while you would not accept it yourselves⦆ meaning: even if it were given to you, you would not take it, unless you overlook it. Allah is more Self-Sufficient than you, so do not assign to Allah what you dislike.

It was also said that the meaning is: ﴿And do not aim at the bad part of it to spend from﴾ meaning: do not turn away from lawful wealth and aim at the unlawful, making your spending from it.

Here is mentioned the hadith which Imam Ahmad narrated: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, Aban ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from as-Sabbah ibn Muhammad, from Murrah al-Hamdani, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah has distributed among you your characters just as He has distributed among you your provisions. Allah gives the world to whomever He loves and whomever He does not love, but He gives religion only to those whom He loves. Whoever Allah gives religion to, He has loved him. By the One in whose hand is my soul, a servant does not submit (become Muslim) until his heart and tongue submit, and he does not believe until his neighbour is safe from his evils." They said: "What are his evils, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "His oppression and his injustice. A servant does not earn wealth from unlawful means and then spend from it, and it be blessed for him in it; nor does he give charity from it, and it be accepted from him; nor does he leave it behind his back except that it becomes his provision to the Fire. Indeed Allah does not erase evil with evil, but He erases evil with good. Indeed the bad does not erase the bad."

The correct view is the first one. Ibn Jarir said: al-Husayn ibn 'Amr al-'Anqazi narrated to me, my father narrated to me, from Asbat, from as-Suddi, from 'Adi ibn Thabit, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib concerning the words of Allah: ﴿O you who believe, spend from the good things you have earned and from what We have brought forth for you from the earth. And do not aim at the bad part of it to spend from﴾ to the end of the verse. He said: It was revealed concerning the Ansar. The Ansar, when the time of harvesting the palm dates came, would bring out bunches of unripe dates from their gardens and hang them on a rope between the two pillars in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the poor of the Muhajirun would eat from it. A man among them would go to the dry and worthless dates and put them in with the bunches of unripe dates, thinking that this was permissible. So Allah revealed concerning those who did that: ﴿And do not aim at the bad part of it to spend from﴾.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Majah, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak narrated it, by way of as-Suddi, from 'Adi ibn Thabit, from al-Bara', in similar words. Al-Hakim said: "Sahih according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it." [Tafsir al-Tabari (5/559, 560), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (1822), al-Mustadrak (2/285). al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (2/58): "This is a sahih chain, its narrators are trustworthy, and it has a witness from the hadith of 'Awf ibn Malik, narrated by the authors of the four Sunan."]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Israil, from as-Suddi, from Abu Malik, from al-Bara': ﴿And do not aim at the bad part of it to spend from, while you would not accept it yourselves unless you overlook it﴾. He said: It was revealed about us. We were people of palm trees, and a man would bring from his palm trees according to how much or little he had. A man would bring a bunch and hang it in the mosque, and the People of the Suffah had no food. When one of them became hungry he would come and strike it with his stick, and the unripe and ripe dates would fall from it, and he would eat. But some people who did not desire good would bring a bunch in which there was dry and worthless dates, or a broken bunch, and hang it up. So it was revealed: ﴿And do not aim at the bad part of it to spend from, while you would not accept it yourselves unless you overlook it﴾. He said: If one of you were given a gift like what he gave, he would not take it except with overlooking and shame. So after that, one of us would bring the best of what he had.

At-Tirmidhi narrated it likewise, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi, from 'Ubayd Allah, who is Ibn Musa al-'Absi, from Israil, from as-Suddi, who is Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Malik al-Ghifari, whose name is Ghazwan, from al-Bara', and he mentioned something similar.

Then he said: This is a hasan gharib hadith.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu al-Walid narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Kathir narrated to us, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, from his father: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade two kinds of dates: al-Ju'rur and the variety called al-Hubayq. The people used to aim at the worst of their fruit and then bring it out in charity, so this was revealed: ﴿And do not aim at the bad part of it to spend from﴾. [al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (1/402), and al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (6/76) by way of Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi with this chain, and al-Hakim said: "A hadith sahih according to the condition of al-Bukhari."]

Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Husayn, from az-Zuhri [with this chain]. Then he said: Abu al-Walid traced it back from Sulayman ibn Kathir, from az-Zuhri, and its wording is: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade al-Ju'rur and the variety called al-Hubayq to be taken in charity. [Sunan Abi Dawud no. (1607).]

An-Nasa'i narrated this hadith by way of 'Abd al-Jalil ibn Humayd al-Yahsubi, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Umamah, and he did not say "from his father," and he mentioned something similar. Ibn Wahb likewise narrated it from 'Abd al-Jalil.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Yahya ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn as-Sa'ib, from 'Abdullah ibn Ma'qil, concerning this verse: ﴿And do not aim at the bad part of it to spend from﴾. He said: The earnings of a Muslim are not bad, but he should not give in charity dry and worthless dates, a counterfeit dirham, or anything that has no good in it.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Sa'id narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Hammad, who is Ibn Abi Sulayman, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from 'A'ishah who said: A dabb lizard was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he did not eat it, nor did he forbid it. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, should we feed it to the poor?" He said: "Do not feed them what you do not eat." [Musnad (6/105).]

He then narrated it from 'Affan, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same chain, and in it: "Shall I feed it to the poor?" He said: "Do not feed them what you do not eat."

Ath-Thawri said: from as-Suddi, from Abu Malik, from al-Bara', concerning ﴿while you would not accept it yourselves unless you overlook it﴾: it means that if a man were owed something by another man, and the debtor gave him that, he would not take it unless he saw that it had been reduced from his right. Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿while you would not accept it yourselves unless you overlook it﴾ means: if you were owed something by someone, and he came to you with less than your right, you would not accept it at full value until you reduced it. He said: That is His saying: ﴿unless you overlook it﴾. "So how do you accept for Me what you do not accept for yourselves, when My right over you is from the best and finest of your wealth!?"

Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir, and he added: This is His saying: ﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love﴾ [Al 'Imran: 92]. Then he narrated by way of al-'Awfi and others, from Ibn 'Abbas, something similar, and likewise many others mentioned it.

His saying: ﴿And know that Allah is Ever Free of need, Praiseworthy﴾ means: even though He commands you to give charity and to give the good part of it, He is free of need of it. He only does this so that the wealthy and the poor may be equal, like His saying: ﴿It is not their meat nor their blood that reaches Allah, but piety from you reaches Him﴾ [al-Hajj: 37]. He is free of need of all His creation, and all His creation is in need of Him. He is vast in bounty, and what is with Him does not run out. Whoever gives charity from good earnings should know that Allah is free of need, of wide giving, generous and bountiful; He will reward him for it and multiply it for him many times over, for He lends to one who is not poor and not unjust. He is al-Hamid, meaning the Praised in all His actions, sayings, legislation and decree. There is no god but Him, and no lord besides Him.

* *

His saying: ﴿The Shaytan threatens you with poverty and commands you to immorality, while Allah promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty, and Allah is All-Encompassing and Knowing﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us, Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn as-Sa'ib, from Murrah al-Hamdani, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The Shaytan has an inspiration (lamma) upon the son of Adam, and the angel has an inspiration. As for the inspiration of the Shaytan, it is a promise of evil and a denial of the truth; as for the inspiration of the angel, it is a promise of good and an affirmation of the truth. Whoever finds that, let him know it is from Allah, and let him praise Allah; and whoever finds the other, let him seek refuge in Allah from the Shaytan." Then he recited: ﴿The Shaytan threatens you with poverty and commands you to immorality, while Allah promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty﴾ to the end of the verse.

Likewise at-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa'i narrated it in the books of tafsir of their Sunans, both from Hannad ibn al-Sari. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2988), Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11051).]

Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih, from Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, from Hannad, with the same chain. [Sahih Ibn Hibban no. (40), Mawarid.] At-Tirmidhi said: Hasan gharib; it is the hadith of Abu al-Ahwas, meaning Sallam ibn Sulaym, and we do not know it as marfu' except from his narration. Thus he said. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh also narrated it in his tafsir, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Rustah, from Harun al-Farwi, from Abu Damrah, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abdullah, from Ibn Mas'ud, as marfu', similar to it.

However, Mis'ar narrated it from 'Ata' ibn as-Sa'ib, from Abu al-Ahwas 'Awf ibn Malik ibn Nadhlah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and he made it his own saying (mawquf). And Allah knows best.

The meaning of His saying: ﴿The Shaytan threatens you with poverty﴾ is: he frightens you with poverty, so that you hold back what is in your hands and do not spend it seeking Allah's pleasure. ﴿And commands you to immorality﴾ means: alongside his forbidding you to spend out of fear of destitution, he commands you to sins, offences, prohibitions, and opposing what is good (al-khalaq). Allah said: ﴿And Allah promises you forgiveness from Him﴾, meaning in exchange for what the Shaytan commands you of immorality; ﴿and bounty﴾, meaning in exchange for what the Shaytan frightens you of poverty. ﴿And Allah is All-Encompassing and Knowing.﴾

* *

His saying: ﴿He gives wisdom to whom He wills﴾. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: it means knowledge of the Qur'an, its abrogating and abrogated (nasikh and mansukh) parts, its clear (muhkam) and allegorical (mutashabih) parts, its earlier and later parts, its lawful and unlawful parts, and its parables.

Juwaybir related, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, in a marfu' report: "Al-hikmah is the Qur'an." That is, its tafsir (exegesis). Ibn 'Abbas said: "For indeed the righteous and the wicked have recited it." Ibn Mardawayh narrated it. (al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (2/66) to Ibn Mardawayh in his tafsir, and its isnad is very weak.)

Ibn Abi Najih related, from Mujahid: "By al-hikmah is meant accuracy in speech."

Layth ibn Abi Sulaym related, from Mujahid: "﴿He gives wisdom to whom He wills﴾ is not prophethood, rather it is knowledge, understanding (fiqh) and the Qur'an."

Abu al-'Aliyah said: "Al-hikmah is the fear of Allah, for the fear of Allah is the head of all wisdom."

Ibn Mardawayh related, through the route of Baqiyyah, from 'Uthman ibn Zufar al-Juhani, from Abu 'Ammar al-Asadi, from Ibn Mas'ud, in a marfu' report: "The head of wisdom is the fear of Allah." (Al-Bayhaqi narrated it and declared it weak in Shu'ab al-Iman, no. 744, through Muhammad ibn Wasifi from Baqiyyah; al-Bayhaqi also narrated it by another route as a mawquf report from Ibn Mas'ud.)

Abu al-'Aliyah, in another narration from him, said: "Al-hikmah is the Book and understanding." Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: "Al-hikmah is understanding." Abu Malik said: "Al-hikmah is the Sunnah." Ibn Wahb related, from Malik, that Zayd ibn Aslam said: "Al-hikmah is reason (al-'aql)." Malik said: "It occurs to my heart that al-hikmah is fiqh (deep understanding) in the religion of Allah, and a matter that Allah places in the hearts from His mercy and bounty. What clarifies this is that you find a man intelligent in worldly affairs, with insight into them, and you find another weak in his worldly affairs but knowledgeable in his religion and perceptive about it, whom Allah grants that and withholds this. So al-hikmah is fiqh in the religion of Allah."

Al-Suddi said: "Al-hikmah is prophethood."

The sound view, as the majority (al-jumhur) held, is that al-hikmah is not restricted to prophethood; rather it is more general than that, and its highest level is prophethood. Risalah (messengerhood) is more specific. However, the followers of the prophets have a share of good by way of following, as occurs in some hadiths: "Whoever memorizes the Qur'an has had prophethood placed between his two shoulders, except that it is not revealed to him." (Its isnad includes Isma'il ibn Rafi' al-Madani, whom Ahmad, Ibn Ma'in and al-Nasa'i declared weak, and Ibn 'Adi said: his narrations are all subject to scrutiny.) Waki' ibn al-Jarrah related it in his tafsir from Isma'il ibn Rafi', from a man he did not name, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, and his statement.

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' and Yazid related to us, both saying: Isma'il (meaning Ibn Abi Khalid) related to us, from Qays (that is, Ibn Abi Hazim), from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "There is no envy except in two: a man whom Allah has given wealth and has empowered him to spend it in the right way, and a man whom Allah has given wisdom, so he judges by it and teaches it." (Musnad, 1/432.)

Al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated it in the same way, through multiple routes, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid. (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 73; Sahih Muslim, no. 816; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 5840; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4208.)

* *

As for His statement: ﴿And none will be reminded except the people of understanding﴾, meaning: none benefits from the admonition and remembrance except one who has intellect and reason by which he comprehends the address, and the meaning of the speech.

Allah commands His believing servants to spend (and here the word means charity, as Ibn 'Abbas said) from the good things of the wealth they have earned which He has provided for them. Mujahid said: this means trade, by Him making it easy for them.

'Ali and al-Suddi said: "From the good things of what you have earned" means gold and silver, and from the fruits and crops which He has caused to grow for them from the earth.

Ibn 'Abbas said: He commanded them to spend from the best, finest and most precious wealth, and He forbade them to give in charity from the worst and most despicable wealth, which is its bad part. For this reason He said: ﴿And do not aim at the bad part of it to spend from, while you would not accept it yourselves⦆ meaning: even if it were given to you, you would not take it, unless you overlook it. Allah is more Self-Sufficient than you, so do not assign to Allah what you dislike.

It was also said that the meaning is: ﴿And do not aim at the bad part of it to spend from﴾ meaning: do not turn away from lawful wealth and aim at the unlawful, making your spending from it.

Here is mentioned the hadith which Imam Ahmad narrated: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, Aban ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from as-Sabbah ibn Muhammad, from Murrah al-Hamdani, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah has distributed among you your characters just as He has distributed among you your provisions. Allah gives the world to whomever He loves and whomever He does not love, but He gives religion only to those whom He loves. Whoever Allah gives religion to, He has loved him. By the One in whose hand is my soul, a servant does not submit (become Muslim) until his heart and tongue submit, and he does not believe until his neighbour is safe from his evils." They said: "What are his evils, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "His oppression and his injustice. A servant does not earn wealth from unlawful means and then spend from it, and it be blessed for him in it; nor does he give charity from it, and it be accepted from him; nor does he leave it behind his back except that it becomes his provision to the Fire. Indeed Allah does not erase evil with evil, but He erases evil with good. Indeed the bad does not erase the bad."

The correct view is the first one. Ibn Jarir said: al-Husayn ibn 'Amr al-'Anqazi narrated to me, my father narrated to me, from Asbat, from as-Suddi, from 'Adi ibn Thabit, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib concerning the words of Allah: ﴿O you who believe, spend from the good things you have earned and from what We have brought forth for you from the earth. And do not aim at the bad part of it to spend from﴾ to the end of the verse. He said: It was revealed concerning the Ansar. The Ansar, when the time of harvesting the palm dates came, would bring out bunches of unripe dates from their gardens and hang them on a rope between the two pillars in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the poor of the Muhajirun would eat from it. A man among them would go to the dry and worthless dates and put them in with the bunches of unripe dates, thinking that this was permissible. So Allah revealed concerning those who did that: ﴿And do not aim at the bad part of it to spend from﴾.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Majah, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak narrated it, by way of as-Suddi, from 'Adi ibn Thabit, from al-Bara', in similar words. Al-Hakim said: "Sahih according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it." [Tafsir al-Tabari (5/559, 560), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (1822), al-Mustadrak (2/285). al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (2/58): "This is a sahih chain, its narrators are trustworthy, and it has a witness from the hadith of 'Awf ibn Malik, narrated by the authors of the four Sunan."]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Israil, from as-Suddi, from Abu Malik, from al-Bara': ﴿And do not aim at the bad part of it to spend from, while you would not accept it yourselves unless you overlook it﴾. He said: It was revealed about us. We were people of palm trees, and a man would bring from his palm trees according to how much or little he had. A man would bring a bunch and hang it in the mosque, and the People of the Suffah had no food. When one of them became hungry he would come and strike it with his stick, and the unripe and ripe dates would fall from it, and he would eat. But some people who did not desire good would bring a bunch in which there was dry and worthless dates, or a broken bunch, and hang it up. So it was revealed: ﴿And do not aim at the bad part of it to spend from, while you would not accept it yourselves unless you overlook it﴾. He said: If one of you were given a gift like what he gave, he would not take it except with overlooking and shame. So after that, one of us would bring the best of what he had.

At-Tirmidhi narrated it likewise, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi, from 'Ubayd Allah, who is Ibn Musa al-'Absi, from Israil, from as-Suddi, who is Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Malik al-Ghifari, whose name is Ghazwan, from al-Bara', and he mentioned something similar.

Then he said: This is a hasan gharib hadith.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu al-Walid narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Kathir narrated to us, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, from his father: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade two kinds of dates: al-Ju'rur and the variety called al-Hubayq. The people used to aim at the worst of their fruit and then bring it out in charity, so this was revealed: ﴿And do not aim at the bad part of it to spend from﴾. [al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (1/402), and al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (6/76) by way of Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi with this chain, and al-Hakim said: "A hadith sahih according to the condition of al-Bukhari."]

Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Husayn, from az-Zuhri [with this chain]. Then he said: Abu al-Walid traced it back from Sulayman ibn Kathir, from az-Zuhri, and its wording is: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade al-Ju'rur and the variety called al-Hubayq to be taken in charity. [Sunan Abi Dawud no. (1607).]

An-Nasa'i narrated this hadith by way of 'Abd al-Jalil ibn Humayd al-Yahsubi, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Umamah, and he did not say "from his father," and he mentioned something similar. Ibn Wahb likewise narrated it from 'Abd al-Jalil.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Yahya ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn as-Sa'ib, from 'Abdullah ibn Ma'qil, concerning this verse: ﴿And do not aim at the bad part of it to spend from﴾. He said: The earnings of a Muslim are not bad, but he should not give in charity dry and worthless dates, a counterfeit dirham, or anything that has no good in it.

I said: "O Messenger of Allah, should we feed it to the poor?" He said: "Do not feed them what you do not eat." [Musnad (6/105).]

He then narrated it from 'Affan, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same chain, and in it: "Shall I feed it to the poor?" He said: "Do not feed them what you do not eat."

Ath-Thawri said: from as-Suddi, from Abu Malik, from al-Bara', concerning ﴿while you would not accept it yourselves unless you overlook it﴾: it means that if a man were owed something by another man, and the debtor gave him that, he would not take it unless he saw that it had been reduced from his right. Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿while you would not accept it yourselves unless you overlook it﴾ means: if you were owed something by someone, and he came to you with less than your right, you would not accept it at full value until you reduced it. He said: That is His saying: ﴿unless you overlook it﴾. "So how do you accept for Me what you do not accept for yourselves, when My right over you is from the best and finest of your wealth!?"

Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir, and he added: This is His saying: ﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love﴾ [Al 'Imran: 92]. Then he narrated by way of al-'Awfi and others, from Ibn 'Abbas, something similar, and likewise many others mentioned it.

His saying: ﴿And know that Allah is Ever Free of need, Praiseworthy﴾ means: even though He commands you to give charity and to give the good part of it, He is free of need of it. He only does this so that the wealthy and the poor may be equal, like His saying: ﴿It is not their meat nor their blood that reaches Allah, but piety from you reaches Him﴾ [al-Hajj: 37]. He is free of need of all His creation, and all His creation is in need of Him. He is vast in bounty, and what is with Him does not run out. He is al-Hamid, meaning the Praised in all His actions, sayings, legislation and decree. There is no god but Him, and no lord besides Him.

* *

His saying: ﴿The Shaytan threatens you with poverty and commands you to immorality, while Allah promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty, and Allah is All-Encompassing and Knowing﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us, Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn as-Sa'ib, from Murrah al-Hamdani, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The Shaytan has an inspiration (lamma) upon the son of Adam, and the angel has an inspiration. As for the inspiration of the Shaytan, it is a promise of evil and a denial of the truth; as for the inspiration of the angel, it is a promise of good and an affirmation of the truth. Whoever finds that, let him know it is from Allah, and let him praise Allah; and whoever finds the other, let him seek refuge in Allah from the Shaytan." Then he recited: ﴿The Shaytan threatens you with poverty and commands you to immorality, while Allah promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty﴾ to the end of the verse.

Likewise at-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa'i narrated it in the books of tafsir of their Sunans, both from Hannad ibn al-Sari. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2988), Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11051).]

Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih, from Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, from Hannad, with the same chain. [Sahih Ibn Hibban no. (40), Mawarid.] At-Tirmidhi said: Hasan gharib; it is the hadith of Abu al-Ahwas, meaning Sallam ibn Sulaym, and we do not know it as marfu' except from his narration. Thus he said. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh also narrated it in his tafsir, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Rustah, from Harun al-Farwi, from Abu Damrah, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abdullah, from Ibn Mas'ud, as marfu', similar to it.

However, Mis'ar narrated it from 'Ata' ibn as-Sa'ib, from Abu al-Ahwas 'Awf ibn Malik ibn Nadhlah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and he made it his own saying (mawquf). And Allah knows best.

The meaning of His saying: ﴿The Shaytan threatens you with poverty﴾ is: he frightens you with poverty, so that you hold back what is in your hands and do not spend it seeking Allah's pleasure. ﴿And commands you to immorality﴾ means: alongside his forbidding you to spend out of fear of destitution, he commands you to sins, offences, prohibitions, and opposing what is good (al-khalaq). Allah said: ﴿And Allah promises you forgiveness from Him﴾, meaning in exchange for what the Shaytan commands you of immorality; ﴿and bounty﴾, meaning in exchange for what the Shaytan frightens you of poverty. ﴿And Allah is All-Encompassing and Knowing.﴾

* *

His saying: ﴿He gives wisdom to whom He wills﴾. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: it means knowledge of the Qur'an, its abrogating and abrogated (nasikh and mansukh) parts, its clear (muhkam) and allegorical (mutashabih) parts, its earlier and later parts, its lawful and unlawful parts, and its parables.

Juwaybir related, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, in a marfu' report: "Al-hikmah is the Qur'an." That is, its tafsir (exegesis). Ibn 'Abbas said: "For indeed the righteous and the wicked have recited it." Ibn Mardawayh narrated it. (al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (2/66) to Ibn Mardawayh in his tafsir, and its isnad is very weak.)

Ibn Abi Najih related, from Mujahid: "By al-hikmah is meant accuracy in speech."

Layth ibn Abi Sulaym related, from Mujahid: "﴿He gives wisdom to whom He wills﴾ is not prophethood, rather it is knowledge, understanding (fiqh) and the Qur'an."

Abu al-'Aliyah said: "Al-hikmah is the fear of Allah, for the fear of Allah is the head of all wisdom."

Ibn Mardawayh related, through the route of Baqiyyah, from 'Uthman ibn Zufar al-Juhani, from Abu 'Ammar al-Asadi, from Ibn Mas'ud, in a marfu' report: "The head of wisdom is the fear of Allah." (Al-Bayhaqi narrated it and declared it weak in Shu'ab al-Iman, no. 744, through Muhammad ibn Wasifi from Baqiyyah; al-Bayhaqi also narrated it by another route as a mawquf report from Ibn Mas'ud.)

Abu al-'Aliyah, in another narration from him, said: "Al-hikmah is the Book and understanding." Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: "Al-hikmah is understanding." Abu Malik said: "Al-hikmah is the Sunnah." Ibn Wahb related, from Malik, that Zayd ibn Aslam said: "Al-hikmah is reason (al-'aql)." Malik said: "It occurs to my heart that al-hikmah is fiqh (deep understanding) in the religion of Allah, and a matter that Allah places in the hearts from His mercy and bounty. What clarifies this is that you find a man intelligent in worldly affairs, with insight into them, and you find another weak in his worldly affairs but knowledgeable in his religion and perceptive about it, whom Allah grants that and withholds this. So al-hikmah is fiqh in the religion of Allah."

Al-Suddi said: "Al-hikmah is prophethood."

The sound view, as the majority (al-jumhur) held, is that al-hikmah is not restricted to prophethood; rather it is more general than that, and its highest level is prophethood. Risalah (messengerhood) is more specific. However, the followers of the prophets have a share of good by way of following, as occurs in some hadiths: "Whoever memorizes the Qur'an has had prophethood placed between his two shoulders, except that it is not revealed to him." (Its isnad includes Isma'il ibn Rafi' al-Madani, whom Ahmad, Ibn Ma'in and al-Nasa'i declared weak, and Ibn 'Adi said: his narrations are all subject to scrutiny.) Waki' ibn al-Jarrah related it in his tafsir from Isma'il ibn Rafi', from a man he did not name, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, and his statement.

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' and Yazid related to us, both saying: Isma'il (meaning Ibn Abi Khalid) related to us, from Qays (that is, Ibn Abi Hazim), from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "There is no envy except in two: a man whom Allah has given wealth and has empowered him to spend it in the right way, and a man whom Allah has given wisdom, so he judges by it and teaches it." (Musnad, 1/432.)

Al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated it in the same way, through multiple routes, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid. (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 73; Sahih Muslim, no. 816; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 5840; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4208.)

* *

As for His statement: ﴿And none will be reminded except the people of understanding﴾, meaning: none benefits from the admonition and remembrance except one who has intellect and reason by which he comprehends the address, and the meaning of the speech.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verses 270–271:

He, may He be exalted, informs that He knows all that those who do good deeds perform of charitable spending and vowed offerings. This includes His recompense for that with the fullest reward for those who do it seeking His Face and hoping for His promise. He threatens those who do not act in obedience to Him, who instead oppose His command, deny His report, and worship others besides Him, so He says: ﴿And for the wrongdoers there are no helpers﴾, meaning, on the Day of Resurrection they will have no one to rescue them [[In manuscripts A and W: "yunqidhahum" (rescue them).]] from the punishment and vengeance of Allah.

* *

His saying: ﴿If you disclose your charities, then they are excellent﴾, meaning: if you make them apparent, then excellent is what they are.

* *

His saying: ﴿But if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you﴾. In this is an indication that concealing charity is better than displaying it, because it is further from showing off (riya', seeking to be seen by people), unless displaying it results in a greater benefit, such as people following the example. In that case it would be better from this standpoint. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one who recites the Qur'an aloud is like the one who gives charity openly, and the one who recites the Qur'an quietly is like the one who gives charity quietly." [[Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (4/151), Abu Dawud in al-Sunan no. (1333), and al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan no. (2919), from the hadith of 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir (may Allah be pleased with him). al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith."]]

The principle is that concealment is better, due to this verse and due to what is established in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim), from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Seven will be shaded by Allah under His shade on a Day when there is no shade but His: a just ruler; a young man who grew up in the worship of Allah; two men who loved each other for the sake of Allah, coming together and parting on that basis; a man whose heart is attached to the mosque whenever he leaves it until he returns to it; a man who remembered Allah in private and his eyes overflowed with tears; a man who was called by a woman of rank and beauty and said, 'I fear Allah'; and a man who gave a charity and concealed it so that his left hand does not know what his right hand gives." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (660, 1423), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1031).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, al-'Awwam ibn Hawshab informed us, from Sulayman ibn Abi Sulayman, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When Allah created the earth, it began to shake, so He created the mountains and placed them upon it, and it settled. The angels marvelled at the creation of the mountains and said: 'O Lord, is there anything in Your creation stronger than the mountains?' He said: 'Yes, iron.' They said: 'O Lord, is there anything in Your creation stronger than iron?' He said: 'Yes, fire.' They said: 'O Lord, is there anything in Your creation stronger than fire?' He said: 'Yes, water.' They said: 'O Lord, is there anything in Your creation stronger than water?' He said: 'Yes, wind.' They said: 'O Lord, is there anything in Your creation stronger than wind?' He said: 'Yes, the son of Adam who gives charity with his right hand and conceals it from his left.'" [[al-Musnad (3/124).]]

We have mentioned, regarding the virtue of Ayat al-Kursi, that Abu Dhar said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which charity is best?" He said: "A secret gift to a poor person, or the effort of one of modest means." Ahmad narrated it. [[al-Musnad (5/178).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through 'Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, from Abu Dhar, with the same wording, and he added: Then he recited this verse: ﴿If you disclose your charities, then they are excellent, but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you﴾, to the end of the verse. [[al-Tabarani also narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (8/269), through Khalid ibn Abi Yazid, from 'Ali ibn Yazid, with the same chain.]]

And in the hadith that is narrated: "Secret charity extinguishes the anger of the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan no. (2386), from the hadith of Anas (may Allah be pleased with him). It is also reported from a group of the Companions, and it is a mutawatir hadith.]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Husayn ibn Ziyad al-Muharibi, the teacher of the Banu Muharib, narrated to us, Musa ibn 'Umayr informed us, from 'Amir al-Sha'bi regarding His saying: ﴿If you disclose your charities, then they are excellent, but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you﴾. He said: It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr and 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both). As for 'Umar, he brought half of his wealth and handed it to the Prophet (ﷺ). The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "What have you left behind for your family, O 'Umar?" He said: "I have left them half of my wealth." As for Abu Bakr, he brought all of his wealth, nearly concealing it from himself, until he handed it to the Prophet (ﷺ). The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "What have you left behind for your family, O Abu Bakr?" He said: "The promise of Allah and the promise of His Messenger." 'Umar wept and said: "May my father be sacrificed for you, O Abu Bakr! By Allah, we never competed for any good except that you were ahead." [[al-Asbahani narrated it in al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib no. (1643), through Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah ibn Musa ibn 'Isa, from al-Sha'bi, with the same wording.]]

This hadith is also narrated through another route, from 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him). [[Abu Dawud narrated it in al-Sunan no. (1678) and al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan no. (3675), through Hisham ibn Sa'd, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him). al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith."]] We have cited it here only for al-Sha'bi's statement that the verse was revealed concerning this matter. Furthermore, the verse in general indicates that concealing charity is better, whether it is obligatory or recommended. However, Ibn Jarir narrated through 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding the interpretation of this verse, that he said: Allah made secret voluntary charity superior to its public form, and He said it is seventy times better. And He made the public form of obligatory charity superior to its secret form, and He said it is twenty-five times better.

* *

His saying: ﴿And He will remove from you some of your misdeeds﴾, meaning: in exchange for the charities, especially when they are secret, good will come to you in raising your ranks, and He will expiate your misdeeds from you. It has been recited as "wa yukaffiru 'ankum" with a dammah, and it has been recited as "wa nukaffir" with a jazm (apocopate), as a conjunction upon the position of the answer to the condition, which is His saying: ﴿then they are excellent﴾, like the saying: "fa-asaddaqa wa akun" (so I would give charity and be among the righteous). [[In manuscripts J, A and W: "upon the place (mahall)".]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do﴾, meaning: nothing of that is hidden from Him, and He will recompense you for it, [glory be to Him and praise be to Him]. [[Addition from manuscript W.]]

(3675), through Hisham ibn Sa'd, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him). al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith."]] We have cited it here only for al-Sha'bi's statement that the verse was revealed concerning this matter. * *

His saying: ﴿And He will remove from you some of your misdeeds﴾, meaning: in exchange for the charities, especially when they are secret, good will come to you in raising your ranks, and He will expiate your misdeeds from you. It has been recited as "wa yukaffiru 'ankum" with a dammah, and it has been recited as "wa nukaffir" with a jazm (apocopate), as a conjunction upon the position of the answer to the condition, which is His saying: ﴿then they are excellent﴾, like the saying: "fa-asaddaqa wa akun" (so I would give charity and be among the righteous). [[In manuscripts J, A and W: "upon the place (mahall)".]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do﴾, meaning: nothing of that is hidden from Him, and He will recompense you for it, [glory be to Him and praise be to Him]. [[Addition from manuscript W.]]

Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa'i said: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah [[In manuscripts J, A, and W: "ibn Abd al-Salam".]] ibn Abd al-Rahim informed us, [[In manuscript J: "Haddathana" (he related to us).]] al-Firyabi informed us, Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Ja'far ibn Iyas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "They disliked giving charity to their relatives among the polytheists, so they asked, and he (ﷺ) granted them permission, and this verse was revealed: ﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills. And whatever good you spend is for yourselves, and you spend only seeking the Face of Allah. And whatever good you spend will be repaid to you, and you will not be wronged﴾" [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11052).]].

Similarly, Abu Hudhayfah, Ibn al-Mubarak, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri, and Abu Dawud al-Hafari narrated it from Sufyan, meaning al-Thawri, with this chain.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn Atiyyah informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman, meaning al-Dashtaki, related to me, my father related to me, from his father, Ash'ath ibn Ishaq related to us, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he used to order that charity be given only to the people of Islam, until this verse was revealed: ﴿It is not upon you to guide them﴾ to its end, and so he ordered charity to be given after it to everyone who asks you, of every religion [[Ibn Mardawayh and al-Diya' al-Maqdisi are credited with this narration by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (2/86).]]. The hadith of Asma' bint Abi Bakr concerning this will come under the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over religion and do not expel you from your homes﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 8], [if Allah wills] [[Addition from manuscripts J and A.]].

* *

As for His words: ﴿And whatever good you spend is for yourselves﴾, it is like His words: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul﴾ [Fussilat: 46; al-Jathiyah: 15], and similar examples in the Qur'an are numerous [[In manuscript W: "numerous" (without the feminine ending).]].

* *

As for His words: ﴿and you spend only seeking the Face of Allah﴾, al-Hasan al-Basri said: "The believer's spending is for himself, and the believer, when he spends, spends only seeking the Face of Allah."

And Ata' al-Khurasani said: "It means: when you give for the Face of Allah, then it is no concern of yours what the recipient does." This is a good meaning. Its summary is that the giver, when he gives seeking the Face of Allah, his reward has fallen upon Allah, and it is not incumbent upon him, in reality, whether the recipient is righteous, wicked, deserving, or otherwise; he is rewarded for his intention. The basis for this is the completion of the verse: ﴿And whatever good you spend will be repaid to you, and you will not be wronged﴾. And the hadith recorded in the Two Sahihs, through the chain of Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A man said: I will surely give charity tonight. So he went out with his charity and placed it in the hand of a prostitute. In the morning, people were talking: Charity was given to a prostitute! He said: O Allah, to You belongs praise, for a prostitute! I will surely give charity tonight. So he went out with his charity and placed it in the hand of a wealthy man. In the morning, they were talking: Charity was given tonight to a wealthy man! He said: O Allah, to You belongs praise, for a wealthy man! I will surely give charity tonight. So he went out with his charity and placed it in the hand of a thief. In the morning, they were talking: Charity was given tonight to a thief! He said: O Allah, to You belongs praise, for a prostitute, for a wealthy man, and for a thief! He was then approached and told: As for your charity, it has been accepted; as for the prostitute, perhaps it will keep her chaste from her fornication; perhaps the wealthy man will take a lesson and spend from what Allah has given him; and perhaps the thief will keep himself chaste from his theft" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (1421), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1022).]].

* *

As for His words: ﴿for the poor who have been confined in the way of Allah﴾, it means: the emigrants who have devoted themselves to Allah and His Messenger, and settled in Medina, having no means by which they can earn for themselves what suffices them. And ﴿they cannot go about in the land﴾ means: travel for the purpose of earning a living. And "going about in the land" means travel. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when you travel in the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer﴾ [al-Nisa': 101]. He, the Exalted, also said: ﴿He knows that there will be among you those who are ill, and others who travel in the land seeking of Allah's bounty, and others who fight in the cause of Allah﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 20], to the end of the verse.

* *

As for His words: ﴿The ignorant one thinks them wealthy because of their modesty﴾, that is: the one ignorant of their affair and their condition thinks them wealthy because of their restraint in their clothing, their state, and their speech. On this meaning is the hadith agreed upon for its authenticity, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The poor man is not the one who goes around and is turned away by a date or two dates, or a morsel or two morsels, or a meal or two meals. Rather, the poor man is the one who finds no sufficiency to suffice him, and whose need is not recognized so that charity may be given to him, and who does not ask people for anything." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4539), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1039).] Ahmad also narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud [al-Musnad (1/384)].

* *

As for His words: ﴿You will recognize them by their mark﴾, that is: by what appears to people of understanding of their qualities, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Their mark is on their faces﴾ [al-Fath: 29], and He said: ﴿And you will surely know them by the tone of their speech﴾ [Muhammad: 30]. And in the hadith in the Sunan: "Beware of the insight of the believer, for he looks with the light of Allah," then he recited: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for those who perceive [al-mutawassimin]﴾ [al-Hijr: 75] [[Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Sunan, no. (3127), through the chain of Amr ibn Qays, from Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with him, as a marfu' hadith. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a gharib hadith; we only know it from this route, and it has been narrated from some scholars."]].

* *

As for His words: ﴿They do not ask people persistently﴾, that is: they do not press in asking, nor burden people with what they do not need. For whoever asks while he has what suffices him from asking has indeed pressed in asking. Al-Bukhari said: Ibn Abi Maryam related to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, Shurayk ibn Abi Namir related to us: that Ata' ibn Yasar and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Amrah al-Ansari said: "We heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The poor man is not the one who is turned away by a date or two dates, nor a morsel or two morsels. Rather, the poor man is the one who keeps himself chaste. Recite if you wish: ﴿They do not ask people persistently﴾,'" meaning His words [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4539).]].

Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Isma'il ibn Ja'far al-Madini, from Shurayk ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Namir, from Ata' ibn Yasar alone, from Abu Hurayrah, with the same wording [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1039).]].

Al-Nasa'i said [[In manuscript W: "And al-Nasa'i narrated it, and its wording is:"]]: Ali ibn Hujr informed us, Isma'il related to us, Shurayk, who is Ibn Abi Namir, informed us, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "The poor man is not the one who is turned away by a date or two dates, or a morsel or two morsels. Rather, the poor man is the one who keeps himself chaste. Recite if you wish: ﴿They do not ask people persistently﴾" [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11053).]].

Al-Bukhari narrated, from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (1476).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn Abd al-Ala informed us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Ibn Abi Dhi'b informed me, from Abu al-Walid, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The poor man is not the one who goes around to you, so that you give him a morsel at a time. Rather, the poor man is the one who keeps himself chaste, who does not ask people persistently."

Ibn Jarir said: Mu'tamir related to me, from al-Hasan ibn Matik [[In manuscripts J and A: "al-Hasan ibn Babil"; in manuscript W: "Ayman ibn Nabil".]], from Salih ibn Suwayd, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "The poor man is not the one who goes around and is turned away by a meal or two meals. Rather, the poor man is the one who keeps modest in his home, who does not ask people for anything he needs. Recite if you wish: ﴿They do not ask people persistently﴾."

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi related to us, Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far related to us, from his father, from a man of Muzaynah, that his mother said to him: "Will you not go and ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as people ask him?" So I went to ask him, and I found him standing and delivering a sermon, and he was saying: "Whoever seeks to be chaste, Allah will keep him chaste; whoever seeks self-sufficiency, Allah will make him self-sufficient; and whoever asks people while he has the equivalent of five awqiyah, he has indeed pressed in asking." So I said to myself: My she-camel is better than five awqiyah, and her companion [a young man] has another she-camel which is better than five awqiyah. So I returned without asking [[Al-Musnad (4/138).]].

Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah related to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Rijal related to us, from Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa'id, from his father, who said: "My mother sent me to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to ask him. So I came to him and sat down. He said: He faced me and said: 'Whoever seeks self-sufficiency, Allah will make him self-sufficient; whoever seeks to be chaste, Allah will keep him chaste; whoever seeks to be restrained, Allah will suffice him; and whoever asks while he has the value of an uqiyah, he has indeed pressed in asking.' So I said: My camel Al-Yaqutah is better than an uqiyah. So I returned and did not ask him."

Likewise Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated it, both from Qutaybah. Abu Dawud added: and Hisham ibn Ammar; both from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Rijal with its chain, similarly [[Al-Musnad (3/9); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (1628); Sunan al-Nasa'i (5/98).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to me, Abu al-Jamahir related to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Rijal related to us, from Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa'id, who said: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever asks while he has an uqiyah is a persistent asker." And the uqiyah is forty dirhams [[Ibn Khuzaymah narrated it in his Sahih, no. (2447), and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, no. (846), through the route of Abd Allah ibn Yusuf, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Rijal with the same chain.]].

Ahmad said: Waki' related to us, Sufyan related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from a man of Banu Asad, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever asks while he has an uqiyah, or its equivalent, has indeed asked persistently" [[Al-Musnad (4/36).]].
