They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is his sufficiency?" He said: "Fifty dirhams, or its equivalent in gold."

The People of the Four Sunan have indeed narrated it from the hadith of Hakim ibn Jubayr al-Asadi al-Kufi [[Al-Musnad (1/388); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (1626); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (650); Sunan al-Nasa'i (5/97); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (1840).]]. Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj abandoned him, and a number of the imams weakened him because of this hadith.

**Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 272–274 (Part 2 of 2)**

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hadrami narrated to us, Abu Husayn Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: It reached al-Harith, a man from Quraysh who was in Syria, that Abu Dharr was in need, so he sent him three hundred dinars. He said: "Abdullah (Abu Dharr) could not find a man who is easier for him than me. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Whoever asks while he has forty [dirhams] has begged persistently.' And the family of Abu Dharr have forty dirhams, forty sheep, and two servants." Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash said: "He means two servants."

[Note: al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/150). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (9/331): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih except Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus, who is trustworthy."]

Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad informed us, Abdul-Jabbar informed us, Sufyan informed us, from Dawud ibn Sabur, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Whoever asks while he has forty dirhams, then he is a persistent beggar (mulhif), and it is like the sand of the cinder (salaf al-mallah)." He means: the sand.

An-Nasa'i narrated it from Ahmad ibn Sulayman, from Yahya ibn Adam, from Sufyan, who is Ibn Uyaynah, with its chain similar to it.

[Note: Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 2375.]

His saying: ﴿And whatever good you spend, indeed Allah is Knowing of it﴾. That is: nothing of it is hidden from Him, and He will reward it with the fullest and most complete reward on the Day of Resurrection, when they will be most in need of it.

* *

His saying: ﴿Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly, will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾. This is praise from Him, exalted is He, for those who spend in His cause and seek His pleasure at all times, by night or by day, and in all conditions, secretly or openly. Even spending on one's family enters into this, as established in the two Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, when he visited him while he was ill in the year of the Conquest, and in another narration in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage: "Indeed, you will not spend an expenditure seeking thereby the Face of Allah except that you will be raised by it in rank and station, even what you put into the mouth of your wife."

[Note: Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4409, 6373; Sahih Muslim, no. 1628.]

Al-Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Bahz narrated to us, both said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Adi ibn Thabit, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Yazid [in one copy: "Ibn Zayd"] al-Ansari narrate from Abu Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Indeed, when a Muslim spends on his family an expenditure, seeking reward for it, it is recorded as charity for him." Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it from the narration of Shu'bah with this chain.

[Note: al-Musnad (4/122); Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 55; Sahih Muslim, no. 1002.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb narrated to us, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn Urayb al-Maliki, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "This verse was revealed: ﴿Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly, will have their reward with their Lord [and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve]﴾ concerning the companions of the horses."

[Note: Abu al-Shaykh narrated it in al-Azamah (no. 1283) through the chain of Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman, and in its chain is Sa'id ibn Sinan, who is abandoned (matruk) in narration.]

Hanash al-San'ani said, from Ibn Abbas regarding this verse, he said: "They are those who feed horses in the cause of Allah." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, then said: "Similarly it has been narrated from Abu Umamah, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, and Makhul."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Yahya ibn Yaman informed us, from Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mujahid ibn Jabr, from his father, who said: Ali had four dirhams. Ibn Jarir also narrated it through the route of Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mujahid, and he is weak. However, Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through another route from Ibn Abbas that it was revealed concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib.

And whatever good you spend is for yourselves, and you spend only seeking the Face of Allah. And whatever good you spend will be repaid to you, and you will not be wronged﴾" [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11052).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn Atiyyah informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman, meaning al-Dashtaki, related to me, my father related to me, from his father, Ash'ath ibn Ishaq related to us, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he used to order that charity be given only to the people of Islam, until this verse was revealed: ﴿It is not upon you to guide them﴾ to its end, and so he ordered charity to be given after it to everyone who asks you, of every religion [[Ibn Mardawayh and al-Diya' al-Maqdisi are credited with this narration by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (2/86).]]. The hadith of Asma' bint Abi Bakr concerning this will come under the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over religion and do not expel you from your homes﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 8], [if Allah wills] [[Addition from manuscripts J and A.]].

Its summary is that the giver, when he gives seeking the Face of Allah, his reward has fallen upon Allah, and it is not incumbent upon him, in reality, whether the recipient is righteous, wicked, deserving, or otherwise; he is rewarded for his intention. The basis for this is the completion of the verse: ﴿And whatever good you spend will be repaid to you, and you will not be wronged﴾. And the hadith recorded in the Two Sahihs, through the chain of Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A man said: I will surely give charity tonight. So he went out with his charity and placed it in the hand of a prostitute. In the morning, people were talking: Charity was given to a prostitute! He said: O Allah, to You belongs praise, for a prostitute! I will surely give charity tonight. So he went out with his charity and placed it in the hand of a wealthy man. In the morning, they were talking: Charity was given tonight to a wealthy man! He said: O Allah, to You belongs praise, for a wealthy man! I will surely give charity tonight. So he went out with his charity and placed it in the hand of a thief. In the morning, they were talking: Charity was given tonight to a thief! He said: O Allah, to You belongs praise, for a prostitute, for a wealthy man, and for a thief! He was then approached and told: As for your charity, it has been accepted; as for the prostitute, perhaps it will keep her chaste from her fornication; perhaps the wealthy man will take a lesson and spend from what Allah has given him; and perhaps the thief will keep himself chaste from his theft" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (1421), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1022).]].

* *

As for His words: ﴿for the poor who have been confined in the way of Allah﴾, it means: the emigrants who have devoted themselves to Allah and His Messenger, and settled in Medina, having no means by which they can earn for themselves what suffices them. And ﴿they cannot go about in the land﴾ means: travel for the purpose of earning a living. And "going about in the land" means travel. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when you travel in the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer﴾ [al-Nisa': 101]. He, the Exalted, also said: ﴿He knows that there will be among you those who are ill, and others who travel in the land seeking of Allah's bounty, and others who fight in the cause of Allah﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 20], to the end of the verse.

* *

As for His words: ﴿The ignorant one thinks them wealthy because of their modesty﴾, that is: the one ignorant of their affair and their condition thinks them wealthy because of their restraint in their clothing, their state, and their speech. On this meaning is the hadith agreed upon for its authenticity, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The poor man is not the one who goes around and is turned away by a date or two dates, or a morsel or two morsels, or a meal or two meals. An-Nasa'i narrated it from Ahmad ibn Sulayman, from Yahya ibn Adam, from Sufyan, who is Ibn Uyaynah, with its chain similar to it.

[Note: Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 2375.]

His saying: ﴿And whatever good you spend, indeed Allah is Knowing of it﴾. That is: nothing of it is hidden from Him, and He will reward it with the fullest and most complete reward on the Day of Resurrection, when they will be most in need of it.

* *

His saying: ﴿Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly, will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾. This is praise from Him, exalted is He, for those who spend in His cause and seek His pleasure at all times, by night or by day, and in all conditions, secretly or openly. Even spending on one's family enters into this, as established in the two Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, when he visited him while he was ill in the year of the Conquest, and in another narration in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage: "Indeed, you will not spend an expenditure seeking thereby the Face of Allah except that you will be raised by it in rank and station, even what you put into the mouth of your wife."

[Note: Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4409, 6373; Sahih Muslim, no. 1628.]

Al-Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Bahz narrated to us, both said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Adi ibn Thabit, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Yazid [in one copy: "Ibn Zayd"] al-Ansari narrate from Abu Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Indeed, when a Muslim spends on his family an expenditure, seeking reward for it, it is recorded as charity for him." Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it from the narration of Shu'bah with this chain.

[Note: al-Musnad (4/122); Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 55; Sahih Muslim, no. 1002.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb narrated to us, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn Urayb al-Maliki, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "This verse was revealed: ﴿Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly, will have their reward with their Lord [and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve]﴾ concerning the companions of the horses."

[Note: Abu al-Shaykh narrated it in al-Azamah (no. 1283) through the chain of Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman, and in its chain is Sa'id ibn Sinan, who is abandoned (matruk) in narration.]

Hanash al-San'ani said, from Ibn Abbas regarding this verse, he said: "They are those who feed horses in the cause of Allah." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, then said: "Similarly it has been narrated from Abu Umamah, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, and Makhul."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Yahya ibn Yaman informed us, from Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mujahid ibn Jabr, from his father, who said: Ali had four dirhams. He spent one dirham by night, one dirham by day, one dirham secretly, and one dirham publicly, so this verse was revealed: ﴿Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly﴾.

Ibn Jarir also narrated it through the route of Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mujahid, and he is weak. However, Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through another route from Ibn Abbas that it was revealed concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib.

* *

His saying: ﴿Then for them is their reward with their Lord﴾: that is, on the Day of Resurrection, in return for what they did of spending in acts of obedience; ﴿and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾. Its explanation has already preceded.

Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa'i said: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah [[In manuscripts J, A, and W: "ibn Abd al-Salam".]] ibn Abd al-Rahim informed us, [[In manuscript J: "Haddathana" (he related to us).]] al-Firyabi informed us, Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Ja'far ibn Iyas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "They disliked giving charity to their relatives among the polytheists, so they asked, and he (ﷺ) granted them permission, and this verse was revealed: ﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills. And whatever good you spend is for yourselves, and you spend only seeking the Face of Allah. And whatever good you spend will be repaid to you, and you will not be wronged﴾" [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11052).]].

Similarly, Abu Hudhayfah, Ibn al-Mubarak, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri, and Abu Dawud al-Hafari narrated it from Sufyan, meaning al-Thawri, with this chain.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn Atiyyah informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman, meaning al-Dashtaki, related to me, my father related to me, from his father, Ash'ath ibn Ishaq related to us, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he used to order that charity be given only to the people of Islam, until this verse was revealed: ﴿It is not upon you to guide them﴾ to its end, and so he ordered charity to be given after it to everyone who asks you, of every religion [[Ibn Mardawayh and al-Diya' al-Maqdisi are credited with this narration by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (2/86).]]. The hadith of Asma' bint Abi Bakr concerning this will come under the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over religion and do not expel you from your homes﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 8], [if Allah wills] [[Addition from manuscripts J and A.]].

* *

As for His words: ﴿And whatever good you spend is for yourselves﴾, it is like His words: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul﴾ [Fussilat: 46; al-Jathiyah: 15], and similar examples in the Qur'an are numerous [[In manuscript W: "numerous" (without the feminine ending).]].

* *

As for His words: ﴿and you spend only seeking the Face of Allah﴾, al-Hasan al-Basri said: "The believer's spending is for himself, and the believer, when he spends, spends only seeking the Face of Allah."

And Ata' al-Khurasani said: "It means: when you give for the Face of Allah, then it is no concern of yours what the recipient does." This is a good meaning. Its summary is that the giver, when he gives seeking the Face of Allah, his reward has fallen upon Allah, and it is not incumbent upon him, in reality, whether the recipient is righteous, wicked, deserving, or otherwise; he is rewarded for his intention. The basis for this is the completion of the verse: ﴿And whatever good you spend will be repaid to you, and you will not be wronged﴾. And the hadith recorded in the Two Sahihs, through the chain of Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A man said: I will surely give charity tonight. So he went out with his charity and placed it in the hand of a prostitute. In the morning, people were talking: Charity was given to a prostitute! He said: O Allah, to You belongs praise, for a prostitute! I will surely give charity tonight. So he went out with his charity and placed it in the hand of a wealthy man. In the morning, they were talking: Charity was given tonight to a wealthy man! He said: O Allah, to You belongs praise, for a wealthy man! I will surely give charity tonight. So he went out with his charity and placed it in the hand of a thief. In the morning, they were talking: Charity was given tonight to a thief! He said: O Allah, to You belongs praise, for a prostitute, for a wealthy man, and for a thief! He was then approached and told: As for your charity, it has been accepted; as for the prostitute, perhaps it will keep her chaste from her fornication; perhaps the wealthy man will take a lesson and spend from what Allah has given him; and perhaps the thief will keep himself chaste from his theft" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (1421), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1022).]].

* *

As for His words: ﴿for the poor who have been confined in the way of Allah﴾, it means: the emigrants who have devoted themselves to Allah and His Messenger, and settled in Medina, having no means by which they can earn for themselves what suffices them. And ﴿they cannot go about in the land﴾ means: travel for the purpose of earning a living. And "going about in the land" means travel. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when you travel in the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer﴾ [al-Nisa': 101]. He, the Exalted, also said: ﴿He knows that there will be among you those who are ill, and others who travel in the land seeking of Allah's bounty, and others who fight in the cause of Allah﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 20], to the end of the verse.

* *

As for His words: ﴿The ignorant one thinks them wealthy because of their modesty﴾, that is: the one ignorant of their affair and their condition thinks them wealthy because of their restraint in their clothing, their state, and their speech. On this meaning is the hadith agreed upon for its authenticity, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The poor man is not the one who goes around and is turned away by a date or two dates, or a morsel or two morsels, or a meal or two meals. Rather, the poor man is the one who finds no sufficiency to suffice him, and whose need is not recognized so that charity may be given to him, and who does not ask people for anything." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4539), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1039).] Ahmad also narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud [al-Musnad (1/384)].

* *

As for His words: ﴿You will recognize them by their mark﴾, that is: by what appears to people of understanding of their qualities, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Their mark is on their faces﴾ [al-Fath: 29], and He said: ﴿And you will surely know them by the tone of their speech﴾ [Muhammad: 30]. And in the hadith in the Sunan: "Beware of the insight of the believer, for he looks with the light of Allah," then he recited: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for those who perceive [al-mutawassimin]﴾ [al-Hijr: 75] [[Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Sunan, no. (3127), through the chain of Amr ibn Qays, from Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with him, as a marfu' hadith. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a gharib hadith; we only know it from this route, and it has been narrated from some scholars."]].

* *

As for His words: ﴿They do not ask people persistently﴾, that is: they do not press in asking, nor burden people with what they do not need. For whoever asks while he has what suffices him from asking has indeed pressed in asking. Al-Bukhari said: Ibn Abi Maryam related to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, Shurayk ibn Abi Namir related to us: that Ata' ibn Yasar and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Amrah al-Ansari said: "We heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The poor man is not the one who is turned away by a date or two dates, nor a morsel or two morsels. Rather, the poor man is the one who keeps himself chaste. Recite if you wish: ﴿They do not ask people persistently﴾,'" meaning His words [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4539).]].

Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Isma'il ibn Ja'far al-Madini, from Shurayk ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Namir, from Ata' ibn Yasar alone, from Abu Hurayrah, with the same wording [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1039).]].

Al-Nasa'i said [[In manuscript W: "And al-Nasa'i narrated it, and its wording is:"]]: Ali ibn Hujr informed us, Isma'il related to us, Shurayk, who is Ibn Abi Namir, informed us, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "The poor man is not the one who is turned away by a date or two dates, or a morsel or two morsels. Rather, the poor man is the one who keeps himself chaste. Recite if you wish: ﴿They do not ask people persistently﴾" [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11053).]].

Al-Bukhari narrated, from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (1476).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn Abd al-Ala informed us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Ibn Abi Dhi'b informed me, from Abu al-Walid, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The poor man is not the one who goes around to you, so that you give him a morsel at a time. Rather, the poor man is the one who keeps himself chaste, who does not ask people persistently."

Ibn Jarir said: Mu'tamir related to me, from al-Hasan ibn Matik [[In manuscripts J and A: "al-Hasan ibn Babil"; in manuscript W: "Ayman ibn Nabil".]], from Salih ibn Suwayd, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "The poor man is not the one who goes around and is turned away by a meal or two meals. Rather, the poor man is the one who keeps modest in his home, who does not ask people for anything he needs. Recite if you wish: ﴿They do not ask people persistently﴾."

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi related to us, Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far related to us, from his father, from a man of Muzaynah, that his mother said to him: "Will you not go and ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as people ask him?" So I went to ask him, and I found him standing and delivering a sermon, and he was saying: "Whoever seeks to be chaste, Allah will keep him chaste; whoever seeks self-sufficiency, Allah will make him self-sufficient; and whoever asks people while he has the equivalent of five awqiyah, he has indeed pressed in asking." So I said to myself: My she-camel is better than five awqiyah, and her companion [a young man] has another she-camel which is better than five awqiyah. So I returned without asking [[Al-Musnad (4/138).]].

Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah related to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Rijal related to us, from Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa'id, from his father, who said: "My mother sent me to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to ask him. So I came to him and sat down. He said: He faced me and said: 'Whoever seeks self-sufficiency, Allah will make him self-sufficient; whoever seeks to be chaste, Allah will keep him chaste; whoever seeks to be restrained, Allah will suffice him; and whoever asks while he has the value of an uqiyah, he has indeed pressed in asking.' So I said: My camel Al-Yaqutah is better than an uqiyah. So I returned and did not ask him."

Likewise Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated it, both from Qutaybah. Abu Dawud added: and Hisham ibn Ammar; both from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Rijal with its chain, similarly [[Al-Musnad (3/9); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (1628); Sunan al-Nasa'i (5/98).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to me, Abu al-Jamahir related to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Rijal related to us, from Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa'id, who said: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever asks while he has an uqiyah is a persistent asker." And the uqiyah is forty dirhams [[Ibn Khuzaymah narrated it in his Sahih, no. (2447), and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, no. (846), through the route of Abd Allah ibn Yusuf, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Rijal with the same chain.]].

Ahmad said: Waki' related to us, Sufyan related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from a man of Banu Asad, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever asks while he has an uqiyah, or its equivalent, has indeed asked persistently" [[Al-Musnad (4/36).]].

Imam Ahmad also said: Waki' related to us, Sufyan related to us, from Hakim ibn Jubayr, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from his father, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever asks while he has what suffices him, his asking will come on the Day of Resurrection as scratches, or wounds, upon his face." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is his sufficiency?" He said: "Fifty dirhams, or its equivalent in gold."

The People of the Four Sunan have indeed narrated it from the hadith of Hakim ibn Jubayr al-Asadi al-Kufi [[Al-Musnad (1/388); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (1626); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (650); Sunan al-Nasa'i (5/97); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (1840).]]. Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj abandoned him, and a number of the imams weakened him because of this hadith.

**Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 272–274 (Part 2 of 2)**

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hadrami narrated to us, Abu Husayn Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: It reached al-Harith, a man from Quraysh who was in Syria, that Abu Dharr was in need, so he sent him three hundred dinars. He said: "Abdullah (Abu Dharr) could not find a man who is easier for him than me. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Whoever asks while he has forty [dirhams] has begged persistently.' And the family of Abu Dharr have forty dirhams, forty sheep, and two servants." Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash said: "He means two servants."

[Note: al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/150). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (9/331): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih except Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus, who is trustworthy."]

Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad informed us, Abdul-Jabbar informed us, Sufyan informed us, from Dawud ibn Sabur, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Whoever asks while he has forty dirhams, then he is a persistent beggar (mulhif), and it is like the sand of the cinder (salaf al-mallah)." He means: the sand.

An-Nasa'i narrated it from Ahmad ibn Sulayman, from Yahya ibn Adam, from Sufyan, who is Ibn Uyaynah, with its chain similar to it.

[Note: Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 2375.]

His saying: ﴿And whatever good you spend, indeed Allah is Knowing of it﴾. That is: nothing of it is hidden from Him, and He will reward it with the fullest and most complete reward on the Day of Resurrection, when they will be most in need of it.

* *

His saying: ﴿Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly, will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾. This is praise from Him, exalted is He, for those who spend in His cause and seek His pleasure at all times, by night or by day, and in all conditions, secretly or openly. Even spending on one's family enters into this, as established in the two Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, when he visited him while he was ill in the year of the Conquest, and in another narration in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage: "Indeed, you will not spend an expenditure seeking thereby the Face of Allah except that you will be raised by it in rank and station, even what you put into the mouth of your wife."

[Note: Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4409, 6373; Sahih Muslim, no. 1628.]

Al-Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Bahz narrated to us, both said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Adi ibn Thabit, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Yazid [in one copy: "Ibn Zayd"] al-Ansari narrate from Abu Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Indeed, when a Muslim spends on his family an expenditure, seeking reward for it, it is recorded as charity for him." Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it from the narration of Shu'bah with this chain.

[Note: al-Musnad (4/122); Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 55; Sahih Muslim, no. 1002.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb narrated to us, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn Urayb al-Maliki, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "This verse was revealed: ﴿Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly, will have their reward with their Lord [and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve]﴾ concerning the companions of the horses."

[Note: Abu al-Shaykh narrated it in al-Azamah (no. 1283) through the chain of Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman, and in its chain is Sa'id ibn Sinan, who is abandoned (matruk) in narration.]

Hanash al-San'ani said, from Ibn Abbas regarding this verse, he said: "They are those who feed horses in the cause of Allah." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, then said: "Similarly it has been narrated from Abu Umamah, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, and Makhul."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Yahya ibn Yaman informed us, from Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mujahid ibn Jabr, from his father, who said: Ali had four dirhams. He spent one dirham by night, one dirham by day, one dirham secretly, and one dirham publicly, so this verse was revealed: ﴿Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly﴾.

Ibn Jarir also narrated it through the route of Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mujahid, and he is weak. However, Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through another route from Ibn Abbas that it was revealed concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib.

* *

His saying: ﴿Then for them is their reward with their Lord﴾: that is, on the Day of Resurrection, in return for what they did of spending in acts of obedience; ﴿and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾. Its explanation has already preceded.

When Allah Most High mentioned the righteous who spend their wealth, who give out zakat (obligatory alms), and who bestow kindness and charity upon those in need and upon relatives in all circumstances and at all times, He began to mention the consumers of ribā (usury) and those who consume people's wealth falsely, along with various kinds of doubtful dealings. He informed about them on the Day of their emergence from their graves and their rising to their resurrection and gathering. He said:

﴿Those who consume ribā will not rise except as one rises whom Satan has driven to madness by his touch.﴾ That is, they will not rise from their graves on the Day of Resurrection except as the one who is seized by a fit rises during his seizure and the devil's stricken state, for he rises in a hideous manner.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: The consumer of ribā will be raised on the Day of Resurrection insane and choking. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, who said: It was also narrated from ʿAwf ibn Malik, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, al-Suddi, al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas and Muqatil ibn Hayyan something similar to this.

It is related from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas, ʿIkrimah, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah and Muqatil ibn Hayyan that they said concerning His words, ﴿Those who consume ribā will not rise except as one rises whom Satan has driven to madness by his touch,﴾ meaning: they will not rise on the Day of Resurrection. Likewise said Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated, through the hadith of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam, from Damrah ibn Habib, from Ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, from his father, that he used to recite: "Those who consume ribā will not rise except as one rises whom Satan has driven to madness by his touch, on the Day of Resurrection."

Ibn Jarir said: al-Muthanna related to me: Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us: Rabiʿah ibn Kulthum related to us: my father related to us, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: It will be said on the Day of Resurrection to the consumer of ribā: "Take your weapon for war." And he recited: ﴿will not rise except as one rises whom Satan has driven to madness by his touch,﴾ and said: That is when he rises from his grave.

In the hadith of Abu Saʿid concerning the Night Journey (al-Isra'), as mentioned in Surat Subhan, that the Prophet (ﷺ) passed that night by a people who had bellies like houses. He asked about them and it was said: "These are the consumers of ribā." Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in an extended form.

Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah related to us: al-Hasan ibn Musa related to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from ʿAli ibn Zayd, from Abu al-Salt, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I came upon a people whose bellies were like houses, in which there were snakes visible from outside their bellies. I said: 'Who are these, O Jibril?' He said: 'These are the consumers of ribā.'"

Imam Ahmad also narrated it from Hasan and ʿAffan, both from Hammad ibn Salamah, with this same chain. There is weakness in its chain of narration.

Al-Bukhari narrated from Samurah ibn Jundub in the lengthy hadith of the dream: "We came upon a river — I think he said: red like blood — and in the river was a man swimming, and on the bank of the river was a man who had gathered many stones beside him. That swimmer kept swimming, then he would come to the one who had gathered the stones, and he would open his mouth and the other would throw a stone into it." He also mentioned in its explanation that the one in the river is the consumer of ribā. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 7047.]

* *

His words: ﴿That is because they said: "Trade is only like ribā," while Allah has permitted trade and forbidden ribā.﴾ That is: they were recompensed this way because of their objection to the rulings of Allah in His legislation. This was not an analogy on their part (qiyas) of ribā to trade, because the polytheists did not acknowledge the legitimacy of the basic principle of trade which Allah legislated in the Qur'an. Had this been an analogy, they would have said: "Ribā is only like trade." Rather, they said: ﴿Trade is only like ribā,﴾ meaning: it is its equivalent. So why is this forbidden and that permitted? This is an objection on their part to the Sharia: "This is like that, yet He has permitted this and forbidden that!"

* *

His saying, Most High: ﴿And Allah has permitted trade and forbidden ribā﴾ may be part of the speech as a rebuttal to them, meaning: they said what they said as an objection, despite their knowledge that Allah has distinguished between this and that in ruling. He is the Wise, the All-Knowing, whose judgment none can repel, and He is not questioned about what He does, while they will be questioned. He knows the realities of matters and their benefits, and what benefits His servants, so He permits it for them, and what harms them, so He forbids them from it. He is more merciful to them than a mother to her infant child. For this reason He said: ﴿So whoever has received an admonition from his Lord and desists, for him is what has passed, and his affair is up to Allah.﴾ That is: whoever has received Allah's prohibition of ribā and desisted at the time the Sharia reached him, for him is what has passed of the transactions, in accordance with His saying: ﴿Allah has pardoned what has passed﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 95]. And as the Prophet (ﷺ) said on the day of the Conquest of Makkah: "Every ribā of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic period) is abolished under these two feet of mine, and the first ribā I abolish is the ribā of al-ʿAbbas." [Note by Shaykh Ahmad Shakir, may Allah have mercy on him, in ʿUmdat al-Tafsir (2/189): "The Hafiz Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, made an error here, for this did not happen on the day of the Conquest of Makkah, but rather in the Farewell Pilgrimage, in his (ﷺ) sermon at ʿArafah." I say: This has been stated explicitly in the narration of ʿAmr ibn al-Ahwas, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) during the Farewell Pilgrimage say: "Indeed every ribā of the Jahiliyyah is abolished…" and he mentioned the hadith. It was narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. 3334, and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. 3087.] He did not command them to return the excess taken during the time of Jahiliyyah, but pardoned what had passed, as Allah Most High said: ﴿For him is what has passed and his affair is up to Allah.﴾

Saʿid ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi said: ﴿For him is what has passed﴾ means that what he had consumed of ribā before the prohibition is his.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was read upon Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Hakam: Ibn Wahb informed us: Jarir ibn Hazim informed me, from Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani, from Umm Yunus — meaning his wife al-ʿAliyah bint Ayfaʿ — that ʿAʾishah, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), was told by Umm Muhabbah (the umm walad of Zayd ibn Arqam): "O Mother of the Believers, do you know Zayd ibn Arqam?" She said: "Yes." She said: "I sold him a slave on credit until the stipend for eight hundred, then he needed its price, so I bought it back from him before the due date for six hundred." ʿAʾishah said: "Evil is what you bought and evil is what you sold! Inform Zayd that he has nullified his jihad with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) unless he repents." She said: I asked: "What if I leave the two hundred and take the six hundred?" She said: "Yes: ﴿So whoever has received an admonition from his Lord and desists, for him is what has passed.﴾" [In another copy: "min" — the correct reading is as in the other copies.]

This report is well known, and it is evidence for those who prohibit the ʿinah (a sale device used to circumvent ribā), along with what has come concerning it in the hadiths established in the Book of Rulings. To Allah belongs praise and grace.

Then Allah Most High said: ﴿And whoever returns﴾ — that is, to ribā, doing it after the prohibition of Allah reached him — ﴿those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.﴾ He has deserved the punishment and the proof has been established against him. For this reason He said: ﴿Those are the companions of the Fire, they will abide therein forever.﴾

Abu Dawud said: Yahya ibn Maʿin related to us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Raja' al-Makki informed us, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUthman ibn Khuthaym, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: When the verse was revealed: ﴿Those who consume ribā will not rise except as one rises whom Satan has driven to madness by his touch,﴾ the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever does not abandon al-Mukhabarah, let him be warned of war from Allah and His Messenger." [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 3406.]

Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak, through the hadith of Ibn Khuthaym, and said: "Sahih according to the condition of Muslim, though he did not record it." [Al-Mustadrak (2/286); in it the wording is: "wa lam yukhrijahu" (though he did not record it).]

Al-Mukhabarah was prohibited; it is sharecropping in exchange for a portion of what the land produces. Al-Muzabanah is buying fresh dates on the palm trees for dried dates on the ground. Al-Muhaqalah is buying grain in its ear in the field for grain on the ground. These things and what resembles them were prohibited only as a means of closing the door to ribā, since equality between the two items cannot be known before drying. For this reason the jurists said: "Ignorance of equivalence is like certainty of excess." From this, they forbade things according to what they understood of the narrowing of the paths leading to ribā and the means conveying to it. Their perspectives differed according to the knowledge Allah bestowed upon each of them. Allah the Most High has said: ﴿And above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowing.﴾ [Yusuf: 76.]

The chapter of ribā is among the most difficult chapters for many people of knowledge. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, the Commander of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "There are three matters I wished the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had made a clear covenant with us about, a covenant we could adhere to: the grandfather, the kalalah (one who leaves neither father nor child), and some chapters of ribā." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 5588, and Muslim in his Sahih, no. 3032.] He meant by this some issues in which there is a trace of ribā. The Sharia testifies that every prohibited thing has a means to it that is like it, because what leads to the prohibited is itself prohibited, just as what the obligation cannot be completed without is itself obligatory.

It is established in the two Sahihs from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed the lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear, and between them are doubtful matters. Whoever avoids doubtful matters has cleared himself regarding his religion and his honour, and whoever falls into doubtful matters has fallen into the unlawful, like a shepherd who grazes around the sanctuary, about to graze within it." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 52; Sahih Muslim, no. 1599.]

In the Sunan, from al-Hasan ibn ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt." [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2518; Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/327). Al-Hafiz Ibn Rajab extensively discussed it in Jami' al-ʿUlum wa al-Hikam (1/278), ed. al-Risalah.] In another hadith: "Sin is that which stirs in the heart and the soul is troubled by it, and you dislike that people should see it." In another narration: "Consult your heart, even if people give you verdicts and give you verdicts." [Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (4/228) through the chain of al-Zubayr ibn ʿAbd al-Salam, from Ayyub, from Wabisah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Al-Thawri said, from ʿAsim, from al-Shaʿbi, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "The last thing revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the verse of ribā." Al-Bukhari narrated it from Qabisah, from him. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4544.]

Ahmad said, from Yahya, from Saʿid ibn Abi ʿArubah, from Qatadah, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib, that ʿUmar said: "Among the last things revealed is the verse of ribā, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed away before explaining it to us, so abandon ribā and what casts doubt."

It was narrated by Ibn Majah and Ibn Mardawayh. [Al-Musnad (1/36); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2276. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (2/198): "This chain is sahih and its narrators are trustworthy."]

Ibn Mardawayh narrated through Hayyaj ibn Bastam, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Abu Nadrah [[In Ms. J and A: "from Abu Basrah".]], from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: "'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, addressed us and said: 'Indeed, I may forbid you from things that are good for you and command you to things that are not good for you. Among the last verses of the Qur'an to be revealed is the verse on riba (usury), and indeed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died without explaining it to us. So leave that which makes you doubtful for that which does not make you doubtful.'"

Ibn Majah said: Amr ibn 'Ali al-Sayrafi narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Zubayd, from Ibrahim, from Masruq, from 'Abd Allah (i.e., Ibn Mas'ud), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Riba has seventy-three doors" [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (2275). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (2/198): "This is a sound chain (isnad)."]].

Al-Hakim narrated it in his al-Mustadrak, from the hadith of Amr ibn 'Ali al-Fallas, with a similar chain, and he added: "The least of it is that a man marries his mother, and the gravest form of riba is the violation of the honour of a Muslim man." He said: "It is sound according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it" [[al-Mustadrak (2/37).]].

Ibn Majah said: 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Idris narrated to us, from Abu Ma'shar, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Riba has seventy sins (huwb), the least of which is that a man marries his mother" [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (2274). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (2/197): "This chain is weak."]].

Imam Ahmad said: Hushaym narrated to us, from 'Abbad ibn Rashid, from Sa'id ibn Abi Khayrah [[In Ms. A: "from Sa'id ibn Jubayr".]], narrated to us al-Hasan (since about forty or fifty years ago), from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A time will come upon the people when they will consume riba." It was said to him: "All of the people?" He said: "Whoever does not consume it will be touched by its dust." Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah also narrated it through other routes, from Sa'id ibn Abi Khayrah [[In Ms. A: "Sa'id ibn Abi Jurrah".]], from al-Hasan, with the same wording [[al-Musnad (2/494); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (1331); Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/243); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (2278).]].

From this category, which is the prohibition of the means that lead to the forbidden, is the hadith that Imam Ahmad narrated: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Muslim ibn Subayh, from Masruq, from 'A'ishah, who said: "When the verses at the end of al-Baqarah concerning riba were revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to the mosque, recited them, and forbade trade in wine."

The group (al-Jama'ah) other than al-Tirmidhi also recorded it through several routes, from al-A'mash with this wording [[al-Musnad (6/46); Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (4540, 4541); Sahih Muslim, no. (1580); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (3490); al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Nasa'i, no. (11055); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3382).]]. This is the wording of al-Bukhari's narration when commenting on the verse: "So he forbade trade." In another wording of his, from 'A'ishah, she said: "When the verses at the end of Surat al-Baqarah concerning riba were revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited them to the people, then forbade trade in wine." Some of the scholars (a'immah) who discussed this hadith said: When he forbade riba and its means, he forbade wine and what leads to it of trade and the like, just as he (peace be upon him) said in the hadith agreed upon: "May Allah curse the Jews: fat was forbidden to them, so they melted it, sold it, and consumed its price" [[Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (2223), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (1582), from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

It has already been mentioned, in the hadith of 'Ali, Ibn Mas'ud and others, in the commentary on the cursing of the one who makes a woman lawful (muhallil) at His words ﴿until she marries another husband﴾ [al-Baqarah: 230], the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Allah curses the one who consumes riba, the one who pays it, its two witnesses, and its scribe." They said: Witnessing and writing it occur only when it is presented in the form of a legitimate contract while its inner reality is corrupt. So the consideration is given to its meaning, not its outward form, because "actions are judged by intentions" (al-a'mal bi'l-niyyat), and in the Sahih: "Indeed Allah does not look at your forms or your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (2564), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

The Imam, the great scholar (al-'Allamah) Abu al-'Abbas Ibn Taymiyyah, authored a book on "Invalidating Tahlil" (Ibtal al-Tahlil) [[It is a sound book, recently published in an edited edition.]] which included the prohibition of engaging in the means that lead to every falsehood, and it suffices in this and is healing. May Allah have mercy on him and be pleased with him.

God tells us that He destroys interest (ribā), meaning He eliminates it. This may happen either by removing it entirely from the hand of its owner, or by depriving him of the blessing of his wealth, so that he gains no benefit from it. Rather, it punishes him through it in this world and holds him accountable for it on the Day of Resurrection. As He said: ﴿Say: "The evil and the good are not equal, even if the abundance of the evil impresses you."﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 100]. He also said: ﴿And He puts the evil on top of one another, heaps it all together, and places it in Hell.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 37]. And He said: ﴿And whatever you give in interest to increase within people's wealth, it does not increase with Allah﴾ [the verse] [[Addition from manuscripts ج، أ، و.]] [Ar-Rum: 39].

Ibn Jarir said, regarding His words ﴿Allah destroys interest﴾: This is similar to the report transmitted from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Interest, however much it increases, ends in decline."

This hadith was narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad. He said: Hajjaj [[Addition from manuscripts ج، أ، و.]] told us: Shurayk told us, from al-Rukayn ibn al-Rabi' [ibn 'Umayla al-Fazari] [[Addition from manuscript ج.]], from his father, from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Indeed, interest, however much it increases, its end will be decline." [[Al-Musnad (1/395).]] It was also narrated by Ibn Majah, from al-Abbas ibn Ja'far, from Amr ibn 'Awn, from Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah, from Isra'il, from al-Rukayn ibn al-Rabi' ibn 'Umayla al-Fazari, from his father, from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "No one increases in interest except that the end of his affair is decline." [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (2289). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (2/199): "This chain is sound, and its narrators are trustworthy."]]

This is from the category of dealing that produces the opposite of the intended result. As Imam Ahmad said: Abu Sa'id, client (mawla) of the Banu Hashim, told us: al-Haytham ibn Rafi' al-Tatari told us: Abu Yahya, a man [[In manuscript ج: "a man who came out"]] from the people of Makkah, related from Farrukh, client of Uthman: that 'Umar, who at that time was Amir al-Mu'minin, went out to the mosque and saw food scattered about. He said: "What is this food?" They said: "Food that was brought to us." He said: "May Allah bless it and whoever brought it." It was said: "O Commander of the Faithful, it has been hoarded (ihtikar)." He said: "And who hoarded it?" They said: "Farrukh, client of Uthman, and so-and-so, client of 'Umar." So he sent for them both, summoned them, and said: "What led you two to hoard the food of the Muslims?" They said: "O Commander of the Faithful, we buy with our own wealth and sell!" 'Umar said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Whoever hoards food against the Muslims, Allah will afflict him with poverty or with leprosy.'" At that, Farrukh said: "I covenant with Allah and with you that I will never return to hoarding food again." As for the client of 'Umar, he said: "We only buy with our wealth and sell." Abu Yahya said: "I indeed saw the client of 'Umar afflicted with leprosy."

Ibn Majah also narrated it from the hadith of al-Haytham ibn Rafi', with the same chain. [[Al-Musnad (1/21) and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (2155).]] Its wording is: "Whoever hoards food against the Muslims, Allah will afflict him with leprosy and poverty."

* *

As for His words ﴿and He makes charities grow﴾: it was read with a dammah on the yā' and light (non-doubled) pronunciation, from "rabā al-shay'u yarbū" and "arbāhu yurbīhi", meaning he increased it and made it grow, so it grows. It was also read "wayurabbī" with a dammah and doubled rā', from tarbiyah (nurturing), as al-Bukhari said: 'Abdullah ibn Munir told us, he heard Abu al-Nadr; 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abdullah ibn Dinar told us, from his father, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever gives in charity the equivalent of a date from lawful earnings, and Allah accepts only what is good, then indeed Allah receives it with His right hand, then nurtures it for its giver, just as one of you nurtures his foal, until it becomes like a mountain."

He narrated it thus in the Book of Zakat. In the Book of Tawhid he said: Khalid ibn Makhlad said, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, from 'Abdullah ibn Dinar, and he mentioned its chain, similar to it. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (1410) and (7430).]]

Muslim also narrated it in the Book of Zakat from Ahmad ibn 'Uthman ibn Hakim, from Khalid ibn Makhlad, and mentioned it. [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1014).]] Al-Bukhari said: Muslim ibn Abi Maryam, Zayd ibn Aslam, and Suhayl also narrated it, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ.

I say: As for the narration of Muslim ibn Abi Maryam, al-Bukhari alone mentioned it. As for the route of Zayd ibn Aslam, Muslim narrated it in his Sahih, from Abu al-Tahir ibn al-Sarh, from Ibn Wahb, from Hisham ibn Sa'd, from Zayd ibn Aslam, with it. [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1014).]] As for the hadith of Suhayl, Muslim narrated it from Qutaybah, from Ya'qub ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Suhayl, with it. [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1014).]] And Allah knows best.

Al-Bukhari said: Warqa' narrated from Ibn Dinar, from Sa'id ibn Yasar [[In manuscript أ: "ibn Bashshar".]], from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (1410, 7430).]]

This hadith was also traced through this route by the hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi, from al-Hakim and others, from al-Asamm, from al-'Abbas al-Marwazi [[In manuscripts أ، و: "al-Duri".]], from Abu al-Nadr Hashim ibn al-Qasim, from Warqa' (he is Ibn 'Umar al-Yashkuri), from 'Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Sa'id ibn Yasar [[In manuscript أ: "ibn Bashshar".]], from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever gives in charity the equivalent of a date from lawful earnings, and nothing good ascends to Allah except the good, then indeed Allah receives it with His right hand, and nurtures it for its owner, just as one of you nurtures his foal, until it becomes like Uhud." [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Bayhaqi (4/176).]]

This hadith was narrated in the same way by Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i, all of them from Qutaybah, from al-Layth ibn Sa'd, from Sa'id al-Maqburi. Al-Nasa'i also narrated it through Malik, from Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari, and through the route of Yahya al-Qattan, from Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan. All three transmitted from Sa'id ibn Yasar Abu al-Hubab al-Madani, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, and mentioned it. [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1014); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (661); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (7735).]]

It was also narrated from Abu Hurayrah through another route. Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Amr ibn 'Abdullah al-Awdi told us, Waki' told us, from 'Abbad ibn Mansur, al-Qasim ibn Muhammad told us, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, accepts charity and takes it with His right hand, then nurtures it for one of you, just as one of you nurtures his colt or his foal, until indeed a morsel becomes like Uhud." And its confirmation in the Book of Allah is His words: ﴿Allah destroys interest and makes charities grow﴾.

Likewise Ahmad narrated it from Waki', and it is in Waki's Tafsir. al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Waki', with it, [[Al-Musnad (2/471) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (662).]] and said: "Hasan sahih." Likewise al-Thawri narrated it from 'Abbad ibn Mansur, with it. Ahmad also narrated it from Khalaf ibn al-Walid, from Ibn al-Mubarak, from 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Damrah and 'Abbad ibn Mansur, both from Abu Nadrah, from al-Qasim, with it. [[Al-Musnad (2/404).]]

Ibn Jarir narrated it from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Ishaq [[In manuscripts أ، و: "from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Malik Zanjawayh".]], from 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed when a servant gives in charity from good earnings, Allah accepts it from him and takes it with His right hand, and nurtures it as one of you nurtures his young horse or his foal. And indeed a man gives in charity a morsel, and it grows in the hand of Allah, or he said: in the palm of Allah, until it becomes like Uhud. So give in charity." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (6/19).]]

Likewise Ahmad narrated it from 'Abd al-Razzaq. [[Al-Musnad (2/268).]] This is a strange route with a sound chain, but its wording is strange, and the preserved version is the one mentioned earlier. It was also narrated from 'A'isha, Mother of the Believers, and Imam Ahmad said:

Abd al-Samad told us, Hammad told us, from Thabit, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'A'isha, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah nurtures for one of you a date or a morsel, just as one of you nurtures his colt or his foal, until it becomes like Uhud." Ahmad alone narrated it through this route. [[Al-Musnad (6/251).]]

Al-Bazzar said: Yahya ibn al-Mu'alla ibn Mansur told us, Isma'il told us, my father told me, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from 'Amrah, from 'A'isha, from the Prophet ﷺ, and from al-Dahhak ibn 'Uthman, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Indeed a man gives in charity from lawful earnings, and Allah accepts only what is good, so the Merciful receives it with His hand and nurtures it, just as one of you nurtures his colt, or his servant, or he said: his foal." Then he said: "We do not know anyone who narrated it from Yahya ibn Sa'id ibn 'Amrah except Abu Uways." [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. (931), Kashf al-Astar. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said: "Abu Uways is weak (layyin), and al-Bazzar mentioned that he alone narrated it."
Note: Kashf al-Astar does not contain "from al-Dahhak, from Abu Hurayrah," because it is recorded in the two Sahihs and therefore is not among the additions (zawa'id).]]

* *

As for His words ﴿And Allah does not love every ungrateful sinner﴾: meaning He does not love one who is ungrateful in heart and sinful in speech and action. It is necessary to note the connection in ending this verse with this attribute: the one who deals in interest is not content with what Allah has apportioned to him of lawful provision, and does not suffice with the permissible earning He has prescribed for him. Rather, he strives to consume people's wealth falsely, through various kinds of evil gains. Thus he is ungrateful for the blessing upon him, and a wrongdoer, sinful by consuming people's wealth falsely.

Then Allah said, praising the believers who are devoted to their Lord, obedient to His command, and thankful to Him, who do good to His creation by establishing prayer and giving zakat, informing of the honor prepared for them, and that on the Day of Resurrection they will be safe from consequences. He said: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, establish prayer, and give zakat, for them is their reward with their Lord, and there is no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.﴾

God tells us that He destroys interest (ribā), meaning He eliminates it. This may happen either by removing it entirely from the hand of its owner, or by depriving him of the blessing of his wealth, so that he gains no benefit from it. Rather, it punishes him through it in this world and holds him accountable for it on the Day of Resurrection. As He said: ﴿Say: "The evil and the good are not equal, even if the abundance of the evil impresses you."﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 100]. He also said: ﴿And He puts the evil on top of one another, heaps it all together, and places it in Hell.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 37]. And He said: ﴿And whatever you give in interest to increase within people's wealth, it does not increase with Allah﴾ [the verse] [[Addition from manuscripts ج، أ، و.]] [Ar-Rum: 39].

Ibn Jarir said, regarding His words ﴿Allah destroys interest﴾: This is similar to the report transmitted from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Interest, however much it increases, ends in decline."

This hadith was narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad. He said: Hajjaj [[Addition from manuscripts ج، أ، و.]] told us: Shurayk told us, from al-Rukayn ibn al-Rabi' [ibn 'Umayla al-Fazari] [[Addition from manuscript ج.]], from his father, from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Indeed, interest, however much it increases, its end will be decline." [[Al-Musnad (1/395).]] It was also narrated by Ibn Majah, from al-Abbas ibn Ja'far, from Amr ibn 'Awn, from Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah, from Isra'il, from al-Rukayn ibn al-Rabi' ibn 'Umayla al-Fazari, from his father, from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "No one increases in interest except that the end of his affair is decline." [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (2289). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (2/199): "This chain is sound, and its narrators are trustworthy."]]

This is from the category of dealing that produces the opposite of the intended result. As Imam Ahmad said: Abu Sa'id, client (mawla) of the Banu Hashim, told us: al-Haytham ibn Rafi' al-Tatari told us: Abu Yahya, a man [[In manuscript ج: "a man who came out"]] from the people of Makkah, related from Farrukh, client of Uthman: that 'Umar, who at that time was Amir al-Mu'minin, went out to the mosque and saw food scattered about. He said: "What is this food?" They said: "Food that was brought to us." He said: "May Allah bless it and whoever brought it." It was said: "O Commander of the Faithful, it has been hoarded (ihtikar)." He said: "And who hoarded it?" They said: "Farrukh, client of Uthman, and so-and-so, client of 'Umar." So he sent for them both, summoned them, and said: "What led you two to hoard the food of the Muslims?" They said: "O Commander of the Faithful, we buy with our own wealth and sell!" 'Umar said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Whoever hoards food against the Muslims, Allah will afflict him with poverty or with leprosy.'" At that, Farrukh said: "I covenant with Allah and with you that I will never return to hoarding food again." As for the client of 'Umar, he said: "We only buy with our wealth and sell." Abu Yahya said: "I indeed saw the client of 'Umar afflicted with leprosy."

Ibn Majah also narrated it from the hadith of al-Haytham ibn Rafi', with the same chain. [[Al-Musnad (1/21) and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (2155).]] Its wording is: "Whoever hoards food against the Muslims, Allah will afflict him with leprosy and poverty."

* *

As for His words ﴿and He makes charities grow﴾: it was read with a dammah on the yā' and light (non-doubled) pronunciation, from "rabā al-shay'u yarbū" and "arbāhu yurbīhi", meaning he increased it and made it grow, so it grows. It was also read "wayurabbī" with a dammah and doubled rā', from tarbiyah (nurturing), as al-Bukhari said: 'Abdullah ibn Munir told us, he heard Abu al-Nadr; 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abdullah ibn Dinar told us, from his father, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever gives in charity the equivalent of a date from lawful earnings, and Allah accepts only what is good, then indeed Allah receives it with His right hand, then nurtures it for its giver, just as one of you nurtures his foal, until it becomes like a mountain."

He narrated it thus in the Book of Zakat. In the Book of Tawhid he said: Khalid ibn Makhlad said, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, from 'Abdullah ibn Dinar, and he mentioned its chain, similar to it. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (1410) and (7430).]]

Muslim also narrated it in the Book of Zakat from Ahmad ibn 'Uthman ibn Hakim, from Khalid ibn Makhlad, and mentioned it. [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1014).]] Al-Bukhari said: Muslim ibn Abi Maryam, Zayd ibn Aslam, and Suhayl also narrated it, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ.

I say: As for the narration of Muslim ibn Abi Maryam, al-Bukhari alone mentioned it. As for the route of Zayd ibn Aslam, Muslim narrated it in his Sahih, from Abu al-Tahir ibn al-Sarh, from Ibn Wahb, from Hisham ibn Sa'd, from Zayd ibn Aslam, with it. [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1014).]] As for the hadith of Suhayl, Muslim narrated it from Qutaybah, from Ya'qub ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Suhayl, with it. [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1014).]] And Allah knows best.

Al-Bukhari said: Warqa' narrated from Ibn Dinar, from Sa'id ibn Yasar [[In manuscript أ: "ibn Bashshar".]], from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (1410, 7430).]]

This hadith was also traced through this route by the hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi, from al-Hakim and others, from al-Asamm, from al-'Abbas al-Marwazi [[In manuscripts أ، و: "al-Duri".]], from Abu al-Nadr Hashim ibn al-Qasim, from Warqa' (he is Ibn 'Umar al-Yashkuri), from 'Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Sa'id ibn Yasar [[In manuscript أ: "ibn Bashshar".]], from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever gives in charity the equivalent of a date from lawful earnings, and nothing good ascends to Allah except the good, then indeed Allah receives it with His right hand, and nurtures it for its owner, just as one of you nurtures his foal, until it becomes like Uhud." [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Bayhaqi (4/176).]]

This hadith was narrated in the same way by Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i, all of them from Qutaybah, from al-Layth ibn Sa'd, from Sa'id al-Maqburi. Al-Nasa'i also narrated it through Malik, from Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari, and through the route of Yahya al-Qattan, from Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan. All three transmitted from Sa'id ibn Yasar Abu al-Hubab al-Madani, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, and mentioned it. [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1014); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (661); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (7735).]]

It was also narrated from Abu Hurayrah through another route. Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Amr ibn 'Abdullah al-Awdi told us, Waki' told us, from 'Abbad ibn Mansur, al-Qasim ibn Muhammad told us, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, accepts charity and takes it with His right hand, then nurtures it for one of you, just as one of you nurtures his colt or his foal, until indeed a morsel becomes like Uhud." And its confirmation in the Book of Allah is His words: ﴿Allah destroys interest and makes charities grow﴾.

Likewise Ahmad narrated it from Waki', and it is in Waki's Tafsir. al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Waki', with it, [[Al-Musnad (2/471) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (662).]] and said: "Hasan sahih." Likewise al-Thawri narrated it from 'Abbad ibn Mansur, with it. Ahmad also narrated it from Khalaf ibn al-Walid, from Ibn al-Mubarak, from 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Damrah and 'Abbad ibn Mansur, both from Abu Nadrah, from al-Qasim, with it. [[Al-Musnad (2/404).]]

Ibn Jarir narrated it from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Ishaq [[In manuscripts أ، و: "from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Malik Zanjawayh".]], from 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed when a servant gives in charity from good earnings, Allah accepts it from him and takes it with His right hand, and nurtures it as one of you nurtures his young horse or his foal. And indeed a man gives in charity a morsel, and it grows in the hand of Allah, or he said: in the palm of Allah, until it becomes like Uhud. So give in charity." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (6/19).]]

Likewise Ahmad narrated it from 'Abd al-Razzaq. [[Al-Musnad (2/268).]] This is a strange route with a sound chain, but its wording is strange, and the preserved version is the one mentioned earlier. It was also narrated from 'A'isha, Mother of the Believers, and Imam Ahmad said:

Abd al-Samad told us, Hammad told us, from Thabit, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'A'isha, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah nurtures for one of you a date or a morsel, just as one of you nurtures his colt or his foal, until it becomes like Uhud." Ahmad alone narrated it through this route. [[Al-Musnad (6/251).]]

Al-Bazzar said: Yahya ibn al-Mu'alla ibn Mansur told us, Isma'il told us, my father told me, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from 'Amrah, from 'A'isha, from the Prophet ﷺ, and from al-Dahhak ibn 'Uthman, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Indeed a man gives in charity from lawful earnings, and Allah accepts only what is good, so the Merciful receives it with His hand and nurtures it, just as one of you nurtures his colt, or his servant, or he said: his foal." Then he said: "We do not know anyone who narrated it from Yahya ibn Sa'id ibn 'Amrah except Abu Uways." [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. (931), Kashf al-Astar. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said: "Abu Uways is weak (layyin), and al-Bazzar mentioned that he alone narrated it."
Note: Kashf al-Astar does not contain "from al-Dahhak, from Abu Hurayrah," because it is recorded in the two Sahihs and therefore is not among the additions (zawa'id).]]

* *

As for His words ﴿And Allah does not love every ungrateful sinner﴾: meaning He does not love one who is ungrateful in heart and sinful in speech and action. It is necessary to note the connection in ending this verse with this attribute: the one who deals in interest is not content with what Allah has apportioned to him of lawful provision, and does not suffice with the permissible earning He has prescribed for him. Rather, he strives to consume people's wealth falsely, through various kinds of evil gains. Thus he is ungrateful for the blessing upon him, and a wrongdoer, sinful by consuming people's wealth falsely.

Then Allah said, praising the believers who are devoted to their Lord, obedient to His command, and thankful to Him, who do good to His creation by establishing prayer and giving zakat, informing of the honor prepared for them, and that on the Day of Resurrection they will be safe from consequences. He said: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, establish prayer, and give zakat, for them is their reward with their Lord, and there is no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.﴾

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him: Allah the Exalted says, commanding His believing servants to fear Him and forbidding them from what brings them closer to His wrath and distances them from His pleasure: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah﴾, i.e., fear Him and be mindful of Him in what you do, ﴿and give up what remains of riba (usury, the interest-based gain on loans)﴾, i.e., abandon what is still owed to you from the excess over the principal amounts, after this warning, ﴿if you are believers﴾, i.e., in what Allah has legislated for you, namely the permissibility of trade and the prohibition of riba and other things.

Zayd ibn Aslam, Ibn Jurayj, Muqatil ibn Hayyan and al-Suddi mentioned that this context was revealed concerning the clan of Amr ibn Umayr from Thaqif and the clan of al-Mughirah from the Banu Makhzum. There had been riba between them in the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic period). When Islam came and they embraced it, Thaqif sought to collect it from them, and they disputed among themselves [in some manuscripts: "fa-tashajarū", they quarrelled]. The Banu al-Mughirah said: "We will not pay riba in Islam." Attab ibn Asid, the governor of Makkah, wrote about this to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and this verse was revealed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wrote back with it to him: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and give up what remains of riba, if you are believers. But if you do not, then be informed of a war from Allah and His Messenger﴾. They said: "We repent to Allah, and we give up what remains of riba," and they all abandoned it.

This is a severe threat and a binding warning for whoever persists in dealing in riba after the warning. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: ﴿then be informed of a war﴾, i.e., be certain of a war from Allah and His Messenger. It has already been mentioned, through the narration of Rabi'ah ibn Kulthum, from his father, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "On the Day of Resurrection it will be said to the one who consumes riba: 'Take up your weapons for war.'" Then he recited: ﴿But if you do not, then be informed of a war from Allah and His Messenger﴾.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿But if you do not, then be informed of a war from Allah and His Messenger﴾. Whoever persists in riba and does not desist from it, it is incumbent upon the leader of the Muslims to ask him to repent; if he desists, well and good, otherwise he shall strike his neck.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Hisham ibn Hassan narrated to us, from al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin, that they both said: "By Allah, these money-changers (sayarifah) are consumers of riba, and they have indeed been informed of a war from Allah and His Messenger. Had there been a just imam over the people, he would have asked them to repent; if they repented, well and good, otherwise he would have put the sword among them." Qatadah said: "Allah has threatened them with death, as you hear, and has made them outcasts (bahrajan) wherever they are found. So beware of the riba that mixes into these sales, for Allah has widened the lawful and made it good, so let not poverty drive you to disobey Him." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "Allah has threatened the consumer of riba with death." Ibn Jarir narrated this.

Al-Suhayli said: For this reason Aishah said to Umm Muhabbah, the freedwoman of Zayd ibn Arqam, concerning the matter of 'inah (a deceptive sale device): "Tell him that his jihad with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has been nullified, unless he repents." She singled out jihad because it is the opposite of His saying: ﴿then be informed of a war from Allah and His Messenger﴾. He said: "This meaning has been mentioned by many [in some manuscripts: 'mentioned by Ibn Battal']." He said: "But its chain of transmission to Aishah is weak."

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But if you repent, you shall have your principal; you will not wrong, nor be wronged﴾, i.e., by taking the excess, ﴿nor be wronged﴾, i.e., by having the principal reduced either; rather, you shall have what you gave without any increase over it or any decrease from it [in some manuscripts: "nor any shortfall"].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Ishkab narrated to us, Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Shaiban, from Shabib ibn Gharqadah al-Bariqi, from Sulayman ibn al-Ahwas, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave a sermon during the Farewell Pilgrimage and said: "Indeed every riba of the Jahiliyyah is placed under you entirely. You shall have your principal; you will not wrong, nor be wronged. And the first riba to be waived is the riba of al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib; it is all waived." Thus I found it: Sulayman ibn al-Ahwas.

Ibn Mardawayh said: al-Shafi'i narrated to us, Mu'adh ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Musaddad informed us, Abu al-Ahwas informed us, Shabib ibn Gharqadah narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Amr, from his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed every riba of the riba of the Jahiliyyah is waived. You shall have your principal; you will not wrong, nor be wronged." [Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan, no. 3334, from Musaddad with this chain, and Ibn Majah narrated it in his Sunan, no. 3055, through the route of Abu al-Ahwas.]

It was also narrated in a similar way from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Abu Hurrah [in one manuscript: "Abu Hamzah"] al-Raqashi, from Amr, namely Ibn Kharijah, and he mentioned it.

* *

His saying: ﴿And if the debtor is in hardship, then let there be postponement until a time of ease. But that you give charity is better for you, if you only knew﴾: Allah the Exalted commands patience toward the one in hardship who cannot find repayment, saying: ﴿And if the debtor is in hardship, then let there be postponement until a time of ease﴾ [i.e.] not as the people of the Jahiliyyah used to do, when one of them would say to his debtor when the debt fell due: "Either you pay, or you increase it."

Then He encourages remission of the debt and promises for that good and great reward, saying: ﴿But that you give charity is better for you, if you only knew﴾, i.e., that you forgo the principal entirely and remit it to the debtor. Hadiths have come through multiple routes from the Prophet (ﷺ) on this:

The first hadith: from Abu Umamah As'ad ibn Zurarah [al-Naqib, the Chief]. Al-Tabarani said: Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb al-Rajjani narrated to us, Yahya ibn Hakim al-Muqawwim narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Bakr al-Bursani narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us, Asim ibn Ubayd Allah narrated to me, from Abu Umamah As'ad ibn Zurarah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever would love that Allah shelter him on the Day when there is no shade but His shade, let him ease the lot of the one in hardship or remit it for him." [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (1/304). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (4/134): "Asim is weak, and he did not meet As'ad ibn Zurarah."]

Another hadith: from Buraydah. Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Abd al-Warith narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Juhadah narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Buraydah, from his father, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Whoever gives respite to one in hardship, for him is charity equal to [the debt] every day." Then I heard him say: "Whoever gives respite to one in hardship, for him is charity twice [the debt] every day." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I heard you say: 'Whoever gives respite to one in hardship, for him is charity equal to [the debt] every day,' then I heard you say: 'Whoever gives respite to one in hardship, for him is charity twice [the debt] every day'?" He said: "For him is charity equal to [the debt] every day before the debt falls due. When the debt falls due and he gives him respite, for him is charity twice [the debt] every day." [Al-Musnad (5/360).]

Another hadith: from Abu Qatadah al-Harith ibn Ribi al-Ansari. Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Abu Ja'far al-Khatmi informed us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, that Abu Qatadah had a debt owed to him by a man, and he would come to him seeking repayment, but the man would hide from him. One day he came, and a boy came out, and he asked him about him. The boy said: "Yes, he is in the house eating khazirah (a dish of meat and porridge)." So he called out: "O so-and-so, come out, for I have been told you are here." He came out to him, and said: "What keeps you hidden from me?" He said: "I am in hardship and have nothing with me." He said: "By Allah, are you truly in hardship?" He said: "Yes." Then Abu Qatadah wept and said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever relieves his debtor, or erases it for him, will be in the shade of the Throne on the Day of Resurrection.'" It was also narrated by Muslim in his Sahih. [Al-Musnad (5/308); I did not find it in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of Abu Qatadah, and Allah knows best.]

Another hadith: from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman. The hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: al-Akhnas Ahmad ibn Imran narrated to us [he is Ahmad ibn Imran al-Akhnasi; al-Akhnasi is a nisbah, see al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil (2/64)], Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, Abu Malik al-Ashja'i narrated to us, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, from Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will bring one of His servants and say: 'What did you do for Me in the world?' He will say: 'O Lord, I did not do for You even an atom's weight in the world, by which I hope for You,' and he said this three times. At the last of them the servant will say: 'O Lord, You gave me abundant wealth, and I was a man who dealt with people in trade, and it was my character to be lenient.
