Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Abd al-Warith narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Juhadah narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Buraydah, from his father, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Whoever gives respite to one in hardship, for him is charity equal to [the debt] every day." Then I heard him say: "Whoever gives respite to one in hardship, for him is charity twice [the debt] every day." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I heard you say: 'Whoever gives respite to one in hardship, for him is charity equal to [the debt] every day,' then I heard you say: 'Whoever gives respite to one in hardship, for him is charity twice [the debt] every day'?" He said: "For him is charity equal to [the debt] every day before the debt falls due. When the debt falls due and he gives him respite, for him is charity twice [the debt] every day." [Al-Musnad (5/360).]

Another hadith: from Abu Qatadah al-Harith ibn Ribi al-Ansari. Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Abu Ja'far al-Khatmi informed us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, that Abu Qatadah had a debt owed to him by a man, and he would come to him seeking repayment, but the man would hide from him. One day he came, and a boy came out, and he asked him about him. The boy said: "Yes, he is in the house eating khazirah (a dish of meat and porridge)." So he called out: "O so-and-so, come out, for I have been told you are here." He came out to him, and said: "What keeps you hidden from me?" He said: "I am in hardship and have nothing with me." He said: "By Allah, are you truly in hardship?" He said: "Yes." Then Abu Qatadah wept and said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever relieves his debtor, or erases it for him, will be in the shade of the Throne on the Day of Resurrection.'" It was also narrated by Muslim in his Sahih. [Al-Musnad (5/308); I did not find it in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of Abu Qatadah, and Allah knows best.]

Another hadith: from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman. The hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: al-Akhnas Ahmad ibn Imran narrated to us [he is Ahmad ibn Imran al-Akhnasi; al-Akhnasi is a nisbah, see al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil (2/64)], Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, Abu Malik al-Ashja'i narrated to us, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, from Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will bring one of His servants and say: 'What did you do for Me in the world?' He will say: 'O Lord, I did not do for You even an atom's weight in the world, by which I hope for You,' and he said this three times. At the last of them the servant will say: 'O Lord, You gave me abundant wealth, and I was a man who dealt with people in trade, and it was my character to be lenient. I would ease the lot of the one who is well off, and give respite to the one in hardship.' Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say: 'I am most worthy of being eased. Enter Paradise.'"

It was also narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim and Ibn Majah, through various routes, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, from Hudhayfah. Muslim added: "and from Uqbah ibn Amir and Abu Mas'ud al-Badri, from the Prophet (ﷺ)," with something similar. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 2391, 2707, 3451; Sahih Muslim, no. 1560.] The wording is that of al-Bukhari:

Hisham ibn Ammar narrated to us, Yahya ibn Hamzah narrated to us, al-Zuhri narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Abd Allah, that he heard Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "There was a merchant who would lend money to people. When he saw one in hardship, he would say to his servants: 'Overlook him, perhaps Allah will overlook us.' So Allah overlooked him."

Another hadith: from Sahl ibn Hunayf. Al-Hakim said in his Mustadrak: Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, Abu al-Walid Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik narrated to us, Amr ibn Thabit narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, that Sahl narrated to him that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever aids a fighter in the way of Allah, or a warrior, or a debtor in his hardship, or a mukatab (slave seeking manumission) in his freeing, Allah will shelter him on the Day when there is no shade but His shade." Then he said: "Its chain is sound, though they did not record it." [Al-Mustadrak (2/217); al-Dhahabi criticized it in al-Talkhis. I say: rather, it contains Amr ibn Thabit, who is a Rafidi and abandoned in narration.]

Another hadith: from Abd Allah ibn Umar. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ubayd narrated to us, from Yusuf ibn Suhayb, from Zayd al-Ammi, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wishes that his supplication be answered and his distress be relieved, let him relieve the one in hardship." Ahmad alone narrated it. [Al-Musnad (2/23).]

Another hadith [the seventh, per the editions]: From Abu Mas'ud 'Uqbah ibn 'Amr. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Abu Malik informed us, from Ribi ibn Hirash, from Hudhayfah, that a man was brought before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and He said: "What did you do in the world?" The man said: "I did not do an atom's weight of good that I could hope to be rewarded for." He said this to Him three times. In the third time he said: "O Lord, You had given me some wealth in the world, so I used to trade with people. I would make things easy for the one who was well-off, and I would give respite to the one in difficulty." Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: "We are more deserving of that than you. Overlook (the faults of) My servant." So He forgave him. Abu Mas'ud said: "This is how I heard it from the Prophet ﷺ." Muslim also narrated it in this way from the hadith of Abu Malik Sa'd ibn Tariq with the same wording. [Footnote: al-Musnad (4/118) and Sahih Muslim no. 1560.]

Another hadith [the eighth]: From 'Imran ibn Husayn. Imam Ahmad said: Aswad ibn 'Amir narrated to us, Abu Bakr informed us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Dawud, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever is owed a right by a man and gives him respite, for him there is a sadaqah (charity) every day." [Footnote: al-Musnad (4/442).]

This chain is gharib (a rare or strange narration, one reported through a single or unusual route) from this route. Something similar has already been mentioned from Buraydah.

Another hadith [the ninth]: From Abu al-Yasar Ka'b ibn 'Amr. Imam Ahmad said: Mu'awiyah ibn 'Amr narrated to us, Za'idah narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Ribi, who said: Abu al-Yasar narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever gives respite to one in difficulty, or remits (the debt) for him, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will shade him in His shade on a Day when there is no shade but His shade." [Footnote: al-Musnad (3/427).]

Muslim also narrated it in his Sahih by another route, from the hadith of 'Ubadah ibn al-Walid ibn 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: My father and I went out seeking knowledge among this clan of the Ansar before they perished. The first of them we met was Abu al-Yasar, a companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and with him was a servant carrying a bundle of pages. Abu al-Yasar was wearing a cloak and a Ma'afiri garment, and his servant was also wearing a cloak and a Ma'afiri garment. My father said to him: "O uncle, I see in your face a trace of anger?" He said: "Yes. I had a claim against so-and-so son of so-and-so, of the Haramiyy clan [in another manuscript: al-Harani; in another: al-Hizami]. I went to his family, greeted them, and asked: 'Is he here?' They said: 'No.' Then a young son of his came out to me, a bold lad, and I asked: 'Where is your father?' He said: 'He heard your voice, so he entered my mother's room.' I said: 'Come out to me, for I know where you are.' So he came out, and I asked: 'What made you hide from me?' He said: 'By Allah, I will tell you the truth and not lie to you. I feared, by Allah, that I would tell you something and lie to you, and that I would promise you and break my promise. I was a companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I was in difficulty.'" I said: "By Allah?" He said: "By Allah." I said: "By Allah?" He said: "By Allah." Then he brought his document and erased it with his hand, and said: "If you find the means to repay, then repay me; otherwise you are free (from the debt)." Abu al-Yasar said: "My eyes saw it, and my ears heard it, and my heart retained it" (and he pointed to the place of his heart's attachment) — "the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying: 'Whoever gives respite to one in difficulty, or remits (the debt) for him, Allah will shade him in His shade.'" He mentioned the rest of the hadith. [Footnote: Sahih Muslim no. 3006.]

Another hadith [the tenth]: From the Commander of the Believers 'Uthman ibn 'Affan. 'Abd Allah ibn Imam Ahmad (in the Musnad of his father) said: Abu Yahya al-Bazzaz Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahim narrated to me, al-Hasan ibn Bishr ibn Salm al-Kufi narrated to us, al-'Abbas ibn al-Fadl al-Ansari narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Ziyad al-Qurashi, from his father, from Mihjan, the freedman of 'Uthman, from 'Uthman, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Allah will shade a person in His shade, on a Day when there is no shade but His shade, the one who gives respite to one in difficulty, or remits (the debt) for a debtor." [Footnote: Zawa'id al-Musnad (1/73).]

Another hadith [the eleventh]: From Ibn 'Abbas. Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid narrated to us, Nuh ibn Ja'wanah al-Sulami al-Khurasani narrated to us, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to the mosque, saying with his hand thus — and 'Abd al-Rahman gestured with his hand toward the ground — "Whoever gives respite to one in difficulty or remits (the debt) for him, Allah will protect him from the heat of Hell. Verily, the deed of Paradise is hard, requiring effort, on a mound (three times). Verily, the deed of the Fire is easy, in a level place. The happy one is the one who is protected from trials. There is no swallow more beloved to Allah than a swallow of anger which a servant suppresses; no servant suppresses it for the sake of Allah except that Allah fills his inside with faith." Ahmad alone narrated it. [Footnote: al-Musnad (1/327).]

Another route: al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Buranni, judge of al-Hadithah in the lands of Rabi'ah, narrated to us, al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Sada'i narrated to us, al-Hakam ibn al-Jarud narrated to us, Ibn Abi al-Mut'id (the maternal uncle of Ibn 'Uyaynah) narrated to us, from his father, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever gives respite to one in difficulty until his ease, Allah will give him respite for his sin until his repentance." [Footnote: al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/151). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (4/135): "In it is al-Hakam ibn al-Jarud, whom al-Azdi declared weak, and the teacher of al-Hakam and his teacher's teacher, I do not know them."]

Then Allah, the Exalted, says, admonishing His servants and reminding them of the passing of this world and the perishing of its wealth and other things, and of the coming of the Hereafter, and of their return to Him, and of His reckoning of His creation for what they did, and His recompense to them for what they earned of good and evil. He warns them of His punishment, saying:

﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah; then every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged.﴾

It has been narrated that this verse was the last verse of the Great Qur'an to be revealed. Ibn Lahi'ah said: 'Ata' ibn Dinar narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The last of the whole Qur'an to be revealed was: ﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah; then every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged.﴾ The Prophet ﷺ lived nine nights after the revelation of this verse, then died on Monday, two nights into Rabi' al-Awwal. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it from the hadith of al-Mas'udi, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The last verse revealed was: ﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah.﴾

al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Yazid al-Nahwi, from 'Ikrimah, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, who said: The last thing revealed of the Qur'an was: ﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah; then every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged.﴾ [Footnote: Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 11057.]

Similarly, al-Dahhak and al-'Awfi narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas. al-Thawri narrated from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The last verse revealed was: ﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah,﴾ and between its revelation and the death of the Prophet ﷺ there were thirty-one days.

Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said: The last verse revealed was: ﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah,﴾ the verse. Ibn Jurayj said: They say that the Prophet ﷺ lived nine nights after it, and he fell ill on Saturday and died on Monday. Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

'Atiyyah narrated from Abu Sa'id, who said: The last verse revealed was: ﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah; then every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged.﴾

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 282 (part 1 of 2):

This noble verse is the longest verse in the Mighty Qur'an. Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said:

Yunus narrated to us: Ibn Wahb informed us [[In manuscript C: "Anba'anā" (he informed us).]]: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab narrated to me that it had reached him that the last verse of the Qur'an to be revealed to the Throne was the verse of debt.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Affan narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: When the verse of debt was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first to deny was Adam, peace be upon him. When Allah created Adam, He wiped over his back and brought forth from it whatever was to be created of his offspring until the Day of Resurrection. He began presenting his descendants to him, and he saw among them a man who was radiant. He said: 'O Lord, who is this?' He said: 'He is your son Dawud (David).' He said: 'O Lord, how long is his life?' He said: 'Sixty years.' He said: 'Lord, increase his life.' He said: 'No, unless you give him from your own life.' Adam's life was a thousand years, so He added to him forty years, and He wrote a document about that and called the angels to witness it. When Adam was near death and the angels came to him, he said: 'Verily, there remain forty years of my life.' It was said to him: 'You had given them to your son Dawud.' He said: 'I did not do that.' So Allah brought forth the document, and He called the angels to witness it."

And Aswad ibn 'Amir narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, and mentioned it, and added in it: "So Allah completed for Dawud one hundred years, and completed for Adam a thousand years."

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it like this, from Yusuf ibn Habib, from Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, from Hammad ibn Salamah [with the same chain] [[Added from manuscripts A and W.]].

This is a very strange (gharib) hadith, and 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an has an objectionable (munkar) element in his narrations. Al-Hakim also narrated it in his Mustadrak in similar wording, from the hadith of al-Harith ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Dhubab [[In manuscript A: "Ibn Abi Dhi'ab".]], from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah; and through the narration of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from al-Sha'bi, from Abu Hurayrah; and by the route of Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah; and from the hadith of Hisham [[In manuscripts C and A: "Tammam".]] ibn Sa'd, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and he mentioned it in similar wording [[Al-Mustadrak (1/64, 2/586).]].

As for His saying: ﴿O you who believe, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down﴾. This is a guidance from Him, exalted is He, to His believing servants: when they deal with one another in transactions involving a deferred term, they should write them down, so that this is more preserving of their amount and their due date, and more precise regarding the witness to them. He drew attention to this at the end of the verse when He said: ﴿That is more just in the sight of Allah, more upright for testimony, and closer to preventing you from doubting﴾.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿O you who believe, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down﴾: It was revealed concerning the salam (advance sale) for a known term.

Qatadah said, from Abu Hassan al-A'raj [[In manuscripts C and A: "Abi Hayyan".]], from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "I testify that a loan guaranteed for a specified term is something Allah has made lawful and permitted," and then he recited: ﴿O you who believe, when you contract a debt for a specified term﴾. Narrated by al-Bukhari.

It is established in the two Sahihs, through the narration of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from Ibn Abi Najih, from 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir, from Abu al-Minhal, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) came to Madinah, and its people were paying in advance for fruits for two or three years. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever pays in advance, let him pay in advance for a known measure, a known weight, and a known term" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (2240) and Sahih Muslim, no. (1604).]].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿fa-ktubūhu (then write it down)﴾, it is a command from Him, exalted is He, to write it [in this situation] [[Added from manuscripts C, A and W.]] for documentation and preservation. If it is said: It is established in the two Sahihs, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We are an unlettered nation; we neither write nor calculate" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (1913) and Sahih Muslim, no. (1080).]], then what is the reconciliation between this and the command to write? The answer: debt, in and of itself, does not at all require writing, because the Book of Allah has been made easy by Allah for people to memorize, and the Sunnah is also preserved from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). What Allah commanded to be written is only particular matters that occur between people, so they were commanded with a command of guidance, not a command of obligation, as some scholars have held.

Ibn Juraij said: Whoever takes a debt should write it down, and whoever buys should call witnesses.

Qatadah said: It was mentioned to us that Abu Sulayman al-Mar'ashi, a man who had accompanied Ka'b, once said to his companions one day: "Do you know of an oppressed person who called upon his Lord and was not answered?" They said: "How could that be?" He said: "A man sold something on credit without calling witnesses or writing it down. When its payment became due, his creditor denied it, so he called upon his Lord and was not answered, because he had disobeyed his Lord."

Abu Sa'id, al-Sha'bi, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Hasan, Ibn Juraij, Ibn Zayd, and others said: That was obligatory, then it was abrogated (naskh) by His saying: ﴿But if one of you entrusts another, let the one who is entrusted fulfill his trust﴾.

Imam Ahmad said: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Layth narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Rabi'ah, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he mentioned: "A man from the Children of Israel asked one of the Children of Israel to lend him a thousand dinars. He said: 'Bring me witnesses whom I may call to witness.' He said: 'Allah is sufficient as a witness.' He said: 'Bring me a guarantor.' He said: 'Allah is sufficient as a guarantor.' He said: 'You have spoken the truth.' So he gave it to him for a specified term. The man set out on the sea and accomplished his need. Then he sought a ship to reach him by the term he had set, but he found no ship. So he took a piece of wood and hollowed it out, put a thousand dinars and a letter inside it, addressed to his creditor, then sealed its opening, then brought it to the sea and said: 'O Allah, You know that I borrowed a thousand dinars from so-and-so, and he asked me for a guarantor, and I said: Allah is sufficient as a guarantor, and he was content with that. He asked me for a witness, and I said: Allah is sufficient as a witness, and he was content with that. I have strived to find a ship to send the money to him, but I did not find one, so I entrust it to You.' Then he threw it into the sea until it drifted into it, and he departed, still seeking a ship to his land. Meanwhile, the man who had lent him the money went out looking, perhaps a ship would bring him his money, and there was the piece of wood containing the money. He took it home as firewood, and when he broke it open he found the money and the letter. Then the man who had borrowed came, brought him a thousand dinars, and said: 'By Allah, I have not ceased striving to find a ship to bring you your money, but I did not find a ship until the one I came on.' He said: 'Did you send me anything?' He said: 'Did I not tell you that I did not find a ship before this one I came on?' He said: 'Verily, Allah has already delivered on your behalf what you sent in the piece of wood, so go back with your thousand, rightly guided.'"

This is a sound (sahih) chain [[Al-Musnad (2/348).]]. Al-Bukhari narrated it in seven places in his Sahih, through sound routes, in a suspended form (mu'allaq) with a definitive wording: he said, "And al-Layth ibn Sa'd said," and mentioned it. It is said that in some of these he narrated it from 'Abd Allah ibn Salih, the scribe of al-Layth, from him [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (1498, 2291, 2404, 2430, 2744, 6261, 2063).]].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and let a scribe write between you justly﴾, i.e., with equity and truth, and let him not deviate in his writing against anyone, and let him write only what they have agreed upon, without addition or reduction.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And let not a scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him, so let him write﴾, i.e., let not one who knows how to write refuse when asked to write for people, and there is no hardship upon him in that. Just as Allah taught him what he did not know, let him also give charity to others who do not do well at writing, and let him write, as came in the hadith: "Among charity is that you help a craftsman or make something for a clumsy person" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (2518), from the hadith of Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. And in another hadith: "Whoever conceals knowledge that he knows will be bridled on the Day of Resurrection with a bridle of fire" [[Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (2/304), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

Mujahid and 'Ata' said: It is obligatory upon the scribe to write.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And let the one upon whom the truth is due dictate, and let him fear Allah, his Lord﴾, i.e., let the debtor dictate to the scribe what is due upon him of debt, and let him fear Allah in that. ﴿And let him not diminish anything from it﴾, i.e., let him not conceal anything from it. ﴿But if the one upon whom the truth is due is foolish﴾, i.e., placed under restraint due to wastefulness or the like, ﴿or weak﴾, i.e., a minor or insane, ﴿or is unable to dictate himself﴾, either due to a speech impediment or ignorance of what is correct in that matter. ﴿Then let his guardian dictate with justice.﴾

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And call upon two witnesses from among your men﴾, it is a command to call witnesses along with writing, for greater documentation. ﴿And if there are not two men, then a man and two women﴾. This applies only to property and matters intended for property. The two women were placed in the position of one man only because of the deficiency of women's intellect, as Muslim said in his Sahih: Qutaybah narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Abi 'Amr, from al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "O women, give charity and increase your seeking of forgiveness, for I have seen that you are the majority of the people of the Fire." A discerning woman among them said: "Why is that, O Messenger of Allah, that we are the majority of the people of the Fire?" He said: "You curse much and you deny the favor of your husbands. I have not seen anyone more overpowering to a person of understanding than you, deficient in intellect and religion." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the deficiency in intellect and religion?" He said: "As for the deficiency of her intellect, the testimony of two women equals the testimony of one man; this is the deficiency of intellect. And she stays nights without praying, and breaks her fast in Ramadan; this is the deficiency of religion" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (80).]].

As for His saying: ﴿from those whom you accept as witnesses﴾, it indicates the requirement of justice (adalah) in witnesses. This is a restricted ruling, which al-Shafi'i applied to every unrestricted command in the Qur'an regarding calling witnesses without a condition. Whoever rejects the unknown-character witness (mastur) has used this verse, which indicates that the witness must be just and acceptable.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿that one of them may err, so the other may remind her﴾, meaning: if one of the two women forgets the testimony, ﴿so one of them may remind the other﴾, i.e., she will be reminded of what the witnessing was based upon. For this reason, others read: "fa-tudhakkira" with a shadda, from tadhkar (remembrance). Whoever says that her testimony along with the other's makes it like the testimony of a man has gone too far; the correct view is the first. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called﴾, it was said: its meaning is that when they are called to bear witness, they are obliged to respond. This is the view of Qatadah and al-Rabi' ibn Anas. This is like His saying: ﴿And let not a scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him, so let him write﴾. From here it is derived that bearing witness is a collective obligation (fard kifayah).

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verse 282 (part 2 of 2):

It is said, and this is the position of the majority, that what is meant by His words, ﴿And let not the witnesses refuse when they are summoned﴾, is summoning them to give testimony, because of the literal meaning of His words, ﴿the witnesses﴾, and the witness in its literal sense is one who has taken on (the testimony). So when he is called to give it, he must respond, if it has become specifically incumbent upon him; otherwise it is a communal obligation (fard kifayah). And Allah knows best.

Mujahid, Abu Mijlaz and others said: If you are called to bear witness, you have the choice; but once you have given testimony and are then called (to give it), you must respond.

It is established in Sahih Muslim and the Sunan, through the chain of Malik, from Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Amrah, from Zayd ibn Khalid, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I not inform you of the best of witnesses? The one who brings his testimony before he is asked for it."

As for the other hadith in the two Sahihs: "Shall I not inform you of the worst of witnesses? Those who give testimony before they are asked to testify," and likewise his saying: "Then there will come a people whose oaths precede their testimony, and whose testimony precedes their oaths." And in another narration: "Then there will come a people who give testimony without being asked to testify." Those are the false witnesses. It has also been reported from Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan al-Basri that it covers both situations: bearing (the testimony) and giving it.

* *

His words, ﴿And do not be weary of writing it, whether it is small or large, up to its term﴾, are part of the guidance: it is a command to write down the debt, whether small or large. So He says, ﴿And do not be weary﴾, meaning: do not become tired of writing down the right, in whatever state it is, whether little or much, ﴿up to its term﴾.

* *

His words, ﴿That is more just in the sight of Allah, and more upright for testimony, and closer to preventing doubt﴾, mean: this which We have commanded you, of writing down the right when it is deferred, is ﴿more just in the sight of Allah﴾, that is, more equitable; ﴿and more upright for testimony﴾, that is, more firm for the witness, for when he sets down his writing and then looks at it, he recalls the testimony by it, since there is a possibility that, had he not written it, he would forget it, as is generally the case in reality; ﴿and closer to preventing doubt﴾, and nearer to avoiding suspicion, rather, when disputes arise you return to the document you wrote, and it will decide between you without doubt.

* *

His words, ﴿except when it is a present trade that you conduct among yourselves, for then there is no blame upon you that you do not write it﴾, mean: when the sale is of a present commodity, hand to hand, there is no harm in not writing it, since the prohibited consequence of not writing it does not arise.

As for calling witnesses to a sale, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And take witnesses when you trade with one another﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah related to us, Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn Bukayr related to me, Ibn Lahi'ah related to me, Ata' ibn Dinar related to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr concerning the words of Allah, ﴿And take witnesses when you trade﴾, meaning: call witnesses to your right whether there is a term in it or not; so call witnesses to your right in every case. He said: It was similarly reported from Jabir ibn Zayd, Mujahid, Ata' and al-Dahhak.

Al-Sha'bi and al-Hasan said: this command is abrogated by His words, ﴿But if one of you entrusts another, let the one who is entrusted discharge his trust﴾.

The majority hold that this command is to be understood as guidance and recommendation, not as obligation. The evidence for this is the hadith of Khuzaymah ibn Thabit al-Ansari, which Imam Ahmad narrated:

Abu al-Yaman related to us, Shu'ayb related to us, from al-Zuhri: Imarah ibn Khuzaymah al-Ansari related to me, that his paternal uncle related to him, and he was one of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), that the Prophet (ﷺ) bought a horse from a Bedouin, and the Prophet (ﷺ) asked him to follow him so that he could pay him the price of his horse. The Prophet (ﷺ) walked quickly and the Bedouin walked slowly, and men began to intercept the Bedouin and haggle with him over the horse, not realizing that the Prophet (ﷺ) had bought it, until some of them raised the price for the Bedouin above the price the Prophet (ﷺ) had agreed. So the Bedouin called out to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: If you want to buy this horse, buy it, otherwise I will sell it. When the Prophet (ﷺ) heard the Bedouin's call, he stood and said: "Did I not already buy it from you?" The Bedouin said: No, by Allah, I have not sold it to you. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Rather, I have already bought it from you." So the people gathered around the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Bedouin, and they were disputing, and the Bedouin kept saying: Bring a witness who will testify that I sold you it. Whoever of the Muslims came would say to the Bedouin: Woe to you! The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would only say what is true. Until Khuzaymah came, and he listened to the exchange between the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Bedouin, while the Bedouin was saying: Bring a witness who will testify that I have sold you it. Khuzaymah said: I testify that you have indeed sold it to him. The Prophet (ﷺ) turned to Khuzaymah and said: "On what basis do you testify?" He said: On the basis of your truthfulness, O Messenger of Allah. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made Khuzaymah's testimony equal to the testimony of two men.

Abu Dawud related it in the same way from the hadith of Shu'ayb, and al-Nasa'i from the narration of Muhammad ibn al-Walid al-Zubayri; both from al-Zuhri, with it in a similar form.

However, caution lies in calling witnesses, due to what Imam al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak narrated through the narration of Mu'adh ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari, from Shu'bah, from Firas, from al-Sha'bi, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Three people supplicate Allah and their supplication is not answered: a man whose wife is bad-tempered and he does not divorce her; a man who handed over an orphan's property before he reached maturity; and a man who lent money to someone without calling witnesses."

Then al-Hakim said: Its chain is sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim). He said: They did not record it, because the companions of Shu'bah halted this hadith at Abu Musa, and they only agreed upon the chain of Shu'bah's hadith with this isnad: "Three people will be given their reward twice."

* *

His words, ﴿And let no scribe or witness be harmed﴾. It is said: its meaning is that neither the scribe nor the witness should be harmed, so that one writes contrary to what is dictated, or another testifies contrary to what he heard, or conceals it entirely. This is the view of al-Hasan, Qatadah and others.

It is also said: its meaning is that one should not harm them, as Ibn Abi Hatim said: Usayd ibn Asim related to us, al-Husayn, meaning Ibn Hafs, related to us, Sufyan related to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas concerning this verse, ﴿And let no scribe or witness be harmed﴾. He said: A man comes to them and calls them to write or to testify, and they say: We are busy; and he says: You have been commanded to respond. So he has no right to harm them.

Then he said: It was similarly reported from Ikrimah, Mujahid, Tawus, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, Atiyyah, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Rabi' ibn Anas and al-Suddi.

* *

His words, ﴿And if you do so, it is indeed transgression on your part﴾: that is, if you oppose what you have been commanded, and do what you have been forbidden, then it is a transgression (fisq) that rests upon you, meaning it is binding upon you; you cannot turn away from it nor be free of it.

* *

His words, ﴿And fear Allah﴾: that is, fear Him and watch over Him, follow His command and abandon what He forbids. ﴿And Allah teaches you﴾, like His words: ﴿O you who believe, if you fear Allah, He will grant you a criterion﴾ [al-Anfal: 29], and like His words: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion of His mercy and will make for you a light by which you will walk﴾ [al-Hadid: 28].

* *

His words, ﴿And Allah is Knower of all things﴾: that is, He knows the realities of matters, their benefits and their outcomes, so nothing among things is hidden from Him; rather, His knowledge encompasses all that exists.

He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿And if you are on a journey﴾, that is, travelling, ﴿and you contract a debt for a specified term﴾, ﴿and you do not find a scribe﴾ to write it for you. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Or they find one but do not find parchment, an inkwell, or a pen, so let there be ﴿pledges taken into possession﴾, that is, let there be, in place of writing, pledges held in the hand of the creditor."

The words ﴿pledges taken into possession﴾ have been cited as evidence that a pledge (rahn) is binding only once it is taken into possession, which is the view of al-Shafiʿi and the majority. Others cited it as evidence that the pledge must be held in the possession of the pledgee (murtahin). This is a narration from Imam Ahmad, and a group of scholars held this view.

Others among the early scholars (al-salaf) cited this verse as evidence that a pledge is legislated only during travel. This was said by Mujahid and others.

It is established in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim), from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died while his armour was pledged to a Jew for thirty measures of barley, which he had pledged as sustenance for his family. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (2508). I did not find it in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of Anas; it is in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of ʿAʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]] In another narration: "from the Jews of Madinah." [[The narration is in Sunan al-Nasaʾi (7/288).]] In the narration of al-Shafiʿi: "with Abu al-Shahm the Jew." [[Musnad al-Shafiʿi (p. 251).]] The detailed discussion of these matters is in my book "al-Ahkam al-Kabir", and to Allah belongs all praise and favour, and in Him is sought help.

* *

As for His words: ﴿So if one of you trusts another, let the one who is trusted fulfil his trust﴾, Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with a good chain (isnad), from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, that he said: "This verse abrogated what came before it."

Al-Shaʿbi said: "If one of you trusts another, there is no harm if you do not write it down or call witnesses."

* *

As for His words: ﴿And let him fear Allah, his Lord﴾, it refers to the one who is trusted. This is as in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan, through the chain of Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Samurah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The hand is responsible for what it has taken until it returns it." [[Al-Musnad (5/12); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (3561); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (1266); al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Nasaʾi, no. (5783); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (2400).]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿And do not conceal the testimony﴾, that is, do not hide it, do not withhold it, and do not fail to make it known. Ibn ʿAbbas and others said: "False testimony is among the greatest of the major sins, and so is concealing it." For this reason He said: ﴿And whoever conceals it, his heart is sinful﴾. As-Suddi said: "That is, his heart is wicked." This is like His words, exalted is He: ﴿And we will not conceal the testimony of Allah; indeed, we would then be among the sinners﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 106]. He also said: ﴿O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both. So do not follow [your own] desire, lest you not be just. And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse to give it, then indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted﴾ [An-Nisa': 135]. Likewise He says here: ﴿And do not conceal the testimony; and whoever conceals it, his heart is sinful, and Allah is Knowing of what you do﴾.

Ibn Kathir said: Allah, may He be exalted, informs us that to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them and between them. He is the One who knows what is in them. Neither the outward matters nor the inward secrets and hidden thoughts are concealed from Him, however subtle or hidden they may be. He also informs us that He will call His servants to account for what they have done and for what they have concealed in their breasts, as He said: ﴿Say: Whether you conceal what is in your breasts or reveal it, Allah knows it. He knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and Allah is over all things competent﴾ [Al-Imran: 29], and He said: ﴿He knows the secret and what is more hidden﴾ [Ta-Ha: 7]. The verses on this subject are very numerous. In this verse He has added to knowledge something further, namely the reckoning for it. For this reason, when this verse was revealed, it weighed heavily upon the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, and they feared it, and feared Allah's reckoning of them for both great and small deeds. This was from the strength of their faith and certainty.

Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, my father Abu Abd al-Rahman, that is al-Ala, narrated to me, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: When this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And whether you show what is in yourselves or conceal it, Allah will bring you to account for it. Then He will forgive whom He wills and punish whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent﴾, it weighed heavily upon the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and knelt down, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have been charged with deeds that we can bear: prayer, fasting, jihad and charity, and this verse has been sent down to you which we cannot bear." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you wish to say what the two peoples of the Scripture before you said: 'We hear and we disobey'? Rather, say: 'We hear and we obey, Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final return.'" When the people acknowledged it and their tongues submitted to it, Allah sent down after it: ﴿The Messenger believes in what has been revealed to him from his Lord, and the believers. Each one believes in Allah, His angels, His books and His messengers. We make no distinction between any of His messengers. And they say: We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final return﴾. When they did this, Allah abrogated it (naskh), and sent down: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It will have what it has earned, and it will bear what it has earned. Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make errors﴾, until the end.

Muslim narrated it alone, from the hadith of Yazid ibn Zurayʿ, from Rawh ibn al-Qasim, from al-Ala, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, and he mentioned the like of it, and its wording is: "When they did that [Allah abrogated it] and sent down: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity...﴾" He said: "Yes." ﴿Our Lord, do not burden us as You burdened those before us﴾. He said: "Yes." ﴿Our Lord, do not load upon us that which we have no ability to bear﴾. He said: "Yes." ﴿Pardon us, forgive us, and have mercy upon us. You are our protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people﴾. He said: "Yes."

The hadith of Ibn Abbas concerning this: Imam Ahmad said: Waki narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Adam ibn Sulayman, I heard Said ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿And whether you show what is in yourselves or conceal it, Allah will bring you to account for it﴾, something entered their hearts from it that had never entered their hearts from anything else. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Say: We hear and we obey and we submit." So Allah cast faith into their hearts, and Allah sent down: ﴿The Messenger believes in what has been revealed to him from his Lord, and the believers. Each one believes in Allah, His angels, His books and His messengers. We make no distinction between any of His messengers. And they say: We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final return﴾, up to His saying: ﴿So give us victory over the disbelieving people﴾.

Muslim narrated it in the same way, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Kurayb and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, all three from Waki, with the same chain, and he added: ﴿Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make errors﴾. He said: "I have done so." ﴿Our Lord, do not burden us as You burdened those before us﴾. He said: "I have done so." ﴿Our Lord, do not load upon us that which we have no ability to bear﴾. He said: "I have done so." ﴿Pardon us, forgive us, and have mercy upon us. You are our protector [so give us victory]﴾. He said: "I have done so."

Another chain from Ibn Abbas: Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Mamar informed us, from Humayd al-Araj, from Mujahid, who said: I entered upon Ibn Abbas and said: "O Abu Abbas, I was with Ibn Umar and he recited this verse and wept." He said: "Which verse?" I said: ﴿And whether you show what is in yourselves or conceal it﴾. Ibn Abbas said: "When this verse was revealed it caused the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) great distress and great anger." He said: They said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are ruined, if we are to be held to account for what we say and what we do. As for our hearts, they are not in our hands." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Say: We hear and we obey." They said: "We hear and we obey." He said: Then this verse abrogated it: ﴿The Messenger believes in what has been revealed to him from his Lord, and the believers. Each one believes in Allah﴾ to ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It will have what it has earned, and it will bear what it has earned﴾. So what the soul merely thinks was excused for them, and they were held to account for their deeds.

Another chain: Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Yunus ibn Yazid informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Said ibn Marjanah, who heard him narrate that while he was sitting with Abdullah ibn Umar, he recited this verse: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And whether you show what is in yourselves or conceal it, Allah will bring you to account for it. Then He will forgive whom He wills﴾, the verse. He said: "By Allah, if Allah holds us to account for this, we will be ruined." Then Ibn Umar wept until his sobbing could be heard. Ibn Marjanah said: "I stood up and went to Ibn Abbas and related to him what Ibn Umar had said and what he had done when he recited it." Abdullah ibn Abbas said: "May Allah forgive Abu Abd al-Rahman. By my life, the Muslims felt from it when it was revealed the same as what Abdullah ibn Umar felt." Then Allah sent down after it: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾ to the end of the surah. Ibn Abbas said: "This whispering was something the Muslims could not bear, and the matter came to the point where Allah, mighty and majestic, decreed that for the soul is what it has earned and upon it is what it has merited, in word and in deed."

Another chain: Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, Ishaq narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from al-Zuhri, from Salim: that his father recited: ﴿And whether you show what is in yourselves or conceal it, Allah will bring you to account for it﴾, and his eyes shed tears. His action reached Ibn Abbas, who said: "May Allah have mercy on Abu Abd al-Rahman. He did as the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did when it was revealed. Then the verse after it abrogated it: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾."

These are sound chains from Ibn Abbas, and it is established from Ibn Umar just as it is established from Ibn Abbas.

Al-Bukhari said: Ishaq narrated to us, Rawh narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Khalid al-Hadhdhaʾ, from Marwan al-Asfar, from a man of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), I think it was Ibn Umar: ﴿And whether you show what is in yourselves or conceal it﴾. He said: "It was abrogated by the verse that follows it."

In the same way it is narrated from Ali, Ibn Masʿud, Kaʿb al-Ahbar, al-Shaʿbi, al-Nakhaʿi, Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi, Ikrimah, Said ibn Jubayr and Qatadah, that it was abrogated by the verse that follows it.

It is also established by what the compilers of the six books narrated, by way of Qatadah, from Zurarah ibn Awfa, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has overlooked for me, on behalf of my community, what its souls think, so long as they do not speak it or act upon it."

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-Araj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah said: When My servant intends an evil deed, do not record it against him. If he does it, record it as one evil deed. When he intends a good deed and does not do it, record it as a good deed. If he does it, record it as ten." This is the wording of Muslim. It is also in his independent narrations, through Ismail ibn Jafar, from al-Ala, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Allah said: When My servant intends a good deed and does not do it, I record it for him as a good deed. If he does it, I record it as ten good deeds up to seven hundred times. When he intends an evil deed and does not do it, I do not record it against him. If he does it, I record it as one evil deed."

Abd al-Razzaq said: Mamar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us, from Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah said: When My servant resolves to do a good deed, I record it for him as a good deed so long as he does not do it. If he does it, I record it for him as ten times its like. When he resolves to do an evil deed, I forgive it for him so long as he does not do it. If he does it, I record it for him as its like." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) also said: "The angels said: My Lord, your servant intends to do an evil deed, and He is more perceptive of it. He said: Watch him. If he does it, record it as its like. If he leaves it, record it for him as a good deed, for he left it for My sake." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) also said: "When one of you (Muslims) perfects his Islam, every good deed he does is recorded as ten times its like, up to seven hundred times, and every evil deed is recorded as its like, until he meets Allah, mighty and majestic."

Muslim alone narrated it, from Muhammad ibn Rafiʿ, from Abd al-Razzaq, with this context and wording, and part of it is in Sahih al-Bukhari.

Muslim also said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, from Hisham, from Ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever intends a good deed but does not do it, a good deed is recorded for him. Whoever intends a good deed and does it, [ten] is recorded for him, up to seven hundred times. Whoever intends an evil deed but does not do it, it is not recorded. If he does it, it is recorded." Muslim alone narrated it, to the exclusion of the other compilers.

[Muslim] narrated to us: Shaybān ibn Farrūkh narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Wārith narrated to us, from al-Jaʿd Abū ʿUthmān, who narrated to us Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUtāridī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), what he relates from his Lord, the Exalted, that He said: "Indeed Allah wrote down the good deeds and the bad deeds, then He made that clear. Whoever intends a good deed but does not do it, Allah writes it for him with Himself as a complete good deed. And if he intends it and does it, Allah writes it for him with Himself as ten good deeds up to seven hundred times, up to many multiples. And whoever intends a bad deed but does not do it, Allah writes it for him with Himself as a complete good deed. And if he intends it and does it, Allah writes it as one bad deed."

Then Muslim narrated it from Yahyā ibn Yahyā, from Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān, from al-Jaʿd Abū ʿUthmān, in this chain, with the same meaning as the narration of ʿAbd al-Wārith, and he added: "And Allah erases it, and none perishes before Allah except one who is destroyed."

And in the narration of Suhayl, from his father, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: Some people from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came and asked him: "We find within ourselves things that any one of us would consider too great to speak of." He said: "Have you really found that?" They said: "Yes." He said: "That is the clear faith (ṣarīḥ al-īmān)."

This is the wording of Muslim, and it is also in Muslim through the route of al-Aʿmash, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), with it. Muslim also narrated, from the hadith of Mughīrah, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the whisperings (waswasah), and he said: "That is the clear faith." [In A and W: "That is pure faith."]

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding: ﴿And whether you show what is in your selves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it﴾, that it was not abrogated; rather, when Allah gathers the creatures on the Day of Resurrection, He will say: "I will inform you of what you concealed within your selves, which My angels did not witness. As for the believers, He will inform them and forgive them what they spoke to themselves about, and this is His saying: ﴿Allah will call you to account for it﴾, meaning: He will inform you. As for the people of doubt and suspicion, He will inform them of what they concealed of denial, and this is His saying: ﴿So He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills﴾, and this is His saying: ﴿But He will call you to account for what your hearts have earned﴾ [al-Baqarah: 225], meaning: of doubt and hypocrisy." Al-ʿAwfī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk narrated something close to this from him.

Ibn Jarīr narrated similar from Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk. And from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī that he said: it is muḥkamah (decisive), not abrogated. Ibn Jarīr chose this view, and argued that being called to account does not necessarily entail punishment, and that Allah, the Exalted, may call to account and forgive, and may call to account and punish, by the hadith he narrated at this verse, saying: Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, Ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us, from Saʿīd and Hishām (ḥ). And Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to me, Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, Hishām narrated to us, both of them said in their hadith: from Qatādah, from Ṣafwān ibn Muḥriz, who said: "While we were circumambulating the House with ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar, and he was circumambulating, a man approached him and said: 'O Ibn ʿUmar, what did you hear the Messenger of Allah (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam) say about the private conversation (najwā)?' He said: 'I heard the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The believer will draw near to his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, until He places His covering (kanaf) upon him, and He makes him acknowledge his sins, saying: 'Do you recognize such-and-such?' He will say: 'My Lord, I recognize it,' twice, until when He has brought him to what Allah willed, He will say: 'Indeed I concealed them for you in the world, and today I forgive them for you.'" He said: "Then his book of good deeds, or his record, will be given to him in his right hand. As for the disbelievers and the hypocrites, they will be called out before the witnesses: ﴿These are the ones who lied against their Lord. Surely the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers﴾ [Hūd: 18]."

This hadith is recorded in the two Ṣaḥīḥs and others through multiple routes from Qatādah, with it.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: My father narrated to us, Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Umayyah [in C: "from Āminah"], who said: I asked ʿĀ'ishah about this verse: ﴿And whether you show what is in your selves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it﴾. She said: "No one has asked me about it since I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about it, and he said: 'This is Allah's pledge (mubāyaʿah) with the servant: what befalls him of fever, misfortune, and wealth he places in the hand of his sleeve, then searches for it and is alarmed, then finds it in his pocket. Indeed the believer comes out of his sins just as red gold comes out of the furnace [from the kīr] [addition from Tafsir al-Ṭabarī].'"

Likewise al-Tirmidhī narrated it, and Ibn Jarīr, through the route of Ḥammād ibn Salamah, with it. Al-Tirmidhī said: "Gharīb; we do not know it except from this narration."

I say: His shaykh ʿAlī ibn Zayd ibn Jud'ān is weak, and he is erratic in his narrations. He narrates this hadith from the wife of his father, Umm Muḥammad Umayyah bint ʿAbd Allah, from ʿĀ'ishah, and there is no other narration from her in the books.

**Ibn Kathir's Commentary (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 285–286 (Part 1 of 2)**

The narrations on the virtues of these two noble verses, may Allah benefit us by them.

The first hadith: Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us, Shu'bah informed us, from Sulayman, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Whoever recites the two verses," and Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from Abu Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the two verses from the end of Surat al-Baqarah in a night, they will suffice him."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5008.]]

It was also narrated by the rest of the compilers (al-jama'ah) through the route of Sulayman ibn Mihran al-A'mash, with its chain, in the same wording.[[Sahih Muslim, no. 808; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1397; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2881; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 8019; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 1368.]] It is also in the two Sahihs through the route of al-Thawri, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd al-Rahman, from him, with the same wording.[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5009, and Sahih Muslim, no. 807; however, in Muslim it is from Zuhayr, from Mansur, with it.]] It is also in the two Sahihs from 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Alqamah, from Abu Mas'ud, — 'Abd al-Rahman said: "Then I met Abu Mas'ud, and he narrated it to me."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5008, and Sahih Muslim, no. 808.]]

Thus Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated it: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, Shari'k narrated to us, from 'Asim, from al-Musayyab ibn Rafi', from 'Alqamah, from Abu Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever recites the two verses from the end of Surat al-Baqarah in his night, they will suffice him."[[Musnad Ahmad (4/118).]]

The second hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Husayn narrated to us, Shaybān narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ribi', from Kharashah ibn al-Hurr, from al-Ma'rur ibn Suwayd, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been given the closing verses of Surat al-Baqarah from a treasure beneath the Throne, which no prophet before me was given."[[Musnad Ahmad (5/151).]]

It was also narrated by Ibn Mardawayh, from the hadith of al-Ash'ari, from al-Thawri, from Mansur, from Ribi', from Zayd ibn Zibyan, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been given the closing verses of Surat al-Baqarah from a treasure beneath the Throne."[[Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Shu'ab al-Iman, no. 2404, through the route of al-Ash'ari with it.]]

The third hadith: Muslim said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, Malik ibn Mighwal narrated to us (ḥ). And Ibn Numayr and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us together, from 'Abd Allah ibn Numayr — and their wordings are close — Ibn Numayr said: My father narrated to us, Malik ibn Mighwal narrated to us, from al-Zubayr ibn 'Adiy [in manuscript A: "ibn 'Ali"], from Talhah, from Murrah, from 'Abd Allah, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey, he was brought to the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha), which is in the seventh heaven. To it ends what ascends from the earth, and it is taken from there; and to it ends what descends from above it, and it is taken from there. He (Allah) said: ﴿When there covered the Lote Tree that which covered﴾ [al-Najm: 16]. He said: "Golden moths." He said: "And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was given three things: he was given the five prayers, he was given the closing verses of Surat al-Baqarah, and whoever among his nation did not associate anything with Allah was forgiven the grave sins."[[Sahih Muslim, no. 173.]]

The fourth hadith: Ahmad said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Razi narrated to us, Salamah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Marthad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Yazani, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir al-Juhani, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "Recite the two verses from the end of Surat al-Baqarah, for I have been given them from beneath the Throne." This is a sound (hasan) chain, but they did not record it in their books.[[Musnad Ahmad (4/147).]]

The fifth hadith: Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Kamil narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Harbi narrated to us, Musaddad informed us [in manuscript A: "Musarrif informed us"], Abu 'Awanah informed us [in manuscripts Jim and A: "from Abu 'Awanah"], from Abu Malik, from Ribi', from Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We have been preferred over the people with three things: these verses from the end of Surat al-Baqarah were given to me from a treasure house beneath the Throne, which no one was given before me, and no one will be given after me."[[Narrated by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 8022, through the route of Adam ibn Abi Iyas, from Abu 'Awanah, with it.]]

Then he narrated it from the hadith of Nu'aym ibn Abi Hindi, from Ribi', from Hudhayfah, with something similar.

The sixth hadith: Ibn Mardawayh said: 'Abd al-Baqi ibn Nafi' narrated to us, Isma'il ibn al-Fadl informed us, Muhammad ibn Hatim ibn Bazi' informed us, Ja'far ibn 'Awn informed us, from Malik ibn Mighwal, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from 'Ali, who said: "I do not see anyone who understood Islam sleeping until he recites the closing verses of Surat al-Baqarah, for they are a treasure that your Prophet (ﷺ) was given from beneath the Throne."

And Waki' narrated it from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Umayr ibn 'Amr al-Kharifi, from 'Ali, who said: "I do not see anyone who understands, to whom Islam has reached, sleeping until he recites the Verse of the Throne and the closing verses of Surat al-Baqarah, for they are from a treasure beneath the Throne."[[Narrated by Ibn al-Darib in Fada'il al-Qur'an, no. 169, through the route of Abu Ishaq, from 'Umayr ibn Sa'id, with it. Al-Nawawi said: "Sahih according to the conditions of al-Bukhari and Muslim."]]

The seventh hadith: Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi said: Bundar narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ash'ath ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Jarmi [in manuscript A: "al-San'ani"], from Abu Qilabah, from Abu al-Ash'ath al-San'ani, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah wrote a Book two thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. From it He sent down two verses with which He concluded Surat al-Baqarah, and they are not recited in a house for three nights, and a devil approaches it." Then he said: "This is a gharib hadith." Thus al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah with it, and said: "Sahih according to the conditions of Muslim, though they did not record it" [in manuscript A: "and he did not record it"].[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2882; al-Mustadrak (1/562).]]

The eighth hadith: Ibn Mardawayh said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Madyan narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm informed us, Isma'il ibn 'Amr informed us, Ibn Abi Maryam informed us, Yusuf ibn Abi al-Hajjaj narrated to me, from Sa'id, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) recited the end of Surat al-Baqarah and the Verse of the Throne, he would smile and say: "They are from the treasure of the Most Merciful beneath the Throne." And when he recited: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾ [al-Nisa': 123], and ﴿And that man will have nothing except what he strives for, and that his effort will be seen, then he will be recompensed for it with the fullest recompense﴾ [al-Najm: 39–41], he would say "Inna lillah" and become humble.[[Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (2/7), attributing it to Ibn Mardawayh; its chain contains unknown narrators.]]

The ninth hadith: Ibn Mardawayh said: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Kufi narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Hamzah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Bakr [in manuscript A: "ibn Bukayr"] narrated to us, Makki ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Humayd narrated to us, from Abu Malih, from Ma'qil ibn Yasar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been given the Opening of the Book (al-Fatihah) and the closing verses of Surat al-Baqarah from beneath the Throne, and the mufassal is a supererogatory addition."[[Narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak and declared it sahih (1/559), through the route of 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Humayd with something similar; al-Dhahabi responded: "In it is 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Humayd, whom they abandoned."]]

The tenth hadith: It has already preceded in the virtues of al-Fatihah, from the narration of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Isa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was with Jibril, he heard a creaking from above him. Jibril raised his gaze to the sky and said: "This is a gate that has been opened in the sky, which has never been opened before." He said: "An angel descended from it, came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and said: 'Rejoice in two lights that you have been given, which no prophet before you was given: the Opening of the Book, and the closing verses of Surat al-Baqarah. You will not recite a letter from them except that you will be given it.'" Narrated by Muslim and al-Nasa'i, and this is his wording.[[Sahih Muslim, no. 806; Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/138).]]

[The eleventh hadith: Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi said in his Musnad: Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, Safwan narrated to us, Ayfa' ibn 'Abd Allah al-Kula'i narrated to us [in al-Isabah: "Ayfa' ibn 'Abd al-Kula'i"], who said: A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, which verse in the Book of Allah is greatest?" He said: "The Verse of the Throne: ﴿Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence﴾." He said: "Then which verse in the Book of Allah do you love to befall you and your nation?" He said: "The end of Surat al-Baqarah, for it does not leave any good in this world or the Hereafter except that it encompasses it."[[Sunan al-Darimi, no. 3380; Ibn Hajar said in al-Isabah (1/139): "It is mursal or mu'dal."]]] [Addition from manuscript Jim.]

So His statement, the Exalted: ﴿The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord﴾ is an informing about the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding that.

Ibn Jarir said: Bishr narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said when this verse was revealed: "And it is right for him to believe."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (6/124).]]

Al-Hakim also narrated in his Mustadrak: Abu al-Nadr al-Faqih narrated to us, Mu'adh ibn Najdah al-Qurashi narrated to us, Khallad ibn Yahya narrated to us, Abu 'Aqil narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When this verse was revealed upon the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "It is right that he should believe." Then al-Hakim said: "Its chain is sahih, though they did not record it." [[Al-Mustadrak (2/287); al-Dhahabi responded: "Munqati' (disconnected)," because Yahya ibn Abi Kathir saw Anas but did not hear from him.]]

* *

His statement: ﴿And the believers﴾ is a conjunction with ﴿the Messenger﴾. Then He informed about all of them, saying: ﴿Each one believes in Allah, His angels, His books, and His messengers. We make no distinction between any of His messengers.﴾ So the believers believe that Allah is One, the Unique, the Single, the Eternal Refuge, there is no deity other than Him and no lord besides Him. They affirm all the prophets, messengers, and books sent down from the heaven upon the chosen servants of Allah, the messengers and prophets, and they make no distinction between any of them, so that they believe in some and disbelieve in others. Rather, all of them are, in their view, truthful, righteous, rightly guided, and guiding to the paths of goodness. Although some of them abrogated the law of others by the permission of Allah, all were ultimately abrogated by the law of Muhammad (ﷺ), the Seal of the Prophets and Messengers, upon whose law the Hour will be established, and a group of his nation will remain upon the truth, prevailing.

* *

His statement: ﴿And they say: We hear and we obey﴾, meaning: we hear Your word, O our Lord, and we understand it, act upon it, and comply by carrying out the deeds required by it. ﴿Your forgiveness, our Lord﴾: a request for forgiveness, pardon, mercy, and kindness.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn Harb al-Mawsili narrated to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding the statement of Allah: ﴿The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and the believers﴾ up to His statement: ﴿Your forgiveness, our Lord﴾. He said: "I have indeed forgiven you." ﴿And to You is the destination﴾, meaning: to You is the return and the final place on the Day when the reckoning takes place.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 2, verses 285–286 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Bayan, from Hakim, from Jabir, who said: When the verse ﴿The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and so do the believers. Each one believes in Allah, His angels, His books, and His messengers, [saying], "We make no distinction between any of His messengers." And they say, "We hear and we obey. [We seek] Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final return."﴾ was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Gabriel said: "Allah has praised you and your Ummah well, so ask, and you will be given." So he asked: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾ until the end of the verse.[1]

* *

As for His saying, ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾, it means He does not burden anyone beyond his ability. This is among His kindness toward His creation, His compassion for them, and His benevolence toward them. This is the abrogating verse that lifted what the Companions had feared, in His saying: ﴿Whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it﴾. That is, even if He calls to account and questions, He will only punish for what a person is able to prevent. As for what cannot be prevented, such as the whisperings and the talk of the soul, a person is not held responsible for it, and disliking evil whisperings is a sign of faith.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿It has what it earned﴾, meaning good, ﴿and it bears what it earned﴾, meaning evil. This applies to the deeds that fall under obligation. Then Allah, Exalted is He, said, guiding His servants to ask Him, and He has guaranteed them a response, just as He guided and taught them to say: ﴿Our Lord, do not hold us accountable if we forget or make mistakes﴾, meaning if we neglect an obligation out of forgetfulness, or commit a prohibited act in the same way, ﴿or err﴾, meaning we go wrong in an action, out of ignorance of its legal ruling.

It has been established in Sahih Muslim, in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, that [Allah] said: "Yes," and in the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, Allah said: "I have done it."

Ibn Majah in his Sunan, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih,[2] narrated from the hadith of Abu 'Amr al-Awza'i, from 'Ata'. Ibn Majah said in his narration: from Ibn 'Abbas. Al-Tabarani and Ibn Hibban said: from 'Ata', from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has removed from my Ummah error, forgetfulness, and what they have been compelled to do." It has been narrated through other chains, and Ahmad and Abu Hatim criticized it,[3] and Allah knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abu Bakr al-Hudhali narrated to us, from Shahr, from Umm al-Darda', from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed Allah has overlooked for my Ummah three things: error, forgetfulness, and compulsion." Abu Bakr said: I mentioned that to al-Hasan, and he said: "Indeed, and do you not recite it as Quran: ﴿Our Lord, do not hold us accountable if we forget or err﴾?"[4]

* *

As for His saying, ﴿Our Lord, and do not place upon us a burden like that which You placed upon those before us﴾, meaning do not impose upon us difficult deeds, even if we are able to bear them, as You prescribed for the past nations before us, such as the shackles and burdens that were upon them. Through Your Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), the Prophet of mercy, You removed these in Your law which You sent him with, the upright, easy, and tolerant religion.

It has been established in Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Allah said: 'Yes.'"

And from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Allah said: 'I have done it.'" The hadith has come through several chains from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "I was sent with the tolerant, easy monotheism (al-hanifiyyah al-samhah)."[5]

* *

As for His saying, ﴿Our Lord, and do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear﴾, meaning with obligations, calamities, and trials. Do not test us with what we cannot endure.

Makhul said regarding His saying, ﴿Our Lord, and do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear﴾: "It is estrangement and sexual desire." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it. "Allah said: 'Yes.'" And in the other hadith: "Allah said: 'I have done it.'"

* *

As for His saying, ﴿And pardon us﴾, meaning regarding what is between us and You, of our shortcomings and slips that You know of. ﴿And forgive us﴾, meaning regarding what is between us and Your servants, so do not expose us before them for our bad deeds and ugly actions. ﴿And have mercy on us﴾, meaning regarding what is yet to come, so do not, by Your granting of success, cause us to fall into another sin. For this reason they said: the sinner needs three things: that Allah pardon him regarding what is between him and Allah, that He conceal him from His servants so as not to disgrace him before them, and that He protect him so that he does not fall into the like of it. It has already been mentioned in the hadith that Allah said: "Yes." And in the other hadith: "Allah said: 'I have done it.'"

* *

As for His saying, ﴿You are our Protector﴾, meaning You are our Guardian and our Helper, in You we place our trust, You are the One sought for help, and upon You we rely, and there is no power or strength for us except through You, ﴿so give us victory over the disbelieving people﴾, meaning those who denied Your religion, rejected Your oneness and the message of Your Prophet, worshipped other than You, and associated others with You among Your servants. So grant us victory over them, and make the final outcome ours over them in this world and the Hereafter. Allah said: "Yes." And in the hadith narrated by Muslim from Ibn 'Abbas: "Allah said: 'I have done it.'"

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, that Mu'adh, may Allah be pleased with him, whenever he finished this surah, [and reached] ﴿so give us victory over the disbelieving people﴾, would say: "Amin."[6]

Waki' narrated it from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from a man, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, that when he completed al-Baqarah he would say: "Amin."[7]

[Note from the manuscript: End of the tafsir of Surah al-Baqarah. All praise, grace, favor, and beautiful good praise belong to Allah, and Allah is sufficient for us and the best disposer of affairs. May Allah's blessings be upon our master Muhammad, his family, and all his companions. Followed, God willing, by Surah Al 'Imran.]
